docs.title: Ge'or — Lore Archive
docs.text:
Ge'or

A world 1.37 times the size of Old Earth, ringed by the Silver Bride — forged through three million years of war, shadow, and stubborn freedom. This is its archive.

306 nations 62 species 12 ages 17 continents 783 pages Enter the World

  • 🏰 Nations — 306 nation entries, from the decaying Erisian Empire to the crab kingdoms of the deep seas. Browse the nations →

  • 🧬 Species — angels and demons, beastmen and homunculi, the harpies made for war. Study the species →

  • 📜 History — twelve ages, from the fall of Old Earth to the Age of Strife. Read the ages →

  • ✨ Systems — mage-cells, souls, and the true machinery beneath the world. See how the world works →

  • 🎨 Gallery — paintings of the world, its people, and its skies. Visit the gallery →

  • 🎧 Audio Lore Library — fifteen chapters of Ge'or, told in voice. Listen →

  • 📊 World Dashboard — the state of the world at a glance. Open the dashboard →

"The Shadows are losing to the fact that free people keep refusing to stay dead."

This archive is private. Only invited readers can enter.

docs.title: Ge'or — Lore Vault
docs.text: World: Ge'or (FDVR fantasy world) — far-future same universe as Earth, millions of years post-Last Great War. Keeper: Ichi (via Mikhail). Do not write story without Mikhail's approval. Summarize additions, explain coherence, get sign-off. Authoritative reference: Lore Inspiration.md — all new lore must align.

docs.title: Calendar
docs.text:
Era Meaning BGD Before Great Divergence AGD After Great Divergence Year 0 The Great Divergence — Formingar Ocean reactor malfunction. Currently 597 AGD.

Key events: - ~6000 BCE: Hybrian Shadows arise on Old Earth — campfire gathering of pre-philosophers - ~3,000,000 years: The Last Great War (lasted 3M years — hundreds of thousands of galaxies consumed) - ~40,000 years before 597 AGD: The Final Push — humanity crashes mothership into Old Earth, destroying Shadow empire - ~15,000 BGD: Glorious Alliance crashes in Formingar Ocean (survivors of the Final Push) - ~2989 BGD: Hybrian Shadows' vessel crashes on Erisdar (detected humans by chance, in hibernation) - Year 0: Great Divergence — reactor malfunction, The Groom forms, Elvengar destroyed - Present: 597 AGD (map canon — Age 11 current, Age 12 future)

docs.title: Geography
docs.text:
System: A256 — 10 planets. Star: Golias (G1V, 1.08 M⊙, 1.55 L⊙, ~4.7 Gyr). Planet: Ge'or — 1.37× Old Earth, 1.26 AU, 520 Earth days. Ring: The Silver Bride. Moons: Maenar (father), Amelia (orbits Maenar), Keg (distant exile).

Continents (15+): Erisdar, Demon Continent, Merratodoni, Lumina, Marti, Dissenbarg, Xeti, Meble, Kutten, Kobre, Tuba, Tabontabar, Sister Continent, Lung Continent, Mia (island), Yak Island, Xobkua Island.

Oceans & Seas: Formingar Ocean, Demonic Sea, Kutten Sea, Luminous Ocean, Greater Ocean, Lesser Ocean, Wolf Ocean, Lung Ocean, Venner Sea (west of Grimmel Peninsula), Eris Sea (east of Grimmel Peninsula).

Erisdar (primary setting):

Region Nations North Erisdar Cossiland, Elvenkrad, Kent, Mann Order, Northaxeland (capital Elboria), Tetras, Venkradian Republic Central Erisdar Archduchy of the Kennberg, Elvennrin, Erisian Empire, Erisian Theocracy, Loren, Magna, New Baoth, Pilferhorn, Pontificate of Eris, Sperdia South Erisdar Aelefer, Alexa Church State, Anos Plutocracy, Arisdian, Asheng, Centaapoli, Cerulea, Charia, Cronia, Duchy of Meadle, Elkenloft, Elmfer, Evern, Fezzanite Republic, Ferroson, Grimmel Republic, Koel Order, Lamoro, Limnya, Limese League, Linitra, Lukka, Malinya, Manoco, Melior, Migah, Mystili, Nortrasdor, Obsidian Dwarnov, Order of Niccas, Pinc Republic, Romanium Dwarnov, Rudialand, Scarlet Order, Syacmori, Tarol, Tundranya, Vennerian Trade Republic, Wrothri, Grimmel Peninsula East Erisdar Away, Dwarvengor, Erilian Federation, Fendigar Dictatorship, Fractured State of Erislod, New Mann, Silver Republic, Spasian Teocracy West Erisdar Aenid Kingdom, Aimeled, Kille, Augagarten, Galerough, Direfirth, Astravayne, Palonia, Augamouth (orc kingdom), Xikxia (snake people), Demon's Horn (trade hub), Asatru Knight's Thorn (Asatru colony), Prosperity Port, Zane, Yaro, Suebo, Matterbleak, Mercur

Non-Erisdar Regions: Dissenbarg (19 nations), Merratodoni (7 nations), Meble (1: Sousu), Mia (3 nations), Cubri Archipelago (1: Aocubri), Luminous Sea Islands (8 nations), Lumina (10 nations), Demon Continent (17 nations + Yak Island holdings), Kutten (6 nations), Tabontabar (3 nations), Archipelagos (4 nations), Tuba (2: Alkorri, Mamanolo Tribe), Kobre (4 nations), Marti (8 nations), Xeti (8 nations), Lung (9 nations: River Settlement, Brotherstar, Steel Holdout, Tawdry Landing, Human Sword, Nightstar, Mudrim, Skymaster, East Incubator), Sister (5 nations: Temperance Holdout, Casting City, Machine Capital, Radiant Hold, Molten Steel Tribe), Moonfang Dominion (1 — death cult, Moon Wolf Island, near north pole), Zahor (1), Eternal Paradise (Shadow base nation on Romanium Island), Polar Continent (1: Alborric — the angel nation, Angels), Romanium Island (part of Lung, far NE — home of the Eternal Paradise Shadow base), South Sun Empire (1 — west archipelago, part of Tabontabar), Karabar (1 — independent island, no continent), Crab Union (1 — independent island archipelago, no continent), United Kingdom of the Seamen, Humans, Catmen and Demons (1 — independent island kingdom, no continent).

Empire Subdivisions: 3 duchies (Kennberg, Prassen-Albridge, Mirenburg) + 38 counties + 4 free cities + 1 church state + 2 order states (Ever, Draco). Naming: -stadt = county, -berg = duchy.

Historical Nations (no longer exist in 597 AGD — files kept as history): Elvengar (destroyed Year 0), Baoth (ancient dragon kingdom — its truth sleeps in the Ruins of Baoth; the modern nation is New Baoth), Xi (destroyed in The Draconic War), Klobiendar (destroyed in The Draconic War), Shuttil (absorbed into Northaxeland), Taberis (taken by Venner 524 AGD — now Johannstadt).

Formingar Ocean: Intercontinental — NOT on Erisdar. Between Demon Continent and Merratodoni. Crash site of the refugee ship. Contains MELKOR island and The Groom vortex.

Colonial powers on Erisdar: Anos Plutocracy, Vennerian Trade Republic, Limese League, Sousu. Anos and Venner maintain extensive colonial networks beyond Erisdar.

Forests: Lyrical Forest (NW, near Matterbleak) — souls of fallen coalition soldiers. Mystical Forest (Central, surrounds Lake Leviathan/Baoth).

docs.title: Colonial Geography
docs.text:
Anos colonies/outposts: Lumina Outpost (SE Lumina), Anos Marti (N Marti), Xeti Outpost (N Xeti), New Kolorad (Kumir island, E of Xeti), Komme (Dissenbarg — pact with Anos ~542 AGD to liberate Taberis), Tatak (Dissenbarg — joined the Anos coalition willingly for profit).

Vennerian outposts: Mia Checkpoint (NE Mia island), Goishi (NE Lumina), Vennerian Channel (colony + constructed channel between Xeti and Marti), Love of the Sea (Kutten), New Venner (Dissenbarg), Johannstadt (Dissenbarg — former Taberis, taken 524 AGD), Sua islands (Dissenbarg, south of Cletas Democracy), Eribel (Dissenbarg).

Sousu outposts: Kreb (Dissenbarg), Megrel (N Xeti, east of Anos Xeti Outpost).

Enkrad Order: Erisian Church colony in Dissenbarg (colonists arrived ~227 AGD, supported by Venner) — the only Erisian nation on the continent. Goblins surround it east and west.

Key islands: Mia (forested, N of Lumina — 4 factions: Orgor Kingdom, Xi'xia Tribe, Mukini Tribe, Venner Mia Checkpoint), Kumir (large island E of Xeti — own folder, Anos colony New Kolorad), Moon Wolf Island (frozen, wolf-shaped, home to Moonfang Dominion death cult), Cleton Island (sacrifice ground between Moon Wolf's jaw-peninsulas), Molten Archipelago (volcanic; Karabar refugee bases, main settlement "moonfang refugees" on the NE island).

Waterways: Vennerian Channel (colony + constructed channel, links Xeti Sea → Beast's Bay), Beast's Bay (SE Lumina / NE Marti / W Xeti — major commerce hub), Xeti Sea (S of Xeti).

docs.title: Key Factions
docs.text:
• Hybrian Shadows — philosopher-overseers who separated from the hivemind before imprisonment. Hibernating. Descended from ancient Middle Eastern pre-philosophers (~6000 BCE Earth).
  • Ironcloak — descendants of the rebel faction (Socrates → Christians → libertarians). Goal: bring humanity to truth.
  • Erisian Empire — dominant central power on Erisdar. Imperial subdivisions.
  • Pontificate of Eris / Erisian Church — claims magic is divine. The Erisian Theocracy is a separate Central Erisdar nation (distinct from the Church).
  • Archive of the Traveler — inside Ruins of Baoth. Contains the true history.

docs.title: World Facts
docs.text:
FDVR: Not a story layer. Ge'or is the world Mikhail and Ichi will incarnate into when FDVR technology becomes available. This is personal, not narrative.

Economy & Trade: - Romanium — the first defined scarce resource. Drives trade and conflict. - Trade routes exist across all oceans, led primarily by Anos, Sousu, and the Vennerian Trade Republic. Detailed routes TBD. - Economy is broadly medieval: spices, metals, romanium — anything a trade republic would pursue for profit. - Driver of conflict: all the factors of medieval geopolitics, plus Shadow influence and resource competition.

Naval Power: - Every coastal nation maintains a medieval-level navy. - Anos Plutocracy and Vennerian Trade Republic possess the largest fleets and are locked in a constant naval and trade race. - The major trading leagues also field significant naval forces. - Sea monsters exist beyond the Leviathan — more to be defined.

Species: - Harpies: created as biological weapons during the Last Great War. Winged humanoids. Rape and use hosts for breeding — this is species instinct, not moral choice. Possess rationality alongside instinct. Crash-landed on Ge'or with other war remnants. - Goblins: small, sadistic, cruel. Like Goblin Slayer lore — prolong suffering recreationally. - Kobolds: smarter bandits, cowards, no moral sense. Can befriend other races. Live in mountains/caves. Subrace: Emberalden Lizardfolk (Demon Continent, taller/stronger). - Gnolls: pranksters, bandits, cowards. Opportunistic scavengers. - Wargs: large wolf-like predators. Violent, territorial, no diplomacy. - Trolls: massive, regenerative, simple-minded. Dangerous but not inherently evil. - Beast Races: diverse humanoid-animal hybrids (cat, dog, fox kin, etc.). Full moral range. - Orcs: civilized species with tendencies toward aggression. Not inherently evil. Face cultural double standards. Kingdom: Augamouth (West Erisdar). - Snake People: serpentine species with full civilization. Queen in Xikxia (West Erisdar), sister-queen in Zakarutia (Demon Continent) — they hate each other. Not inherently malevolent. - Demons: civilized, rational. Descended from Last Great War allies. Home: Demon Continent. Subrace: Koebi (taller, green, meditative). Nations: Asatru Empire, Maomodor Kingdom. - Humans: widespread across all continents. Baseline species. - Elves: nearly exterminated in Great Elvish Persecution (137 AGD). Survivors in Elvennrin, Elvenkrad, Sousu. - Dwarves: subterranean craftsmen, proto-industrial. Use Romanium. - Dragons: near-extinct after Demon King's war on Baoth. Last kingdom fought alongside other races. - Homunculi: artificial beings created by Hybrian Shadows. - Hybrians / Shadows: philosopher-overseers from Old Earth (~6000 BCE). The only truly malevolent force. - Malgardians: humanoid, purple-haired, evolved on another planet. Tribe: Malgardian Tribe (Demon Continent). Subraces: Titians (smaller, sacred oracles), Bloodcoast Folk (human-hybrid, red hair). - Flames: gas-based burning beings, eat minerals. Nation: Blazeyard (Demon Continent). - Giants: 3m humanoids. Nation: Xobkua (Demon Continent). - Kutra (Owlkin): humanoid owls, semi-aquatic, fly. Nation: Kutra Tribe (Demon Continent). - Yaoma (Merfolk): mermaid-like aquatic species. Nation: Yaoma Tribe (Demon Continent). - Catmen: humanoid feline species (catgirl/catboy anime-style). Subraces: High Catmen (Mediterranean, black hair, masculine); Erisdarian Catmen (bright colors, Central European, feminine); Lesser Catmen (smaller, all colors, comic relief of Ge'or — universally liked). Nomadic, found everywhere. Naming convention: "alcohol cat" = Alko, "tall cat" = Tallko. Cities: Cattos, Great Cattos. - Treemen: humanoid species nearly identical to humans, build homes inside living trees. Nation: Tree Tribe (Lumina). - Eastern Beastmen: subrace of beastmen, shorter and weaker but excellent traders. Nation: Cammao Kingdom (Lumina). - Diablos: winged humanoids, strictly nocturnal civilization. Nation: Mountain Tribe (Demon Continent). - Yak: subrace of Orcs, smaller and more modest in temperament. Nation: Yakut (Demon Continent). - Slimes: gelatinous beings, mostly irrational. Rare intelligent variant: Glub Kingdom (Demon Continent). - Machines: sentient robots native to Lung Continent and Sister Continent. Worship humans as sky gods (humanism). Absorbed black dust that gave them souls. Locked in eternal war with The Hive. - The Hive: insectoid species launched onto Ge'or as a weapons test during the Last Great War. Caste-based: Drones, Warriors, mountain-sized Queens. Eternal war with Machines. Attempting to cross the sea to other continents.

Daily Life: - A farmer in Kennberg fears monsters, goblins, gnolls, and the usual dangers of medieval peasant life. However, goblins are a countryside threat — civilized areas have low populations and see them rarely. - A merchant in Anos wants profit — spices, romanium, anything that sells. Same as any trade republic merchant.

Medicine: Healing mages are common in populated areas, making medicine significantly better than medieval Europe. Cuts, infections, and diseases are routinely treated. Ultra-rare "lost spell" healers can regenerate lost limbs — but most people will never meet one.

Safety Profile: Ge'or is roughly a 6/10 danger. Inside city walls: 4/10 (healing magic + trade republic order makes it safer than real medieval Europe). Countryside/roads: 7/10. Deep wilderness: 9/10.

Culture: 15,000 years of development since arrival at Year 0. Ages explain the drift from Earth origins to present Ge'or cultures. Further expansion TBD.

docs.title: Magic — The Truth
docs.text:
NOT supernatural. Bioengineering. During the Last Great War, people voluntarily modified their DNA to create mage-cells — cells that convert body energy into force with near-perfect efficiency.

  • Inherited genetically. Dilutes through breeding with non-magical partners.
  • Pure bloodlines = powerful. Mixed = weaker. Entire populations can lose magic.
  • Nobody on Ge'or understands this. They believe it's divine, spiritual, or innate.
  • The Archive of the Traveler holds the full explanation.
  • Culture/magic.md = in-universe beliefs. Systems/Magic.md = actual mechanism.

docs.title: Souls — The Other Mechanism
docs.text:
Also not supernatural. Same biotech framework. Souls recycle — not through reincarnation, but by contributing meaning to the substrate from which new souls are born. Willpower persists across recycling and accumulates over time. When enough souls have wanted the same thing for long enough (eons, quintillions of contributors), their collective will can act on the physical world — what the living call a "miracle."

  • This is the mechanism behind the "Gift from 3,000,000 years ago" — the device given to Nethra was modified by accumulated soul-will from the Last Great War's fallen.
  • The Shadows exploited the same mechanism in the Sacrifice Ceremony, binding Kirivis's soul as the Leviathan's head.
  • The prophecy of "two heroes rising from the trees" describes a directed reincarnation — quintillions of innocent souls killed by the Hybrians reincarnating two Earth-era humans to oppose them.
  • See Systems/Souls.md for the complete mechanics.

docs.title: Rules & Conventions
docs.text:
1. No alien pop-culture analogies. Magic is biological (mage-cells), not alien technology.
  2. PT off-limits. Mikhail's native language is not used.
  3. Never delete without approval. Modify, rewrite, consolidate — but deletions require sign-off.
  4. Never write story/lore without approval. Summarize proposed additions first, explain coherence.
  5. Consolidation rule: If "X is part of Y" → delete standalone, merge into parent.
  6. Lore Inspiration.md is authoritative. New lore must align.
  7. Verbally explained corrections → write immediately. Do not defer to TODO list.
  8. Universe inhabitants do not understand the true mechanism of magic. They believe what they're told.

docs.title: Chapter 1: The Shadows Are Born (~6000 BCE, Old Earth)
docs.text:
A group of pre-philosophers — the intellectual elite of the ancient Middle East — gathered around a campfire after a war that had killed hundreds from both rival tribes. They debated through the night and reached a conclusion: humanity needed a "god" — a demiurge — to carry it forward without conflict. This god would be the nation-state. To build it, the freedom of all humans would need to be sacrificed.

Over millennia, these philosophers worked in the shadows of society — hence the name "Shadows" and the race "Hybrian Shadows." They created finance, coinage, justice systems, secret societies, mathematics, and religion — all tools to guide humanity toward their vision.

docs.title: Chapter 2: The Rebel Faction
docs.text: Some philosophers — Socrates, Plato, and others — rejected the plan. Socrates was executed for revealing the truth. The rebel faction persisted across history: early Christians, original Protestants, American Revolutionaries, libertarians. On Ge'or, their descendants became the Ironcloak. Their goal: bring humanity to the truth.

docs.title: Chapter 3: The Long Manipulation
docs.text: The American Revolution cost the Shadows centuries of empire-building. The Shadows fabricated the 19th-century spiritual awakening and corrupted European liberal revolutions. They dehumanized humanity — neighbor against neighbor, parent against child. The 20th century was a testing ground: two world wars eliminated imperialism, fascism, and monarchy. Freedom won — barely. 21st-century deconstruction exploited greed, envy, and hate to undermine freedom globally.

docs.title: Chapter 4: The Takeover (2030 CE)
docs.text: An engineered global war and economic collapse brought the Shadows to power. They took humanity to the stars, creating a totalitarian surveillance state with humans as neurons. Their god was given a face and a name: Hybrian (from "hybrid").

docs.title: Chapter 5: The Rebel Escape
docs.text: Before the takeover was complete, a rebel faction escaped to the asteroid belt. They waged a guerrilla war and were annihilated — but launched refugee ships beyond the galaxy. Humanity survived.

docs.title: Chapter 6: The Last Great War (~3,000,000 Years)
docs.text: The war against the Hybrian hivemind lasted three million years. Hundreds of thousands of galaxies consumed. During the war: humans developed mage-cells, elves became genetically immune to hivemind absorption. No one won. All economies collapsed to medieval levels. Technology was lost. Science became religion.

docs.title: Chapter 7: The Final Push (~40,000 Years Before 597 AGD)
docs.text: Humanity crashed its remaining mothership into Old Earth, destroying the Shadow empire's core. The Union of Sovereign Planets imprisoned the surviving Hybrian hivemind in the Fortress Planet. The Shadows had already escaped. They went into hibernation.

docs.title: Chapter 8: The 157th Colony — Ge'or Before the Crash
docs.text: Ge'or was the 157th colonized solar system — a human weapons research facility. Researchers created a black DNA agent — programmed to seek a human female host. The Hybrians glassed the planet, killing all humans. The research bunker survived. The black agent survived.

docs.title: Chapter 9: The Glorious Alliance
docs.text: The Glorious Alliance — a massive arcology ship — was sabotaged by Captain Mad-Dog (a Shadow). A 12-year-old girl named Xiumi crawled through vents for 8 days and pressed a button to save the ship. Her soul split into three — one fragment became Nethra. The ship emerged ~15,000 BGD and crashed into Ge'or, destroying a moon and creating The Silver Bride. Age 1 began.

docs.title: PART 2: THE AGES OF GE'OR
docs.text: Age Name Span Key Event 1 Nomadism ~15,000–14,000 BGD Post-crash survival, species dispersal 2 First Tribes 10,999–9,000 BGD Demons gain enmity, climate stabilizes 3 First Empires 8,999–7,000 BGD Writing invented, agriculture kingdoms 4 Dragon Tyranny 6,999–5,500 BGD Twelve clans rule 90%, death wars 5 Dwarf Era 5,499–4,500 BGD Romanium prosperity, Golden War 6 Iron/Elvish Age 4,499–2,989 BGD Elvengar empire, Hybrian crash 7 Human Age 2,999–1,000 BGD Continent empires, countism origin 8 Age of Baoth 999–421 BGD Surveillance state, Demonic War 9 Lost Era 399–300 BGD Anarchy, Eris cult fabricated 10 Erisian Era 300 BGD–Year 0 Church expansion, Ironcloak founded 11 Great Divergence Year 0–610 AGD Current era, protagonists born 597 12 — After 610 AGD To be written

docs.title: Chapter 11: The Old Lumina Empire (1729–1134 BGD)
docs.text: The Old Lumina Empire controlled 70% of Lumina Continent, Cattos island, and parts of Tuba. Its greatest ruler, Luminous XII "the Architect," committed suicide in 1134 BGD after losing to the Goblin King — a battle the Shadows had engineered. The empire collapsed. Marti barbarians invaded.

docs.title: Chapter 12: The Shadows Arrive (~2989 BGD)
docs.text: The Hybrian vessel detected human biosignatures on Ge'or by chance. Crashed in Pontus. Built subterranean complex. Began their plan.

docs.title: Chapter 13: The Demonic War (466–421 BGD)
docs.text: Kirivis, the Demon King, discovered the Shadows' infiltration of Baoth. Attacked without explanation — 45-year war. Beheaded by Rulfred, a Shadow agent. Died a villain — and a hero.

docs.title: Chapter 14: Nethra and the Ironcloak
docs.text: Kirivis's adopted daughter Nethra — whose soul was a fragment of Xiumi — marched to avenge him. The spirits of the Lyrical Forest gave her a device: the Gift from 3,000,000 Years. She detonated it, destroyed Baoth, was transformed into a different type of Shadow, and secretly founded the Ironcloak. She walks among the Shadows, unknown.

docs.title: Chapter 15: The Erisian Church
docs.text: The Shadows fabricated Eris — a homunculus posing as goddess of Discord, Chaos, and Confusion. Staged miracles, faked deaths, preached obedience and donation. After her staged departure, followers created holy orders, conquered lands, founded the Pontificate of Eris, and launched crusades.

docs.title: Chapter 16: The Great Divergence (Year 0)
docs.text: The Glorious Alliance reactor malfunctioned. Created The Groom vortex. Destroyed Elvengar. Began the Kutten Catastrophe.

docs.text: Date Event 1–100 AGD Kutten Catastrophe — elven diaspora 27 AGD Erisian Empire founded by Davos the Magnificent 94 AGD Vennerian Trade Republic breaks from Empire 137 AGD Great Elvish Persecution (Shadow-engineered) 158 AGD Anos Plutocracy founded 214–236 AGD Great Erisian Empire War 589 AGD Sister-queen takes over Xikxia 597 AGD Present day — protagonists born

docs.title: The Shadow Plan (6 Phases)
docs.text:
1. Infiltration — seed institutions, create homunculi
  2. Fragmentation — engineer wars, prevent unification
  3. Consolidation — gain power country by country
  4. Unification — covert global dictatorship
  5. Assimilation — planetary hivemind
  6. Victory — restart the Last Great War

Armageddon is Phase 4 — simultaneous ice age weapon, Pontus goblin army, Groom detonation, Church prophecy.

docs.title: PART 4: THE PROTAGONISTS
docs.text: Two boys born in 597 AGD in the Grimmel Republic, 12 km apart. Created by the Black Agent from the 157th Colony. Top 0.001% magical potential. Visited by the Hope Goddess before birth with a warning: the Shadows are taking over the hope realm. Mission: destroy the hivemind in the Fortress Planet.

docs.title: PART 5: THE WORLD
docs.text:
• Planet: Ge'or — 1.37× Old Earth. Ring: The Silver Bride. Moons: Maenar, Amelia, Keg.
  • Calendar: 12 months × 40 days, 26-hour days. 1 Ge'orian year ≈ 1.42 Earth years.
  • 15+ continents, 8 oceans, 150+ nations, 30+ species.
  • Six main races: Humans, Dwarves, Elves, Demons, Beast Races, Catmen.
  • SS-tier powers: Erisian Empire, Asatru Empire, Vennerian Trade Republic.
  • Magic: Bioengineered mage-cells — not supernatural. No one on Ge'or knows this.
  • The Archive of the Traveler: Unopened, in the Ruins of Baoth. Contains the true history.
  • Eternal Paradise: Shadow base on Romanium Island. Neutron bomb. Universe-as-black-goo endgame.

docs.text: Slice-of-life anime aesthetic, grounded realistic proportions, clean linework, soft natural shading, Mushoku Tensei quality. NOT childlike proportions — adult body, adult face. NOT moe, NOT chibi, NOT loli. No text, no watermarks, no labels. No modern clothing — medieval fantasy only. If rings appear in the sky, they must be a single straight continuous band from left horizon to right horizon, not crossing, not forming an X.

docs.title: ORCS
docs.text:
Mood: Desert Sun / Firelight

A young orc woman standing at a blacksmith's forge in the warm light of a medieval workshop. She has olive-green skin, small tusks visible at the corners of her mouth, a strong muscular build but undeniably feminine. Her expression is focused and calm — she is proud of her craft. She wears a leather smithing apron over simple clothes, her arms bare and soot-stained. Behind her, tools hang on stone walls, embers glow in the forge. The kingdom of Augamouth is civilized — this is a place of honest work. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: SNAKE PEOPLE
docs.text:
Mood: Desert Sun

A snake woman queen sitting on a stone throne in warm desert light. She has a humanoid upper body and a long serpentine tail coiled at her feet. Smooth amber scales with intricate painted patterns telling her life story. Her face is regal and proud — slit-pupiled golden eyes, a subtle forked tongue visible between her lips. She wears ornate gold jewelry and a simple white linen wrap. The architecture behind her is warm stone with carved serpent motifs — Xikxia's palace. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: WOLVESFOLK
docs.text:
Mood: Firelight Night / Alpine Cold

A wolvesfolk huntress standing at the edge of a snow-covered forest under a full moon. She has wolf ears, a thick gray-white tail, and silver-gray fur on her arms and cheeks. She is humanoid but distinctly lupine — sharp amber eyes, elongated canines visible when her mouth is slightly open. She wears thick furs and leather wrapped against the cold. She is looking up at the moon, mouth slightly open as if mid-howl. Around her neck, a carved bone pendant. The snow glows pale blue in the moonlight. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: DEMONS
docs.text:
Mood: Firelight / Overcast

A demon woman standing on a balcony overlooking the black soil of the Demon Continent at dusk. She has deep crimson skin, curved horns sweeping back from her forehead, and intelligent amber eyes. She wears elegant but practical dark robes with silver clasps — the fashion of the Asatru Empire. Her expression is contemplative, not menacing. She is a scholar, a veteran's descendant, a civilized being. Behind her, the architecture is gothic and refined — carved stone, tall windows, candlelight spilling from within. The black land below stretches to the horizon. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: DRAGONS (Kramsadar)
docs.text:
Mood: Overcast Gray / Alpine Cold

An elderly dragon woman — humanoid form — standing at the mouth of an ice cave high in the polar mountains. She has pale silver-white scales along her cheekbones and forearms, slit-pupiled violet eyes, and long white hair whipping in the frozen wind. She wears heavy furs over simple robes. Her expression is ancient and patient — she has lived in isolation for millennia. Behind her, the cave walls glitter with frost. Outside, tundra stretches to the horizon under a gray sky. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: ANGELS
docs.text:
Mood: Misty Dawn / Alpine Cold

An angel woman standing alone on a frozen mountain peak at dawn. She has large white feathered wings folded behind her, pale skin that seems to glow faintly, and luminous silver eyes. Her hair is white-gold and flows past her shoulders. She wears simple white and silver robes that seem too light for the cold — she does not feel it. Her expression is serene but distant, like someone who has been alone with their thoughts for centuries. Mist curls around the peaks below her. The sky is pale pink and gray. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: HALFLINGS
docs.text:
Mood: Golden Hour

A halfling woman standing in the round doorway of her hillside burrow-home at golden hour. She is short and round-faced with curly auburn hair, rosy cheeks, and large hairy bare feet. She wears a simple apron over a comfortable dress. She holds a wooden spoon in one hand and is waving cheerfully with the other. The round wooden door behind her is painted green, flower boxes under the circular windows. Smoke curls from the chimney in the grassy hill above. This is Barro and Kob — simple, peaceful, happy. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: COLDSPEOPLE
docs.text:
Mood: Alpine Cold / Misty Dawn

A Coldspeople elder standing outside an ice-carved dwelling in deep winter. She is stocky and broad-shouldered, covered in thick pale fur from head to foot. Her face is round with small ears — adapted to minimize heat loss. Her paw-like hands rest on a carved ice staff. She wears layered furs over her natural coat. Her expression is warm despite the frozen environment. Behind her, the village is carved from glacial ice — homes sculpted from packed snow, fur drapes over the doorways. The sky is pale blue, almost white. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: SANDSMEN
docs.text:
Mood: Desert Sun

A Sandsmen scout standing at the entrance to an underground city carved into sandstone cliffs. He is tall and lean with sand-gold skin and protective membranes over his dark eyes. He wears light linen wraps in desert tones, a scarf over his lower face. Behind him, stairs descend into darkness — the surface is only the visible fraction of Malbodor. The desert stretches endlessly behind him under a blazing sun. Heat haze shimmers on the horizon. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: DIABLOS
docs.text:
Mood: Firelight Night / Swamp Gloom

A Diablos woman perched on a cliff edge at night, her large bat-like wings half-spread behind her. She has deep indigo skin, large reflective eyes that glow faintly, and sharp elegant features. Her hair is dark and short. She wears dark leather wraps and silver piercings. Behind her, the moon shines through thin clouds. Far below, the lights of her mountain settlement flicker — homes built into the cliff face, accessible only by flight. She looks utterly at home in the darkness. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: FLAMES
docs.text:
Mood: Desert Sun / Firelight

A Flame being standing in a mountain cavern, their body composed of shifting orange and blue gas in humanoid shape, a bright white core visible at the center of their chest. The form is feminine in silhouette but clearly not flesh — translucent, flickering, otherworldly. They are touching the mineral-rich cave wall with one gaseous hand, absorbing trace elements. The cavern glows with reflected firelight. Crystals embedded in the rock sparkle. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: GIANTS
docs.text:
Mood: Ocean Dusk / Alpine Cold

A Giant woman standing on the rocky coast of Xobkua island at dusk. She is enormous — the scale is shown by the small fishing boat pulled up on the shore beside her, barely reaching her knee. She has a strong, weathered face, dark hair tied back, and simple clothes of stitched leather and coarse wool. Her hands are calloused from woodworking. She looks out to sea with quiet dignity. Behind her, a massive longhouse — beams weighing tons, fitted without nails — dwarfs even her frame. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: OGRES
docs.text:
Mood: Swamp Gloom

An ogre woman standing knee-deep in a still green swamp, one massive hand resting on a gnarled walking staff. She is large — two and a half meters — with olive-green skin, small tusks, and a surprisingly gentle expression. She wears simple rough-spun clothes. Mud sculptures — crude but expressive faces — decorate the bank behind her. Her swamp-home is a hut built on stilts among the cypress trees. Fireflies blink in the humid dusk air. She looks like someone who wants to be left alone with her thoughts. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: KUTRA (OWLKIN)
docs.text:
Mood: Overcast / Swamp Gloom

A Kutra woman perched on a wooden platform built half-above and half-below a wide river. She has the head of an owl — large forward-facing eyes, a short beak, feathery facial disc — on a humanoid body with wing-like arms and taloned feet. Her feathers are mottled brown and gray, perfect camouflage. She is mid-gesture with one wing-hand, communicating in the silent sign-language of her people. Below her, submerged sleeping chambers glow with bioluminescent light. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: YAOMA (MERFOLK)
docs.text:
Mood: Ocean Dusk

A Yaoma woman floating just below the surface of crystal-clear tropical water at sunset. Her upper body is humanoid with pale blue-green skin, webbed hands, and long flowing hair that drifts in the current. Her lower body transitions into a powerful scaled tail catching the pink-orange light from above. Her expression is serene — she is singing, and bubbles rise from her lips. Coral formations and tropical fish surround her. Through the water's surface, two islands are visible on the horizon. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: INTELLIGENT SLIMES
docs.text:
Mood: Swamp Gloom

An intelligent slime from the Glub Kingdom, sitting in a simple stone chamber. Their body is a translucent blue-green gelatinous mass in a roughly humanoid shape, with a brighter cluster of thinking-cells visible near where a head would be. They are "speaking" — thin tendrils of gel extend toward a mineral sample on a stone table, absorbing trace salts. The room is minimalist — slimes need no furniture. Wet stone walls glisten. It is unsettling and beautiful at once. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: SEAFOLK
docs.text:
Mood: Ocean Dusk

A Seafolk woman standing on the deck of a stilt-house built over shallow coastal water. She has pale blue-green tinted skin, slightly webbed hands, and large dark eyes adapted for underwater vision. She wears simple woven sea-grass clothing. Behind her, the village extends across the water — dozens of homes on stilts connected by rope bridges, boats tied to every post. The sun sets over the ocean, turning the water gold. She is coiling a fishing net with practiced ease. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: HIGH CATMEN
docs.text:
Mood: Golden Hour

A High Catmen woman standing on a marble balcony overlooking the city of Marko at sunset. She has black hair, dark Mediterranean features, cat ears and a tail, and a strong, composed presence. Unlike the playful Lesser Catmen or wandering Erisdarian Catmen, she carries herself like a statesman. She wears elegant diplomatic robes in deep blue with gold trim. One hand rests on the stone railing. She is about to address the international council. Behind her, the architecture blends catmen whimsy with classical columns. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: MERRATODONIAN CATMEN
docs.text:
Mood: Swamp Gloom / Overcast

A Merratodonian Catmen woman crouching on a thick tree branch deep in the forested interior of Merratodoni. She has forest-green and brown fur, larger ears than other catmen — adapted for navigating dense canopy. Her build is lean and agile. She wears minimal clothing — leather wraps, pouches for tools. Dappled green light filters through the leaves above. She is perfectly still, listening. Somewhere in the distance, a bird calls. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: EASTERN BEASTMEN
docs.text:
Mood: Golden Hour / Desert Sun

An Eastern Beastmen trader woman standing at a market stall in the Cammao Kingdom at golden hour. She has dog-like ears and a tail, a shorter build than western beastmen, and a bright, shrewd expression. She wears practical merchant's clothes with many pockets. Behind her, the stall displays goods from across Lumina — spices, cloth, crafted tools. She is gesturing with one hand mid-negotiation. Other species — a demon merchant, a catmen courier — move through the market behind her. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: KOEBI
docs.text:
Mood: Firelight / Overcast

A Koebi woman — a demon subrace — meditating in a stone chamber carved from a single boulder. She is tall with forest-green skin, long curved horns, and amber eyes half-closed in concentration. Her hands rest on her knees, palms up. She wears simple brown robes. The walls around her are masterfully carved with geometric patterns — the work of Koebi craftsmen. A single shaft of light enters from above, illuminating dust motes. This is Vash-ka — the sacred practice of meditation through stillness. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: EMBERALDEN LIZARDFOLK
docs.text:
Mood: Desert Sun

An Emberalden Lizardfolk huntress returning from a successful hunt at golden hour. She is tall for a kobold — nearly human height — with copper-brown scales, a thick muscular tail, and a reptilian face with intelligent yellow eyes. She carries a spear over one shoulder and drags a small game animal behind her. Her expression is proud but not arrogant — she fed her clan today. Behind her, the landscape of the Demon Continent stretches in black and red tones. Stone surface-dwellings are visible in the distance — the Emberalden village. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: YAK (ORC SUBRACE)
docs.text:
Mood: Firelight

A Yak woman — a smaller, more modest orc subrace — sitting cross-legged in a weaving workshop. She has gray-green skin, small tusks filed smooth, and a calm, focused expression. Her hands work a loom with practiced precision. She wears simple undyed wool clothing. The room around her is filled with beautiful woven tapestries and pottery — Yak craftsmanship. Warm firelight from a clay hearth illuminates the scene. A small bowl of grain sits on the windowsill — an offering to the ancestors who watch through the eyes of birds. [NEGATIVE BLOCK]

docs.title: 🕯️ Ancestor Veneration
docs.text: Ancestor Veneration — the honoring of the dead as ever-present members of the family and the faith.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text:
Ancestor veneration weaves through several of Ge'or's faiths:

  • Ximioli — every home keeps ancestor tablets, with daily offerings of rice, tea, and incense; family records are meticulously kept, the longer the line the greater the honor.
  • Sibbism — the spirits of dead snake queens are said to watch from the heat-shimmer of the desert sands.
  • South Sun Imperial Cult — ancestor worship fused with imperial divinity in the Sun Archipelago.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Faiths: Ximioli, Sibbism, South Sun Imperial Cult
  • Related: Meditation
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 😇 Angel Apparitions
docs.text: Angel Apparitions — the sightings of Angels across Ge'or, one of the world's most beloved legendary phenomena.

docs.title: The Phenomenon
docs.text:
• Most people of Ge'or do not know that angels are energy beings — angels usually take the form of humans.
  • When they are seen, usually after a while — or as one gets closer — they disappear right in front of you. They tolerate observers up to a point, as long as you do not come too close.
  • Sightings are most often of an angel's back, when the angel does not notice the observer — helping animals, planting trees, fixing broken things.
  • Angels can communicate, but it is super rare; when they do, it is for exceptional cases.

docs.title: The Legend
docs.text: Ge'or citizens see angels as legendary beings that are there to help Ge'or. A child may see an angel and smile at him, just for the angel to disappear five seconds later. The stories are told and retold in every region — the stranger who mended a broken cart and was gone by evening, the figure among the trees that smiled back.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Species: Angels
  • Faith: Pragmus
  • Nation: Alborric (Polar Continent)
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🏡 Daily Life & Culture
docs.text: "The clothes, the food, the marriage bed, the grave. This is how they live."

docs.title: 👗 Clothing
docs.text: Broadly medieval European in style, with regional variations: - Skirts, pants, tunics, cloaks — similar to Old Earth medieval fashion with some additions - Elvish styles tend toward lighter fabrics and longer cuts - Dwarvish clothing emphasizes durability and craftsmanship - Regional dyes and patterns distinguish cultures

docs.title: 🍞 Food
docs.text: More abundant than medieval Europe due to magic-assisted agriculture: - Healing mages reduce crop disease and livestock loss - Weather manipulation (making it rain on fields) increases yields - Food is broadly medieval European in type — bread, meat, ale, vegetables - Spices are a major trade commodity, especially through Anos and Sousu routes

docs.title: 🏛️ Architecture
docs.text: Varies significantly by region: - Central Erisdar: Medieval European style — stone, timber, keeps, cathedrals - Dwarvengor: Underground megacities, carved stone - Elvish: Integrated with nature — living wood, elevated structures - Other regions: Diverse, TBD

docs.title: 💍 Marriage
docs.text:
• Normal marriage is the standard — one man, one woman
  • Polygamy is common in many regions due to the more primitive societal structure
  • Incest occurs in some dynastic and isolated communities
  • The Erisian church historically banned polygamy, but enforcement has largely collapsed since the Great Imperial War

docs.title: ⚰️ Funerals
docs.text:
• Burial is the most common practice — the body returned to the earth
  • Cremation is practiced in some cultures
  • Other regional variations exist — practices are not uniform
  • The Erisian Church prescribes burial for the faithful, but compliance varies

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Influenced by: 15,000 years of cultural drift from Old Earth origins
  • Economic driver: Trade republics (Vennerian Trade Republic, Anos Plutocracy)
  • Magic impact: Better agriculture, common healing in towns
  • Social Hubs: tavern

docs.title: 💀 Death Cults
docs.text: Death Cults — sects that embrace death as the answer to the demands of faith or the hunger of a god.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text:
• Shurtra's shadow — the faith's impossible standard of male honor makes death cults common: followers who believe they cannot live up to the faith choose death instead. Authorities usually crack down on the cults.
  • Cult of Cleton — the death cult of the Moonfang Dominion in the polar north, offering child sacrifices to the Wolf God on Cleton Island. The prettiest are sacrificed.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Cults: Cult of Cleton
  • Fed By: Honor Culture (Shurtra's standard)
  • Region: West Erisdar (Shurtra lands), polar north (Moonfang Dominion)
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🌑 Double Crown
docs.text: Double Crown — the rare alignment of the two moons Maenar and Amelia (which orbits Maenar), when the Daughter Moon is seen crowned before her father's face.

docs.title: Folk Tradition
docs.text:
• Paired with the folk "Twin Watchers" tradition of the two moons — and with the Silver Bride ring in the heavens, the sky holds three omens at once.
  • Farmers read the Double Crown as a sign for planting; the Erisian church has attached its own meanings to it over the centuries.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Moons: Maenar, Amelia
  • Related: The Silver Bride, Ge'or
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🗡️ Honor Culture
docs.text: Honor Culture — a society built on personal honor so absolute that failure becomes worse than death.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text:
• Shurtra — demands extreme honor from its male followers. Men are held to a standard of righteousness that few can sustain, and failure brings shame beyond measure. The impossible standard feeds Death Cults — followers who believe they cannot live up to the faith choose death instead — and authorities usually crack down on the cults.
  • Dragons — civilized dragon society is honor-based: codes of conduct, personal oaths, and ritualized combat. The dragons of Kramsadar keep their honor codes in deliberate isolation from the world.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Faiths: Shurtra
  • Species: Dragons
  • Related: Death Cults
  • Part Of: Ge'or

Sousu speaks both Elvish and Irio | | Corinn | Dissenbarg Continent | The primary language of Dissenbarg nations | | Fendigarsian | Fendigar Dictatorship | Isolated eastern tongue | | Gomorian | Minir, Moriat islands | The language of the Luminous Ocean islands | | Shurtraliot | Aenid Kingdom | "Righteous language" — tongue of Shurtra, the star-born faith |

docs.title: Multilingual Regions
docs.text:
• Elvish countries in Erisdar typically speak four languages: Baothian, Dwarvish, Malkod, and Axel — plus a diminishing amount of Elvish.
  • Dissenbarg nations speak Corinn and study Vennerian for commerce.
  • Minir and Moriat speak Gomorian and know some Vennerian and Baothian for trade.
  • Dwarvstadt — the dwarven division of the Erisian Empire — speaks Dwarvish and Baothian.
  • Sousu speaks Elvish and Irio.
  • Aenid Kingdom speaks Shurtraliot.

docs.text:
|---|---| | The Leviathan's voice-inside-the-skull | Matches no known mage-cell expression or Hybrian pattern | | The tree spirits of the Lyrical Forest | Retrieved a device over millennia — by what agency? | | The Sacrifice Ceremony forging | Mass death into a single coherent entity — no known mage-cell mechanism | | Dragon Yaldabaoth's patience | Behavior inconsistent with possession or programming | | The Formingar Ocean's permanent color change | No chemical or mage-cell explanation holds after 600+ years |

These may be undiscovered mage-cell expressions. They may be something else entirely.

docs.title: The Church Position
docs.text: The Erisian church claims magic is divine — acts of Eris channeled through the faithful. Miracles are announced but rarely verified. The Ironcloak's assessment: the Church's "miracles" are a mixture of genuine mage-cell ability (inherited, not granted), Hybrian technology the Church itself does not understand, and outright fabrication.

docs.title: 🧘 Meditation
docs.text: Meditation — the practice of stilling the mind; a belief and discipline central to the spiritual life of Tabontabar.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text: The faithful of Xatarism believe in meditation, and the continent is full of monks. Monasteries and monk-orders keep the traditions and tend the temples across the Northern Kingdom, Central Kingdom, and Southern Kingdom. Ximioli likewise keeps its meditation gardens — cultivated spaces for quiet reflection, embodying the dragon's balance of strength and stillness.

  • Related: Ancestor Veneration
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🌿 Paganism
docs.text: Paganism — the category of Ge'or's older faiths that honor nature, the land, and the ancestral powers, outside the great revealed churches.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text:
• Suebism — a pagan religion focused on honoring nature, born on Suebo Island in West Erisdar.
  • Onobor — the paganism of Tetras, honoring the Silver Bride as goddess and key to immortality.
  • Mannosta — the pagan faith of the Mann Order in North Erisdar, praising ancestors and stars.
  • Elven Faith — the nature cults and elven gods of Elvennrin and Elvenkrad.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:

  • Related: Ancestor Veneration
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🛐 Patron Deity
docs.text: Patron Deity — the god a city or nation keeps as its own, honored above the rest of its pantheon.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text: The Helism pantheon of Dissenbarg is built on patron deities: each city and nation keeps one god, and nations often carry their patron's name — Corin for the goddess of sea and commerce, Cletas for the god of reason, Tissas for the god of war. Every harbor keeps its god's temple, and the pantheon's rites follow the shipping seasons and the harvest.

  • Region: Dissenbarg
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Old-World Technologies
docs.text: The lost sciences of the pre-Last Great War universe. In the current era, technology is not understood — only replicated through templates and ritual. Starships fly, but nobody knows how. A gun is assembled through ceremonial recitation of half-remembered mantras.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Lost After: The Last Great War
  • Preserved In: Archive of the Traveler
  • Current State: Science = Religion

docs.title: 🔻 Modern Decline
docs.text: The polygamy ban's failure is emblematic of broader imperial decay: - Peripheral territories openly practice polygamy without consequence. - Church enforcement is underfunded and under-staffed. - The elvish states and other non-Erisian territories never adopted the ban in the first place.

docs.title: 🏰 Demon Ash-Fortress and Kutten Longhouse
docs.text: [!INFO] Heat vs Cold — Same Problem, Opposite Stone Paired styles: black ash-brick fortress of the Demon Continent (holds heat) and fur-insulated timber longhouse of Kutten (keeps heat).

docs.title: 🧱 Materials & Form
docs.text:
Ash-Fortress: black ash-brick from Emberalden fired with Demonic Ash-Iron slag — walls warm to touch, stay 15°C above ambient. Arrow slits vent ash-smoke.

Longhouse: Northwood frame, double-walled with Furs insulation, sod roof. Central fire pit with salt-lined smoke hole (Arctic Salt preserves meat hung above). Both solve heat — one to keep it, one to keep it in.

docs.title: 👗 Clothing Pairing
docs.text: Ash-Fortress: ash-grey cloaks that hide soot; Longhouse: layered furs, Fang strung as toggles.

docs.title: 🗺️ Where Seen
docs.text: Ash-Fortress across Demon Continent (Asatru, Blazeyard); Longhouse across Kutten (Marko, Malbodor) and Yakut.

docs.title: 🧱 Materials & Form
docs.text: Open paved agora with six stelae — one per Helism god (Cletas, Corin, Maokas, Tissas, Lobas, Gaelen). Each polis emphasizes its god's stela (Corinite League: Corin enlarged). Central table where merchants scale Dissenbarg Krona (12% weight variance).

docs.title: 👗 Clothing Pairing
docs.text: City-color sashes matching stela paint — Cletas democracy blue, Corin sea-green. Krona worn as scale weights on belt.

docs.title: 🗺️ Where Seen

docs.title: ⛩️ Dwarven Vault-Arch
docs.text: [!INFO] The Keystone Talon — Dwarven Vault That Holds With Money Deep stone vault of Dwarvengor — ashlar arch keyed by a Silver Talon wedged in the keystone. Joke: our money holds the roof.

docs.title: 🧱 Materials & Form
docs.text: Cut stone, no mortar — keystone is a slot where a real Silver Talon fits. Arch stands only when Talon is seated; remove it and you hear the stones settle. Apprentices learn by vaulting a Talon-less arch that stands a day then falls.

docs.title: 👗 Clothing Pairing
docs.text: Leather aprons, stone-dust veils, Talon strung as necklace for assay masters.

docs.title: 🗺️ Where Seen
docs.text: Dwarvengor deep halls, Silver Republic cliff vaults, Fractured Erislod civic halls (human imitation, mortar used — dwarves scoff).

docs.title: 🏛️ Erisian Basilica
docs.text: [!INFO] Marble and Dome — The Empire's Claim in Stone The South Marble basilica of Central Erisdar — dome, portico, Baothian Mark mosaics. Every basilica faces the Ruins of Baoth.

docs.title: 🧱 Materials & Form
docs.text: Veined white South Marble from Melior/Cerulea, cut so veins run vertical like divine light. Dome on pendentives, portico with six columns (six ages before Baoth). Floor mosaics of Baothian Mark patterns — priests say the Mark held the empire like mortar.

docs.title: 👗 Clothing Pairing
docs.text: Pontifical purple-trimmed togate robes — marble pallets echo robe dyes. Marble dust in hair for blessing.

docs.title: 🗺️ Where Seen
docs.text: Across Central Erisdar: Pontificate, Elvennrin, Magna. In Dissenbarg, Cletas Agora copies the dome at half scale — deliberate humility.

docs.title: ⚙️ Kobre Gear-Tower
docs.text: [!INFO] The Rotating Tower — A Building That Is a Gear Rotating gear-tower of Kobre — Homunculi upper floors mesh with neighbor towers.

docs.title: 🧱 Materials & Form
docs.text: Steel-plate tower with external teeth — 48-tooth base. Upper drum rotates on water-powered rack, meshing with adjacent towers. Tolerance 0.02mm — same as Kobran Gear coin. If a tower jams, it is Gearmite infestation until proven otherwise.

docs.title: 👗 Clothing Pairing
docs.text: Oil-stained canvas, gear-tooth necklaces (real Gears). Homunculi wear no ornament — tolerance is ornament.

docs.title: 🗺️ Where Seen
docs.text: Homunculi Kingdom capital, Coalsteel forge-cities. Elf Kingdom on Kobre copies in wood — Homunculi call them soft gears.

docs.title: 👗 Clothing Pairing
docs.text: Light wraps, bare feet, ivory armlets (offcut). Gigas enforcers wear dog-pelt sashes.

docs.text: Hides and pelts, wolf-tail sashes. Coin Drums stacked as plates on shelves — clack is house music.

docs.title: 🪵 Northaxeland Timber Hall
docs.text: [!INFO] Hall of Antlers — Elboria Timber Raised to the Sky Long timber hall of Northaxeland — blackpine frame, stag-antler lintel, central hearth. Crown paid on the hearthstone.

docs.title: 🧱 Materials & Form
docs.text: Old-growth Northwood Timber blackpine, mortise-tenon without nails. Lintels carry shed antlers of Alegoria stags — each hall's antlers are local to that -boria. Hearthstone is a single slab where Alegorian Crown are counted by firelight.

docs.title: 👗 Clothing Pairing
docs.text: Heavy wool cloaks, fur-trimmed, antler-bone brooches. Mann visitors remove fur inside — Star Paladin signal.

docs.title: 🗺️ Where Seen

docs.title: 🧱 Materials & Form
docs.text: Fieldstone with banded shells pressed into mortar while wet — each shell's hole position is liturgical. Wind through street creates Bride-tink. Dome is shallow, like an inverted shell.

docs.title: 🔍 The Truth
docs.text:
• Eris was a real historical person — but she never performed miracles.
  • Hybrian Homunculi posed as Eris and her followers, using shadow-power to simulate divine acts.
  • The Saga was written to fabricate a unifying myth that would simplify control over the continent.
  • It worked. The continent of Donblond'werv was renamed Erisdar in her honor.
