docs.title: Alegoria Bloom
docs.text: [!INFO] When the dragon's fire makes the north flower — Day 20, Month 4, the spring rite of Alegoria Held on the 20th day of the 4th month (Ge'orian Calendar), when northern snows break.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Alegoria Bloom commemorates the day Julian the Dragon Tamer proved his worth to the dragon Fireborn and, in Alegorian theology, became one with god. After Julian's death and his incarnation into Fireborn, his companions Plenio (elf), Diana (human), and Korvald (kobold) led the Axel peoples of what became Northaxeland in guerrilla war against Baoth. The first spring after their victory at Shuttil — Julian's birthplace — the valleys that had been burnt black thrust up white alegor lilies. The Axels declared it Fireborn's breath blessing the earth, and the date became Bloom.

docs.title: Rituals
docs.text:
• The Lily Crown — children weave crowns of white alegor lilies and wear them until sunset; to keep one past dusk without it wilting is considered Fireborn's favor.
  • Fireborn's Breath — at dawn, Elven Faith priests and Alegorian clergy light a hilltop beacon with dragon-oil. Villages compete to keep their beacon burning longest against the wind.
  • Tale of Two Prophets — elders recite Julian's prophecy that two prophets will come to be tested by Fireborn-Julian. Each household names one deed of worthiness done since last Bloom.
  • Plowman's Mock — nobles dress as plowmen and plowmen as nobles for the afternoon; satire of birth-rank is licensed, and in Elboria the mock-council can pass non-binding decrees.

docs.title: Who Celebrates
docs.text: Majority faith across Northaxeland (capital Elboria and its borias — Ameboria, Elveteria, Siboria, Tiboria), Venkradian Republic, and Loren. Also observed in the Ameboria district of Kent, where Alegorians are in civil war against the Erisian majority — there, Bloom is both prayer and defiance. Cossiland, Elvenkrad, and Tetras keep a quieter Bloom, blended with Elven Faith rites at Dragonreach.

docs.title: Economics
docs.text:
Bloom is the north's spring market — seed, livestock, and marriage contracts all open at Bloom fairs.

  • Currency spent: Alegorian Crown — Northern silver struck at the Elboria mint with Alegoria's stag-antlers on the obverse. All Bloom fair tolls, lily-crown prizes, and beacon-oil sales price in Crowns. The Crown's strict weight regulation makes it the only coin Elven Faith temples will accept for sanctuary exchange, so refugees hoard Crowns for Bloom.
  • Border traders from Central Erisdar must change Erilia to Crowns at the Elboria scales — the one day the north refuses Erilia outright.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Alegoria — founded by Axels under Julian the Dragon Tamer, dragon Fireborn
  • Region: Northaxeland, Venkradian Republic, Loren, Ameboria (Kent)
  • Date: Day 20, Month 4 (Ge'orian Calendar) — spring thaw, white lily bloom
  • Currency used: Alegorian Crown — Northern silver, exclusive at Bloom fairs

docs.title: Bride-Tide
docs.text: [!INFO] When the ring turns the sea to silver — Day 10, Month 8, high tide under The Silver Bride Celebrated on the 10th day of the 8th month (Ge'orian Calendar) — the year's highest spring tide beneath the ring.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Bride-Tide honors The Silver Bride — Ge'or's ring, formed from the destroyed sister-moon of Maenar and Amelia. On the 10th of Month 8 the ring's albedo peaks over the northern oceans; tides surge, and at night the sea reflects the Bride so perfectly that sailors say the sky has fallen. Fisherfolk learned to set nets by that light centuries before any priest codified it. Sousu pearl divers claim the Bride was a gift to them — their trench east of Meble catches the ringlight and breeds the pearls they set in the Meblean Pearl. In Spasia, the same shells that become Spasian Shell currency are said to be Bride-scales shed into the sea.

docs.title: Rituals
docs.text:
• Pearl Diving at Ringlight — Sousu divers descend at midnight without lamps, navigating by ringlight alone. The first pearl brought up is not sold but threaded on a silver hoop and hung on the harbor shrine for the year.
  • Blessing of the Shells — in Meble and Spasia, priests bless shells and pearls that will become Meblean Pearl and Spasian Shell currency — the year's most auspicious coin is the first blessed batch.
  • Tide Market — for 26 hours the tide is high enough that Sousu's reef causeway stays submerged; trade moves only by boat. Prices are called out in song to carry over water.
  • Lovers' Veil — couples exchange thin silver veils and stand ankle-deep in the surf until the ring clears the horizon.

docs.title: Who Celebrates
docs.text: Maritime Ge'or — first of all Meble (Sousu, Sousu Manga, Sousu Cherlote, and outposts Kreb and Megrel), then every harbor that lives by The Silver Bride's light: Vennerian Trade Republic ports, Dissenbarg's Corinite League cities, Matterbleak and Prosperity Port in West Erisdar, and the Elvennrin coast in Central Erisdar. Even the Erisian church keeps Bride-Tide as a minor feast, though its liturgy insists the ring is Eris's halo.

docs.title: Economics
docs.text:
Bride-Tide is the annual liquidity event for pearl and shell coin.

  • Currency spent: Meblean Pearl — the sole nation's pearl-in-silver-hoop. At Bride-Tide, all harbor prices in Meble and at Beast's Bay pearl stalls are quoted in Pearls; the year's first blessed Pearl batch sells at a 30 percent premium to collectors who will wear the coin as jewelry. Spasian Shell is blessed alongside Pearls and circulates in tandem for small change.
  • Inland buyers convert Erilia and Vennerian Ducat into Pearls at the Sousu mint on the reef — the mint waives its assay fee on this night only.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: The Silver Bride — the ring itself, venerated across Alegoria, Erisian church, and elven Veil of Lament
  • Region: Maritime — Meble (Sousu), Vennerian Trade Republic harbors, Dissenbarg league ports
  • Date: Day 10, Month 8 (Ge'orian Calendar) — peak albedo and spring tide
  • Currency used: Meblean Pearl — blessed pearl-hoop, premium first batch; Spasian Shell for small change

docs.title: Eris Ascendance
docs.text: [!INFO] The radiant lie made holy — Day 15, Month 1, when Eris rose to the heavens Celebrated on the 15th day of the 1st month (Ge'orian Calendar) — the Erisian New Year.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Eris Ascendance marks the mythic ascension of Eris, Goddess of Discord, as codified in The Eris Saga and promulgated by the Erisian church. According to Church canon, on this winter day Eris shed her mortal veil and took her throne above Ge'or, choosing her seven Apostles — Alexa, Draco, Niccas, Ever, Aris, Malich, and Maldorn — to carry her word to the continent that would bear her name, Erisdar.

The truth, preserved only in the [[World/Worlds, Planets and Dimensions/Ge'or/Ruins of Baoth|Ruins of Baoth]] and known to the Ironcloak, is that the ascension is fabrication — engineered by the Hybrian Shadows around 400 BGD to centralize human kingdoms. Yet as of 597 AGD, the lie rules the calendar. Even skeptics in the Erisian Empire keep the holiday, if only because the Empire's mints, courts, and tax collectors do.

docs.title: Rituals
docs.text:
• The White Procession — in the Pontificate of Eris and Erisian Theocracy, clergy in white and silver reenact Eris's ascent up cathedral steps, culminating with the unveiling of a silvered icon bearing her discord-apple.
  • Apostle Readings — each of the seven Apostles is invoked in order; towns founded by an Apostle (like Alexa Church State, Draco Order, Order of Niccas, Ever Order, and Arisdian) add a local refrain to the canon.
  • Oath of Discord — children born in the preceding year are presented at the altar, where parents swear to raise them "in discord and therefore in truth."
  • Night of Lamps — every household hangs a paper lamp. In Central Erisdar cities, the lamps are released over the river at dusk.

docs.title: Who Celebrates
docs.text: The majority faith across Central Erisdar — the Erisian Empire, Pontificate of Eris, Archduchy of the Kennberg, and most counties ending in -stadt — observes Ascendance as the highest holy day. The South Erisdar church states (Alexa Church State, Arisdian, Order of Niccas) and the colonial Enkrad Order in Dissenbarg also observe it, though Dissenbarg's Helism majority treats it as a foreign import. In Northaxeland and other Alegoria lands, it is deliberately ignored.

docs.title: Economics
docs.text:
Ascendance is the peak spending festival of the Erisian world. Tithes, lamp-makers, icon-painters, and pilgrim inns see a month's revenue in a week.

  • Currency spent: Erilia — the Cracking Coin of Central Erisdar. All tithes must be paid in Erilia at Pontifical mints; pilgrim tolls, lamp markets, and cathedral fairs price exclusively in Erilia.
  • In border markets, Vennerian Ducat and Alegorian Crown are exchanged into Erilia at punitive rates set by Church moneychangers.
  • Offerings of Romanium dust are pressed into votive coins and left at shrines, then collected by the Church treasury.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Erisian church — fabricated goddess Eris, Apostles of Eris
  • Region: Central Erisdar — Erisian Empire, Pontificate of Eris, Archduchy of the Kennberg
  • Date: Day 15, Month 1 (Ge'orian Calendar) — Erisian New Year, ~400 BGD mythic origin
  • Currency used: Erilia — all tithes and fair trade in the Cracking Coin

docs.title: Featherfall
docs.text: [!INFO] Every feather is a god and the sky gives them freely — Day 15, Month 12, the sacred molt of Tuba Held on the 15th day of the 12th month (Ge'orian Calendar) — peak molt of the Tuba storm-birds.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Featherfall is the high holy day of Mamanolism on Tuba — the beastmen faith of the Mamanolo Tribe that holds all animals are divine. On Tuba, the sacred storm-birds molt once a year on the northern cliffs; the air fills with flight feathers that drift like snow into the jungle canopy. The Mamanolo bird-tenders teach that the molt is the birds' gift — the gods shedding a piece of themselves for mortals to steward. Because Mamanolism holds that a mouse is as divine as a dragon, Featherfall honors every creature that sheds, but it is the storm-bird's broad flight feather, sealed in sap-resin and notched for denomination as the Tubian Feather, that gives the festival its economic weight.

docs.title: Rituals
docs.text:
• The Catch — at dawn, Mamanolo children climb into the lower canopy with woven baskets to catch falling feathers before they touch the ground. A feather caught in air is gift; one picked from ground is found.
  • Feather Grading — bird-tenders grade each feather by iridescence — full-spectrum feathers (shimmering all colors) are the highest denomination. The year's best feather is sealed in clear resin, notched, and hung in the tribal hall.
  • Thanksgiving to Every Beast — no animal is killed on Featherfall. Every kill made in the prior month is recounted with a spoken thanks to its spirit.
  • Alkorri Exile Warning — Alkorri traders attend to remind the market that counterfeiting a Feather is exile — Alkorri enforces the taboo even though Alkorri follows Sytrenis, not Mamanolism.

docs.title: Who Celebrates
docs.text: Tuba — the Mamanolo Tribe (north coast, sole canonical nation of Mamanolism) and its beastmen enclaves, plus neighboring Alkorri (Lesser Catmen), the Harpies Tribe (who watch the molt from eastern mountains), and the Vennerian offshoot Vennerian Pride (which adopted the Feather locally).

docs.title: Economics
docs.text:
Featherfall is Tuba's mint day — the year's new coin supply literally falls from the sky.

  • Currency spent: Tubian Feather — a single preserved flight feather of the sacred storm-bird, sealed in clear sap-resin and notched at the quill for denomination. A full-spectrum Feather can buy a canoe; lesser grades buy grain, fish, and jungle medicines. On Featherfall, all debts on Tuba are settled in Feathers, and the newly graded Feathers enter circulation. At Beast's Bay, Feathers trade as luxury curios at 10x inland value.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Mamanolism — all animals divine, Mamanolo Tribe animist faith, storm-bird sacred
  • Region: Tuba Continent — Mamanolo Tribe, Alkorri, Harpies Tribe, Vennerian Pride, Goblin Island
  • Date: Day 15, Month 12 (Ge'orian Calendar) — storm-bird molt, air dark with feathers
  • Currency used: Tubian Feather — sacred feather in resin, lightest coin in Ge'or

docs.title: Forge-Quench
docs.text: [!INFO] Hammer, coal, and water that sings — Day 5, Month 2, the cold-forged heart of Kobre Celebrated on the 5th day of the 2nd month (Ge'orian Calendar) — deep winter, when the forge burns hottest.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Forge-Quench is the winter forge festival of Kobre — the dwarven continent west of Tuba where Dwarvism's Coal Doctrine is the spiritual heart. In the Coalsteel Kingdom (southeast to central Kobre), the doctrine teaches Life should be treated as coal — burn peacefully in the dark to enlighten the world: silent craft, communal hearths, ancestor coal added to the family fire. The first Forge-Quench was the night the Coalsteel Kingdom's great communal hearth was rekindled after the continent's Hybrian-engineered Homunculi war left it cold. Rather than mourn, the Coal dwarves hammered. The Homunculi Kingdom homunculi heard the hammering across the border and, that year, did not raid.

docs.title: Rituals
docs.text:
• Silent Hammering — from dusk to midnight, Coal dwarves work without speaking. The only sound is hammer on anvil — the Coal Doctrine prayer.
  • The Quench — at midnight, the year's masterwork (blade, gear, or plate) is quenched in snow-melt drawn before dawn. The hiss is listened to like an oracle — a clear sing is a good year; a dull thud is a warning.
  • Ancestor Coal — a piece of coal from each family's cremation pyre is added to the communal hearth. The dead's warmth joins the community's warmth.
  • Gear Meshing — homunculi-forged Kobran Gear sets are stacked and turned — if counterfeit teeth are off by a hair, they jam.

docs.title: Who Celebrates
docs.text: Kobre — the Coalsteel Kingdom (spiritual heart), Diamonds Kingdom (walled against homunculi, but which keeps Quench behind its wall), Elf Kingdom (elven exiles who adopted Gear for trade), and warily the Homunculi Kingdom itself — which keeps a parallel Quench on its side of the border, hammering on the same night without invitation or welcome.

docs.title: Economics
docs.text:
Forge-Quench is the assay and futures market for Kobre steel and precision gear.

  • Currency spent: Kobran Gear — interlocking steel gears forged by homunculi to 0.02mm tolerance on water-powered hobbers. Teeth count is denomination: 12-tooth base, 24/36/48 higher. Gears mesh — stack a purse and turn the top; counterfeit jams. On Forge-Quench, all Kobre contracts for steel plate, coal, and furnace work are priced in Gears; the quench-masterwork is sold at auction in Gears, and its price becomes the continent's steel reference.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Coal Doctrine — southern branch of Dwarvism, Coalsteel Kingdom communal hearth
  • Region: Kobre Continent — Coalsteel Kingdom, Diamonds Kingdom, Elf Kingdom, Homunculi Kingdom
  • Date: Day 5, Month 2 (Ge'orian Calendar) — deep winter forge, communal quench
  • Currency used: Kobran Gear — interlocking steel gear, teeth-count denomination

docs.title: Groom Remembrance
docs.text: [!INFO] The world remembers the red water — Day 1, Month 7, anniversary of the Great Divergence Observed on the 1st day of the 7th month (Ge'orian Calendar) — the fixed anniversary of Year 0.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Groom Remembrance mourns the Great Divergence — the reactor malfunction of the Glorious Alliance refugee ship in the Formingar Ocean at Year 0 that created The Groom vortex, destroyed Elvengar, and birthed the ring opposite the heavens. The folk pairing of Bride and Groom — beauty above, horror below — endures because it is visible: The Silver Bride crowns the sky while The Groom stains the ocean red. The date is the only thing all calendars agree on — every Ge'orian reckoning since counts from this day.

docs.title: Rituals
docs.text:
• Silence at Noon — at the hour the reactor is said to have breached, all work stops for 26 minutes (one Ge'orian hour). Bells toll once, then silence. In Central Erisdar the silence is enforced by the Pontificate of Eris; in Northaxeland it is kept voluntarily.
  • Red Water Offering — coastal villages pour undyed water mixed with red clay back into the sea, saying "we return what we cannot keep."
  • Gold That Is Not Touched — a single unworked gold nugget, said to be Groom-gold, is displayed under glass. No one touches it — the Remembrance teaches that The Groom's gold kills within hours those who handle what has been near the vortex.
  • The Two Rings Prayer — Elven elders name the destroyed sister-moon that became The Silver Bride as the Veil of Lament, while human priests call it the Bride — both agree to look up and then down, and to remember that one ring was made by grief and the other by error.

docs.title: Who Celebrates
docs.text: A pan-Ge'orian observance, not tied to a single faith — which is why the Erisian church tries quietly to absorb it into Eris Ascendance and fails every year. Kept on every continent that trades across the Greater Ocean and Formingar Ocean: Erisdar (all regions), Dissenbarg, Merratodoni, Meble (Sousu), and the free isles (Karabar, Zahor). Dwarves of Kobre keep it at the communal hearth — adding a black coal to the fire for the dead of Elvengar.

docs.title: Economics
docs.text:
Remembrance is deliberately anti-commercial — markets close for the noon silence — but the day before and after are heavy with pilgrimage, charity, and gold-smithing.

  • Currency spent: Erilia — alms are collected in Erilia for families who lost kin in Year 0 and for the shrines that house Groom-gold under glass. On Meble and at Beast's Bay, the same alms are given in Meblean Pearl and Vennerian Ducat respectively, then converted to Erilia at the Pontifical exchange before being entered in the Remembrance ledger.
  • Goldsmiths sell memory rings — thin iron bands with a single gold fleck sealed under crystal — priced in Erilia.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Universal / The Groom — the Great Divergence (Year 0), paired with The Silver Bride
  • Region: Pan-Ge'orian — Formingar Ocean rim, Central Erisdar, Dissenbarg, Merratodoni, Meble (Sousu), free isles
  • Date: Day 1, Month 7 (Ge'orian Calendar) — anniversary of Year 0, 597 years ago in 597 AGD
  • Currency used: Erilia — alms and memory rings; Meblean Pearl and Vennerian Ducat converted at shrines

docs.title: Helism Hexatheon
docs.text: [!INFO] Six gods, one harbor, one feast — Day 30, Month 6, the midsummer council of Helism Celebrated on the 30th day of the 6th month (Ge'orian Calendar) — midsummer, when shipping and harvest align.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Helism Hexatheon — the Feast of Six — is the only day the entire Helism pantheon is honored together. On Dissenbarg, each nation keeps its own patron — Corin (sea and commerce) in Corin, Cletas (reason) in Cletas Democracy, Maokas (agriculture) in Mienna, Tissas (war) in Tissas, Lobas (nature) in Temas, and Gaelen (construction) in Aeon — and for the rest of the year each harbor prays to its own god. Hexatheon was instituted by the Corinite dock-priests of Taebea three centuries ago when a storm, a war, and a famine struck in the same season; the priests declared that all six domains had been neglected at once, and that only a joint rite could make the continent whole again.

docs.title: Rituals
docs.text:
• The Sixfold Procession — in every Dissenbarg port, six effigies (ship, scales, sheaf, spear, branch, trowel) are carried from their temples to the harbor and floated on a single raft. Which effigy lists first is read as the coming season's omen.
  • Harbor Truce — no Dissenbarg city may collect harbor dues on Hexatheon; all ships, even rival Corinite League vessels, dock free. To violate the truce is to offend Corin.
  • Weighing of the Krona — merchants bring their Dissenbarg Krona to the temple scales; Cletas priests weigh them publicly and mark underweight coins with a chalk C — shaming the issuing city.
  • Six Tables — every household sets six small offerings (saltwater, ink, grain, iron, wood, stone) before a communal feast of grilled sea-fish and new grain.

docs.title: Who Celebrates
docs.text: All twelve Helism-majority nations of Dissenbarg: Cletas Democracy, Taebea, Tessa, Klatia, Corin, Aeon, Citrea, Temas, Mienna, Monik, Maedon, and Tissas — plus the Anos-held Tatak (which honors Corin for profit) and Komme (which honors Tissas). Even the Erisian colony Enkrad Order observes a sanitized Hexatheon to keep the peace.

docs.title: Economics
docs.text:
Hexatheon is the one day Dissenbarg's fractured coinage pretends to be one currency. The harbor truce and public assay move more metal than any trade fair.

  • Currency spent: Dissenbarg Krona — Nineteen mints, one name. Every city stamps its god on the obverse. On Hexatheon, all nineteen Kronas must be accepted at face value in harbor markets — merchants carry scales the other 479 days, but on this night they carry only purses. The public weighing at the Cletas temple is the year's reference rate; Venner and Anos factors at Beast's Bay adjust their Krona discounts the next morning based on which city's coins were chalk-marked.
  • Offerings are bought in Krona; temple courts then tithe the Krona to maintain the harbors.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Helism — pantheon of Corin, Cletas, Maokas, Tissas, Lobas, Gaelen; Patron Deity tradition
  • Region: Dissenbarg Continent — 12 Helism-majority nations plus Tatak and Komme
  • Date: Day 30, Month 6 (Ge'orian Calendar) — midsummer harbor feast, 19-city raft rite
  • Currency used: Dissenbarg Krona — six gods on the obverse, one truce rate for the night

docs.title: Hunt Night (Moonfang)
docs.text: [!INFO] The Wolf God hunts and the pretty are taken — Day 40, Month 12, the longest night on Moon Wolf Island Held on the 40th day of the 12th month (Ge'orian Calendar) — midwinter, when Moon Wolf Island does not see the sun.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Hunt Night (Moonfang) is the annual sacrifice rite of the Moonfang Dominion — the death cult on frozen Moon Wolf Island near the north pole, whose island itself is shaped like a wolf's head and whose god is Cleton, the Wolf God. The cult teaches that isolation is salvation, that the outside world is damned, that poverty is holy and beauty is the mark of Cleton's hunger. Each year, the prettiest children are selected and sent to Cleton Island — the barren rock caught between the two peninsulas that form the wolf's open mouth, as if the wolf itself is devouring its prey. The rite predates any calendar the cult will name. Its doctrine — codified in the hierarchy that rules Moonfang absolutely — is that Cleton demands youth to sustain the world's order, and that Wargs (massive wolf-predators that roam freely near settlements, sacred as the island's shape) are his messengers. To kill a warg is death. To question the selection is to be fed to him.

docs.title: Rituals
docs.text:
• The Selection — priests parade the year's children; the prettiest are marked with a white ash handprint. Families are ordered to be grateful. The selected are dressed in undyed wool and walked — never carried — to the shore.
  • The Walk to Cleton — at dusk, the selected are ferried to Cleton Island in the wolf's mouth. No adult may remain on the island after the boat pulls away. None return. The faithful consider this an honor.
  • Night of the Warg Howl — Wargs are left unpenned. Settlements extinguish all but one lantern per house and listen to howling. A house whose lantern gutters is said to be noted by Cleton for next year.
  • Silence of the Molten South — on the Molten Archipelago to the far southwest, Karabar's refugee bases — where escapees find they have traded one cage for another in forced labor — keep a counter-rite: a silent line, no lanterns, facing north, remembering names the Dominion forbids speaking.

docs.title: Who Celebrates
docs.text: Moonfang Dominion on Moon Wolf Island — exclusively Humans, pale and lean from generations of cold, hunger, and fear. No other nation celebrates Hunt Night; Karabar's bases keep the counter-rite in grief, not worship. Even traders who winter near the Wolf Ocean give Moon Wolf Island a wide berth on this date — the only Ge'orian festival no outsider is invited to witness.

docs.title: Economics
docs.text:
Moonfang has no mint. The cult teaches that wealth and ambition are sins against Cleton's design; poverty is holy.

  • Currency spent: Barter — no minted coin. The Dominion runs on barter in fangs, bones, dried fish, and warg-pelts (pelts may not be from a killed warg — only found dead are permitted, so the economy is literally scavenged). For external accounting — escapees paying Karabar boatmen, refugee base levies at the Molten Archipelago — prices are reckoned in Freeport Doubloon, the Freeport Concord coin of Karabar, Zahor, and the United Kingdom of the Seamen that any port honors. An escapee's passage south is quoted as "three fangs and a Doubloon."
  • On Hunt Night itself, no trade is permitted. To be caught bartering on Hunt Night is heresy.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Cult of Cleton — Wolf God Cleton, child sacrifice on Cleton Island, sacred Wargs
  • Region: Moonfang Dominion — Moon Wolf Island (Wolf Ocean); counter-rite at Molten Archipelago (Karabar refuge)
  • Date: Day 40, Month 12 (Ge'orian Calendar) — midwinter longest night, annual selection
  • Currency used: Barter (fangs/bones) — no mint; external refuge trade in Freeport Doubloon; Wolf Ocean isolation

docs.title: Liberty Day
docs.text: [!INFO] No crown, no church — only freedom — Day 4, Month 11, the birthday of the Republic Celebrated on the 4th day of the 11th month (Ge'orian Calendar) — anniversary of the Human Republic's founding oath.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Liberty Day is the national day of the Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni and, by extension, the highest holiday of Krowretism. It marks the founding oath sworn after the exodus ~100 BGD — when the first dissidents who rejected Eris as demon fled Erisdar and its Erisian church, crossed the Greater Ocean, and raised a rag-paper banner reading No crown, no church — only freedom. The oath was not to a king or a god, but to the inner god Krowret — the divine spark the Church had tried to cut them off from. Every Liberty Day, Krowretist preachers remind the crowd that Eris is not a goddess but a demon and that purification of the world from Eris is mandate — the Republic funds the Ironcloak for exactly this reason.

docs.title: Rituals
docs.text:
• The Oath Remade — at noon, every citizen present swears the founding oath anew. Visitors are invited to swear or stay silent — silence is respected, but noted.
  • Iconoclasm Hour — effigies of Eris — collected through the year from Erisdar imports — are burnt in a single furnace. To throw an Eris icon you yourself once owned is considered especially meritorious.
  • Debate Liturgy — sermons are debates. Any citizen may mount the platform and argue against the preacher — the preacher is expected to lose at least once. Prayers are votes; the year's community resolutions are read as liturgy.
  • Frontier Muster — militia and settler companies display their gear for the westward colonization of middle Merratodoni. Families sign settlement charters on the spot.

docs.title: Who Celebrates
docs.text: Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni universally — Humans, Catmen (Merratodonian Catmen), Beast Races, Elves, and Dwarves within its borders — plus the majority-human Crab Union, which keeps Liberty Day even though its own founding was separate. Purple Coast dwarves, now unifying with the Republic, keep Liberty Day as guests and increasingly as kin.

docs.title: Economics
docs.text:
Liberty Day is the Republic's fiscal new year — the treasury prints, the frontier is funded, and the year's Liberty is tested against the world's distrust.

  • Currency spent: Merratodoni Liberty — rag-paper Liberty in purple-black Purple Coast dye, Ironcloak watermark. All settlement charters, militia bounties, and Ironcloak sponsorship are priced in Liberty. The treasury traditionally prints a commemorative Liberty Day note that trades at a premium to collectors at Beast's Bay even as Anos factors discount the ordinary Liberty.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Krowretism — Church of Krowretism (inner god Krowret, demon Eris, sponsor of Ironcloak)
  • Region: Merratodoni — Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni (heartland), Crab Union, Purple Coast (unifying)
  • Date: Day 4, Month 11 (Ge'orian Calendar) — founding oath anniversary, exodus ~100 BGD
  • Currency used: Merratodoni Liberty — paper Liberty, charters, bounties, Ironcloak pledge

docs.title: Maw Feast
docs.text: [!INFO] The mountain opens its mouth and the night is fed — Day 40, Month 9, the Diablos fast broken Held on the 40th day of the 9th month (Ge'orian Calendar) — the last moonless night before the harvest moon.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Maw Feast belongs to the Diablos of the Mountain Tribe on Yak Island, east of the Demon Continent — the nocturnal, winged humanoids whose faith is Demonism. The name Maw is theirs: the cliff-face council hollow on Yak Island is called the Maw because at night, lit only by moon-silver lanterns, its dark opening looks like a mouth swallowing the stars. The feast was codified around 400 BGD by Shara Half-Moon in her Moon Letters — twelve admonitions that remain Demonism's only quasi-scripture — as the one night the Night Council must not sit in judgment, but eat together and speak plainly. Demonist theology teaches that daylight is for taking and night is for accounting; Maw Feast is the night the Diablos account for their own hunger rather than others'.

docs.title: Rituals
docs.text:
• Wing-Silence Broken by Feast — the council opens as always with wing-silence — all present extend wings until wind is the only sound — then, instead of judgment, a single low hum that breaks into shared food.
  • Mouth of the Mountain Offering — the first ingot of moon-silver from a new vein and the first bolt of shadow-silk are not sold but hung on the Maw's lip as night-decor — visible only to those who fly after dark. At Maw Feast they are taken down, cut, and distributed.
  • Thermal Prayer Flights — at midnight, Diablos fly an empty circuit of Yak Island with no cargo — prayer as patrol. To return with "nothing to report" is praised as confirming stillness.
  • Sound-Dampening Chant — Diablos mages layer humming that hushes the cliff halls; guests from Estran and the Asatru Empire who stay up all night are seated in the dampened circle.

docs.title: Who Celebrates
docs.text: Universal among Diablos of the Mountain Tribe on Yak Island. Small Diablos enclaves and night-workers in Asatru-controlled territory on the Demon Continent mainland foothills keep a smaller Maw. Estran traders who time their voyages to meet Diablos at dusk are honored guests — their cunning and night-savvy complements Diablo patrol rhythms.

docs.title: Economics
docs.text:
Maw Feast is the Diablos' accounting night — the Mountain Tribe reconciles its moon-silver and silk ledgers and settles all inter-cliff debts.

  • Currency spent: Demonic Ember — the warm ashen iron of the Demon Continent and Yak Island. Embers are iron discs fired with demon ash that stay warm to the touch for days; counterfeits go cold by morning. On Maw Feast, all debts within the Mountain Tribe are settled in Embers at the Maw's edge — the year's only census. Estran traders exchange Freeport Doubloon into Embers at the dusk outposts, but the tribe's internal settlement is Ember-only.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Demonism — Diablos faith of the Mountain Tribe, Moon Letters of Shara Half-Moon, Kirivs-bin nocturnal branch
  • Region: Yak Island (Mountain Tribe) and Demon Continent foothills
  • Date: Day 40, Month 9 (Ge'orian Calendar) — last moonless night before harvest moon
  • Currency used: Demonic Ember — warm iron Ember, island census and debt settlement

docs.title: Purple Unfurling
docs.text: [!INFO] The coast runs purple into the republic — Day 1, Month 10, the joining of Purple Coast and republic Held on the 1st day of the 10th month (Ge'orian Calendar) — founding date of the joint council.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Purple Unfurling commemorates the unification of the Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni and the Purple Coast — the great political project of 597 AGD. Around 100 BGD the first Krowretist refugees fled Erisdar's Erisian church to build a frontier democracy in northeastern Merratodoni; for six centuries they and the dwarf-dominated Purple Coast southeast of them were neighbors. In 597 AGD their joint councils convened for the first time, drafting the administrative union that will make middle Merratodoni's empty interior a shared frontier. The name is literal: on Unfurling Day, a single giant purple banner — woven from Purple Coast sea-snail dye — is unfurled from the Republic's capitol to the Coast's harbor.

docs.title: Rituals
docs.text:
• The Unfurling — at noon, the purple banner is run from capitol to coast (or, in smaller towns, from schoolhouse to dock). Every citizen must touch it at least once as it passes.
  • Oath of the Middle — Krowretist preachers and dwarven elders jointly swear to settle the unpopulated middle of Merratodoni together. Children plant a sapling for every mile of interior they hope to farm.
  • Ironcloak Review — the Ironcloak — sponsored and sheltered by the Church of Krowretism — parades in plain clothes and receives the year's funding pledge from the joint council.
  • Paper Burning — old territorial charters that divided Republic and Coast are burnt in a single furnace; the ash is mixed with purple dye and used to print the next year's council stationery.

docs.title: Who Celebrates
docs.text: Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni and Purple Coast jointly — plus the sister republic Crab Union and Barro and Kob, who see their own futures in the union. The dwarf-dominated Coast brings Dwarves and Catmen alongside the Republic's Humans, Catmen, Beast Races, Elves, and Dwarves.

docs.title: Economics
docs.text:
Unfurling is a political festival with a commercial tail — the joint council announces the year's land grants, infrastructure levies, and Romanium frontier claims.

  • Currency spent: Merratodoni Liberty — the paper Liberty, rag-paper printed in purple-black ink from Purple Coast dyes with Ironcloak watermarks. All joint-council pledges, land-grant fees, and Ironcloak sponsorship are priced in Liberty — the one coin both Republic and Coast trust.
  • The giant purple banner itself is later cut into strips and sold as Unfurling ribbons for Liberty apiece — the ribbon is both souvenir and receipt.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Krowretism — Church of Krowretism (inner god Krowret, demon Eris, sponsor of Ironcloak)
  • Region: Merratodoni — Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni + Purple Coast, colonizing middle Merratodoni westwards; sister Crab Union
  • Date: Day 1, Month 10 (Ge'orian Calendar) — joint council founding, 597 AGD unification
  • Currency used: Merratodoni Liberty — paper Liberty, council pledges and ribbon sales

docs.title: Temas Harvest
docs.text: [!INFO] Grain from the plains that feeds a continent — Day 25, Month 9, the inland thanksgiving of Temas Celebrated on the 25th day of the 9th month (Ge'orian Calendar) — when the inland plains are shorn and the grain roads open.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Temas Harvest is the agrarian thanksgiving of Temas, the inland grain plain of Dissenbarg whose fertile fields feed the continent through the ports of Citrea. The patron of Temas in the Helism pantheon is Lobas, god of nature, and the harvest is his high day. The rite predates the Corinite storm-council that created Helism Hexatheon — Harvest is older, muddier, and less interested in harbors. The festival began as a threshers' vow: after the last sheaf was cut, the reapers would not taste the new grain until the Lobas priests had blessed it and the first wagon had been dispatched to Citrea. Breaking the vow was blamed for the next year's blight.

docs.title: Rituals
docs.text:
• The Uncut Corner — every field leaves its northeast corner uncut for Lobas — "the god's acre." At sundown, children run into the standing grain to drive out the harvest hare, and elders toss a sheaf back into the corner as thanks.
  • First Wagon to Citrea — the year's first grain wagon, garlanded with woven straw, rolls from Temas to Citrea's harbor. No toll may be levied on it; every village along the road adds a loaf. In Citrea the loaves are broken and shared with dockworkers before the grain is sold.
  • Straw Man of Lobas — a wicker figure of the god is built from last year's straw and burnt on the threshing floor; its ash is scattered on the field that will be sown first next spring.
  • Harvest Truce of Spears — Tissas — god of war, patron of neighboring Tissas — is formally asked to keep his spears sheathed until the grain is stored. Priests of Tissas attend and must answer "he will."

docs.title: Who Celebrates
docs.text: Heartland Temas and its grain-road neighbors — Citrea (which moves the grain), Mienna, Monik, and Maedon (who share Maokas's agriculture but honor Lobas on this day alone). The Corinite League cities (Corin, Taebea, Tessa, Klatia) keep a merchants' Harvest at the Beast's Bay grain exchange.

docs.title: Economics
docs.text:
Temas Harvest is the pricing day for Dissenbarg grain — the year's most important commodity. The price set at Citrea on Harvest afternoon becomes the continent's benchmark until next Harvest.

  • Currency spent: Dissenbarg Krona — on Harvest, the Temas and Citrea Kronas trade at parity, erasing the usual 12 percent weight variance. All first-wagon grain is sold in Kronas, and the Citrea harbor dues are then calculated in Kronas for the rest of the year's shipments. Farmers settle in Krona but reckon in hands of grain — one notch on a Dissenbarg Krona is one hand of grain.
  • Anos factors from Tatak and Venner factors from Sua who buy Dissenbarg grain convert their Anosi Mark and Vennerian Ducat into Kronas at Harvest.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Helism — patron Lobas (nature), guest rites for Maokas and Tissas
  • Region: Temas — inland Dissenbarg, grain road to Citrea
  • Date: Day 25, Month 9 (Ge'orian Calendar) — last sheaf cut, first wagon dispatched
  • Currency used: Dissenbarg Krona — grain benchmark price, Citrea harbor market

docs.title: 🏙️ City-State
docs.text: City-State — a sovereign state consisting of a single city and its surrounding land.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text:
• Corin — the maritime city-state of Dissenbarg, senior partner of the Corinite League; its streets are canals, and its Merchant Council is elected by ship-captains.
  • Suebo — an island city-state on Suebo Island, West Erisdar, birthplace of Suebism.
  • Yaro — a coastal city-state of West Erisdar.
  • Zane — a river city-state, built across a river with its people living on both banks.
  • Marko — the merchant city-state of Kutten (see Semi-Republic).

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nations: Corin, Suebo, Yaro, Zane, Marko
  • Related: Merchant Republic
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🤝 Coalition
docs.text: Coalition — a voluntary union of states around a dominant power, joined by pact rather than conquest.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text:
The Anos Plutocracy rules parts of Dissenbarg through coalition, not conquest:

  • Komme — joined Anos about 55 years ago (~542 AGD) after intense negotiations, concluding the Anos–Komme Agreement to work together to liberate Taberis from Venner. The pact was a deliberate response to Venner's expansion.
  • Tatak — a huge territory, comparable in size to Johannstadt, that willingly entered the Anos coalition for profit.

The contrast with Venner is sharp: where Venner conquered Taberis illegally, Anos binds its Dissenbarg partners by agreement.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Members: Komme, Tatak
  • Lead Power: Anos Plutocracy
  • See: Anos–Komme Agreement, The Taberis War
  • Contrast: Colonial Empire
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🌐 Colonial Empire
docs.text: Colonial Empire — a power that rules through a network of colonies, outposts, and controlled territories across the oceans.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text:
• Anos Plutocracy — maintains a global colonial network: Anos Lumina Outpost, Anos Marti, Anos Xeti Outpost, New Kolorad, Anos Cattos, Anos-Arebed, Arrow of Anos, Tatak, Komme, Anos Maloca, and Kolorad (Anos). Some holdings were conquered; some joined by Coalition.
  • Vennerian Trade Republic — the largest colonial and commercial empire on Ge'or: Vennerian Goishi, Vennerian Aelefer Channel, New Eris, Vennerian Pride, Love of the Sea, Mia Checkpoint, New Venner, Johannstadt, Sua, Eribel, Neopao, and Koln. Venner's Dissenbarg holdings grew from the Sua foothold to the illegal takeover of Taberis.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Powers: Anos Plutocracy, Vennerian Trade Republic
  • Related: Coalition, Tributary System
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🗳️ Democracy
docs.text: Democracy — rule by the vote of common citizens rather than by birth or by steel.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text: The Cletas Democracy is one of the few true democracies on Ge'or. Its system is imperfect — property requirements limit the franchise — but it stands as a genuine alternative to autocracy. The nation is named for Cletas, the god of reason of the Helism pantheon, whose judgment the assemblies invoke.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Cletas Democracy
  • Patron: Cletas (god of reason)
  • Contrast: Monarchy, Theocracy
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 👑 Empire
docs.text: Empire — a vast multi-territory realm under one supreme sovereign, holding many peoples by conquest or inheritance.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text:
• Erisian Empire — the dominant central power of Erisdar, its authority decaying; a modified feudal structure of duchies, counties, free cities, and order states under the Emperor.
  • Asatru Empire — the red-dominant demon empire of the Demon Continent.
  • South Sun Empire — the imperial state of the Sun Archipelago, where the Emperor is descended from the Sun.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Empires: Erisian Empire, Asatru Empire, South Sun Empire
  • Related: Monarchy, Feudalism
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Feudalism
docs.text: Feudalism is a system of land-based governance common across Ge'or, particularly on Erisdar. Under feudalism, land is held by nobles in exchange for military service and loyalty to a higher lord or monarch.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text: Feudal structures vary by region. The Erisian Empire operates under a modified feudal system with duchies, counties, free cities, and church states all answering to the Archduchy of the Kennberg. Other regions employ different variations — some more rigid, others more decentralized.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Empire: Erisian Empire
  • System: Land tenure, vassalage, noble hierarchy
  • Region: Erisdar

docs.title: 🌍 International Republic
docs.text: International Republic — a republic of many species and many faiths, where no single people or creed rules.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text: Demon's Horn, on its horn-shaped peninsula in West Erisdar, is Ge'or's international republic. Drawn by intercontinental trade between Erisdar and the Demon Continent, its population is diverse — humans, demons, and many other races — and religiously it is open ground: it hosts all faiths.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Demon's Horn
  • Region: West Erisdar
  • Character: Multi-species, all faiths, trade-driven
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🔮 Mage Republic
docs.text: Mage Republic — a state governed by mages, where magical mastery and philosophy define the ruling class.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text: Palonia, in West Erisdar, is Ge'or's mage republic. Its mages are highly philosophical and sophisticated, and its magic schools are famous across the world — people everywhere hear of Palonian magic. The republic's faith, Palonism, is a variation of Shurtra reshaped by its arcane culture: philosophy and magic are the highest devotion.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Palonia
  • Faith: Palonism
  • Region: West Erisdar
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🐍 Matriarchal Monarchy
docs.text: Matriarchal Monarchy — absolute monarchy held by women, with succession passing through the female line.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text:
The Snake People of Xikxia and Zakarutia live under matriarchal monarchy. Queens rule absolutely — the Queen's word is law — and succession passes to the eldest daughter. A council of Matriarchs, elder females of each major bloodline, can veto a Queen's decree with unanimous vote. Male snake people hold no political power, serving instead as generals, scholars, and artisans.

Both snake nations are monarchies ruled by queens — sisters who deeply hate each other.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Species: Snake People
  • Nations: Xikxia, Zakarutia
  • Related: Monarchy
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: ⚓ Merchant Republic
docs.text: Merchant Republic — a republic of trade, where the wealth of the sea and the market is power itself, and the merchant class rules.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text:
• Corin — the maritime city-state of Dissenbarg, senior partner of the Corinite League. Its ruling Merchant Council is elected by ship-captains rather than landowners — a government more competent at navigation than legislation, but effective at keeping trade flowing. Its patron is Corin, goddess of sea and commerce.
  • Vennerian Trade Republic — the great trade republic of the south, its colonial and commercial empire the largest on Ge'or.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nations: Corin, Vennerian Trade Republic
  • Related: Semi-Republic, Colonial Empire
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 👑 Monarchy
docs.text: Monarchy — rule by a single hereditary sovereign.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text:
Monarchy is the most common system on Ge'or, with regional variants:

  • Centralized monarchy with bureaucratic administration — the Northern Kingdom of Tabontabar.
  • Imperial bureaucracy — the Central Kingdom, ruled through scholar-officials appointed by examination and merit.
  • Martial monarchy — the Southern Kingdom, where the king rules through military strength.
  • Elective monarchy — Estran of the High Catmen.
  • Absolute monarchy — see Matriarchal Monarchy for the snake queens.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nations: Northern Kingdom, Central Kingdom, Southern Kingdom, Estran, and many others
  • Contrast: Republic, Theocracy
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: ⚔️ Order-State
docs.text: Order-State — a nation governed as a military order, where rank is earned through proven combat ability rather than birth.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text:
• Enkrad Order — the Erisian church colony in Dissenbarg, a fortified order-state surrounded by goblin territories east and west.
  • Koel Order and Order of Niccas — independent orders of the Grimmel Peninsula.
  • Scarlet Order — the order of the peninsula's south.
  • Draco Order and Ever Order — order states within the Erisian Empire.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nations: Enkrad Order, Koel Order, Order of Niccas, Scarlet Order, Draco Order, Ever Order
  • Related: Theocracy
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🏛️ Republic
docs.text: Republic — a state with no hereditary crown, governed by elected councils, assemblies, or merchant bodies that rule in the name of the public interest.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text:
Republics take many forms across Ge'or:

  • Mage Republic — Palonia, ruled by philosophical mages.
  • International Republic — Demon's Horn, many species and all faiths.
  • Semi-Republic — Marko, elected High Catmen rulers.
  • Merchant Republic — Corin and the Vennerian Trade Republic, wealth as power.
  • Simpler republics: Silver Republic, Lumina Republic, Pinc Republic, Fezzanite Republic, Venkradian Republic, Grimmel Republic.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Contrast: Monarchy, Theocracy
  • Region: Worldwide
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: ⚖️ Semi-Republic
docs.text: Semi-Republic — a state midway between republic and oligarchy, where elections exist but voting power follows wealth and stake.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text: Marko, the merchant city-state of Kutten, is a semi-republic. Its High Catmen rulers are elected by a council of merchant families and guild representatives — not democratic in the universal sense, since voting power correlates with economic stake, but more open than any monarchy on Ge'or. The elected rulers serve fixed terms, charged above all with keeping Marko neutral and its trade flowing.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Marko
  • Region: Kutten
  • Elected: High Catmen rulers
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: ⛪ Theocracy
docs.text: Theocracy — rule by priests and holy councils, where the faith and the state are one.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text:
• Aeon — a theocratic state in Dissenbarg governed by a council of star-reading mystics, isolated from the secular trade networks; its patron is Gaelen, goddess of construction.
  • Spasian Teocracy — the only official religion is the Spasian Faith.
  • Erisian Theocracy and the Pontificate of Eris — the Erisian church-states of Erisdar.
  • Alexa Church State — the Erisian apostolic state of the Grimmel Peninsula.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nations: Aeon, Spasian Teocracy, Erisian Theocracy, Pontificate of Eris, Alexa Church State
  • Contrast: Republic, Monarchy
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🪙 Tributary System
docs.text: Tributary System — slow conquest by economics and politics: a power turns foreign states into tributaries and vassals over years, without open war.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text: Venner is practicing the tributary system across Dissenbarg. Its influence grows steadily, and it is slowly taking over the continent's politics, turning its states into tributaries and vassals — though it will take longer yet for the process to succeed. The Corinite League is already being slowly integrated, with formal annexation expected within years.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Power: Vennerian Trade Republic
  • Region: Dissenbarg
  • See: Corinite League, Colonial Empire
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.text: |:---|:---|:---| | Continental Identity | Unified under Donblond'werv | Divided into Erisdar (North, East, West, Central) | | Religious Authority | Diverse localized pantheons | Hegemony of the Erisian Church | | Demographics | Balanced multi-species kingdoms | Heavily human-dominated; Elves recovering from near-genocide | | Legal Frameworks | Absolute global treaties | "Cracking" localized laws; dwindling dogmatic enforcement |

docs.title: 🏛️ Major Global Powers of the AGD Era
docs.text:
• Erisian Empire: The dominant, aggressive geopolitical superpower of Central Erisdar that rose to prominence in the mid-AGD centuries. It is currently facing severe institutional decay.
  • Pontificate of Eris: The central spiritual authority that holds immense soft power over Eastern and Northern Erisdar, mapping and maintaining the official "Eris Saga" historical canon.
  • The Restored Elvish States: Independent sovereign enclaves that successfully broke away from Imperial influence after 500 AGD, re-establishing ancient cultural practices.

docs.title: BGD ERA — Before the Great Divergence
docs.text: Date Event ~15,000 BGD ~15,000 BGD MELKOR island forms around the wreckage. ~15,000–14,000 BGD Age 0 — The Lost Era. Post-crash chaos. Survivors cling to the crash site; first dispersal begins. ~14,000–11,000 BGD Age 1 — Age of Nomadism. Survivors live as wanderers. No permanent settlements. ~10,999–9,000 BGD Age 2 — Age of First Tribes. Tribal societies form. Species begin differentiating by region. ~8,999–7,000 BGD Age 3 — Age of First Empires. First civilizations rise. Elvengar founded on Kutten — the first great elven kingdom. ~6,999–5,500 BGD Age 4 — Dragon Tyranny. Dragons rule 90% of Ge'or. Intense territorial warfare brings them to near-extinction. ~5,499–4,500 BGD Age 5 — Dwarf Era. Dwarves dominate through underground megacities fueled by Romanium. Economic collapse when Romanium runs out. ~4,499–2,989 BGD Age 6 — Iron/Elvish Age. Post-Romanium collapse. Dwarven economy in ruins. Elvengar rises. Ends with the Hybrian crash at Pontus. ~2989 BGD Hybrian Shadows arrive. Damaged vessel crashes in Pontus (eastern Erisdar). Shadows chose Pontus for its mountain-surrounded isolation. Begin hibernation. ~2989–1989 BGD Phase 1 of the Shadow Plan. First millennium: study Ge'or, create Homunculi, infiltrate institutions, build secret cult. ~1989–989 BGD Phase 2 of the Shadow Plan. Build global influence network. Engineer wars. Manipulate historical figures. ~1729 BGD Old Lumina Empire founded by the beastman Emperor Kaelor I. A great beastmen empire — will eventually control 70% of Lumina Continent, Cattos island, and parts of Tuba. ~1667 BGD Masaaki Sytrenis born — "Sytrenis the Diplomat," the catmen hero who will end the catmen extermination and the Termopolas threat (see Sytrenis). ~1645 BGD The Metrak Incident. At twenty-two, Masaaki Sytrenis and his party stop the waking Metrak, a mountain-sized war-mechanoid of the Last Great War hidden in the now-Munchon region. Emperor Atanides dies; Termopolas is ravaged; the Tunwif–Termopolas conflict follows, and "Sytrenis the Diplomat" ends the catmen persecution. ~1134 BGD Old Lumina Empire falls. Shadow operation: Luminous XII defeated by Goblin King (engineered). Brother Hoelio killed. Luminous XII commits suicide. Empire collapses. The beastmen — the empire's own people — slowly return to savagery, forgetting their old ways. Maomism rises among the survivors. Lumina enters a tribal dark age. ~989–421 BGD Phase 3 of the Shadow Plan. Target Baoth as pan-continental super-state. Infiltrate Baoth's upper echelons. Possess Goldenborn. ~526 BGD Kirivis receives the bright tablet. Begins 60 years of obsessive study. ~476 BGD Kirivis has an epiphany. Deciphers the tablet. Falls into deep depression. Spends 10 years planning, sending secret teams across Ge'or. ~466–421 BGD The Demonic War. Kirivis attacks Baoth without explanation. 45 years of war. 421 BGD Baoth destroyed. Kirivis storms the dragon hall. Rulfred reveals himself as Shadow agent. Kirivis beheaded. Crowd cheers. Rulfred becomes king. 421 BGD Nethra survives. Kirivis's adopted daughter, age 13, escapes. ~420 BGD Nethra's march. Gathers loyalists. Brother Maoth sacrificed holding the line. Nethra reaches Rulfred's throne room. ~420 BGD The Lyrical Forest prophecy. Lyrical Forest spirits give Nethra a modified Shadow device — "a gift from 3,000,000 years ago." ~420 BGD Nethra transformed. Device detonates in throne room. Nethra becomes a different type of Shadow. Baoth's ruins are final. ~419 BGD Ironcloak founded. Nethra secretly creates the order. Nethrian Revelation transcribed. ~400–200 BGD Erisian Church fabricated. Eris (homunculus) performs staged miracles. Gathers followers. Fakes deaths and resurrections. ~300–100 BGD Church Militant. Holy orders conquer lands. Force conversions. Pontificate of Eris founded as Shadow headquarters. ~200–0 BGD Crusades launched. Waves of holy war expand Church control. Pre-Year 0 Elvengar flourishes. The first great elven kingdom dominates Kutten. Elves are the dominant civilization.

docs.title: YEAR 0 — The Great Divergence
docs.text: Date Event Year 0 The Great Divergence. Formingar Ocean reactor malfunctions. The Groom vortex forms. Elvengar destroyed. Year 0 The Silver Bride ring — formed from destroyed third moon — becomes Ge'or's defining celestial feature.

docs.text: Date Event 1–100 AGD The Kutten Catastrophe. Toxic rains and poisoned air desertify Kutten. Elves flee in great diaspora. 1–100 AGD Elven refugees found Luzia and Maemon on Merratodoni. 27 AGD Erisian Empire founded. Kingdom of Shamaradan atoned by Eris. Renamed under Davos the Magnificent. ~50–100 AGD Kutten recolonization begins. Settlers from Erisdar and Demon Continent arrive. 94 AGD Vennerian Trade Republic breaks from Erisian Empire. Independence purchased with wealth. 122–130 AGD Northaxeland Crusades. 137 AGD Great Elvish Persecution. Erisian church campaigns to eliminate elves. Shadow-engineered operation. 158 AGD Anos Plutocracy founded. Kingdom of Tiphar collapses after Lima and Venner invade to rescue Princess Charlotte. Anos city breaks away. 170–597 AGD Great Ascension of Trade. Maritime republics rise. Colonial networks expand. 214–236 AGD ~227 AGD ~290 AGD 322 AGD ~400–500 AGD ~466 AGD 500s AGD 524 AGD ~530 AGD Asatru Empire stabilizes after civil war. General Doma's successors consolidate the reduced empire. ~542 AGD Anos–Komme Agreement. After intense negotiations, Komme joins Anos in a pact to work together to liberate Taberis from Venner. 544 AGD Venner invades Minir island. Conquers Neopao and Koln. Dukedam becomes forced puppet. 557 AGD Hermes Kennensbach born. ~570 AGD Hermes becomes Emperor. Begins reform attempts. Fails. Empire continues to crack. ~575 AGD Current Gigas dog-god born. Telepathic canine, now 22 years old in 597 AGD. ~580–590 AGD Kentian Civil War begins. Rebels control northeast Kent. ~585 AGD Mann Order invaded by Erilian Federation. Tiaboria captured. Refugees flee to Fractured State of Erislod, forming New Mann. 589 AGD Xikxia taken over. Zakarutian queen's sister exiled. Raises army of 8,000. Marches on Xikxia. Declares independence. 589–597 AGD Zakarutia rebuilds fleet. Archaic navy modernizing for reconquest. 597 AGD Rex Pollo IV elected in Vennerian Trade Republic. 597 AGD The Protagonists born — Emrys Eisenheart and twin sister Ichi, and Lucien Mortvagn 12 km away. Black agent incarnates. Hope Goddess vision. Prophecy fulfilled. 600 AGD 602 AGD ~597 AGD South Sun Empire emperor compromised. Eunuch homunculi installed in court. 597 AGD Present day — Age 11 (Great Divergence). 248 sovereign nations. The Shadows prepare Armageddon.

docs.title: Trade Routes
docs.text:
Ge'or trades in spheres, not a web. Measured off the 597 AGD political map (scale bar 0–8000 km, 3.1 km/px): Ge'or spans ~49,000 km — a world 1.37× Earth. Bulk goods move under 2,000 km; heavy goods under 5,000 km seasonal; only luxuries survive multi-leg hauls past 8,000 km. Medieval hulls need a port every ~800 km. Most believe the world is flat — Lung and Sister receive no traders at all. The direct Merratodoni ↔ Demon Continent run is marked INFEASIBLE (measured, see § Measured Distances).

Sphere & Power Home Feasible Route (with resupply) Key Outposts & Currency Why it works ERISDAR SPHERE — Anos Plutocracy South Erisdar Erisdar ↔ Luminous Ocean island chain → Dissenbarg ↔ Meble Lumina, Marti, Xeti, Kumir, Komme/Tatak (Dissenbarg), Meble Pearls trench — Anosi Mark Island chain (Luminous Sea Islands, Meble) gives resupply every ~600–1,200 km, measured 4,900 km total (33 days). Anos counts grain, not chokepoints ERISDAR SPHERE — Vennerian Trade Republic South Erisdar Erisdar → Vennerian Channel → Beast's Bay → Dissenbarg (via Luminous Ocean western edge) Mia, Goishi, Vennerian Channel, Kutten, New Venner, Johannstadt, Sua, Eribel — Vennerian Ducat / West Erisdarian Guilder Venner built the chokepoint. Shortest legal way east — everyone pays ERISDAR SPHERE — Sousu (Meble) Meble Meble ↔ Luminous Sea Islands ↔ Dissenbarg ↔ Xeti Kreb (Dissenbarg), Megrel (Xeti) — Meblean Pearl / Luminous Pearl Short hops only. Measured 2,200 km Erisdar↔Meble, ~5,000 km Meble↔Dissenbarg with chain. Meble file: "Remote from Erisdar and Merratodoni" — Sousu does not run Merratodoni; it feeds Dissenbarg/Xeti. 300m pearl divers can't provision a Greater Ocean crossing BEAST'S BAY SPHERE — Lumina / Marti / Xeti / Tuba Central Ge'or Lumina ↔ Marti (Aelefer Channel) ↔ Xeti (Vennerian Channel) ↔ Beast's Bay ↔ Tuba (Lesser Ocean, 2 seasonal legs via Goblin Island) Beast's Bay hub, Aelefer Channel (Lumina-Marti land bridge), Vennerian Channel (Marti-Xeti), Vennerian Pride (Tuba) — Luminal Tusk / Martian Drum / Xetian Coil / Tubian Feather The densest sphere. Lumina/Marti/Xeti ring Beast's Bay — bay-rim ports sit 200–1,500 km apart (bay circumference, not centroid). Marti-Xeti are land-connected via Vennerian Channel — wagons, not ships. This is where Lumina Spices and Marti Hides change hands 3 times before reaching Erisdar KUTTEN-DEMON-WEST ERISDAR CORRIDOR Kutten / Demon Continent / West Erisdar West Erisdar ↔ Demon's Horn (strait ~1,000 km) ↔ Demon Continent ↔ Demonic Sea (seasonal ~5,500 km) ↔ Kutten Love of Sea (Kutten), Yakut, Demon's Horn (free port), Augagarten — Kutten Fang / Demonic Ember Measured, not guessed: Demon's Horn↔West Erisdar is a strait (Asatru enclave sits on the West Erisdar coast per the map — the border is adjacent). Kutten is ~5,500 km across the Demonic Sea — a monsoon-season lane (Indian-Ocean-style: dhows ran 3,000–5,000 km seasonal legs). Kutten Furs/Salt cross it with the autumn wind, never all year. Only heavy/luxury goods pay for the passage KOBRE-TUBA SOUTHERN SPHERE Kobre / Tuba Kobre ↔ (two ~3,000 km legs via Goblin Island) ↔ Tuba ↔ Lesser Ocean → Lumina Coalsteel forges, Goblin Island (Tuba south), Mamanolo — Kobran Gear / Tubian Feather Measured: Kobre↔Tuba ≈ 6,500 km centroid, but Goblin Island splits the run into two ~3,000 km seasonal legs (file: "sailing west from Goblin Island lands on Kobre's southern coast"). Not 500 km — but doable twice a year, like the Indian Ocean dhow trade. Kobre Coal/Gear goes to Tuba, then Lumina, then Erisdar via Beast's Bay — never direct to Demon/Merratodoni GREATER OCEAN SPHERE — Merratodoni (expedition lane) Merratodoni (center, Greater Ocean) Merratodoni ↔ Tabontabar (~5,900 km) and ↔ West Dissenbarg (~5,900 km) — one convoy per season, ships that may not come back Human Republic, Purple Coast, Crab Union harbors, Luzia — Merratodoni Liberty Measured: Merratodoni's nearest land is Tabontabar at ~5,900 km. No near neighbor exists — the Liberty is printed to fund one brave convoy a season (Purple Dye is precious enough to justify it). Everything else is 10,000+ km NO-GO FAR EAST — Tabontabar / South Sun Empire East of Sun Archipelago Tabontabar ↔ Sun Archipelago ↔ South Sun Empire (internal sea, ~4,000 km chain) Northern Kingdom, Central Kingdom, Southern Kingdom — Tabontabar Triad / South Sun Aureus Internal archipelago trade. South Sun file: "west archipelago of Tabontabar" — adjacent, not distant. No regular route to Erisdar — measured 16,000+ km with no chain FREE PORTS — Neutral Exchange Free Isles At every hub, but ships come to them Karabar (golden forest), Zahor (south of Lung), United Kingdom of the Seamen (South Crab Archipelago), Demon's Horn — Freeport Doubloon Not a route — a service. Free ports honor all currencies (Freeport Concord). Every captain stops to exchange

docs.title: Trade Rivalry — 4 Corners, not 1 race
docs.text:
• Anos (counts) vs Venner (taxes) — core Erisdar ↔ Dissenbarg race (4,900 km island lane), as before.
  • Sousu (holds islands) — 3rd power with Pearls/Cowries/Jade, resupply chains on Luminous Ocean. Neutral, respected.
  • Merratodoni Liberty (prints) — underwrites the only Greater Ocean convoys (5,900 km to Tabontabar / west Dissenbarg). Ships may not come back — the coin prices that risk. Most distrusted by old empires.
  • Niche monopolies — Asatru Empire/Kutten/Kobre run the north-south industrial corridor via Demon's Horn (strait) + Demonic Sea (monsoon). Freeport Concord runs neutral exchange everywhere.

Languages of trade: Venner Trade Pidgin on deck, Anosi Cant in counting houses, Erisian Common on ledgers, Trade Sign Cant in gale — 100 bloc tongues ashore.
