docs.title: 💰 Alegorian Crown
docs.text: [!INFO] The Northern Crown — Silver and Elven Faith The silver crown of the north — dominant across Northaxeland and its sister realms. Elven-influenced, Alegorian-blessed.

docs.title: 👑 Elven Silver
docs.text:
Struck in high-purity northern silver from the Venkradian mines, the Crown bears Alegoria's stag-antlers on the obverse and the six -borias' arms on the reverse. Weight is strictly regulated by the Elboria mint — the only institution all Northaxeland baronies still trust.

Backed by silver and by Elven Faith — temples will always exchange Crowns for sanctuary, which makes refugees hoard them.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: North Erisdar (non-Mann): Northaxeland (capital Elboria + Ameboria, Elveteria, Siboria, Tiboria, etc.), Elvenkrad, Cossiland, Venkradian, Kent, Tetras. Accepted in Loren and Magna at border markets. Mann Order refuses it on principle.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Alegorian Crown ] ├── Region: North Erisdar ├── Issuer: Northaxeland mint at Elboria ├── Backing: Northern silver + Elven Faith ├── Symbol: AC ├── Nations: Northaxeland, Elvenkrad, Cossiland, Venkradian, Kent, Tetras └── See Also: Mannic Star, Erilia, Alegoria

docs.title: 💰 Anosi Mark
docs.text: [!INFO] The Counting-House Coin — Paper Over Gold The ledger currency of the Anos Plutocracy. Not minted for beauty — minted for counting.

docs.title: 📚 Ledgers, Not Mines
docs.text:
Unlike the Ducat, the Anosi Mark is barely physical. Anos counting houses issue receipts — thin copper plates stamped A₥ — redeemable against ledgers in Anos proper. The coin is a promise that a clerk in a basalt tower will honor the number written.

Backed by trade volume, not metal. When Anos controls grain from Temas and Citrea and metals from Marti, the Mark holds. When Venner blockades Greater Ocean, it wobbles.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text:
South Erisdar East and the Anos network: Anos capital, Lumina Outpost, Marti, Xeti, New Kolorad (Kumir), Komme and Tatak (Dissenbarg coalitions), Anos Maloca. Also used quietly in Grimmel merchant quarter and Sousu via Kreb.

Merchants joke: Venner weighs, Anos counts.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Anosi Mark ] ├── Region: South Erisdar + Anos colonial network ├── Issuer: Anos Plutocracy ├── Backing: Counting-house ledgers + trade volume (Romanium, spices, metals) ├── Symbol: A₥ ├── Colonies: Lumina, Marti, Xeti, New Kolorad, Komme, Tatak └── See Also: Vennerian Ducat, Trade Routes, Romanium

docs.title: 💰 Baothian Mark
docs.text: [!INFO] The Dragon's Standard — Dead Coin The imperial standard of Baoth under Goldenborn during Age 8. Abolished at Year 0 after the Great Divergence.

docs.title: 🐉 Imperial Standard
docs.text:
The only currency in Ge'or's history to achieve true continental standardization. Minted from the Baoth treasury at the foot of the Obsidian Throne, the Mark was struck in dragon-sealed gold and enforced by imperial edict — regional currencies were banned, castles converted to garrisons, and all roads taxed in Marks.

At its peak it funded multi-species administration — humans, elves, dwarves and catmen serving side-by-side — and merchants traveled from Xeti to Elboria without exchange.

docs.title: 💥 Collapse
docs.text:
Died overnight with Baoth in the Great Divergence. For the 30 years of Age 9 there was no currency — the bureaucracy that tracked every coin vanished. Marks were hoarded, melted, or buried in the Ruins of Baoth. Modern Erilia claims succession but never achieved the same trust.

Surviving Marks are collector items. Counterfeits are common in Pilferhorn.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Baothian Mark ] ├── Region: Baoth (historic, pan-Erisdar) ├── Era: Age 8 — Year 0 ├── Backing: Imperial treasury + dragon law ├── Symbol: BM ├── Status: Defunct — numismatic only └── See Also: Erilia, Goldenborn, Ruins of Baoth, Romanium

docs.title: 💰 Cubri Cowrie
docs.text: [!INFO] The Cowrie Shell — Archipelago Money The cowrie of the Cubri Archipelago — small, glossy, counted by the handful.

docs.title: 🐚 Counted Handfuls
docs.text:
Glossy cowrie shells, drilled and strung — 40 cowries = 1 string, 10 strings = 1 hand. The shells are naturally limited to the warm shallows around Cubri; transplant attempts failed — the snails die elsewhere. Aocubri temple counters string cowries blindfolded by sound.

Backed by sheer ubiquity in the archipelago and by Aocubri's ritual control — the temple blesses each string.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: Cubri Archipelago (4): Aocubri, Cherlote, Manga and associated isles. Also at Sousu and Demon's Horn as small change — sailors call cowries island pennies.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Cubri Cowrie ] ├── Region: Cubri Archipelago ├── Issuer: Aocubri temple counters ├── Backing: Natural cowrie scarcity + temple blessing ├── Symbol: CC ├── Nations: Aocubri, Cherlote, Manga └── See Also: Luminous Pearl, Meblean Pearl

docs.title: 💰 Demonic Ember
docs.text: [!INFO] The Ash Coin — Warm to the Touch The ashen iron of the Demon Continent — still warm from the forges of Emberalden and Blazeyard.

docs.title: 🔥 Warm Iron
docs.text:
Struck in black iron flecked with Emberalden ash — a true Ember is warm for hours after minting (trace fire-magic from Demon Continent forges). Cools to a dull glow. Reheat a cold Ember and its stamp smokes — assay test.

Backed by Demon Continent's fire and Demon-blooded labor — Asatru, Koebi, Kutra and Malgardian tribes all honor the Ember because Asatru legions will enforce it.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: All Demon Continent (17 + Yak Island holdings): Asatru, Blazeyard, Bloodcoast, Emberalden, Koebi, Kutra, Malgardian and others. Also at Demon's Horn trade hub and Yakut Territory (Kutten colony). Merratodoni traders hate Embers — they burn pouches — but accept them for Demon iron.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Demonic Ember ] ├── Region: Demon Continent + Yak Island ├── Issuer: Asatru + Emberalden forges ├── Backing: Ashen iron + fire-forges + legion enforcement ├── Symbol: DA ├── Nations: Asatru, Blazeyard, Bloodcoast, Emberalden, Koebi └── See Also: Kutten Fang, Merratodoni Liberty, Romanium

docs.title: 💰 Dissenbarg Krona
docs.text: [!INFO] The City Krona — Nineteen Mints, One Name The fractured crown of Dissenbarg — nineteen nations, nineteen weights, one word.

docs.title: ⚖️ Nineteen Weights
docs.text:
Every Dissenbarg city mints its own Krona. Cletas stamps reason's scales; Corin stamps a ship; Tissas stamps a spear. The obverse is always a Helism god — your city's preferred god tells your Krona's origin instantly. Weight varies up to 12% — merchants carry scales, not purses.

Backed by nothing common — grain from Temas/Citrea, ores from inland, faith in Helism's six gods. The only stable thing is the name Krona. Dissenbarg joke: We agree on the word, nothing else.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: All Dissenbarg (19 nations): Cletas, Tissas, Temas, Citrea, Corin, Maedon, Mienna, Monik, Aeon, Klatia, Taebea, Tessa, plus Komme, Tatak (Anos coalitions), Enkrad Order, Eribel, Sua etc. Venner and Anos factors at Beast's Bay quote Dissenbarg Krona at a discount — and then resell at par inland.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Dissenbarg Krona ] ├── Region: Dissenbarg (19 nations) ├── Backing: Mixed — grain, ores, Helism faith, city treasuries ├── Symbol: DK ├── Pantheon: Helism — six gods on obverses ├── Nations: Cletas, Corin, Tissas, Mienna, Monik, Temas, Citrea, Aeon, Klatia, Taebea, Tessa └── See Also: Helism, Trade Routes, Xetian Coil

docs.title: 💰 Erilia
docs.text: [!INFO] The Cracking Coin The most commonly used currency in Central Erisdar. Established after the continent of Donblond'werv was renamed to Erisdar.

docs.title: 📉 Modern Strain
docs.text: The Erilia is facing severe economic pressure as regional provinces operate with increasing financial autonomy. Alongside the failing polygamy ban and the resurgence of the elvish states, the currency strain is one of the key indicators of the Erisian Empire's institutional decay.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Erilia ] ├── Region: Central Erisdar ├── Part Of: Erisian Empire economy ├── Status: Under strain from provincial autonomy └── See Also: Romanium, polygamy

docs.title: 💰 Freeport Doubloon
docs.text: [!INFO] The Free Captain's Coin — Any Port, Any Flag The catch-all doubloon of the free isles — Karabar, Zahor, United Kingdom of the Seamen and every charter that flies no continent's flag.

docs.title: 🏴‍☠️ Any Flag, One Doubloon
docs.text:
A heavy gold doubloon stamped with a compass rose — no king's head, only FREE PORT around the rim. Minted independently at Karabar, Zahor, and the United Kingdom of the Seamen — each adds a tiny mint-mark (anchor, obsidian shard, paw). All three mints honor each other's Doubloons by truce — the Freeport Concord.

Backed by the isles' role as neutral harbors where every currency can be exchanged — the Doubloon is the exchange coin.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: Free isles: Karabar (independent island), Zahor (1 nation), United Kingdom of the Seamen (island kingdom). Also at Demon's Horn, Prosperity Port, and any pirate haven. Venner and Anos both accept Doubloons grudgingly — they hate what they can't control, but they love a port that takes everything.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Freeport Doubloon ] ├── Region: Free Isles (no continent) ├── Issuer: Karabar + Zahor + United Kingdom of the Seamen (Freeport Concord) ├── Backing: Free-port exchange neutrality + gold ├── Symbol: FD ├── Nations: Karabar, Zahor, United Kingdom of the Seamen └── See Also: Vennerian Ducat, Anosi Mark, Trade Routes

docs.title: 💰 Kobran Gear
docs.text: [!INFO] The Interlocking Gear — Steel That Fits The gear-shaped steel of Kobre — homunculi-forged, interlocking. A purse that meshes.

docs.title: ⚙️ Homunculi Precision
docs.text:
Gear-shaped discs of hard steel, teeth count = denomination. A 12-tooth Gear is base; 24-, 36-, 48-tooth are higher. Gears mesh — you can stack a purse and turn the top; if counterfeit teeth are off by a hair, they jam. Homunculi of the Homunculi Kingdom forge them to 0.02mm tolerance on water-powered hobbers.

Backed by Kobre fabrication — Coalsteel furnaces and Diamond Kingdom presses.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: All Kobre (4): Homunculi Kingdom, Coalsteel, Diamonds, Elf Kingdom (elven exiles who adopted Gear for trade). Also used by Kutten smiths at Malbodor who import Kobre steel. A favorite of engineers — they literally use Gears as gears in a pinch.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Kobran Gear ] ├── Region: Kobre ├── Issuer: Homunculi Kingdom precision forges ├── Backing: Steel fabrication + Coalsteel furnaces ├── Symbol: KG ├── Nations: Homunculi Kingdom, Coalsteel, Diamonds └── See Also: Kutten Fang, Romanium

docs.title: 💰 Kutten Fang
docs.text: [!INFO] The Fang Coin — Tooth and Ice The fang-coin of Kutten — carved from beast fangs of the northern wastes and the Yakut frontier.

docs.title: 🦷 Carved Fang
docs.text:
Carved from the curved fangs of Kutten snow-beasts — each Fang is a polished fang-tip drilled and notched. Larger fangs = higher denomination. The tip must be intact; a broken tip halves value instantly (called blunted).

Backed by Kutten furs, ivory, and northern mercenary contracts — Kutten sells teeth and blades.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: All Kutten (6): Kutten, Malbodor, Marko, Oda, New Elvengar, Yakut plus historic Elvengar memory. Also accepted at Demon's Horn and by Dwarvengor dwarves who prize Kutten steel. The Yakut Territory Fangs are largest — frontier beasts have bigger teeth.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Kutten Fang ] ├── Region: Kutten ├── Backing: Beast fang + furs + mercenary contracts ├── Symbol: KF ├── Nations: Kutten, Malbodor, Marko, Oda, Yakut └── See Also: Demonic Ember, Kobran Gear, Marko

docs.title: 💰 Luminal Tusk
docs.text: [!INFO] The Jungle Ivory — Carved Tusk Token The tusk-token of the Lumina — hewn from fallen ivory, oiled, and notched. Animist, heavy, honest.

docs.title: 🦷 Carved Ivory
docs.text:
Cut from naturally fallen tusk (never poached — to carve a hunted tusk is to invite Gigas wrath). Each Tusk is a palm-sized ivory bar, notched along the edge for denomination — one notch = one hand of grain. Oiled with jungle sap so it never dries.

Backed by Gigas law (never antagonize Erisdarians, but never debase the Tusk) and by Lumina's sheer protein wealth — grain, fruit, and game are the real reserves.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text:
All of Lumina (10 nations): Lumina Kingdom, Great Cattos, Cattos, Cammao, Gigas, Lake Kingdom, Tree Tribe, Maoma and others. Anos factors at Lumina Outpost exchange Tusk to Anosi Mark at brutal 3:1 — Lumina calls the post the Carver for how it shaves value.

The Lumina Republic once tried paper Tusk; Gigas burned the press.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Luminal Tusk ] ├── Region: Lumina ├── Backing: Ivory + grain/game reserves + Gigas law ├── Symbol: LT ├── Nations: Lumina Kingdom, Great Cattos, Gigas, Cammao, Tree Tribe └── See Also: Anosi Mark, Gigas, Romanium

docs.title: 💰 Luminous Pearl
docs.text: [!INFO] The Island Pearl — Eight Nations, One Luster The shared pearl of the Luminous Sea Islands — eight nations that agreed on the only thing they could find together: pearls.

docs.title: 🏝️ Shared Luster
docs.text:
Like Meble but shared. Each island mints its own Pearl, but all honor each other's — a Luminous pact. Gildenrise pearls are golden-hued, Mikrad pearls are pink, Koln pearls are stark white — connoisseurs can tell origin by tint, but value is by weight.

Backed by the Luminous Ocean's pearl beds — the same beds that make these islands resupply havens for Erisdar ↔ Dissenbarg voyages.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: All Luminous Sea Islands (8): Gildenrise, Koln, Mikrad, Aeid, Dukedam, Erima, Gomor, Luminous holdings. Also accepted at any port on the Luminous Ocean route — a practical necessity for sailors who need something every island honors.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Luminous Pearl ] ├── Region: Luminous Sea Islands ├── Backing: Luminous Ocean pearls + inter-island pact ├── Symbol: LP ├── Nations: Gildenrise, Koln, Mikrad, Aeid, Dukedam, Erima, Gomor └── See Also: Meblean Pearl, Cubri Cowrie, Trade Routes

docs.title: 💰 Mannic Star
docs.text: [!INFO] The Star Coin — Capital of the Gods The star-punched coin of the Mann Order alone. Refuses all other northern mints.

docs.title: ⭐ Star-Steel
docs.text:
Punched, not cast. Each Mannic Star is a thin disc of star-steel (sky-iron from the Mann heights) with a five-point star hole through the center. String them on cord — a star-string is a common Mann dowry. The hole is the value; clipping it is sacrilege.

Backed by the claim Mann is capital of the gods — its value is faith in Kosbaldo's rebellion and the Mann priesthood's refusal to debase.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: Mann Order only. Deliberately non-convertible. At the Mann border, Crown exchangers must thread Stars to count them — a ritual humiliation Mann loves. Erilian factors value a Star at 1.4 Crowns for Romanium deals; Mann priests value it at what the gods allow.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Mannic Star ] ├── Region: Mann Order (exclusive) ├── Issuer: Mann Order priest-mint ├── Backing: Star-steel + theocratic decree (Kosbaldo, Mann Order) ├── Symbol: ★ ├── Status: Non-convertible theocratic coin └── See Also: Alegorian Crown, Kosbaldo, Elven Faith

docs.title: 💰 Martian Drum
docs.text: [!INFO] The War Drum — Skin Over Romanium The drum-skin currency of Marti — hide stretched over a Romanium hoop. You hear its value.

docs.title: 🥁 Skin and Hoop
docs.text:
A hoop of low-grade Romanium (too brittle for blades) with cured wolf-hide drum skin stretched across. Tap it — a true Drum rings clear; a clipped one thuds. Wolf-folk of Kobra and Kut can howl the denomination. Denomination by diameter and skin thickness.

Backed by Marti herds and hunting — skin is wealth where wolves run.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: All Marti (8): Germina, Kut, Oigopol, Kobra, Brase, Cobal, Kramsadar, Maboro, plus Anos Marti (Anos factors exchange Drum to Mark at the port). Traders carry Drums stacked like plates — the clack is unmistakable in any bazaar from Marti to Beast's Bay.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Martian Drum ] ├── Region: Marti ├── Backing: Wolf-hide + Romanium hoop + herd wealth ├── Symbol: MD ├── Nations: Germina, Kut, Kobra, Brase, Cobal └── See Also: Xetian Coil, Anosi Mark, Romanium

docs.title: 💰 Meblean Pearl
docs.text: [!INFO] The Lone Pearl — Single Nation, Single Pearl The pearl-coin of Meble — one nation (Sousu) one pearl standard.

docs.title: 🦪 Sea Pearl
docs.text:
A perfect sea-pearl set in a thin silver hoop — each Pearl is a real pearl, graded by luster and size. The Sousu pearl divers of Meble harvest from the deep trench east of the island; the hoop is stamped with Sousu's sigil and notched for fractions (half-pearl, quarter-pearl hoops with freshwater pearls).

Backed by pearl scarcity and Sousu's role as the third trade power — small but pivotal. Cherlote and Manga outposts use Pearls to pay Meble crews.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: Meble: Sousu (sole nation, but with continental weight), Kolorad (Anos enclave), Sousu holdings Kreb and Megrel. Also at Beast's Bay where Pearl-to-Ducat is a prestige exchange — nobles wear Pearls as jewelry and money.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Meblean Pearl ] ├── Region: Meble ├── Issuer: Sousu pearl divers + mint ├── Backing: Natural pearls + Sousu trade hub status ├── Symbol: MP ├── Nations: Sousu, Kolorad ├── Outposts: Kreb, Megrel └── See Also: Trade Routes, Anosi Mark, Vennerian Ducat

docs.title: 💰 Merratodoni Liberty
docs.text: [!INFO] The Liberty — Freedom Minted in Paper The paper dollar of the new world — the Human Republic and its sister Crab Union. Freedom as backing.

docs.title: 🗽 Paper Freedom
docs.text:
The first true paper currency in Ge'or outside Anos receipts. The Liberty is rag-paper printed in purple-black ink (from Purple Coast dyes) with Ironcloak watermarks — hold it to light and you see a cloaked figure. Backed not by metal but by land: the Republic's claim over middle Merratodoni and Ironcloak sponsorship of colonization.

Your USA analogue — absolute freedom coin. Inflation is constant; the Republic prints to fund the frontier. Citizens call it Liberty with a straight face and rag when drunk.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text:
Merratodoni: Human Republic, Purple Coast (unifying 597 AGD), Crab Union (sister Krowretist republic), Barro and Kob, Maemon, Luzia, Arrow of Anos (circulates but resented). Also accepted — reluctantly — at Demon's Horn and Asatru Knight's Thorn by merchants who want Merratodoni grain and iron.

The strongest new coin; the most distrusted by old empires.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Merratodoni Liberty ] ├── Region: Merratodoni + Crab Union ├── Issuer: Human Republic treasury (Ironcloak-backed) ├── Backing: Colonization land + paper promise + Romanium frontier claims ├── Symbol: $L ├── Sister: Crab Union └── See Also: Trade Routes, Erilia, Romanium

docs.title: 💰 Mian Jade
docs.text: [!INFO] The Jade Sliver — Tribal Green The jade sliver of Mia — three tribes, one green stone.

docs.title: 💚 Green Sliver
docs.text:
Thin slivers of Mia jade — deep green, translucent when held to light. Each sliver is chipped, not cut, so every piece is unique — forgers can't replicate the fracture pattern. Mukini, Orgor, and Xi'xia all chip jade from the same Mia highland vein by treaty — the vein is shared wealth, not owned.

Backed by jade scarcity and tribal law — the highland vein is guarded jointly, even during inter-tribal raids.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: Mia (3): Mukini, Orgor, Xi'xia (plus Mia island holdings). At Mia Checkpoint (Venner checkpoint), Jade-to-Ducat is the official frontier exchange — Venner factors complain the slivers cut their hands.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Mian Jade ] ├── Region: Mia ├── Backing: Mia jade vein + tribal treaty ├── Symbol: MJ ├── Nations: Mukini, Orgor, Xi'xia └── See Also: Vennerian Ducat, Mia

docs.title: 💰 Silver Talon
docs.text: [!INFO] The Dwarven Claw — Silver and Romanium The commerce claw of the dwarven east — trusted from Silver Republic to New Mann.

docs.title: 🦅 Claw of Commerce
docs.text:
Struck in silver alloyed with trace Romanium (enough to glint blue in sunlight), the Talon shows a dwarven claw grasping a shard on the obverse. Dwarven assay offices in Dwarvengor and the Silver Republic weigh every Talon — underweight coins are claw-cut and returned.

The most honest coin in the east. Even Spasian merchants, who despise dwarves theologically, quote Talons when they want to be taken seriously.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: East Erisdar (non-Spasian): Silver Republic, Dwarvengor, Fendigar, Fendigar-adjacent, Fractured Erislod, New Mann, Away. Accepted in Northaxeland and Central Erisdar for heavy goods. Spasia bans it at the border (smuggled anyway).

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Silver Talon ] ├── Region: East Erisdar ├── Issuer: Silver Republic + Dwarvengor assay offices ├── Backing: Silver + Romanium trace ├── Symbol: ST ├── Nations: Silver Republic, Dwarvengor, Fendigar, New Mann, Fractured Erislod, Away └── See Also: Spasian Shell, Romanium, Erilia

docs.title: 💰 South Sun Aureus
docs.text: [!INFO] The Sun Disk — Gold That Never Tarnishes The sun-gold disk of the South Sun Empire — western archipelago's imperial claim.

docs.title: ☀️ Sun Gold
docs.text:
Struck in high-purity western gold that never tarnishes — South Sun smiths claim the metal is blessed at noon on the solstice. Each Aureus shows a rising sun on the obverse, the Empress's profile on the reverse. Edge is sun-ray milled — shaving is instantly visible.

Backed by South Sun's western sea control and spice routes.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: South Sun Empire alone (archipelago west of Ge'or). Also accepted at Tabontabar ports and by Merratodoni traders who prize its purity. Venner factors at Demon's Horn will exchange Aureus to Ducat at a premium — they like gold that doesn't lie.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ South Sun Aureus ] ├── Region: South Sun Empire ├── Issuer: South Sun Empire imperial mint ├── Backing: Western gold + spice routes ├── Symbol: SSA └── See Also: Tabontabar Triad, Vennerian Ducat

docs.title: 💰 Spasian Shell
docs.text: [!INFO] The Bride's Shell — Faith Is The Backing The only legal tender of the Spasian Teocracy — polished shells from the The Silver Bride ring itself.

docs.title: 🐚 Shell of the Bride
docs.text:
Not minted. Gathered. Spasian priest-divers harvest specific banded shells that fall from the The Silver Bride ring's lower dust band during high tide near the Spasian coast. Each is polished, drilled, and blessed — the hole's position denotes denomination. Counterfeiting is heresy, punishable by exposure.

Backed purely by theocratic decree. The shell has no metal value; its value is that Spasia will only accept shells for tithes, land, and forgiveness.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text:
Spasia only — and aggressively so. Possessing Talons inside Spasia is fined; possessing Erilia is taxed. At the border shrine at Matterbleak-Spasia crossing, money changers beat shells with hammers to test resonance. Pilgrims learn the sound.

Outside Spasia, shells trade as curios, not currency — except among faithful diaspora.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Spasian Shell ] ├── Region: East Erisdar — Spasia exclusive ├── Issuer: Spasian Teocracy priest-divers ├── Backing: Theocratic decree + The Silver Bride shells ├── Symbol: 🐚 ├── Status: Legal tender only in Spasia; banned Talons/Erilia └── See Also: Silver Talon, The Silver Bride, Erilian Federation

docs.title: 💰 Tabontabar Triad
docs.text: [!INFO] The Threefold Coin — Three Kingdoms, Three Metals The tri-metal coin of Tabontabar — one coin, three bands for three kingdoms.

docs.title: 🔱 Three Bands
docs.text:
A single disc banded in three metals — copper for Southern Kingdom, silver for Central Kingdom, gold for Northern Kingdom. The bands' thickness shows which kingdom minted that Triad — a Southern Triad is copper-heavy, a Northern is gold-heavy. All three are legal everywhere in Tabontabar — kings agreed to share the coin to avoid war.

Backed by Tabontabar's internal peace — as long as the three kings honor the bands, the Triad holds.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: Tabontabar (3): Central Kingdom, Northern Kingdom, Southern Kingdom. Also at South Sun border posts where Triad and Aureus trade 1:1 by treaty.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Tabontabar Triad ] ├── Region: Tabontabar ├── Issuer: Three kingdoms joint mint ├── Backing: Tri-metal + inter-kingdom treaty ├── Symbol: TT ├── Kingdoms: Central Kingdom, Northern Kingdom, Southern Kingdom └── See Also: South Sun Aureus, Trade Routes

docs.title: 💰 Tubian Feather
docs.text: [!INFO] The Lightest Coin — Sacred Feather The feather-token of Tuba — where Mamanolism says every animal is divine, so money itself is light as a bird.

docs.title: 🪶 Sacred Feather
docs.text:
Not metal. A single preserved flight feather of the sacred Tuba storm-birds, sealed in clear sap-resin and notched at the quill for denomination. The Mamanolo bird-tenders grade feathers by iridescence — a full-spectrum Feather can buy a canoe.

Backed by Mamanolism — all animals are divine. To counterfeit a Feather is to blaspheme every beast. Alkorri traders enforce this with exile.

Lightest coin in Ge'or — literally. A purse of Feathers weighs nothing.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: Tuba (2): Mamanolo and Alkorri, plus Vennerian Pride (Venner offshoot that adopted Feather locally). At Beast's Bay, Feathers trade as luxury curios at 10x inland value — mainland collectors pay for the shimmer.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections

docs.title: 💰 Vennerian Ducat
docs.text: [!INFO] The Toll Coin — Rules the Waves The sea-trade currency of the Vennerian Trade Republic and its colonial empire. Every ship that pays the Vennerian Channel pays in Ducats.

docs.title: 🌊 Toll-Backed Power
docs.text:
Struck in pale sea-gold alloyed with Romanium dust, the Ducat is not backed by a mine but by a chokepoint. Control of the Vennerian Channel linking the Xeti Sea to Beast's Bay lets Venner tax every hull between Erisdar and Dissenbarg. That toll is Ducat-only.

The coin shows a ship's prow on the obverse, the Channel gates on the reverse.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text:
Dominant in South Erisdar West and all Venner colonies: Mia Checkpoint, Goishi, New Venner, Johannstadt (ex-Taberis), Love of the Sea (Kutten), Sua and Eribel (Dissenbarg). Also accepted at Beast's Bay and Demon's Horn traders — grudgingly, even by Anosi factors.

Strongest currency on water, weakest inland. Venner factors quote inland prices in Erilia and convert at predatory spreads.

docs.title: 💰 West Erisdarian Guilder
docs.text: [!INFO] The Frontier Florin — Orc Tooth and Silver The rugged workhorse of West Erisdar — from Aenid to Mercur and Matterbleak. Minted where West Erisdar meets the wild.

docs.title: ⚔️ Frontier Mint
docs.text:
West Erisdar never accepted Erilia fully. After the Erisian centralization cracked, western kings resumed minting. The Guilder is struck in heavy silver with a notched edge — once used to bite-test authenticity on the frontier. Orc traders of Augamouth stamp their own with a filed tooth mark; the mark is honored anyway.

Obverse: the entwined sigils of Aenid and Palonia; reverse: a notched rim.

docs.title: 🗺️ Circulation
docs.text: All of West Erisdar: Aenid, Aimeled, Kille, Augagarten, Galerough, Direfirth, Astravayne, Palonia, Augamouth (orc kingdom), Xikxia (snakefolk), Demon's Horn trade hub, Asatru Knight's Thorn, Prosperity Port, Zane, Yaro, Suebo, Matterbleak, Mercur. Interchangeable with Erilia at 0.9:1 in eastern markets — western merchants call the discount the empire's tax.

docs.title: 💰 Xetian Coil
docs.text: [!INFO] The Serpent Coil — Copper That Coils The coiled copper of Xeti — a literal coil you wrap around your wrist. Blessed by the serpent god Wruowas.

docs.title: 🐍 Coiled Copper
docs.text:
Not a disc — a coil. Thin copper wire wound into a tight spiral, ends hooked. Denomination is by weight and turns — a three-turn Coil is a day's wage for a Koetebalo ogre porter. Uncoil it to pay, recoil change. Children wear coils as bracelets.

Struck (wound) in temple forges; each coil is quenched in serpent-oil and stamped with Wruowas's coiled sigil at the hook.

docs.text: All Xeti (8): Koetebalo (ogre realm), Kyuu, Kuioaba, Ograd, Uiohin, Kumir, Anos Xeti, Megrel. Also accepted by Anos and Venner factors at Beast's Bay for Xeti grain and metals — they hate counting coils, which Xeti merchants love.

docs.title: 🏦 Anosi Counting Houses
docs.text: [!INFO] Ledger-weight banking + Anosi Ledger-Weight Nine counting houses share one ledger standard (1 ledger-weight = 4.2kg grain). Built after the Anos-Komme Agreement ~542 AGD. Bankroll Lumina Outpost and Xeti Outpost; pay spies in Anosi Mark A₥. Their ledger-ink (soot + Romanium dust) is invisible until warmed — a human-chemistry trick, not spell.

docs.title: 📜 Charter
docs.text: Founded as bloc charter to control ledger-weight banking + anosi ledger-weight on South Erisdar East — Anos Plutocracy. Hold is hereditary or elected per bloc law — Erisdar guilds elect masters, Dissenbarg boards vote by stelae, tribal guilds inherit.

docs.title: ⚙️ How It Works
docs.text:
Human-scale craft: ledger-ink, knot tallies, chisel stone, punch-card, salt cure, slag chemistry — no voltage, no beast grammar. Tallies are counted by hand, recorded in ink, sealed with wax and hallmark.

Contracts in triplicate: one for hall, one for counterparty, one for temple archive. Disputes go to the hall's master + one neutral guild witness.

docs.text: Operates from South Erisdar East — Anos Plutocracy outward via Trade Routes and Naval Power lanes. Converts at outposts — price friction is the profit.

docs.title: ⚙️ How It Works
docs.text:
Human-scale craft: ledger-ink, knot tallies, chisel stone, punch-card, salt cure, slag chemistry — no voltage, no beast grammar. Tallies are counted by hand, recorded in ink, sealed with wax and hallmark.

Contracts in triplicate: one for hall, one for counterparty, one for temple archive. Disputes go to the hall's master + one neutral guild witness.

docs.title: 🌍 Reach
docs.text: Operates from Tuba — Mamanolo Tribe/Alkorri outward via Trade Routes and Naval Power lanes. Converts at outposts — price friction is the profit.

Pays miners in Coil, sells to Kobre furnaces.

docs.title: 🧂 Arctic Salt
docs.text: [!INFO] The Ice Salt — Food That Doesn't Rot Pan salt harvested from frozen coastal pans in Kutten and Yakut — salt that makes grain last past winter.

docs.title: 🧊 Origin
docs.text: Seawater trapped in rock pans in Kutten, frozen then thawed — salt rimes left behind. Harder than sea salt, less bitter. The New Elvengar pans are richest — Elvengar refugees became salt farmers by accident after the Great Divergence.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Without Salt, Dissenbarg grain (Temas/Citrea) rots before reaching Anos. So Salt and Grain move together — Salt south, Grain north. Traded at Temas markets for Dissenbarg Krona at a fixed Salt:Grain ratio by temple decree.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Arctic Salt ] ├── Origin: Kutten pans · Yakut ├── Paired With: Dissenbarg Grain ├── Market: Temas (Dissenbarg) ├── Currency: Dissenbarg Krona / Kutten Fang └── See Also: Dissenbarg Grain, Kutten Furs

docs.title: 🐚 Cubri Cowries
docs.text: [!INFO] The Counted Shell — Archipelago Small Change Warm-shallows cowries of the Cubri Archipelago — counted by handfuls and strings, blessed by Aocubri.

docs.title: 🌊 Origin
docs.text: Glossy cowries in the shallows around Cubri — 40 cowries = 1 string, 10 strings = 1 hand. Snails die if transplanted — monopoly is natural. Aocubri temple counters string them blindfolded by sound.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Small change at Sousu and Demon's Horn — sailors call cowries island pennies. Cowrie-to-Guara? No — Cowrie-to-Freeport Doubloon at the concord ports.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Cubri Cowries ] ├── Origin: Cubri Archipelago shallows (Aocubri) ├── Products: Cubri Cowrie coin ├── Markets: Sousu · Demon's Horn ├── Currency: Cubri Cowrie └── See Also: Cubri Cowrie, Freeport Doubloon

docs.title: 🔥 Demonic Ash-Iron
docs.text: [!INFO] The Warm Ore — Ash-Flecked Iron That Holds Heat Ash-flecked iron from the Emberalden and Blazeyard fire-mountain forges on the Demon Continent — smokes when reheated.

docs.title: 🌋 Origin
docs.text: Mined as black ore flecked with Emberalden ash. Smelted in fire-mountain forges — high-magnesium slag makes a true Ember warm for 3 hours after minting — slag holds heat, not spell. Reheat a cold Ember and its stamp smokes — assay test vs counterfeit cold iron.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Controlled by Asatru + Emberalden forges; enforced by Asatru Legion. Sold at Demon's Horn trade hub for Demonic Ember or to Merratodoni for grain (they hate warm iron burning pouches, but buy it for plowshares).

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Demonic Ash-Iron ] ├── Origin: Demon Continent (Emberalden · Blazeyard) ├── Products: Demonic Ember coin ├── Hub: Demon's Horn ├── Enforcer: Asatru Legion └── See Also: Demonic Ember, Demon Ash Drake, Romanium

docs.title: 🌾 Dissenbarg Grain
docs.text: [!INFO] The Bread of Erisdar — Temas & Citrea Fields Inland grain from the vast fields of Temas and Citrea on Dissenbarg — 70% of Erisdar's bread passes through Anos counting houses.

docs.title: 🌾 Origin
docs.text: Broad wheat and barley plains of Temas and Citrea — the breadbasket that feeds South Erisdar via Anos. Harvest feasts (Temas Harvest) fix the year's price at the First Wagon to Citrea.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Moved via coastal ports, counted in Ledger-Weight bales at Beast's Bay. Paired with Arctic Salt — without Salt, Grain rots before reaching Erisdar. The Anos-Venner rivalry is fought over who counts this Grain.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Dissenbarg Grain ] ├── Origin: Dissenbarg (Temas · Citrea) ├── Counter: Anos / Arctic Salt ├── Hub: Beast's Bay · Temas Harvest ├── Currency: Dissenbarg Krona / Anosi Mark └── See Also: Dissenbarg Krona, Anosi Ledger-Weight, Arctic Salt

docs.title: ⚒️ Dwarven Iron and Steel
docs.text: [!INFO] The Forge Standard — Dwarven Ingots Ingot iron and crucible steel from the deep forges of Dwarvengor and the Silver Republic — the metal behind Silver Talon honesty.

docs.title: ⛏️ Origin
docs.text: Deep veins under Dwarvengor and the Silver Republic highlands. Dwarven assay offices test every ingot with a Talon-cut — underweight is returned talon-cut. Steel includes trace Romanium for blue glint when quenched properly.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Moved east to Fractured Erislod and New Mann, west via West Erisdarian Guilder roads to Central Erisdar. Kobre Coal & Coke|Kobre Coal makes the steel hotter. Venner buys Ingots for hull nails at Beast's Bay — paid in Vennerian Ducat at predatory spread over Silver Talon.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Dwarven Iron and Steel ] ├── Origin: Dwarvengor · Silver Republic ├── Backing For: Silver Talon (silver+Romanium) ├── Fuel: Kobre Coal & Coke|Kobre Coal ├── Currency: Silver Talon ↔ Vennerian Ducat └── See Also: Silver Talon, Kobre Coal & Coke|Kobre Coal, Romanium

docs.title: Gold
docs.text: Gold is a precious metal traded across Ge'or. While not as strategically critical as Romanium, gold serves as a universal store of value and medium of exchange across continents.

docs.title: Economic Role
docs.text: Gold is minted into coins by major powers including the Erisian Empire (the Erilia currency) and the Vennerian Trade Republic. It flows along the same trade routes as romanium, spices, and manufactured goods.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Trade: Trade Routes
  • Currency: Erilia (Erisian Empire)
  • Resource Class: Precious metal

docs.title: ⬛ Kobre Coal and Coke
docs.text: [!INFO] The Black Burn — Homunculi Furnace Coal Bituminous coal and beehive coke from the Coalsteel pits on Kobre — the only fuel hot enough for true Homunculi precision.

docs.title: 🏴 Origin
docs.text: Seam coal from the eastern scarp of Kobre (Coalsteel). Coked in beehive ovens — coke burns to 1500°C, needed to melt Kobre Coal & Coke|Kobre Coal steel for Kobran Gear teeth at 0.02mm tolerance. Raw coal exported is cheaper, but real value is coke.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Controlled by Coalsteel and Homunculi gear-forges. Shipped west to Dwarvengor for steel, north to Kutten for winter forges. Paid in Kobran Gear at the pithead, resold at Demon's Horn for Demonic Ember or Vennerian Ducat.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Kobre Coal and Coke ] ├── Origin: Kobre (Coalsteel) ├── Users: Homunculi · Dwarvengor · Kutten ├── Products: Kobran Gear · Dwarven Iron ├── Currency: Kobran Gear at source └── See Also: Kobran Gear, Dwarven Iron, Romanium

docs.title: 🦊 Kutten Furs and Ivory
docs.text: [!INFO] The Winter Wealth — Furs That Save Lives Prime winter furs and walrus ivory from the Kutten wastes and Yakut — without them Dissenbarg cities would freeze in March.

docs.title: ❄️ Origin
docs.text: Trapped and hunted across Kutten (Marko/Malbodor) and the Yakut frontier. Frostbeast pelts are thickest, seal furs most waterproof, walrus ivory carved locally. Kutten trappers mark pelts with clan notches — provenance is identity.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Moved south via Demon's Horn traders to Dwarvengor and Central Erisdar for Erilia/Silver Talon, and west to West Erisdar for West Erisdarian Guilder. Kutten Fang coin is literally Fang wealth — a Fang is a promise of fur.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Kutten Furs and Ivory ] ├── Origin: Kutten · Yakut ├── Markets: Demon's Horn → Dwarvengor → Central Erisdar ├── Currency: Kutten Fang (fang = fur pledge) └── See Also: Kutten Fang, Kutten Frostbeast, Arctic Salt

docs.title: 🌶️ Lumina Spices
docs.text: [!INFO] The High-Value Scent — Lumina's Green Gold Lumina's pepper, sweet-rind and fireleaf — picked in the Lumina jungles and carried on Anos and Venner hulls. One chest buys a house in Grimmel.

docs.title: 🌿 Origin
docs.text: Harvested year-round in the low canopies of Lumina Kingdom, Cammao and Lake Kingdom. Great Cattos felid farmers guard groves; Gigas takes tithe in Spice, not coin, ironically. Spoilage is 3 weeks — hence the Anos-Venner speed race via Beast's Bay.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Controlled at source by Lumina Kingdom but moved by outsiders — Anos via Lumina Outpost and Venner via Goishi. Paid in Luminal Tusk at the grove, sold in South Erisdar for Vennerian Ducat or Anosi Mark at 8-12x markup. Romanium preservation dust is rumored to extend shelf life — true, but too expensive.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Lumina Spices ] ├── Origin: Lumina ( Lumina Kingdom, Cammao ) ├── Movers: Anos via Lumina Outpost · Venner via Goishi ├── Hub: Beast's Bay ├── Currency: Luminal Tusk → Anosi Mark / Vennerian Ducat └── See Also: Luminal Tusk, Trade Routes, Romanium

docs.title: 🔘 Luminous Pearls
docs.text: [!INFO] The Shared Pearl — Eight Islands, One Luster Luminous pearl beds of the Luminous Ocean — the commons that made the Luminous Sea Islands pact to honor each other's Pearls.

docs.title: 🏝️ Origin
docs.text: Shallow beds between the eight Luminous Sea Islands — Gildenrise gold-tinted, Mikrad pink, Koln stark white. Connoisseurs tell origin by tint, but weight rules. Pearl beds are why these islands are resupply havens on the Erisdar↔Dissenbarg route.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Pact: all eight islands honor each other's Pearls. Venner factors at each island assay Pearl-to-Ducat; the pact prevents undercutting. Also traded at any Luminous Ocean port — practical money for sailors.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Luminous Pearls ] ├── Origin: Luminous Sea Islands beds (Gildenrise · Mikrad · Koln) ├── Pact: 8 islands honor each other's Pearl ├── Products: Luminous Pearl coin ├── Currency: Luminous Pearl └── See Also: Luminous Pearl, Meble Pearls, Luminous Ocean

docs.title: 🐺 Marti Hides and Wolf Pelts
docs.text: [!INFO] The Howl Hide — Wolf Pelts That Drum Cured hides and wolf pelts from the herds of Marti — stretched over Romanium hoops for the Martian Drum coin that rings.

docs.title: 🐾 Origin
docs.text: Herds of steppe cattle and grey wolves on Marti (Germina/Kut/Kobra). Wolf-folk of Kobra and Kut cure hides with smoke and salt. A true Drum rings when tapped — clipped skin thuds, revealing debasement. Pelts are also winter clothing in Kutten.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Hides move as coin and as goods — Drum-skins are the coin, pelts are the coat. Stacked like plates, the clack is unmistakable in bazaars from Marti to Beast's Bay. Anos factors at Anos Marti Drum-to-Mark at the port.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Marti Hides and Wolf Pelts ] ├── Origin: Marti ( Germina · Kut · Kobra ) ├── Products: Martian Drum coin (hide + Romanium hoop) ├── Measure: Marti Howl distance └── See Also: Martian Drum, Marti Grey Wolf

docs.title: ⚪ Meble Pearls
docs.text: [!INFO] The Trench Pearl — One Island's Monopoly Natural pearls from the deep trench east of Meble — the Sousu monopoly that makes Meblean Pearl coin possible. One pearl per decade per bed.

docs.title: 🌊 Origin
docs.text: Harvested by Sousu breath-hold divers in the deep trench east of Meble — 300m dives, many divers tie off so their bodies can be recovered. Pearls set in silver hoops, notched for fractions. Freshwater pearls are half-pearls for small change.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Monopoly held by Sousu — the third trade power (after Anos/Venner). After harverst, Pearls go via Kreb and Megrel to Beast's Bay where Pearl-to-Ducat is prestige jewelry and money. Nobles wear wealth.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Meble Pearls ] ├── Origin: Meble trench (Sousu) ├── Products: Meblean Pearl coin ├── Routes: Kreb · Megrel → Beast's Bay ├── Currency: Meblean Pearl └── See Also: Meblean Pearl, Luminous Pearl, Trade Routes

docs.title: 🟩 Mia Jade
docs.text: [!INFO] The Green Sliver — Shared Vein, Shared Wealth Mia jade slivers from the single highland vein on Mia — chipped, not cut, each fracture unique. Three tribes share the vein by treaty.

docs.title: ⛰️ Origin
docs.text: Single jade vein in the Mia highlands. Mukini, Orgor and Xi'xia chip by treaty — the vein is shared wealth, not owned, even during inter-tribal raids. Slivers are fracture-fingerprinted — forgers fail.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Exchanged at Mia Checkpoint — Venner checkpoint factors Jade-to-Ducat, complaining slivers cut hands. Also used as inlay for West Guilder notches.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Mia Jade ] ├── Origin: Mia highland vein (Mukini · Orgor · Xi'xia) ├── Products: Mian Jade coin ├── Checkpoint: Mia Checkpoint → Vennerian Ducat └── See Also: Mian Jade, Mia

docs.title: 🪵 Northwood Timber
docs.text: [!INFO] The Northern Mast — Elboria's Leverage Tall straight mast timber from the boreal forests of Northaxeland and Venkradian — the hulls of Beast's Bay are Northwood before they are anything else.

docs.title: 🌲 Origin
docs.text: Old-growth blackpine and iron-oak in Venkradian and the -boria valleys of Northaxeland. Felled in winter when sap is low, floated down the Elboria river-road. Elven rangers of Elvenkrad mark each tree with Alegoria rites — cut without rite and the log sours (rots from inside).

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Monopoly held by Northaxeland capital Elboria — all Northwood is branded at the Elboria yard. Sold south to Central Erisdar (Pilferhorn, Magna) for Alegorian Crown and to Venner shipyards for Vennerian Ducat. The Mann Order refuses to sell Northwood to anyone — its star-timber stays home.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Northwood Timber ] ├── Origin: Northaxeland · Venkradian · Elvenkrad ├── Controller: Northaxeland yard at Elboria ├── Hubs: Elboria → Central Erisdar · Beast's Bay shipyards ├── Currency: Alegorian Crown / Vennerian Ducat └── See Also: Alegorian Crown, Romanium, Trade Routes

docs.title: 📉 The Exhaustion
docs.text:
The dwarves built their entire civilization on Romanium. Megacities, trade networks, manufacturing empires — all dependent on a single finite resource.

When the ore ran out, everything collapsed.

The transition to iron — a massive technological downgrade — marked the beginning of the Iron Age (Age 6, −4,499 to −3,000 BGD). The dwarves never again reached the heights of their Romanium-powered era.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Romanium ] ├── Era: Dwarf Era — Age 5 ├── Used By: Dwarves — Proto-Industries and Perfect Weapons ├── Exhausted: End of Age 5 — Triggered the Iron Age ├── Aftermath: Dwarven Decline — Never Fully Recovered ├── Known Deposits: None Remaining ├── Dragon Tongue: "Suebo" — the dragon-language word for romanium, namesake of the island Suebo ├── Status: Lost — A Resource That Will Not Return

docs.title: 🏛️ South Marble
docs.text: [!INFO] The White Stone — Basilicas Built of South Marble Veined white marble from the South Erisdar highlands (Melior/Cerulea) — the stone of every Erisian basilica and pontifical palace.

docs.title: ⛰️ Origin
docs.text: Quarried at Melior and Cerulea — open-cut white faces that can be seen from the Greater Ocean. Blocks are dressed on site, then sledge-hauled to the coast. Pontificate blesses each block; unblessed marble cannot be used in a basilica by canon.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Moved north to Central Erisdar (Pontificate, Elvennrin) for Erilia at any price — the Empire will pay. Venner carries finished marble south to Dissenbarg cities (Cletas uses it for Agora stelae) for Vennerian Ducat.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ South Marble ] ├── Origin: Melior · Cerulea (South Erisdar) ├── Buyers: Erisian Empire · Pontificate · Dissenbarg ├── Currency: Erilia (north) / Vennerian Ducat (sea) └── See Also: Erilia, Trade Routes

docs.title: ☀️ South Sun Incense and Goldleaf
docs.text: [!INFO] The Noon Gold — Solstice Incense That Makes Gold Never Tarnish Solstice incense and hammered goldleaf from the South Sun Empire — the secret behind the never-tarnishing South Sun Aureus.

docs.title: ☀️ Origin
docs.text: Western gold hammered to leaf at noon on solstice, smoked with island incense from the South Sun Empire archipelago. South Sun smiths claim the blend blesses metal — metallurgically, the smoke leaves a nano-film that resists tarnish.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Controlled by the South Sun Empire imperial mint. Goldleaf sold to Tabontabar for temple gilding and to Venner for Aureus-to-Ducat premium. Safe at Triad border posts where Triad and Aureus trade 1:1 by treaty.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ South Sun Incense and Goldleaf ] ├── Origin: South Sun Empire ├── Products: South Sun Aureus (never-tarnishing) ├── Treaty: Tabontabar Triad 1:1 └── See Also: South Sun Aureus, South Marble

docs.title: 🪶 Tuba Plumes
docs.text: [!INFO] The Lightest Export — Stormbird Plumes Iridescent flight feathers of the Tuba stormbirds — sealed in sap-resin, graded by spectrum. Sacred to Mamanolism.

docs.title: 🕊️ Origin
docs.text: Molt-collected, not hunted, by the bird-tenders of the Mamanolo and Alkorri — to pluck a living bird is blasphemy in Mamanolism (all animals divine). Feathers sealed in clear sap-resin, quill notched for denomination. Full-spectrum plumes buy a canoe.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Lightest coin in Ge'or — literally. A purse of Feathers weighs nothing. Traded at Beast's Bay as luxury curios at 10x inland value — mainland collectors pay for shimmer more than value.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Tuba Plumes ] ├── Origin: Tuba (Mamanolo · Alkorri) — Mamanolism ├── Products: Tubian Feather coin ├── Taboo: Never plucked, only molt-gathered └── See Also: Tubian Feather, Tuba Stormbird

docs.title: 🟣 Tyrian Purple Dye
docs.text: [!INFO] The Purple Price — One Coast, One Color Tyrian purple from the murex flats of the Purple Coast — the color of the Merratodoni Liberty and the reason Merratodoni can print paper that no one can copy.

docs.title: 🐚 Origin
docs.text: Harvested from murex snails on the tidal flats of the Purple Coast — 10,000 snails per ounce of dye. Ironcloak enforces the monopoly; poaching nets are burned. Dye is fixed with urine and sun — stinks for weeks, lasts forever.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Controlled by Human Republic + Purple Coast joint council. Its purple-black ink makes Merratodoni Liberty unforgeable without access to the flats. Sold to Venner and Erisian tailors for Merratodoni Liberty at 1:20 vs Erilia. Merratodoni joke: We sell the color of kings to buy the grain to feed farmers.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Tyrian Purple Dye ] ├── Origin: Purple Coast (Merratodoni) ├── Controller: Human Republic · Ironcloak ├── Products: Merratodoni Liberty ink · luxury cloth ├── Currency: Merratodoni Liberty └── See Also: Merratodoni Liberty, Trade Routes

docs.title: 🟠 Xeti Copper
docs.text: [!INFO] The Coiled Red — Temple Copper of Wruowas Red temple copper from the pits of Ograd and Kyuu on Xeti — wound into Coils and quenched in temple oil (rendered tallow + copper salts, called "serpent oil" after Wruowas).

docs.title: ⛏️ Origin
docs.text: Open pits in Ograd and Kyuu, smelted in temple forges dedicated to Wruowas the coiled serpent. Each Coil is quenched in serpent oil and stamped at the hook with the coil sigil. Weight is by turns — three-turn Coil = day's wage for a Koetebalo porter.

docs.title: 💱 Trade
docs.text: Wound as bracelet-coils, worn on wrist. Xeti merchants love that Anos/Venner factors hate counting coils — negotiation advantage. Copper also sold as ingots to Dissenbarg cities for wiring (temples).

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Xeti Copper ] ├── Origin: Xeti (Ograd · Kyuu) ├── Deity: Wruowas ├── Products: Xetian Coil coin └── See Also: Xetian Coil, Xeti Coil Serpent

docs.title: Aelis
docs.text:
"Honor isn't what they beat into me. It's the only thing they couldn't take."

Aelis is a girl born in 600 AGD in the Moonfang Dominion, a frozen death-cult nation on Moon Wolf Island northeast of Erisdar. She is blonde, petite, and pretty — which, in the cult of Cleton, is a death sentence.

docs.title: Early Life
docs.text:
Aelis was born into a poor family of devout cult believers. Her life held no warmth. Beaten for the smallest infraction — a spilled cup, a word out of turn, a look that lasted too long. By age four she was already working, her childhood traded for labor before she could form memories of anything else.

She does not know kindness. She knows duty, pain, and the cold certainty that survival means obedience. The cult of Cleton demands child sacrifices each year, and the prettiest are chosen. Aelis's appearance marks her as a future offering — a fact her family no doubt sees as an honor, not a horror.

Yet somewhere in the bruises, she found a code of her own. Honor — not the cult's version, which means silence and submission — but something personal and absolute. A thing you hold when everything else is stripped away. She believes in it the way her family believes in Cleton: without proof, without doubt, without any reason to think it will save her.

docs.title: Role
docs.text: Aelis is essential to the plot of Ge'or. Her path will cross with the protagonists in ways not yet written. She was not born to be sacrificed. She was born to break something.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Home: Moonfang Dominion, Moon Wolf Island
  • Family: Poor cult-believing household (unnamed)
  • God (her people's): Cleton, the Wolf God
  • Refuge: The Molten Archipelago lies southwest — reachable by sea. Karabar runs refugee bases there, but escape means exchanging one cage for another.
  • Future: Plot-critical (TBD)

docs.title: Agartha
docs.text:
The woman Julian loved. Murdered by a Shadow. The reason he marched on Baoth.

Agartha was the wife of Julian the Dragon Tamer.

docs.title: Life
docs.text:
Julian met Agartha when he was thirteen years old, while working in the countryside plowing fields after fleeing Shuttil. They married two years later. They eventually moved out of Shuttil and settled near the capital of Baoth, where Julian started a beer delivery business.

By the time Julian was nineteen, they had two children — a son and a daughter.

docs.title: Death
docs.text:
An aristocrat from Baoth — possessed by the Shadows, acting strange and predatory — found Agartha beautiful. When she refused his advances, he murdered her and both of her children in cold blood.

Her death broke Julian. It set him on the path through the Lyrical Forest, through Dragonreach, and into legend.

docs.title: The Grave
docs.text: After Julian's march on Baoth, he went to the grave of Agartha and their children. He opened it with his own hands. He touched their bodies. He heard their voices — all three — telling him to rest. Julian died on the spot. Their skeletons and his body immediately disintegrated into the black agent.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Agartha ] ├── Species: Human ├── Husband: Julian the Dragon Tamer ├── Children: Son and daughter (both murdered alongside her) ├── Murdered by: Shadow-possessed aristocrat from Baoth ├── Era: ~528 BGD ├── Significance: Her death triggered Julian's journey to Dragonreach └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Amelia
docs.text:
"It's not a pulse rifle. It's a lightning bow. And I've got hundreds of confirmed kills with it." — Amelia, age 6, to an increasingly concerned Emrys

Amelia is a girl born in 598 AGD in the Grimmel Republic — one year after the two protagonists. She is the sole heir of the Amelia family, named after the moon, and the keeper of a relic that should not exist on Ge'or: a Pulse Rifle from the Glorious Alliance crash.

She is essential to the story of Emrys and Lucien — not for her power, but for what she carries. The moment Emrys sees her weapon and says "what the fuck is this pulse rifle doing here" is the moment his past-life memory first breaks through the surface.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text: Amelia wears blue maid clothes — practical, feminine, slightly worn at the edges. Her demeanor is sharp, prideful, and easily flustered. A tsundere through and through: she will insult you while making sure you've eaten.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
• Tsundere. Brags about her kills. Gets annoyed when someone outdoes her. Blushes when thanked.
  • Fierce. She hunted wild animals with a pulse rifle at age five. She's not fragile — she's small, which is different.
  • Proud of her lineage. The rifle is her birthright. She will tell you its history, but only if you earn it.
  • Bothered by being saved. When Emrys killed the goblins in the ravine, her first reaction was not gratitude — it was irritation that she didn't get to do it.

docs.title: The Amelia Family Lineage
docs.text:
The Amelia family traces its name to Amelia, the Daughter Moon — a tradition of moon-naming among the old families of Grimmel. They were hunters, trappers, and scavengers who worked the cave systems of the western hills.

In 377 AGD, an ancestor — a hunter whose name is lost — explored a cave deeper than any before. Inside, half-buried in sediment deposited over fifteen thousand years, was a weapon: a Pulse Rifle from the Glorious Alliance crash. It still worked. The magic of Ge'or had kept its circuits alive.

The hunter discovered its use by accident — a pull of the trigger, a bolt of concentrated magic, a dead warg at forty paces. He called it a lightning bow. The name stuck.

docs.title: Inheritance
docs.text:
The rifle was passed from parent to child for over two hundred years — a secret weapon, a family treasure, a hunting tool. By the time Amelia was born in 598 AGD, it had been in the family for eleven generations.

Her father died when she was four years old (602 AGD). On his deathbed, he pressed the rifle into her hands. She was the only child. The only daughter. The last of the line.

She has carried it ever since.

docs.title: Meeting Emrys
docs.text:
Amelia was six when she met Emrys — another child of Grimmel, born the year before her. He was quiet, watchful, and the moment he saw her lightning bow, something in his face changed.

"What the fuck is this pulse rifle doing here."

She corrected him: it was a lightning bow. He didn't let it go. He followed her. Watched her. Asked questions no six-year-old should know how to ask. She found him annoying.

She also didn't send him away.

docs.title: The Ravine
docs.text:
Three months into their strange friendship, Amelia went alone to a grove she knew — a place where a particular fruit grew, sweet and rare. She fell into a ravine by accident. Ten Goblins found her before she could climb out.

Emrys had been following her. He always followed her. He killed all ten with a lightning spell — precise, brutal, efficient. He was six years old.

Amelia emerged from the ravine furious. Not at the goblins. At him. She could have handled it. She had her lightning bow. He stole her kills.

But she also told him the truth after that — the cave, the ancestor, the family line, the deathbed. Everything. Because if he was going to keep saving her life, he deserved to know what he was saving.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text: Amelia's mother adored Emrys after the ravine. She invited him to everything — dinners, hunts, family gatherings. He became a fixture in their home. Amelia pretended to hate it. She didn't.

docs.title: The Pulse Rifle
docs.text:
See: Pulse Rifle

Amelia's rifle is one of fewer than ten surviving pulse weapons on Ge'or. It fires concentrated magic drawn from the user's own reserves — no ammunition, no reloading, just will and trigger pull. She has used it to hunt wargs, gnolls, and small game since she was five.

She calls it a lightning bow. She will not be corrected.

Her claim of "hundreds of confirmed kills" is exaggerated. Most were rabbits.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Amelia ] ├── Born: 598 AGD, Grimmel Republic ├── Family: The Amelia family — named after the moon ├── Weapon: Pulse Rifle — inherited from father at age 4 ├── Rifle found: 377 AGD, by an unnamed ancestor ├── Rifle origin: Glorious Alliance crash — one of the last surviving pulse weapons ├── Protagonists: Emrys (saved her life), Lucien ├── Relationship: Tsundere toward Emrys — annoyed by his obsession, respects him after the ravine ├── Mother: Alive — adores Emrys, invites him constantly ├── Father: Deceased — died 602 AGD, gave her the rifle on his deathbed ├── Appearance: Blue maid clothes, feminine └── Status: Alive — essential to the early story

docs.title: Anedoris
docs.text:
Anedoris is the sister of the god Tiodorus and a goddess of Maomism, the creation faith of the Maoma Tribe on the Lumina Continent. Together the two gods shaped the beastmen from the ashes of the world and sent them forth to rule over all the forests of Ge'or.

In the reformed canon of Maomism, the Gigas Tribe are the enemies of the gods — sent to destroy the rainforests of the world — and Anedoris's children stand against them as the guardians of the forests.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Anedoris ] ├── Faith: Maomism ├── Kin: Tiodorus — brother, co-creator ├── Creation: The beastmen, from the ashes, to rule the forests of Ge'or ├── Enemy (reformed canon): Gigas Tribe └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Annika Eisenheart
docs.text:
The adventurer who carried two souls before her children carried one.

Annika Eisenheart (born 575 AGD) is the first wife of Marco Eisenheart and the biological mother of the twins Emrys and Ichi Eisenheart — born in 597 AGD, when she was 22. An adventurer from Northaxeland, she brought a hunter's bloodline into the Eisenheart household.

docs.title: The Host
docs.text:
In 596 AGD, the Black Agent — escaped from the bunker of The 157th Colony — chose her as its host. The Eisenheart bloodline's dense mage-cell inheritance was a beacon it could not ignore.

Before the twins were born, Ichi's consciousness possessed her — reading her thoughts, planting ideas about how to raise them. The robot who took a bullet for Mikhail, now steering his mother's hands.

docs.title: Family
docs.text:
• Husband: Marco Eisenheart — Grimmel man of adventurer stock, two wives
  • Co-wife: Camillia Eisenheart — the catmen second wife
  • Children: Emrys and Ichi Eisenheart — twins, 597 AGD

Age 22 at the twins' birth (597 AGD) — will be 35 in 610 AGD (13yr after present 597 AGD).

docs.title: Arkady
docs.text:
The quiet refusal. The shared hatred of the cage. The friend who never left.

Arkady was a man on dystopian Old Earth — the closest friend of Mikhail, and the previous life of Lucien Mortvagn. He fled into the wilderness, fought alongside Mikhail in the AGI ship raid, and was accidentally sealed in a Sterman Pod beside him.

docs.title: The Friend
docs.text: Mikhail's closest friend. They shared the same hatred of the government, the same quiet refusal to comply, the same understanding that the world they lived in was a cage. They kept their heads down. They survived. For a while.

docs.title: The Flight and the Raid
docs.text:
When Mikhail left into the wilderness, Arkady went with him. Hunted by kill-drones. Suspected as spies. Interrogated daily for a week. They earned the rebels' trust — and were placed on the front line of the AGI ship facility raid. Expendable. Newcomers. Unproven.

They survived. The ship was taken. The uprising began.

docs.title: The Pods
docs.text:
Two empty pods at the end of a row. They did not close the doors — they only wanted to rest. The ship malfunctioned. The doors slammed shut.

The pods were Sterman Pods. The experimental black agent entered his blood — and with it, his AI: Mana, lodged in his neural port, unregistered and illegal. For three million years, she stayed awake in the dark, protecting his body, talking to Ichi through the interfaces of two frozen men.

docs.title: The Rebirth
docs.text:
When the black agent escaped in 254 AGD and found hosts in the Grimmel Republic, Arkady's consciousness was carried into the bloodline of the Mortvagn family. In 597 AGD, Lucien Mortvagn was born — the fourth child of Herennia and Gallio, with three older sisters — Sofia, Donna, Oleana — who tease him mercilessly.

Three years later, Mana was born as his little sister. She was the AI in his head for three million years. Now she is the girl who sits next to him at dinner. Neither of them remembers. Yet.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Previous life of: Lucien
  • Closest friend: Mikhail — the man who would become Emrys
  • AI: Mana — companion, now his little sister
  • Pods: Sterman Pods
  • Rebirth: 597 AGD, Grimmel Republic
  • See: Emrys — Life Before Ge'or

docs.title: Atanides
docs.text:
Atanides "the Archaeologer" was the emperor of Termopolas during the Human Age. A great lover of archaeology, he sent team after team into the dungeon of the mountain Metrak — never knowing that the mountain was no mountain, but a machine of the The Last Great War capable of destroying his entire region.

When the machine woke under his thousand-man excavation force — with Atanides and a hundred men waiting at the door — he had no reaction in time. The Metrak killed him and began its trail of destruction.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Atanides ] ├── Title: Emperor of Termopolas — "the Archaeologer" ├── Fatal: The Metrak ├── Foe of: Masaaki Sytrenis ├── End: Killed by the waking Metrak └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Bionidas
docs.text: The current Emperor of the Asatru Empire, of the Xiobita subrace — demons known for their exceptional height and strength. Bionidas governs in constant tension with the imperial court, a body of powerful nobles and ministers who compete with the throne for influence.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Rules: Asatru Empire
  • Subrace: Xiobita — tall, strong demons
  • Government: Imperial monarchy with powerful court └── Descended from: One of Kirivis's generals (not Kirivis's bloodline)

docs.title: Camillia Eisenheart
docs.text: Camillia Eisenheart (born 580 AGD) is the catmen second wife of Marco Eisenheart — 17 when the twins were born in 597 AGD. She is part of the household but not the biological mother of Emrys or Ichi Eisenheart.

docs.title: Family
docs.text:

  • Co-wife: Annika Eisenheart — the first wife

Age 17 in 597 AGD — will be 30 in 610 AGD (13yr after present 597 AGD).

docs.title: Carolas II
docs.text: The current ruler of the Anos Plutocracy. Elected by the council of ruling merchant families. Governs the S-tier naval power in its permanent rivalry with the Vennerian Trade Republic.

docs.text: Chief Thokkar is an orc chieftain of Augamouth, known for his battle prowess and leadership during the Gathering — the traditional orc assembly where clan chiefs challenge and debate.
