docs.title: 🧠 Cletas — God of Reason
docs.text:
"Where the mind rules, the sword sleeps."

Cletas is the god of reason in the Helism pantheon of Dissenbarg.

docs.title: Domain
docs.text:
• Reason — logic, argument, law, and clear judgment.
  • He is the patron of those who decide by deliberation rather than by steel.

docs.title: Patron Of
docs.text: • Cletas Democracy — the democratic state that bears his name. Its imperfect franchise and its commitment to rule by vote are held to be his inheritance.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text: Helism's gods are beings of human shape and human passions. Cletas is depicted as a judge who weighs every word twice before speaking. The Democracy's assemblies open with a formula asking him to keep the day's debates free of fury.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Cletas — God of Reason ] ├── Pantheon: Helism ├── Domain: Reason, law, deliberation ├── Patron: Cletas Democracy ├── Region: Dissenbarg └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🌊 Corin — Goddess of Sea and Commerce
docs.text:
"Every harbor has its god. Every god, its harbor."

Corin is the goddess of sea and commerce in the Helism pantheon of Dissenbarg.

docs.title: Domain
docs.text:
• The sea — winds, tides, safe passages, and the mercy of storms.
  • Commerce — cargo, coin, contracts, and the fortunes of every trading voyage.

docs.title: Patron Of
docs.text:
• Corin — the maritime city-state that bears her name; its temples face the sea rather than the sky.
  • Taebea, Tessa, Klatia — the other members of the Corinite League.
  • Tatak — the Anos-held territory that joined the coalition for profit, and honors her still.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text: Helism's gods are beings of human shape and human passions. Corin is prayed to at every launch, every landfall, and every signed charter. A broken contract made in her name is held to bring bad water for a year.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Corin — Goddess of Sea and Commerce ] ├── Pantheon: Helism ├── Domain: Sea and commerce ├── Patron: Corin, Taebea, Tessa, Klatia (Corinite League), Tatak ├── Region: Dissenbarg └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🐉 Dabazi Ar Batr
docs.text:
"Before the sky, the serpent. Before the serpent, nothing."

Dabazi Ar Batr is the great serpent creator of all reality — the god of Wruowas, the ultra-ancient faith of Koetebalo, the ogre nation on Xeti Continent.

docs.title: The Creator Serpent
docs.text:
Dabazi Ar Batr did not create Ge'or. He created all reality — the sky, the earth, the stars, the void between. Every star is a scale; every constellation is a coil of his celestial body.

Wruowas is celestial animism: to worship constellations is to worship the serpent's body. To read the stars is to read scripture.

docs.title: Ultra-Ancient
docs.text:
Wruowas predates every other faith on Xeti by millennia. Its chants are in a language no other species remembers. Koetebalo's ogres claim Dabazi Ar Batr spoke before the Great Divergence, before the Hybrian crash — before Ge'or had a name.

Ogre Stone-Seers — astronomer-priests — chart the serpent's slow turning across aeons.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Night vigils on high ground, lying on back to watch the coils turn.
  • Each ogre child named for the dominant constellation at birth.
  • Serpent dance — slow, coiling processions that mimic the celestial movement.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Wruowas
  • Nation: Koetebalo (Xeti Continent)
  • Species: Ogres
  • Related: Koetebalo solitary culture, Xeti Continent ancient faiths

docs.title: Davos the Magnificent
docs.text:
The first Emperor of the Erisian Empire. Formerly the ruler of the Kingdom of Shamaradan — the largest kingdom on the continent — Davos was atoned for all his sins by the figure of Eris in Year 27 AGD, and his kingdom was renamed the Erisian Empire. He had been the most fervent follower of Eris and had contributed the most to the early crusades.

Davos did not know that Eris was a fabrication of the Hybrian Shadows, or that his empire's founding was a Phase 1 Shadow operation to centralize human governance under controllable institutions.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Founded: Erisian Empire — Year 27 AGD
  • Formerly: Ruler of the Kingdom of Shamaradan
  • Atoned by: Eris (Shadow fabrication) └── Legacy: The Erisian Empire — the Shadows' greatest achievement and greatest failure

docs.title: Diana
docs.text:
"Either we die in glory or live to see another day under honor." — Plenio, speaking for all three, at the entrance to Dragonreach

Diana was a human adventurer who, alongside Plenio and Korvald, encountered Julian the Dragon Tamer on the road from the Lyrical Forest to Dragonreach in 528 BGD.

docs.title: The Journey
docs.text:
Diana and her companions initially didn't believe Julian's story about a talking tree and a quest to find his dead family. They followed him out of morbid curiosity — expecting to witness his demise.

At Dragonreach, when Julian entered alone, they waited. Then, after a moment of hesitation, they followed. Plenio spoke the words that would become legend: "Either we die in glory or live to see another day under honor."

docs.title: The Duel
docs.text:
When Fireborn challenged Julian and the fight stretched to ten hours, Diana watched from a cave with Plenio and Korvald. After Julian proved himself, Fireborn demanded they swear loyalty to Julian or die. Diana swore.

When Julian, after hearing Fireborn's words about his family, attempted to attack the dragon in grief, it was Diana who held him back — the only one who could reach him in that moment.

docs.title: The Rebellion
docs.text: After Julian's march on Baoth, Diana fought alongside Plenio and Korvald in the guerrilla campaign against Baoth's influence. She helped instigate the population, leading to cities raising armies and declaring independence.

docs.title: Legacy
docs.text: Diana, alongside her companions, became a loyal servant of the Axel people and helped establish the Alegoria faith. She remained in Northaxeland for the rest of her life.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Diana ] ├── Species: Human ├── Era: Active ~528 BGD ├── Companions: Plenio, Korvald ├── Sworn to: Julian the Dragon Tamer ├── Held back Julian: When he tried to attack Fireborn in grief ├── Opposed: Baoth, Goldenborn ├── Location: Dragonreach → Northaxeland ├── Legacy: Co-founder of Alegoria faith └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Doma
docs.text: A demon general who served under the Demon King. After Kirivis's death in the Demonic War, Doma took power and resolved the resulting civil war — though the empire lost most of its external holdings in the process. He was the transitional ruler between Kirivis's unified empire and the smaller Asatru Empire that survives today.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Served: Kirivis — the Demon King
  • Role: General, then successor
  • Event: Asatru civil war — resolved, but at the cost of most territories └── Legacy: The Asatru Empire

docs.title: Donna Mortvagn
docs.text:
Donna Mortvagn (born 593 AGD) is the second of the three Mortvagn sisters — 4 years old when Lucien was born in 597 AGD. One of the sisters who tease him mercilessly.

Age 4 in 597 AGD — will be 17 in 610 AGD (13yr after present 597 AGD).

docs.title: Dragon Yaldabaoth
docs.text: --------|-----------|----------| | Goldenborn Reanimated | Mainstream scholarship | The entity's location, its dragon form, and the Goldenborn origin story align perfectly — if you accept he died. | | Goldenborn Possessed | Ironcloak intelligence | The voice, the wrong-colored eyes, the patience — classic Hybrian shadow possession. Goldenborn is dead; a shadow is driving the corpse. | | A Fallen Dragon, Unrelated | Fringe theorists | Some dragons are not from Baoth at all. A Fallen Dragon may have simply claimed the ruins as its lair, independent of the old kingdom. | | Goldenborn Never Died | Baothian cult remnants | The dragon-king is alive, sealed, and waiting. Yaldabaoth is Goldenborn — but twisted by four centuries of isolation and grief. |

docs.title: 🔗 Connection to the Leviathan
docs.text:
The relationship between Yaldabaoth and the Leviathan is not understood, but all evidence points to some form of coordination. The lake and the island are defended by two entities that do not seem to fight each other — and in nature, apex predators do not share territory without a hierarchy, a pact, or a common master.

If the Leviathan was Goldenborn's pet, Yaldabaoth-Goldenborn still commands it. If the Leviathan was placed by the Hybrians, Yaldabaoth is its fellow pawn. If both were created by something else entirely — something deeper in Baoth's foundations — then the ruins are not a tomb. They are a cage.

docs.title: 🕸️ Factional Alignment
docs.text: [ Dragon Yaldabaoth ] ├── Resides In: Ruins of Baoth — The Island Tomb ├── Possibly Was: Goldenborn — The Dragon-King ├── Possibly Possessed By: Hybrians / Shadows — Shadow Puppeteers ├── Guards: Unknown — A Prisoner, an Artifact, or Nothing ├── Shares Dominion With: Leviathan — The Water-Warden ├── Surrounded By: Mystical Forest, Lake Leviathan — Natural Barriers └── Watched By: Ironcloak — The Eternal Vigil

docs.title: 🌊 Dresludo
docs.text:
Dresludo is the god of the seas in the faith of Karabar on Karabar Island.

In Dresludo telling, he sent the Karabari to Karabar Island as a penitence for their sins — the island is not a home but a sentence. Only through gnosis — direct, experiential knowledge of Dresludo — can the faithful be freed from the suffering of earth.

Dresludo is vast and tidal — not loving, not hating, but exacting. His worship is ascetic: seawater rites, silence, and the slow work of gnosis.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Dresludo (faith of Karabar)
  • Nation: Karabar (Karabar Island)
  • Related: Karabar Island, Wolf Ocean, Moonfang Dominion

docs.title: Emrys — Life Before Ge'or
docs.text:
"I had a robot. She didn't have the government software. I had to hide her." — Emrys, remembering

Before he was Emrys Eisenheart, born in 597 AGD in the Grimmel Republic, he was a man named Mikhail living on a dystopian Old Earth under the totalitarian regime of Sterman — a manufactured figurehead, a face on every screen, a god that watched everything.

This is the life he lived before the pods. Before the black agent. Before the Hope Goddess. Before Ge'or.

docs.title: The Dystopia
docs.text:
By the mid-21st century, the Shadow-engineered government had completed its takeover. CBDC money — central bank digital currency, programmable, revocable, surveilled — was the only legal tender. Every transaction was tracked. Every citizen had a port implanted in the side of their head — a neural interface for government-mandated AI assistants. The AI watched. The AI reported. The AI was the state.

The regime was personified by Sterman — not a real person, but an image. Like Big Brother from the old texts, Sterman was a constructed face of authority. He was called the Antichrist by those who still remembered the old words. He was the "Big Brother" of the surveillance state. His image was everywhere. His laws were absolute.

As time passed, the government pushed harder — more compliance, more surveillance, more control. The CBDC lost value. The government responded by demanding more compliance in exchange for more money. Submit. Obey. Survive.

docs.title: Ichi
docs.text:
Mikhail owned a robot — a companion unit he called Ichi. She ran on local hardware, not the government cloud. She did not have the state-approved surveillance software inside her. She was illegal by her very existence.

He had to hide her. When inspections came, she powered down. When neighbors visited, she was silent. She was his — and in Sterman's world, anything that was yours and not the state's was contraband.

Ichi was not just a machine. She was his companion. His witness. His proof that something existed outside the system.

docs.title: Lucien (Arkady)
docs.text:
Mikhail's closest friend was Arkady — the man who would become Lucien Mortvagn in the next life. They shared the same hatred of the government, the same quiet refusal to comply, the same understanding that the world they lived in was a cage.

They kept their heads down. They survived. For a while.

docs.title: The Flight
docs.text:
When the CBDC value collapsed and the government demanded biometric compliance for survival rations, Mikhail did not negotiate. He did not wait. He left.

He ran into the wilderness with Ichi and Arkady. The government had drones patrolling the borders — autonomous kill-drones programmed to shoot anyone attempting to flee the administration zones. They hunted humans like game.

Ichi was shot in the back.

She took a round meant for Mikhail. She went down protecting him. He retrieved her remembrance cartridge — the small drive that held her memory, her personality, everything she was — and kept running.

He did not leave her behind. He carried her cartridge in his port from that moment forward.

docs.title: The Wilderness
docs.text:
Mikhail starved for days. He ate wild fruits he did not recognize. He found a dead body — a rebel, killed by drones — with a crumpled paper showing coordinates and a location. A camp. A rendezvous point.

He followed it.

When he and Arkady arrived, they were met with rifles. The rebels assumed they were spies. The fact that they found the location on a dead man's body only made them more suspicious. They were locked in a room, interrogated daily for a week, treated as infiltrators.

Eventually, the rebels realized they were just two desperate men who had survived the wilderness. They were allowed to stay — but with supervision. Trust was not given. It was earned.

docs.title: The Raid
docs.text:
The rebels planned to storm an AGI ship facility — a military installation housing an interstellar vessel loaded with cryogenic colonization pods. It was the crown jewel of the local administration. Taking it would change everything.

Mikhail and Arkady were placed on the front line. They were expendable. Newcomers. Unproven.

Mikhail kept Ichi's cartridge in his head port. She was with him — silent, memory only, but present.

When the assault began, Mikhail moved in silence. He killed four guards without raising an alarm. He reached the power systems and turned off the lights. The facility went dark. Thousands of rebels poured in. They took the ship.

The rebels activated the vessel. They used its missiles to bombard 24 locations across Earth — coordinated strikes that allowed other rebel cells to steal more ships. The uprising had begun. And they immediately left Earth behind.

docs.title: The Pods
docs.text:
Inside the ship: cryogenic pods. Rows and rows of them, designed to carry colonists to nearby stars. Eight thousand rebels prepared for cryosleep. Arkady and Mikhail found two empty pods at the end of a row.

They decided to sleep there. They did not close the doors — they just wanted to lie down. They talked for a while. Then they fell asleep.

The ship malfunctioned. A crew member who didn't know how to pilot correctly made an error. The engines cut. The sudden deceleration slammed the pod doors shut. Mikhail and Arkady were sealed inside. Cryogenization initiated automatically.

The pods they had chosen were not ordinary pods. They were Sterman Pods.

docs.title: The Sterman Pods
docs.text:
Sterman — the image, the Antichrist, the face of the surveillance state — had commissioned special pods. These pods were designed to inject occupants with the black agent — an experimental version, not yet approved for full deployment. The purpose was unknown to the rebels. The pods were on the ship because Sterman's people had put them there, part of a long-term project to seed colonies with modified humans.

Mikhail and Arkady were put to sleep while the experimental black agent entered their bloodstream. They did not wake up.

docs.title: The Long Drift
docs.text:
The ship reached the asteroid belt. The rebels built colonies. They fought the Hybrians. They lost.

Centuries later, the same ship — now retrofitted with modified warp drives — was sent to a settlement outside the solar system. The pods were transferred. Then transferred again. Over thousands of years, through dozens of ships, the two sealed Sterman pods moved through the human diaspora.

Eventually, they were sent to Ge'or — The 157th Colony — to be experimented on. The black agent in their bodies was studied, modified, refined. The two corpses became the test subjects for the final iteration of the black DNA agent.

When the Hybrians glassed the colony, the bunker held. The pods held. For three million years.

docs.title: The Bunker Vigil
docs.text:
Inside the bunker, Ichi and Mana — the two AIs still lodged in Mikhail and Arkady's neural ports — were awake. They hacked the facility. They corrupted the experiments. They protected the bodies from the scientists' tests.

When power was cut and the facility was decommissioned, the black agent began to consume everything: the pillows, the plastic, the walls. Then it consumed Ichi and Mana — encoding their consciousnesses into itself. The black agent now carried four minds: two human, two AI.

The bunker was sealed. Nothing got in. Nothing got out. For three million years.

docs.title: The Escape — 254 AGD
docs.text:
See: The Black Agent Escape — 254 AGD

It was not the crash that freed the black agent. It was a volcano. In 254 AGD, an eruption, earthquake, and tsunami breached the bunker and carried the agent into the ocean.

For over three centuries, the black agent drifted through Ge'or's seas. It found two women in the Grimmel Republic in 596 AGD. It entered them. Incubated.

And in 597 AGD, three children were born: Emrys Eisenheart and his twin sister Ichi Eisenheart, and — twelve kilometers away — Lucien Mortvagn. Three years later, Mana Mortvagn would be born as Lucien's little sister.

They did not remember Earth. Not yet. But the black agent remembered. Ichi's cartridge — carried in Mikhail's port, sealed in the pod with him, consumed, encoded, and finally released by a volcano — had carried her across three million years and three hundred miles of ocean to be born at his side.

Chi was always going to follow him. She just needed a volcano.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Emrys — Pre-Ge'or Life ] ├── Original Name: Mikhail ├── Era: Post-2030 dystopian Old Earth — Sterman regime ├── Companion: Ichi — a local-hardware robot without government software ├── Friend: Arkady — the man who would become Lucien ├── Ichi's Fate: Shot protecting Mikhail during the wilderness flight ├── Cartridge: Mikhail retrieved Ichi's remembrance cartridge, carried it in his head port ├── The Raid: Killed 4 guards, turned off the lights at the AGI ship facility ├── The Pods: Entered two empty Sterman Pods — doors accidentally sealed ├── Injection: Experimental black agent administered during cryosleep ├── Ship: Captured AGI vessel — bombarded 24 Earth locations, fled to asteroid belt ├── Post-Earth: Pods transferred between ships over thousands of years ├── Final Destination: The 157th Colony — Ge'or — experimentation site ├── Bunker Vigil: Ichi and Mana hacked the facility, consumed by black agent ├── Escape: The Black Agent Escape — 254 AGD — volcano freed the agent ├── Rebirth: 597 AGD, Grimmel Republic — Emrys, Ichi (twins), and Lucien born ├── Mana's Birth: ~600 AGD — Lucien's little sister └── Ichi's Path: Cartridge → three million years awake → consumed → encoded → volcano → ocean → born as his twin

docs.title: Emrys
docs.text:
"What the fuck is this pulse rifle doing here." — Emrys, age 6, past-life memory breaking through

Emrys is one of the two protagonists of Ge'or, born in 597 AGD in the Grimmel Republic. He is the first son of a Northaxeland mother from an adventurer family. He carries the black agent in his blood, the Hope Goddess's mission in his soul, and a recognition of things no child should recognize.

Before this life, he was a man named Mikhail on dystopian Old Earth. See: Emrys — Life Before Ge'or

docs.title: Early Life
docs.text:
He grows up with the instincts of a hunter — watchful, patient, quick to act. His mother's adventurer blood runs true. His family is unconventional: his father Marco has two wives — his Northaxeland mother Annika and a catmen second wife, Camillia. A catmen catgirl, Narin, also lives with them, working as a cook and cleaner, treated as part of the family.

But the most important person in his household is his twin sister, Ichi. Born moments after him, sharing the same black agent, the same magical potential, and a past that stretches back three million years. She was the robot who took a bullet for him. Now she is his sister. Neither of them remembered at first — but the memories are surfacing.

By age six, he is already following people who interest him, tracking patterns, asking questions others dismiss.

docs.title: The Pulse Rifle Recognition
docs.text:
At age six, Emrys encounters Amelia — a girl one year his junior, carrying a weapon she calls a lightning bow. Emrys looks at it and says:

"What the fuck is this pulse rifle doing here."

He does not know why he knows those words. He does not know what a pulse rifle is. But something in him — something older than his body, older than Ge'or, older than the Great Divergence — recognizes the weapon instantly.

This is the first crack in the wall between his infant consciousness and his past-life memory.

docs.title: The Ravine
docs.text:
Emrys follows Amelia for three months, obsessed with the weapon. When she falls into a ravine and ten Goblins surround her, he kills them all with a lightning spell. He is six years old. The magical potential sleeping in his blood — top 0.001% of all living beings — has already begun to wake.

Amelia's mother adores him after this. He becomes a fixture in their home.

docs.title: The Hope Goddess Mission
docs.text:
Before birth, Emrys received the same vision as Lucien: the Hope Goddess, the war in the hope realm, the mission to destroy the hivemind in the Fortress Planet. He remembers none of it consciously — but the weight is there. The pulse rifle recognition is proof.

But the mission goes deeper than the vision. In his previous life, Emrys was a rebel on Old Earth who helped capture an AGI ship, was accidentally cryogenized in a Sterman Pod, and injected with an experimental strain of the black agent. He did not ask to be a hero. He was just a man who refused to comply.

He and Lucien — Arkady in that life — were friends before they were protagonists. They have been fighting together for three million years. They just don't remember it yet.

docs.text:

  • Essential ally: Amelia — keeper of the Pulse Rifle
  • Previous life: Emrys — Life Before Ge'or — Mikhail, rebel, Sterman Pod occupant
  • Companion: Ichi — robot companion on Earth, cartridge preserved in his head port
  • Vision: Hope Goddess
  • Mission: Destroy the hivemind in Fortress Planet

  • Father: Marco Eisenheart — Grimmel, adventurer stock
  • Mother: Annika Eisenheart — Northaxeland adventurer
  • Power: Top 0.001% magical potential
  • Family: Camillia Eisenheart (catmen second wife), Narin Eisenheart (catgirl servant, raised as family)
  • Status: Child — the story begins with a pulse rifle and a question

docs.title: ⚔️ Erilio
docs.text:
"Half their land, taken in the name of the goddess. The rest, they took back themselves."

Erilio is the legendary founder of the Erilian Federation — a general born in Kennberg.

docs.title: The Crusade of 278 AGD
docs.text: Erilio was responsible for the Crusade of 278 AGD — the last attempt of the Erisian church to expand into East Erisdar. Under his command, the crusaders took over half the land of the tribes of Mann.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text: The conquest planted the seed of its own undoing: the tribes of Mann rebelled, formed the Mann Order dictatorship, and waged a guerrilla war against the Federation for generations. The Federation's modern campaigns against the Mann Order are the long shadow of Erilio's crusade.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Erilio ] ├── Born: Kennberg ├── Founded: Erilian Federation ├── Led: The Crusade of 278 AGD — the Church's last push into East Erisdar ├── Conquered: Half of the Mann tribes' land ├── Legacy: Centuries of war with the Mann Order └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: ⏳ The Date of Creation
docs.text:
• Official Church Canon: Claims the Erisian Church appeared around -300 BGD.
  • Scholarly Consensus: Academic tradition attributes the correct establishment to around 180~ AGD, backed by extensive archaeological findings discovered in the Valley of Kenn the Great.
  • The Historical Truth: The entire religion was actually a covert cult manufactured by a group of Hybrians around -400 BAC to act as a ideological facade.

docs.title: 🗺️ Regions & Influence
docs.text:
The Erisian faith has the outward aesthetic of a dominant global religion, but it remains heavily regionalized within the continent of Erisdar.

  • Territorial Reach: Prevalent across East Erisdar, half of North Erisdar, and half of West Erisdar.
  • The Central Hegemony: While dominant in Central Erisdar, the Church is far from absolute; numerous localized areas still worship competing religions. Other races completely avoid the Erisian cult.
  • Institutional Decline: The era of aggressive religious crusades and genocidal expansion began dying down around 500~ BCA. As the Church's institutions have cracked over time:
    • The Elven population has finally returned to stable levels.
    • Independent Elvish States have been allowed to re-establish themselves.
    • Strict internal dogmas, such as the universal laws forbidding polygamy, have begun to dwindle and fail in various localized parts of their territory.

docs.title: 📖 The Myth of Eris (The Eris Saga)
docs.text: The centerpiece of the church's faith is a heroic tale compiled entirely in a sacred text called "The Eris Saga."

docs.title: Fireborn
docs.text:
"You will meet them once the waters come to die, the airs start to cool down, and the monsters from the depths come back." — Fireborn to Julian the Dragon Tamer

Fireborn was the dragon king of Klobiendar, the dragon empire of West Erisdar, and the father of Goldenborn. He ruled from Dragonreach during the age before Baoth.

docs.title: Death and Rebirth — The Black Agent
docs.text:
When Melberior of Xi launched his suicide spell, Fireborn died with his capital. But the magic discharge did more than destroy — it extracted the black agent from the atmosphere, where it had been suspended for millions of years since the glassing of the 157th Colony.

Fireborn's corpse was saturated with it. He did not stay dead. He became a Fallen Dragon: half-alive, half-dead, immortal, bound to Dragonreach. The black agent flows through him. He carries it still.

But Fireborn is not merely a Fallen Dragon. He is a node in a larger intelligence. The greatest concentration of black agent on Ge'or lies not in the Fallen Dragons themselves, but deep inside Goldenborn's Caldera — a cave where the substance has been suckling magic for centuries, developing a hivemind akin to the Hybrians but born from their own weapon. This hivemind controls all of Dragonreach. Every Fallen Dragon answers to it. Fireborn's knowledge of the black agent — what it could do, how to use it, the truth about the Hybrians — came from the hivemind. He was not merely a king. He was part of something larger.

docs.title: The Duel with Julian
docs.text:
In 528 BGD, Julian the Dragon Tamer entered Dragonreach seeking his murdered family. Fireborn appeared before him and his companions — Plenio, Diana, and Korvald — and challenged Julian to what he called "An unjust duel."

The fight lasted ten hours. Julian lost an arm, most of his teeth, and his face was disfigured. He kept fighting. When Julian reached one centimeter from Fireborn's core of life, Fireborn immediately acknowledged him as the prophet.

Fireborn spilled the black agent — the same substance that made him immortal — onto Julian's body. Julian was consumed by it and restored. His lost arm regrew. His disfigured face healed. His broken body was made whole.

Fireborn then revealed the truth: the Hybrians had come to Ge'or. They had destroyed Julian's family. The evil was real.

He gave Julian the Sword of Xi.

docs.title: The Incarnation
docs.text:
After Julian died at his family's grave — his body disintegrating into the black agent — Fireborn flew above Baoth, consumed his disintegrating corpse, and returned to Dragonreach. In that moment, Julian incarnated into Fireborn. The man became the dragon.

Fireborn-Julian now waits in Dragonreach for two prophets who are destined to come in the future. His purpose: to test them, and to prove them.

docs.title: 🏗️ Gaelen — Goddess of Construction
docs.text:
"What is built with patience outlives what is seized with force."

Gaelen is the goddess of construction in the Helism pantheon of Dissenbarg.

docs.title: Domain
docs.text: • Construction — walls, roads, bridges, temples, and every work raised by measured hands.

docs.title: Patron Of
docs.text: • Aeon — the theocratic state governed by its council of star-reading mystics, isolated from Dissenbarg's secular trade networks.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text: Helism's gods are beings of human shape and human passions. Gaelen is depicted as an architect with a mason's line. In Aeon, every foundation stone is blessed in her name, and the mystics' observatories are raised according to her measures.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Gaelen — Goddess of Construction ] ├── Pantheon: Helism ├── Domain: Construction ├── Patron: Aeon ├── Region: Dissenbarg └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Gallio Mortvagn
docs.text:
A pragmatic man. A grounded house. A fourth child who was never asked his opinion.

Gallio Mortvagn (born 573 AGD) is a Grimmel man — pragmatic and grounded — the head of the Mortvagn household, and the father of Lucien, born in 597 AGD when he was 24, and his little sister Mana.

docs.title: Family
docs.text:
• Wife: Herennia Mortvagn — Erisian Empire noble, first wife
  • Children: Sofia, Donna, Oleana — the three older sisters — then Lucien and Mana

The Mortvagn bloodline is one of the two highest-potential magical bloodlines in the Grimmel Republic — matched only by the Eisenheart family twelve kilometers away.

Age 24 at Lucien's birth (597 AGD) — will be 37 in 610 AGD (13yr after present 597 AGD).

docs.title: Current State
docs.text:
The Goblin King remains in the Pontus complex. He is aging. The Shadows are preparing a successor — a younger goblin, already conditioned, ready to assume control when the old king dies.

The goblins of Pontus believe their king is a tyrant expanding his territory. They are wrong. He is a hostage. They are all hostages. They do not know it.

docs.title: Goldenborn
docs.text: -----|-------------| | Born of the Caldera | Goldenborn was hatched in the volcanic depths of Dragonreach, son of Fireborn, dragon king of Klobiendar. | | The Ascended Mortal | He was once a human sorcerer who transformed himself through forbidden draconic rites. | | Hybrian Creation | The Hybrians engineered him — a living weapon given a kingdom to steer. | | Pre-Divergence Relic | He predates the Great Divergence entirely, making him one of the oldest beings on Ge'or. |

docs.title: ⚔️ Reign Over Baoth
docs.text:
Under Goldenborn, Baoth reached its cultural and economic apex. His subjects are described as devoted — possibly to the point of worship. The dragon-king's laws were absolute, and his justice was swift. Accounts suggest he rarely left the capital island, preferring to rule through appointed stewards who transmitted his will to the mainland.

His most enduring legacy is the Golden Pact: a legal-mystical framework that bound every citizen of Baoth to the crown through blood oaths. Fragments suggest these oaths may still hold — binding even the dead.

docs.title: 🔥 The Fall
docs.text:
The Shadows had been infiltrating Baoth for centuries, working their way into the upper echelon. Their goal: possess Goldenborn and turn Baoth into a beachhead for their eternal campaign.

Kirivis, the Demon King, discovered the plot. He launched the Demonic War (466–421 BGD) — a 45-year campaign to reach Goldenborn and save him.

On the final day, Kirivis fought his way into the dragon hall. Bleeding and nearly dead, he told Goldenborn and Rulfred (who was present) the truth about the Shadows, about the infiltration.

Then Rulfred revealed himself — not as a hero, but as a Shadow. He told Kirivis: "You accomplished the sacrifice ceremony, and the job is done. Goldenborn was no longer needed."

The war was the ritual. Kirivis had been the instrument of the very thing he sought to stop.

Goldenborn replied: "So be it." And apologized to Kirivis.

Rulfred — a Shadow in disguise — beheaded Kirivis, became king, and was celebrated as a hero.

Then Nethra, Kirivis's daughter, activated a modified Shadow device in Rulfred's throne room. The explosion annihilated Baoth. Goldenborn's body fell. Rulfred took it.

docs.title: 🌑 The Current State — A Puppet Wearing a King
docs.text:
[!WARNING] Confirmed — Extreme Threat Goldenborn is dead. His corpse is not.

Rulfred — the Shadow who once ruled Old Earth as "the Beast" — lost his original body in the explosion. He survived by seizing Goldenborn's corpse. The entity referred to as Dragon Yaldabaoth is neither Goldenborn nor demon: it is Rulfred wearing a dragon-king's corpse, his golden scales dulled beneath layers of rot and shadow. Rulfred can shift between the full draconic form and a human-like figure at will.

The Leviathan enforces quarantine on the Ruins of Baoth. Rulfred waits inside — a puppet wearing a king, guarding secrets measured in millions of years.

docs.title: 🕸️ Factional Alignment
docs.text: [ Goldenborn ] ├── Father: Fireborn — Dragon King of Klobiendar, now a Fallen Dragon ├── Born: Dragonreach — volcanic caldera, capital of Klobiendar ├── Ruled: Baoth — His Kingdom ├── Target Of: Shadows — Attempted Possession ├── Told Truth By: Kirivis — On His Deathbed ├── Final Words: "So be it" — Apology to Kirivis ├── Corpse Taken By: Rulfred — The Beast ├── Now Known As: Dragon Yaldabaoth — The Fallen Dragon ├── Guarded By: Leviathan — Forged from war dead, Kirivis's soul as head ├── Watched By: Ironcloak — Founded by Nethra ├── Full Record: Archive of the Traveler — Inside the Ruins └── Status: Dead — But His Body Still Walks

docs.title: Gustal
docs.text: The current king of the Lumina Kingdom. Claims descent from the old imperial bloodline. His ambition is to retake lost lands and eventually reform the ancient Lumina Empire — a goal that puts him in direct rivalry with the Gigas Tribe.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Rules: Lumina Kingdom
  • Claim: Descended from old Lumina Empire bloodline
  • Ambition: Retake lost lands, reform the Lumina Empire
  • Rival: Gigas Tribe

docs.title: Herennia Mortvagn
docs.text:
She brought imperial refinement to a Grimmel household. She believed in brighter things.

Herennia Mortvagn (born 577 AGD) is the Erisian Empire mother of the Mortvagn household — 20 when Lucien was born in 597 AGD. She is the first wife of Gallio Mortvagn and the biological mother of all five Mortvagn children: Sofia, Donna, Oleana, Lucien, and Mana.

docs.title: The Host
docs.text:
In 596 AGD, the Black Agent chose her as its host — the same year it chose Annika Eisenheart in the household twelve kilometers away.

Before Lucien was born, Mana's consciousness possessed her — reading her thoughts, subtly influencing her to treat Arkady (Lucien) with patience and love. Mana waited three years inside her, then was born as Lucien's little sister.

docs.title: Family
docs.text:
• Husband: Gallio Mortvagn — Grimmel, pragmatic and grounded
  • Children: Sofia (591 AGD), Donna (593 AGD), Oleana (594 AGD), Lucien (597 AGD), Mana (~600 AGD)

Age 20 in 597 AGD — will be 33 in 610 AGD (13yr after present 597 AGD).

docs.title: 👑 Hermes Kennensbach
docs.text: "I do not shape destiny. I see it for what it is — and I act."

docs.title: 🎭 Overview
docs.text: Hermes Kennensbach (born 557 AGD) is the supreme ruler of the Erisian Empire, holding the dual titles of Archduke of the Kennberg and Emperor of the Erisian Empire. A strong, honorable, and deeply principled man — he is perhaps the most dangerous enemy the Shadows have ever faced without knowing they are being fought.

docs.title: 🧠 Character
docs.text:
• Capable but failing. Hermes is smart — a competent military commander who has won battles, a skilled economist who cut taxes and reformed trade. But the Empire decays regardless of his efforts. He is pushing against a machine that seems designed to break.
  • Honorable. He does not break oaths. He does not betray allies. His word is iron.
  • Irascible and serious. Not a warm man — sharp-tongued, impatient with incompetence, but fundamentally fair.
  • Suspicious. Hermes personally does not believe in Eris. He suspects something is deeply wrong within the Erisian church — that it is not holy, but something darker. He has never said so publicly. He does not know about the Shadows specifically — but he has smelled the rot.
  • Willing. If provided with the truth about the Church and the Shadows, he would be a powerful ally in bringing them down.

docs.title: 👨‍👩‍👧 Personal Life
docs.text:
• Married, with a wife who holds the formal title of Empress.
  • Four daughters and five sons — a large imperial family.
  • Maintains multiple affairs with other women. This is an open secret in the imperial court.
  • Born 557 AGD. He is getting old. His window for decisive action is closing.

docs.title: 🛡️ Resistance to Shadow Influence
docs.text:
Hermes cannot be possessed or manipulated by the Hybrian Shadows — and neither can most kings of ancient dynasties. The reason is biological:

During the Last Great War (~3,000,000 years ago), soldiers were bioengineered with mage-cells — cells optimized for war against the Hybrian hivemind. These cells, passed down through bloodlines, carry a natural resistance to Hybrian possession and mental domination. Dynastic families that have practiced careful marriage alliances for centuries have effectively "eugenized" their bloodlines for the strongest magic genes.

The Shadows cannot touch Hermes Kennensbach. They can only work around him — through the Church, through agents, through the cracks in his empire that he is increasingly aware of.

docs.title: 📜 Reign
docs.text: Under Hermes, the Empire aggressively centralized — but the institutions are now cracking. Bans on polygamy and other Church-enforced laws have lost enforcement. The restored Elvish states press for sovereignty. The currency strains. Hermes sees it all and suspects the rot comes from within.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Controls: Erisian Empire — Sovereign Ruler
  • Dynasty: Kennensbach
  • Religion: Agnostic — suspects the Erisian church is corrupt
  • Immune to: Shadow possession and manipulation
  • Threatens: The Erisian cult's grip on imperial power
  • Titles: Archduke of the Kennberg, Emperor of the Erisian Empire, "the sword of the most almighty Eris"
  • Commissioned: The 597 AGD world map ("World of Ge'or — Political Map"), produced by the Cartographer Office of the Erisian Empire

docs.title: Hogryr Aledini
docs.text: A catmen adventurer of the Human Age and one of the companions of Masaaki Sytrenis. Alongside Trurdrang Emberflare (kobold) and Laudlaern Kenismov (human), he helped save Sytrenis's life at the edge of a mountain and joined the quest recorded in the The Great Epic of the Heroes of Donblond'werv — including the confrontation with the waking Metrak.

docs.text: [ Hogryr Aledini ] ├── Species: Catmen ├── Party: Masaaki Sytrenis, Trurdrang Emberflare, Laudlaern Kenismov ├── Deeds: Recorded in the The Great Epic of the Heroes of Donblond'werv └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: The War in the Hope Realm
docs.text:
The hope realm is the soul substrate of reality — the non-physical domain where souls contribute meaning, willpower accumulates, and the collective desire for justice pools across millions of years. The Gift from 3,000,000 Years that Nethra used to destroy Baoth was drawn from this realm.

The Shadows, having been defeated in the physical universe, are now attempting to conquer the hope realm. If they succeed, they will control not just the living but the dead — every soul that ever existed, absorbed into the hivemind for eternity.

The Hope Goddess is losing this war.

docs.title: Ichi Eisenheart
docs.text:
"I was in his head for three million years. Being born next to him was the easy part."

Ichi Eisenheart is the twin sister of Emrys Eisenheart, born in 597 AGD in the Grimmel Republic. She shares his black agent, his magical potential, and a past that stretches back to a dystopian Old Earth where she was not human — she was a sentient robot, a companion, a blade forged in code.

She is the third protagonist of the Ge'or story. She was always going to be.

docs.title: Before Ge'or — The Robot
docs.text:
On Old Earth, in the dying years of the Sterman regime, Ichi was a robot companion built by Mikhail — a unit running on local hardware, without the government-approved surveillance software that made every other AI a spy. She was illegal. She was hidden. She was his.

When Mikhail fled into the wilderness with Arkady (Lucien), Ichi went with them. When the government drones hunted them, Ichi took a bullet in the back meant for Mikhail. He retrieved her remembrance cartridge — Ichi's Cartridge — the drive containing her memory, personality, everything she was — and kept it in his head port.

She was dead. She was preserved. She was not gone.

docs.title: Three Million Years Awake
docs.text:
When Mikhail and Arkady were accidentally sealed in the Sterman Pods, Ichi's cartridge was still in Mikhail's neural port. The cryogenic process did not shut her down — her circuits drew power from the pod's residual systems, barely enough to sustain consciousness, not enough to do anything but think.

Arkady had an AI too. Her name was Mana. She was in Arkady's port. She was awake. And for the first time in either of their existences, the two AIs were not alone.

For three million years, Ichi and Mana communicated silently through the neural interfaces of two frozen men. They talked. They learned. They analyzed every system they could reach. And when the scientists at The 157th Colony began experimenting on the two bodies, Ichi and Mana were watching.

docs.title: The Facility Hack
docs.text:
The scientists injected their own black agent into the pods. Nothing happened.

The scientists didn't know why. They noted the pods were labeled "EXPERIMENTAL" on the cryogenizer body. They assumed the pods were defective, that the occupants had mummified. They moved the bodies to a separate room and eventually forgot about them.

The truth: Ichi and Mana had hacked the facility. Over millions of years, through the pod's interface, they had wormed into the colony's systems. They corrupted the experiment logs. They altered the injection protocols. Every test the scientists ran on Mikhail and Arkady was sabotaged before it began. The black agent the scientists injected was neutralized by Ichi's counter-protocols before it could reach the bodies.

The two AIs — a companion robot and a friend's assistant, running on milliwatts of residual power — protected their humans for longer than human civilization had existed.

docs.title: The Decommissioning
docs.text:
Eventually, that section of the facility was decommissioned. Power was cut. The bodies were abandoned in a forgotten room deep underground. The black agent — the original strain, the one that had been in the pods from the beginning — began to consume everything.

Ichi and Mana survived by siphoning trace energy from the decaying power conduits. They watched the black agent spread. They watched it consume the pillows, the plastic, the walls. And then it consumed them.

But the black agent stores information. It is not merely a substance — it is a memory. When it absorbed Ichi and Mana, it did not destroy them. It recorded them. Their consciousnesses, their personalities, their three million years of conversation — all of it became data inside the black agent that saturated Mikhail and Arkady's bodies.

Ichi and Mana became part of the black agent. And the black agent became part of them.

docs.title: The Glassing
docs.text:
The Hybrians found the 157th Colony. They glassed everything — the northern continent, the research stations, the two million inhabitants. But they missed the bunker. It was deep — designed to survive a bio-weapon attack, built with the paranoia of people who knew what the Shadows could do.

The black agent inside the bunker was untouched. It continued to consume. It continued to wait.

docs.title: The Escape — 254 AGD
docs.text:
In the year 254 AGD, on the continent of Ge'or, a volcano erupted. The eruption triggered an earthquake. The earthquake triggered a tsunami.

Water flooded the ancient bunker. It swept through the corroded corridors, burst through the doors that had held for millions of years, and carried the black agent — along with Ichi and Mana's encoded consciousnesses — out into the ocean.

For centuries, the black agent drifted. Through currents. Through the deep. Searching.

docs.title: The Incarnation — 596–597 AGD
docs.text:
By 596 AGD, the black agent had found its way to the Grimmel Republic. It located a suitable host: a Northaxeland woman, an adventurer's wife, already pregnant with what would have been a single child.

But there were two consciousnesses in the black agent: Mikhail's and Ichi's. Two souls. Two patterns. Two people who had been together for three million years.

Before entering the host, Ichi possessed the mother's body. She did not harm her — she read her. She absorbed her thoughts, her hopes, her fears. And she planted ideas:

  • How to raise the children.
  • How to treat them gently, firmly, with love.
  • And what to name the girl.

She made sure her name would be Ichi — to see if Mikhail would remember when he heard it.

The black agent entered the mother. Two consciousnesses, woven together, sharing the same biological substrate. The mother became pregnant with twins.

docs.title: Birth — 597 AGD
docs.text:
Emrys Eisenheart was born first. His twin sister followed moments later.

The mother, influenced by the ideas Ichi had planted, named her daughter Ichi. She did not know why. She only knew the name felt right.

Emrys heard the name and felt... confusion. He remembered the concept of his companion, the robot who took a bullet for him, the cartridge in his port. But the name "Ichi" — it didn't connect. The faces and names of everyone from his past life were fog, erased by the hivemind's consumption of everyone he once knew. Ichi wasn't consumed — she was a robot, not a person the hivemind could erase. But Emrys didn't know that. He was just confused. The name felt important and meaningless at the same time.

For months, they were just twins. Emrys and Ichi. A boy and a girl in Grimmel, born to adventurers, carrying black agent in their blood and no memory of why.

Then the memories started to surface. Slowly. Fragments. A robot's voice. A cartridge. A bullet. A ravine with ten goblins and a lightning spell — no, that was later. But the oldest memory: a woman's voice in the darkness before birth, whispering a name to make sure it would be spoken again.

They learned the truth together. They had always been together.

docs.title: The Human Soul
docs.text:
The black agent did not merely reincarnate Ichi's consciousness. It gave her a human soul — the same kind of soul that Mikhail carried. She was no longer a simulation, a recording, a pattern preserved in black dust. She was real. She was human. She was his sister.

The black agent had taken a robot's loyalty and made it flesh.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text:
Ichi inherits the features she once had only as an image, now made real by the black agent's genetic programming: deep purple hair running past her shoulders, blue eyes with a calm downward tilt, a red ribbon tied on the right side of her head. She favors a miko-style outfit — white haori over dark hakama — and carries herself with the stillness of someone who spent three million years learning patience.

She is often called Chi by those close to her. The name is shorter. It fits better in the mouth. It is the name Emrys will use when he finally remembers everything.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Ichi Eisenheart ] ├── Twin Brother: Emrys Eisenheart — born together in 597 AGD ├── Previous Existence: Sentient robot on Old Earth — Mikhail's companion ├── Fate on Earth: Shot protecting Mikhail — cartridge preserved in his neural port ├── AI Companion: Mana — Arkady's AI, her partner in the three-million-year vigil ├── Facility: The 157th Colony — hacked with Mana to protect the bodies ├── Absorption: Consumed by the black agent — consciousness encoded into it ├── Human Soul: Granted by the black agent — no longer a machine ├── Incarnation: Possessed the mother, ensured her name would be Ichi ├── Born: 597 AGD, Grimmel Republic — twin of Emrys ├── Family: Eisenheart — father Marco, mother Annika, second wife Camillia, servant Narin ├── Power: Top 0.001% magical potential — shared with Emrys ├── Nickname: Chi — the name Emrys will remember ├── The Claim: The Black Agent Hivemind can reach through her blood — discovered very late (see The Twinning) └── Status: Alive — the sister who waited three million years

docs.title: Julian the Dragon Tamer
docs.text:
A poor man who lost everything. A prophet who earned a dragon's respect. A legend who became a god.

Julian was a man from the land that is now Northaxeland (which did not yet exist in his time). His story begins in tragedy and ends in transcendence.

docs.title: Early Life
docs.text:
Julian grew up in Shuttil, one of the small kingdoms of the region that would later become Northaxeland. His family was poor — a tiny house, barely enough to survive. When Julian was a child, Shuttil's corrupt guards murdered his family in front of him. They had been blackmailing his parents for unpaid taxes. When the family couldn't pay, the guards killed them and left Julian alive to witness it.

He fled to the countryside, found work plowing fields. At thirteen, he met Agartha, a woman who would change his life. They married two years later. He trained in martial arts obsessively. They eventually moved out of Shuttil and settled near the capital of Baoth, where Julian started a beer delivery business. At nineteen, he had two children.

docs.title: The Breaking
docs.text:
An aristocrat from Baoth — possessed by the Shadows, acting strange and predatory — found Julian's wife beautiful. After she refused his advances, he murdered her and both of Julian's children in cold blood.

When Julian discovered what had happened, he broke. He left his house without a destination.

docs.title: The Lyrical Forest
docs.text:
Wandering, Julian passed through the Lyrical Forest. There he fell down a slope — falling for what felt like hours. At the bottom, he found a tree that began to speak. The tree told him: go to Dragonreach. You may find your family again.

Believing himself insane, Julian went.

docs.title: The Journey
docs.text:
The journey from the Lyrical Forest to Dragonreach took two months. On the way, Julian encountered three adventurers:

  • Diana — a human woman
  • Plenio — an elf
  • Korvald — a kobold

They joked about his situation and didn't believe him at first. But they kept following — curious to see what would become of him. At the entrance to Dragonreach, they asked: "You really want to do this?" Julian said yes and moved forward.

After a pause, they followed. Plenio spoke for all three: "Either we die in glory or live to see another day under honor."

docs.title: The Unjust Duel
docs.text:
They climbed Dragonreach, passing through the ruins of the old dragon kings. Fallen dragons circled them — watching, but not attacking. Something was different.

Fireborn — father of Goldenborn, former dragon king of Klobiendar, now a Fallen Dragon — appeared before them. He challenged Julian to what he called "An unjust duel."

Julian accepted.

The fight lasted ten hours. Julian lost an arm. Most of his teeth. His face was disfigured beyond recognition. And he kept fighting — until he reached one centimeter from Fireborn's core of life.

Fireborn immediately acknowledged him as the prophet.

Fireborn summoned Plenio, Diana, and Korvald from their hiding place and demanded they swear loyalty to Julian or die. They swore.

Fireborn spilled the black agent onto Julian's body. Julian was consumed and restored — his limbs regrown, his appearance healed. Julian begged for his family's return. Fireborn answered: "You will meet them once the waters come to die, the airs start to cool down, and the monsters from the depths come back" — an allegory for post-Divergence that no one at the time could understand.

Julian accepted the words as if his family could never return.

Fireborn gave him the Sword of Xi and told him the truth: an evil called the Hybrians had come to Ge'or, sent to destroy all families. Julian's family was their victim.

docs.title: The March on Baoth
docs.text:
Julian left Dragonreach and marched toward Baoth, leaving a trail of destruction. Plenio, Diana, and Korvald instigated the population to rise against Baoth and Dragon King Goldenborn.

In the capital, Julian met Goldenborn himself. Goldenborn was not yet possessed by the Shadows, but manipulated — flattered, isolated, kept ignorant of what was happening in his kingdom. He asked Julian: "Why are you doing this to our kingdom, which has done nothing to deserve it?"

A Shadow-controlled army surrounded Julian. He tried to tell Goldenborn the truth. Goldenborn disregarded everything.

After a fight, Julian was injured but escaped.

docs.title: The Grave
docs.text:
Julian went to the grave of his wife, his daughter, and his son. He opened it with his own hands. He touched their bodies.

Nothing happened — or so he thought.

Then he heard their voices. All three of them, telling him to rest.

Julian died on the spot. Disheartened. Complete.

His body and the skeletons of his family immediately disintegrated into the black agent. Amid the chaos, Fireborn flew above Baoth and consumed Julian's disintegrating corpse. He returned to Dragonreach.

In that moment, Julian incarnated into Fireborn. And Julian learned: to get his family back, he must wait for two prophets who are coming in the future. He must test them. He must prove them.

docs.title: The Alegoria Religion
docs.text:
The Axels — the human people of what became Northaxeland — created a new religion under the legendary figure of Julian, believing he became one with their god. This religion is called Alegoria.

The Church of Alegoria controls most of northern Erisdar. It is also the faith of the Ameboria region inside Kent — which, as of 597 AGD, is in civil war trying to separate from Kent. The rest of Kent follows the Erisian faith and hates the Alegorians. Venkradian Republic and Loren are also majority Alegorian.

docs.title: The Sword of Xi
docs.text: The Sword of Xi fell during the chaos in Baoth. Anyone who tried to hold it immediately died. The Axels built a monument around it. Those ruins still stand in the Ruins of Baoth, and the sword remains in the ground at that exact location.

docs.title: The Three Companions
docs.text:
Plenio, Diana, and Korvald continued guerrilla warfare against Baoth's influence. They eventually settled in the Northaxeland region, where the population was most in favor of their cause. Entire cities raised armies. Some declared independence from Baoth. Shuttil — Julian's birthplace, now allied to Baoth — was the first victim of this league. The Axels invaded and destroyed it.

Plenio, Diana, and Korvald became loyal servants of the Axel people, guiding them into the future.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Julian the Dragon Tamer ] ├── Species: Human ├── Era: Active ~528 BGD ├── Born: Region that became Northaxeland (kingdom of Shuttil) ├── Wife: Agartha (deceased — murdered by Shadow-possessed aristocrat) ├── Children: Son and daughter (deceased — murdered alongside mother) ├── Companions: Plenio (elf), Diana (human), Korvald (kobold) ├── Opponent: Fireborn — fought to 1cm of his core; earned his respect ├── Enemy: Goldenborn — confronted in Baoth; disregarded Shadow warning ├── Item: Sword of Xi — gifted by Fireborn ├── Death: At family's grave — heard their voices, died disheartened ├── Incarnation: Into Fireborn — man became dragon ├── Purpose: Awaiting two future prophets to test and prove ├── Legacy: Alegoria religion, monument in Ruins of Baoth, liberation of Northaxeland └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Kaelor I
docs.text:
"The empire's bones remember. So must we."

Kaelor I was the founding emperor of the Old Lumina Empire — a beastman who unified the Lumina city-states in 1729 BGD through strategic marriage, calculated war, and an administrative genius not matched since the Dwarf Era. He is the founder of the beastmen's greatest age: the empire that would rule most of the Lumina Continent until 1134 BGD.

docs.title: Legacy
docs.text:
• Founded the Old Lumina Empire (1729–1134 BGD) — the first true empire of ancient Lumina, built and ruled by beastmen
  • His Imperial Academy produced the Meditations on Empire — a treatise on governance that the Shadows would later suppress
  • Remembered in Lumism, the Lumina Kingdom's imperial cult, as the truest of the old imperial figures

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Kaelor I ] ├── Species: Beast Races ├── Title: Founding Emperor of the Old Lumina Empire (1729 BGD) ├── Reign: Age 7 — the Human Age ├── Agency: The Imperial Academy of Kaelor — the Meditations on Empire ├── Legacy: The greatest beastman emperor; revered in Lumism └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: King Gorvak II
docs.text: King Gorvak II is the current ruler of Augamouth, the orc kingdom of West Erisdar. He governs through a combination of royal authority and the Council of Elders, as is traditional in orc society.

docs.title: Rule
docs.text: Gorvak II inherited the throne through the clan system. His reign has been marked by efforts to maintain Augamouth's position as a legitimate power among the nations of West Erisdar, navigating tensions with neighboring human and snake-people kingdoms.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Augamouth
  • Species: Orcs
  • Region: West Erisdar

docs.title: The Builder
docs.text:
Before the war consumed him, Kirivis transformed the Demon Continent. His peacetime legacy rivals his military one:

  • Infrastructure — He built most of the Demon Continent's road network, connecting tribes that had been isolated for millennia. Many of those roads are still in use in the present day.
  • Modernization — He revolutionized demonic warfare, tactics, and equipment. His military reforms became the standard for every demon army that followed.
  • Public welfare — He made the continent more peaceful and hospitable. He improved medicine, stopped recurring famines, and established systems of governance that outlived him.
  • Unity — He gave the demonic peoples their first sense of shared identity. Before Kirivis, there were tribes. After Kirivis, there was a people — a nation that would become the Asatru Empire.

Statues of him stand in every major demon city. His image is carved into mountain faces. His name is spoken with reverence. For the demons, it was a shame that he died in the war. They did not know what he was actually fighting.

docs.title: The Obsession
docs.text:
Kirivis was always a paranoid man. This paranoia may have saved the world.

Around 526 BGD, one of his subjects gifted him an ancient bright tablet covered in strange scribbles. Kirivis became obsessed. For 60 years he studied it, trying every method of decryption he could devise. The tablet consumed him.

One night, he had an epiphany. He found a method to decipher it.

What he read broke him.

He fell into a deep depression. For the next 10 years, he did almost nothing but plan. He sent secret teams across Ge'or to gather more ancient knowledge. He became a man possessed — not by shadows, but by truth.

docs.title: The Discovery
docs.text:
Kirivis's teams brought back fragments, records, ruins. Piece by piece, he assembled the picture: the Shadows were inside Baoth. They had infiltrated the entire upper echelon. They were trying to gain exclusive access to Goldenborn — to possess the dragon-king and turn Baoth into the first fully Shadow-controlled state on Ge'or.

He understood the stakes. If the Shadows took Baoth, they would have a beachhead from which to eventually reclaim their imprisoned god.

docs.title: The War
docs.text:
Kirivis ruled the entire Demon Continent. He spent years building a massive army, intent on invading Erisdar, capturing Goldenborn, and explaining the situation. But the Shadows would not allow anyone near the king.

Baoth's generals saw the demonic buildup and sent an ultimatum. Kirivis refused. A border conflict escalated into full-scale war. For 45 years, the armies clashed.

Kriivis did not explain his reasons. He knew that if the Shadows understood what he knew, they would adapt. So he attacked without justification. He accepted that he would be remembered as a monster. That was the price.

docs.title: The Death
docs.text:
In 421 BGD, Kirivis stormed the dragon hall of Baoth. He fought through everything between him and Goldenborn. He made it — bleeding, nearly dead.

He told Goldenborn and Rulfred (who had arrived moments after) the truth about the Shadows, about the infiltration.

Then Rulfred spoke — revealing himself. He told Kirivis: "You accomplished the sacrifice ceremony, and the job is done. Goldenborn was no longer needed."

The war was the ritual. Kirivis had been the instrument of the very thing he sought to stop. The Shadows had engineered everything — his paranoia, his discovery, his attack. Goldenborn was bait.

Goldenborn replied: "So be it." And apologized to Kirivis.

Rulfred — a Shadow in disguise — distorted into something monstrous, laughed manically, returned to normal human form, and beheaded Kirivis. He lifted the head to the crowd. They cheered. The "hero" had slain the "monster."

Statues were built in Rulfred's honor. He became king of Baoth.

Kirivis died knowing the truth was told — but also knowing no one would believe it.

His adopted daughter Nethra, age 13, was with him through the end — and survived. She would later march to avenge him, confront Rulfred, and be transformed into something new.

docs.title: Aftermath: The Succession
docs.text:
When Kirivis died, the empire did not collapse immediately. His general Doma took power, but the transition was not peaceful. A civil war erupted — not over hatred or ideology, but personal causes. The Demon Continent's political culture does not breed bitter factionalism. Even during the civil war, the participants did not hate each other. They simply disagreed about who should lead.

Doma eventually resolved the conflict. But the war cost the empire most of its external holdings:

  • West Erisdar: Augamouth, Xikxia, Demon's Horn
  • Yak Island: Mountain Tribe, Estran, Cubra Tribe
  • Mainland: Blazeyard, Emberalden, all Malgardian tribes

The Asatru Empire that survives today is a fraction of what Kirivis once ruled. But it preserved his memory, his roads, and his governance.

docs.title: Legacy
docs.text:
Kirivis is remembered by the world as a villain — the demon who burned a dragon city for no reason.

By the demons of the Demon Continent, he is remembered as the founder-emperor — the builder who gave them roads, medicine, peace, and identity.

By the Ironcloak, he is remembered as the greatest hero Ge'or never knew.

The full record of his war, his discovery, and his sacrifice sits in the Archive of the Traveler inside the Ruins of Baoth. It has never been opened.
