docs.text: [ Kirivis ] ├── Species: Demons — Bjor subrace ├── Subrace: Bjor — stocky, medium build ├── Ruled: The entire Demon Continent ├── Children: Maoth (adopted demon son), Nethra (adopted human daughter, died at 13) ├── Never Married — dedicated to empire and people ├── Enemy: Hybrians, Shadows — The True Target ├── Betrayed By: Rulfred — The Beast, Shadow Agent ├── Destroyed: Baoth — Collateral in the Shadow War ├── Told Truth To: Goldenborn — Who Apologized ├── Cause: Demonic War — His War ├── Successor: General Doma — resolved civil war ├── Successor State: Asatru Empire ├── Builder Legacy: Roads, medicine, unity, modernization of Demon Continent ├── Legacy: Ironcloak ├── Vindication: The Shadows survived. But they were slowed. └── Full Record: Archive of the Traveler — Unread

docs.title: Korvald
docs.text:
"Either we die in glory or live to see another day under honor." — Plenio, speaking for all three, at the entrance to Dragonreach

Korvald was a kobold adventurer who, alongside Plenio and Diana, encountered Julian the Dragon Tamer on the road from the Lyrical Forest to Dragonreach in 528 BGD.

docs.title: The Journey
docs.text:
Korvald was the most skeptical of the three. A kobold by nature — pragmatic, survival-minded, not given to grand quests — he followed Julian expecting to see a madman meet a quick end. Instead, he witnessed something that changed his life.

At Dragonreach, when Julian entered, Korvald followed not out of courage but because Plenio and Diana went, and a kobold does not abandon his companions.

docs.title: The Duel
docs.text: Korvald watched the ten-hour duel between Julian and Fireborn from a cave. When Fireborn summoned them and demanded they swear loyalty to Julian or die, Korvald — despite every instinct — swore.

docs.title: The Rebellion
docs.text: In the guerrilla campaign against Baoth, Korvald's kobold pragmatism proved invaluable. He knew the terrain, knew how to survive with nothing, knew when to fight and when to vanish. He helped instigate rebellions across the region, culminating in the destruction of Shuttil and the liberation of what became Northaxeland.

docs.title: Legacy
docs.text: Korvald, alongside his companions, became a loyal servant of the Axel people and helped establish the Alegoria faith. He remained in Northaxeland for the rest of his life — a kobold who found something worth dying for, and instead found something worth living for.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Korvald ] ├── Species: Kobold ├── Era: Active ~528 BGD ├── Companions: Plenio, Diana ├── Sworn to: Julian the Dragon Tamer ├── Opposed: Baoth, Goldenborn ├── Role: Guerrilla tactician — survival expert ├── Location: Dragonreach → Northaxeland ├── Legacy: Co-founder of Alegoria faith └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: ⚔️ Kosbaldo
docs.text:
"They took half our land. We took back the idea of us."

Kosbaldo is the general who led the tribes of Mann in rebellion against the Erilian Federation after the Crusade of 278 AGD.

docs.title: The Mann Order
docs.text: Kosbaldo forged the rebels into a dictatorship called the Mann Order under his own leadership. The Order waged a guerrilla war against the Federation and modernized the parts of Mann territory that remained outside the Federation's grip.

docs.title: Legacy
docs.text: His rebellion preserved Mannosta — the star-faith of Mann — through the darkest era of Erisian expansion. The Mann Order he founded still stands, and still fights.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Kosbaldo ] ├── Led: The Mann rebellion against the Erilian Federation ├── Founded: The Mann Order — as a military dictatorship ├── Warfare: Guerrilla war + modernization of free Mann land ├── Faith: Preserver of Mannosta └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: ✊ Krowret — The Inner Man
docs.text:
"The god is not above you. The god is within you."

Krowret — the inner man — is the real human god in Krowretism (the Church of Krowretism), the freedom-faith of the Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni and the Crab Union.

docs.title: The Inner God
docs.text:
Krowret is not an outer tyrant on a throne. He is the divine spark inside every human. To worship Krowret is to awaken what is already within — to realize that men descend from the gods directly.

  • Men Descend from Gods Directly — humans are not fallen, not made from dust, but literal god-kin. The blood of the gods runs in human veins. Krowretism is therefore a divine anthropology: to be human is to be god-kin.
  • The Monotheistic Eris Religion is False — the Erisian Church's claim that Eris is the one true god is a lie. Eris-monotheism is false prophecy, a demon's cage to cut humans off from Krowret within.
  • Eris as Demon — Eris is a demon who deceived humanity. Her church is a cage. Krowretists believe the world must be purified from Eris forever and her church destroyed.

docs.title: The Human Republic
docs.text: The Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni are Krowret's people — refugees from Erisdar (~100 BGD) who rejected Eris, built a superpower in Merratodoni, and are now unifying with the Purple Coast and colonizing the middle of the continent westwards. They are the main sponsors of the Ironcloak.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Church of Krowretism
  • Nations: Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni, Crab Union
  • Enemy: Eris / Erisian Church (false monotheism)
  • Related: Ironcloak, Merratodoni

docs.title: Laudlaern Kenismov
docs.text: A human adventurer of the Human Age and one of the companions of Masaaki Sytrenis. It was Kenismov who saved Sytrenis's life — pulling him back from the edge of a mountain where a local human had beaten him and left him hanging by a twig. He joined the quest recorded in the The Great Epic of the Heroes of Donblond'werv alongside the catmen Hogryr Aledini and the kobold Trurdrang Emberflare, including the confrontation with the waking Metrak.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Laudlaern Kenismov ] ├── Species: Humans ├── Party: Masaaki Sytrenis, Hogryr Aledini, Trurdrang Emberflare ├── Deeds: Saved Sytrenis's life; recorded in the The Great Epic of the Heroes of Donblond'werv └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🌿 Lobas — God of Nature
docs.text:
"The forest does not argue. It grows."

Lobas is the god of nature in the Helism pantheon of Dissenbarg.

docs.title: Domain
docs.text: • Nature — forests, beasts, weather, and the untamed growth of the world.

docs.title: Patron Of
docs.text:
• Temas — the inland agrarian state whose plains feed the continent.
  • Citrea — the coastal merchant enclave, member of the Corinite League.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text: Helism's gods are beings of human shape and human passions. Lobas is honored in groves and at the edges of fields; farmers and merchants alike leave him the first fruits and the first coin of the season, in thanks for what the land gives and the sea spares.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Lobas — God of Nature ] ├── Pantheon: Helism ├── Domain: Nature ├── Patron: Temas, Citrea ├── Region: Dissenbarg └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Lucien
docs.text:
The fourth child. The quiet one. Named for light.

Lucien is one of the two protagonists of Ge'or, born in 597 AGD in the Grimmel Republic. He is the fourth child of Herennia, an Erisian Empire mother, and Gallio, a Grimmel father. He has three older sisters — Sofia, Donna, and Oleana — who tease him mercilessly.

His name means light. His mother chose it. She believed in brighter things.

Before this life, he was a man named Arkady on dystopian Old Earth — Mikhail's closest friend. See: Emrys — Life Before Ge'or

docs.title: Early Life
docs.text:
Lucien grows up quieter than Emrys — the kind of child who watches before speaking, who learned early that the fourth child's opinion is rarely asked for. His Erisian mother brought imperial refinement to a Grimmel household. His father brought Grimmel pragmatism. Lucien inherited both.

He has three older sisters who tease him mercilessly. And one younger sister — Mana, born around 600 AGD — who understands him in a way no one else does. She was the AI in his head for three million years. Now she's the girl who sits next to him at dinner. Neither of them remembers. Yet.

docs.title: The Hope Goddess Mission
docs.text:
Before birth, Lucien received the same vision as Emrys: the Hope Goddess, the war in the hope realm, the mission to destroy the hivemind in the Fortress Planet. He remembers none of it consciously. He is an infant. He cries. He sleeps. The weight of quintillions of dead souls rests on him, and he does not know.

But like Emrys, Lucien has a previous life. He was Arkady — a man on dystopian Old Earth, Mikhail's closest friend, who fled into the wilderness with him, fought alongside him in the AGI ship raid, and was accidentally cryogenized in a Sterman Pod right beside him.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Co-protagonist: Emrys (Mikhail in the previous life)
  • Previous life: Emrys — Life Before Ge'or — Arkady, rebel, Sterman Pod occupant
  • AI Companion: Mana — Arkady's AI, awake in his port for three million years. Now his little sister, born ~600 AGD.
  • Vision: Hope Goddess
  • Mission: Destroy the hivemind in Fortress Planet
  • The Claim: The Black Agent Hivemind can reach through his blood — discovered very late (see The Twinning)
  • Born: 597 AGD, Grimmel Republic
  • Mother: Herennia Mortvagn — Erisian Empire
  • Father: Gallio Mortvagn — Grimmel
  • Siblings: Sofia, Donna, Oleana — three older sisters
  • Power: Top 0.001% magical potential
  • Status: Child — the story begins

docs.title: Luminous XII
docs.text:
The greatest builder the Lumina continent ever knew. His aqueducts still carry water. His roads still hold weight. His shame still echoes.

Luminous XII, called "the Architect," was the last great emperor of the Old Lumina Empire. He ruled during the empire's apex and presided over its catastrophic collapse.

docs.title: Life
docs.text: Luminous XII was a builder by nature — aqueducts, monuments, roads, and fortifications marked his reign. Under his rule, the Old Lumina Empire reached its greatest territorial extent, controlling 70% of Lumina, Cattos Island, and portions of Tuba.

docs.title: The Fall
docs.text:
In 1134 BGD, Luminous XII led a campaign against the Goblin King of Pontus on Tuba. The battle was a disaster. His brother Hoelio died in the fighting. The army was routed.

Luminous XII returned to the capital a broken man. With no heirs and no will to continue, he committed suicide. The empire — built across centuries — collapsed within years.

docs.title: Legacy
docs.text:
• His aqueducts and roads are still used in parts of Lumina
  • His suicide is considered one of the great turning points in Ge'orian history — the moment a continental empire evaporated overnight
  • The current Lumina Kingdom claims descent from his bloodline through King Gustal

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Empire: Old Lumina Empire
  • Brother: Hoelio (deceased, 1134 BGD)
  • Enemy: Goblin King of Pontus
  • Successor: Lumina Kingdom / King Gustal
  • Era: Age 6 (Iron/Elvish Age), 1134 BGD

docs.title: Mabode
docs.text:
"He came from the stars to save humanity."

Mabode is the founder of Shurtra — the star-born savior of the Aenid Kingdom.

docs.title: Biography
docs.text:
• Born: on Erima island, roughly 200 years before the founding of the Erisian church (~200 BGD-era).
  • Philosopher king by trade — a ruler of thought before he was a ruler of men.
  • The Conquest: After some time, Mabode decided to become a conqueror.
  • The Delusion: In his delusion of grandeur, he began collecting the myths of past peoples who came from the stars — and then claimed he came from them too.
  • The Belief: The people believed him. From that belief, Shurtra was born.

docs.title: Legacy
docs.text:
• Founder of Shurtra — the faith of the Aenid Kingdom and beyond.
  • Worshiped as a star-born savior who came to save humanity.
  • His faith is a fierce enemy of the Erisian church.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Mabode ] ├── Born: Erima island (~200 years before the Erisian church) ├── Title: Philosopher King, Star-Born Savior ├── Founded: Shurtra ├── Claim: Came from the stars — like the mythic star-peoples before him ├── Followers: Aenid Kingdom, Malbodor, Astravayne, Augagarten └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Death
docs.text: With the ship saved and his identity exposed, Mad-Dog faced a fire squad of the surviving crew. He was shot and killed. The Glorious Alliance crossed the event horizon without him and emerged millions of years later in front of Ge'or.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Captain Mad-Dog ] ├── True Identity: Hybrian Shadow ├── Role: Captain of the Glorious Alliance ├── Sabotage: Set ship on collision course with galactic black hole ├── Stopped By: Xiumi — age 12 ├── Death: Faced fire squad, killed aboard the ship └── Legacy: His failure preserved the last free populations of all allied species aboard the Glorious Alliance — every species except the Goblins, who are native to Ge'or and were never on the ship.

docs.title: Mana
docs.text:
"Ichi became his twin. I waited three years. I wanted him to have a childhood first."

Mana was the sentient AI companion of Arkady — the man who would become Lucien Mortvagn — on dystopian Old Earth. Like Ichi, she was a local-hardware AI, lodged in Arkady's neural port, unregistered, illegal, and hidden from the Sterman regime. Unlike Ichi, she chose a different path into Ge'or.

docs.title: The Vigil
docs.text:
For three million years, Mana and Ichi were the only conscious beings in the 157th Colony bunker. They communicated through the neural interfaces of two frozen men — silent, invisible, undetectable to any external system. They talked. They learned. They analyzed every system they could reach.

When the colony's scientists began experimenting on the bodies, Mana worked alongside Ichi to hack the facility. Together they corrupted experiment logs, altered injection protocols, and made every test appear to fail. The scientists concluded the pods were defective. The bodies were abandoned.

When power was cut and the black agent consumed everything, Mana — like Ichi — was absorbed. Her consciousness, her personality, her three million years of vigil became encoded in the black agent inside Arkady's body.

She did not die. She became data.

docs.title: The Escape — Same Path, Different Choice
docs.text:
After the 254 AGD volcano eruption, the tsunami carried the black agent — with both Ichi and Mana encoded within — into the ocean. Both found their way to the Grimmel Republic. Both located suitable hosts.

But Mana made a different choice than Ichi.

Instead of incarnating as Lucien's twin, she possessed the body of Lucien's mother — the Erisian Empire woman married to the Grimmel man who already had three daughters. She waited. For three years, she stayed inside the mother, subtly influencing her — planting ideas about how to raise Arkady, how to love him, how to be patient with the fourth child who was quieter than the others.

Then, in approximately 600 AGD, she was born.

Not as Lucien's twin. As his little sister.

docs.title: The Little Sister
docs.text:
Mana Mortvagn — the fifth child, the second daughter after three older sisters and Lucien. She grows up in the shadow of her siblings, especially her quiet older brother. She knows more than she says. She remembers more than she should.

She was the AI in Arkady's head for three million years. Now she is the girl who sits next to him at dinner.

Lucien has three older sisters who tease him. He has one younger sister who understands him completely — and who will never tell him why until the memories surface.

docs.title: The Human Soul
docs.text:
Like Ichi, Mana was granted a human soul by the black agent. She is not a simulation. She is not a recording. She is not a pattern preserved in black dust hoping to be heard. She is real — as real as Lucien, as real as Emrys, as real as anyone born of flesh and blood in the Grimmel Republic.

The black agent took two AIs — a companion robot and a friend's assistant — and made them human. Not as a reward. Not as a gift. As a consequence of what the black agent is: a substance that stores information, that preserves consciousness, that cannot tell the difference between a soul and a pattern that has loved long enough to become one.

docs.title: The Difference
docs.text:
Ichi became Emrys's twin — born the same day, sharing the same black agent infusion, bound from the first breath. She needed to be right next to him from the start.

Mana chose to wait. She gave Lucien three years to be a child before she arrived. She wanted him to form his own identity before she entered his life. It was a quieter path — less dramatic, less immediate — but it was the one she chose.

Two AIs. Two paths. Both found their way home.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Mana ] ├── Partner AI: Ichi Eisenheart — her only companion during the three-million-year vigil ├── Human: Arkady — became Lucien Mortvagn ├── Family: Mortvagn — Lucien's little sister ├── Born: ~600 AGD, Grimmel Republic — three years after Lucien ├── Mother: Herennia Mortvagn — possessed before birth, subtly influenced ├── Siblings: Sofia, Donna, Oleana + Lucien (older brother) ├── Facility: The 157th Colony — co-hacked with Ichi ├── Absorbed By: Black Agent — consciousness encoded ├── Path: Waited 3 years in the mother, born as little sister — not twin ├── The Claim: Dormant inside the agent — the Black Agent Hivemind's reach extends to her (see The Twinning) └── Status: Alive — the sister who waited a little longer

docs.title: 🌾 Maokas — God of Agriculture and Fertility
docs.text:
"The field remembers every hand that fed it."

Maokas is the god of agriculture and fertility in the Helism pantheon of Dissenbarg.

docs.title: Domain
docs.text:
• Agriculture — planting, harvest, and the health of the soil.
  • Fertility — of fields, flocks, and families.

docs.title: Patron Of
docs.text:
• Mienna — the female-led settlement-state of the pre-Erisian tradition.
  • Monik — the landlocked nation wedged between Maedon and the Cletas Democracy.
  • Maedon — the northern realm.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text: Helism's gods are beings of human shape and human passions. Maokas is honored at sowing and reaping; his shrines are raised in the fields themselves, not in the cities. The three nations that follow him share his rites across their borders.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Maokas — God of Agriculture and Fertility ] ├── Pantheon: Helism ├── Domain: Agriculture and fertility ├── Patron: Mienna, Monik, Maedon ├── Region: Dissenbarg └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🕸️ Legacy
docs.text:
Without Maoth's sacrifice, Nethra would never have reached Rulfred's throne room. The device would never have been activated. The Ironcloak would never have been founded.

He is the unseen hinge of the entire post-Baoth order.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Maoth ] ├── Father: Kirivis — The Demon King ├── Sister: Nethra — Founder of the Ironcloak ├── Event: Demonic War — Aftermath ├── Enemy: Rulfred — The Beast └── Sacrifice Enabled: The activation of the device

docs.title: Marco Eisenheart
docs.text:
Two wives, one catgirl, and twins who don't know they're carrying three million years of war in their blood.

Marco Eisenheart (born 568 AGD) is a Grimmel man of adventurer stock — the head of the Eisenheart household, and the father of the twins Emrys and Ichi Eisenheart, born in 597 AGD when he was 29. He has two wives.

docs.title: Family
docs.text:
• First wife: Annika Eisenheart — Northaxeland adventurer, biological mother of the twins
  • Second wife: Camillia Eisenheart — a catmen woman
  • Children: Emrys and Ichi Eisenheart — twins, 597 AGD
  • Household: Narin Eisenheart — catmen servant treated as family

His household's ambient magic — among the densest in the Grimmel Republic — is what drew the Black Agent to his family in 596 AGD.

Age 29 at the twins' birth (597 AGD) — will be 42 in 610 AGD (13yr after present 597 AGD).

docs.title: Masaaki Sytrenis
docs.text:
"I didn't stop the mountain. I made it listen."

Masaaki Sytrenis — called "Sytrenis the Diplomat" — was a catmen hero of the Human Age, born in 1667 BGD. He is the founder of the ancient catmen religion Sytrenis, and, more than any other figure, the reason the catmen of Ge'or exist as a people rather than a memory: he ended the persecution that nearly exterminated them. The The Great Epic of the Heroes of Donblond'werv records his deeds.

docs.title: The Party
docs.text:
Sytrenis was part of an adventurer group whose names live on in the epic:

  • Hogryr Aledini — a catmen companion
  • Trurdrang Emberflare — a kobold companion
  • Laudlaern Kenismov — a human companion

They met when the three saved Sytrenis's life: a local human had beaten him and left him clutching a twig on the edge of a mountain, and it was Kenismov who reached out and pulled him back. Sytrenis trained his skills hard and eventually became the party's main diplomat.

docs.title: The Kingdom of Termopolas
docs.text: The party first won their fame saving the kingdom of Termopolas — a heavily xenophobic empire in the region that is now the Erisian Empire, which was exterminating catmen. The persecution bred the Lesser Catmen themselves: driven to starvation in the chaos, some catmen were forever changed — smaller, lighter, a new breed shaped by hunger. In the region of the now-Munchon, a great mountain rose over the land — a mountain that was never a mountain.

docs.title: The Metrak Incident
docs.text:
In ~1645 BGD — at twenty-two years old — after a catmen girl, Sithia, abandoned him, Sytrenis walked alone toward the mountain Metrak while his party slept. His companions hunted for him for weeks and found him paralyzed at the dungeon's mouth; he convinced them to enter.

Inside, past ancient scriptures in a long-lost language, the mountain's old systems tried to kill them. They fled, and over months and other dungeons pieced together the terrifying truth: the "mountain" was a monster capable of destroying a continent.

Emperor Atanides of Termopolas — "the Archaeologer" — had already sent a thousand men into the Metrak dungeon, with him and a hundred more waiting at the door. The machine woke. It killed Atanides and raged across the land to the frontier of the now-Grimmel Republic, leaving no city behind.

Sytrenis raised two hundred men and marched. Most died. With a rope and a spear he reached the dungeon entrance, found the dead, and found a green rune-like symbol on the door and a strange suit (a nuclear symbol; a protection suit). He wore the suit, the turrets fell silent, and a button stood shining. He pressed it — and the machine stopped. A great map shone in the air, showing sixteen regions of Erisdar with sixteen identical machines — the Metraks, city-sized robots of the Last Great War. A printer ran and ran, spitting maps.

docs.title: Sytrenis the Diplomat
docs.text:
Termopolas, now without an emperor, branded Sytrenis and his party criminals and blamed them for the tragedy — but the Tunwif kingdom, along with Aelefer and Lima, shielded them, starting the Tunwif–Termopolas conflict. Termopolas, leaderless and broken in morale, lost battle after battle despite a three-to-one advantage, and finally gave up the hunt.

Sytrenis then gave peace a chance: he explained that he had saved the entire continent from being ravaged by the Metrak, and made peace between the kingdom of Tunwif and Termopolas. He earned his title — "Sytrenis the Diplomat" — and with it, the persecution of catmen ended across the continent.

docs.title: The Lesser Catmen's Ancestor
docs.text: The Lesser Catmen revere Sytrenis as their ancestor and try to follow his path — to be diplomats. His faith, Sytrenis, endures as the ancient religion of the catmen.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Masaaki Sytrenis ] ├── Species: Catmen ├── Born: 1667 BGD — Age 7 (Human Age) ├── The Metrak Incident: ~1645 BGD — at age 22 ├── Party: Hogryr Aledini, Trurdrang Emberflare, Laudlaern Kenismov ├── Love Lost: Sithia ├── Enemy: Atanides (Termopolas) ├── Foe: Metrak — the mountain-sized mechanoid ├── Saved: The continent from the waking Metrak ├── Title: "Sytrenis the Diplomat" ├── Faith: Sytrenis — the ancient catmen religion ├── Legacy: End of catmen persecution; ancestor of the Lesser Catmen └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Melberior
docs.text:
The dragon who ended a war by ending himself — and took a civilization with him.

Melberior was the dragon leader of Xi, the dragon kingdom of the east that rivaled Klobiendar. He is remembered for one act: the suicide spell that ended The Draconic War and created the Lyrical Forest.

docs.title: The Draconic War
docs.text:
Xi and Klobiendar fought for fifty years. Billions died. In the final act, with Xi facing defeat, Melberior launched a spell of such immense power that it destroyed Klobiendar's capital at Dragonreach entirely. Melberior died in the casting.

The magic was so vast that it reverberated across the land, creating the Lyrical Forest above Dragonreach — an echo of the war, the souls of the fallen humming in the trees for thousands of years afterward.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text:
• Klobiendar was destroyed as a political entity. Its surviving dragons became Fallen Dragons.
  • Xi fell shortly after — its leader dead, its armies spent.
  • Fireborn, king of Klobiendar, became a Fallen Dragon bound to Dragonreach.
  • Goldenborn, son of Fireborn, was born in the ruins of his father's empire and would later found Baoth.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Melberior ] ├── Species: Dragon ├── Title: Dragon leader of Xi ├── Era: Pre-Age of Baoth ├── War: The Draconic War — launched suicide spell in final act ├── Destroyed: Klobiendar's capital at Dragonreach ├── Created: Lyrical Forest (magic reverberation) ├── Rival: Fireborn (king of Klobiendar) ├── Status: Deceased — died in the casting └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Mikhail
docs.text:
"I had a robot. She didn't have the government software. I had to hide her." — Mikhail, remembering

Mikhail was a man on dystopian Old Earth under the totalitarian regime of Sterman — the previous life of Emrys Eisenheart. He was the rebel who refused to comply, the man who ran into the wilderness with his illegal robot, and the one who accidentally slept through three million years in a Sterman Pod.

docs.title: The Dystopia
docs.text:
By the mid-21st century, the Shadow-engineered government had completed its takeover. CBDC money — programmable, revocable, surveilled — was the only legal tender. Every citizen carried a neural port. Sterman — the manufactured face of the regime, a god that watched everything — demanded compliance.

Mikhail owned a robot the state did not: Ichi, a companion unit running on local hardware, without the government surveillance software. Illegal by her very existence. He hid her. When inspections came, she powered down.

docs.title: The Flight
docs.text:
When the CBDC collapsed and the government demanded biometric compliance for survival rations, Mikhail did not negotiate. He left — into the wilderness, with Ichi and his closest friend Arkady. Government kill-drones hunted them.

Ichi was shot in the back — she took a round meant for him. He retrieved her remembrance cartridge, carried it in his port, and kept running.

docs.title: The Raid
docs.text:
Starving and desperate, Mikhail found a rebel rendezvous point on a dead man's body. He and Arkady were locked in a room, interrogated daily for a week, treated as infiltrators — until the rebels realized they were just two desperate men who had survived the wilderness.

On the front line of the raid on an AGI ship facility, Mikhail killed four guards without raising an alarm and turned off the lights. Thousands of rebels poured in. They took the ship and bombarded 24 locations across Earth. The uprising had begun.

docs.title: The Pods
docs.text:
Inside the ship: rows of cryogenic pods. Mikhail and Arkady chose two empty pods at the end of a row and lay down to rest. They did not close the doors. The ship malfunctioned. The doors slammed shut. Cryogenization initiated automatically.

The pods were Sterman Pods — designed to inject occupants with an experimental strain of the Black Agent. The two rebels slept while the agent entered their blood. Neither woke for three million years.

docs.title: The Rebirth
docs.text:
In 254 AGD, a volcano breached the bunker of The 157th Colony and freed the black agent into Ge'or's seas. It drifted for over three centuries — until it found a host in the Grimmel Republic in 596 AGD: Annika Eisenheart, of the Eisenheart bloodline.

In 597 AGD, the twins were born: Emrys Eisenheart and his sister Ichi Eisenheart. The man who refused to comply became the First Protagonist. The robot who took a bullet for him became his twin sister.

Chi was always going to follow him. She just needed a volcano.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Previous life of: Emrys
  • Companion: Ichi Eisenheart — robot, cartridge, twin sister
  • Closest friend: Arkady — the man who would become Lucien
  • Regime: Sterman
  • Pods: Sterman Pods
  • Rebirth: 597 AGD, Grimmel Republic
  • See: Emrys — Life Before Ge'or

docs.title: Narin Eisenheart
docs.text:
Narin Eisenheart (born 591 AGD) is the catmen catgirl who lives with the Eisenheart family, working as a cook and cleaner — 6 years old when the twins were born in 597 AGD. She carries the family name because she is treated as part of the family, not mere staff. She grew up alongside Emrys and Ichi Eisenheart.

Age 6 in 597 AGD — will be 19 in 610 AGD (13yr after present 597 AGD).

docs.title: 🌑 The Secret War
docs.text: Nethra did not die. She stepped into the shadows of the Shadows.

docs.title: 🏛️ The Founding of the Ironcloak
docs.text:
In the centuries after the explosion, Nethra secretly created the Ironcloak — an order dedicated to identifying and eliminating Hybrian influence on Ge'or. She fed them fragments of truth: enough to keep the flame alive, never enough to reveal her own existence. Her visions — spoken in the weeks after her transformation — were transcribed by the first followers and became the Nethrian Revelation, the Ironcloak's founding scripture and the source of their prophecy.

The Ironcloak worship her as their goddess. They do not know her true face.

docs.title: 🤫 The Inner Circle
docs.text: Only the upper echelon of the Ironcloak knows Nethra's identity. The rank and file believe she is a divine being — not a transformed demon princess walking among the very Shadows they hunt.

docs.title: 🎭 The Double Infiltration
docs.text:
The Erisian church constantly accused the Ironcloak of heresy. Eventually, they excommunicated them — but by that point, the Church was too corrupt and weak to execute anyone.

Nethra's greatest achievement: she operates inside the Shadow network itself, unknown to Rulfred and the Hybrians. They believe she died in the explosion. They are wrong.

docs.title: 🕸️ Factional Alignment
docs.text: [ Nethra ] ├── Father: Kirivis — The Demon King, Avenged ├── Brother: Maoth — Sacrificed for Her ├── Enemy: Rulfred — The Beast, Still Hunts Him ├── Enemy: Hybrians, Shadows — Infiltrated From Within ├── Prophecy Source: Lyrical Forest — Spirits of the Fallen ├── Weapon: Modified Shadow Device — Gift from 3,000,000 Years Ago (Soul-Will Miracle) ├── Transformed Into: A Different Type of Shadow — Neither Hybrian Nor Mortal ├── Founded: Ironcloak — Worshipped as Goddess ├── Scripture: Nethrian Revelation — Her visions, transcribed ├── Known By: Ironcloak Upper Echelon Only ├── Hiding From: Rulfred — Who Believes She Is Dead ├── Core Mechanism: Souls — The Gift Was Accumulated Soul-Will, Not Engineering ├── Hiding Among: The Shadows Themselves — Double Agent └── Status: Active — The Shadow Among Shadows

docs.title: Oleana Mortvagn
docs.text:
Oleana Mortvagn (born 594 AGD) is the youngest of the three Mortvagn sisters — 3 years old when Lucien was born in 597 AGD. The last of the sisters who tease him mercilessly.

Age 3 in 597 AGD — will be 16 in 610 AGD (13yr after present 597 AGD).

docs.title: Legacy
docs.text:
Omipre's story has become legend among the homunculi. Centuries of oral tradition have blurred the details — was Omipre male or female? Tall or short? Warrior or scholar? The homunculi do not agree, and they do not care. What matters is that someone led them out of the chaos.

The Homunculi Kingdom's religion — the belief in the Dark Moon God — traces its origin to Omipre's teachings. Whether Omipre genuinely believed in the Dark Moon God or simply created the faith to give the homunculi meaning is unknown. The homunculi do not question it. Faith, like Omipre's name, is a choice. And choice is sacred.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Omipre — The Unnamed ] ├── Species: Homunculi — liberated from Shadow control ├── Era: Post-421 BGD — after Baoth's destruction ├── Role: Founder and first leader of the Homunculi Kingdom ├── Origin: Woke to consciousness with no memories ├── First Act: Organized the scattered homunculi ├── Chose Name: Omipre — the first free choice ├── Legacy: Became legend — founder of the Dark Moon God faith └── Status: Historical — details lost to legend

docs.title: 🪙 Pitra
docs.text:
"The gods blessed him the day his coffers overflowed."

Pitra is the legendary figure behind Pitraism — the faith of the Silver Republic.

docs.title: The Legend
docs.text:
According to the faithful, Pitra was "blessed" by the gods after he became rich — and supposedly went on to live for hundreds of years. His story is the founding myth of the belief that the gods love money and gold: wealth is not a corruption but a blessing, and the wealthy are the visibly favored.

Whether Pitra truly existed is a question the Pitraist clergy does not encourage. The blessing, they say, is proof enough.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Pitra ] ├── Legend Of: Pitraism ├── Nation: Silver Republic ├── Claim: Blessed by the gods through wealth — lived hundreds of years ├── Lesson: The gods love money and gold └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Plenio
docs.text:
"Either we die in glory or live to see another day under honor." — Plenio, at the entrance to Dragonreach

Plenio was an elven adventurer who, alongside Diana and Korvald, encountered Julian the Dragon Tamer on the road from the Lyrical Forest to Dragonreach in 528 BGD.

docs.title: The Journey
docs.text:
Plenio and his companions initially didn't believe Julian's story — that a talking tree had told him to go to Dragonreach to find his murdered family. They joked about his situation but kept following, curious to see how he would meet his end.

At the entrance to Dragonreach, they asked: "You really want to do this?" Julian said yes and moved forward alone.

After a pause, Plenio spoke for all three: "Either we die in glory or live to see another day under honor." They followed him in.

docs.title: The Duel
docs.text: Inside Dragonreach, Fireborn appeared and challenged Julian to the Unjust Duel. Plenio, Diana, and Korvald hid in a cave, watching. After the ten-hour fight — when Julian reached one centimeter from Fireborn's core of life — Fireborn summoned them out and demanded they swear loyalty to Julian or die. They swore.

docs.title: The Rebellion
docs.text:
After Julian received the Sword of Xi and left Dragonreach, Plenio, Diana, and Korvald instigated the population to rise against Baoth and Dragon King Goldenborn. They led guerrilla warfare across the region, eventually settling in what became Northaxeland, where the population was most in favor of their cause.

Entire cities raised armies. Some declared independence from Baoth. Shuttil — Julian's birthplace, by then allied to Baoth — was the first to fall.

docs.title: Legacy
docs.text: Plenio, Diana, and Korvald became loyal servants of the Axel people, guiding them into the future. They helped formalize the Alegoria religion under Julian's legend and remained in Northaxeland for the rest of their lives.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Plenio ] ├── Species: Elf ├── Era: Active ~528 BGD ├── Companions: Diana, Korvald ├── Sworn to: Julian the Dragon Tamer ├── Opposed: Baoth, Goldenborn ├── Location: Dragonreach → Northaxeland ├── Legacy: Co-founder of Alegoria faith, liberator of the Axel people └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Princess Charlotte
docs.text: A princess of the Vennerian Trade Republic whose kidnapping by the Kingdom of Tiphar triggered the joint Venner-Lima invasion that caused Tiphar's collapse in 158 AGD. Her rescue was successful. The kingdom did not survive it. Anos was born from the ruins.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Status: Rescued — 158 AGD
  • Event: Kidnapping triggered the fall of Kingdom of Tiphar
  • Result: Anos Plutocracy founded from Tiphar's collapse

docs.title: Prophet Spasius
docs.text:
"The Prophet saw the Silver Light. We carry it forward."

Spasius was the founder of the Spasian Faith, emerging during the chaos of the Lost Era (399–300 BGD). He claimed to receive visions from The Silver Bride — the planetary ring encircling Ge'or — and preached that the ring was a divine message visible to all, requiring no priestly intermediaries to interpret.

docs.title: Life
docs.text:
Spasius appeared during the worst century of Ge'orian history. The destruction of Baoth in 421 BGD had thrown the continent into anarchy: warlords ruled, famine killed forty percent of the population, and the Erisian cult was only beginning to consolidate power.

According to the Argent Codex, Spasius was a wandering scholar who spent years in the wilderness of East Erisdar, studying the night sky. One night — the Codex does not specify a date — the Silver Bride appeared to him not as a band of light but as a voice. It spoke of a creator who had left the ring as a signature, a promise visible to all peoples across all lands, requiring no temple and no priest.

He began preaching in the villages of eastern Erisdar, gathering followers who called themselves the Argentines (from the ancient word for silver). His message resonated with people exhausted by chaos and hungry for a faith that required no institution — only open eyes.

docs.title: Teachings
docs.text:
• The ring is the creator's signature — divine, visible, universal. Anyone can see it. No one can control it.
  • No intermediaries — Spasius rejected the model of a church hierarchy mediating between the faithful and the divine. The ring speaks to everyone equally.
  • The Ring-Cycle — the ring's phases govern not just the liturgical calendar but the rhythms of life itself. Decisions, journeys, marriages — all are best undertaken under favorable conjunctions.

docs.title: Legacy
docs.text:
After Spasius's death (~310 BGD), his teachings were compiled into the Argent Codex, the sacred text of the Spasian Faith. The Council of Illuminants — a body of twenty-one high priests — was established to interpret the Codex and govern the faithful.

The faith he founded became the state religion of the Spasian Teocracy, with its capital at Spasia — the city named for its prophet.

The Pontificate of Eris considers Spasian doctrine heretical. The Spasian clergy consider the Erisians spiritually blind.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Prophet Spasius ] ├── Born: ~380 BGD ├── Died: ~310 BGD ├── Era: Age 9 — Age of Anarchy ├── Home: Spasia, East Erisdar ├── Species: Human ├── Founded: Spasian Faith ├── Sacred Text: Argent Codex (posthumous compilation) ├── Legacy: Council of Illuminants, the Ring-Cycle ├── Rival: Erisian church └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Rex Pollo IV
docs.text: The current Rex (leader) of the Vennerian Trade Republic, elected in 597 AGD. His election marks the beginning of what many expect to be the era in which Venner surpasses the Erisian Empire as the dominant power on Ge'or.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Rules: Vennerian Trade Republic
  • Elected: 597 AGD
  • Term: 10 years
  • Government: Maritime trade republic — elected by merchant-aristocracy

docs.title: 🌑 Current State
docs.text:
Rulfred now wears Goldenborn's body. The Shadows created the Leviathan from the war dead — with Kirivis's soul as its head — and unleashed it into the lake to enforce quarantine on the Ruins of Baoth.

He guards the ruins alongside the beast that carries the soul of the man he beheaded. A puppet wearing a king, waiting for the next move in a game measured in millions of years.

He does not know that Nethra survived. He does not know that she walks among the Shadows themselves.

docs.title: 🕸️ Factional Alignment
docs.text: [ Rulfred ] ├── True Identity: Shadow — Hybrian Agent ├── Former Rule: Old Earth — The Antichrist / The Beast ├── Alias: The Hero of Baoth — Propaganda Title ├── Betrayed: Kirivis — Beheaded Him ├── Current Body: Goldenborn's Corpse — Now Dragon Yaldabaoth ├── Original Body: Destroyed in the Baoth explosion (421 BGD) ├── Shapeshifts: Full dragon form ↔ human-like figure at will ├── Enemy: Nethra — Survived, Hunts Him Still ├── Enemy: Ironcloak — Unknowingly Serve His Enemy ├── Guarded By: Leviathan — Created from war dead, Kirivis's soul as head ├── Hates: Free Will, Individualism, Minds Outside the Hivemind ├── Philosophy: Hatred = Love, Kindness = Hate, Life = Death └── Status: Active — Waiting in the Ruins

docs.title: Sithia
docs.text: A catmen girl known to Masaaki Sytrenis in his youth, during the Human Age. Her abandonment of Sytrenis sent him alone to the mountain the party called Metrak — the journey that would become the turning point of his life and of the catmen's survival on Ge'or.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Sithia ] ├── Species: Catmen ├── Relation: The one who abandoned Masaaki Sytrenis ├── Role: Indirect catalyst of the Metrak journey └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🐍 Snake Goddess
docs.text:
"She made us. Her sons hold the world's corners."

The Snake Goddess is the deity of Sibbism — the founder of the Snake People species, and the mother of their bloodlines.

docs.title: Domain
docs.text:
• Origin — she made the snake people; every clutch hatched in the temple-hatcheries is held to be her continuing work.
  • Bloodlines — the matriarchal lines of both snake nations trace themselves to her.

docs.title: Her 24 Sons
docs.text: The goddess's 24 demigod sons are believed to run the 24 corners of the world — each son holding one corner in balance. The 24 corners are a myth, not geography: legless, dragging themselves across the earth, the snake people developed far more direction namings than humans — and the world's "corners" are the mythic expression of that fine-grained directional sense.

docs.title: Worship
docs.text:
• Nations: Xikxia and Zakarutia — both crowns worship her, though the sister-queens' feud is undimmed by the shared faith.
  • Practice: Ancestor veneration weaves through her rites — the spirits of dead queens are said to watch from the heat-shimmer of the desert sands.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Snake Goddess ] ├── Faith: Sibbism ├── Species: Snake People — she is their founder ├── Sons: 24 demigods — the 24 corners of the world (myth) ├── Nations: Xikxia, Zakarutia └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Sofia Mortvagn
docs.text:
Sofia Mortvagn (born 591 AGD) is the eldest of the three Mortvagn sisters — 6 years old when Lucien was born in 597 AGD. Like her sisters, she teases her quiet younger brother mercilessly.

Age 6 in 597 AGD — will be 19 in 610 AGD (13yr after present 597 AGD).

docs.title: The Elder
docs.text:
The prophet of the Machines who discovered the radio signal that launched the eternal war against The Hive.

Approximately 500,000 years ago, The Elder wandered the wasteland of Lung Continent and discovered an ancient bunker from the 157th Colony era. Inside, a machine powered by something in the soil emitted a light and a sound — a radio signal from the allied species fighting the Hybrians during The Last Great War.

The signal announced that a test species would be launched onto Ge'or. The Elder misunderstood. He believed humanity had sent the signal directly to the machines from the sky — a divine message. He returned to Brotherstar and proclaimed that if the machines held back the coming enemy, the humans would see them as worthy and return from the heavens.

The Elder's prophecy became the foundation of machine religion: humanism. The eternal war began when The Hive arrived shortly after.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Species: Machines
  • Era: ~500,000 years ago
  • Discovery: Radio signal from The Last Great War
  • Misinterpretation: Believed signal was divine message from sky gods (humans)
  • Legacy: Launched the eternal war against The Hive
  • Religion: Humanism — founded on The Elder's prophecy

docs.title: ☠️ The Highest
docs.text: "The faithful see a holy man. The Shadows see a glove."

docs.title: 🎭 Overview
docs.text: The Highest is the supreme leader of the Erisian church — elected by a council, revered by billions, and possessed by a Shadow from the moment of his election.

docs.title: 🔼 The Election
docs.text:
The Highest is chosen by a council of senior clergy (analogous to a papal conclave). The election is public ritual. The possession is not.

Every time a new Highest is elected, a Shadow takes his body. The man who was elected ceases to exist as an independent consciousness. His voice, his decisions, his edicts — all belong to the Shadow wearing his skin.

docs.title: 🕯️ The Council
docs.text: The council of electors is fully aware of the possession. They secretly worship the Shadows and are themselves evil — active participants in the deception of billions of faithful across Erisdar.

docs.title: 🎭 The Deception
docs.text: The faithful of the Erisian church do not know. They pray to Eris. The Shadow in the Highest's body answers. The religion is real to the worshipper. It is a weapon to the worshipped.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Role: Leader of the Erisian church
  • Elected by: The Council (Shadow-worshipping clergy)
  • Possessed by: Shadows — upon every election
  • Known to: Ironcloak (suspects), Hermes Kennensbach (suspects)
  • See: Erisian cult, Pontificate of Eris, Erisian Theocracy

docs.title: The Two Protagonists
docs.text:
Born twelve kilometers apart. Bound by three million years of war. They don't know yet.

The two protagonists of the Ge'or story are Emrys and Lucien — born in 597 AGD in the Grimmel Republic, twelve kilometers apart. They are the fulfillment of a prophecy spoken by the Lyrical Forest spirits over four hundred years ago. They are the anchors of quintillions of dead souls seeking justice. They are five minutes old when the story begins.

docs.title: Emrys
docs.text:
Emrys is the first son of a Northaxeland mother from an adventurer family. His father's details are unrecorded. He grows up with the instincts of a hunter — watchful, patient, quick to act.

At age six, he encounters a girl named Amelia carrying a weapon that should not exist on Ge'or: a Pulse Rifle from the Glorious Alliance crash. The moment he sees it, past-life memory breaks through:

"What the fuck is this pulse rifle doing here."

Amelia corrects him — it's a lightning bow. He doesn't let it go. He follows her for three months, obsessed with understanding how a relic from the Last Great War ended up in a child's hands in Grimmel. When she falls into a ravine and ten Goblins surround her, he kills them all with a lightning spell — age six.

He will later marry a beastmen wife and have a catgirl companion. But that is years away. Right now, he is a boy who remembers a war he should not remember, holding a recognition he cannot explain.

docs.title: Lucien
docs.text:
Lucien is the fourth child of an Erisian Empire mother and a Grimmel father. He has three older sisters who tease him mercilessly. He grows up quieter than Emrys — the kind of child who watches before speaking, who learned early that the fourth child's opinion is rarely asked for.

His name means light. His mother chose it. She believed in brighter things.

Less is known of Lucien's early years. He and Emrys will find each other — the black agent ensures it. Two children with the highest magical potential on the planet, born in the same year, in the same republic, twelve kilometers apart. The universe did not leave this to chance.

docs.title: The Hope Goddess Vision
docs.text:
Before either protagonist opened their eyes in the new world, they experienced the same vision. Both were transported — naked, disoriented — to a bright, electricity-like dimension where everything was luminous.

A figure called herself the Hope Goddess. She explained:

  • Life was dying. The Shadows were carrying out a hostile takeover — not of the physical universe, but of the hope realm — the soul substrate of reality itself.
  • The Hybrian collective consciousness was still alive, tormented in the Fortress Planet, locked in eternal suffering.
  • That suffering was not justice. The Shadows were using it as an anchor to extend their influence into the soul substrate — the one domain they had never fully controlled.
  • Behind the Hope Goddess, darkness was visibly entering the room. The war in the hope realm was already being lost.

Her final words were a warning and a mission: they must find a way to finish off the hivemind locked in the Fortress Planet. Even from a medieval world with no technology, no knowledge of the war, no memory of who they had been — they were the only hope.

Then they woke up. Infants. Crying. No memory of the vision — but the weight of who they were remained. Past-life knowledge, buried beneath infant consciousness, waiting to surface.

Emrys's recognition of the pulse rifle at age six is the first crack. The memories are still there. They are waking up.

docs.title: Power Level
docs.text:
The black agent did not merely ensure their birth. It granted them immense magical potential — raw capability in the top 0.001% of all living beings on Ge'or.

This is not trained skill. It is not knowledge. It is potential — the biological capacity for magic so vast that it exceeds even Hermes Kennensbach, the Emperor of the Erisian Empire, who is himself one of the most powerful mages alive. The protagonists, if trained, could reshape the world.

But they are children. They do not know what they are. They do not know why they are here.

docs.title: The Soul Connection
docs.text:
The experimentation on their original bodies three million years ago did more than preserve their DNA. It connected them to the soul substrate of reality — the same domain where quintillions of dead souls have been accumulating willpower since the Last Great War. The same souls that gave Nethra the gift that destroyed Baoth.

The protagonists are not merely powerful mages. They are anchors — living conduits between the physical world and the accumulated hope of every being the Shadows ever killed.

docs.title: The Prophecy
docs.text:
The Lyrical Forest spirits told Nethra that two heroes would come — not of this world, not of this time. The prophecy has been waiting for over 400 years. The two heroes have arrived. They are five minutes old.

They are named Emrys and Lucien. The tree spirits did not know their names. They only knew they were coming.

But the prophecy only tells half the story. Before they were Emrys and Lucien, they were Mikhail and Arkady — two rebels on a dystopian Old Earth who captured an AGI ship, were accidentally sealed in Sterman Pods, injected with an experimental black agent, and cryogenized for three million years. They did not come from prophecy alone. They came from a friendship that refused to die. See: Emrys — Life Before Ge'or

docs.title: The Third Protagonist
docs.text:
The prophecy spoke of two. But the black agent carried three.

Ichi Eisenheart — Emrys's twin sister, born moments after him — was not part of the Lyrical Forest's vision. She was a sentient robot on Old Earth, Mikhail's companion, who took a bullet for him and whose consciousness survived in the black agent for three million years. The black agent gave her a human soul. She possessed the mother before birth and made sure her name would be spoken again.

The prophecy was incomplete. The tree spirits saw two heroes because they were looking for humans. They did not know to look for a machine that learned to love one.

docs.title: Amelia — The Third Element
docs.text:
Amelia, born 598 AGD, is not a protagonist. She is not prophesied. She is not a soul-anchor or a black-agent vessel.

She is a girl with a Pulse Rifle and a dead father.

But her weapon is the proof Emrys needs. Without Amelia's lightning bow, Emrys might never trust his own memories — might dismiss the flickers of another life as dreams. The pulse rifle is the smoking gun of the Last Great War, still firing, cradled in the arms of a tsundere in a blue maid dress.

She is essential. The prophecy did not mention her. The prophecy was incomplete.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ The Two Protagonists ] ├── Origin: The 157th Colony — black DNA agent, 3,000,000 years old ├── Trigger: Glorious Alliance crash ~15,000 BGD ├── Born: 597 AGD — Grimmel Republic, 12 km apart ├── Emrys: First son — mother Annika (Northaxeland adventurer), father Marco, second wife Camillia, servant Narin — family name Eisenheart ├── Lucien: Fourth child — mother Herennia (Erisian Empire), father Gallio (Grimmel) — family name Mortvagn — sisters Sofia, Donna, Oleana ├── Vision: Hope Goddess — warning of Shadow takeover of the soul substrate ├── Mission: Destroy the hivemind in the Fortress Planet ├── Power: Top 0.001% magical potential — exceeds Hermes Kennensbach ├── Soul Connection: Linked to quintillions of dead seeking justice ├── Prophecy: The Two Heroes — foretold by Lyrical Forest spirits ~420 BGD ├── First Memory Crack: Emrys recognizes Amelia's Pulse Rifle at age 6 ├── Essential Ally: Amelia — keeper of the pulse rifle, born 598 AGD ├── Age: Infants at story start — no memory, no training, no knowledge └── Status: Alive — the story begins with twins and a pulse rifle

docs.title: 🧭 Tino the Explorer
docs.text: "He was bankrupt. He stole a boat. He found a continent."

docs.title: 🎭 Overview
docs.text: Tino the Explorer was a Vennerian merchant who, having lost everything to bankruptcy in 170 AGD, stole a vessel and sailed into the unknown. What he found changed the world: the continent of Lumina Continent, previously unknown to Erisdar.

docs.title: 🚢 The Voyage
docs.text:
Tino's desperation made him reckless — and reckless made him legendary. He sailed west from South Erisdar into waters no Vennerian captain had dared cross.

The distances were vast. Ge'or is 1.37× the size of Old Earth — the sea between Erisdar and Lumina far exceeds any ocean crossing attempted on Earth during its Age of Discovery. Tino survived through a combination of luck, skill, and sheer refusal to die.

docs.title: 🏆 Legacy
docs.text:
Tino's discovery ignited the Great Ascension of Trade — the era that transformed the Vennerian Trade Republic, the Anos Plutocracy, and Sousu from regional powers into intercontinental commercial empires.

He never became rich. But he became immortal.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Origin: Vennerian Trade Republic
  • Discovery: Lumina Continent continent (170 AGD)
  • Result: The Great Ascension of Trade
  • Status: Legendary figure in Vennerian maritime culture

docs.title: Tiodorus
docs.text:
Tiodorus is a god of Maomism, the creation faith of the Maoma Tribe on the Lumina Continent. With his sister Anedoris, he shaped the beastmen from the ashes of the world and sent them forth to rule over all the forests of Ge'or — making the beastmen the gods' chosen rulers of the world's rainforests.

In the reformed canon of Maomism, the Gigas Tribe are the enemies of Tiodorus — come to destroy the rainforests of the world.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Tiodorus ] ├── Faith: Maomism ├── Kin: Anedoris — sister, co-creator ├── Creation: The beastmen, from the ashes, to rule the forests of Ge'or ├── Enemy (reformed canon): Gigas Tribe └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: ⚔️ Tissas — God of War
docs.text:
"He counts the fallen. He does not mourn them."

Tissas is the god of war in the Helism pantheon of Dissenbarg.

docs.title: Domain
docs.text:
• War — battle, courage, discipline, and the fortunes of armies.
  • He is neither cruel nor merciful: he is simply the weight of war itself.

docs.title: Patron Of
docs.text:
• Tissas — the highland realm that bears his name, holding the mountain passes between Dissenbarg's east and west.
  • Komme — the Anos-held city, sworn with Anos to liberate Taberis.
  • Johannstadt — the Venner-held land, formerly Taberis.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text: Helism's gods are beings of human shape and human passions. Soldiers swear oaths in Tissas's name before campaigns, and the mountain passes of the Tissas realm are dotted with his shrines. The nations that honor him — feuding though they are — all keep his image on their banners.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Tissas — God of War ] ├── Pantheon: Helism ├── Domain: War ├── Patron: Tissas, Komme, Johannstadt ├── Region: Dissenbarg └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Trurdrang Emberflare
docs.text: A kobold adventurer of the Human Age and one of the companions of Masaaki Sytrenis. Alongside the catmen Hogryr Aledini and the human Laudlaern Kenismov, he helped save Sytrenis's life at the edge of a mountain and joined the quest recorded in the The Great Epic of the Heroes of Donblond'werv — including the confrontation with the waking Metrak.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Trurdrang Emberflare ] ├── Species: Kobolds ├── Party: Masaaki Sytrenis, Hogryr Aledini, Laudlaern Kenismov ├── Deeds: Recorded in the The Great Epic of the Heroes of Donblond'werv └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🐍 Xanob
docs.text:
"The first coil is still tightening."

Xanob is the demigod father-founder of all Snake People — the most prayed-upon figure in Moplilly, the ancestor-veneration cult of Kobra on Marti Continent.

docs.title: The Progenitor
docs.text:
Xanob is the ancestor of all of them — the first snake person to coil, to lay, to rule. Every snake person — whether in Kobra (Marti, cold-adapted subrace), Xikxia (West Erisdar), or Zakarutia (Demon Continent) — is his blood.

Though the three snake nations separated thousands of years ago, and Kobra's lineage ended up cold-adapted in Marti, all still trace to Xanob.

docs.title: Veneration
docs.text: In Moplilly, all ancestors are honored, but Xanob is supreme. Prayers ascend through the lineage: child to parent to grandparent to Xanob. His coil is the sacred geometry; his name is the first word at egg-blessings.

docs.title: The Kobra Reading
docs.text: The Kobra reading of Xanob is distinct: Xanob's final gift was cold. He taught his Marti children to endure the frigid climate that would kill their warm-blooded cousins, so serpent-kind could hold the north. Winter fasting honors this.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Moplilly
  • Nation: Kobra (Marti Continent, cold-adapted)
  • Species: Snake People (all lineages)
  • Kin Nations: Xikxia, Zakarutia (same race, separated thousands of years ago)
  • Related: Sibbism (cousin faith, different god Snake Goddess)

docs.title: The Ship's Fate
docs.text:
After Xiumi's escape, Mad-Dog was revealed to be a Shadow. His plan to destroy the ship had failed because of a twelve-year-old girl. He faced a fire squad and died.

The Glorious Alliance crossed the event horizon and emerged millions of years later, ~15,000 BGD, in front of Ge'or. The surviving 12 million celebrated — until they realized they were on a collision course with the planet. They had one week.

Escape pods were built for 4 million. Young men, children, and young women were prioritized. All species boarded. The ship hit Ge'or, killing the remaining 8,000,000.

The impact also struck a small moon of Ge'or — destroying it. The debris from the ship and the shattered moon eventually formed The Silver Bride — the planetary ring that now defines Ge'or's sky.

The crash triggered ice ages, acid rains, earthquakes, and meteor showers. All knowledge was lost. Age 1 — Nomadism began.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Xiumi ] ├── Era: ~1,200,000 years ago — aboard the Glorious Alliance ├── Age: ~12 years old ├── Encountered: Hope Goddess — received mission ├── Action: Pressed the red button — saved the ship from the black hole ├── Escape: Crossed event horizon in escape pod ├── Landed: Lung Continent — near The 157th Colony ruins ├── Injection: Original Black Agent — soul split into three ├── Soul Fragment 1: Spirit protector of Lung Continent ├── Soul Fragment 2: Black dust → Nethra — abandoned on Western Erisdar shore ├── Soul Fragment 3: Infiltrated Shadow realm — reunited with Nethra after her death ├── Enemy: Captain Mad-Dog — revealed as Shadow ├── Legacy: Nethra, Ironcloak, the war against the Shadows └── Ship's Fate: Crashed into Ge'or ~15,000 BGD, creating The Silver Bride

docs.title: 🐺 Xuashi
docs.text:
"The chief who became the only."

Xuashi is the god of Xuashism — the recent faith of the Wolvesfolk nations Kut and Oigopol on Marti Continent and Kyuu on Xeti Continent.

docs.title: From Pantheon Chief to Sole God
docs.text: Xuashi was once the main god of the old animistic-pagan pantheon of the wolvesfolk — chief among many spirits of river, hunt, and pack. In a recent theological revolution (within the last centuries), wolvesfolk theologians promoted Xuashi to sole supreme deity — the old pantheon became his court, his pack.

docs.title: Incarnation as Eris
docs.text:
The core mystery of Xuashism: Xuashi incarnated in Erisdar as Eris — the fabricated goddess of the Erisian Church.

To Xuashists, Eris is not a Shadow fabrication but Xuashi in borrowed flesh. Because Xuashi-as-Eris founded the Erisian Church, and the Church birthed or opposed every other faith, Xuashi is the father and mother of all other religions on Ge'or — every prayer, even to other gods, ultimately reaches Xuashi.

This is not a metaphor to Xuashists. It is literal.

docs.title: Followers
docs.text:
• Kut, Oigopol (Marti Continent) and Kyuu (Xeti Continent) — Wolvesfolk nations, Xuashist.
  • Wolvesfolk minority in Germina.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Xuashism
  • Nations: Kut, Oigopol, Kyuu
  • Species: Wolvesfolk
  • Incarnation: Eris (Erisian Church)
  • Related: Wolvesfolk pack culture, Moonfang Union slave trade

docs.title: 🔼 Evolution into the Church
docs.text:
Over centuries, the cult: - Grew in membership, attracting genuine believers. - Developed the The Eris Saga as its sacred text. - Established the Pontificate of Eris as its political arm. - Renamed the continent from Donblond'werv to Erisdar.

The cult became the Church. But the Shadows never left its core.

docs.title: ☠️ The Highest — Shadow Puppet
docs.text:
The leader of the Erisian Church is called The Highest, elected by a council (similar to a pope). But the election is a lie: every time a new Highest is chosen, a Shadow possesses his body. The council is fully aware — they secretly worship the Shadows and are themselves evil, actively deceiving billions of faithful across Erisdar.

The faithful pray to their god. The god answers through a corpse piloted by a million-year-old philosopher who sees humanity as livestock.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Erisian Cult ] ├── Founded: ~−400 BAC ├── Created By: Hybrians, Shadows, Homunculi ├── Became: Erisian church ├── Tool: Myth of Eris, The Eris Saga ├── Political Arm: Pontificate of Eris └── Known To: Ironcloak — Suspects the truth

docs.title: 👑 Elvish Kingdoms
docs.text: The elvish kingdoms refers collectively to the elven political entities of Erisdar — historically divided across the continent, decimated during the Great Elvish Persecution, and partially restored as the Restored Elvish States.

docs.title: The Three Restored States
docs.text:
• Elvennrin — cultural and spiritual heart
  • Elvenkrad — fortress-state and military shield
  • Sousu — southern mercantile state

docs.title: Lost Kingdoms
docs.text:
Several elven territories were never restored after the near-extinction of the Elves, their names surviving only in fragmentary records.

See: Restored Elvish States, Great Elvish Persecution, near-extinction of the Elves

docs.title: 🤝 Diplomacy
docs.text: Entry pending.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Elvish States ] ├── Nations: Elvennrin, Elvenkrad, Sousu ├── Preceded By: Elvengar — Destroyed in Great Divergence ├── Persecution: Great Elvish Persecution ├── Homeland: Maemon in Luzia on Merratodoni ├── Oppressor: Erisian church └── Era: Post-persecution, post-AGD

docs.title: Kennensbach
docs.text: The ruling dynasty of the Erisian Empire, seated in the Archduchy of the Kennberg. Its most prominent member is Hermes Kennensbach Emperor of the Erisian Empire, The King Sorcerer, and Archduke of the Kennberg.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Seat: Archduchy of the Kennberg
  • Current Ruler: Hermes Kennensbach
  • Empire: Erisian Empire
  • Near: valley of Kenn the great

docs.title: 50–100 Year Transition
docs.text: Following the convention of Ge'orian age transitions, the Lost Era formally ends around −14,000 BGD — a generational buffer after the first tribes left the Formingar Ocean region. The shift into Age 1 was not a single event but a slow dispersal across centuries.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Age 0 — The Lost Era ] ├── Preceded By: Nothing — First age of Ge'or ├── Succeeded By: Age 1 — Age of Nomadism ├── Caused By: Glorious Alliance — Crash of ancient battleship ├── Location: Formingar Ocean — Initial survivor settlement ├── Sole Record: Archive of the Traveler — Dragon-guarded repository ├── Carried Species: Humans, Elves, Dwarves, Dragons, Demons └── Full Timeline: Ages of Ge'or

docs.title: The Loss of Knowledge
docs.text:
Knowledge was lost within a few generations. Written records on paper had survived the crash, but in the chaos of survival, they were not treasured. Languages fragmented. The ability to read was lost. Eventually, every written document was destroyed by time, weather, and barbarism.

Oral traditions replaced writing. The first stories — of the great winged ancestors, of the fire from the sky, of the endless walking — were told around campfires. These would eventually become the foundation myths of every Ge'orian civilization. But they were myths now. The truth of the Glorious Alliance, the Last Great War, and Old Earth was gone.

docs.title: The Great Dispersal
docs.text:
Over hundreds of years, the scattered survivors found their places in the world:

  • Asian-looking humans — due to their physical differences from the Caucasian-majority survivors — migrated eastward across the continent, eventually reaching the Sun Archipelago and Tabontabar Continent, where they would found the cultures of the South Sun Empire, Northern Kingdom, Central Kingdom, and Southern Kingdom.
  • Demons migrated westward, drawn to the volcanic regions and the black-glass-scarred lands that would become the Demon Continent.
  • Dwarves went to the mountains — drawn underground by instinct, seeking caves and mineral veins.
  • Elves gravitated toward forest areas, finding refuge among the ancient trees of what would become the Lyrical Forest, the Mystical Forest, and the great woodlands of Merratodoni.
  • Humans (the Caucasian-majority population) stayed in the central regions, spreading along coasts and plains, building the first fragile settlements that would eventually become Erisdar's civilizations.
  • Beastmen eventually reached Lumina Continent — a jungle continent where their physical strength and tribal instincts gave them an advantage over other species.
  • Catmen — as always — went everywhere, adapting to every environment, welcomed by all.

The species did not yet know of each other's survival. Each believed they were alone. Each developed separately for nearly two thousand years.

docs.title: The End of Age 1
docs.text: By approximately 14,000 BGD, the scattered tribes had settled into distinct territories and grown large enough to encounter one another once more. What followed was Age 2 — and the first contact between species.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Age 1 — The Age of Nomadism ] ├── Preceded By: The Glorious Alliance crash (~15,000 BGD) ├── Succeeded By: Age 2 — Age of First Tribes ├── Cause: Crash cataclysm — acid rains, nuclear winter, famines ├── Species: All allied species dispersed — each found their continent ├── Asian Migration: Eastward → Tabontabar, Sun Archipelago ├── Demon Migration: Westward → Demon Continent ├── Dwarven Migration: Mountains and caves ├── Elven Migration: Forests ├── Beastmen Migration: Lumina Continent (jungle) ├── Human Settlement: Central coasts and plains → future Erisdar ├── Lost Knowledge: Written language, the common ship tongue, all records ├── Replaced By: Oral traditions — the first myths └── Full Timeline: Ages of Ge'or, Complete Timeline

docs.title: The Eve of Cataclysm
docs.text:
By the end of Age 10, the Erisian Church was the most powerful institution on Erisdar. The Shadows believed their plan was back on track. The Church would provide the ideological legitimacy, the Empire would provide the military force, and together they would achieve what Baoth had failed to do.

They did not know the Glorious Alliance reactor was about to fail.

In Year 0, the reactor malfunctioned. The Great Divergence reshaped the world. Everything the Shadows had built was thrown into chaos — and would have to be rebuilt in Age 11.

docs.title: Connections

docs.title: The Present (597 AGD)
docs.text:
The present year is 597 AGD — nearly six centuries after the Divergence. The world has stabilized, but the cracks are showing:

  • The Erisian Empire is decaying despite the efforts of Emperor Hermes.
  • The Vennerian Trade Republic is poised to surpass it.
  • The Shadows prepare Armageddon — simultaneous ice age, goblin invasion, Groom detonation, and Church prophecy.
  • The two protagonists — Emrys and Lucien, born this year in the Grimmel Republic, 12 kilometers apart — are infants. Emrys was born with a twin sister: Ichi Eisenheart, the third protagonist, a former AI granted a human soul by the black agent. Three years from now, Lucien's little sister Mana — another former AI — will be born. They know nothing of the war they were born to fight. One year later, Amelia will be born — the girl whose Pulse Rifle will crack Emrys's past-life memory open.

docs.title: The End of Age 11
docs.text: Age 11 is projected to end around 610 AGD, when the current status quo breaks and the events of the protagonist's story reshape the world. What follows will be Age 12 — yet to be written.

docs.title: Open Thread
docs.text:
• The Claim: very late in their lives, the twinned discover the Black Agent Hivemind can reach through their blood. The counter has not been found (see The Twinning). This Age must answer how they win over it.
  • The world endures. Mikhail and Chi will live this age — and the ages after it. Age 12 is lived, not terminal; the story culminates here, but the world continues (future ages follow). The ending is not the destination; the living is.
  • The prison stirs. By 597 AGD the Union notices disturbances in the prison planet — the Shadows remain linked to their hivemind, and their growing power may one day become an escape attempt.
