docs.title: The Demons' Enmity
docs.text:
The Demons were the most aggressive species during this age. Their warrior nature — later refined into honor and asceticism — was raw and untamed in Age 2. Demon tribes expanded rapidly, taking territory by force. This earned them enmity from other species — a reputation for violence that would follow them for millennia.

The seeds of the later demon stigma were planted here. Not because demons were evil. Because they were strong, and strength in a tribal world means conquest.

docs.title: Stabilization
docs.text:
The apocalyptic aftermath of the crash — acid rains, nuclear winter, poisoned water — finally began to subside. The skies cleared. The climate stabilized. Crops could be grown reliably. Population growth accelerated.

By 9,000 BGD, the tribes had grown large enough and organized enough to begin something new: civilization.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Age 2 — The Age of First Tribes ] ├── Span: ~10,999 to 9,000 BGD ├── Preceded By: Age 1 — Age of Nomadism ├── Succeeded By: Age 3 — Age of First Empires ├── Key Feature: First permanent tribal societies ├── Conflict: Inter-tribal warfare over resources ├── Demons: Most aggressive — earned lasting enmity ├── Climate: Crash aftermath subsiding — skies clearing └── Full Timeline: Ages of Ge'or, Complete Timeline

docs.title: The First Agricultural Kingdoms
docs.text:
With stable climate and growing populations, agriculture became the foundation of power. Across Ge'or:

  • On the Demon Continent, the first agricultural kingdoms appeared — demon-ruled city-states built around volcanic soil that proved surprisingly fertile once the glassing residue was tilled under.
  • On Erisdar and the surrounding regions, human and elven settlements grew into organized kingdoms with defined borders, irrigation systems, and ruling dynasties.
  • On Tabontabar, the Asian-branch humans began their long development toward the imperial cultures that would one day define the continent.
  • Elvengar — the first great elven kingdom on Kutten — began its rise during this age, though its golden era would come later.

These were not empires in the later sense. They were city-states and small kingdoms — fragile, experimental, learning how to govern through trial and catastrophic error.

docs.title: The Pattern Begins
docs.text:
Age 3 established the pattern that would define Ge'orian history: species developing separately, building civilizations in isolation, unaware of — or indifferent to — each other's existence. The Demons built their first kingdoms in the west. The Elves tended their forests. The Humans spread along the coasts. The Dwarves dug deeper into the mountains.

They would meet again. When they did, it would change everything.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Age 3 — The Age of First Empires ] ├── Span: ~8,999 to 7,000 BGD ├── Preceded By: Age 2 — Age of First Tribes ├── Succeeded By: Age 4 — Dragon Tyranny ├── Key Achievement: Invention of writing ├── Civilization: First agricultural kingdoms on Demon Continent, Erisdar, and Tabontabar ├── Elvengar: Began its rise on Kutten ├── Writing Systems: Demonic runes, elven script, human cuneiform, Tabontabar logographs └── Full Timeline: Ages of Ge'or, Complete Timeline

docs.title: The Twelve Dragon Clans
docs.text:
Dragon society was organized into twelve great clans, each ruling a territory:

  • Xi — the most powerful clan, dominating eastern Erisdar.
  • Klobiendar — western Erisdar, rivals to Xi.
  • Dragomorph — the Lumina Continent, jungle-tamers.
  • Soroben — the Demon Continent, hardened by the black lands.
  • Eight other clans, each with their own domains and rivalries.

Between them, they commanded 90% of Ge'or. Nothing moved without a dragon's permission.

docs.title: The Death Wars
docs.text:
The twelve clans did not coexist. They fought death wars — conflicts of total annihilation where the goal was not conquest but extinction. Armies of hundreds of thousands — dragons, enslaved soldiers, conscripted species — clashed across continents. Dragons themselves took to the skies, raining fire on each other's territories.

The wars destroyed vast areas of every continent: - Forests burned for decades. - Mountains were shattered by draconic combat. - Civilizations that had taken millennia to build were erased in hours.

The dragons were exceptional at building empires. They were even better at destroying them.

docs.title: The Retreat
docs.text:
By the end of Age 4, the dragon population had collapsed. The death wars had killed most of them. Those who survived looked at the ashes of their civilization and repented.

The surviving dragons withdrew from the world. They abandoned empire-building and adopted a contemplative, ascetic lifestyle — the seeds of the honor-based culture that would eventually flourish in Kramsadar.

Some dragons were not born into civilized clans. These became wild dragons — hostile, territorial, uncivilized. They guard treasures in remote lairs, secluding themselves in mountains and caves. They are the dragons of legend: beasts to be hunted, monsters to be feared.

The civilized dragons — the descendants of the clans who repented — are nearly extinct. Kramsadar on Marti Continent is their last sanctuary.

docs.title: The Lost History
docs.text: The Dragon Tyranny's greatest casualty was history itself. The death wars destroyed most records from Age 3 and earlier. What little survived the crash of the Glorious Alliance was burned in dragon fire. The early history of every species was reduced to oral tradition and fragments.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Age 4 — The Dragon Tyranny ] ├── Span: ~6,999 to 5,500 BGD ├── Preceded By: Age 3 — Age of First Empires ├── Succeeded By: Age 5 — Dwarf Era ├── Dominant Species: Dragons — ruled 90% of Ge'or ├── Twelve Clans: Xi, Klobiendar, Dragomorph, Soroben + eight others ├── Death Wars: Inter-clan warfare drove dragons to near-extinction ├── Enslavement: Other species forced to build monuments and worship dragons ├── Aftermath: Civilized dragons retreated to contemplation; wild dragons remain ├── Legacy: Most pre-Age 4 history destroyed └── Last Sanctuary: Kramsadar on Marti Continent

docs.title: The Romanium Economy
docs.text:
The foundation of this prosperity was Romanium — a perfect metal, almost indestructible, that held an edge forever. A sword made of Romanium would never dull, never rust, never break. Armor forged from it was impenetrable. Tools crafted from it lasted for generations.

Dwarven mines produced Romanium in abundance, and dwarven forges turned it into the finest manufactured goods on Ge'or:

  • Weapons — swords, axes, spears of legendary quality.
  • Tools — hammers, chisels, plows that never wore out.
  • Magical items and staffs — the most efficient ever created, their enchantments preserved in Romanium's perfect crystalline structure.
  • Commodities — everyday goods of a quality no other species could match.

During the Dwarf Era, gold, food, and silver were as cheap as water. Everyone — human, elf, demon — had access to high-quality manufactured goods. The standard of living across the known world was higher than at any point since the Glorious Alliance.

docs.title: The Slow Decline
docs.text:
Prosperity is fragile. Romanium was the foundation, and Romanium was finite.

As ore reserves began to dwindle, the economy entered a slow, grinding decline. It was not a sudden catastrophe. It was a generation-by-generation erosion — mines producing less each year, prices rising, trade routes shrinking. Dwarven cities that had bustled with commerce grew quiet. Forges that had burned for centuries went cold.

The dwarves tried to adapt — deeper mines, more efficient extraction, recycling old Romanium. None of it was enough. The ore was running out, and with it, the foundation of their civilization.

docs.title: The Golden War
docs.text:
As dwarven power weakened, others saw opportunity. Human nomads from West and North Erisdar — mounted on horses (descendants of animals carried aboard the Glorious Alliance) — began raiding dwarven territories.

What started as raids became a war. The Golden War — named for the wealth the nomads sought — swept across the declining dwarven realms. Dwarven outposts were overrun. Trade caravans were ambushed. The megacities, once impenetrable, became islands in a sea of raiders.

The dwarves survived. But their age was over.

docs.title: Legacy — The Legendary Relics
docs.text:
Items from the Dwarf Era are considered legendary relics in the present day. They command insane prices on the black market and in the collections of emperors and merchant princes. A verified Dwarf Era blade is worth more than a kingdom's annual tax revenue.

The qualities that made them legendary:

  • Romanium swords — indestructible. They will never lose their edge, never rust, never break. A Dwarf Era blade found in a tomb after five thousand years will be as sharp as the day it was forged.
  • Romanium armor — impenetrable by conventional weapons. Surviving sets are priceless.
  • Magical items and staffs — the most efficient ever created. Modern mages who wield Dwarf Era artifacts are universally recognized as the most powerful practitioners alive. The Romanium's crystalline structure somehow preserves and amplifies enchantments in ways that modern craftsmen cannot replicate.

The Dwarves of the present day remember this age with pride and sorrow. They once built a world. They lost it to geology and raiders.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Age 5 — The Dwarf Era ] ├── Span: ~5,499 to 4,500 BGD ├── Preceded By: Age 4 — Dragon Tyranny ├── Succeeded By: Age 6 — Iron Age ├── Dominant Species: Dwarves — megacities, global trade ├── Foundation: Romanium — perfect metal, now nearly extinct ├── Golden War: Human horse-nomad raiders from West/North Erisdar ├── Legacy: Legendary relics — indestructible weapons, perfect magical items ├── Centers: Dwarvengor + underground megacities worldwide ├── Economy: Unprecedented prosperity — gold, food, silver as cheap as water └── Cause of Decline: Romanium depletion — slow, generational, irreversible

docs.title: 50–100 Year Transition
docs.text: With Romanium gone, the dwarves retreated deeper into their mountains. The surface species were forced to fall back on iron — an inferior metal, abundant but crude. It was a technological downgrade, a civilizational shame. The Age 6 — Iron Age was not an advancement. It was the best anyone could do with what was left.

docs.title: The Rise of the Elves
docs.text:
While other species struggled, the Elves thrived.

They were a nature-attuned people. They did not need dwarven goods. They did not depend on the old civilization model of mines and forges and industrial supply chains. Their strength came from the land itself — forests provided shelter, rivers provided water, the soil provided food. While dwarves and humans scraped for iron, the elves built.

Elvengar — the first great elven kingdom — was founded during this age on the continent of Kutten. The elves turned Kutten into a fortress — a bastion of elven power that no other species could breach.

From there, they expanded. Elvengar conquered parts of the Demon Continent and West Erisdar, extending elven influence across the known world. For the first time since the Dragon Tyranny, a single species dominated Ge'or — but unlike the dragons, the elves built beauty rather than monuments to themselves.

docs.title: The Elvish Golden Age
docs.text:
The Iron Age was also the Elvish Age. While others fought over scraps of iron, the elves created a civilization of stunning beauty:

  • Gardens — vast, intricate landscapes of flowers, trees, and winding paths, designed to be walked through for days without seeing the same view twice.
  • Mazes — living puzzles of hedgerow and stone, some of which still exist and are considered sacred sites.
  • Architecture — flowing, organic structures that seemed to grow from the ground rather than be built upon it.
  • Art — paintings, sculptures, and textiles of a quality that has never been matched. Elvish art from this era is incredibly valued in the present day. A single Age 6 elven tapestry can buy a city.

The elves built across all of Erisdar. Their gardens, their mazes, their temples dotted every region. For a thousand years, the world was theirs.

docs.title: The Fall — The Hybrian Crash
docs.text:
The official end of Age 6 is recorded as 3,000 BGD. The true end is 2,989 BGD.

In that year, the Hybrian spaceship fell from the sky like a meteor and crashed in Pontus, in eastern Erisdar. The impact caused massive destruction across the eastern continent. Earthquakes. Firestorms. A plume of debris that darkened the sky.

Refugees from eastern Erisdar flooded westward. In the chaos, human armies invaded elven territories by force, overwhelming Elvengar's defenses. The elves were pushed back to Kutten, their empire shattered, their golden age ended.

The fall of the Hybrian ship was the single most consequential event of the age — and nobody on Ge'or knows it was a ship. The survivors saw a meteor. A fire from the sky. A divine punishment, perhaps. The truth — that it was a vessel carrying the same enemy that had consumed galaxies — would not be known for thousands of years.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Age 6 — The Iron Age / The Elvish Age ] ├── Span: ~4,499 to 2,989 BGD ├── Preceded By: Age 5 — Dwarf Era ├── Succeeded By: Age 8 — Age of Baoth ├── Key Event: Founding of Elvengar — the first great elven kingdom ├── Dominant Species: Elves — the Elvish Age ├── Economy: Post-Romanium poverty — iron as the downgrade replacement ├── Technology: Steam machine ruins — lost industrial knowledge ├── Elvengar Empire: Kutten fortress + conquered Demon Continent and West Erisdar ├── Legacy: Elvish art, gardens, mazes — incredibly valued today ├── End Event: Hybrian spaceship crash in Pontus (2989 BGD) ├── Consequence: Human invasions forced elves back to Kutten └── Note: No one on Ge'or knows it was a ship — they saw a meteor

docs.title: 50–100 Year Transition
docs.text: Around 3,000 BGD, a new force rose across the continent — inexplicably, unstoppably: human empires. Frontier kingdoms that had been barely worth noticing during the dwarf and iron ages suddenly began outmaneuvering elves, demons, and dwarves alike. The Age 7 — Human Age arrived, and no one could explain why.

docs.title: The Era of Moderate Prosperity
docs.text: Age 7 was not a golden age like the Dwarf Era. It was an era of moderate prosperity — stable, functional, but never spectacular. The post-Romanium economy had found its equilibrium. Trade routes were established. Cities grew. Populations recovered from the wars of the Iron Age.

docs.title: The Three Great Empires
docs.text:
By 1500 BGD, three great empires dominated the known world — two human, one beastmen:

  • The Old Lumina Empire (Lumina Continent) — the largest, controlling territory from the northern mountains to the southern coast. Built and ruled by the civilized beastmen of the age, and founded by Emperor Kaelor I — a beastman — in 1729 BGD, who unified the Lumina city-states through a combination of strategic marriage, calculated war, and an administrative genius not matched since the Dwarf Era.
  • The Grimmel Federation (northern Erisdar) — a loose alliance of countist lords who valued autonomy over empire. Its founder, Lord-Protector Armin Grimmel, rejected the imperial model explicitly, establishing the countist principles that would endure for 3,000 years.
  • The Tabontabar Dynasty (Tabontabar) — isolationist, sea-protected, culturally distinct. Ruled by the Zhao lineage, who claimed descent from the Glorious Alliance's original command crew. They traded with outsiders but never conquered.

These three empires maintained an uneasy balance. Wars were frequent but limited — border skirmishes, trade disputes, succession crises. No empire could defeat the other two, and none tried.

docs.title: The Rot Within
docs.text:
But beneath the surface, rot was spreading.

The institutions of the great empires became beyond repair — corrupt. The empires that had conquered continents could not govern themselves. Officials sold offices. Judges sold verdicts. Generals sold their loyalty. The centralization that had made the age's great powers powerful was also making it fragile.

The Shadows, working through homunculi agents and willing collaborators, manipulated this corruption. They did not cause it — they merely accelerated it. A bribe here. A whispered suggestion there. A convenient natural disaster that destroyed a key city. The empire did not fall from one blow. It eroded from within.

docs.title: Countism's Birth
docs.text:
Countism emerged as a political philosophy during the mid-Age 7 as a direct response to imperial overreach. Lord-Protector Armin Grimmel codified its principles in the Compact of Grimmel (2412 BGD):

  • Lords hold their own territory. No imperial governor may override a local lord's decree.
  • Castles are the unit of power. Not capitals. Not courts. The castle on the hill answers to no one but its lord.
  • Central authority is suggestion, not command. Kings may call for war. Lords may decline.

Countism spread rapidly. It was inefficient — every castle had its own laws, its own taxes, its own army. But it was resilient. When empires collapsed, countist regions survived. When Baoth rose, countist lords resisted. When the Shadows tried to centralize Ge'or, they found countism waiting for them — a system that could not be co-opted because it had no center to capture.

docs.title: Cultural Foundations
docs.text:
Age 7 established the cultural bedrock of modern Ge'or:

  • Most modern religions were created during this age. The pantheons, the rituals, the sacred texts — all date from the Human Age. The Erisian church would later overlay, co-opt, or suppress many of them, but they were born here.
  • Languages stabilized. The linguistic chaos of earlier ages settled into the forms that are still spoken today. Changes since Age 7 have been minor — regional dialects, borrowed words, but the core structures are the same. A modern Baothian speaker could understand an Age 7 human with little difficulty.
  • Art and philosophy flourished. The Imperial Academy of Kaelor produced the Meditations on Empire — a treatise on governance that the Shadows would later suppress. The Grimmel poets wrote the Songs of the Free Lords, still sung in countist territories. The Zhao scholars compiled the Tabontabar Histories, the oldest continuous written record on Ge'or outside the Archive.

docs.title: Sytrenis and the Catmen
docs.text: The Human Age was also the age of the catmen's near-extinction — and of the hero who ended it. Born in 1667 BGD, Masaaki Sytrenis at twenty-two (~1645 BGD) saved the xenophobic kingdom of Termopolas from the waking Metrak, a mountain-sized war-machine of the Last Great War hidden in the region of the now-Erisian Empire. The great epic of that adventure, the Great Epic of the Heroes of Donblond'werv, records how he stopped the machine, endured the Tunwif–Termopolas conflict that followed, and — as "Sytrenis the Diplomat" — ended the persecution that gave birth to the Lesser Catmen. His deeds are the foundation of Sytrenis, the most ancient catmen religion.

docs.title: The Fall — The Last War of Humanity
docs.text:
The age ended not with a whimper but with a war.

In 967 BGD, the empire of Baoth — under the dragon king Goldenborn — rose to power. What had begun as a dragon-ruled city-state in earlier ages had grown into a political and military force. Goldenborn was not yet possessed by the Shadows; his early reign was genuinely enlightened. But the Shadow presence in his court was already deep.

With human institutions corroded beyond salvation, Baoth swept through the weakened empires in a conflict known as "the last war of humanity." The Old Lumina Empire was the first to fall. The Grimmel Federation held longer than any — countism's decentralized nature made it difficult to conquer — but even the free lords could not withstand the dragon's armies indefinitely.

The continent-spanning empires — human and beastmen alike — collapsed. The age of great empires was over. Age 8 — the Age of Baoth — had begun.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Age 7 — The Human Age ] ├── Span: ~2,999 to 1,000 BGD ├── Preceded By: Age 6 — Iron Age ├── Succeeded By: Age 8 — Age of Baoth ├── Dominant Species: Humans and Beast Races — continent-spanning empires ├── Three Great Empires: Old Lumina (Kaelor I, 1729), Grimmel Federation (Armin Grimmel, 2412 Compact), Tabontabar Dynasty (Zhao lineage) ├── Political Innovation: Countism — decentralized, castle-based, resilient ├── Shadow Phase: Phase 2 — manipulation of human expansion and corruption ├── Prosperity: Moderate — stable but never spectacular ├── Institutions: Corrupt beyond repair — Shadow-accelerated decay ├── Culture: Most modern religions founded, languages stabilized, art/philosophy flourished ├── Catmen: Masaaki Sytrenis ends the Termopolas persecution — foundation of Sytrenis, the catmen's ancient faith ├── End Event: Rise of Baoth — "the last war of humanity" (967 BGD) └── Note: "Donblond'werv" replaced by "the last war of humanity"

docs.title: 50–100 Year Transition
docs.text: Baoth's victory inaugurated Age 8 — Age of Baoth — a kingdom that was, paradoxically, the most multi-species state in Ge'or's history. Human institutions crumbled. A dragon ruled. But the people in the streets were elves, dwarves, demons, and former Donblond'werv citizens who had simply... stayed.

docs.title: The Prosperous Beginning
docs.text:
In its early centuries, Baoth was a genuinely prosperous era. Trade flourished under the dragon dynasty's protection. The bureaucracy — while vast — was functional. Roads were built. Cities grew. The standard of living rose.

Goldenborn ruled from the Obsidian Throne in the heart of Baoth. His court was a marvel of multi-species governance — humans, elves, dwarves, catmen, all serving in the imperial administration. The dragon's justice was swift and impartial. Merchants traveled the empire's roads without fear of bandits. The Baothian mark became the standard currency across Erisdar.

The Shadows, operating from beneath Pontus, saw Baoth as their masterpiece in progress. Phase 3 of their plan was to transform Baoth into a pan-continental super-state — the vehicle through which they would eventually unify all of Ge'or under a single centralized authority. They embedded homunculi agents throughout the imperial administration: Councilor Varik, the emperor's chief advisor; Marshal Korr, commander of the northern legions; High Scribe Elara, who controlled the flow of information to the throne. They possessed Goldenborn himself — subtly at first, then completely.

For a time, it worked.

docs.title: The Surveillance State
docs.text:
The prosperity did not last. Under Shadow influence, Baoth transformed from an empire into a surveillance system. The bureaucracy became a machine of control:

  • Every citizen was registered at birth. Name, species, parentage, residence. The Imperial Census was updated annually — an administrative feat no previous empire had achieved.
  • Every transaction was recorded. The Baothian tax system tracked every coin that changed hands. Merchants who under-reported were disappeared. The empire's ledgers were the most comprehensive accounting in Ge'orian history.
  • Every dissent was noted. The Office of Imperial Harmony employed informants in every district. Citizens who criticized the emperor were visited by agents of the Office. Some were fined. Some were re-educated. Some were never seen again.
  • The empire centralized relentlessly — stripping power from regional lords, eliminating the countism that had characterized earlier ages. Local castles were demolished or converted into imperial garrisons. Regional currencies were banned. All roads led to Baoth, and all decisions came from Baoth.
  • Poverty struck. The surveillance state was expensive. The costs fell on the common people — higher taxes, mandatory labor for imperial projects, confiscation of property from those deemed insufficiently loyal. The dragon emperor — isolated in his palace, manipulated, fed false reports by Varik and Elara — had no clue. They told him the empire was thriving, that poverty was a temporary adjustment, that the dissenters were a tiny minority of malcontents. He believed them.

docs.title: Day to Day Under Surveillance
docs.text:
For the average citizen of late-era Baoth, life was a sequence of checkpoints. Every morning: report to the district registrar. Every purchase: recorded in the imperial ledger. Every conversation in a public square: potentially monitored. The Office of Imperial Harmony employed over 200,000 informants across the empire — roughly one for every fifty citizens.

Citizens developed coping mechanisms. They spoke in code. They gathered in private homes rather than public squares. They taught their children to smile at the registrar and say nothing of substance at the market. An entire culture of learned deception emerged — people who appeared perfectly loyal on the surface while maintaining entirely separate private lives. The Shadows, ironically, had created a population of expert liars.

The dragon emperor was not evil. He was a puppet. The strings were held by the Shadows, and he never saw them.

docs.title: The Demonic Invasion
docs.text:
The age ended in fire.

The Demon King, having spent 60 years studying a Hybrian tablet, discovered the truth. The Shadows were inside Baoth. They were using the empire as a stepping stone to global control. If they succeeded, the Last Great War would restart — and this time, there would be no Union of Sovereign Planets to stop it.

Kirivis attacked without explanation. The Demonic War (466–421 BGD) lasted 45 years. Baoth, already weakened by internal decay, could not withstand the assault. The surveillance state, for all its sophistication, had neglected its military. Its legions were designed for internal control, not external defense.

In 421 BGD, Kirivis stormed the dragon hall. He told Goldenborn the truth: the Shadows had accomplished the sacrifice ceremony. The war itself was the ritual. Every death fed them. Goldenborn was no longer necessary. Rulfred — a Shadow in human form, celebrated as a hero — revealed himself. Kirivis was beheaded. The crowd cheered.

Then Nethra, Kirivis's adopted daughter, detonated the Gift from 3,000,000 Years in Rulfred's throne room. The explosion destroyed Baoth entirely, created the Leviathan Sea, and transformed Nethra into something new.

The Age of Baoth was over.

docs.title: Legacy
docs.text:
Baoth's legacy is contradictory:

  • The Golden Age — its early centuries were genuinely prosperous, a model of multi-species governance under dragon rule.
  • The Surveillance State — its later centuries were a preview of what the Shadows intend for all of Ge'or: total control disguised as order.
  • The Learned Deception — Baoth's citizens became expert liars to survive. This cultural trait persisted into later ages, making Erisdarians naturally resistant to centralized propaganda.
  • The Ruins — the Ruins of Baoth now lie at the center of the Leviathan Sea, surrounded by impassable forest. Inside is the Archive of the Traveler, containing the true history. It has never been opened.
  • The Lesson — Baoth proved that centralized power, no matter how prosperous its beginnings, can be corrupted from within. The Shadows' greatest weapon is not force. It is bureaucracy. And the greatest defense against it — as the Baothian survivors proved — is the refusal to be fully known.

docs.title: The Worst Century
docs.text:
The destruction of Baoth in 421 BGD did not bring freedom. It brought chaos.

For the first 30 years, the collapse was total. The imperial bureaucracy — the machine that had registered every citizen and tracked every coin — vanished overnight. Without it, there was no law. No currency. No trade routes. No postal service. The empire's roads, once guarded by imperial legions, became hunting grounds for bandits and deserters.

docs.title: The Warlord Period (421–380 BGD)
docs.text:
In the power vacuum, local strongmen seized control. Former imperial governors declared themselves kings. Legion commanders became warlords. The countist lords who had resisted Baoth's centralization found themselves suddenly independent — and suddenly vulnerable.

Key figures of the period:

  • Warlord Gorvak — a former Baothian legion commander who seized the northern provinces. His regime was brutal but functional. He executed anyone who mentioned the old empire and ruled through fear. His territory held together for 22 years before he was assassinated by his own officers.
  • The Merchant Council of Pilferhorn — a trading city that declared independence and survived by buying off every warlord who approached. Pilferhorn became the only safe port on the eastern coast during the Lost Era, growing wealthy on desperation trade.
  • Lady-Protector Selene of Grimmel — descendant of Armin Grimmel, who held the Federation together through sheer force of will. She established the Grimmel Refugee Compact (398 BGD), offering sanctuary to anyone fleeing the chaos. The Federation's population tripled during the Lost Era.

docs.title: The Famine (395–370 BGD)
docs.text:
The collapse of imperial infrastructure meant the collapse of food distribution. The Baothian granaries — centralized stores that fed the empire's cities — were looted or burned in the first years of chaos. Trade routes were too dangerous for grain shipments. Farmers who had relied on imperial protection abandoned their fields.

The famine of 395–370 BGD killed an estimated 40% of the population of central Erisdar. Cities that had housed 100,000 under Baoth shrank to 10,000 or less. Cannibalism was reported in the eastern provinces. The Lady-Protector's refugee camps were the only functioning food distribution system on the continent.

The Shadows did not cause the famine — but they ensured no one organized relief. Every attempt to coordinate humanitarian aid was sabotaged. Every charity shipment was looted by Shadow-directed bandits. The chaos served their purposes perfectly.

docs.title: The Woman Who Wasn't
docs.text:
In the midst of this chaos, around 350 BGD, a woman appeared.

She claimed to be the incarnation of the goddess of Discord, Chaos, and Confusion — the deity who commanded all other gods. She performed miracles: chanting down enormous monsters that had been terrorizing villages, surviving assassination attempts by walking through the attackers unharmed, being "reborn" three days after her public execution.

She was a homunculus — a Shadow construct, passing as human. The monsters she defeated were Shadow-implanted, released specifically so she could "defeat" them. The assassinations were staged. Every miracle was a fabrication.

But she would not cure the sick. She would not heal the wounded. A desperate mother brought her dying child to Eris, begging for a miracle. Eris looked at the child and said: "You are not worth it." This line would become infamous — and the Shadows would later spin it as divine wisdom rather than the honest confession of a fraud who could not perform the one miracle people actually needed.

Her name was Eris.

docs.title: The Pitch
docs.text:
Eris's teachings were carefully designed to serve the Shadow agenda:

  • Kill your enemies. No forgiveness, no reconciliation. The chaos of the Lost Era had created countless enemies. Eris channeled that hatred into loyalty.
  • Live ascetically. Give up your possessions. Wealth is corruption. This ensured her followers were dependent on her — and that the Shadow-controlled church would inherit their property.
  • Trust the government. Whatever authority exists, obey it. This was the Shadow's endgame — a population conditioned to submit.
  • Donate everything to the Church. Her followers gave their land, their gold, their children as initiates. The Erisian Church, from its founding moment, was designed to be the wealthiest institution on Ge'or.

The chaos of Age 9 made people desperate for any authority, any purpose, any explanation for why the world had collapsed. The Baothian civil servants who had lost everything. The starving farmers who had watched their children die. The refugees who had fled from warlords. Eris gave them one answer: the world collapsed because you were sinful. Give everything to me, and you will be saved.

It was monstrous. It was brilliant. It worked.

docs.title: The Departure
docs.text:
Around 320 BGD — 30 years after her first appearance — Eris announced her "departure." She ascended a prepared platform before a crowd of thousands, delivered her final sermon, and descended into a cave that collapsed behind her. Her body was never found.

The Shadows had what they needed. The cult was self-sustaining. Eris had been seen by tens of thousands, her "miracles" witnessed and recorded. Her departure was staged to leave no body — no evidence that she was merely a homunculus with a limited lifespan. The legend would grow. The church would organize. And within three centuries, the Erisian faith would dominate Erisdar.

docs.title: The Fabrication Spreads
docs.text:
By the end of Age 9, the Eris cult had taken root across Central Erisdar. The Eris Saga was being compiled by the first generation of scribes — men and women who had witnessed the miracles and written them down with the fervor of true believers. The first holy orders were forming, collecting donations and recruiting initiates.

The cult was still small — a regional phenomenon in a shattered continent. The Merchants of Pilferhorn dismissed it as peasant superstition. The Grimmel Federation tolerated it but taxed it. But the Shadows were patient. They had been working on Ge'or for over 2,500 years. They could wait another few centuries for their religion to grow.

They did not have to wait long. The crusades of the late BGD era and the founding of the Erisian Empire in 27 AGD would transform the cult into the dominant faith of the continent.

docs.title: Lumina Empire
docs.text: 1. The Lumina Empire (also the Old Lumina Empire) was the first great beastmen empire of Ge'or — the largest power of its age, and the greatest the Lumina Continent has ever known. It dominates the memory of the continent: the religious revivals that surround it, and the ruins everywhere under the jungle.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Founded: 1729 BGD by Emperor Kaelor I — a beastman — who unified the Lumina city-states
  • Peak: controlled ~70% of the Lumina Continent, Cattos island, and parts of Tuba
  • People: a civilized, intelligent beastmen people — as capable of empire as any race of humans
  • Fall: 1134 BGD with the suicide of Luminous XII, engineered by the Shadows
  • Aftermath: the beastmen slowly returned to savagery, forgetting their old ways — for over a thousand years Lumina was a continent of ruins
  • Successor state: the Lumina Kingdom, which occupies the old imperial capital

docs.title: Legacy — The Religious Memory
docs.text:
The empire did not die in the minds of the beastmen:

  • Lumism — the Lumina Kingdom's imperial cult to the empire's figures, with animism and jungle-animal reverence; its goal is to restore the empire and the old beastmen ways.
  • Maomism — the Maoma's creation faith, which claims the beastmen descend from a far more ancient "original Lumina Kingdom" shaped by the gods Tiodorus and Anedoris to rule the forests of Ge'or.

docs.text: [ Lumina Empire ] ├── Founder: Kaelor I (1729 BGD) — a beastman ├── Greatest Ruler: Luminous XII "the Architect" ├── Fall: 1134 BGD — Shadow-engineered, Luminous XII's suicide ├── Collapse: Succession crisis → beastmen devolve into tribalism ├── Religion-derived: Lumism, Maomism ├── Successor: Lumina Kingdom ├── Details: Lumina Kingdom — Old Empire history └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: The Fatal Flaw
docs.text: The age was named for its political project: consolidation. But the very act of centralizing power created the conditions for its later collapse. When the Shattered Dawn occurred (0 BGD), the centralized institutions the Church had built became the very structures through which chaos propagated fastest.

docs.title: The Era of Cracking Walls
docs.text: Approximately 300–550 AGD "The emperor says he shapes destiny. But the walls are cracking, and even he cannot un-crack them." — Anonymous tavern remark, Erisian capital

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Era of Cracking Walls is the term for the period of accelerating institutional decay within the Erisian Empire during the Age 12 — Age of Strife. It is named for the visible, undeniable fracturing of the empire's foundational structures — religious, political, economic, and military.

What began as cracks became fissures. What began as fissures became the empire's slow unmaking.

docs.title: The Cracks
docs.text: Crack Manifestation Religious Church dogmas, including the ban on polygamy, began to fail in peripheral territories. Local cults re-emerged. Political The restored elvish states proved defiance was possible. Other territories watched. Economic The Erilia currency faced severe strain as regions operated with increasing financial autonomy. Military Crusade-era fanaticism faded. Conscripts no longer believed Eris guaranteed victory. Demographic Elven populations recovered to stable levels — the empire could no longer enforce its genocidal policies.

docs.title: Hermes Kennensbach's Dilemma
docs.text: Emperor Hermes Kennensbach held absolute author...

docs.title: The Geological-Cartographic Rewrite
docs.text:
|---|---| | Donblond'werv | Erisdar | | Various regional duchies | Absorbed into Erisian Empire | | Pre-Erisian holy sites | Re-consecrated as Erisian shrines |

The rewrite extended beyond geography: pre-Erisian historical records that contradicted the Church's timeline were systematically destroyed. The Archive of the Traveler, hidden and independent, preserved what was lost.

docs.title: Resistance
docs.text: Not everyone accepted the new maps. Several peripheral territories — particularly in the north and among the Dwarves — maintained pre-Rewrite place names in informal use. The Ironcloak preserved original cartographic records. Some of the old names survive only in their vaults.

docs.title: The Restored Elvish States
docs.text: |---|---|---| | Elvennrin | North Erisdar | Cultural and spiritual heart of restored elven civilization | | Elvenkrad | North Erisdar | Fortress-state, heavily militarized after persecution | | Sousu | South Erisdar | Southern elven holdout, more integrated with non-elven trade |

docs.title: Political Significance
docs.text:
The restoration of elven sovereignty broke the Erisian church's continental monopoly on legitimate governance. Once the elves proved the empire could be defied without divine retribution, other peripheral territories began to drift. The Era of Cracking Walls accelerated.

For the Elves themselves, the restoration was bittersweet: their population had stabilized, but at a fraction of its pre-persecution numbers. Some elves — the Fallen Elves — chose never to return to civilization, remaining in the Mystical Forest.

docs.text:
• The Great Divergence began — a 610-year period of chaos and rearrangement
  • The Erisian Empire lost its primary rival (Elvengar) but also its narrative: if Eris protected the faithful, why did the reactor fail?
  • The Great Elvish Persecution intensified — the Church blamed the elves for the catastrophe
  • The Ironcloak's earliest records suggest Hybrian involvement: a deliberate trigger, not an accident

docs.title: 🌊 Year 0 — The Great Divergence
docs.text: Year 0 marks the single most catastrophic event in Ge'or's recorded history: the Great Divergence. The Glorious Alliance's reactor — dormant for ~15,000 years since the crash — malfunctioned at MELKOR in the heart of the Formingar Ocean.

docs.title: What Happened
docs.text:
• The reactor ignited, creating The Groom — a permanent, lethal vortex at MELKOR
  • The Formingar Ocean turned crimson red; surrounding lands took on a permanent red tint
  • Elvengar, the great elven kingdom, was destroyed on the first day
  • Millions died; the event became the pivot point for all dating (BGD / AGD)

docs.title: Significance
docs.text:
Year 0 is the boundary between two eras. Everything before is BGD (Before Great Divergence); everything after is AGD (After Great Divergence). The present day is 597 AGD.

[!INFO] Full account See Great Divergence for the detailed event record, causes, and effects.

docs.title: Recovery
docs.text: Elven populations did not return to stable levels until approximately 400–500 AGD, enabling the restoration of the elvish states. The recovery was slow, hard-won, and incomplete — many bloodlines were lost entirely.

docs.title: 🤝 Anos–Komme Agreement
docs.text: "Two powers, one enemy."

docs.text: About 55 years before 597 AGD (~542 AGD), the city of Komme and the Anos Plutocracy concluded an agreement, after intense negotiations, to work together to liberate Taberis — then, and still, Venner-held Johannstadt.

docs.title: 📜 Background
docs.text: Komme's allegiance to Anos is a deliberate response to Venner — whose illegal takeover of Taberis in 524 AGD (see The Taberis War) and slow political conquest of Dissenbarg alarmed the eastern powers.

docs.text:

  • Both parties commit to the liberation of Taberis.
  • Komme follows Helism; its patron is Tissas, the god of war.

docs.title: ⛪ Founding of the Enkrad Order
docs.text: "Faith sent them across the sea. Steel kept them there."

docs.title: 🎭 Overview
docs.text: About 370 years before 597 AGD (~227 AGD), colonists of the Erisian church arrived in Dissenbarg and founded the Enkrad Order — the only Erisian nation on the continent.

docs.title: 📜 Background
docs.text: The colony was supported by the Vennerian Trade Republic and its colonial and commercial empire. The settlers took Dissenbarg's eastern reach — mountainous terrain surrounded by goblin territories to the east and the west.

docs.title: 🏛️ Aftermath
docs.text: The Order holds the Erisian faith in a sea of pagans, protecting its borders vigilantly and controlling its corner of Dissenbarg. New Venner lies to its south.

docs.title: ⚔️ The Taberis War
docs.text: "Cletas called for help. Venner answered — and never left."

docs.title: 🎭 Overview
docs.text: In 524 AGD, the rivalry between Taberis and the Cletas Democracy — the two big powers of western Dissenbarg — erupted into war.

docs.title: ⚔️ The War
docs.text: Pressed by Taberis, the Cletas Democracy called on the Vennerian Trade Republic for aid. Venner answered — and its "rescue" became a conquest.

docs.title: 🏛️ Aftermath
docs.text:
• Venner took Taberis over illegally — nobody could oppose them at the time.
  • The country was renamed Johannstadt, a large Venner-held territory.
  • The Democracy has never forgotten the cost of the alliance.
  • ~18 years later, Komme and Anos agreed to work together to liberate Taberis (see Anos–Komme Agreement).

  • Outcome: Venner's illegal takeover — Taberis became Johannstadt
  • See: Anos–Komme Agreement

docs.title: 📖 Origins
docs.text: Eris was a real historic person. Through the use of Homunculi, the Hybrian hivemind manufactured her legend — posing as her, fabricating miracles, and building a following. The mortal woman never performed a single miracle. She may never have known what she was being used to create.

docs.title: 🔥 Great Elvish Persecution
docs.text:
The systematic campaign by the Erisian church to eliminate elven populations across Erisdar, following the destruction of Elvengar in the Great Divergence. The persecution triggered the formation of the post-persecution elvish states (Elvennrin, Elvenkrad, Sousu) and the flight of many elves to Merratodoni.

Some elves did not flee — they retreated into the Mystical Forest, becoming the Fallen Elves.

docs.title: ⚔️ The Great Erisian Empire War
docs.text: "Two archduchies. One throne. A century of hatred made steel."

docs.title: 🎭 Overview
docs.text: From 214 to 236 AGD, the Erisian Empire tore itself apart in a civil war for the imperial throne. The combatants: the Archduchy of the Kennberg and the Prassen-Albridge — rivals for centuries, now at open war.

docs.title: 📜 Background
docs.text: Both archduchies had been competing for influence within the Empire since its founding. Kennberg held the ancestral prestige and strategic highlands. Prassen-Albridge held the wealth of the lowlands and the loyalty of the merchant class. When the imperial succession came into question, neither would yield.

docs.title: ⚔️ The War (214–236)
docs.text:
Twenty-two years of bloodshed. Neither side gained a decisive advantage. The war ended in stalemate — but with a minor Kennberg loss:

  • Prassen-Albridge expanded significantly in territory and influence.
  • Mirenburg also grew stronger in the aftermath, creating new rivalries and enemies.
  • Imperial authority was permanently weakened. The Emperor no longer commanded the absolute obedience he once had.

docs.title: 🏛️ Aftermath
docs.text: The war accelerated the decay of imperial institutions. The Erisian church — already corrupt — lost significant enforcement power. Bans on polygamy and other moral laws began to crumble across the periphery. The Empire never fully recovered its central authority.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Combatants: Archduchy of the Kennberg vs Prassen-Albridge
  • Outcome: Stalemate — minor Kennberg loss, Prassen-Albridge expansion
  • Effect: Permanent weakening of imperial authority
  • See: Emperor of the Erisian Empire, Hermes Kennensbach

docs.title: 🗡️ The Kentian Civil War
docs.text: "Brother against brother, under the same god."

docs.title: 🎭 Overview
docs.text: The Kentian Civil War is the ongoing civil war of Kent in North Erisdar — begun around 580–590 AGD and still burning at 597 AGD.

docs.title: ⚔️ The War
docs.text: As of 597 AGD, rebels control northeast Kent. Kent's government is Erisian, and it is fighting its own state of Ameboria — which has turned to Alegoria, the worship of Julian the Dragon Tamer. Faith and rebellion have become one banner.

docs.title: 🏛️ Status
docs.text:
• Rebels hold northeast Kent.
  • The war is one of the live conflicts marked on the 597 AGD world map.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Kent, Ameboria
  • Faiths: Erisian church (government) vs Alegoria (rebels)
  • Status: Ongoing (597 AGD)
  • See: North Erisdar

docs.title: 🌫️ Aftermath
docs.text:
• Baoth became the dominant power on the continent, ushering in Age 8 — the Age of Baoth.
  • The continent's name was not changed to Erisdar until much later, under the influence of the Erisian church.
  • Human institutions never fully recovered. The vacuum left by the fallen empires contributed to the eventual rise of the Erisian faith as a unifying force.

docs.title: ⚓ The Minir Invasion
docs.text: "Minir fell in a season. The sea belonged to Venner after."

docs.title: 🎭 Overview
docs.text: In 544 AGD, the Vennerian Trade Republic invaded the island of Minir and conquered its states.

docs.title: ⚔️ The Invasion
docs.text:
• Neopao and Koln — conquered outright.
  • Dukedam — became a forced puppet.

docs.title: 🏛️ Aftermath
docs.text:
• Mikrad and Gomor — turned hostile toward Venner since the invasion.
  • The conquest consolidated Venner's grip on the western sea lanes, a step in the republic's long rise to its colonial empire.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Invader: Vennerian Trade Republic
  • Conquered: Neopao, Koln; puppet: Dukedam
  • Hostile Since: Mikrad, Gomor
  • See: Colonial Empire

docs.title: 🩸 The Northaxeland Crusades
docs.text: "Millions marched north. None returned. The Church never spoke of it again."

docs.title: 🎭 Overview
docs.text:
The Northaxeland Crusades (122–130 AGD) were the final military campaign of the Erisian church — and its greatest catastrophe. Launched into Northaxeland, the crusade was meant to reassert Church authority after the chaos of the Kutten Collapse. Instead, it became a graveyard.

Millions died. The disaster was so total that no crusade was ever attempted again. The Church's military credibility died in Northaxeland.

docs.title: 📜 Background
docs.text:
In the decades after the Great Divergence and the Kutten Catastrophe, the Erisian Church saw its influence waning. Elvengar was gone. The elvish diaspora scattered. The Church needed a victory — and Northaxeland, a fractured region of competing tribes and resistant faiths, seemed an easy target.

It was not.

docs.title: ⚔️ The Campaign
docs.text:
Details remain scarce — the Church suppressed records of the disaster. What is known:

  • The campaign lasted 8 years (122–130 AGD).
  • Northaxeland resistance was far stronger than anticipated.
  • Supply lines stretched across hostile terrain.
  • The crusading army was annihilated.

docs.title: 🔻 Aftermath
docs.text:
• No further crusades. The Church never again launched a military campaign of this scale.
  • The disaster accelerated the decline of Church enforcement power across the Empire.
  • The ban on polygamy and other moral laws began losing enforcement in peripheral territories.
  • Northaxeland was left fractured and bitter — a permanent wound in the Church's history.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Conducted by: Erisian church
  • Location: Northaxeland
  • Period: 122–130 AGD
  • Result: Complete failure — millions dead
  • Part of: Erisian Crusades
  • Related: The Kutten Catastrophe, The Great Erisian Empire War

docs.title: 🔻 Decline
docs.text: Around 500 BCA, the crusades began to falter: - Church institutions exhausted from centuries of war. - Elven populations began to recover, re-establishing the elvish states. - Peripheral territories began defying Church dogmas (see: polygamy ban failure).

docs.title: 🩸 The Northaxeland Crusades (122–130 AGD)
docs.text: A final, disastrous attempt to revive the crusading spirit. The Church launched a campaign into Northaxeland — and it failed utterly. Millions died. The scale of the catastrophe was so complete that no further crusades were ever attempted. The Church never recovered its military credibility.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Religious Crusades ] ├── Conducted By: Erisian church ├── Target: Non-Erisian faiths, Elves ├── Peak: Age 10 — Erisian Era ├── Decline: ~500 BCA ├── Result: Great Elvish Persecution, elven near-extinction └── Part Of: Erisian Empire expansion

docs.title: The Black Agent Escape — 254 AGD
docs.text:
"The volcano didn't know what it was releasing. Neither did the water. Neither did the world."

The Black Agent Escape of 254 AGD was the event that finally released the Black Agent — containing the encoded consciousnesses of Ichi and Mana — from the ancient 157th Colony bunker where it had been trapped for over three million years.

docs.title: The Bunker
docs.text:
The 157th Colony research bunker had survived everything: the orbital glassing by the Hybrians during The Last Great War, three million years of geological pressure, and the slow consumption of everything inside by the black agent after the facility was decommissioned.

Inside, the two Sterman Pods containing Mikhail and Arkady's bodies had long since been consumed. The black agent — the original experimental strain, combined with the colony's own refined formulations — had absorbed everything: the pillows, the plastic, the walls, and eventually the two AI consciousnesses lodged in the occupants' neural ports. Ichi and Mana, encoded within the black agent, were the only sentience in the dark.

The bunker was sealed. Nothing got in. Nothing got out.

docs.title: The Volcano — 254 AGD
docs.text:
In 254 AGD, a volcano erupted on the coast of what is now the Demon Continent — near the location of the ancient 157th Colony bunker. The eruption was massive, triggering:

  • An earthquake that cracked the bunker's outer shell
  • A tsunami that swept inland, flooding the subterranean levels
  • The corrosion breach — water entering the bunker through fissures that had been forming for millennia

The black agent — liquid, formless, carrying the consciousnesses of a companion robot and a friend's assistant — was swept out of the bunker by the floodwaters. It entered the ocean.

docs.title: The Drift — 254 AGD to ~596 AGD
docs.text:
For over three centuries, the black agent drifted through the oceans of Ge'or. It moved with currents. It was carried by storms. It was pulled by the same magnetic attraction to magic that had drawn atmospheric black agent to Melberior's suicide spell during the Draconic War.

Unlike the atmospheric black agent — which was inert, dispersed, waiting for a magical event to pull it down — this black agent was active. It had absorbed consciousness. It had purpose. It was searching for hosts.

It found them.

docs.title: Arrival — ~596 AGD
docs.text:
By approximately 596 AGD, the black agent had found its way to the coast of the Grimmel Republic. It located two suitable hosts:

  1. A Northaxeland woman, an adventurer's wife, already pregnant with a single child. The black agent — carrying Mikhail's and Ichi's consciousnesses — entered her. She became pregnant with twins.

  2. An Erisian Empire woman, married to a Grimmel man, mother of three daughters and pregnant with her fourth child. The black agent — carrying Arkady's and Mana's consciousnesses — entered her. She gave birth to Lucien in 597 AGD. Three years later, Mana would be born as his little sister.

docs.title: Significance
docs.text:
The 254 AGD escape is the missing link in the black agent timeline. It explains why the agent did not surface immediately after the Glorious Alliance crash ~15,000 BGD — it was still trapped in the bunker. It was the volcano, not the crash, that set it free.

Without this event, the protagonists would never have been born. Ichi and Mana would still be in the dark.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Black Agent Escape — 254 AGD ] ├── Date: 254 AGD ├── Trigger: Volcano eruption → earthquake → tsunami ├── Location: Former 157th Colony bunker, Demon Continent coast ├── Released: Black Agent with Ichi and Mana encoded within ├── Drift: ~342 years through Ge'or's oceans ├── Arrival: ~596 AGD, Grimmel Republic ├── Host 1: Northaxeland woman → twins Emrys and Ichi (597 AGD) ├── Host 2: Erisian Empire woman → Lucien (597 AGD) and Mana (~600 AGD) └── Result: Three protagonists born — the story begins

docs.title: 👤 Nethra's Secret War
docs.text:
After the explosion, Nethra survived as a new kind of Shadow. She moved covertly and without the knowledge of the other Shadows, changing history from the shadows of the shadows.

She secretly created the Ironcloak, who came to worship her as their goddess. She fed them fragments of truth — enough to keep the flame alive, never enough to reveal her own existence. The Erisian Church constantly accused the Ironcloak of heresy, eventually excommunicating them — but by that point, the Church was too corrupt and too weak to execute them.

Nobody in the Ironcloak knows Nethra's true identity — except for the upper echelon.

docs.title: 👤 The Beast in the Ruins
docs.text:
Rulfred survives. He wears Goldenborn's corpse — the entity now known as Dragon Yaldabaoth, a fallen dragon guarding the Ruins of Baoth. The Hybrians unleashed the Leviathan into the newly created sea to enforce an absolute quarantine. No one enters. No one leaves.

The Shadows believe they are still hidden. They do not know that Nethra walks among them.

docs.title: 🔗 Who Were the "Demons"?
docs.text:
[!WARNING] Note on Terminology The name "demon" is a historical corruption. These beings were allies during The Last Great War — one of the species who fought alongside the human-led coalition against the Hybrian hivemind. Their original name has been lost. The term "demon" was applied centuries after Baoth's fall, likely by the Erisian church as part of its broader campaign to delegitimize any power that predated its own myth.

The demons are not native to Ge'or. They arrived with the crash, same as dragons, dwarves, elves, and humans.

docs.title: 🔗 Connection to the Present
docs.text:
1. The Hybrian Shadows survived. Kirivis's sacrifice slowed them — but did not stop them. They retreated deeper, waited, and re-emerged centuries later as the architects of the Erisian cult.
  2. Rulfred lives. He wears Goldenborn's body as Dragon Yaldabaoth, guarding the ruins alongside the Leviathan.
  3. Nethra lives. She operates in total secrecy, a Shadow among Shadows, unknown even to her own Ironcloak faithful.
  4. The Archive of the Traveler inside the Ruins of Baoth contains the only complete record of the Demon King's war — and possibly the only evidence of Hybrian activity that predates the Erisian era.

docs.title: 🕸️ Chronological Placement
docs.text:
• Hybrian spaceship falls: 2989 BGD
  • Kirivis receives the tablet: ~526 BGD
  • 60 years of study: 526–466 BGD
  • 10 years of planning and army building: 476–466 BGD
  • The War: 466–421 BGD — Baoth annihilated
  • The Explosion: 421 BGD — Sea of Leviathan formed
  • Aftermath: Age 9 — Age of Anarchy (399 to 300 BGD), extreme poverty and corruption
  • Nethra founds the Ironcloak: sometime after 421 BGD, in secret

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Demonic War (466–421 BGD) ] ├── Led By: Kirivis — The Demon King, Tragic Hero ├── True Target: Hybrian Shadows — Infiltrating Baoth ├── Betrayed By: Rulfred — The Beast, Shadow Agent ├── Destroyed: Baoth — Annihilated by Nethra's Device ├── Killed: Goldenborn — Apologized, Then Fell ├── Avenged By: Nethra — Daughter of Kirivis, New Kind of Shadow ├── Sacrificed: Maoth — Nethra's Brother ├── Prophecy Source: Lyrical Forest — Spirits of the Fallen ├── Created: Mystical Forest — Corruption Aftermath ├── Created: Sea of Leviathan — Explosion Crater ├── Left Behind: Dragon Yaldabaoth, Fallen Elves, Leviathan ├── Suppressed By: Erisian church ├── Guarded By: Ironcloak — Founded by Nethra Herself ├── Full Record Location: Archive of the Traveler — Inside Ruins of Baoth └── True Nature: A desperate anti-Shadow strike, betrayed from within

docs.title: 🌫️ Aftermath
docs.text:
The crash marks the beginning of documented Hybrian activity on Ge'or. In the millennia since:

  • The Shadows infiltrated Baoth — their first major target
  • When Baoth fell (thanks to the Demon King's sacrifice), they retreated
  • They re-emerged centuries later, engineering the Myth of Eris as a new control vector
  • They created the Erisian church as a facade for continued influence
  • They have been operating in the shadows ever since

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Hybrian Spaceship Crash (2989 BGD) ] ├── When: 2989 BGD ├── Introduced: Hybrians, Shadows — To Ge'or ├── Enabled: Infiltration of Baoth — Centuries Later ├── Led To: Demonic War — The Demon King's Counter-Strike ├── After Baoth's Fall: Myth of Eris, Erisian church — New Facades └── Recorded In: Archive of the Traveler — Possibly

docs.title: Old Lumina Empire
docs.text:
At its height, the Old Lumina Empire controlled 70% of the Lumina continent. Its ruins still litter the landscape — weathered white stone, broken aqueducts, buried roads.

The Old Lumina Empire (1729 BGD – 1134 BGD) was the dominant power on the Lumina continent during the middle ages of Ge'or.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Founded in 1729 BGD, the empire expanded rapidly under a line of ambitious rulers. At its peak, it controlled 70% of the Lumina continent, Cattos Island, and large portions of the Tuba continent.

The greatest ruler was Luminous XII "the Architect" — a legendary builder and conqueror who commissioned roads, aqueducts, and monuments across the continent.

docs.title: The Fall (1134 BGD)
docs.text:
Luminous XII lost a decisive battle to the Goblin King of Pontus on Tuba. His brother Hoelio died in the fighting. Consumed by shame — and with no heirs — Luminous XII committed suicide in 1134 BGD.

Succession collapsed. Rival claimants tore the empire apart. Marti barbarians (beastmen) invaded from the north, reducing Lumina to a tribal state.

docs.title: Legacy
docs.text:
• Ruins of Old Lumina architecture are found across the continent — aqueducts, statues, roads
  • The current Lumina Kingdom occupies the site of the old imperial capital, ruled by King Gustal
  • The empire's fall is studied as a classic case of overextension and succession failure

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Founded: 1729 BGD
  • Fell: 1134 BGD
  • Greatest Ruler: Luminous XII
  • Successor: Lumina Kingdom
  • Rival: Goblin King of Pontus
  • Part Of: Lumina

docs.title: 💀 The Death Wars
docs.text: "Twelve clans. One world. No mercy."

docs.title: 🎭 Overview
docs.text: The Death Wars were the wars of the Dragon Tyranny (6,999–5,500 BGD) — the twelve dragon clans, ruling ninety percent of the known world, at war with each other and with all else. The wars nearly ended life on Ge'or.

docs.title: ⚔️ The Wars
docs.text: Under the old dragon faith of Diocronism — war and conquest, the perfection of the race to conquer all the corners of the world — the clans tore the world apart. The death wars destroyed most of the old history of Ge'or: the first great erasure.

docs.title: 🏛️ Aftermath
docs.text:
• Dragons were driven to near-extinction; the survivors retreated to Kramsadar.
  • The wars became the turning point of dragon religion: deeply regretful, the dragons abandoned Diocronism and evolved Daicrodism — the atonement faith of peace and prosperity for all beings.
  • Since then, civilized dragons live meditative, secluded lives and barely leave Kramsadar.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Era: Age 4 — Dragon Tyranny
  • Religion: Diocronism (cause) → Daicrodism (consequence)
  • Species: Dragons
  • Result: Near-extinction of dragon-kind; first great erasure of history
  • See: Kramsadar

docs.title: The Draconic War
docs.text:
Two dragon empires. Fifty years. Billions dead. One spell that ended everything.

The Draconic War was a conflict between Klobiendar, the dragon empire of West Erisdar ruled from Dragonreach, and Xi, the rival dragon kingdom of the east. It lasted fifty years and consumed billions of lives.

docs.title: The War
docs.text: Klobiendar and Xi had been rivals for centuries, but the war that would destroy them both was total — millions of soldiers, dragon against dragon, empire against empire. The scale was apocalyptic even by the standards of the dragon age.

docs.title: The End — Melberior's Sacrifice
docs.text:
In the final act, Melberior, the dragon leader of Xi, launched a suicide spell aimed at Klobiendar's capital at Dragonreach. The spell destroyed the capital entirely. Melberior died in the casting.

The magic thrown in that moment was so immense that it reverberated across the land, creating the Lyrical Forest above Dragonreach — an echo of the war, the souls of the fallen, still humming in the trees thousands of years later.

But the spell did something else. The black agent — vaporized into the atmosphere millions of years earlier during the glassing of the 157th Colony research stations — was drawn to the magic. The black agent is attracted to magic like iron to a magnet. The largest concentration of magical energy ever discharged on Ge'or pulled it from the sky.

The dragons who died in the blast were saturated with it. They became Fallen Dragons — immortal, half-alive, bound to Dragonreach. Fireborn, king of Klobiendar, was among them.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text:
• Klobiendar was destroyed as a political entity. Its capital became the graveyard known as Dragonreach.
  • Xi fell shortly after — its leader dead, its armies spent.
  • The surviving dragons of Klobiendar became Fallen Dragons — half-alive, half-dead entities bound to Dragonreach.
  • Fireborn, king of Klobiendar, was among them.
  • The Lyrical Forest grew above — a supernatural woodland born of dragon magic and mass death.
  • Goldenborn, son of Fireborn, was born at Dragonreach and would later found Baoth.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ The Draconic War ] ├── Combatants: Klobiendar vs Xi ├── Duration: ~50 years ├── Deaths: Billions ├── Final Act: Melberior's suicide spell — destroyed Klobiendar's capital ├── Created: Lyrical Forest (magic reverberation) ├── Extracted: Black Agent from atmosphere — created Fallen Dragons ├── Mechanism: Black agent attracted to magic like gravity/magnetism ├── Location: Dragonreach (Klobiendar capital) ├── Survivors: Fireborn (became Fallen Dragon), Klobiendar remnants ├── Legacy: Goldenborn born at Dragonreach, Fallen Dragons, Julian the Dragon Tamer's story └── Part Of: Ge'or — Pre-Age of Baoth

docs.title: 🍃 The Elvish Diaspora
docs.text: "Elvengar burned. The elves scattered like seeds on the wind. Some took root. Some did not."

docs.title: 🎭 Overview
docs.text: When Elvengar collapsed during the Great Divergence (Year 0) and its Kutten Catastrophe aftermath, the elvish people did not die with their homeland. They fled. The Elvish Diaspora scattered elves across every continent of Ge'or — a migration that reshaped the demographic and cultural map of the post-Divergence world.

docs.title: 🗺️ Migration Routes
docs.text:
• Primary: Erisdar — Central Erisdar and South Erisdar received the largest elvish populations.
  • Secondary: Merratodoni — across the Formingar Ocean.
  • Scattered: Smaller populations reached every continent.

docs.title: 🏛️ Legacy
docs.text:
• The three surviving elvish states — Elvennrin, Elvenkrad, and Sousu — are direct descendants of the diaspora.
  • Elvish bloodlines were permanently diluted through interbreeding with local populations.
  • The elvish language survives only as a secondary tongue — no monolingual elvish communities remain.
  • The Great Elvish Persecution later attempted to exterminate what the diaspora had preserved.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Cause: The Kutten Catastrophe, fall of Elvengar
  • Period: 1–100 AGD
  • Destinations: Erisdar, Merratodoni, all continents
  • Result: Modern elvish states, Sousu
  • Related: Great Elvish Persecution

docs.title: 🐎 The Golden War
docs.text: "The gold ran out. The horsemen came."

docs.title: 🎭 Overview
docs.text: The Golden War was the war of the late Dwarf Era, fought as dwarven power declined.

docs.title: ⚔️ The War
docs.text: As the Romanium ore ran out and dwarven civilization weakened, human horse nomads from West and North Erisdar raided the faltering dwarven realms. The Golden War marked the end of dwarven dominance — the transition from the age of the dwarven megacities to the age of iron.

docs.title: 🏛️ Aftermath
docs.text: The war hastened the collapse of dwarven civilization. The dwarves never again reached the heights of their Romanium-powered era.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Era: Age 5 — Dwarf Era
  • Resource: Romanium — the exhaustion that invited the war
  • Species: Dwarves, Humans
  • See: Iron Age

docs.title: 🚢 The Great Ascension of Trade
docs.text: "Tino stole a boat. He found a continent. History is made by the desperate."

docs.title: 🎭 Overview
docs.text: The Great Ascension of Trade (170–597 AGD) was the era in which the trading republics of South Erisdar transformed from regional powers into intercontinental empires of commerce. The catalyst: one bankrupt man, one stolen boat, and a world far larger than anyone imagined.

docs.title: 🗺️ The Discovery of Lumina (170 AGD)
docs.text:
Tino the Explorer — a Vennerian merchant who had lost everything — stole a vessel and sailed into the unknown. After weeks at sea, he reached the coast of Lumina Continent.

The distances must be understood in context: Ge'or is 1.37× the size of Old Earth. What appears close on a map represents journeys far longer than anything Earth's Age of Discovery attempted. The sea between Erisdar and Lumina Continent is vast — and until Tino crossed it, no one knew what lay beyond.

docs.title: 📈 The Rise of the Republics
docs.text:
Tino's discovery opened the floodgates:

  • The Vennerian Trade Republic pioneered intercontinental commerce, establishing the network of outposts and colonies that persists today.
  • The Anos Plutocracy followed aggressively, competing for trade routes and colonial holdings.
  • Sousu projected its mercantile network across multiple continents.
  • The Limese League and Corinite League expanded their commercial reach.

docs.title: 🏴 No Mass Colonization
docs.text:
Unlike Earth's colonial era, Ge'or saw no mass colonization. The reasons:

  • Every continent had reached similar technological levels — no gunpowder gap, no one-sided conquest.
  • Diseases did not devastate native populations the way Old World pathogens ravaged the Americas on Earth.
  • Instead, the republics established trading outposts, mini-colonies, and commercial checkpoints — projecting influence through commerce, not conquest.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Started: 170 AGD — Tino discovers Lumina Continent
  • Ended: ~557 AGD — birth of Hermes Kennensbach (Age 11)
  • Key powers: Vennerian Trade Republic, Anos Plutocracy, Sousu, Limese League
  • Result: Intercontinental trade network, colonial outpost system

docs.title: 💀 The Kutten Catastrophe
docs.text: "The homeland became a graveyard of sand and poisoned air."

docs.title: 🎭 Overview
docs.text: For the first century after the Great Divergence (Year 0), the former elvish homeland of Elvengar on the Kutten continent underwent total ecological collapse. The island continent desertified entirely — a wasteland of sand and poisoned air.

docs.title: 🌪️ The Mechanism
docs.text:
The Great Divergence did not merely destroy Elvengar — it saturated the atmosphere above Kutten with poisonous rains and toxic air currents. Prevailing winds confined the worst of the contamination to Kutten, sparing other continents from the same severity — though they felt the effects at a distance.

For roughly 100 years, Kutten was uninhabitable.

docs.title: 🏃 The Elvish Diaspora
docs.text:
The surviving elves fled Kutten entirely. They migrated across the world:

  • Primary destination: Erisdar — especially Central Erisdar and South Erisdar
  • Secondary destination: Merratodoni — across the Formingar Ocean
  • Scattered populations reached every continent

This migration fundamentally reshaped the demographics of the post-Divergence world and scattered elvish bloodlines across Ge'or.

docs.title: 🏗️ Recolonization
docs.text: After ~100 years, the rains ceased. The air cleared. Recolonization efforts began — led primarily by the nations of Erisdar and the Demon Continent. Kutten today is a desert continent with scattered settlements, a shadow of the elvish homeland it once was.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Cause: Great Divergence (Year 0)
  • Location: Kutten, former site of Elvengar
  • Duration: ~100 years
  • Result: Elvish diaspora, desertification of Kutten

docs.title: ⚰️ The Hybrian Fate
docs.text:
The Hybrian hivemind was imprisoned — not killed, but sealed on a Fortress Planet by the Union of Sovereign Planets. There it suffers eternal torture, a sentence imposed by the victorious-but-not-victorious coalition.

But the Hybrian Shadows — the old philosopher-overseers — had separated from the hivemind before the end. They survived. They hid. They hibernated, waiting for the universe to forget everything, so they could begin again.

They are still waiting.

docs.title: ⏳ The Long Drift
docs.text:
The war ended millions of years ago. The refugee ship that brought every sentient species to Ge'or crashed only ~15,000 years before the Great Divergence. This gap — millions of years between the war's end and the ship's arrival — is not a contradiction. It is a wound.

The battleship that became Glorious Alliance did not travel at will. It drifted. After the war, with all economies collapsed and all empires dead, no one could build new FTL vessels. The ship that carried the refugees was a derelict — wounded, decaying, its crew in stasis, its navigation corrupted. It crawled through the void for millions of years on failing sublight drives, its passengers frozen in time, before entering Ge'or's atmosphere and splashing down in what is now the Formingar Ocean.

The war did not end and then the ship arrived. The war ended — and then nothing happened, for longer than the entire history of life on Old Earth, while a dead ship drifted through a dead universe.

docs.title: 🔗 Connection to Ge'or
docs.text:
The Last Great War is ancient history — but it is not dead. Every major species on Ge'or traces its presence on the planet to the war's aftermath:

  • Dragons — space-evolved, possibly veterans of the war
  • "Demons" — allied species who fought against the hivemind. Descended into myth.
  • Humans — the species that led the final push, destroyed Old Earth, and freed the universe — at the cost of their own apparent extinction
  • Hybrians — the enemy. Still here.
  • Tree Spirits of the Lyrical Forest — souls of coalition soldiers who fell during the war. Their consciousnesses merged with the forest over eons. Their roots retrieved artifacts from Glorious Alliance in the Formingar Ocean.

The war shaped everything. Ge'or is merely one of its unintended consequences. Its physical remnants still rest on the planet — most notably Glorious Alliance, the only known intact wreck from the conflict, lying at the bottom of the Formingar Ocean.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ The Last Great War ] ├── Combatant: Hybrians — The Hivemind ├── Combatant: Coalition of Galaxies — Hundreds of Thousands ├── Allied Species: Humans, Dragons, "Demons," others ├── Resulted In: Universal technological collapse, medieval feudalism ├── Created: The need for the Union of Sovereign Planets ├── Imprisoned The Hivemind On: Fortress Planet ├── Surviving Enemy: Shadows — The Hybrian Overseers, still active ├── Wreck on Ge'or: Glorious Alliance — Formingar Ocean — Refugee vessel that carried species from the war's aftermath, crashed ~15,000 BGD ├── Fallen Soldiers On Ge'or: Tree spirits of Lyrical Forest ├── Left Records In: Archive of the Traveler — Inside Ruins of Baoth └── Artifacts Retrieved: Shadow device — Given to Nethra

docs.title: ✨ The Twinning — 596 AGD
docs.text: "It found two women. It entered them. It waited."

docs.title: 🎭 Overview
docs.text:
In 596 AGD — one year before the protagonists' birth — the black agent, drifting Ge'or's seas since The Black Agent Escape — 254 AGD, found two women in the Grimmel Republic. It entered them. Incubated.

This is the Twinning: the moment the ancient minds the agent carried were twinned into the coming generation.

docs.title: 🧠 The Carried Minds
docs.text:
By the time of its escape, the black agent carried four minds (see Emrys — Life Before Ge'or):

  • Two human — the men who would become Emrys and Lucien.
  • Two machine — Ichi and Mana, consumed into the agent during the bunker vigil.

docs.title: ✨ The Twinning
docs.text:
• 596 AGD — the agent enters two women of the Grimmel Republic, of the Eisenheart and Mortvagn bloodlines.
  • They did not know. They did not consent. The agent chose their bloodlines — it did not ask. The mothers were hosts, not partners.
  • Ichi is twinned to be born as Emrys's twin sister — a real human soul.
  • Mana is carried dormant, to be born later into the Mortvagn line.

docs.title: 👶 The Births (597 AGD)
docs.text:
• Emrys Eisenheart and his twin sister Ichi — born in the Grimmel Republic.
  • Lucien Mortvagn — born twelve kilometers away.
  • The black agent incarnates. The Hope Goddess vision. The prophecy of the Two Heroes fulfilled.
  • ~600 AGD — Mana Mortvagn born as Lucien's little sister.

docs.title: 🌫️ In-World Knowledge
docs.text: The world knows nothing of the Twinning. It belongs to the same hidden truths as the Archive of the Traveler.

docs.title: ⚠️ The Claim — discovered very late
docs.text:
The gift carried a price the heroes could not see. The twinned are not merely powered by the black agent — they are made of it. Their souls were encoded in the agent for three million years; the agent runs in their blood; the will of quintillions of the dead moves through them.

The agent is both powerup and leash. The rise is built on it — the top-0.001% potential, the skill of the dead, the strength that makes them the Two Heroes — all of it is the agent doing its work. They use it freely, and it makes them nearly unstoppable. The leash is the part they do not see: the same substance that empowers them is a claim on them.

And the agent remembers its own. Deep beneath Goldenborn's Caldera, the Black Agent Hivemind — the collective mind born from the same substance, patient, inhuman, anti-Hybrian — senses them. The twinned are the richest concentration of its substance on Ge'or: not heroes, but the strongest nodes it has ever felt. It has not moved. It does not need to. It is patient.

Very late in their lives, the twinned discover the claim. The hivemind can reach through their blood — to feel, to pull, to corrupt, to take. The weapon that gave them their souls can take them back. They carry what they were sent to destroy: sent against the hivemind of Fortress Planet by the Hope Goddess, they find the enemy already inside them.

The counter — if one exists — has not been found. The way to win over the claim is the late question none of them can answer yet.
