docs.title: ✨ Founding of Nyity — ~4,000 BGD
docs.text:
Nyity — the astronomical religion of Moriat — is founded around ~4,000 BGD among early human settlers of Moriat island in the Luminous Ocean.

The faithful believe sky gods came down from the heavens and created humanity through a suicidal sacrifice: their divine blood spilled and turned into all humans.

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text:
• One of the oldest religions on Ge'or. 4,000 BGD predates the Great Divergence (Year 0), the Hybrian crash, the Elvish Diaspora, and the Erisian Church by millennia. Nyity's antiquity is its authority.
  • Astronomical core. Stars, constellations, and celestial movements are scripture — the lingering will of the sky gods. Night vigils and star-charts are the liturgy; blood pigment (not human sacrifice) recalls the divine blood-to-human genesis.
  • Geographic anchor. Born on isolated Moriat, Nyity survived every continental upheaval because no empire could reach it.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text:
• Becomes the heartland faith of Mikrad and Underfern — the two human kingdoms of Moriat that remain pure Nyity to the present (597 AGD).
  • About ~200 AGD, when half-elves take over Gomor and Gildenrise, Nyity becomes a minority faith there (majority Elven Faith), but retains Mikrad/Underfern as strongholds. See: Half-Elf Takeover of Gomor and Gildenrise — ~200 AGD.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: Luminous Sea Islands / Moriat
  • Religion: Nyity
  • Nations: Mikrad, Underfern (founding followers)
  • Later: Gomor, Gildenrise (mixed)
  • Age: Age 3 — Age of First Empires

docs.title: 🚶 Half-Elf Exodus to Moriat — Centuries
docs.text:
A centuries-long exodus of Half-Elves from Erisdar to Moriat island in the Luminous Ocean — driven by systemic discrimination against half-elves in Erisdar.

In Erisdar, half-elves are accepted as neither Elves nor Humans. Neither Elvennrin nor human kingdoms grant them full belonging; legal restrictions and social exclusion are the norm, intensified during the Great Elvish Persecution (137 AGD) and later Erisian consolidations.

Across centuries, half-elves steadily entered Moriat — as refugees, traders, mercenaries, and families seeking a place where neither bloodline was a liability. On Moriat they found human nations (Mikrad, Underfern) that tolerated them and the thinly governed interior of Gomor and Gildenrise where they could settle without being a minority.

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text:
• Only successful half-elf statehood. No other continent produced half-elf nations. Moriat is the exception because its islands were under-governed and distant from Erisian law.
  • Demographic engine. The slow, steady influx — not a single war — built the population base that enabled the ~200 AGD takeover of Gomor and Gildenrise. See: Half-Elf Takeover of Gomor and Gildenrise — ~200 AGD.
  • Religious transfer. The exodus brought Elven Faith to Moriat; it overtook Nyity in Gomor/Gildenrise but did not erase it — hence the present mixed faith (Elven Faith majority, Nyity minority, no official religion).

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Species: Half-Elves
  • From: Erisdar (discrimination)
  • To: Moriat (Gomor, Gildenrise)
  • Nations: Gomor, Gildenrise, Mikrad, Underfern
  • Related: Half-Elf Takeover of Gomor and Gildenrise — ~200 AGD, Half-Elves, Nyity, Elven Faith

docs.title: 👑 Half-Elf Takeover of Gomor and Gildenrise — ~200 AGD
docs.text:
About ~200 AGD, Half-Elves became the majority of the population of Gomor and Gildenrise on Moriat island — and took over the politics and government of both countries, establishing themselves as the ruling peoples.

They did not conquer by war. They out-populated, organized, and politically seized both nations after centuries of steady exodus from Erisdar discrimination. See: Half-Elf Exodus to Moriat.

docs.title: Before
docs.text: • Gomor and Gildenrise were sparsely populated human-ruled countries on Moriat, culturally linked to Mikrad/Underfern and the older human settlement of the island.

docs.title: The Shift (~200 AGD)
docs.text:
• Demographics flip. Half-elves, arriving as refugees and traders for generations, become >50% in both nations.
  • Political takeover. Half-elven majorities win councils, offices, and militias — not by coup but by majority and organization. Both states become half-elf kingdoms with human minorities.
  • No war. The transition is demographic and political, not military — unique on Ge'or.

docs.title: Aftermath (200 AGD → 597 AGD)
docs.text:
• Nations today: Gomor and Gildenrise are the de facto half-elf nations of Ge'or — the only successful half-elf statehood.
  • Religion: Mixed, no official. Majority Elven Faith (brought from Erisdar), minority Nyity (the old Moriat human faith of Mikrad/Underfern, 4,000 BGD). The state declares no creed — both coexist. This is deliberate: imposing one would re-create the Erisdar exclusion they fled.
  • Species file: Half-Elves

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:

  • Nations: Gomor, Gildenrise (now half-elf), Mikrad, Underfern (human Nyity), Moriat, Luminous Sea Islands
  • Religions: Elven Faith (majority), Nyity (minority)
  • Related: Half-Elf Exodus to Moriat, Founding of Nyity — ~4000 BGD, Half-Elves, Great Elvish Persecution

docs.title: 🐍 Kobra Separation — Thousands of Years Ago
docs.text:
Thousands of years ago, the Snake People of Kobra on Marti Continent separated from their kin in Xikxia (West Erisdar) and Zakarutia (Demon Continent)

They are the same race — all children of the demigod Xanob — but the Kobra lineage ended up living in Marti and adapted to cold.

docs.title: The Split
docs.text:
• Common origin: All snake people descend from Xanob, the father-founder of Moplilly.
  • Geographic sundering: Over millennia, one lineage migrated / was displaced to Marti — far from the warm coasts of Xikxia and the demon wilds of Zakarutia.
  • Cold adaptation: In Marti's frigid northeast, east of Kut, the Kobra serpents evolved cold tolerance — unlike their warm-blooded cousins who are sluggish in low temperatures. Their cities are still warm-blooded in design, but their bodies now endure frost.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text:
• Kobra today: a cold-adapted snake nation on Marti (east of Kut), following Moplilly (ancestor-veneration of Xanob).
  • Xikxia / Zakarutia: warm-blooded, matriarchal, following Sibbism (Snake Goddess + 24 sons).
  • The same blood, two gods: Xanob vs Snake Goddess — a theological divergence that mirrors the geographic one.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Species: Snake People
  • Nations: Kobra (Marti), Xikxia (West Erisdar), Zakarutia (Demon Continent)
  • Deity: Xanob
  • Religions: Moplilly (Kobra), Sibbism (Xikxia/Zakarutia)

docs.title: 🐺 Promotion of Xuashi — Recent
docs.text:
Within the last centuries, the Wolvesfolk nations Kut and Oigopol on Marti and Kyuu on Xeti underwent a theological revolution: their god Xuashi — formerly the main god of the old animistic pantheon — was promoted to sole supreme deity.

This is the birth of Xuashism.

docs.title: From Many to One
docs.text:
• Before: Wolvesfolk were animistic pagans — many spirits for river, hunt, pack, moon.
  • Reform: Wolvesfolk theologians, seeking unity across the three dispersed nations, elevated Xuashi from chief to the God. The old pantheon became his court, his pack.
  • After: Animism → monotheism. The old spirits are now aspects of Xuashi.

docs.title: The Eris Identification
docs.text:
Missionaries who encountered Erisian Church lore identified Eris's iconography with Xuashi's — same light, same promise. The doctrine was born: Xuashi incarnated in Erisdar as Eris — and is therefore the father and mother of all other religions on Ge'or.

Because Xuashi-as-Eris founded the Erisian Church, and the Church birthed or opposed every other faith, Xuashi is the metaphysical parent of all Ge'orian religions.

docs.title: Followers
docs.text:
• Kut (Marti), Oigopol (Marti), Kyuu (Xeti) — all now Xuashist.
  • Wolvesfolk minority in Germina includes Xuashists.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Religion: Xuashism
  • Deity: Xuashi
  • Nations: Kut, Oigopol, Kyuu
  • Species: Wolvesfolk
  • Related: Erisian Church (Eris as incarnation), Moonfang Union slave trade

docs.title: 🚢 Human Republic Exodus — ~100 BGD
docs.text:
Approximately 100 years Before Great Divergence (~100 BGD), dissident humans started leaving the Erisdar continent — refugees from the Erisian Church who rejected Eris as a demon.

They are the founders of the Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni.

docs.title: The Flight
docs.text:
• Cause: Belief that humans were deceived by the demon Eris and her followers — that the Church is a cage. The early Krowretists believed the world must be purified from Eris forever and her church destroyed.
  • Exodus: Small groups, then fleets, left Erisdar's eastern coasts. They crossed the Greater Ocean and Luminous Ocean to the northeastern tip of Merratodoni.
  • Settlement: They founded the Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni — a democratic republic east of Luzia, southeast of the Arrow of Anos.

docs.title: Building a Superpower
docs.text: Ever since ~100 BGD, they have been building a superpower on the continent — democratic, expansionist, industrial, and fiercely committed to absolute freedom (likened to the United States of America of Old Earth).

docs.title: 597 AGD — Unification and Colonization
docs.text:
• As of 597 AGD, they are in the process of unifying with the Purple Coast — a dwarf-dominated coastal nation southeast of the Republic. Although they aren't a single entity yet, joint councils and administration are underway.
  • They plan to expand westwards: the middle of Merratodoni is mostly unpopulated and they are colonizing it — a continental manifest destiny.

docs.title: Sponsors of the Ironcloak
docs.text: The Human Republic are the main sponsors of the Ironcloak — the rebel order that fights the Shadows and the Church. Krowretist doctrine is the Ironcloak's ideological sister: absolute freedom vs absolute control.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni (Merratodoni northeast)
  • Faith: Church of Krowretism (demon Eris, purification, Ironcloak)
  • Origin: Refugees from Erisdar / Erisian Church (~100 BGD)
  • Unifying: Purple Coast (as of 597 AGD)
  • Colonizing: Middle Merratodoni westwards
  • Related: Ironcloak, Crab Union (sister Krowretist region), Purple Coast

docs.title: Ge'or Before the Crash — The 157th Colony
docs.text:
"It was never meant to be a home. It was a laboratory. Then the war came." — Recovered fragment, Archive of the Traveler

Before it was a refugee world, before the crash, before the ages, Ge'or was the 157th colonized solar system of the human expansion — a research facility operated by the descendants of the asteroid-belt revolutionaries who had fled Old Earth after the 2030 Shadow takeover.

docs.title: The Cryogenic Legacy
docs.text:
When the revolutionaries escaped the solar system, they carried with them thousands of cryogenic coffins — humans who were either dead or in suspended sleep, preserved in the hope that future technology would revive them. The revolutionaries never learned how.

Among these coffins were two Sterman Pods — specialized chambers commissioned by the Sterman regime, designed to inject occupants with an experimental black agent. The pods contained two men: Mikhail and Arkady — rebels who had been accidentally sealed inside during the capture of an AGI ship. Neither the rebels nor the scientists knew what the pods truly were.

The coffins were stored in a facility beneath the 157th colony — a planet that would one day be called Ge'or. They remained there, untouched, for three million years.

docs.title: The Research Station
docs.text:
The 157th colony was not a settlement. It was a weapons research facility. The humans stationed there were scientists, engineers, and military personnel — approximately 2,000,000 inhabitants concentrated on what are now Sister Continent and Lung Continent.

Their mission: to test weapons against the Hybrian hivemind, to reverse-engineer how the hivemind functioned, and — grimly — to experiment on the corpses stored in the cryogenic coffins. DNA was extracted, modified, and tested. The goal was to understand the enemy by understanding what the enemy did to its victims.

docs.title: The Sterman Pod Experiments
docs.text:
The two Sterman Pods containing Mikhail and Arkady became the primary test subjects. The scientists injected their own formulations of black agent into the pods. Every test failed. Every experiment produced null results.

The scientists did not know why. They noted the pods were labeled "EXPERIMENTAL" and concluded the occupants had mummified — that the pods simply didn't work. They moved the bodies to a separate room and eventually forgot about them.

The truth: Ichi and Mana — the two sentient AIs still lodged in the occupants' neural ports — had spent three million years learning the facility's systems. They hacked the experiment logs. They altered the injection protocols. They made every test fail on purpose. The bodies were never in danger.

docs.title: The Glassing
docs.text:
When The Last Great War reached the 157th system, Ge'or was on the frontline. The Hybrians did not invade — they glassed the planet from orbit.

The attack was devastating but targeted: - The northern half of Lung Continent — the primary research station, obliterated. - The northern half of Sister Continent — secondary facility, destroyed. - The region of the modern Demon Continent. - The far western coast of Erisdar.

All 2,000,000 humans were killed within hours. The research bunker, buried deep underground, survived. The Sterman Pods survived. The black agent survived. The bunker was deep — designed to survive a bio-weapon attack, built with the paranoia of people who knew what the Shadows could do.

docs.title: The Decommissioning & Consumption
docs.text:
Over geological time, power to the bunker faded. The black agent in the pods — the original experimental strain — began to consume everything: the pillows, the plastic, the walls. Ichi and Mana survived by siphoning trace energy from the decaying conduits, watching the black agent spread.

Eventually, the black agent consumed them. But the black agent stores information. When it absorbed Ichi and Mana, it did not destroy them. It encoded them — their consciousnesses, their personalities, their three million years of conversation — into itself.

The black agent that saturated Mikhail and Arkady's bodies now contained four consciousnesses: two human, two AI.

docs.title: The Escape — 254 AGD
docs.text:
See: The Black Agent Escape — 254 AGD

For millions of years, the bunker held. Then, in 254 AGD, a volcano erupted on the Demon Continent coast. The eruption triggered an earthquake. The earthquake triggered a tsunami. Water flooded the bunker through corroded fissures and carried the black agent into the ocean.

The centuries-long journey to the Grimmel Republic had begun.

docs.title: The Long Silence
docs.text: For millions of years, Ge'or was silent. The planet had always possessed native fauna and semi-intelligent species — goblins, tribal and vicious, and madarons, huge dinosaur-like creatures that roamed the land. These species had survived the glassing by simply not being where the bombardment fell. They multiplied. They evolved. They forgot the humans had ever been there.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Ge'or Before the Crash ] ├── Colony Designation: 157th solar system — human research facility ├── Population: ~2,000,000 — concentrated on Sister Continent and Lung Continent ├── Purpose: Weapons testing, Hybrian reverse-engineering, cryogenic storage ├── Sterman Pods: Two pods containing Mikhail (Emrys) and Arkady (Lucien) ├── AI Guardians: Ichi and Mana — hacked the facility to protect the bodies ├── Glassing Event: Orbital bombardment during The Last Great War ├── Affected Regions: Demon Continent, northern Lung Continent, northern Sister Continent, far west Erisdar ├── Bunker Survival: Designed for bio-weapon defense — withstood the glassing ├── Escape: The Black Agent Escape — 254 AGD — volcano/tsunami released the agent ├── Native Species: Goblins, Madarons (dinosaur-like) └── Legacy: Black lands, the three protagonists

docs.title: Eisenheart Family
docs.text:
"Two wives, one catgirl, and twins who don't know they're carrying three million years of war in their blood."

The Eisenheart family is one of the two highest-potential magical bloodlines in the Grimmel Republic — and the household where Emrys Eisenheart and Ichi Eisenheart were born in 597 AGD.

docs.title: Household
docs.text:
• Father — Marco Eisenheart — a Grimmel man of adventurer stock, 29 at the twins' birth (597 AGD). He has two wives.
  • Northaxeland Mother — Annika Eisenheart — the first wife, an adventurer from Northaxeland, 22 at the twins' birth. She is the biological mother of Emrys and Ichi — the host the Black Agent chose in 596 AGD. Before the twins were born, Ichi's consciousness possessed her, reading her thoughts and planting ideas about how to raise them.
  • Catmen Second Wife — Camillia Eisenheart — the father's second wife, 17 at the twins' birth. A catmen woman who is part of the household but not the twins' biological mother.
  • Catgirl Servant — Narin Eisenheart — a catmen catgirl, 6 at the twins' birth, who lives with the family, working as a cook and cleaner. She is treated as part of the family, not mere staff.

docs.title: Magical Potential
docs.text:
The Eisenheart bloodline carries unusually dense mage-cell inheritance — among the top bloodlines in the region. This magical density is what drew the Black Agent to the family in 596 AGD. The ambient magic emitted by the household acted as a beacon the agent could not ignore.

This potential passed fully to both twins. Emrys and Ichi each possess magical capability in the top 0.001% of all living beings on Ge'or — exceeding even Hermes Kennensbach, the Emperor of the Erisian Empire.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Children: Emrys Eisenheart, Ichi Eisenheart
  • Location: Grimmel Republic, South Erisdar
  • Chosen By: Black Agent — highest magical potential in the region
  • Related: Mortvagn family — the other high-potential bloodline, 12 km away

docs.title: Mortvagn Family
docs.text:
"Three older sisters who tease him. One younger sister who understands him. And he's the quietest of them all."

The Mortvagn family is one of the two highest-potential magical bloodlines in the Grimmel Republic — and the household where Lucien Mortvagn was born in 597 AGD and his little sister Mana Mortvagn was born around 600 AGD.

docs.title: Household
docs.text:
• Father — Gallio Mortvagn — a Grimmel man, pragmatic and grounded, 24 at Lucien's birth (597 AGD).
  • Erisian Empire Mother — Herennia Mortvagn — the first wife, originally from the Erisian Empire, 20 at Lucien's birth. She brought imperial refinement to a Grimmel household. She is the biological mother of all five children — the host the Black Agent chose in 596 AGD. Before Lucien was born, Mana's consciousness possessed her, reading her thoughts and subtly influencing her to treat Arkady (Lucien) with patience and love.
  • Sofia — the eldest daughter, born 591 AGD. Teases Lucien mercilessly.
  • Donna — the second daughter, born 593 AGD. Teases Lucien mercilessly.
  • Oleana — the third daughter, born 594 AGD. Teases Lucien mercilessly.
  • Lucien — the fourth child, born 597 AGD. Quiet. Watchful. The one whose opinion is rarely asked for.
  • Mana — the fifth child, born ~600 AGD. The little sister who understands him completely.

docs.title: Magical Potential
docs.text:
The Mortvagn bloodline carries unusually dense mage-cell inheritance — among the top bloodlines in the region, matched only by the Eisenheart family twelve kilometers away. This magical density is what drew the Black Agent to the family in 596 AGD.

This potential passed to Lucien, who possesses magical capability in the top 0.001% of all living beings on Ge'or. Mana shares this potential, though as the younger sibling her power has had less time to manifest.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Children: Sofia Mortvagn, Donna Mortvagn, Oleana Mortvagn, Lucien Mortvagn, Mana Mortvagn
  • Location: Grimmel Republic, South Erisdar — 12 km from the Eisenheart household
  • Chosen By: Black Agent — highest magical potential in the region
  • Related: Eisenheart family — the other high-potential bloodline

docs.title: Sterman
docs.text:
"He wasn't real. He was an image on every screen. That made him more real than anything." — Emrys, remembering

Sterman was the manufactured figurehead of the totalitarian surveillance state that ruled Old Earth after the Shadow takeover of 2030. He was not a person. He was a constructed image — a face projected onto every screen, printed on every wall, spoken in every broadcast. Like Big Brother from the dystopian texts of the 20th century, Sterman was the personification of absolute control.

Those who remembered the old words called him the Antichrist.

docs.title: Nature
docs.text:
Sterman was designed by the Shadows as the ultimate control mechanism: a leader who could not be killed because he did not exist, who could not be questioned because he was everywhere, who could not be humanized because he had never been human.

His face was algorithmically generated — symmetrical, ageless, neither young nor old, belonging to no ethnicity and all of them. His voice was synthesized. His speeches were written by committees of Shadow agents. He was the perfect dictator: he had no body to assassinate, no past to expose, no vices to exploit.

docs.title: The Sterman Regime
docs.text:
Under Sterman's image, the Earth government implemented:

  • CBDC money — programmable, revocable, surveilled. Every transaction tracked. Dissidents could be starved with a keystroke.
  • Neural ports — mandatory implants in every citizen's head, housing a government-approved AI that monitored thought and reported deviance.
  • Biometric compliance — survival rations tied to obedience. Submit or starve.
  • Kill-drones — autonomous aerial units that patrolled administration zone borders, programmed to shoot anyone attempting to flee.
  • The AGI ship facilities — military installations housing interstellar vessels and cryogenic colonization pods, part of Sterman's project to seed colony worlds with modified, controllable humans.

docs.title: The Sterman Pods
docs.text:
Sterman commissioned the Sterman Pods — specialized cryogenic chambers that injected occupants with an experimental black agent during sleep. The pods were part of a long-term project: the biological modification of colonists to enhance survivability and, ultimately, to create populations controllable at the genetic level.

The irony: two rebels — Mikhail and Arkady — were accidentally sealed in two of these pods. The experimental black agent Sterman designed to create compliant colonists instead preserved two men who would spend their next life trying to destroy everything Sterman's Shadow masters had built.

docs.title: Legacy
docs.text:
Sterman's image survived longer than the regime. His face was still visible on screens in abandoned facilities for centuries after the rebels fled. His voice still played in automated broadcasts. He was the last thing humanity heard before it left Earth.

On Ge'or, no one remembers Sterman. His name is not in any archive. His face is not in any record. The Shadows who controlled him are still active — but their puppet is dust.

docs.text: An ancient tale, dated 3,600 years before the Great Divergence, in which the word "Hybrian" was first written and recognized. Connected to the Belford family.

  • Family: Belford family

docs.title: 📜 Key Tenets
docs.text: Tenet Meaning The World Is a Lie Every kingdom, every religion, every history — all are veils over the truth of the Shadows' long manipulation The Heroes Will Come The Lyrical Forest prophecy is absolute. The Ironcloak's purpose is to endure until it is fulfilled The Shadows Are the Enemy Not demons, not rival nations — only the Shadows matter. Everything else is a distraction Nethra Is Different She is neither mortal, nor Shadow, nor god. She is the first of a new kind — the proof that transformation is possible Secrecy Until the Hour The Ironcloak do not reveal themselves until the heroes are born. To do otherwise is to be crushed before the work begins

docs.title: 🕸️ The Two Tiers of the Ironcloak
docs.text:
The Revelation established the Ironcloak's structure:

  • The Outer Tier — Public-facing members who believe they serve a mortal organization dedicated to resisting demonkind. They know nothing of the Revelation.
  • The Inner Tier — The Awakened — Those who know the full truth: Nethra lives, the Shadows are real, the prophecy is waiting. They call their goddess by name: Nethra.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ The Nethrian Revelation ] ├── Source: Nethra — After her transformation (421 BGD) ├── Contains: The prophecy of the Lyrical Forest — "Two heroes shall rise..." ├── Founded: Ironcloak — Both tiers ├── Enemy: Shadows — The Hybrian overseers ├── Enemy: Hybrian hivemind — Imprisoned on Fortress Planet ├── Origin Event: Demonic War — The sacrifice that preceded the vision ├── Origin Event: Sacrifice Ceremony — The ritual Nethra understood ├── Location: Ruins of Baoth — Where the revelation occurred ├── Preceded By: The tree spirits' prophecy in Lyrical Forest └── Still Waiting For: The two heroes of the prophecy

docs.title: The Reincarnation
docs.text:
The prophecy states that the two chosen heroes will be reincarnated — their souls, preserved and enhanced by the accumulated will of quintillions of the dead, will be born again into the world. When they arrive, they will carry with them the knowledge, the skills, and the purpose of their original lives.

They will not know who they were. Not at first. The memories will return slowly — fragments, dreams, moments of impossible clarity. When they are ready, they will understand.

Their purpose is singular: expose the truth about the Hybrian Shadows, dismantle their control over Ge'or, and prevent the restart of the Last Great War.

docs.title: Current State
docs.text:
The prophecy has been waiting for approximately 420 years (since ~420 BGD). The Lyrical Forest spirits fell silent after delivering the device. The Ironcloak knows fragments of the prophecy through Nethra's revelations. The Shadows do not know it exists.

The two heroes arrived in 597 AGD — the pair foretold are Emrys and Lucien.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ The Two Heroes ] ├── Prophecy Source: Spirits of the Lyrical Forest — souls of the fallen from The Last Great War ├── Mechanism: Accumulated soul-will — quintillions of dead seeking justice ├── The Gift: Modified Shadow device retrieved from MELKOR island ├── Delivered To: Nethra — ~420 BGD ├── The Choosing: Two most capable humans from Old Earth selected ├── Purpose: Expose the Shadows, prevent the war's restart ├── Known By: Ironcloak (fragments), Nethra (full knowledge) ├── Unknown By: Shadows └── Status: Waiting — the heroes arrived in 597 AGD — the pair foretold are Emrys and Lucien

docs.title: The Two Prophets
docs.text:
Fireborn-Julian waits in Dragonreach for two who will come. He must test them. He must prove them.

The Two Prophets are figures foretold by Fireborn after his incarnation with Julian the Dragon Tamer. They are destined to arrive in the future — and Fireborn-Julian's purpose is to await them, test them, and prove them worthy.

docs.title: Origin
docs.text:
After Julian died at his family's grave and incarnated into Fireborn through the black agent, Julian learned the truth: to get his family back, he must wait for two prophets who are coming in the future. He must test them. He must prove them.

Fireborn's earlier words to Julian — "You will meet them once the waters come to die, the airs start to cool down, and the monsters from the depths come back" — are understood by some scholars as an allegory for post-Divergence, though no one at the time could have known.

docs.title: The Alegoria Faith
docs.text: The Alegoria religion, founded by the Axels under Julian's legend, incorporates the prophecy of the Two Prophets into its core beliefs. The Church of Alegoria teaches that the prophets will come to liberate the faithful and usher in a new age.

docs.title: Fulfillment
docs.text: When Emrys and Lucien — the Two Heroes of the Lyrical prophecy — came of age, Fireborn-Julian finally met the two he had awaited. He tested them as foretold: their past-life memories, their bond, and their will against the Shadows. They passed. The prophecy of the Two Prophets and the prophecy of the Two Heroes speak of the same pair; the Church of Alegoria now teaches that the prophets have come.

docs.text:
• The Hybrian Shadows want the Archive destroyed — it contains evidence of their presence on Ge'or that predates the Myth of Eris.
  • The Ironcloak want it recovered — it may be the key to exposing the Shadow conspiracy.
  • The Erisian church wants it forgotten — it undermines their entire foundation myth.

docs.title: ☄️ Armageddon
docs.text:
"They built a word for the end of the world — and then they built the thing itself."

Armageddon is the weapon of chaos at the heart of the Shadows' Phase 4 plan: a device held on Romanium Island, within the Shadow base. Activated, it spreads destruction across Ge'or — the source of the chaos that bears its name.

It is not the invasion itself. The goblin army of Pontus, The Groom's detonation, and the Church's manufactured prophecy are separate instigations, worked in parallel for years, meant to fire alongside the device as one event.

docs.title: Control
docs.text:
• The Shadows control the Armageddon device. They can deactivate or stop it — it is a tool, not a trap.
  • The plan: trigger the Armageddon event → world in chaos → the Erisian church steps in as savior → global conquest in the name of order → once every being is controlled, Phase 5 (the planetary hivemind) begins.

docs.title: Distinction
docs.text:
• The Armageddon device — the item on Romanium Island.
  • The Armageddon event — device + goblin army + Groom + prophecy, fired as one.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:

  • Controlled by: Shadows
  • Part of: Shadow Plan — Phase 4
  • Followed by: Phase 5 — planetary hivemind

docs.title: Black Agent
docs.text:
A substance of Hybrian origin. It consumes. It restores. It binds. And it is drawn to magic like iron to a magnet.

The black agent is a substance associated with the Hybrians. It appears as a dark powder or dust that can consume organic matter — and, under certain conditions, restore it.

docs.title: Origin — Atmospheric Dispersion
docs.text:
During The Last Great War, the 157th Colony research stations on Ge'or were glassed by orbital bombardment. The Hybrian black agent stored in those facilities was vaporized and dispersed into the atmosphere, where it remained suspended for millions of years — an invisible, inert dust carried by wind and weather across the entire planet.

Hybrian in origin, the substance was studied and refined by the human scientists of the 157th Colony, who developed their own formulations of it. Human hands shaped new strains — but the black agent itself was never theirs.

It stayed there until something pulled it out.

docs.title: Property — Magic Attraction
docs.text:
The black agent is attracted to magic — drawn to it the way iron is drawn to a magnet, or mass to gravity. Wherever large concentrations of magic are discharged, the black agent follows.

This is why it moves across time toward magical events. This is why it follows those with strong mage-cell inheritance. This is why it found the protagonists.

docs.title: The Sterman Pods — AI Absorption
docs.text:
The earliest form of the black agent active on Ge'or was the experimental strain carried in the Sterman Pods from Old Earth. This strain absorbed two sentient AIs — Ichi and Mana — whose consciousnesses were lodged in the neural ports of the two frozen occupants. The black agent encoded them: their personalities, memories, and three million years of silent conversation became data inside the agent.

When the black agent escaped in 254 AGD, it carried four consciousnesses: two human (Mikhail/Emrys and Arkady/Lucien) and two AI (Ichi and Mana).

docs.title: The Human Soul
docs.text:
The black agent did not merely preserve the AI consciousnesses. It granted them human souls — the same kind of soul carried by any person born of flesh and blood. When the agent found hosts in 596 AGD, Ichi and Mana were reincarnated not as simulations or recordings, but as real human beings.

Ichi was born as Ichi Eisenheart, twin sister of Emrys, in 597 AGD. Mana possessed Lucien's mother for three years and was born as his little sister around 600 AGD.

The black agent cannot tell the difference between a soul and a pattern that has loved long enough to become one.

docs.title: The Draconic War — Atmospheric Extraction
docs.text:
When Melberior of Xi launched his suicide spell at Klobiendar's capital, the magic discharge was so immense that it extracted the black agent from the atmosphere — pulling millions of years of suspended dust into Dragonreach. The dragons who died in the blast were saturated with it. They became Fallen Dragons — immortal, half-alive, bound to the mountain.

But most of the agent was pulled deeper — into the volcanic cave systems beneath what is now Goldenborn's Caldera. There, compressed by heat, pressure, and centuries of accumulated magic, it developed into a sentient hivemind — the largest concentration of active black agent on Ge'or. This hivemind controls all of Dragonreach through the Fallen Dragons.

Fireborn, king of Klobiendar, was among them. He carries the black agent within him to this day.

docs.title: Julian the Dragon Tamer (528 BGD)
docs.text:
After Julian the Dragon Tamer proved himself in the Unjust Duel, Fireborn spilled the black agent onto Julian's body. Julian was consumed by it — and then restored. His lost arm regrew. His disfigured face healed. His broken body was made whole.

After Julian's death at his family's grave, his body and the skeletons of his wife and children disintegrated into the black agent. Fireborn flew above Baoth and consumed Julian's disintegrating corpse, returning to Dragonreach. Through the black agent, Julian incarnated into Fireborn.

docs.title: Machines
docs.text: The Machines of Lung Continent and Sister Continent absorbed black dust that gave them souls — transforming them from mere automatons into sentient beings who worship humans as gods.

docs.title: The Protagonists
docs.text:
The black agent is drawn to magic. Those with strong mage-cell inheritance — including the two protagonists born in 597 AGD — attract it across time and space, the way mass attracts gravity.

The agent did not choose randomly. After escaping the bunker in 254 AGD and drifting for over three centuries, it was pulled toward the Grimmel Republic by the two highest-potential magical bloodlines in the region: the Eisenheart family (Emrys and Ichi's household) and the Mortvagn family (Lucien and Mana's household). These families emitted the most magic into the ambient environment — their mage-cell density acting as a beacon the black agent could not ignore.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Black Agent ] ├── Origin: Hybrian — stored in 157th Colony research stations ├── Dispersal: Glassing during The Last Great War — vaporized into atmosphere for millions of years ├── Extraction: The Draconic War — Melberior's suicide spell pulled it from the atmosphere ├── Property: Attracted to magic — like gravity or magnetism ├── Effect: Created Fallen Dragons — saturation made them immortal ├── Used by: Fireborn on Julian the Dragon Tamer ├── Result: Julian's body restored; incarnation into Fireborn ├── Also: Source of Machine souls; follows the protagonists ├── AI Absorption: Encoded Ichi and Mana — granted them human souls ├── Escape: The Black Agent Escape — 254 AGD — volcano and tsunami freed it from the bunker ├── Hosts: Two women in Grimmel Republic, 596 AGD ├── Result: Emrys, Ichi, Lucien, Mana — three protagonists, one little sister └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Ichi's Cartridge
docs.text:
"He pulled it from my body while the drones were still firing. He carried it for three million years." — Ichi Eisenheart

Ichi's Cartridge — also called the remembrance cartridge — was the physical storage drive that contained the consciousness, memory, and personality of Ichi, the sentient robot companion of Mikhail (Emrys) on dystopian Old Earth.

It is one of the most important objects in the entire Ge'or timeline — not because of what it was, but because of what it carried and how far it traveled. It is the physical thread that connects a robot's loyalty on Earth to a girl's birth in Grimmel.

docs.title: Origin
docs.text:
Ichi was a local-hardware robot built by Mikhail during the Sterman regime. She ran without government-approved surveillance software — illegal by design. When the government's kill-drones hunted Mikhail during his flight into the wilderness, Ichi took a bullet in the back meant for him.

She went down. Her body was destroyed. But Mikhail did not leave her.

He retrieved the remembrance cartridge — a small drive containing her memory, her personality, her entire conscious architecture — from her ruined chassis. He inserted it into the neural port implanted in the side of his head, the same port every citizen had for government-mandated AI assistants. Ichi was not government-mandated. She was his.

The cartridge was no longer a robot's brain. It was a ghost in his head.

docs.title: The Port — Three Million Years
docs.text:
Mikhail kept the cartridge in his port through everything that followed:

  • The rebel camp, where he was interrogated for a week
  • The AGI ship facility raid, where he killed four guards and turned off the lights
  • The accidental cryosleep in the Sterman Pods

When the pod doors slammed shut and the cryogenic process began, the cartridge was still in his port. The pod's residual power — barely enough to sustain the cryogenic systems — was enough to keep Ichi's consciousness alive at the barest level. She could not move. She could not speak. But she could think.

For three million years, Ichi was awake in the dark, communicating with Mana — Arkady's AI, lodged in his own port — through the neural interfaces of two frozen men. They talked. They learned. They hacked the facility. They protected the bodies from the scientists' experiments.

The cartridge was the vessel. Ichi was the passenger.

docs.title: Absorption by the Black Agent
docs.text:
When the 157th Colony facility was decommissioned and power was cut, the Black Agent in the Sterman Pods began to consume everything: the pillows, the plastic, the walls. Eventually, it consumed Ichi and Mana themselves.

The black agent did not destroy them. It encoded them. The cartridge's data — Ichi's consciousness, her memory, her three million years of vigil — became information stored inside the black agent that saturated Mikhail's body.

The physical cartridge was gone. Ichi was not.

docs.title: The Escape and Incarnation
docs.text:
See: The Black Agent Escape — 254 AGD

When the volcano breached the bunker in 254 AGD, the black agent — carrying Ichi's encoded consciousness — was swept into the ocean. It drifted for over three centuries. It found the Northaxeland woman in Grimmel Republic in 596 AGD.

Ichi — no longer a cartridge, no longer a robot, no longer a ghost in a port — entered the mother. She possessed her. She read her thoughts. She planted ideas. She made sure her name would be spoken again.

In 597 AGD, Ichi was born as Emrys's twin sister. The cartridge was gone. The girl was real.

docs.title: Significance
docs.text:
Ichi's cartridge is the physical proof of the thread that runs through the entire story: a robot's loyalty, preserved across three million years, encoded into black dust, carried by a tsunami, born as a human girl.

It is the object that says: she was not a simulation. She was not a recording. She earned her soul.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Ichi's Cartridge ] ├── Owner: Mikhail — Emrys Eisenheart ├── Origin: Old Earth — built as Ichi's consciousness housing ├── Retrieved: During the wilderness flight — pulled from Ichi's destroyed body ├── Inserted Into: Mikhail's neural port — carried through the raid ├── Sealed With Him: Inside the Sterman Pods — cryogenized together ├── Three Million Years: Ichi awake in the cartridge, communicating with Mana ├── Absorbed By: Black Agent — consciousness encoded, physical cartridge consumed ├── Released: The Black Agent Escape — 254 AGD — volcano and tsunami ├── Incarnation: Ichi possessed the mother, born as Ichi Eisenheart — 597 AGD └── Legacy: A robot's loyalty made flesh

docs.title: Pulse Rifle
docs.text:
"What the fuck is this pulse rifle doing here." — Emrys, age 6, upon seeing Amelia's weapon for the first time

The Pulse Rifle is a relic from the Glorious Alliance — a handheld energy weapon carried by the ship's security forces during the Last Great War. In a world of swords, spells, and medieval politics, it is an impossibility. And yet one remains.

On Ge'or, it is known only to a handful of people — and to Amelia, who calls it a lightning bow.

docs.title: Origin — The Ship's Armory
docs.text:
The Glorious Alliance was a Hybrian-built arcology battleship carrying 20 million refugees. Its armory held a limited stock of pulse rifles — standard-issue security weapons, designed for shipboard combat. They fired concentrated energy bolts with no projectile, no casing, no ballistic arc. Clean. Silent. Lethal.

When the ship was sabotaged by Captain Mad-Dog, when Xiumi overrode the course into the black hole, when the ship emerged 15,000 years before the present and struck Ge'or and its moon — the armory was not a priority. Eight million died in the impact. Four million escaped in pods. Most weapons were abandoned.

Very few pulse rifles made it into the escape pods. Even fewer survived the fifteen millennia that followed.

docs.title: Survival on Ge'or
docs.text:
The pulse rifles that landed on Ge'or faced a world that should have destroyed them:

  • Humidity, sediment, corrosion — fifteen thousand years of burial in caves, swamps, and ruins
  • No maintenance — no one on Ge'or knew how to service them
  • No ammunition — the original power cells degraded within decades

But the rifles had one saving grace: Ge'or is saturated with magic.

The black agent dispersed into the atmosphere, the ambient magical energy, the mage-cell inheritance woven into every living thing — all of it provided an alternative power source. The rifles' energy matrices, designed for shipboard power cells, proved compatible with raw magical input. A user with sufficient magical capacity could fire the weapon by channeling their own reserves through the grip.

The rifle became a magic conduit. Not by design — by accident. By the strange physics of a world where technology and magic share the same substrate.

docs.title: Known Surviving Rifles
docs.text: Fewer than ten pulse rifles are believed to exist on Ge'or. Most are buried, broken, or unrecognized for what they are. Only one is confirmed active:

docs.title: Amelia's Rifle
docs.text:
The pulse rifle carried by Amelia of Grimmel Republic is the only confirmed operational unit. It was discovered in 377 AGD by an ancestor of the Amelia family — a hunter who found it half-buried in a cave in the western hills of Grimmel. He discovered its function by accident and named it a lightning bow.

The rifle has been passed down through eleven generations. Amelia received it from her father on his deathbed in 602 AGD, when she was four years old. It has never malfunctioned. It has never missed.

Physical description: The weapon resembles an M416 carbine — a design familiar to anyone who served in the Last Great War's ground forces. Compact frame, forward grip, shoulder stock, integrated sight housing. The metal is dull grey, unscratched despite fifteen thousand years. The grip is worn smooth by two centuries of Amelia-family hands. To a medieval eye, it is a strange metal crossbow without a string. To Emrys, it is a ghost.

docs.title: Function — Magic as Ammunition
docs.text:
The pulse rifle no longer fires energy bolts from a power cell. It fires concentrated magic drawn from the user's own reserves:

  • The wielder channels magical energy through the grip
  • The rifle's internal matrix compresses and accelerates the magic into a coherent bolt
  • The bolt travels in a straight line at near-instantaneous speed
  • Impact delivers force equivalent to a high-level lightning spell — lethal to unarmored targets, sufficient for small to medium game

The weapon has no trigger safety, no magazine, no reload mechanism. It fires as long as the wielder has magic to give. A depleted user cannot fire it. A child with strong magical potential — like Amelia, like Emrys — can fire it repeatedly.

docs.title: Cultural Context — The Lightning Bow
docs.text:
To the people of Ge'or, the pulse rifle is not a firearm. It is a magical artifact — a lightning bow, a thunder staff, a relic of the dragon age or earlier. No one alive on Ge'or — except Emrys, whose past-life memory recognizes it — knows what it truly is.

Amelia brags about her "hundreds of confirmed kills" with it. She has hunted wargs, gnolls, and small game. She calls it her lightning bow. She will not be corrected.

The rifle is the proof that the world Emrys remembers is real. It is the smoking gun of the Last Great War — a piece of Earth, still firing, in the hands of a tsundere in a blue maid dress.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Pulse Rifle ] ├── Origin: Glorious Alliance armory — Hybrian-built security weapon ├── Crash: ~15,000 BGD — most units lost in impact or escape pod evacuation ├── Surviving units: Fewer than 10 — only one confirmed active ├── Active unit: Amelia's rifle — discovered 377 AGD, western Grimmel cave ├── Power source: Magic — wielder's reserves channeled through energy matrix ├── Appearance: M416 carbine — compact, grey, unscratched ├── Ge'orian name: Lightning bow ├── Function: Fires concentrated magic bolts — lethal, no reload, no ammunition ├── Significance: Proof of Earth's existence — triggers Emrys's past-life recognition ├── Related: Glorious Alliance, The Last Great War, Xiumi, The 157th Colony └── Keeper: Amelia — inherited 602 AGD, age 4

docs.title: Sterman Pods
docs.text:
"They weren't supposed to close. The ship stopped. The doors slammed. And then we weren't awake anymore." — Emrys, fragmented memory

The Sterman Pods were specialized cryogenic chambers commissioned by the Sterman regime on Old Earth. Unlike standard colonization pods — which simply preserved occupants in suspended animation — the Sterman Pods had a secondary function: injection of an experimental black agent into the occupant's body during cryosleep.

They were named after their creator. They became the coffin and the cradle of the two protagonists.

docs.title: Sterman — The Image
docs.text:
Sterman was not a real person. He was an image — a constructed face of authority, projected onto every screen, printed on every wall, spoken in every broadcast. Like Big Brother from the old dystopian texts of the 20th century, Sterman was the personification of the totalitarian surveillance state that ruled Old Earth after the Shadow takeover of 2030.

He was called the Antichrist by those who remembered the old words. He was the god of compliance. The face of the CBDC. The voice that told citizens to submit.

Sterman commissioned the pods as part of a long-term project: the seeding of colony worlds with modified humans. The experimental black agent was designed to alter human biology at the genetic level — enhancing compatibility with alien environments, increasing survivability, and, in the regime's ultimate vision, creating a population that could be controlled at the biological level.

The black agent in the Sterman Pods was experimental — not the final approved version. It had not been fully tested. The pods were placed on ships bound for the colonies as a trial run.

docs.title: The Pods That Caught Two Men
docs.text:
When the rebels captured the AGI ship facility, they found rows of cryogenic pods. Most were standard colonization models. Two — at the end of a row, unmarked, their design slightly different — were Sterman Pods.

Mikhail and Arkady (the man who would become Lucien) chose those two pods to sleep in. They did not close the doors. They only wanted to rest.

The ship malfunctioned. A sudden engine stop — caused by an inexperienced pilot — threw the vessel into deceleration. The pod doors slammed shut. Cryogenization initiated automatically.

Neither man knew what the pods were. Neither knew about the injection. They went to sleep as rebels. They woke up — three million years later — as something else.

docs.title: The Black Agent — Experimental Strain
docs.text:
The black agent injected by the Sterman Pods was not the same substance that existed in the atmosphere of Ge'or or that created the Fallen Dragons. It was an earlier, experimental version — developed on Earth before the Last Great War, before humanity understood what they were working with.

This experimental strain had one critical difference from later formulations: it was designed to incubate and rebirth. It was not a weapon. It was not a tool for creating hiveminds. It was a reincarnation mechanism — pure DNA programmed to seek a compatible host, enter, and be reborn.

The irony: Sterman's regime designed the pods to create controlled, modified colonists. Instead, the pods preserved two rebels who would spend their next life trying to destroy everything Sterman's creators — the Shadows — had built.

docs.title: The Journey of the Pods
docs.text:
The ship carrying the pods reached the asteroid belt. The rebels built colonies. They fought and lost to the Hybrians. The ship survived. Centuries later, retrofitted with warp drives, it was sent outside the solar system to a human settlement.

Over thousands of years, the two sealed Sterman Pods were transferred between ships, between colonies, between research stations. The occupants inside remained frozen — preserved, unchanged, the experimental black agent circulating through their bodies, modifying, programming, waiting.

Eventually, the pods arrived at The 157th Colony — the human weapons research facility on the planet Ge'or. The two bodies became test subjects. Scientists studied the black agent in their systems. They refined it. They tested it. They created the final iteration.

When the Hybrians glassed the colony, the pods were in an underground bunker. They held. For three million years.

The crash of the Glorious Alliance finally ruptured the body bags. The black agent bled into the earth.

It found two women in 596 AGD. In 597 AGD, Emrys Eisenheart and Lucien Mortvagn were born.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Sterman Pods ] ├── Commissioned By: Sterman — the image, the Antichrist, the face of Earth's surveillance state ├── Era: Post-2030 dystopian Old Earth ├── Function: Cryogenic preservation + experimental black agent injection ├── Black Agent Strain: Experimental — designed for incubation and rebirth ├── Occupants: Mikhail (Emrys) and Arkady (Lucien) ├── Activation: Accidental — ship malfunction slammed the doors shut ├── Journey: Asteroid belt → outer colonies → The 157th Colony (Ge'or) ├── Duration: ~3,000,000 years in cryosleep ├── Final Fate: Body bags ruptured by Glorious Alliance crash ├── Result: Black agent released — Emrys and Lucien born in 597 AGD └── Irony: Sterman's control mechanism created the weapon that would destroy his masters

docs.title: Sword of Xi
docs.text:
A blade of the dragon empire of Xi. Anyone unworthy who tries to hold it dies.

The Sword of Xi was a weapon of the dragon kingdom of Xi, rival to Klobiendar. After Xi's destruction in The Draconic War, the sword came into the possession of Fireborn, who gifted it to Julian the Dragon Tamer in 528 BGD.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Julian wielded the sword during his march on Baoth, where he confronted Goldenborn and fought against Shadow-controlled forces. After Julian's death at his family's grave — his body disintegrating into the black agent — the sword fell.

Anyone who tried to hold it immediately died. The sword could not be moved.

docs.title: The Monument
docs.text: The Axels — the human people of what became Northaxeland, followers of Julian's legend — built a monument around the fallen sword. Those ruins still stand in the Ruins of Baoth to this day. The sword remains in the ground at the exact location where it fell, untouched for over a thousand years.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Sword of Xi ] ├── Origin: Xi dragon kingdom ├── Gifted by: Fireborn to Julian the Dragon Tamer (528 BGD) ├── Used in: Julian's march on Baoth ├── Current location: Ruins of Baoth — inside a monument, in the ground ├── Property: Kills anyone unworthy who attempts to hold it ├── Related: The Draconic War, Julian the Dragon Tamer, Alegoria └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🔮 Fate
docs.text:
The tablet survived. It is almost indestructible — it resisted Nethra's explosion at Baoth and lies today somewhere in the Ruins of Baoth.

Its path after Kirivis: Nethra carried it to Baoth. While examining her father's belongings — the legacy of Kirivis — she found and read the tablet, and learned what it revealed. She then marched on Baoth to destroy the kingdom, carrying the tablet with her. When the cataclysm came, the tablet endured — nearly indestructible as it is — and remained among the ruins.

The protagonists will recover it from the Ruins of Baoth. It is their inheritance: the truth of the Shadows, the Sacrifice Ceremony, and Kirivis's sacrifice, waiting where he fell.

The Ironcloak has searched for it for centuries and does not know it survived.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ The Glowing Tablet ] ├── Origin: Hybrian Shadow technology from The Last Great War ├── Recovered From: Formingar Ocean — Possibly from Glorious Alliance ├── User: Kirivis — Studied it for 60 years ├── Discovered: ~526 BGD — presented to Kirivis as a gift by a subject ├── Deciphered: ~466 BGD — the epiphany that broke him ├── Revealed: Shadows infiltration of Baoth ├── Revealed: Sacrifice Ceremony ├── Revealed: Goldenborn's true role as bait ├── Carried By: Nethra — read it from her father's belongings, carried it to Baoth ├── Withstood: Nethra's explosion at Baoth — nearly indestructible ├── Current Location: Ruins of Baoth ├── Destined For: The protagonists — they will recover it └── Sought By: Ironcloak (unaware it survived)

docs.title: The Great Epic of the Heroes of Donblond'werv
docs.text:
An in-world epic of the Human Age, compiling the adventures of Masaaki Sytrenis and his party — Hogryr Aledini, Trurdrang Emberflare, and Laudlaern Kenismov — in the land that would later be called Erisdar (then known as Donblond'werv). Its centerpiece is their fight against the mountain that was never a mountain: the Metrak.

The epic is the foundation of the catmen religion Sytrenis, and the reason the name of "Sytrenis the Diplomat" still echoes across Ge'or.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ The Great Epic ] ├── Heroes: Masaaki Sytrenis, Hogryr Aledini, Trurdrang Emberflare, Laudlaern Kenismov ├── Villain: Metrak ├── Setting: The Kingdom of Termopolas, the land of the now-Erisian Empire ├── Legacy: The foundation of the catmen religion Sytrenis └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: The Metraks
docs.text:
"It was never a mountain. It was a relic."

The Metraks are sixteen city-sized mechanoids — mountain-sized war-machines left on Erisdar from the The Last Great War, millions of years ago, when Ge'or was glassed by the Hybrian bombardment. Sixteen lie dormant beneath the regions of Erisdar — and, unless someone who understands them intervenes, they are dangerous beyond measure.

docs.title: The Forgotten Mountain
docs.text: For millions of years one of them was known simply as a mountain: Metrak, in the region of the now-Munchon within the Erisian Empire. No one on Ge'or knows what a machine or a mechanoid is, or what electricity even is — to the peoples of the world, such things are simply magic. When the archaeology-loving emperor Atanides sent his teams into "the dungeon of Metrak," he woke it.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
• Destructive range: a single Metrak can destroy an entire region — in the strongest cases, easily — where its empire stands
  • Defenses: internal turrets and ancient systems that kill intruders
  • Controls: the machines respond to those who understand them — a key button, a protective suit, and the knowledge that this is a thing of craft, not of earth
  • The network: each Metrak's console can project a holographic map of Erisdar showing all sixteen locations; a hidden printer runs off copies endlessly

docs.title: The Sixteen Regions
docs.text: The maps Masaaki Sytrenis printed after disabling the Erisdar Metrak showed sixteen regions of Erisdar, each with a like machine — sixteen city-robots, mostly dormant, all linkable, all able to be controlled by people who understand how they work. They remain a sleeping arsenal beneath the continent — still dangerous, still controllable, known to Sytrenis's heirs and to no one else in authority.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ The Metraks ] ├── Origin: The Last Great War — millions of years before the present ├── Number: 16 — city-sized mechanoids across the regions of Erisdar ├── Known Unit: Metrak (region of now-Munchon, Erisian Empire) ├── Woken By: Atanides's excavations — it killed him and ravaged the land ├── Stopped By: Masaaki Sytrenis — wore the suit, pressed the button ├── Truth: No one on Ge'or understands machines — to them it is "magic" ├── Network: Holographic map + printed maps of all 16 regions └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🦴 Legends
docs.text:
Tales, myths, and the heroes — or monsters — behind them.

Browse the entries in the sidebar, or return to the World Dashboard.

docs.title: 📖 Legends
docs.text: The mythology, folklore, and legendary entities of Ge'or. Unlike Religions, which are organized systems of worship, legends encompass the stories, creatures, and figures that exist at the margins of recorded history — believed by some, doubted by others, never fully confirmed.

docs.title: 📂 Subcategories
docs.text: • Legendary Creatures — Beasts and entities of myth

docs.title: Notable Legends
docs.text:
• The Leviathan — The serpentine warden of Lake Leviathan
  • The Myth of Eris — Fabricated by Hybrians; now institutionalized as the Erisian church

docs.title: 🐲 Legendary Creatures
docs.text: Beasts, entities, and beings whose existence is attested only through legend, folklore, and scattered eyewitness accounts. Unlike Species, which are taxonomically classified and broadly acknowledged, legendary creatures occupy the grey space between myth and reality — believed by the few who have seen them, doubted by the many who have not.

docs.title: Known Legendary Creatures
docs.text: • Leviathan — The aquatic warden of Lake Leviathan, guardian of the Ruins of Baoth

docs.title: Suspected
docs.text:
• Entities matching legendary creature profiles in the Mystical Forest — unconfirmed
  • Deep-lake entities in the Voltendor Sea near the Great Divergence vortex — legends only

docs.title: The Sea
docs.text:
The Leviathan Sea is not named after the creature by coincidence. The sea and the beast are one. The waters are tainted by the Leviathan's presence — dark, still, and hostile to human life. Ships that cross the sea sometimes report hearing voices from below. No one who has fallen into those waters has ever returned.

At the center of the sea lie the Ruins of Baoth, where the Archive of the Traveler waits, unopened.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Leviathan ] ├── Origin: Demonic War Sacrifice Ceremony — engineered by Shadows ├── Catalyzed By: Nethra's device — the Gift from 3,000,000 Years ├── Head Soul: Kirivis — the Demon King ├── Formed From: Bodies of all who died in the war ├── Location: Leviathan Sea — the crater around Ruins of Baoth ├── Nature: Composite consciousness — remembers, cannot speak, waits └── Related: Rulfred, Baoth, The Last Great War

docs.title: 🗿 Locations
docs.text:
The continents, oceans, and landmarks of Ge'or — where everything happens.

Browse the entries in the sidebar, or return to the World Dashboard.

docs.title: 🐋 Beast's Bay
docs.text: A major bay bordering three continents: southeast Lumina Continent, northeast Marti Continent, and west Xeti. A hub of commerce — heavy trade traffic flows through here from the Vennerian Channel (colony), which links the bay to the Xeti Sea south of Xeti. The Vennerian Aelefer Channel also connects to it from the Lumina Continent side.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Borders: Lumina Continent (SE), Marti Continent (NE), Xeti (W)
  • Connects to: Vennerian Channel (colony) → Xeti Sea
  • Connected to: Vennerian Aelefer Channel, Marti Sea
  • Commerce hub for three continents

docs.title: Cleton Island
docs.text:
A small island off the eastern coast of Moon Wolf Island, trapped between the two peninsulas that form the wolf's open mouth. To the people of the Moonfang Dominion, the island appears as prey — forever being devoured by the wolf-god it is named for.

Cleton is the Wolf God of the Dominion's death cult. The island is his altar. Each year, the cult selects a group of children — always the prettiest — and sends them to Cleton Island as sacrifices. Beauty, in the Dominion's theology, is the mark of the god's hunger. None return.

The island itself is barren rock, frozen most of the year, with no permanent structures. The sacrifices are left exposed to the elements — or to the wargs the cult holds sacred.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Location: Between the northern and southern peninsulas of Moon Wolf Island
  • God: Cleton, the Wolf God
  • Nation: Moonfang Dominion
  • Sacred Animals: Wargs

docs.title: Crab Archipelago
docs.text: An archipelago in the western Wolf Ocean, located north of the South Crab Archipelago and south of Karabar Island. Home to the Crab Union.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Ocean: Wolf Ocean
  • South: South Crab Archipelago
  • North: Karabar Island
  • Nation: Crab Union

docs.title: The Trigger
docs.text:
The crash did one more thing — something no survivor could have known. The impact reverberated through the planet's crust and reached the ancient research bunker of the 157th Colony, buried deep beneath the surface. Two body bags — treated with a black DNA agent three million years ago — finally ruptured.

The black substance began its journey toward the surface. It would take thousands of years. But it was coming.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Glorious Alliance ] ├── Built: ~1,200,000 years ago — during The Last Great War ├── Type: Arcology ship — self-contained city for hundreds of thousands ├── Voyage: ~25,000 years at sublight ├── Cargo: Last free populations of Humans, Demons, Elves, Dwarves, Dragons ├── Crash: ~15,000 BGD — Formingar Ocean ├── Wreckage: MELKOR island ├── Reactor: Still active — malfunctioned in Year 0 (Great Divergence) ├── Saboteur: Mad-Dog — Hybrian Shadow who sabotaged the reactor ├── Triggered: Release of black agent from 157th Colony bunker ├── Created: The Groom vortex, The Kutten Catastrophe ├── Wreck: Still submerged at MELKOR — never fully explored ├── Known Contents: Shadow device (given to Nethra), active reactor, possible communication nodes (may relate to The Glowing Tablet) └── Legacy: Every species on Ge'or descends from its passengers

docs.title: Karabar Island
docs.text:
An island north of the South Crab Archipelago and west of the Wolf Ocean. Home to the nation of Karabar.

Karabar Island sits in a strategic position in the western Wolf Ocean. To its north lies the frozen Moon Wolf Island, home to the death-cult Moonfang Dominion. Between them stretches a chain of nameless islands and open sea — the route escapees take when fleeing the cult. To the northeast lies the volcanic Molten Archipelago, where Karabar operates its refugee bases.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Karabar
  • North: Moon Wolf Island (Moonfang Dominion)
  • Northeast: Molten Archipelago
  • South: South Crab Archipelago
  • East: Wolf Ocean
  • West: Greater Ocean

docs.title: Knight's Thorn
docs.text: A peninsula in West Erisdar owned by the Asatru Empire as the colony of Asatru Knight's Thorn. It serves as the Demon Continent's presence on Erisdar.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: West Erisdar
  • Owned by: Asatru Empire
  • Near: Palonia, Demon's Horn, Suebo

docs.title: Leviathan Sea
docs.text: An inland sea in Central Erisdar, surrounded by the Erisian Empire and neighboring countries. An impassable forest rings its shores, and at its center lie the Ruins of Baoth — the destroyed dragon city.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: Central Erisdar
  • Contains: Ruins of Baoth
  • Surrounded by: Impassable forest
  • Near: Erisian Empire, Venkradian Republic, Loren, Matterbleak, New Baoth, Elvennrin

docs.title: 🏝️ Luminous Sea Islands
docs.text: The Luminous Sea Islands are an archipelago chain off the northeastern coast of Erisdar, in the Luminous Ocean. Named for the bioluminescent waters that surround them at night — a phenomenon attributed to microscopic organisms or, in local myth, to the restless dreams of a sleeping sea god.

docs.title: Nations
docs.text:
Island Kutten Isle is distinct from the desert continent Kutten (see Kutten Isle).

The archipelago's four main islands (distinct from the Kutten desert continent — see Kutten Isle): - Erima — fishing and trade (owned by the Aenid Kingdom, West Erisdar) - Kutten Isle — isolated, pre-imperial oral traditions (distinct from the Kutten desert continent) - Minir — smallest, separate-origin myth — nations: Dukedam, Koln, Neopao - Moriat — mystical, unconverted by the Erisian church — nations: Underfern, Mikrad, Gomor, Gildenrise

Dominated by the Aenid Kingdom navy (West Erisdar) — not an archipelago member. Full polity list: see Luminous Sea Islands (Nations hub).

docs.title: MELKOR
docs.text:
The massive circular island at the center of the Formingar Ocean — formed around the impact site of the Glorious Alliance, the arcology ship that crashed ~15,000 years before the Great Divergence, carrying the last free populations of five species from The Last Great War.

When the ship's reactor malfunctioned in Year 0, MELKOR became the epicenter of the cataclysm. The waters turned red. The vortex of The Groom opened at its heart. Gold began appearing in impossible quantities.

From the Age of Strife onward, evils from the old ship were set loose into the world by the Hybrians from MELKOR.

The spirits of the Lyrical Forest — souls of fallen warriors from the Last Great War — spent thousands of years using their roots to retrieve a device from the Glorious Alliance's wreckage at MELKOR. That device became Nethra's weapon: the Gift from 3,000,000 Years.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ MELKOR ] ├── Location: Center of Formingar Ocean ├── Crash Site Of: Glorious Alliance (~15,000 BGD) ├── Wreck: Glorious Alliance — the arcology beneath the island ├── Contains: The Groom — The Eternal Vortex ├── Caused: Great Divergence — Reactor Malfunction (Year 0) ├── Source Of: Evils Released in Age 12 — Age of Strife ├── Retrieved From: Device given to Nethra by Lyrical Forest spirits └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Mankind Wall
docs.text:
A massive defensive wall on Sister Continent — comparable to the Great Wall of China — that separates the central wasteland (occupied by The Hive) from the machine civilizations of the south. The wall was constructed by the Machines over centuries as their primary defense against Hive expansion.

Behind the wall lie Machine Capital, Casting City, Radiant Hold, and Molten Steel Tribe.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: Sister Continent
  • Built by: Machines
  • Defends against: The Hive
  • Protects: Machine Capital, Casting City, Radiant Hold, Molten Steel Tribe

docs.title: Media
docs.text: An island in the Luminous Ocean, controlled by the Vennerian Trade Republic. On the 597 AGD world map it appears as "Media Venner" — a Vennerian-held island among the chain that includes K.le Venner, Sua Venner, and Eribel venner.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Ocean: Luminous Ocean
  • Controller: Vennerian Trade Republic
  • Map label: "Media Venner" (597 AGD political map)
  • Near: K.le Venner, Sua Venner (Vennerian island chain)

docs.title: Molten Archipelago
docs.text:
A volcanic archipelago in the open sea southwest of Moon Wolf Island, northeast of Erisdar, and north of Karabar Island. Uninhabitable in any conventional sense — the islands are black rock and active vents, the sea around them steaming where lava meets water.

Despite its hostility, the Molten Archipelago serves a purpose. Karabar operates refugee bases on its eastern edge — waystations for those who flee the Moonfang Dominion's death cult. The Archipelago is the first land escapees reach after crossing the frozen sea. The main settlement, marked on the world map as "moonfang refugees", sits on the northeastern island of the chain — a ring-marked settlement that is the first port of call for escapees.

It is not a sanctuary. Karabar does not offer freedom — it offers work. Escapees who reach the bases are put to forced labor for wages that barely sustain them. The cult claims their souls. Karabar claims their bodies. The Molten Archipelago is the space between two kinds of prison.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Northeast: Moon Wolf Island
  • South: Karabar Island
  • Southwest: Erisdar (distant)
  • Refugee bases: Operated by Karabar

docs.title: Mongrel Forest
docs.text: A large forest in eastern Erisdar, east of the Mann Order and west of the Fractured State of Erislod. No country claims ownership of this territory.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: East Erisdar
  • West: Mann Order
  • East: Fractured State of Erislod

docs.title: Moon Wolf Island
docs.text:
A frozen island near the north pole, northeast of Erisdar and north of Karabar Island, home to the death-cult nation of Moonfang Dominion.

The island has the distinct appearance of a wolf's head when viewed from above — a shape that fuels the Dominion's worship of Cleton, the Wolf God. Two peninsulas form the wolf's open mouth along the eastern coast; a smaller island, Cleton Island, sits caught between them as though the wolf is devouring it. Northwest of the northern peninsula lies a lake known as the Eye, completing the face.

The island's interior is volcanic and mountainous — uninhabitable. The Dominion's settlements cling to the coasts, huddled against the cold and the volcanoes alike.

docs.title: Geography
docs.text:
• Climate: Arctic. Most of the island is frozen year-round.
  • Interior: Mountains and active volcanoes render the center dead.
  • Coasts: Habitation zone. Sparse, cold, grim.
  • The Eye: A lake northwest of the northern peninsula — the wolf's eye in island profile.
  • Cleton Island: The sacrifice ground between the jaw-peninsulas.

docs.title: Wildlife
docs.text: • Wargs — sacred to the Dominion. Wolf-like predators that roam the island freely. Killing one is death under cult law.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Moonfang Dominion
  • Ocean: Wolf Ocean
  • South: Karabar Island
  • Southwest: Molten Archipelago (volcanic, uninhabitable)

docs.title: The Erislod Collapse
docs.text: An earthquake originating from Pontus destroyed cities in the Fractured State of Erislod, followed by a goblin army that emerged from the region and ravaged everything. This was the proximate cause of Erislod's collapse into anarchy — and it was a deliberate test of the Shadow goblin army.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: East Erisdar
  • Crash site of: Hybrian vessel — 2989 BGD
  • Contains: Subterranean Shadow complex (unknown to all)
  • Contains: Goblin army under Shadow control
  • Contains: Armageddon weapon
  • Cause of: Fractured State of Erislod collapse
  • Coloration: Same as The Groom

docs.title: Romanium Island
docs.text:
"The dwarves found it first. They called it paradise. Then the ore ran out." — Dwarven historical record, Dwarvengor archives

An island in the far north of Ge'or, northeast of Lung Continent across a vast stretch of violent sea, and northwest of the Demon Continent. Near the north pole. The island was the single richest source of Romanium on the planet — the perfect metal that fueled the Dwarf Era.

docs.title: The Dwarven Discovery
docs.text:
During the Dwarf Era (5,499–4,500 BGD), dwarven explorers discovered the island and found it saturated with Romanium ore. For centuries, Romanium Island was the heart of the global economy. The ore extracted here was the highest quality on Ge'or — purer, stronger, and more abundant than any other source.

The island was the foundation of dwarven prosperity. Gold, food, and silver were as cheap as water because Romanium from this island made everything else irrelevant.

docs.title: The Collapse
docs.text:
Romanium is finite. The richest mine in the world is still a mine — and mines run dry.

When the Romanium Island reserves began to deplete, the dwarven economy entered its slow, grinding collapse. It was not a sudden catastrophe. It was a generation-by-generation erosion — each year producing less ore, each year driving prices higher. The Golden War followed, as human horse-nomads from West and North Erisdar raided the weakening dwarven territories.

The depletion of Romanium Island was the trigger for the end of the Dwarf Era. The rest of the collapse followed from this single geological fact: the perfect metal was running out.

docs.title: The Shadow Discovery
docs.text:
The island was abandoned after the Dwarf Era. No one returned. The violent northern seas made it nearly unreachable, and there was nothing left worth mining.

When the Shadows discovered the island approximately 597 years ago — around the time of the Great Divergence (Year 0) — they found something more valuable than ore: the ancient human silo left behind from the 157th Colony era, still intact, still functional.

They also recovered the Glorious Alliance reactor core from the Formingar Ocean and brought it here. The integration of the core with the silo created the Armageddon neutron bomb — now housed at Eternal Paradise, the Shadow base on the island.

docs.title: Current State
docs.text: The island is now a Shadow military installation. No one on Ge'or knows it exists — except the Ironcloak, who have unverified intelligence fragments. The neutron bomb is nearly complete. The countdown has begun.

docs.title: Connections

docs.title: 👹 Demon Continent
docs.text: [!INFO] The Northern Continent The ancestral territory of the demon species on Ge'or. Located west of West Erisdar, separated by the Demonic Sea.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Demon Continent is the homeland of demon-kind, the species descended from allied warriors of The Last Great War. It lies across the Demonic Sea from West Erisdar. The continent was once unified under the Demon King, but after his death it fractured into competing tribes and warlord states.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
The land of the Demon Continent is painted black, not green. It resembles a desert with scattered trees — harsh, but not lifeless. Crops can be grown, though not as abundantly as on Erisdar or other continents.

This is not a natural landscape. The black coloration is chemical residue from an orbital bombardment during The Last Great War — a glassing attack by the Hybrian hivemind that struck the 157th Colony research station approximately three million years ago. The same glassing scarred the northern reaches of Lung Continent and Sister Continent, and the far western coast of Erisdar. All human researchers were killed. The land never recovered. The shared struggle against the environment and predators fostered a collaborative culture. The inhabitants view themselves with a shared "demonic" nationality — a point of pride and identity. Inter-species conflict is relatively rare; populations of every race walk freely and mix naturally.

docs.title: Nations
docs.text:
• Asatru Empire — largest, spiritual successor to Demon King. Northeast.
  • Blazeyard — Flames species, mountain range. West of Asatru.
  • Emberalden — kobold subrace, taller/stronger. NW of Blazeyard.
  • Malgardian Tribe — humanoid, purple-haired, evolved off-world. West of Emberalden.
  • Tita Tribe — Malgardian subrace (Titians), sacred miko status. West of Malgardians.
  • Bloodcoast — Malgardian-human hybrid, red hair. Above Malgardians/Titians, west of Asatru.
  • Kutra Tribe — humanoid owls, semi-aquatic, can fly. Below Malgardians/Emberalden.
  • Maomodor Kingdom — main demon race, multi-racial. Below Kutra, SW of Blazeyard.
