docs.title: Dragonreach
docs.text:
"Either we die in glory or live to see another day under honor." — Plenio, Diana, and Korvald, before entering Dragonreach

The Dragonreach mountains stretch across western Erisdar, forming a natural spine from the northern coasts of Kille down through Augagarten and into the wildlands south of Matterbleak. The peaks are ancient — worn smooth by wind and ice — but it is not their age that makes them feared. It is what lives inside them.

Dragonreach was the capital of Klobiendar, the dragon empire of West Erisdar that rivaled Xi, the dragon kingdom of the east. It is now a graveyard.

docs.title: The Draconic War
docs.text: The Draconic War pitted Klobiendar against Xi — two dragon empires, millions of soldiers, fifty years of slaughter. Billions died. In the final act, Melberior, the dragon leader of Xi, launched a suicide spell that destroyed Klobiendar's capital entirely. Melberior died in the casting. The magic was so immense that it reverberated across the land, creating the Lyrical Forest above Dragonreach — the souls of the fallen, the echo of the war, still humming in the trees.

docs.title: Fallen Dragons
docs.text:
Dragonreach is full of Fallen Dragons — half-alive, half-dead, similar to the entity in the Ruins of Baoth. They are not exactly conscious. They are not exactly dead. They can speak. They are usually violent unless a person proves worthy of their respect.

The most prominent of them is Fireborn — former dragon king of Klobiendar, father of Goldenborn, now a Fallen Dragon who still holds court in the deepest chambers of the mountain.

Adventurers attempt to enter Dragonreach. Most meet their demise. The few who survive speak of caverns that descend deeper than the mountains rise, of circling shapes in the dark that watch without attacking, and of a presence that judges before it kills.

docs.title: Julian the Dragon Tamer
docs.text:
See: Julian the Dragon Tamer

In 528 BGD, a man named Julian entered Dragonreach. His family had been murdered by a Shadow-possessed aristocrat from Baoth. He came seeking them back. He found Fireborn instead.

After a ten-hour duel — in which Julian lost an arm, most of his teeth, and his face was disfigured, yet kept fighting until he reached one centimeter from Fireborn's core of life — Fireborn acknowledged him as the prophet. Fireborn spilled the black agent onto Julian, restoring his body. He gave Julian the Sword of Xi and told him the truth: the Hybrians had come to Ge'or to destroy all families — and Julian's was their victim.

Julian's story ended at his family's grave, where he touched their bodies, heard their voices telling him to rest, and died on the spot. His corpse disintegrated into the black agent. Fireborn flew above Baoth and consumed his disintegrating form. Julian incarnated into Fireborn — and learned he must wait for two prophets yet to come, whom he must test and prove.

docs.title: Treasure & Danger
docs.text:
The Sword of Xi fell during the chaos in Baoth. Anyone who tried to hold it immediately died. A monument was built around it — those ruins still stand in the Ruins of Baoth, and the sword remains in the ground at that exact location.

Dragonreach itself holds many more treasures for those who are brave. Fireborn's words: "Many more treasures are held in Dragonreach for those that are brave." Treasure hunters from Augamouth and Astravayne still disappear into the caves. Few return.

docs.title: Great Eris Wall
docs.text: A massive defensive wall that protects the entire territory of the Pontificate of Eris and extends into the Erisian Theocracy, covering most of that nation's lands as well. Most major cities in both the Pontificate and the Theocracy are situated behind the wall's protection.

docs.title: Origin
docs.text:
The wall exists because of the barbarian invasions. In the past, the people of Aimeled — followers of Charlmelism — were heavily barbarian, and together with the Aenid, they used to invade the Erisian Theocracy. To stop them, the Erisian Theocracy and the Pontificate of Eris built the Great Eris Wall.

The invasions are long past, but the wall remains — and the rivalry with the descendants of those barbarians never truly ended.

docs.title: Origin
docs.text:
The Lyrical Forest was created by the Draconic War. When Melberior, dragon leader of Xi, launched a suicide spell that destroyed Klobiendar's capital at Dragonreach, the magic was so immense it reverberated across the land, creating the Lyrical Forest above the mountains — an echo of the war, the souls of the fallen humming in the trees.

In 528 BGD, Julian the Dragon Tamer passed through the Lyrical Forest on his way to Dragonreach. He fell down a slope for hours and found a talking tree that told him to go to Dragonreach to find his family.

Later, Nethra marched through the forest to avenge Kirivis. The tree spirits — souls of fallen coalition soldiers from the Last Great War — gave her a device modified by accumulated soul-will. She detonated it in Baoth.

docs.title: ⚠️ Distinction
docs.text:
The Lyrical Forest is not the Mystical Forest. They are completely separate locations: - Lyrical Forest — NW Erisdar, near Matterbleak and the Dragonreach mountains - Mystical Forest — Central Erisdar, surrounding Lake Leviathan and the Ruins of Baoth

The similarity in names has caused confusion among scholars and cartographers, but they are distinct entities with distinct properties.

docs.title: The Talking Tree
docs.text:
"Go to Dragonreach. You may find your family again." — The tree at the bottom of the Lyrical Forest

The Talking Tree is a sentient tree located deep within the Lyrical Forest. It spoke to Julian the Dragon Tamer in 528 BGD, setting him on the path to Dragonreach.

docs.title: The Encounter
docs.text:
After his family was murdered, Julian wandered without direction. Passing through the Lyrical Forest, he fell down a slope — falling for what felt like hours. At the bottom, he found a tree that began to speak.

The tree told him: go to Dragonreach. You may find your family again.

Julian, believing himself insane, went anyway.

docs.title: Nature
docs.text: The tree is likely one of the spirits of the Lyrical Forest — a manifestation of the souls that inhabit the wood. The Lyrical Forest was created by the magic reverberation of The Draconic War, and its trees carry the echoes of the fallen. Whether the Talking Tree was one specific soul or a collective voice is unknown.

docs.title: ⚠️ The Leviathan
docs.text:
The lake's sole permanent resident, the Leviathan, was not merely unleashed — it was created here. Forged in secret by the Shadows from the bodies of everyone who died in the Demonic War, with Kirivis's soul bound as its head, the Leviathan was released into these waters to enforce an absolute quarantine on the ruins. Any vessel that touches the water beyond the shoreline is destroyed. It does not pursue beyond the treeline. It does not surface to be seen. It does not sleep.

It guards Rulfred — the Shadow now wearing Goldenborn's corpse as Dragon Yaldabaoth.

docs.title: 📜 History
docs.text:
The forest was not always this way. Pre-Baothian records describe the region as temperate woodland — dense, but traversable. The transformation occurred during or immediately after the Demonic War, suggesting the forest was corrupted alongside the kingdom.

Some theorists believe the forest is not a barrier, but a containment field — grown deliberately to seal something inside. It is unclaimed by any nation, existing as a no-man's-land between civilization and the dead kingdom.

docs.title: Goldenborn's Caldera
docs.text:
A mountain of gold. A cave of hunger. A mind that has been thinking for centuries.

Goldenborn's Caldera is a massive volcanic mountain in Dragonreach, West Erisdar. Its shape resembles Mount Fuji — a near-perfect cone rising from the rugged peaks — but what makes it remarkable is the gold. Pure gold decorations, hammered into the rock face by dragon claws millennia ago, cover portions of the mountain. They catch the light at dawn and glow like a second sun.

Adventurers from across Ge'or dream of raiding the caldera. The gold is real. The rumors say there are tons of it — dragon hoards, imperial tribute, treasure accumulated over thousands of years. Most who go do not return.

docs.title: The Cave — Black Agent Concentration
docs.text:
The caldera was the epicenter of Melberior's suicide spell during the Draconic War — the largest magical discharge in Ge'orian history. The spell pulled the black agent from the atmosphere, saturating the dead dragons and creating the Fallen Dragons.

But most of it did not become dragons.

Deep inside the caldera, in a cave system carved by volcanic heat and ancient magic, the largest concentration of black agent on Ge'or has been gathering for centuries — suckling magic from the mountain, the earth, the fallen dragons themselves. It never stopped. It never dispersed. It only grew.

docs.title: The Hivemind
docs.text:
Over the centuries, the black agent inside the caldera developed something unprecedented: a hivemind. Akin to the Hybrian collective consciousness — but born from a different source, shaped by a different hatred.

This hivemind hates the Hybrians. It was created by the weapon that destroyed the dragons, by the Shadows' own war, by the black agent they themselves engineered. Their enemy's enemy. It is not benevolent. It is not an ally. But its primary drive is opposition to the Shadows.

The hivemind controls Dragonreach. Every Fallen Dragon — including Fireborn — answers to it. When Fireborn recognized the black agent, when he knew what it could do, when he healed Julian with it — that knowledge came from the hivemind. The dragon king was not merely a host. He was a node in a larger intelligence.

docs.title: Possession and Construction
docs.text:
The hivemind possesses animals in the surrounding region — birds, wolves, mountain goats, insects — and uses them to build. Deep inside the caldera, a facility is taking shape: tools, relics, structures assembled by possessed creatures working in eerie coordination. No human has ever seen it. No one knows it exists.

But the relics it produces sometimes escape. They appear in the lower valleys, in the treasure hunters' camps, in the markets of Augamouth and Astravayne. These relics fuel the endless raids on Dragonreach — and the endless deaths.

docs.title: The Gold Economy
docs.text: The gold on the caldera's flanks is real and vast. It drives a significant portion of the regional economy, attracting adventurers, treasure hunters, and prospectors. But the gold is a lure. Most who climb for it encounter the War Wolves, or the Fallen Dragons, or worse. The caldera takes more than it gives.

docs.title: Kobre Continent
docs.text: A continent west of Tuba Continent, south of the Formingar Ocean and the Demon Continent. The southeastern corner of Kobre aligns with the latitude of Goblin Island — sailing west from Goblin Island lands on Kobre's southern coast.

docs.title: History
docs.text: Kobre's extreme isolation shaped its politics. For millennia, the only rivals the dwarves and elves had were each other. When the Hybrians attempted a takeover — attracted by the continent's remoteness — they deployed Homunculi as their instruments. But the destruction of Baoth severed the psychic link. The homunculi awoke free, turned on their masters, and established their own hostile nation. The Shadows' Kobre campaign was a rare failure.

docs.title: Lumina Continent

docs.title: 🏜️ Kutten Desert
docs.text: The desertified remains of the Kutten continent — once the homeland of Elvengar, now a wasteland of sand and poisoned memory.

docs.title: 🎭 Formation
docs.text:
During the Kutten Catastrophe (1–100 AGD), the Great Divergence saturated Kutten's atmosphere with toxic rains and poisoned air currents. Over a century, the continent's ecology collapsed entirely. Forests died. Rivers dried. Soil turned to sand.

The desert was not natural — it was manufactured by a million-year-old reactor malfunction.

  • Vennerian presence — the Love of the Sea outpost operates on Kutten.
  • Archaeological significance — the ruins of Elvengar lie somewhere beneath the sand.

docs.title: ⚔️ Enkrad Order — Outpost
docs.text:
"Order through strength. Strength through unity."

The Enkrad Order is an Erisian Church colony in Dissenbarg — the only Erisian nation on the continent. Its colonists arrived 370 years ago (~227 AGD — see Founding of the Enkrad Order), settling Dissenbarg's eastern reach with the support of the Vennerian Trade Republic and its colonial and commercial empire.

On the 597 AGD political map it appears as "ENKRAD ORDER" — slate-gray military order-state on mountainous terrain, between two large Goblin territories. New Venner lies to the south, the Dissenbarg Sea on its coast.

Surrounded by goblins east and west, it holds as a fortified Erisian island among hostile monster realms. As an Order-State, ranks are earned through proven combat, not birth.

docs.text:
A city in Dissenbarg controlled by the Anos Plutocracy, located southwest of Tissas and east of Johannstadt. On the 597 AGD world map it appears as "Anos Komma".

Komme's allegiance to Anos is a deliberate response to Venner: about 55 years ago (~542 AGD), after intense negotiations, Komme and Anos concluded the Anos–Komme Agreement to work together to liberate Taberis — now Venner-held Johannstadt. Komme follows Helism — its patron is Tissas, god of war.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Region: Dissenbarg
  • Northeast: Tissas
  • West: Johannstadt
  • Controller: Anos Plutocracy
  • Patron: Tissas (Helism)
  • Nation file: Nations/Dissenbarg/Komme

docs.title: 🏕️ Kreb
docs.text: A Sousu trading outpost on Dissenbarg Continent. One of several far-flung posts through which the elvish trading city of Sousu projects its mercantile influence beyond its Meble homeland.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Controller: Sousu
  • Continent: Dissenbarg Continent
  • Sister Outpost: Megrel (outpost) (Xeti)

docs.title: 🏗️ New Venner
docs.text:
A peninsula in Dissenbarg controlled by the Vennerian Trade Republic, located east of Aeon across the sea and below the goblin territories, with Enkrad Order to the east.

New Venner is Venner's southern Dissenbarg colonial peninsula — the Vennerian anchor south of the goblin belt and east of the Aeon sea gap.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Region: Dissenbarg
  • West (across sea): Aeon
  • North: Goblin territory
  • East: Enkrad Order
  • Controller: Vennerian Trade Republic
  • Nation file: Nations/Dissenbarg/New Venner

docs.title: 🏝️ Sua
docs.text:
A Vennerian island south of the Cletas Democracy in Dissenbarg, across a stretch of sea. Sua is Venner's outpost — the foothold Venner held before it invaded and took over Taberis (now Johannstadt).

Sua was the staging island for the Taberis War — the Vennerian purchase that made the later annexation of Johannstadt possible.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Region: Dissenbarg
  • North (across sea): Cletas Democracy
  • Controller: Vennerian Trade Republic
  • Related: Johannstadt (former Taberis)
  • Nation file: Nations/Dissenbarg/Sua

docs.title: 🏕️ Tatak
docs.text:
A large territory in Dissenbarg controlled by the Anos Plutocracy, located south of Kolorad and Sousu and south of Kolorad in the chain Sus Principality → Sossan → Kolorad → Tatak.

Home to a major Anos city. Unlike Johannstadt, Tatak was never conquered — it willingly entered the Anos coalition for profit. The territory is huge, comparable in size to Johannstadt. Tatak follows Helism — its patron is Corin, goddess of commerce and sea.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Region: Dissenbarg
  • North: Kolorad, Sousu (Meble)
  • South: Tissas
  • Controller: Anos Plutocracy
  • Patron: Corin (Helism)
  • Nation file: Nations/Dissenbarg/Tatak

docs.title: 🏗️ New Kolorad
docs.text: An Anos colony on Kumir, the large island east of Xeti. Named after the Anos territory of Kolorad on Erisdar.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Controller: Anos Plutocracy
  • Island: Kumir
  • Named for: Kolorad (Anos territory on Erisdar)

docs.title: 📖 Love of the Sea, "Love of the Sea (outpost)"
docs.text: A Vennerian trading outpost on Kutten. Named with the characteristic flair of the Vennerian Trade Republic's far-flung maritime network.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Controller: Vennerian Trade Republic
  • Continent: Kutten

docs.title: 🏮 Goishi, "Goishi (outpost)"
docs.text: A Vennerian trading outpost in the northeast of the Lumina Continent continent. Part of the Vennerian Trade Republic's commercial network.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:

  • Continent: Lumina Continent

docs.title: 💰 Lumina Outpost
docs.text: An Anos trading outpost in the southeast of the Lumina Continent continent. Part of the Anos Plutocracy's colonial network.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:

  • Continent: Lumina Continent

docs.title: 🏗️ Anos Marti
docs.text: An Anos colony on the north coast of the Marti Continent continent. A territorial holding of the Anos Plutocracy.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Controller: Anos Plutocracy
  • Continent: Marti Continent

docs.title: ⛵ Vennerian Channel, "Vennerian Channel (colony)"
docs.text: A Vennerian colony and constructed waterway between the Xeti and Marti Continent continents. The Vennerian Trade Republic built this channel to link the Xeti Sea (south of Xeti) to the Beast's Bay (southeast Lumina / northeast Marti / west Xeti). It serves as both a territorial holding and a vital commercial artery — heavy trade traffic flows through it.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Controller: Vennerian Trade Republic
  • Links: Xeti Sea → Beast's Bay
  • Between: Xeti and Marti Continent
  • Character: Colony + constructed channel

docs.title: 🚢 Mia Checkpoint, "Mia Checkpoint (checkpoint)"
docs.text: A Vennerian checkpoint in the northeast of Mia island, north of the Lumina Continent continent. The checkpoint controls passage through the island's forested terrain and serves as a waystation for Vennerian Trade Republic vessels operating in the northern waters.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections

  • Island: Mia
  • Region: North of Lumina Continent

  • Continent: Xeti
  • Neighbor: Megrel (outpost) (Sousu, to the east)

docs.title: Demonic Sea
docs.text: The sea separating West Erisdar from the Demon Continent. Despite its name, it is a busy commercial route, particularly through Demon's Horn, the primary intercontinental trade hub.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Between: West Erisdar and Demon Continent
  • Trade hub: Demon's Horn

docs.title: 🌊 Dissenbarg Sea
docs.text: The sea surrounding the Dissenbarg Continent, recorded on the 597 AGD world map. Its waters lie between Dissenbarg and the eastern reaches of Erisdar, dotted with islands and the southern routes of the Corinite League.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Continent: Dissenbarg Continent
  • Near: Erisdar (west), Tessalian Tibia (island)
  • Recorded: 597 AGD world map

docs.title: 🌊 Eris Sea
docs.text: The sea east of the Grimmel Peninsula, named for Eris — the fabricated goddess of the Erisian church. The eastern coast of the peninsula — Charia, Lukka, Ferroson, Tundranya, Asheng, Anos — faces this sea.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Peninsula: Grimmel Peninsula (east)
  • Coast: Limese League, Charia, Lukka, Ferroson, Tundranya, Asheng, Anos
  • Counterpart: Venner Sea (west of the peninsula)

docs.title: Formingar Ocean
docs.text: The Formingar Ocean is the largest ocean on Ge'or, lying between the Demon Continent and Merratodoni. It is the crash site of the Glorious Alliance — the refugee ship that brought the surviving species to Ge'or after The Last Great War.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• MELKOR — island formed from the Glorious Alliance's wreckage
  • The Groom — permanent space-time vortex created by the ship's reactor malfunction at Year 0
  • Leviathan Sea — connects to the Formingar via the shattered continental shelf
  • Glorious Alliance — the sunken arcology beneath MELKOR

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Part of the Oceans Loop: Formingar → Kutten Sea → Luminous → Greater → Wolf → Lung → Formingar
  • Crash Site: Glorious Alliance (≈15,000 BGD)
  • Wreck: Glorious Alliance
  • Vortex: The Groom (Year 0)
  • Borders: Demon Continent, Merratodoni

docs.title: Greater Ocean
docs.text:
A major ocean in central Ge'or, bordered by the Luminous Ocean to the west and the Wolf Ocean to the east. At its center lies Merratodoni, an island continent like Australia.

The ocean also borders Erisdar's western and southern coasts — the Silver Coast marks its most prominent continental shoreline. It connects to the Formingar Ocean via the southern straits and serves as the primary maritime route for trade between Erisdar and Merratodoni.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• West: Luminous Ocean, Xeti, Marti Continent
  • North: Dissenbarg Continent
  • Center: Merratodoni
  • East: Sun Archipelago, Tabontabar Continent, South Crab Archipelago, Wolf Ocean
  • Erisdar Coast: The Silver Coast on Erisdar's western and southern shores
  • Southern Straits: connects to the Formingar Ocean
  • South: Open waters

docs.title: Kutten Sea
docs.text: The sea separating Kutten from Mia island and Lumina Continent to the south. Located south of Kutten, east of the Formingar Ocean, and west of the Luminous Ocean.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• North: Kutten
  • South: Mia, Lumina Continent
  • West: Formingar Ocean
  • East: Luminous Ocean

docs.title: 🌊 Lesser Ocean
docs.text: A smaller body of water north/northeast of Erisdar, nestled between the continent and the Luminous Sea Islands. Less traveled than the Greater Ocean, the Lesser Ocean's routes are known only to experienced island navigators.

docs.title: 🌊 Lost Waters
docs.text: A named sea on the northern fringe of the mapped world, recorded on the 597 AGD political map. The waters sit in the region between the northern polar void and the settled lands of North Erisdar — a cold, little-traveled expanse whose name carries an ominous reputation.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Near: North Erisdar (south), polar void (north)
  • Recorded: 597 AGD political map
  • Character: Cold, remote, ominously named

docs.title: 🌊 Luminous Ocean
docs.text: The vast eastern sea separating Erisdar from Dissenbarg Continent. Several island nations dot its waters: Kutten Isle, Moriat, Minir, and Erima — dominated by the Aenid Kingdom navy (West Erisdar).

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: ├── Between: Erisdar and Dissenbarg Continent ├── Contains: Kutten Isle, Moriat, Minir, Erima └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Lung Ocean
docs.text: An ocean east of the Lung Continent and west of the Formingar Ocean, completing Ge'or's global ocean circuit. To its west and north lies the Lung Continent, Kobre Continent, the Demon Continent, and southeast Marti Continent. To its east lies the Formingar Ocean.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• West: Lung Continent, Kobre Continent, Demon Continent, Marti Continent (southeast)
  • East: Formingar Ocean

docs.title: Marti Sea
docs.text: A sea bordering the Lumina Continent to the north, connected to the Lesser Ocean. The Lake Kingdom and New Eris have access to its waters.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• North: Lumina Continent
  • South: Marti Continent
  • Connected to: Lesser Ocean
  • Bay: Beast's Bay

docs.title: 🌊 Merratodoni Sea
docs.text: The sea surrounding the Merratodoni continent, recorded on the 597 AGD political map. Its waters separate Merratodoni from the South Crab Archipelago and the wider Luminous Ocean routes.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Continent: Merratodoni
  • Near: South Crab Archipelago, Sun Archipelago
  • Recorded: 597 AGD political map

docs.title: 🌊 Minir Sea
docs.text: The sea surrounding Minir island in the Luminous Ocean, part of the Luminous Sea Islands region. The sea is named for the island — it is the waters around Minir, marked as "Minir Sea" on world maps.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Island: Minir
  • Ocean: Luminous Ocean
  • Archipelago: Luminous Sea Islands

docs.title: 🌊 Moriat Sea
docs.text: The sea surrounding Moriat island in the Luminous Ocean, part of the Luminous Sea Islands region. Like the Minir Sea, it takes its name from the island it embraces.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Island: Moriat
  • Ocean: Luminous Ocean
  • Archipelago: Luminous Sea Islands

docs.title: Oceans Loop
docs.text:
The Oceans Loop is the continuous oceanic ring that encircles Ge'or, connecting all major bodies of water:

Formingar Ocean → Kutten Sea → Luminous Ocean → Greater Ocean → Wolf Ocean → Lung Ocean → back to Formingar Ocean

This loop is critical for global navigation and trade. Ships that follow the loop can theoretically circumnavigate the entire planet, though violent seas near certain continents make full traversal rare.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Formingar Ocean
  • Kutten Sea
  • Luminous Ocean
  • Greater Ocean
  • Wolf Ocean
  • Lung Ocean
  • Trade Routes

docs.title: 🌊 Venner Sea
docs.text: The sea west of the Grimmel Peninsula, named for the Vennerian Trade Republic that dominates its waters. The Vennerian-controlled coast of the peninsula — Aelefer, Melior, the region near the Order of Niccas — faces this sea.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Peninsula: Grimmel Peninsula (west)
  • Controller: Vennerian Trade Republic
  • Coast: Aelefer, Melior, Cerulea
  • Counterpart: Eris Sea (east of the peninsula)

docs.title: ⚡ Voltendor Sea
docs.text: An electrified sea region where perpetual storms churn the waters. Named for the Voltendor — a natural phenomenon of constant electrical discharge between sea and sky. Sailors avoid these waters; those who must cross do so only during rare calm windows. Local legends attribute the storms to a battle between sky spirits that never ended.

docs.title: Wolf Ocean
docs.text: An ocean in the far northeast of Ge'or. The South Crab Archipelago lies to its west, Karabar Island and Moon Wolf Island to its northwest and north, the Sister Continent to its east, and the Lung Continent beyond that.

docs.title: Islands
docs.text:
• Moon Wolf Island — frozen, wolf-shaped, home to the Moonfang Dominion death cult
  • Cleton Island — sacrifice ground between Moon Wolf's jaw-peninsulas
  • Karabar Island — south of Moon Wolf, independent nation
  • Molten Archipelago — volcanic chain southwest of Moon Wolf, uninhabitable, Karabar refugee bases
  • South Crab Archipelago — to the southwest

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• West: South Crab Archipelago, Karabar Island
  • Northwest: Moon Wolf Island, Karabar Island
  • East: Sister Continent

docs.title: ⚔️ Demon Ash-Pike
docs.text: [!INFO] Demon Continent — Emberalden — Ash-pike for vent-field fight, slag tip holds heat. Vent pike.

docs.title: 🗡️ Form
docs.text: Human mouth + human hand + iron-age tech: forge by coal/coke, quench in water or temple oil (tallow+copper salts), edge by stone. No mage-cell edge — steel is steel, heat is slag chemistry, not spell. Taught as school drills, spoken as Common numbers.

docs.text: Masters certify by cut test: basilica post, timber hall log, vault-arch stone, canopy vine, ash-slab, ice block or gear-tooth gauge. One test per school.

docs.title: Anos Coin Guard
docs.text: [!INFO] The Ledger Guard — Paper Over Gold, Steel Behind Paper Venner weighs. Anos counts — and the Coin Guard makes the count hold.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The military-commercial guard of the Anos Plutocracy — the counting-house oligarchy of South Erisdar that broke from the Kingdom of Tiphar in 158 AGD alongside Tiphar's other heirs (Scarlet Order, Grimmel) and built a global ledger instead of a kingdom. Where Venner built a channel, Anos built receipts: thin copper plates stamped A₥, redeemable against ledgers in the basalt towers of Anos city, backed not by metal but by trade volume — grain from Temas and Citrea, metals from Marti, timber from Lumina.

The Coin Guard is the reason those receipts do not flutter away. Chartered by the council of ruling families under Carolas II's predecessors as the Guard of the Counting-Houses, it escorts grain fleets, garrisons colonial ports, and — when the ledger says a debtor has miscounted — arrives to help him recount. Its companies are recruited from the sons of clerks and the daughters of harbor masters, promoted for arithmetical talent as much as courage; a Coin Guard captain who cannot spot a false manifest is not long a captain.

The Guard's most storied action is not a battle but a blockade-running in the Greater Ocean during a Venner interdiction — a convoy that scattered, reassembled by counting-house signals, and delivered Martian Drum hides and Kobran Gear steel to Anos Marti under Venner noses. Anos chronicles record it by tonnage.

docs.title: Patron
docs.text:
The Anos council of plutocrats — the families who elect the head of the Anos from among themselves — and operationally the counting houses as institutions. Guardsmen swear on the ledger, not a relic: a hand on the bound book, oath that the number written is the number honored. Breach of oath is tried as forgery, which in Anos is worse than desertion.

Relations: the Limese League plays Anos against Venner and the Guard knows it; the Guard's liaison in Lima grins and offers the League better rates anyway, because the game requires both players.

docs.title: Sigil
docs.text: A copper plate stamped A₥ on a slate-black field, crossed behind by two white quills — the Crossed Quills. Counting-house detachments render the A₥ in polished copper leaf that tarnishes honestly; campaign variants render it in chalk so it can be re-stamped after every audit. Commanders add a small Sousu pearl at the plate's corner when detached to Kreb or Megrel — pearls from Meble pay for discretion.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Counting-house security, colonial garrison, and trade-route enforcement. The Coin Guard fields marines, escorted factor columns, and the ledger cavalry — mounted clerks who can ride to a Dissenbarg port like Komme or Tatak (Tatak joined Anos willingly, for profit; Komme by the ~542 AGD pact to liberate Taberis), audit a warehouse in an afternoon, and ride out with the shortfall or a mortgage on the town.

It holds Anos's global span: Lumina Outpost in Lumina, Xeti Outpost in Xeti, New Kolorad on Kumir, Anos Maloca and Arrow of Anos in Merratodoni, Kolorad off Meble, and the Dissenbarg cities that still fly Anos colors because the ledger says they do.

docs.title: Relation to Currencies & Regions
docs.text:
The Guard is the steel behind Anosi Mark — A₥ on copper, promise that a clerk in basalt will honor the number. When Venner blockades the Greater Ocean, the Mark wobbles; when the Guard convoys grain through, it firms. The Guard's pay-chest moves as ledger entries first, plates second — the final settlement always in a counting house, not a field tent.

For foreign dealings it converts to Vennerian Ducat at Beast's Bay and Demon's Horn (grudgingly), to Dissenbarg Krona in Dissenbarg (weighing every city Krona on its own scales), to Meblean Pearl via Sousu at Kreb for Marti metals, and to Martian Drum hides at Anos Marti for herd wealth — the whole network rendered as one ledger spread that, miraculously, usually balances.

docs.title: Asatru Legion
docs.text: [!INFO] The Ember Legion — Demons Who March in Order When Asatru marches, the Demon Continent has decided to be legible.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The standing military order of the Asatru Empire, the Legion is how the Demon Continent's oldest demon civilization translates itself to a world that expects 'demon' to mean horde. Founded in the settlement after Kirivis — the Demon King, founder-emperor — was betrayed and beheaded by Rulfred on the last day of the Demonic War (421 BGD) and his adopted children Maoth and Nethra carried his legacy through the Great Divergence, the Legion was reformed by General Doma after the succession civil war and hardened under Emperor Bionidas (Xiobita line) into its present form.

It garrisons the Asatru Knight's Thorn peninsula in West Erisdar — treated not as colony but as integral imperial territory, the Demon Continent's permanent foothold on Erisdar — and holds the line in Kutten where Asatru influence rebuilt civilization after the Kutten Catastrophe that destroyed Elvengar. Between, it is the empire's voice in every treaty room where Demon Continent is invoked as abstraction and Asatru must make it concrete.

Other demon nations — Maomodor Kingdom, Koebi Tribe, Cubra Tribe, Blazeyard, Emberalden — field their own fighters, but when foreign powers say "the demons will…" they mean this legion.

docs.title: Patron
docs.text:
Kirivis-bin — the way of Kirivis — and through it, indirectly, Kirivis himself as remembered, not as shadow-caricature. The Legion's oath is sworn not to the emperor alone but to Kirivis's axiom: civilization is what you do when you could eat the other. Its chaplains are Kirivs-bin preceptors, its martyrology the 45-year march to save Goldenborn. Commanders keep a small ash-fleck from an Emberalden forge — a literal Demonic Ember — cold in a locket, warmed before battle by holding it over a flame: the coal remembers.

Bionidas is the legal commander-in-chief; the Legion's heart believes its commander remains Kirivis.

docs.title: Sigil
docs.text: A black horned helm over a field of ash-gray, crossed by a vertical ember-red stripe — the Ember Line — representing the surviving fire after the ash. On campaign in West Erisdar the helm is rendered in off-white bone to distinguish from Demon's Horn's own civic flag, with which it is deliberately confused by merchants for prestige. Veteran legions add a small silver ring at the helm's crown for The Silver Bride — demons, like everyone else, march under the same ring.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Expeditionary heavy infantry, demon-line shock, and intercontinental enforcement. The Legion fields disciplined blocks that mix Xiobita and Bjor Demons with allied Koebi spear, Kutra scouts, and Malgardian auxiliaries. Its special competence is holding a treaty line: it will not advance a foot beyond what the map allows, which makes it the most trustworthy — and most frustrating — force to negotiate against.

In West Erisdar it secures Knight's Thorn against Palonia and Direfirth pressure, escorts commerce through the Demonic Sea to Demon's Horn, and enforces Demonic Ember acceptance at ports where merchants would rather price in West Erisdarian Guilder.

docs.title: Relation to Currencies & Regions
docs.text:
The Legion is the enforcement behind the Demonic Ember — warm iron flecked with Emberalden ash, backed by forge-heat and legion discipline. In Demon's Horn and Yakut Territory (Kutten colony), the Ember is legal tender because the Legion will collect it. Outside demon territory the Legion's pay-chest carries West Erisdarian Guilder for West Erisdar transactions and Vennerian Ducat for sea movement; its factors maintain a standing exchange with Dwarvengor assay offices that weight Silver Talon honestly enough to trust.

At Demon's Horn, the Legion's presence makes Ember-to-Ducat conversion the day's first price — the honest one.

docs.title: Enkrad Order
docs.text: [!INFO] The Erisian Island — Faith Holding a Sea of Goblins Three hundred seventy years alone between goblin seas, and still the bells ring.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The Enkrad Order is the only Erisian nation on Dissenbarg — an Erisian Church colony planted ~227 AGD by colonists who sailed with Venner's blessing and settled Dissenbarg's eastern reach (see Founding of the Enkrad Order). Where other Dissenbarg nations are city-states minted in Helism's six gods, Enkrad is a single disciplined order-state.

It sits in mountainous terrain between two vast goblin territories east and west, marked "ENKRAD ORDER" in slate-gray on the 597 AGD political map, with New Venner to its south and the Dissenbarg Sea on its coast. Goblin raids are not an event but a season — the Order's entire calendar is built around them. Children learn spear before letters.

Enkrad has never expanded for conquest. Every wall it raised was because a prior wall fell. Its survival is not to the credit of any empire — the Erisian Empire sends prayers, not troops — but to Venner's commercial interest in an orderly Erisian port on Dissenbarg and to the Order's own fanatical cohesion.

docs.title: Patron
docs.text:
The Erisian church itself, rather than a single apostle. Enkrad's master is styled Guardian of the Erisian Word in Dissenbarg and receives his pallium from the Pontificate of Eris via Vennerian courier. In practice patronage flows through Venner: Vennerian captains carried the colonists, Vennerian coin paid for the first stone of Enkrad Citadel, and Vennerian factors still underwrite Enkrad's gunpowder.

Goblin neighbors call it the gray prayer — an insult Enkrad wears with pride.

docs.title: Sigil
docs.text: A gray stone citadel with a single white Erisian cross above the gate, on a slate field. In war the cross is rendered in chalk on shield and helm so it can be re-whitened after every sortie. Commanders add two small goblin skulls beneath the gate — not triumphalism but accounting: remember why the wall exists.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Pure border defense and colonial hold. Enkrad fields no cavalry of note — the mountains forbid it — but superb heavy infantry, crossbowmen, and citadel artillery that has turned goblin horde attacks into killing fields for three centuries. Its military-council ranks by proven combat ability, not birth, making it the most meritocratic Erisian formation on any continent. Every officer has held a breach.

The Order also operates Dissenbarg's only Erisian hospices, which double as intelligence posts: every wounded caravan driver is debriefed, every goblin captive questioned under chaplain's writ.

docs.title: Relation to Currencies & Regions
docs.text: Enkrad's economy is a hybrid. Internally it mints and taxes in Dissenbarg Krona — its own Enkrad Krona is the heaviest and most trusted Krona on the continent (weighed, not counted). For trade it depends on Vennerian Ducat via Venner and on Meblean Pearl via Sousu's Kreb outpost to the west. Anosi factors from Komme and Tatak will accept Enkrad Krona only at a discount — Enkrad factors return the insult by weighing Anosi coppers on the same scales.
