docs.title: Grimmel Civic Guard
docs.text: [!INFO] The Plow and the Bell — Citizens Who Muster Grimmel has no standing army by law — and the best militia in the south by habit.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The Grimmel Civic Guard is not an order and insists on the point. The Grimmel Republic — founded by settlers who fled both Erisian Empire and Erisian church in the Erisian expansion to build a state too small to oppress and too weak to crusade — forbids a standing army by the Assembly's founding compact. What it has instead is a citizen-militia that musters only when the bell rings, and has rung often enough to become tradition.

Every landholding adult in the Republic is technically a guardsman; practically, the Guard is the farmers, craftsmen, and town clerks who train one day in seven and know every ravine and cave system of Grimmel's rolling farmland and wooded groves. Geography has been Grimmel's ally: between the Limese League and the Vennerian Trade Republic, any invader must cross a power that finds Grimmel more useful as buffer than as prize — a buffer the Guard makes expensive to ignore.

In 596 AGD the Black Agent — carrying the encoded consciousnesses of Mana Mortvagn's lineage — drifted to Grimmel's coast, drawn by the unusually dense mage-cells of the Eisenheart and Mortvagn families. A year later Emrys and Ichi were born to the Eisenhearts; Lucien Mortvagn to the Mortvagns — with Mana Mortvagn to follow. The Guard, unknowing, posted extra watches that winter because something felt watched; the Assembly minutes record it as weather.

docs.title: Patron
docs.text: The Citizens' Assembly and the elected First Citizen (single five-year term). The Guard swears not to a crown or saint but to the bell — the civic bell of Grimmel town, whose rope any citizen may pull. Chaplains are not appointed; any faith may bless a muster, and the Guard has been blessed by Erisian priests, Elven-nature celebrants, and once, memorably, by an Ironcloak preceptor who told them they were already Ironcloak and left before anyone could arrest him. The Assembly apologized to the Pontificate of Eris and kept his pamphlet.

docs.title: Sigil
docs.text: A green sheaf of grain crossed with a wooden bell-clapper on a cream field, bordered in Grimmel's civic blue when fielded formally. No crown, no cross, no stag. Companies add a small Silver Bride-silver disc behind the sheaf when they march at night — not mysticism but practical: polished silver reflects the ring's light well enough to rally by.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Territorial militia, disaster response, and buffer defense. The Guard does not project force — it denies it to others: holding passes, flooding fords, and disappearing into cave systems where, local rumor insists, relics of the Glorious Alliance crash still wait. Its competence is homely and real: logistics by farm wagon, surgery by traveling healer-mages who can close a cut before it poisons, and a habit of winning not battles but weeks — enough for Venner or Limese to decide intervention is cheaper than conquest.

The two magical families are its quiet edge: the Eisenhearts and Mortvagns produce youths whose mage-cell density can, under stress, act as beacons or shields — effects the Guard attributes to luck.

docs.title: Relation to Currencies & Regions
docs.text:
The Guard pays no wages — service is civic duty — but the Assembly's war chest is Erilia and grain. Grimmel exports grain and imports manufactured goods; its market at Grimmel town is where Anosi Mark counting plates from the Anos Plutocracy quarter convert to Erilia at rates the Guard's clerks publish on the bell-house wall to shame gougers. Small Meblean Pearl hoops from Sousu circulate as prestige savings (a Grimmel dowry pearl is a Pearl that stayed).

When Vennerian Ducat prices spike at Beast's Bay, Grimmel feels it as bread prices months later — the Guard's real war is always against that delay.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Grimmel Civic Guard ] ├── Region: South Erisdar — Grimmel Republic / Grimmel Peninsula ├── Patron: Citizens' Assembly + First Citizen; civic bell as oath-object; touched by Eisenheart and Mortvagn lineages ├── Sigil: Green sheaf and bell-clapper on cream; night variant with Silver Bride disc ├── Backing: Erilia + grain; quarter-reserve in Anosi Mark and Meblean Pearl via Sousu ├── Faith: Civic — all faiths may bless, none commands └── See Also: Grimmel Republic, Limese League, Vennerian Trade Republic, Erisian church, Ironcloak, The Silver Bride

docs.title: Ironcloak Vanguard
docs.text: [!INFO] The Forward Cloak — Nethra's Eyes Beyond the Wall The Ironcloak do not mass. They precede.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The Ironcloak Vanguard is the expeditionary cutting edge of the Ironcloak — the rebel tradition that claims descent from Socrates through Plato, the original Christians and Protestants, the American Revolutionaries, the libertarians, and finally the asteroid refugees who preserved humanity against the Shadows for three million years. The main Ironcloak body on Erisdar searches for the Archive of the Traveler inside the Ruins of Baoth; the Vanguard is the formation that operates beyond Erisdar, in the shadows of the Shadows' other holdings.

Formally founded as the Vanguard in the scattering after the Great Divergence, its remit is the intercontinental: Merratodoni (where the Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni and the Merratodoni Liberty economy provide cover), Purification Lands-adjacent shipping, and the long watch on Eternal Paradise on Romanium Island — the Shadow base-state in the far NE where the Hybrians keep their most honest map. Vanguard cadres are small — a dozen at most — and led by a Lantern, a veteran who has read the fragmentary Nethrian Revelation and accepts that the goddess Nethra may walk among the Shadows themselves.

The Vanguard's history is unwritten by design. Its victories are recorded as accidents in other nations' archives — a lighthouse that failed at the right hour, a ledger that burned clean.

docs.title: Patron
docs.text:
Nethra — the Iron Goddess, a different kind of Shadow, daughter of Kirivis who survived his beheading by Rulfred and detonated the device that created Sea of Leviathan. Only the upper echelon knows she is worshipped at all; most Vanguard fighters think they fight for the idea of iron — endurance without worship. The Vanguard's upper cells know better and keep the secret because a goddess who is also a Shadow is a difficult prayer to teach.

Its philosophical patron is the rebel lineage itself; Vanguard instruction begins with Socrates' trial and ends with the choice to board a ship that will not return.

docs.title: Sigil
docs.text: No sigil in the field — the Vanguard is the sigil's absence. When it must mark, it uses a plain iron-gray cloak, unbadged, the fabric weighted to hang without wind. The inverse — a burned Shadow eye — is cut into trees and left on doors to signal we were here, and the Shadow was not.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Forward reconnaissance, sabotage, and deniable liberation. The Vanguard does not hold ground; it spoils it for the Hybrians. Its teams infiltrate through trade, especially via Demon's Horn and Beast's Bay, plant contradictions in colonial administrations (Anos Maloca, Anos Marti, Vennerian Channel outposts), and exfiltrate persons and relics the Shadows would rather keep. In Merratodoni its safe houses move with the caravans between Maemon and Luzia, and its signal is a cloak hung inside-out.

Its signature tactic is the hollow day — a day where everything goes slightly right for the locals and slightly wrong for the master's tally — repeated until a colony decides the master's math is not worth the cost.

docs.title: Relation to Currencies & Regions
docs.text:
The Vanguard carries no standard coin — carrying one standard is how you are caught. Its logistics run on whatever is local: Merratodoni Liberty in Merratodoni (its most honest home, silvered with Romanium promise), Erilia on Erisdar, Vennerian Ducat and Anosi Mark at sea, Demonic Ember when it must deal through Demon's Horn, and Meblean Pearl when diplomats are the mark (pearls are forgettable because they are beautiful). Its hard reserve is Romanium itself — raw, unminted, the one resource all of the Shadows' empires must account for and therefore the hardest to counterfeit as story.

A Vanguard cadre that cannot change its money is a cadre that has already been made.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Ironcloak Vanguard ] ├── Region: Merratodoni primary — operates intercontinentally (Erisdar, Kutten, Lung Continent, Romanium Island) ├── Patron: Nethra (Iron Goddess) — upper echelon; lineage Socrates → Union of Sovereign Planets; opposes Hybrians / Shadows ├── Sigil: Unbadged iron-gray cloak; burned Shadow eye as trail mark; no heraldry by doctrine ├── Backing: Merratodoni Liberty cover + Romanium hard reserve; mission cash in Erilia, Vennerian Ducat, Anosi Mark, Demonic Ember, Meblean Pearl via Sousu and Demon's Horn ├── Seeks: Ruins of Baoth → Archive of the Traveler (with main Ironcloak) └── See Also: Ironcloak, Nethra, Merratodoni Liberty, Eternal Paradise, Hybrians, The Silver Bride

docs.title: Kobre Gearwardens
docs.text: [!INFO] The Interlocking Guard — Steel That Fits A purse that meshes. A line that holds. A gear that will not slip.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The military order of Kobre — a continent south of the Formingar Ocean whose isolation let Hybrians try to take it with Homunculi as agents, and whose liberation came by accident when Baoth's destruction in the Great Divergence shattered the psychic link and the Homunculi awoke free under the Unnamed (later Omipre). The Gearwardens were born in the stabilization that followed centuries of starving war.

Kobre holds four nations — Homunculi Kingdom (the free homunculi), Coalsteel and Diamonds (dwarf kingdoms — Diamonds built a wall against the Homunculi), and Elf Kingdom (elven exiles). The Gearwardens are the only formation drawn from all four in practice if not in name: homunculi-forged, dwarf-tested, elven-carried. Their founding charter was a milling-tolerance agreement. Their first battle was holding a pass while a gear-forge was moved behind the Diamonds wall. They hold that a war won without the forge running is a war paid for in forge-winter later.

Every homunculus still trains in combat from youth; every Coalsteel dwarf still knows how to hold a line; the Gearwardens are what happens when both remember how at the same time.

docs.title: Patron
docs.text:
The Homunculi Kingdom as institution — and through it, the memory of the Unnamed / Omipre, who taught that abandonment by their Silver Bride-calling god did not require abandonment of each other. Formally the Gearwardens are attested by the Coalsteel furnaces and Diamond presses; spiritually they are homunculi communal — no one eats alone, no one holds alone. The Gearwardens' pre-battle shared meal is eaten from one pot, gear-teeth clacking as bowls mesh.

Entry is mutual and banned in mirror: Homunculi are banned from Coalsteel, Diamonds, and Elf Kingdom; outsiders are unwelcome in the Homunculi lands. The Gearwardens are the exception both sides grant because they have seen the alternative.

docs.title: Sigil
docs.text: An interlocking gear and a crossed hammer-pike on a soot-gray field edged in diamond-white. The gear's tooth count signals company: 12-tooth for line, 24 for veteran, 36 for command, 48 for the forge-guard that never leaves the hobber hall. Counterfeit insignia is instantly detectable — real Gearwarden gears mesh and turn; fakes jam. Engineers literally use retired insignia as gears in the field, a fact both dwarves and homunculi consider not improvisation but proof of design.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Precision defense and industrial security. The Gearwardens hold the walls and passes between the Homunculi and dwarven kingdoms, protect the furnace valleys and the The Groom-ward coast of Kobre that still draws [Black Agent|black dust] curiosities, and — critically — guard the fabrication chain that makes the continent's wealth: Coalsteel furnaces, Diamond presses, water-powered hobbers that cut gears to 0.02mm. A Gearwarden line that breaks is not a lost position but a broken supply: every retreat is therefore a re-convergence on the next forge, not a rout.

They loan companies to Kutten smiths at Malbodor who import Kobre steel, and those smiths in turn send Kutten Fang scalps back as receipts — a quiet alliance measured in steel quality, not speeches.

docs.title: Relation to Currencies & Regions
docs.text:
The Gearwardens are the guard behind the Kobran Gear — gear-shaped steel discs where teeth count is denomination, forged by the Homunculi Kingdom to absurd tolerance. Backed by Coalsteel furnaces, Kobre fabrication, and the fact that a counterfeit gear jams a purse — the most literal proof-of-work on Ge'or. The four Kobre nations all use Gear, and even Elf Kingdom exiles adopted it for trade.

For foreign dealings the Gearwardens convert through Demon's Horn and Beast's Bay to Vennerian Ducat for sea freight, and to Kutten Fang via Malbodor for mineral trade; their reserve is steel itself — ingots stamped with gear-tooth edges so a purse of reserves can literally rebuild a hobber.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Kobre Gearwardens ] ├── Region: Kobre — Homunculi Kingdom + Coalsteel, Diamonds, Elf Kingdom ├── Patron: The Unnamed / Omipre + Homunculi Kingdom communal; forged by Coalsteel / Diamonds industry ├── Sigil: Interlocking gear (12/24/36/48-tooth by rank) over hammer-pike on soot-gray, diamond-white edge ├── Backing: Kobran Gear — steel fabrication + tolerance proof; also quotes Kutten Fang and Vennerian Ducat ├── Isolation: Mutual bans between Homunculi and dwarven/elven kingdoms — Gearwardens the exception └── See Also: Homunculi Kingdom, Kobran Gear, Kobre, The Groom, Formingar Ocean, The Silver Bride

docs.title: Koel Order
docs.text: [!INFO] The Peninsula Watch — Faith on the Isthmus Between Grimmel's plows and the League's ledgers, Koel keeps the narrow gate.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
A small independent military-religious order holding the neck of the Grimmel Peninsula in South Erisdar, the Koel Order is the cartographer's afterthought that controls the map. Founded as a frontier priory of the Erisian church during the same wave of southward Erisian expansion that pushed colonists toward Venner and the sea, it never grew into a territorial state — and never needed to. Whoever holds Koel can close South Erisdar's east from its west.

The Order's lands are compact: a fortified isthmus, a port on the Venner Sea side, a customs house on the Eris Sea side, and a string of watchtowers up the peninsula spine. Both the Limese League and the Grimmel Republic have tried to buy influence there; both learned that Koel sells passage but not allegiance. Its archive famously records every bribe offered and refused since 312 AGD — the Book of Closed Gates.

In the Era of Cracking Walls, Koel remained neutral and traded with all sides, then closed the peninsula to armies and opened it to grain — a decision that fed Grimmel through one famine and made Koel beloved by farmers and hated by generals.

docs.title: Patron
docs.text: Erisian church, but locally the patron is Saint Koel, a semi-legendary peninsula hermit who, the story says, held the isthmus alone for forty days against a Grimmel migration with nothing but a bell. The bell still hangs in Koel's gatehouse and is rung whenever a foreign column is sighted. Whether Koel existed matters less than that the bell does.

docs.title: Sigil
docs.text: A gray tower between two blue seas on a white field, an Erisian cross in the tower's window. In war the tower is rendered stark — no cross, just stone — a quiet signal that Koel fights for ground, not for theology, when steel is actually out.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Isthmus wardens and customs knights. Koel fields light cavalry, tower guards, and a corps of precisian clerks who can tell at a glance whether a manifest hides Romanium. Its real power is procedural: control of transit, search, and toll. An army that cannot cross Koel must sail around the peninsula through waters where Venner and Anos both extract their own tolls.

Knights of Koel are famously incorruptible in the small things and flexible in the large — they will argue a barrel count for hours and then let a philosophy through without comment.

docs.title: Relation to Currencies & Regions
docs.text:
The Order's tolls are priced in Erilia for Erisdar traffic and Vennerian Ducat for sea traffic, with a notorious conversion spread that funds the towers. Its vault holds a mixed reserve deliberately balanced between Erilia, Ducats, and Anosi Mark plates — Koel factors joke they are the only honest money changers on the peninsula because both Anos and Venner watch them and each would expose cheating in favor of the other.

Small Meblean Pearl parcels from Sousu pass through Koel customs under seal — pilgrim jewelry and diplomatic gifts that Koel is paid not to open.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Koel Order ] ├── Region: South Erisdar — Grimmel Peninsula isthmus, between Venner Sea and Eris Sea ├── Patron: Saint Koel (hermit of the gate) — via Erisian church ├── Sigil: Gray tower between two seas, Erisian cross in the window; war-variant without cross ├── Backing: Erilia + Vennerian Ducat tolls; reserves in Anosi Mark + Meblean Pearl transit seals via Sousu ├── Role: Peninsula customs and wardens; controls east-west passage └── See Also: Scarlet Order, Grimmel Republic, Limese League, Vennerian Trade Republic, Anos Plutocracy, Erisian church

docs.title: Limese League Condottieri
docs.text: [!INFO] The Contract Sword — Loyalty Priced by the Season Not knights. Not mercenaries. Condottieri — captains who own the company that owns the war.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The military arm of the Limese League — a mercantile league-state of South Erisdar whose capital Lima governs by guild membership rather than blood. Where other nations have orders, Limese has contracts. The Condottieri system was codified after the Era of Cracking Walls, when the League learned the most profitable war is the one you finance on both sides without fighting yourself.

Each condottiere holds a condotta — a season-contract from the League Council granting rights to recruit, garrison, and make war under the League's flag, for a fixed price plus plunder schedule. The Council in Lima does not command the captains; it audits them. Failure is punished not by execution but by bankruptcy — a crueler fate in a league where citizenship is guild shares.

The Condottieri have no home territory beyond the League's port at Lima and the leased garrison at Sus Principality; their strength is warehoused as ships, depots, and Away in East Erisdar, the League's territory south of Sperdia. They have fought for Venner against Anos, for Anos against Venner, and once famously for both in the same month — with two companies observing a private truce while their employers skirmished around them.

docs.title: Patron
docs.text: No saint. The patron is the League Council itself — the guild aldermen of Lima who sign the condotta. Captains swear not to a god but to the contract, sealed with wax from the Meblean Pearl hoop-forges of Sousu (a League affectation: a pearl seal cannot be faked warm). Chaplains of any faith may ride with a company, but none may countermand a contract. The joke among captains: Our Eris is interest, our Helism is six ledgers.

docs.title: Sigil
docs.text: Each company flies its own, but the League's war flag is a golden ledger-book over crossed pike and boarding axe, on a sea-blue field — the ledger open to show a red contract seal. When under League-wide muster the companies add a narrow white border — the White Contract — signaling that this time the League considers breach of faith a capital crime, not a commercial one.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Contract infantry, marines, and siege specialists for hire. Limese Condottieri excel where money matters more than zeal: port seizures, customs house defense, shipboarding, and the precise, low-casualty battles trading powers prefer. They maintain the best pay-chest discipline on Erisdar — desertion is rare because pay is punctually perfect — and the best negotiated surrender practice: a Condottieri captain will accept a garrison's parole and sell it back to its employer for a fee, and both sides consider this honorable.

They are the instrument by which a league with no aristocracy projects force: buy the battle instead of breeding it.

docs.title: Relation to Currencies & Regions
docs.text:
The Condottieri are the most currency-savvy force in South Erisdar. Contracts are priced in whatever the client trusts: Vennerian Ducat for sea powers, Anosi Mark for counting-house powers, Erilia for imperial contracts, and — for the largest league-to-league deals — Meblean Pearl parcels under seal from Sousu, carried by bonded courier and never counted at the table.

League factors in Lima make their margin on exchange, not war: a captain paid in Ducats who needs Erilia for inland hire pays the League's spread both ways. The Condottieri understand this perfectly and consider it the Council's legitimate tithe. They also trade extensively through Demon's Horn, where Demonic Ember and Silver Talon both clear.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Limese League Condottieri ] ├── Region: South Erisdar — Limese League (Lima), with territory Away in East Erisdar ├── Patron: Limese League Council — the condotta (contract) as oath ├── Sigil: Golden ledger over pike and axe on blue; white border for League muster; pearls from Sousu on seals ├── Backing: Multi-currency — Vennerian Ducat, Anosi Mark, Erilia, and Meblean Pearl via Sousu; clearing at Demon's Horn ├── Faith: Guild-loyal — chaplains tolerated, contracts sacred └── See Also: Limese League, Vennerian Trade Republic, Anos Plutocracy, Sousu, Demon's Horn, Away

docs.title: Marti Howl Riders
docs.text: [!INFO] The Howl on the Drum — Skin, Hoop, and Fang You hear them before you see them — a drum that rings true, a howl that answers it.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The confederated war-riders of Marti — a southern continent tethered to Lumina by the Vennerian Aelefer Channel and descending southwest into permafrost toward the southern polar ice. Marti holds eight nations — Germina, Kut, Oigopol, Kobra, Brase, Cobal, Kramsadar, Maboro — plus the outposts Anos Marti (northern, Anosi) and Vennerian Channel (Marti) (Vennerian). The Howl Riders are how that fractured continent stays one story: wolf-pacts and drum-hoops.

The pact is old — older than the Vennerian Aelefer Channel cut, older than the colonial flags. Wolf-folk of Kut and Oigopol (wolvesfolk, not wargs — the distinction matters: wolvesfolk talk, wargs eat) and cold-adapted snake people of Kobra made common cause against Brase coldspeople incursions and Kramsadar dragon highland raids. The drum joined later, when Romanium hoops made the signal carry over tundra wind where horn and smoke fail. Now every Marti nation except Kramsadar — the isolated dragon kingdom in its own sky — sends riders to the seasonal muster at the Germina steppe, where Silver Bride's winter arch is lowest and the drums sound longest.

Anos factors at Anos Marti hire Howl Riders as scouts and pay in Anosi Mark; Venner charters them to patrol the channel approaches. Both are learning that hiring a howl is easier than commanding it.

docs.title: Patron
docs.text:
No single patron. The Howl Riders swear by the Wolf — the composite ancestor of the Kut/Oigopol wolvesfolk — and by the Drum as oath-object. Initiation requires tapping a true Martian Drum (wolf-hide over Romanium hoop — a true Drum rings clear when tapped, a clipped one thuds) and holding the note while a wolf howls the denomination back. Cold-snake Kobra riders add their own rite: a hooded passage through a Kobra frost-gorge in silence until the drum finds them.

Human riders of Germina (multi-ethnic, many descended from Erisdar and Erisdarian Catmen who arrived on Vennerian ships) and dwarf riders of Cobal near the permafrost take the same oath; the wolvesfolk consider this correct — the Drum does not sniff.

docs.title: Sigil
docs.text: A white wolf's head in howl over a taut drum-hoop on a storm-gray field, the hoop rendered in Romanium-blue to show it is hoop, not frame. Companies mark the hoop's diameter as rank: small hoops (patrol), large hoops (war-band). At night the riders add a thin Silver Bride-silver arc above the wolf — the ring under which the muster howl carries farthest.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Wolf cavalry, tundra scouts, and drum-signal corps. The Riders fight as light and medium cavalry on wargs and wolves (large wolf-like predators — territorial and violent, but bonded as mounts through wolvesfolk mediation), as scouts who can read permafrost, and as the continent's living telegraph: drum-skin stretched over Romanium hoops can relay a message across a valley faster than a rider, and wolf-howls can carry denomination and urgency in tone. Marti saying: if the drum rings clear, pay; if it thuds, cut it open — the assay test every trader knows.

They are also the continent's herd guard: Marti wealth is herd — wolves, hides, meat, and the skins that become Drum currency itself — and the riders keep herds alive through winter that kills armies.

docs.title: Relation to Currencies & Regions
docs.text:
The Riders ride on the coin they are: Martian Drum — hide over Romanium hoop, valued by diameter and skin thickness, backed by Marti herds and hunting where skin is wealth. A Drum stacked as plates clacks unmistakably in any bazaar from Marti to Beast's Bay. Anos factors at Anos Marti exchange Drum to Anosi Mark at the port; Vennerian wardens at Vennerian Channel (Marti) quote Drum to Vennerian Ducat for channel passage.

Off-continent the Riders trade Drum for Xetian Coil (Xeti) and Luminal Tusk (Lumina) at Beast's Bay, and for Silver Talon when Kutten Fang scalpers need Marti iron — a barter the riders prefer because it keeps the Anos ledger at arm's length.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Marti Howl Riders ] ├── Region: Marti — Kut, Oigopol, Kobra, Germina, Cobal, plus Anos Marti ├── Patron: The Wolf (ancestral wolvesfolk) + the Drum as oath-object; cold rites of Kobra and Germina steppe muster ├── Sigil: White howling wolf over Romanium-blue drum-hoop on storm-gray; Silver Bride-silver arc at night ├── Backing: Martian Drum (wolf-hide + Romanium hoop, herd wealth) — ports exchange to Anosi Mark and Vennerian Ducat ├── Mounts: Wargs/wolves (bonded via wolvesfolk), tundra and steppe cavalry └── See Also: Marti, Martian Drum, Anosi Mark, Vennerian Channel (Marti), Beast's Bay, The Silver Bride, Sousu

docs.title: Order of Draco
docs.text: [!INFO] The Dragon's Oath — Eris's Draconic Blade The sword-hand of the Empire, sworn to the Apostle Draco — black dragon on gold, and they do not break.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
One of the two order states of the Erisian Empire alongside the Ever Order, the Order of Draco traces its charter to the early consolidation of Central Erisdar under the Erisian crown. Named for Draco, one of the Apostles of Eris, the Order was granted lands, fortresses, and the right to recruit across the 38 counties and 4 free cities in exchange for perpetual service as the Empire's heavy reserve.

Unlike the secular duchies (-berg) and counties (-stadt) of the imperial subdivisions, Draco holds its territory as a religious-military corporation — part of the Empire, yet self-governing under its Grandmaster. Its knights fought at the front of the Crusade of 278 AGD that took half the lands of the Mann tribes, and its banners were the first to fly over the converted marches before Kosbaldo's rebellion reclaimed them.

The Draco knights remember Baoth differently than the chroniclers do. Where the Ruins now drown a dragon kingdom, Draco sees a warning: a dragon king who trusted the wrong oath (Goldenborn and Rulfred). Their motto answers it: Oath kept, dragon fed.

docs.title: Patron
docs.text:
Draco, Apostle of Eris. In Erisian hagiography Draco is the apostle of endurance and iron discipline — the dragon who knelt to Eris. The Order's chaplains teach that Draco's black scales were not color but oath-iron, and every Draco knight who takes the final vow touches a reliquary said to contain a scale from Draco's own mantle (in truth, iron from the Meble forges of Sousu, kept polished to a lie).

The chaplains answer to the Pontificate of Eris in doctrine, but to the Grandmaster in discipline — a tension that has kept Draco more loyal to Central Erisdar than to any pontiff.

docs.title: Sigil
docs.text: A black dragon rampant on a gold field, wings folded, clutching a white Erisian cross. Bordered in imperial crimson when fielded alongside the Erisian Empire's own banners. Knights of rank add a single silver star of The Silver Bride above the dragon's head — not piety but politics, a reminder that even the heavens are under Eris's dominion, as the Empire claims.

docs.title: Role
docs.text: Draco is the Empire's armored fist: heavy cavalry, fortress engineers, and garrison knights. Its companies hold the border marches between Central Erisdar and North Erisdar, ride as shock troops when the Erilian Federation moves against Mann, and provide the honor guard for the Kennberg court at need. Recruitment favors second sons of county knights and proven men-at-arms — birth matters less than oath-keeping, a rare meritocratic streak the Empire tolerates because it works.

docs.title: Relation to Currencies & Regions
docs.text:
Paid and provisioned in Erilia, the cracking coin of Central Erisdar. The Draco treasury at Draco-burg mints no coin of its own — it draws from the Erisian exchequer and from its own estates, then spends in Erilia at Elboria and Kennberg markets. For foreign purchase of Romanium dust and northern silver, its factors exchange Erilia for Alegorian Crown at the Northaxeland border and for Silver Talon in East Erisdar.

Its fortresses sit astride the roads from Central Erisdar to Loren and Magna; every toll is taken in Erilia, every mercenary contract priced in it — the Order is one of the few institutions still propping the currency's trust.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Order of Draco ] ├── Region: Central Erisdar — order state of the Erisian Empire ├── Patron: Draco, Apostles of Eris — via Pontificate of Eris ├── Sigil: Black dragon on gold, silver star of The Silver Bride for commanders ├── Backing: Erilia + imperial estates and tolls; exchanges to Alegorian Crown and Silver Talon for Romanium ├── Currency: Erilia (primary); accepts Alegorian Crown at the northern march └── See Also: Order of Ever, Erisian Empire, Erisian Empire Subdivisions, Erilian Federation, Alegoria

docs.title: Order of Ever
docs.text: [!INFO] The Everlasting Watch — Faith That Does Not Tire Named for the sleepless apostle, Ever watches where Draco strikes — and holds what Draco takes.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The second order state of the Erisian Empire, founded alongside the Draco Order when the Empire formalized its 2 order states, 3 duchies, and 38 counties. If Draco is the sword, Ever is the shield-wall. Named for Ever, the apostle of vigil — the one who never slept while Eris prayed.

Ever's charter was monastic before it was military: a hospitaller rule that built waystations along the pilgrim roads to Lake Leviathan and the Ruins of Baoth. Over centuries the hospices became fortresses, the infirmarians became surgeons of the battlefield, and the rule of prayer became a rule of watch. The Order holds extensive lands in Central Erisdar as a corporate fief, paying no county tax and answering only to its Grand Prior and, nominally, the Emperor.

Ever knights were the logisticians of the Crusade of 278 AGD — they fed Draco's advance — and the rearguard when Kosbaldo's guerrillas cut the supply lines and stranded Erilio's gains in what is now the Mann Order frontier. That failure taught Ever its modern doctrine: never outrun your hospice.

docs.title: Patron
docs.text: Ever, Apostle of Eris. Erisian scripture calls Ever the eye that did not close, who kept watch over Eris through the Forty Nights. The Order's brethren keep a literal night vigil — one chapel in every Ever fortress, lit through every hour, where a brother watches the Silver Bride cross the sky and records its position against Erisian feast days. They claim the ring's light is Ever's lamp; the educated among them know it is geography, not miracle, and keep watching anyway.

docs.title: Sigil
docs.text: A white evergreen tree on a blue field, roots encircling a gold Erisian cross, bordered in silver. The tree is not Elvish — though Alegoria's stag sometimes appears in northern Ever commanderies where the faith bleeds into relations with Northaxeland — but the Order's own symbol of endurance: leaves in winter, watch in war. Veteran priories add a thin silver ring around the cross, echoing The Silver Bride.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Ever fields garrison infantry, field hospitals, and pilgrim road wardens rather than heavy cavalry. Its brothers build and hold: bridges, hospices, granaries, and the fortified villages that make imperial rule feel like order rather than occupation. In war it provides the anvil to Draco's hammer — disciplined spear and crossbow blocks that do not break, and surgeons who save enough of the enemy to convert them.

The Order recruits widely — pious farmers, town surgeons, and even reformed mercenaries — and promotes through literacy and demonstrated steadiness, making it the least aristocratic of the imperial orders.

docs.title: Relation to Currencies & Regions
docs.text: Like Draco, Ever operates on Erilia. Its hospices tithe in kind (grain, cloth, medicines) and convert surplus through Kennberg and Elboria markets, holding hard reserves in Alegorian Crown silver for years when the imperial mint debases. Its waystations along the Lyrical Forest and Mystical Forest routes are trusted exchangers — pilgrims change Crown and West Erisdarian Guilder for Erilia under Ever's cross and feel they have not been cheated, which is rare in Central Erisdar.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Order of Ever ] ├── Region: Central Erisdar — order state of the Erisian Empire ├── Patron: Ever, Apostles of Eris — via Pontificate of Eris and Erisian church ├── Sigil: White evergreen on blue, gold cross with silver ring for The Silver Bride ├── Backing: Erilia tithes + hospice estates; hard reserves in Alegorian Crown ├── Faith: Hospitaller vigil — Erisian church monastic rule, road wardens └── See Also: Order of Draco, Erisian Empire, Ruins of Baoth, Alegoria, Pontificate of Eris

docs.title: Scarlet Order
docs.text: [!INFO] The Red Banner — Action Over Prayer They took the crimson of the drowned ocean and made it a promise: we will not kneel when we should ride.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
A martial-religious order-state in South Erisdar, the Scarlet Order claims its red from the day the Formingar Ocean turned crimson in the Shattered Dawn — when the Formingar reactor failed, Elvengar drowned, and the sea itself was baptized in rust and fallout. Where the Erisian church preaches submission, Scarlet preaches intervention: Eris helps those who saddle up.

Formally Erisian — its knights take vows before an Erisian cross — but temperamentally its own church. Successive pontiffs have tried to rein it in; every attempt has produced a new Scarlet Grandmaster who is more beloved by his knights for having been rebuked. The Order holds compact, fortified lands between Grimmel and the Vennerian Trade Republic, with outposts shadowing the pilgrim roads that feed Central Erisdar.

Scarlet knights are the most formidable heavy horse in South Erisdar — not because their kit is finer than Northaxeland baronial cavalry, but because they charge when others negotiate.

docs.title: Patron
docs.text:
Formally Eris, via the Erisian church, but the true patron is the Shattered Dawn as revelation. Scarlet chaplains preach that the crimson sea was not curse but summons — proof that the world is broken and faith without action is complicity. Their war-cry is For the Red Sea, and every novice spends a vigil night wearing a white cloak dipped at the hem in red dye, then rides until the dye fades to pink — a reminder that zeal, like color, must be renewed.

More practical novices note patronage also flows from Lima and Venner merchants who prefer hiring a cross that rides.

docs.title: Sigil
docs.text: A scarlet cross on a white field, the lower arm lengthened and tipped like a lance point, often rendered as if dripping at the foot — the Bleeding Lance. Command banners add a thin black border taken from the ash of Shattered Dawn chronicles. Opposite Alegoria's stag and Silver Bride-silver, the Scarlet deliberate monochrome is the point: no gold, no stag, only red.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Shock cavalry and rapid intervention. The Order fields lancers, mounted serjeants, and a feared corps of dismounted red-cloaks who fight on foot with poleaxe when terrain denies the horse. Its doctrine is simple: arrive first, hit hardest, offer terms after. It garrisons no great cities — it keeps its strength mobile and rents it to allies (and sometimes, through Limese brokers, to clients) — which makes it both respected and distrusted in South Erisdar.

Relations: cold with the Erisian Theocracy (they hate being out-preached), wary of Grimmel's pacifism, pragmatic with Anos and Venner, fraternal with the Koel Order on the Grimmel Peninsula.

docs.title: Relation to Currencies & Regions
docs.text: The Order prices in Erilia at home — its lands are Erilian-taxed — but campaigns on Vennerian Ducat and Anosi Mark interchangeably, whichever client pays. Its treasury at Scarlet Hall holds a notorious Meblean Pearl reliquary — sea pearls from Sousu set in a silver hoop, worn as both prayer beads and emergency reserve; a joke among factors: Scarlet prays in pearls because prayers bounce.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Scarlet Order ] ├── Region: South Erisdar ├── Patron: Erisian church (formal) — true patron the Shattered Dawn / Formingar Ocean crimson ├── Sigil: Scarlet Bleeding Lance cross on white; black border for command ├── Backing: Erilia inland, Vennerian Ducat / Anosi Mark on campaign, Meblean Pearl reliquary via Sousu ├── Faith: Erisian — action over prayer └── See Also: Koel Order, Grimmel Republic, Pontificate of Eris, The Shattered Dawn, Formingar Ocean, Alegoria

docs.title: Silver Talon Guard
docs.text: [!INFO] The Dwarven Talon — Silver That Weighs True Every Talon cut is a promise the assayer will stand behind.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The military-commercial guard of the Silver Republic in East Erisdar — the property-franchise republic of Argentport whose Council of Eighty rules by land, not birth. The Guard's formal title is Guard of the Argent Assay, founded when the Republic's founding families realized that a coin trusted from Silver Republic to New Mann required guards as honest as its weigh-masters.

Dwaven partnership is the soul of the formation: assay offices in Dwarvengor weigh every Silver Talon — alloyed silver with a trace blue-glancing Romanium — and claw-cut underweight coins on the spot. The Guard provides the arms that make that honesty stick. It garrisons the argentite mines, the coastal shipyards that build the fastest hulls on the Silver Coast, and the banking houses that, during the Era of Cracking Walls, financed both sides of imperial succession disputes and discovered the business model still works.

The Guard's motto, adopted from a dwarven foreman's rebuke — if you cannot weigh it, you cannot guard it — is stitched inside every standard.

docs.title: Patron
docs.text: The Silver Republic's Council of Eighty and, spiritually, Pitra — the legendary figure of Pitraism whose faith declares the gods love money and gold, borrowing its pantheon from the dwarves with Dwarvengor as theological lender. Dwarven inspiration is not hidden; the Guard's chaplains are Pitraist and dwarf-friend alike, and no guardsman confuses the arrangement: Pitra blesses the weighing because dwarves invented the scale.

docs.title: Sigil
docs.text: A silver talon clutching a blue-flecked shard on a charcoal field, the shard rendered with a single Romanium-blue highlight that catches light when standards are silk. Financial detachments add a small assay scissors beneath the talon — the claw-cut promise. The Silver Bride appears nowhere; the Guard's pride is that its silver is earthly, not heavenly, and can be weighed.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Mine garrison, bullion escort, and coastal defense. The Talon Guard fields heavy dwarven-drilled infantry, assay clerks who are also crossbowmen, and a small marine contingent that rides Silver Republic hulls as supercargo-guards. It does not seek battle for glory — it seeks audit: holding a mine until the count is certified, holding a quay until the silver is aboard, holding a debt until it is paid.

In the field beyond the Republic — in Fractured Erislod, New Mann, Away, and the ports where Spasian merchants grudgingly quote Talons to be taken seriously — the Guard operates as armed factor, not occupier.

docs.title: Relation to Currencies & Regions
docs.text:
The Guard is the sword behind the Silver Talon — the most honest coin in the east. Backed by silver + Romanium trace and enforced by the Dwarvengor assay, the Talon is the currency Spasians ban at the border and smuggle anyway. The Guard's treasury settles in Talons first and converts to Erilia only when trading west of Central Erisdar; its officers can quote spreads to Alegorian Crown and West Erisdarian Guilder from memory because they have carried both home as receipts.

Its great rivalry is not with any army but with counterfeit Talons — most stamped in Pilferhorn and washed through Demon's Horn traders who will honor either coin long enough to sell you the wrong one.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Silver Talon Guard ] ├── Region: East Erisdar — Silver Republic (Argentport) + Dwarvengor assay partnership ├── Patron: Silver Republic Council of Eighty — faith Pitraism via Dwarves / Pitra ├── Sigil: Silver talon clutching Romanium-blue shard on charcoal; assay scissors for financial detachments ├── Backing: Silver Talon (silver + Romanium trace) — also quotes Erilia, Alegorian Crown, West Erisdarian Guilder ├── Coast: Silver Coast shipyards and Argentport banking houses └── See Also: Silver Talon, Silver Republic, Dwarvengor, Romanium, Demon's Horn, Alegoria

docs.title: Star Paladins of Mann
docs.text: [!INFO] The Star Hole Knights — Capital of the Gods, Guarded They charge through the star-hole in their own coin.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The sacred military order of the Mann Order in North Erisdar — the military dictatorship built by Kosbaldo after the Crusade of 278 AGD led by Erilio (the Kennberg-born general) took half the lands of the Mann tribes for the Eris cult. The tribes' guerrilla war modernized the unconquered marches and hardened into a state whose capital, Mann, is for Mannosta what no city can be for an Erisian: capital of the gods (Mannosta itself means "greatness of Mann").

The Paladins are Kosbaldo's oath made armor. At the start they were tribal champions with star-steel seized from upland falls; now they are a drilled order of paladins who fight as much for theology as territory. The Erilian Federation to the south — which holds Tiaboria/Tilboria, the great city of the Mann lands — calls them pagans; the Paladins agree and charge anyway. Refugees from the invasion famously crossed the Mongrel Forest east into the Fractured State of Erislod to build New Mann, and Paladin guides led the first columns through the dark.

Many within Mann now follow Alegoria alongside the older Mannosta faith; the Paladins accommodate both — a paladin may pray to the star-hole or the stag-antlers, but he fights for Mann.

docs.title: Patron
docs.text:
Kosbaldo the founder-general, and through him Mann itself as capital of the gods. Liturgically the patron is the twin canopy of Mannosta (star and ancestor worship, now reduced and under siege) and Alegoria (the stag-god whose northern faith dominates Northaxeland and the surrounding sister realms). New brethren choose at initiation whether their star or their stag is carved first on the scabbard — a choice no commander may countermand.

The Paladins' war-name for their faith is simply The Star — as in the Mannic Star coin they refuse to debase.

docs.title: Sigil
docs.text: A five-point star-hole void on a midnight-blue field, edged in star-steel silver — literally the shape punched through the Mannic Star coin, rendered flag-scale so the sky shows through when the banner is moth-holed. Northern companies add staggered stag-antlers of Alegoria behind the star; traditionalist companies render the antlers as shadow, visible only at angle — Mannosta first, Alegoria acknowledged.

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Paladin heavy infantry and star-steel shock. The Paladins field dismounted paladins in star-steel harness, axe and longshield, with light Mongrel Forest scouts who know the paths the refugees took to New Mann. Their doctrine is defensive-offensive: hold the heights that the Federation's Erisian knights must take uphill, then counter through ground you have blessed by keeping it.

They are also the Mann Order's priesthood-at-arms: every Paladin conventicle mints judgment as well as coin, and disputations between Mannosta and Alegorian adherents are settled under the same roof that punches Stars.

docs.title: Relation to Currencies & Regions
docs.text:
The order mints and militates in Mannic Star — the star-punched, string-threaded, deliberately non-convertible theocratic coin of Mann alone. At the border, Crown exchangers must thread Stars to count them — Mann's ritual humiliation of Northaxeland's Alegorian Crown system. Erilian factors value a Star at 1.4 Crowns for Romanium deals; Paladins value it at what the gods allow.

This makes campaigning complex: outside Mann, the Paladins fund themselves in Alegorian Crown (from sympathizers in Elvenkrad and Venkradian) and in Silver Talon when dwarven bankers need Mann timber, but they count only in Stars. Their treasury's hard reserve is star-steel itself — the holed discs — stored on cord as star-strings, the Mann dowry and the Paladins' portable fortress.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Star Paladins of Mann ] ├── Region: North Erisdar — Mann Order (capital Mann, faith Mannosta) ├── Patron: Kosbaldo — faith Mannosta + minority Alegoria; versus Erisian church / Erilian Federation ├── Sigil: Five-point star-hole on midnight-blue, star-steel silver edge; antlers of Alegoria for northern companies; sky of The Silver Bride through the hole ├── Backing: Mannic Star (non-convertible, star-steel, holed) — exchanges to Alegorian Crown and Silver Talon abroad ├── War: Invaded by Erilian Federation — holds Mongrel Forest routes to New Mann └── See Also: Mann Order, Mannic Star, Alegorian Crown, Alegoria, The Silver Bride, Erilian Federation

docs.title: Vennerian Channel Wardens
docs.text: [!INFO] The Toll Wardens — Every Hull Pays Between Xeti Sea and Beast's Bay they built a gate in the water — and then became the gate.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The military-maritime order of the Vennerian Trade Republic — the sea-trade superpower of South Erisdar whose constructed Vennerian Channel linking the Xeti Sea to Beast's Bay is the busiest chokepoint on Ge'or. The Wardens are the force that makes "Venner controls passage — every ship pays" a true sentence rather than a boast.

Formally chartered after the channel's cut (the labor that dammed and dredged between Xeti and Marti is its own dark chapter — Venner chronicles call it engineering), the Wardens garrison the channel gates, the twin forts at its mouths, and the Vennerian colonies that secure its approaches: Mia Checkpoint on Mia island, Goishi on Lumina, New Venner and Johannstadt (ex-Taberis, taken 524 AGD) in Dissenbarg, Love of the Sea in Kutten, and the Vennerian Channel (Marti) and Vennerian Aelefer Channel sister cuts.

In 544 AGD the Wardens provided the marines for the invasion of Minir island — taking Neopao and Koln and reducing Dukedam to puppet — a reminder that toll-collectors can become conquerors when the toll is empire.

docs.title: Patron
docs.text:
The Vennerian Trade Republic Senate of Sea-Lords — plutocrats who own the toll. Wardens swear to the Channel itself as legal person: their oath is witnessed by a pour of seawater taken from the Channel's midpoint, kept in a stoppered vial until discharge. Ship chaplains of any faith may ride, but the Wardens' own ritual is accounting: the toll-book is read aloud each change of watch, and a warden who cannot balance it is relieved before he is rebuked.

Venner is slowly integrating the Corinite League and turning Dissenbarg cities into tributaries; where negotiations stall, the Wardens are the patient hint: the Channel can also close.

docs.title: Sigil
docs.text: A white ship's prow over black channel gates on a sea-blue field, the gates rendered as a Vennerian Ducat on its edge — prow obverse, gates reverse. Command pennants add a Silver Bride-silver thread at the hoist, because Venner claims the ring itself pays toll at night (a joke told only offshore).

docs.title: Role
docs.text:
Maritime chokepoint control, toll enforcement, and naval infantry. The Wardens field gate artillery, chain crews, boarding pikes, and the finest light marines on Ge'or for the specific business of taking a ship intact enough to tax it again. They do not seek open sea battle against the Anos Plutocracy's second-rate-but-still-dangerous fleet unless forced — they seek position: control of Mia means control of Lumina resupply, control of Goishi means sight over Beast's Bay, control of the gates means control of price.

Inland Venner factors quote prices in Erilia and convert to Ducats at predatory spreads; the Wardens ensure no captain evades the spread by running the channel under cover.

docs.title: Relation to Currencies & Regions
docs.text:
The Wardens are the living backing of the Vennerian Ducat — pale sea-gold dusted with Romanium, not valuable because it is scarce but because every hull between Erisdar and Dissenbarg must buy it to pass. The coin is Ducat-or-nothing at the gates; no Anosi Mark plate, no Meblean Pearl hoop, no Silver Talon will open them.

Consequently the busiest honest market on Ge'or is the exchange outside the gates where Anosi factors grudgingly buy Ducats from Vennerian money changers who will, hours later, grudgingly accept Anosi plates for Beast's Bay provisions — the whole Anos-Venner trade race rendered as queue. The Wardens also control Demon's Horn traders' access westward and take their Ducat there too.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Vennerian Channel Wardens ] ├── Region: South Erisdar — Vennerian Trade Republic; garrisons Vennerian Channel / Xeti Sea ↔ Beast's Bay ├── Patron: Vennerian Trade Republic Sea-Lords; oath to the Channel as legal person; Corinite League integration ├── Sigil: Ship prow over channel gates on sea-blue; Ducat edge device; silver thread for The Silver Bride ├── Backing: Vennerian Ducat (toll-backed + Romanium dust) — Ducat-only gates; colonies Mia, Goishi, New Venner, Johannstadt, Love of the Sea ├── Waterway: Vennerian Channel / Xeti Sea / Beast's Bay / Greater Ocean └── See Also: Vennerian Trade Republic, Anos Plutocracy, Anosi Mark, Sousu, Demon's Horn, Marti

The ancestral power base of the Kennensbach dynasty and the economic-military heartland of the Erisian Empire. Ruled by Hermes Kennensbach as Archduke of the Kennberg.

docs.title: 🐉 The Dragon Dynasty
docs.text: Only the ruling dynasty of Baoth was draconic. The king — Goldenborn — was a space-evolved dragon, a being whose species was born not on any planet but in the cold void between stars. The dragon dynasty maintained power through the Golden Pact: a legal-mystical framework that bound every citizen to the crown through blood oaths. The 99% non-dragon population lived, worked, and fought for a ruler who was not their own kind — a system that, remarkably, held for over five centuries.

docs.title: ⚔️ The Last War of Donblond'werv (967 BGD)
docs.text: Before Baoth's rise, the continent of Donblond'werv (later renamed Erisdar) was dominated by sprawling human empires. These empires, at the end of the Human Age, had become corrupt beyond repair — their institutions hollow, their leadership parasitic. Baoth, wielding draconic power and a coalition of species who had been subjugated under human rule, crushed them in the Last War. The human empires fell. Baoth rose. The continent was never again ruled purely by humans.

docs.title: 🔥 The Fall — The Demonic War and the Explosion
docs.text:
By the 5th century BGD, Hybrian Shadows had spent over two millennia infiltrating the institutions of Ge'or. Baoth — the most powerful state on the continent — was their prime target. They infiltrated the upper echelon with the goal of possessing Goldenborn himself.

Kirivis, the Demon King, discovered the plot. He launched the Demonic War — a 45-year campaign to reach Goldenborn and save him.

On the final day (421 BGD), Kirivis reached Goldenborn, but was betrayed by Rulfred — a Shadow posing as Baoth's greatest hero. Rulfred beheaded Kirivis and became king.

Kirivis's daughter Nethra received a modified Shadow device from the tree spirits of the Lyrical Forest. She infiltrated the castle through the sewers, confronted Rulfred, and activated the device. The explosion obliterated the entire kingdom. The crater filled with water, creating the Sea of Leviathan.

Rulfred survived. He took Goldenborn's corpse. The Hybrians unleashed the Leviathan to enforce quarantine on the ruins.

docs.title: 🌫️ The Aftermath
docs.text:
Baoth was never rebuilt. Its ruins sit on an island in the Sea of Leviathan. Three forces now guard what remains:

  • The Mystical Forest — the corrupted woodland ring, unclaimed by any nation
  • The Leviathan — Hybrian warden, unleashed after the explosion
  • Dragon Yaldabaoth — Rulfred wearing Goldenborn's corpse

docs.title: 🧝 Elvennrin
docs.text:
The cultural and spiritual heart of the restored elvish states. After the near-extinction of the Elves, Elvennrin was the first elven nation to re-establish sovereignty — building not on the ruins of Elvengar but on new ground in Central Erisdar. Home to the largest surviving concentration of elven population and the center of elven cultural revival.

Species: Elves Religion: Elven Faith — nature cults and elven gods. A repressed-but-accepted elfic country surrounded by fanatical Erisians, Elvennrin never abandoned its gods.

docs.title: Emperor Hermes Kennensbach
docs.text:
The current Emperor, Hermes Kennensbach, is widely regarded as intelligent and capable. He has:

  • Won several battles personally, establishing himself as a competent military leader.
  • Demonstrated strong economic sense — cutting taxes, reforming trade policies.
  • Attempted to centralize the Empire somewhat, pushing back against the centrifugal forces of countism.

Despite his competence, he is failing. The Empire cracks regardless of his efforts — as if the entire machine were running without oil, doomed to break no matter how skillfully it is maintained. Financial collapse looms. Institutional decay accelerates. His centralization efforts stall.

Character: - Not evil. Good-willed and genuinely wants to stabilize the Empire. - The Shadows attempted to co-opt him — it never worked. He does not know about the Shadows, but he is deeply suspicious of the Erisian Church. He has smelled that something is not right there. He has never said so publicly. - Irascible and very serious — not a warm man, but a fair one. - Willing to help take down the Church if provided with the truth about everything. - Has a wife, four daughters, and five sons. Maintains multiple affairs. - Getting old. His window for decisive action is closing.

docs.title: Church-State Relations
docs.text:
The Erisian Empire is considered "the sword of the Erisian Church." The relationship is symbiotic:

  • The Church spends enormous amounts of money in the Empire and maintains extensive institutions within its borders — cathedrals, monasteries, schools, courts.
  • The Empire provides military force, political legitimacy, and the physical enforcement of Church doctrine.
  • In theory, the Church and Empire are partners. In practice, the tension between secular and religious authority is constant — and Hermes's private suspicions make it more complicated than anyone realizes.

docs.title: Elves
docs.text:
The Empire has a history of irrational, intense hatred toward Elves. They were heavily persecuted for centuries — the Great Elvish Persecution of 137 AGD was only the most organized expression of a deeper cultural hostility. Elves were hunted, expelled, or killed on sight in many imperial territories.

Today, elves are legally permitted to live as citizens within the Empire. The laws have changed. But the culture has not. Elves are still seen with suspicion, treated with coldness, and viewed through narrowed eyes. They are tolerated, not welcomed.

Outside the Empire, in other Erisdarian nations, elves face disdain as well — but the Empire's particular history makes its prejudice uniquely intense.

docs.title: Demons
docs.text: Demons are not seen with the same suspicion as elves. They trade within the Empire and travel freely. The stigma of the name "demon" persists — they are still taught as the antagonists in old histories and church texts — but centuries of exposure have worn down the fear. People tolerate demons, even if they do not embrace them. The old stories say demons are evil. The demon merchant buying grain at the market says otherwise. Most imperials have learned to live with the contradiction.

docs.title: Other Species
docs.text: Dwarves, Catmen, Beast Races, and other species are generally accepted. Dwarvstadt, a county within the Empire, is majority-dwarven and fully integrated into imperial governance.

docs.title: Subdivisions
docs.text:
The Empire is divided into: - 3 Duchies: Kennberg, Prassen-Albridge, Mirenburg - 22 Counties (naming convention: -stadt) - 2 Free Cities: Kelensborgh, Tuvir - 1 Church State: Rroffran

The Archduchy of the Kennberg serves as the imperial heartland and the Emperor's personal domain.

docs.title: Modern Challenges
docs.text:
• Financial collapse — the Erilia currency faces severe strain as provinces operate with increasing autonomy.
  • Institutional decay — the crusades have died down; the Church can no longer enforce its will through pure military force.
  • Failing dogmas — laws like the polygamy ban are crumbling in peripheral territories.
  • Elvish resurgence — elven populations have stabilized; independent elvish states have re-entered the geopolitical arena.
  • The Emperor's age — Hermes Kennensbach will not rule forever, and the succession is uncertain.

docs.title: Erisian Theocracy
docs.text:
"The Pontificate governs. We judge."

The Erisian Theocracy is a religious state in Central Erisdar, distinct from the Pontificate of Eris which it considers too political and insufficiently doctrinaire. While the Pontificate is the theocratic administrative arm of the Erisian church, the Theocracy represents the church's zealot wing — a smaller, harsher territory governed directly by high clergy who reject secular compromise entirely.

Where the Pontificate negotiates with empires and collects tithes, the Theocracy issues decrees and burns heretics. Both answer to the same faith, but they despise each other's methods.

Species: Humans

docs.title: Loren
docs.text:
"Faith needs a gate. We are that gate."

Loren is a march-state on the eastern border of the Pontificate of Eris, positioned between the Pontificate's heartland and the secular territories of Central Erisdar.

docs.title: Religion
docs.text: Loren is majority Erisian — but it holds a huge Alegorian minority, one of the southernmost concentrations of the faith founded under Julian the Dragon Tamer. This makes it an anomaly: an Erisian-majority territory with a massive Alegorian presence, bordering the heart of the Erisian world. Tensions with the Pontificate are constant and theological, not merely political. Along with Northaxeland and Venkradian Republic, Loren's Alegorian minority forms part of the Alegorian bloc of northern and central Erisdar.

docs.title: Magna
docs.text:
"The maps exaggerate. But not by much."

Magna is the largest territorial state in Central Erisdar after the Erisian Empire itself — a sprawling confederation of semi-autonomous counties bound together by shared dwarven ancestry and a mutual distrust of imperial centralization. Unlike Dwarvengor in the east, which is predominantly subterranean, Magna is a surface-dwelling dwarven nation, its cities built into hills and low mountains rather than deep beneath them. This surface orientation has made Magna more diplomatically engaged than its eastern cousin, and considerably wealthier from overland trade.

Governance follows the old dwarven council model: each county sends a representative to the Magna Assembly, which convenes in the Hall of Echoes — a circular chamber carved from a single granite monolith. Decisions require consensus, which in practice means that nothing happens quickly. Magna's political paralysis is legendary; its ability to nonetheless remain prosperous is a source of bewilderment to neighboring states with more efficient governments.

Magna's relationship with the Erisian Empire is cordial but guarded. The Empire recognizes Magna's autonomy; Magna returns the favor by not funding separatist movements in imperial dwarven territories. The arrangement has held for over two hundred years. Relations with Baoth — or rather, the Ruins of Baoth and the Archive of the Traveler — are more complicated: Magna's elders maintain that certain truths buried in the Archive were placed there by dwarven hands during the Dwarf Era, and that Magna holds a ancestral claim to their custody.

Magna is a major nation in Central Erisdar, appearing prominently on multiple maps.

A region within the Erisian Empire. In ancient times the great mountain Metrak stood here — a mountain that was never a mountain, but a city-sized war-machine of the The Last Great War. docs.title: Sperdia
docs.text:
"Between the throne and the altar, someone has to keep the granaries full."

A modest agrarian principality in Central Erisdar, Sperdia occupies the fertile lowlands between the Erisian Empire and the Pontificate of Eris. It has survived not through military might — its army is small, its fortifications aging — but through the quiet indispensability of its harvests. When the Empire and the Pontificate quarrel, both sides still need Sperdian grain, and neither can afford to see those fields burned by the other.

Sperdia is governed by a prince from the Luscan family, a minor noble line that has held the title for eleven generations. The Luscans have perfected a political art that larger powers dismiss as weakness: the strategic neutrality of the essential supplier. Sperdia pays modest tribute to the Erisian church and token fealty to the Imperial crown, but its true allegiance is to the soil. Its population is predominantly human, with a small but established elven minority descended from refugees who fled the destruction of Elvengar in Year 0 — The Great Divergence.

The principality's one point of tension is its proximity to Loren, with which it shares a contested river-border. Water rights on the River Luss have sparked three minor conflicts in the last century — none escalating beyond skirmishes, thanks largely to Sperdian reluctance to fight and Lorenese reluctance to lose access to Sperdian grain markets.

Sperdia is a nation in Central Erisdar. Religion: Erisian.

Species: Humans, Elves

docs.title: Termopolas
docs.text: A heavily xenophobic empire of the Human Age in the region that is now the Erisian Empire. Termopolas would exterminate catmen — a persecution that bred the Lesser Catmen, as starving catmen were changed forever by the ordeal.

docs.title: The Metrak Fall
docs.text: In ~1645 BGD, under Emperor Atanides "the Archaeologer," Termopolas mounted a thousand-man excavation of the mountain-dungeon Metrak. The machine woke, killed Atanides, and laid waste to the land up to the frontier of the now-Grimmel Republic, leaving no city behind. The empire, blameless in its own telling, branded Masaaki Sytrenis's party criminals — but the Tunwif kingdom, Aelefer, and Lima protected them, and the leaderless empire lost war after war even while outnumbering its foes three to one. Sytrenis's diplomacy ended the conflict and the persecution.

docs.title: Crab Union
docs.text: An independent island kingdom in the Crab Archipelago — like the Pacific islands of Old Earth, part of no continent. Sister realm to the United Kingdom of the Seamen (South Crab).

docs.title: People — Seamen and Humans
docs.text:
Seamen is a race. Although their name suggests they live in the sea, they are a land species. They are terrestrial islanders, superb sailors despite living on land — the name is a historical misnomer from early Erisdarian explorers.

  • The Crab Union is a majority human region that follows Krowretism — the Church of Krowretism (demon Eris, purification, absolute freedom).
  • But they also have Seamen among their population — a significant Seamen minority alongside the human Krowretist majority.
  • The twin archipelago to the southeast — South Crab Archipelago — also hosts Seamen, Humans, Catmen, and Demons in the United Kingdom of the Seamen.

The Crab Union's Krowretists share the Human Republic's frontier-freedom ethos, stretched across the sea.

docs.title: Imperial Politics
docs.text: The Asatru Empire's political structure is defined by tension between the emperor and the imperial court. The court is composed of powerful noble families, military commanders, and merchant guilds — each with their own interests. The emperor holds real authority but cannot act unilaterally. Every major decision is a negotiation.

docs.title: Colonial Ambitions
docs.text:
Asatru maintains a modest but meaningful colonial and influence network:

  • Asatru Knight's Thorn — a peninsula in West Erisdar treated as integral imperial territory, more than a colony. It is the Demon Continent's permanent foothold on Erisdar.
  • Kutten — Asatru contributed heavily to the resettlement of Kutten after the Kutten Catastrophe destroyed Elvengar. The empire retains significant influence on the desert continent.
  • Western Erisdar — Asatru holds considerable soft power across the region, built on centuries of trade, diplomacy, and the lingering memory of the old empire's reach.

docs.title: Role on the Demon Continent
docs.text:
The Asatru Empire is seen — by itself and by others — as the representative of the entire Demon Continent to the rest of Ge'or. When foreign powers negotiate with demon-kind, they negotiate with Asatru. This is not always accurate, but it is almost always true in practice.

Other demon nations — Maomodor Kingdom, Koebi Tribe, Cubra Tribe — have their own foreign policies. But Asatru's size, history, and prestige make it the default voice of demonic civilization.

docs.title: Species
docs.text:
• Primary: Demons — Xiobita subrace (imperial line), Bjor subrace (Kirivis's line), and others
  • Minorities: All species trade and travel freely within Asatru territory. The Demon Continent's culture of coexistence extends fully to the empire.

docs.text: The Malgardian Tribe is the origin of the name Malgardian and follows Malgardism majority — a canonical sect of Kirivs-bin that honors the warrior way. As the defining tribe, its customs set the template for all Malgardian faith.

docs.title: Maomodor Kingdom
docs.text: A kingdom on the Demon Continent located below the Kutra Tribe and southwest of Blazeyard. The Maomodor are of the main demon race — like the Asatru Empire — but many other races live within their lands. The Demon Continent sees relatively little inter-species conflict; its inhabitants view themselves with a shared "demonic" nationality, and populations of every type can be found walking freely everywhere.

docs.title: Faith
docs.text: Maomodor Kingdom hosts several faiths but is majority Kirivs-bin — the demonic majority sustains the Way of Kirivis as state spirituality.

docs.text: A tribe on the Demon Continent west of the Malgardian Tribe. The Titians are a subrace of Malgardians, even smaller in stature. In demonic cultures, they are considered miko — sacred beings treated with high respect and reverence.

docs.title: Faith
docs.text: The Tita are diminutive Malgardians revered as priests of Kirivs-bin; their pure, innocent appearance makes them preferred clergy. They follow Malgardism within the Kirivs-bin canon.

docs.title: Yaoma Tribe
docs.text: A tribe on the Demon Continent located south of Zakarutia and east of Xobkua. The Yaoma inhabit two islands and are a mermaid-like civilization.

docs.title: Faith
docs.text: Yaoma Tribe (species Marmots) follows Oceanism — ocean creatures are perfect beings in harmony with Ge'or, the oceans stretching calmly around the world.

docs.title: Current Situation (597 AGD)
docs.text:
• The old Queen still reigns. She is religious, stubborn, and patient.
  • The fleet is nearly ready.
  • Asatru and other regional powers prefer not to intervene — this is a snake-sister affair, and the Demon Continent does not involve itself in family disputes.
  • Augamouth, however, supports Xikxia — providing what aid it can to the rebel sister-queen.

docs.title: Faith
docs.text: Zakarutia is the main ally of Xobkua and follows the Gedarism alliance — centuries united against Asatru Empire dominance, under goddess Miritha.

docs.title: Xobkua
docs.text: A nation on a massive island off the southwest coast of the Demon Continent, southwest of Zakarutia. The island is roughly one-quarter the size of the Demon Continent itself — so large it is considered a continuation of the continent. Xobkua is inhabited by Giants, a humanoid species standing three meters tall.

docs.title: Faith
docs.text: Xobkua follows Gedarism — anti-Kirivs-bin and chief antagonist of the Asatru Empire on the Demon Continent. A cold war, sometimes open war, persists for regional dominance. The prophet Gedar (4000 years ago) declared all Xobkua land as theirs, gift of goddess Miritha of fortune. Zakarutia is Xobkua's centuries-old ally against Asatru dominance.

docs.title: Estran
docs.text: A nation on the island east of the Asatru Empire mainland, located below the Mountain Tribe. Estran is inhabited by High Catmen, a subrace of Catmen with a Mediterranean appearance — typically black-haired and more masculine in build. Like all catmen, they are humanoid with feline features.

docs.title: Faith
docs.text: Estran catmen follow Kludosy — the western-catmen creed that catmen of the Demon Continent are western catmen destined to take the west. Estran are warriors and diplomats who trace their lineage to a family that left Central Erisdar after persecution in the Human Era to seek glory; mutable catmen genes rapidly created the Mediterranean High-Catmen phenotype. Human–catmen offspring are 90% catmen, creating a taboo on such unions.

docs.text: A kingdom on small islands south of Yakut and east of the Yaoma-controlled territory, across a narrow sea. The Glub Kingdom is composed of intelligent Slimes — a rare variant of an otherwise mostly irrational species. These slimes possess enough intellect for diplomacy and governance, sustaining a functioning kingdom.

docs.title: Faith
docs.text: The Glub Kingdom of Slimes follows Slimism, a Kirivs-bin sect demanding equality with all beings on earth, regional recognition, and contribution to the demonic cause.

docs.text: A nation on the island east of the Asatru Empire mainland, right of the Asatru-controlled territory. The Mountain Tribe is composed of Diablos — winged humanoids who follow a nocturnal civilization, sleeping during daylight and working through the night.

docs.title: Faith
docs.text: Mountain Tribe follows Demonism, an ecumenical Kirivs-bin sect that teaches all demons are one race and all demon religions are one — abandon differences to endure the world's harshness.

docs.text: A nation in Dissenbarg. A theocratic state governed by a council of star-reading mystics, isolated from Dissenbarg's secular trade networks. Aeon follows Helism — its patron is Gaelen, the goddess of construction.

docs.title: 🏘️ Citrea
docs.text:
A nation in Dissenbarg. A coastal merchant enclave whose harbors serve as the primary Dissenbarg port for trade with Meble and the southern routes. Citrea follows Helism — its patron is Lobas, the god of nature.

Citrea is a member of the Corinite League, recorded as "Kizita" on the 597 AGD world map.

docs.title: 🗳️ Cletas Democracy
docs.text:
A democratic state in Dissenbarg and one of the few territories where common citizens vote for their leaders. The Cletas Democracy's system is imperfect — property requirements limit the franchise — but it represents a genuine alternative to autocracy.

The Democracy is named for Cletas, the god of reason — its patron in the Helism pantheon. Its history carries a wound from the The Taberis War: when the rival power Taberis pressed it, the Democracy called on Venner for aid — and Venner's "rescue" ended with Venner taking Taberis for itself (524 AGD), renaming it Johannstadt. The Democracy has never forgotten the cost.

docs.title: ⚓ Corin
docs.text:
"The League sails. Corin decides where."

Corin is a city-state in Dissenbarg and the senior partner of the Corinite League, the maritime trade coalition that controls the southern arc of the Silver Coast. While the League operates as a confederation of port-cities, Corin is first among equals — its harbor is the deepest, its merchant fleet the largest, and its ruling Merchant Council the body to which other League members defer in matters of collective policy.

The city's architecture reflects its maritime obsession: Corin's streets are canals rather than roads, its temples face the sea rather than the sky, and its civic calendar is governed by the shipping seasons. The Council is elected by ship-captains rather than landowners — a peculiarity that has produced a government more competent at navigation than legislation, but surprisingly effective at keeping trade flowing. Corin's mage-cell lineages trend toward water-affinity expressions, a biological inheritance that its ruling families have carefully preserved through strategic marriages.

The city's patron is Corin, goddess of sea and commerce in the Helism pantheon — the city-state bears her name, and its sea-facing temples are raised to her.

docs.title: ⚔️ Enkrad Order
docs.text:
"Order through strength. Strength through unity."

The Enkrad Order is an Erisian Church colony in Dissenbarg — the only Erisian nation on the continent. Its colonists arrived 370 years ago (~227 AGD — see Founding of the Enkrad Order), settling Dissenbarg's eastern reach with the support of the Vennerian Trade Republic and its colonial and commercial empire. The Order holds the Erisian faith in a sea of pagans.

docs.title: Map Position
docs.text: Recorded on the 597 AGD political map as "ENKRAD ORDER" — a slate-gray military order-state drawn on mountainous terrain, sitting between two large Goblin territories. New Venner lies to the south, and the Dissenbarg Sea borders its coast.

docs.title: Defense
docs.text: The Order is surrounded by goblins — to the east and to the west. It protects its borders vigilantly and controls those areas of Dissenbarg: a fortified Erisian island among hostile monster realms.

docs.title: Government
docs.text: As an Order-State, the Order operates under a military-council structure, with ranks earned through proven combat ability rather than birth — fitting for a colony that must hold its ground against goblin raids.

docs.title: Religion
docs.text: The Order believes in Eris — it is the Erisian Church's colony in Dissenbarg, sustained by Venner's colonial and commercial empire.

docs.title: Erilian Federation

docs.title: Origins — Erilio & the Crusade of 278 AGD
docs.text: The Federation was founded by the hero Erilio — a general born in Kennberg. He led the Crusade of 278 AGD, the last attempt of the Erisian church to expand into East Erisdar, and took over half the land of the tribes of Mann. The tribes rebelled under Kosbaldo, forming the Mann Order dictatorship, and waged a guerrilla war — modernizing the parts of Mann territory outside the Federation's control.

docs.title: 👁️ Fendigar Dictatorship
docs.text:
A rigidly controlled state in East Erisdar ruled by a single autocrat in the Fendilger lineage. Unlike the republican experiments elsewhere, Fendilger maintained its dictatorial structure through the Era of Cracking Walls — largely by avoiding imperial entanglements and suppressing internal dissent with brutal efficiency.

An atheist, xenophobic kingdom. Traumatized by what happened with Erislod due to Pontus, Fendigar completely closed itself off from society and abandoned its gods. It is autarkian — self-sufficient, sealed, and unwilling to let anyone enter its lands.
