docs.title: Silver Republic
docs.text:
"Silver in the earth, silver in the hands, silver in the vote."

The Silver Republic is a mercantile republic in East Erisdar, named for the rich argentite veins that run beneath its coastal territory and the shimmering the Silver Coast upon which its ports are built. Unlike the guild-based governance of the Limese League or the wealth-threshold system of the Anos Plutocracy, the Silver Republic operates on a property-franchise model: citizenship — and the right to vote for the republic's Council of Eighty — is tied to land ownership, creating a government of propertied interests that styles itself a democracy while excluding the landless majority.

The Republic's wealth flows from two sources: silver mining and shipbuilding. Its dockyards produce the fastest vessels on the eastern seaboard, and its silver coinage — the Argent Mark — circulates as far west as Central Erisdar. During the Era of Cracking Walls, the Republic profited handsomely by financing both sides of several imperial succession disputes, a practice it has never seen reason to discontinue.

Relations with the Spasian Teocracy are strained by proximity and philosophy — the Republic's secular, transactional culture finds the Teocracy's mysticism baffling, while the Teocracy views the Republic's banking houses as temples to greed. With the Erilian Federation, relations are more practical: the Federation buys Republic ships, the Republic buys Federation timber, and neither asks uncomfortable questions about the Federation's occupation zone.

Religion: Pitraism — the faithful believe the gods love money and gold. The Republic is a direct partner and great ally of Dwarvengor, and dwarven religion was the direct inspiration for Pitraism — its pantheon of dozens of gods is mostly borrowed from the dwarves, just as the Romans inspired themselves on the Greeks. The faith's name comes from Pitra, a legendary figure "blessed" by the gods after he became rich, who supposedly lived for hundreds of years.

The Silver Republic is a nation in East Erisdar, near the the Silver Coast.

Species: Humans, Elves

docs.title: Spasian Teocracy
docs.text:
"The Prophet saw the Silver Light. We carry it forward."

The Spasian Teocracy is a religious state in East Erisdar founded around the teachings of the Prophet Spasius, a figure who emerged during the chaos of the Lost Era claiming to have received visions from the Silver Bride — the planetary ring that encircles Ge'or. Unlike the Erisian church, which venerates Eris as a divine figure, the Spasian faith holds that divinity resides in the ring itself, and that the ring's light is a direct conduit to the creator. The Pontificate considers Spasian doctrine heretical; the Spasian clergy consider the Erisians spiritually blind.

Governance is exercised by the Council of Illuminants, a body of twenty-one high priests who interpret the Prophet's writings — collectively known as the Argent Codex — and issue decrees with the force of law. The Council selects its own members from the priestly caste, creating a self-perpetuating theological oligarchy. Public life in Spasia is structured around the Ring-Cycle, a liturgical calendar tied to the phases of the Silver Bride, with major civic decisions deferred to astrologically favorable conjunctions.

The Teocracy maintains tense but non-belligerent relations with the neighboring Silver Republic — the two nations share a coast and a name but little else, the Republic viewing Spasian mysticism as an anachronism and Spasia viewing Republican secularism as a spiritual vacancy. With the Fractured State of Erislod to the north, relations are simpler: the Teocracy sends missionaries, and the fractured villages send them back.

docs.title: The Invasion of 558 AGD
docs.text:
In 558 AGD, the Erilian Federation invaded the Spasian Teocracy and reduced it to a super small land. The Teocracy survives as a tolerated remnant — the Erisian church allows it to exist, and it remains the only country with Spasian as an official religion.

The Spasian Teocracy is a religious state in East Erisdar.

docs.title: Xi
docs.text:
The dragon kingdom of the east. Rival to Klobiendar. Destroyed by its own leader's sacrifice.

Xi was the dragon kingdom of eastern Erisdar, the eternal rival of Klobiendar in the west. The two empires fought The Draconic War — fifty years of slaughter that consumed billions of lives.

docs.title: The War
docs.text: Xi and Klobiendar had been rivals for centuries. When the war turned total, millions of soldiers — dragon against dragon — clashed across Erisdar. The scale was apocalyptic.

docs.title: Melberior's Sacrifice
docs.text: In the final act, Xi's leader Melberior launched a suicide spell that destroyed Klobiendar's capital at Dragonreach. Melberior died in the casting. The magic reverberated across the land, creating the Lyrical Forest.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text: Xi fell shortly after. Its leader was dead. Its armies were spent. The kingdom dissolved into history, leaving behind only the Sword of Xi — a blade that would later be gifted to Julian the Dragon Tamer by Fireborn.

docs.title: Karabar
docs.text: A nation on Karabar Island, located north of the Crab Archipelago and south of Moon Wolf Island in the western Wolf Ocean.

docs.title: Faith — Dresludo
docs.text:
Karabar believes in Dresludo — god of the seas.

They believe Dresludo sent them to the island of Karabar as a penitence for their sins — and that they need to achieve a gnosis state to be able to be freed from the suffering of earth.

Dresludo is the sea itself — vast, indifferent, and just. Karabar is his purgatory. Daily seawater rites and silent meditation facing the Wolf Ocean are the path to gnosis.

docs.title: The Molten Archipelago — Moral Grey Zone
docs.text:
To the north lies the Moonfang Dominion — a death cult that sacrifices its own children to the Wolf God Cleton. Karabar presents itself as a refuge. It operates refugee bases on the eastern edge of the Molten Archipelago, the first landmass Moonfang escapees reach after crossing the frozen sea.

The truth is uglier. Escapees who reach the bases are not freed — they are put to forced labor for wages that barely sustain them. The cult takes their souls. Karabar takes their bodies. To the outside world, Karabar frames this as mercy — they took them in, after all. Better than being fed to a god.

Whether Karabar's ruling class is complicit in this arrangement or merely indifferent is unclear. The result is the same. The Molten Archipelago is not a sanctuary. It is a halfway house between two kinds of death.

docs.title: Coalsteel Kingdom
docs.text: A dwarf nation on the southeastern corner of Kobre Continent, extending into the central region. The Coalsteel dwarves have been locked in a millennia-old rivalry with the Elf Kingdom to their west — a feud born from the continent's extreme isolation. With no external threats or allies for thousands of years, the two species turned on each other.

docs.title: Diamonds Kingdom
docs.text: A dwarf kingdom on the western tip of a peninsula on Kobre Continent, located west of the Homunculi Kingdom. The Diamonds dwarves have constructed a massive wall across the peninsula's neck — their only defense against relentless homunculi attacks. Unlike Coalsteel to the east, Diamonds Kingdom's primary enemy is the homunculi, not the elves.

docs.title: Elf Kingdom
docs.text: An elven kingdom on Kobre Continent, located west of the Coalsteel Kingdom. The elves of Kobre have warred with the dwarves of Coalsteel for millennia — their isolation on this remote continent leaving only each other as rivals. Unlike the scattered elven diaspora elsewhere on Ge'or, the Kobre elves maintained a continuous, unbroken kingdom.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: Kobre Continent
  • East: Coalsteel Kingdom
  • North: Homunculi Kingdom
  • Species: Elves

docs.title: History of Conflict
docs.text:
For centuries after their liberation, the homunculi were warmongers. They waged constant war against:

  • Coalsteel Kingdom — the dwarves to their south.
  • Diamonds Kingdom — the dwarves to their west, who built a massive wall specifically against them.
  • Elf Kingdom — the elves further west, caught in the crossfire.

The wars were not ideological. The homunculi were desperate, hungry, and had no idea how to exist in a world that did not want them. They fought because fighting was the only thing they knew how to do.

docs.title: Stabilization
docs.text:
In recent generations, the Homunculi Kingdom has stabilized. They have:

  • Food — they grow crops now, rather than raiding for sustenance.
  • Coherent society — governance, law, tradition.
  • Diplomacy — tentative, fragile, but real.

They are no longer the berserkers their ancestors were. They are a nation.

docs.title: Trust Issues
docs.text:
Despite their stabilization, the homunculi have deep trust issues with the neighboring kingdoms. Their religious doctrine — that their god abandoned them — extends to foreign policy. They believe the other species of Kobre see them as monsters and would happily see them destroyed.

They are not entirely wrong. The elves and dwarves of Kobre have fought them for centuries. Homunculi are banned from entering the Coalsteel Kingdom, Diamonds Kingdom, and Elf Kingdom. The ban is mutual — the homunculi do not welcome outsiders either.

docs.title: Daily Life
docs.text:
For all their traumatic history, daily life in the Homunculi Kingdom is unremarkable:

  • Agriculture — they grow crops adapted to Kobre's harsh soil.
  • Training — every homunculus trains in combat from youth. They never forgot how to fight, even if they chose to stop.
  • Community — homunculi society is intensely communal. No one eats alone. No one mourns alone. They are all that each other has.

The centuries have worn the sharp edges off their story. The liberation, the Unnamed, the wars — these are still told, but they are becoming legend. The younger generation grows up in a kingdom that has food, laws, and a fragile peace. They wonder if the old stories are even true.

docs.title: History
docs.text: The Hybrians attempted a takeover of Kobre due to its isolation, deploying Homunculi as agents. When Baoth was destroyed, the psychic link shattered and the homunculi awoke free.

docs.title: 🌫️ The Aftermath
docs.text:
Elvengar's destruction had permanent consequences:

  • Elven populations were decimated. The survivors became a scattered, traumatized people.
  • The geopolitical vacuum left by Elvengar's fall contributed to the rise of human empires during later ages, and eventually to the Erisian church's dominance.
  • The Great Elvish Persecution would follow centuries later, as the Church sought to finish what the Divergence started.
  • Some elven refugees fled to the continent of Merratodoni, establishing the empire of Luzia and the homeland of Maemon.

docs.text:

docs.title: Marko
docs.text:
"Come as you are. Trade as you will. Leave richer than you arrived." — Inscription over Marko's central market gate

An international trade hub and semi-republic on Kutten, unique among the nations of Ge'or. Marko is not a kingdom, not a tribe, not a colony — it is a merchant city-state governed by elected High Catmen rulers, where every species trades freely and no one asks where you came from.

Marko is the most prominent settlement on Kutten — the desert continent's gateway to the world.

docs.title: Founding
docs.text:
After the fall of Elvengar and the Kutten Catastrophe that desertified the continent, Kutten was abandoned for a century. When the toxic rains ceased and the air cleared, two groups saw opportunity in the wasteland:

  • Erisdarians — settlers from the Erisian Empire and the southern trade republics, hoping to claim abandoned elven lands.
  • Demon Continent settlers — colonists from Asatru and other demon nations, seeking new territory across the sea.

Neither group could dominate the other. Instead of fighting, they traded. The settlement that became Marko was organized in 322 AGD — a formal recognition of what had already become the de facto arrangement: a neutral ground where Erisdarian and demonic interests could meet and profit.

The High Catmen of Estran saw the opportunity before anyone else. Their merchant families moved in, established trade networks, and — through commerce, diplomacy, and sheer competence — rose to become Marko's ruling class. They have held that position ever since.

docs.title: Government
docs.text:
Marko is a semi-republic. High Catmen are elected as rulers by a council of merchant families and guild representatives. The system is not democratic in the universal sense — voting power correlates with economic stake — but it is more open than any monarchy on Ge'or.

The elected High Catmen rulers serve fixed terms. Their primary responsibility is maintaining Marko's neutrality and ensuring that commerce flows uninterrupted. War is bad for business. Marko has never started one.

docs.title: Trade
docs.text:
Marko is the commercial hub of Kutten. Its trade networks span the known world:

  • Demon Continent — direct trade with Asatru, Maomodor Kingdom, Koebi Tribe, and others.
  • Yak Island — strong ties with Estran (the High Catmen homeland), Yakut, and Cubra Tribe.
  • West Erisdar — Demon's Horn, Augamouth, Xikxia, and Astravayne all trade through Marko.
  • Venner — a major trade partner. Vennerian ships are a common sight in Marko's harbors.

Marko charges no tariffs on goods passing through its markets. It profits instead from banking, warehousing, and the services that naturally accumulate around a neutral trade hub.

docs.title: Foreign Relations
docs.text:
• Estran — the closest ally. The High Catmen of Estran are Marko's ruling class; the two nations are effectively sister-states.
  • Venner — strong trade partnership. Venner values Marko as a neutral port.
  • Yakut — across the sea. Cordial trade relations.
  • Oda — orc kingdom to the northeast. Neutral but stable.
  • Malbodor — the Sandsmen kingdom. Limited interaction — Malbodor is insular.
  • New Elvengar — the elven restoration kingdom. Minimal contact.

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Marko is the most cosmopolitan city on Kutten — perhaps in the region. Its streets host:

  • High Catmen — the ruling merchant class.
  • Humans — Erisdarian traders, settlers, and bankers.
  • Demons — merchants and diplomats from the Demon Continent.
  • Orcs — traders from Augamouth, soldiers-for-hire.
  • Lesser Catmen — everywhere, as always, universally welcome.
  • Snake People — careful not to take sides in the sister-queen feud.
  • Sandsmen — rare, but the occasional desert guide or mineral trader.

No species is turned away. No feud is imported. Marko's neutrality is absolute — and enforced by the simple fact that anyone who breaks it loses access to the most valuable market on Kutten.

docs.title: Religion
docs.text: Marko is the stronghold of Calism — the catmen philosophy-faith. Calism preaches pacifism, docility, and gentleness, seeking only to greaten oneself; it is ecumenical without holding all religions true. Marko's High Catmen rulers embody the faith's practical edge: gentle in trade, but strict — even cruel — toward anything self-destructive. The humans and other species of Marko keep Calism's firmer discipline; the catmen themselves live it lightly, playful and aloof, though they still find self-destructive behavior strange.

docs.text: A kingdom on the Lumina Continent southeast of Vennerian Goishi and the Lumina Kingdom. Cammao is a hub of demonfolk and Eastern Beastmen — and one of the engines of Lumina's economy, moving trade together with the Vennerians and Anos.

docs.title: The Demon Refugees
docs.text: The majority of the demons of Cammao are Erisian church members — refugees. Demons from the Demon Continent do not accept other demons converting to human religions, so those who follow Eris fled across the sea to Lumina, where Cammao's ports took them in. Their faith is why they came; their trade keeps the kingdom rich.

docs.title: Claim to Lumina
docs.text: Gigas considers itself the legitimate ruler of the entire Lumina Continent. Any Lumina nation that refuses to acknowledge this claim risks conflict. The Gigas do not need to conquer their neighbors to enforce their primacy — they simply need to be feared enough that no one challenges it openly.

docs.title: Exception — Erisdarians
docs.text: Gigas has one iron law of foreign policy: never antagonize the Erisdarians. The Erisian Empire, Vennerian Trade Republic, and Anos Plutocracy control the commerce that flows through Lumina. Attacking Erisdarian shipping or outposts would invite economic and military retaliation that even the Gigas cannot afford. Erisdarian traders operate freely in Gigas territory — a pragmatic carve-out in an otherwise belligerent foreign policy.

docs.title: Neighbors
docs.text:
• Lake Kingdom — tense. The Lesser Catmen are too beloved globally to attack directly, but Gigas does not recognize their independence.
  • Cammao Kingdom — neutral. The Eastern Beastmen traders are useful.
  • Lumina Republic — hostile. Human settlers are not welcome on Lumina.
  • Maoma Tribe — subjugated in practice. The Maoma do not openly challenge Gigas supremacy.

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
• Warrior culture — combat prowess determines social standing. The strongest beastmen lead warbands; the weak serve.
  • Priestly caste — a small elite of warrior-priests who interpret the dog-god's telepathic will. They are the only ones permitted direct contact with the god.
  • Catmen minority — tolerated but never trusted. Lesser Catmen are, of course, exempt from Gigas aggression — as they are everywhere.
  • Warmongering but not suicidal — Gigas knows its limits. It does not attack Erisdarian interests, and it does not provoke powers it cannot defeat.

docs.title: Power Ranking
docs.text: Gigas is ranked S-tier — a continental hegemon with military power that rivals the great empires, constrained only by its isolation from the global trade networks controlled by the SS-tier powers.

docs.title: Lumina Kingdom
docs.text:
"The old empire's bones are everywhere. We sit on its heart." — King Gustal, on the throne of the Lumina Kingdom

A kingdom on the Lumina Continent, built on the ruins of the ancient Lumina Empire — a once-great empire of the beastmen, and the greatest power the continent has ever known. The current kingdom occupies the site of the old imperial capital, carries its name, and dreams of reclaiming its legacy.

docs.title: Rise (1729 BGD — Golden Age)
docs.text:
From approximately 1729 BGD to 1134 BGD, the Lumina Empire dominated the continent. At its height, it controlled:

  • 70% of the Lumina continent
  • Cattos island
  • Large portions of the Tuba Continent

It was a civilization of architects, scholars, and warriors — built and ruled by a civilized, intelligent beastmen people, the first true empire to unify the disparate tribes and species of ancient Lumina. In those days the beastmen were as capable of empire as any race of humans: its founding emperor, Kaelor I, was a beastman. Its cities were marvels. Its roads still run beneath the jungle. Its statues — weathered but standing — can be found across the continent, half-consumed by forest.

docs.title: The Shadows Within
docs.text: The Shadows had been inside the Empire since its founding. Every institution, every ministry, every military command — seeded with homunculi, guided by Hybrian agents. They did not want the Empire to rule. They wanted it to fall. This was Phase One of the Shadow plan: Infiltration — seed the institutions, wait, and when the moment is right, make them fall. The Lumina Empire was their first great test.

docs.title: The Fall — Luminous XII
docs.text:
The empire's collapse began with its greatest king.

Luminous XII, called "the Architect," was a legendary beastman ruler — builder of cities, conqueror of lands. Brilliant, visionary, and utterly blind to the rot within. In a campaign on Tuba, the Shadows engineered a war with the Goblin King. A conflict that should have been a trivial border skirmish became a catastrophic defeat through sabotage, corrupted intelligence, and whispered advice in the right ears.

Luminous XII lost the battle. The defeat was not merely military: his brother Hoelio died in the fighting.

Luminous XII returned to the capital shattered. He had no heirs. He had no will to continue. Consumed by shame, he took his own life.

The year was 1134 BGD. The empire died with him. The Pax Lumina — six centuries of stability — ended in fire and blood.

docs.title: The Collapse
docs.text:
Without Luminous XII's legitimacy, the succession collapsed. Rival claimants tore the empire apart from within. The centralized state that had held the continent together for six centuries dissolved in a generation.

And then the beastmen — the empire's own people — broke.

The fall destroyed their pride. Slowly, over generations, the civilized beastmen of Lumina returned to savagery: the roads untraveled, the cities abandoned, the writing forgotten. In the chaos, beastmen kin from Marti Continent crossed the sea and joined the splintering tribes — but no invading power finished the empire. The beastmen simply forgot what they had been.

The civilization that had produced Luminous XII's statues crumbled back into jungle and memory.

For over a thousand years, Lumina was a continent of ruins.

docs.title: Beastmen — Post-Collapse
docs.text:
The beastmen of Lumina today — the Gigas Tribe, the Maoma Tribe, the scattered warbands — are the descendants of the empire that collapsed. They are fierce, tribal, and honor-driven. Physical strength is the measure of worth. Raiding and inter-tribal warfare are the norm. Their culture resembles the beast races of ancient legend: warriors first, everything else second — a far cry from what their ancestors were.

Historically, people know it: the beastmen of old were more civilized and intelligent, and they built empires as readily as any race of humans. Some say the fall of the empire destroyed their pride and made them humble. The old Lumina Empire's ruins are everywhere — and the beastmen walk past them, only half-remembering that those stones were their own making.

docs.title: Religion — Lumism
docs.text: The Lumina Kingdom follows Lumism — the imperial cult of the old Lumina Empire's figures, blended with animism and a reverence for the jungle animals. Its believers hold that the kingdom must return the Lumina Empire and bring back the old ways of the beastmen — restoration is not ambition among the devout, it is duty. For all that, the kingdom remains highly tribal and decentralized, with a slow, genuine push toward modernization.

docs.title: The Current Lumina Kingdom
docs.text: The modern Lumina Kingdom occupies the same location as the old imperial capital. It inherits the name — and the ambition.

docs.title: King Gustal
docs.text: The current ruler, King Gustal, is a human monarch who claims descent from the scattered imperial bloodline. His claim is disputed by scholars but accepted by his subjects. Gustal is no Luminous XII — he is not an architect or a conqueror. But he is ambitious.

docs.title: Ambitions
docs.text: The Lumina Kingdom intends to retake lost lands and eventually reform the Lumina Empire. This is not secret. Gustal speaks of it openly. The other powers of Lumina — especially Gigas — listen carefully.

docs.title: Military
docs.text: Lumina Kingdom is strong enough to rival Gigas. It is not yet strong enough to defeat them. The balance of power on the continent is fragile: two powers, each claiming to be the rightful heir to continental dominance, watching each other across the jungle.

docs.title: The Ruins
docs.text:
Across the Lumina continent, the old empire's remains are visible:

  • Weathered statues of forgotten kings, carved from white stone now stained green by moss.
  • Broken aqueducts that once carried water to cities of a hundred thousand.
  • Road foundations, perfectly straight, now buried under centuries of topsoil.
  • Imperial inscriptions in a script that modern Lumina scholars can barely read.

The past is everywhere. The present is still catching up.

docs.title: Shadow Connection
docs.text:
See also: Shadows, Hybrians, Audio Chapter 5 — The Old Lumina Empire

The fall of the Old Lumina Empire was not merely political decay. It was the Shadows' first documented large-scale operation — proof that infiltration at institutional scale could topple even a six-century superpower. The pattern established here — seed agents, wait generations, engineer a crisis, let the collapse look natural — would be refined and repeated across Ge'or for millennia.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Lumina Kingdom ] ├── Ruler: King Gustal ├── Government: Monarchy ├── Occupies: Site of the old Lumina Empire capital ├── Legacy: Namesake of the ancient beastmen Lumina Empire (1729–1134 BGD) ├── Old Empire: Built and ruled by the beastmen — controlled 70% of Lumina, Cattos island, parts of Tuba ├── Founder: Emperor Kaelor I — a beastman (1729 BGD) ├── Fall: Luminous XII's suicide (1134 BGD) — engineered by Shadows, shame over Goblin King defeat, brother Hoelio's death ├── Collapse: Succession crisis → beastmen devolve into tribalism, forgetting their old ways ├── Religion: Lumism ├── Shadow Role: First Phase One infiltration — Shadows seeded empire since founding, engineered Goblin King war ├── Region: Lumina Continent ├── West: Maoma Tribe ├── East: Vennerian Goishi ├── Rival: Gigas Tribe — competing for continental dominance ├── Ambition: Retake lost lands, reform the Lumina Empire ├── Trade: Historic commerce with Erisdar ├── Species: Humans, Catmen, Beast Races, Lesser Catmen, Erisdarian Catmen └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.text: A human settler nation in central Lumina Continent, located southeast of the Gigas Tribe. The Republic was founded by settlers from the Vennerian Trade Republic who came to Lumina and established themselves in the region — predominantly human, with small Catmen and beastmen minorities living among them.

docs.title: Religion
docs.text: The people of the Lumina Republic believe in Eris — they follow the Erisian church, the same faith they brought with them from the Vennerian lands.

docs.title: Lumina
docs.text: A continent in central Ge'or, named after the Lumina Kingdom, once a powerful empire. Bordered by the Kutten Sea to the north and Beast's Bay to the southwest.

docs.title: Religion
docs.text:
The continent hosts a tangle of faiths:

  • Calism — most catmen of Lumina follow this pacifist, self-greatening philosophy-faith.
  • Sytrenis — the most ancient catmen religion, followed by Great Cattos and most Lesser Catmen.
  • Gigaoism — the theocratic cult of the Gigas Tribe's living telepathic dog-god.
  • Maomism — the Maoma Tribe's creation faith; beastmen as the gods' chosen rulers of the rainforests.
  • Lumism — the Lumina Kingdom's imperial cult to the old Lumina Empire's figures, with animism and reverence for the jungle animals.
  • Taosudism and Mukini Dirt-Faith — the earth-cosmologies of the neighbouring Mia factions, the trolls' Orgor Kingdom and the Mukini Tribe.
  • Erisian church — the faith of the demon refugees in Cammao Kingdom and the human settlers of the Lumina Republic.

The Maoma hold themselves the natural rulers of the world's rainforests — and the Gigas Tribe, their long-time enemies, to be the enemies of their gods, sent to destroy the rainforests of the world.

docs.text:
An island nation in the Luminous Ocean, owned by the Aenid Kingdom. The island is desert — like all of the surrounding Aenid region.

Erima is the birthplace of Mabode — the philosopher king who founded Shurtra, roughly 200 years before the Erisian church. The island's people are fishermen and traders who navigate the treacherous glowing waters with generations of inherited knowledge.

docs.title: Gildenrise
docs.text:
A half-elf kingdom on Moriat island in the Luminous Ocean, located west of Gomor and south of Underfern (north of Gildenrise is Underfern, east is Gomor).

Like Gomor, Gildenrise is a product of half-elf exodus from Erisdar discrimination. Across centuries half-elves entered Moriat; about ~200 AGD they became the majority of Gildenrise's population, seized its politics and government, and entrenched themselves as the nation.

docs.title: Religion
docs.text:
Mixed — no official state religion.

  • Majority: Elven Faith — elven gods, nature reverence, carried from Erisdar and now dominant.
  • Minority: Nyity — the ancient sky-god faith of Mikrad/Underfern (4,000 BGD), preserved by intermarried families and converts.
  • No state creed; both coexist.

docs.title: Gomor
docs.text:
A half-elf kingdom on Moriat island in the Luminous Ocean, located south of Mikrad and Underfern and west of Gildenrise.

Since half-elves are discriminated against in Erisdar, many crossed to Moriat across centuries. About ~200 AGD they became the majority of Gomor's population, took over its politics and government, and established themselves as the ruling people.

docs.title: Religion
docs.text:
Mixed — no official state religion.

  • Majority: Elven Faith — the elven gods and nature cults brought from Elvennrin/Elvenkrad, now the dominant faith among Gomor's half-elves.
  • Minority: Nyity — the old astronomical faith of Moriat's humans (Mikrad/Underfern), kept by half-elves who intermarried or converted. The sky-gods' blood sacrifice myth persists as a human-heritage memory.
  • The state declares no official religion; both are tolerated.

docs.title: Brotherstar
docs.text: The central machine nation on Lung Continent and the spiritual heart of machine civilization. Brotherstar is the site of the original incubator complex — the oldest continuously operating factory on Ge'or. It was here that the machines first developed sentience, and it is here that their religion of humanism was born.

docs.title: The Elder's Prophecy
docs.text:
The prophet "The Elder" — a machine who wandered the wasteland 500,000 years ago — discovered an ancient bunker. Inside was a machine powered by something in the soil, emitting a light and a sound: a radio signal from the allied species fighting the Hybrians during The Last Great War.

The signal announced that a test species would be launched onto Ge'or to evaluate its combat capabilities. The Elder misunderstood. He believed the signal was sent directly to the machines — a divine message from the sky. He returned to Brotherstar and told his people that humanity was testing them. If they held back the coming enemy, the humans would see them as worthy and return.

The enemy — The Hive — arrived shortly after. The machines have been fighting ever since.

docs.title: The Eternal War
docs.text: Brotherstar is the primary frontline against the Hive. Its incubators produce warriors as well as workers. Its legends speak of the day when the war will end and the sky gods will descend.

docs.title: River Settlement
docs.text: A human settlement on the southeastern corner of Lung Continent, founded by Erisdarian explorers who crash-landed there approximately 400 years ago (~200 AGD). Their ships were destroyed. They never recovered the ability to leave.

docs.title: Survival
docs.text:
The settlers found remnants of older civilizations that had also crashlanded on Lung over the millennia. All of them had died out. The River Settlement did not. For 400 years, nothing has happened to them. They do not know why.

The real reason: they have not yet been discovered by the Machines of the interior. Every other crashlanded group was found by machine patrols. When those survivors claimed to be human, the machines — who worship humans as sky gods — did not believe them. They assumed the survivors were demon impostors working for The Hive, and killed them all.

docs.title: Current State
docs.text: The River Settlement has not explored the vast interior of Lung. They know there is a continent beyond their valley, but it is separated by dense woods and mountain ranges that have prevented both their expansion and their discovery by the machines. They live in ignorance of the eternal war raging to the north.

docs.title: Brase
docs.text: A nation of Coldspeople on Marti Continent, located southwest of Germina. The Coldspeople — a humanoid mammalian race adapted to cold — thrive in the frigid climate that borders the southern tundra.

docs.title: Religion — Ulasm
docs.text:
Brase believes in Ulasm — and so do other Coldspeople generally. Ulasm is a pagan animistic faith that worships eagles as divine and worships ancestors — the dead dwell in the Great Cold and watch through eagle eyes. Brase keeps the eagle-feather talismans and dusk funeral pyres.

Other Coldspeople communities in Maboro and the high north share the faith.

docs.text: A dwarf kingdom in the far southwestern reaches of Marti Continent, reached by walking vast distances across uninhabited tundra from Brase. The region is near the southern polar ice — almost permafrost, resembling northern Russia. The Cobal dwarves have adapted to this extreme cold, mining frozen minerals from the ice-bound mountains.

docs.title: Germina
docs.text: A multi-ethnic kingdom on the northwestern Marti Continent, located directly south of the Vennerian Aelefer Channel connecting to Lumina Continent. Germina was colonized by Erisdarian settlers of several types and today is a melting pot: Humans, Erisdarian Catmen, Elves, beastmen (due to proximity), and a large population of Wolvesfolk.

docs.title: Religion — Several
docs.text:
Germina believes in several religions:

  • Catmen there believe in the same religion as the Great Cattos — Sytrenis (ancient catmen faith of Masaaki Sytrenis).
  • A large population are Erisian Church members — brought by Erisdarian settlers and maintained through Vennerian sea lanes.
  • Other faiths persist among the mixed population: Elven Faith among elves, animist practices among beastmen, Xuashism among wolvesfolk immigrants from Kut/Oigopol, and small Nyity and Ulasm minorities via trade.

Germina has no single state religion — it is a religious mosaic.

docs.title: Kobra
docs.text:
A snake nation on Marti Continent, located east of Kut. The Kobra are a cold-adapted subrace of snake people — unlike their warm-blooded kin in Xikxia (West Erisdar) and Zakarutia (Demon Continent), these serpents thrive in frigid climates.

The Kobra snakespeople are the same race as Xikxia and Zakarutia — however they separated thousands of years ago, and the Kobra lineage ended up living in Marti as a distinct population.

docs.title: Religion — Moplilly
docs.text:
Kobra believes in Moplilly — an ancestor-veneration cult where the ancestor of all of them and demigod father-founder Xanob is the most prayed-upon figure. Every scale-painting, egg-blessing, and winter fast honors Xanob's first coil.

Their cousins in Xikxia/Zakarutia instead follow Sibbism (Snake Goddess + 24 sons) — a different god, same blood.

docs.title: Kramsadar
docs.text:
A dragon kingdom in the far southern mountains of Marti Continent, west of the Cobal Kingdom across icy land and tundra. Kramsadar is one of the most isolated nations on Ge'or — half tundra, half near-permafrost, cut off from the rest of the world. The dragons here have lived undisturbed for millennia.

The seclusion is religious: the civilized dragons follow Daicrodism, the atonement faith born of the death wars, and barely leave. Believing themselves a source of pain and misery for the world, they live meditative, secluded lives.

Sailing north from Kramsadar across open ocean leads to distant northern continents.

The faithful believe in their god Xuashi — once the main god of the old animistic pantheon, recently promoted to sole deity — who incarnated in Erisdar as Eris and is the father and mother of all other religions on Ge'or.

  • Humans include Erisian and Nyity adherents, plus Marti coastal cults.
  • Beast people bring their own tribal animisms.
  • Demon merchants carry Kirivs-bin or are irreligious.

Maboro's port tolerates all faiths — the city has a street of temples.

docs.title: Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni
docs.text:
"No crown, no church — only freedom."

A democratic republic in northeastern Merratodoni, located east of Luzia and southeast across a small sea from the Arrow of Anos.

docs.title: Krowretism — The Freedom Faith
docs.text:
The Republic believes in the Church of Krowretism.

  • They are refugees from the Erisdar continent and the Erisian Church — the first dissidents to reject Eris as a demon.
  • Krowretism believes humans were deceived by the demon Eris and her followers — and that they need to purify the world from Eris forever and destroy her church.
  • They are the main sponsors of the Ironcloak — funding, arming, and sheltering the rebel order.
  • They believe in absolute freedom — the highest divine value. Their society is similar to the United States of America of Old Earth — a frontier democracy built by refugees, convinced of its mission.

docs.title: Exodus and Superpower
docs.text:
• ~100 BGD — they started leaving Erisdar approximately 100 years Before Great Divergence — the first wave of Eris-rejectors.
  • They settled in Merratodoni and ever since have been building a superpower on the continent — democratic, expansionist, industrial, and fiercely anti-Erisian.
  • As of 597 AGD, they are in the process of unifying with the Purple Coast — although they aren't a single entity yet. Joint councils and administration are underway.
  • They plan to expand westwards: the middle of Merratodoni is mostly unpopulated and they are colonizing it — a continental manifest destiny westward from the northeast.

The Republic is multi-racial: Humans, Catmen (including Merratodonian Catmen), beastmen, Elves, and Dwarves live within its borders, but its human republican identity and Krowretist faith define it.

docs.title: 🪨 Orgor Kingdom
docs.text: A troll kingdom occupying the southern region of Mia island, north of the Lumina Continent continent. One of the four major factions inhabiting the forested island.

docs.title: Religion — Taosudism
docs.text: The Orgor follow Taosudism, the ancient troll faith. Because water burns, cracks, and pains troll skin, they hold all water-based beings to be corrupt and demonic, and themselves a pure race. Every Orgor drinks only dirt-tempered water — pots of water mixed with soil, the only form that is safe and sacred. Taosudism marks the Orgor as trollkind, and separates them from every other culture on the island.

docs.title: 🐲 Xi'xia Tribe
docs.text: A tribe of wargs inhabiting the center of Mia island, north of the Lumina Continent. They are not a nation and not an organized political entity — they are a tribe, like the goblins' clans. And they are the only wargs in the world born smarter than their kind.

docs.title: The Only Smart Wargs
docs.text:
Everywhere else on Ge'or, wargs are animals — brilliant hunters, but untamable and unreasoning. The Xi'xia are different: they have evolved over millennia into something more. The reason is a perfect storm of the island and its history.

  • Isolation: separated from the mainland, the Mia wargs could not dilute with the wide, wild stock of wargs elsewhere.
  • The Old Lumina Empire: in the age of the beastmen's empire, the Old Lumina Empire conquered the island — and left its peoples upon it: the wargs, the trolls, and the other beastmen of Mia. When the empire fell, the island became a closed world.
  • The Hunt: trapped with trolls and beastmen as rivals, the wargs were hunted for generations. To survive they were forced to evolve their own systems — and by observing the two species they shared the island with, they learned to be smarter.

Wargs are a highly mutable species; give a thousand small generations of pressure, and they change.

docs.title: Communication
docs.text: Xi'xia wargs are sought after across the whole world for one gift: they understand words — and they can communicate back, not by voice, but by gesture. A Xi'xia warg can hold a conversation in signals, respond to command and question, and make itself understood. They cannot speak, but they do not need to.

docs.title: No Religion, No Lords
docs.text: The tribe has no religion — no gods, no rites, no spirits — and no ruling structure beyond the pack. They are an ungoverned people of an ungoverned island, and they answer to no one.

docs.title: The Name
docs.text: They are called Xi'xia for the sound they make when referring to themselves.

docs.text: [ Xi'xia Tribe ] ├── Island: Mia ├── Region: North of Lumina Continent ├── Species: Wargs — the only smarter-than-normal wargs in the world ├── Status: Tribe, not a nation — no organized political entity ├── Religion: None ├── Origin: Isolation + the Old Lumina Empire's conquest + generations hunted by the island's trolls and beastmen ├── Gift: Understand words; communicate by gesture, not voice ├── Traded: Sought after worldwide for their comprehension ├── Neighbors: Orgor Kingdom (south), Mukini Tribe (northwest), Mia Checkpoint (checkpoint) (northeast) └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Moonfang Dominion
docs.text:
A cult-nation on Moon Wolf Island, a frozen island near the north pole northeast of Erisdar. Exclusively human. Comparable to Greenland in climate but far more populated — the cult keeps its people alive to serve.

Moon Wolf Island has the distinct appearance of a wolf's head, a shape that fuels the Dominion's religion. Two peninsulas — one north, one south — form the wolf's open mouth along the eastern coast. Northwest of the northern peninsula lies a lake that reads as the wolf's eye. The island's center is a dead zone of mountains and active volcanoes.

docs.title: The Cult of Cleton
docs.text:
The Moonfang Dominion is a death cult. Their god is Cleton, the Wolf God — a being that demands child sacrifices to sustain the world's order. Each year, the cult gathers a selection of children and sends them to Cleton Island, a smaller island caught between the two peninsulas of the wolf's mouth — as if the wolf itself is devouring it. The children chosen are always the prettiest. Beauty is the mark of Cleton's hunger.

Wargs — massive wolf-like predators native to the island — are treated as sacred animals. Their resemblance to the wolf-shaped island is taken as divine proof. They roam freely near settlements. Attacking one is death.

The cult teaches that the outside world is damned. Isolation is salvation. To question the order is to question Cleton, and to question Cleton is to be fed to him.

docs.title: Geography
docs.text:
• Moon Wolf Island: Frozen, wolf-shaped. Mountains and volcanoes dominate the center. Habitation clings to the coasts.
  • Cleton Island: The sacrifice ground, held in the wolf's mouth between the northern and southern peninsulas.
  • The Eye: A lake northwest of the northern peninsula, completing the wolf's face.
  • The Molten Archipelago: Far southwest across open sea — an uninhabitable volcanic archipelago. Karabar operates refugee bases on its eastern edge. For those who flee the cult, the Archipelago is a destination; for most who reach it, it is a new kind of prison — forced labor for wages that barely keep them alive.

docs.title: Culture
docs.text:
Life in the Dominion is brutality disguised as piety. Beatings are routine. Children work from the moment they can walk. To be poor is to be blessed — the cult teaches that suffering purifies. To be beautiful is to be marked — marked for Cleton's selection.

The people are pale and lean, shaped by generations of cold, hunger, and fear. They speak little. They trust no one. They pray — not from hope, but from a faith beaten into the bones before memory.

docs.title: Notable Individuals
docs.text: • Aelis — born 600 AGD. Blonde, petite, poor family, true believer in honor. A contradiction the cult has not yet noticed.

docs.title: Ameboria
docs.text:
The Alegorian heart inside Kent. Fighting to break free.

Ameboria is a region inside Kent that follows the Alegoria faith. As of 597 AGD, Ameboria is in civil war against Kent, seeking to separate and join the Alegorian north.

docs.title: The Conflict
docs.text:
Kent's majority follows the Erisian faith and despises the Alegorians. Ameboria, deeply loyal to the legend of Julian the Dragon Tamer and the Church of Alegoria, refuses to remain under Erisian rule.

The Kentian Civil War is, at its core, a religious war — Alegoria versus Eris, Julian versus the fabricated god, the north versus the center.

docs.title: The Kentian Civil War
docs.text:
The region of Ameboria in Kent follows the Alegoria faith — the religion of the Axels, founded under Julian the Dragon Tamer. The rest of Kent follows the Erisian faith and despises the Alegorians. Ameboria is fighting to separate from Kent and join the Alegorian north.

docs.title: Mann Order
docs.text:
A country in North Erisdar, located north of the Erilian Federation and east of Cossiland. Currently being invaded by the Erilian Federation, who consider them "pagans" for refusing the Eris cult and following Mannosta — the ancestral faith of the stars. Many within Mann Order's borders now follow Alegoria rather than the old faith.

Founded: By the general Kosbaldo, who led the Mann tribes in rebellion after Erilio's Crusade of 278 AGD took half their land. The Order is a military dictatorship born of guerrilla war.

Religion: Mannosta — many of the Mann Order people are Mannosta pagans. Mann is the capital of the gods for Mannosta — and the capital of the Mann Order itself. Mannosta means "greatness of Mann."

docs.title: The Invasion
docs.text: The Erilian Federation has captured the city of Tilboria (also written "Tiaboria" in some records). The war is ongoing. Many Mann refugees fled past the Mongrel Forest into the east, settling in the Fractured State of Erislod — a land they call New Mann.

docs.title: ❄️ Northaxeland
docs.text:
The northernmost territory in North Erisdar, bordering the frozen wastes beyond habitable Erisdar. Harsh and sparsely populated, Northaxeland's people — the Axels — are known for resilience and a fierce independence.

Northaxeland is the birthplace of the Alegoria religion, founded under the legendary figure of Julian the Dragon Tamer. The Church of Alegoria controls most of northern Erisdar from here. The Axels believe Julian became one with their god through his duel with Fireborn at Dragonreach.

Before Northaxeland existed, the region was a collection of small kingdoms — including Shuttil, Julian's birthplace, which was later destroyed by the Axels during their war for independence from Baoth's influence. The three companions — Plenio, Diana, and Korvald — guided the Axel people to victory and became their loyal servants.

docs.title: Shuttil
docs.text:
The kingdom that killed Julian's family. The first to burn when the Axels rose.

Shuttil was one of the small kingdoms in the region that would later become Northaxeland. It was the birthplace of Julian the Dragon Tamer — and the site of his first tragedy.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Shuttil's guards were corrupt. They blackmailed Julian's family over unpaid taxes. When the family could not pay, the guards murdered Julian's parents in front of him. Julian fled to the countryside — an orphan, a plowman, a boy who had seen too much.

Years later, after Baoth's influence spread across the region, Shuttil became allied to Baoth — a client kingdom serving the dragon king's interests.

docs.title: Destruction
docs.text: When Plenio, Diana, and Korvald led the guerrilla campaign against Baoth after Julian's death, Shuttil was the first victim. The Axels — the human population rallied under Julian's legend — invaded and destroyed the kingdom that had once murdered their prophet's family. Shuttil's lands were absorbed into what became Northaxeland.

docs.title: 🔷 Tetras
docs.text:
A small, fortress-oriented territory in North Erisdar named for its four-point fortification layout. Tetras has maintained military readiness since the Dragon Tyranny era — a holdover from when dragon-king raiders threatened all northern settlements. The dragons are gone, but Tetras has never stopped training.

docs.title: Gnoll & Kobold Tribes
docs.text:
"The weak beg for borders. The strong take what they need."

The Gnolls and Kobold tribes of North Erisdar occupy a swath of rocky, resource-poor highlands that settled nations long ago deemed not worth conquering. This mutual disinterest — the tribes have nothing worth taking, and the tribes want nothing the settled peoples build — has produced an uneasy equilibrium. Gnolls organize in extended hunting packs led by an alpha pair, while kobold warrens operate as collective dens with shared labor and communal hoards. The two species coexist through a brutal but functional hierarchy: gnolls provide protection and raw strength, kobolds provide trap-craft, tunneling, and the meticulous hoard-accounting that passes for kobold governance.

Neither species produces significant mage-cell lineages — their populations were among those diluted most thoroughly during the early tribal wars. What they lack in magical firepower they compensate for in numbers, ferocity, and a cultural refusal to surrender ground. Imperial historians have attempted three documented campaigns to pacify the tribal highlands; all three ended in withdrawal, with the tribes melting into terrain that imperial supply lines could not sustain.

The tribes maintain a long-standing territorial feud with the Harpy clans, who raid kobold hoards from above with infuriating impunity. To the south, they observe the Erisian Empire border forts with the wary respect of predators sizing up a fence — not hostile, but not friendly, and entirely willing to test the fence if hunger demands it.

The Gnoll & Kobold Tribes occupy tribal territories in North Erisdar. See Gnolls and Kobolds for species details.

docs.title: Harpies
docs.text:
"We do not claim the land. We claim the sky above it."

The Harpy territories of North Erisdar are not a nation in the settled sense — there are no walls, no capitals, no standing armies. Instead, the harpy clans follow seasonal flight-paths across the northern highlands, their territories defined by wind-currents and mountain perches rather than surveyed borders. Governance is clan-based and matriarchal: each aerie is led by a senior matron whose authority derives from her ability to read weather patterns and negotiate with the ground-bound peoples below.

Harpies possess a unique form of mage-cell expression that enhances their flight musculature and hollow-bone density, allowing sustained high-altitude travel that few other species can match. This biological advantage has made them invaluable as long-distance messengers and scouts — a role they have parlayed into a protected neutrality. No major power in Erisdar wants harpies as enemies, because no major power can catch them.

Their most notorious trait is their method of reproduction. Harpies lack the biological capacity to carry offspring themselves — instead, they implant fertilized eggs into hosts of other species through forced coupling. The implanted offspring gestates inside the host for several days, feeding on the host's tissues, before tearing its way out. The host rarely survives. This gruesome biology has made harpies universally feared despite their otherwise transactional neutrality, and no diplomatic arrangement with a harpy clan ever includes overnight hospitality.

Relations with the Gnoll and Kobold Tribes are tense and territorial — the harpies raid kobold supply caches from above, while gnoll hunting parties track harpy nesting sites on foot. With the settled nations to the south, the clans maintain a transactional distance: harpy couriers carry messages for coin, but the clans offer nothing more.

The Harpy territories are tribal lands in North Erisdar, inhabited by harpy clans. See Harpies for species details.

docs.title: Alborric
docs.text:
The only nation on the Polar Continent — the southern polar landmass of Ge'or, like Antarctica. Located below Kramsadar on Marti Continent, reached by walking through the permafrost and crossing the frozen polar ocean. Alborric is the sole angelic nation in the world, home to the Angels race, who dwell in the polar mountains.

Their faith is Pragmus — the angels believe themselves the creation and employees of the god of Ge'or, sworn to perfect the world. Though their homeland is the south pole, angels are found across Ge'or, helping quietly and rarely seen.

docs.title: The Silo
docs.text:
The base is built around a massive silo — a structure left behind by the Old Humans of the 157th Colony era, approximately three million years ago. The silo was designed to house a weapon of extraordinary power: a neutron bomb capable of triggering a global ice age.

When the Shadows arrived on Ge'or in 2989 BGD, they did not know the silo existed. They discovered it approximately 597 years ago — around the time of the Great Divergence (Year 0). The malfunction of the Glorious Alliance reactor provided the energy signature that led them to it.

The Shadows recovered the Glorious Alliance's reactor core — the same core whose malfunction created The Groom and caused the Kutten Catastrophe — and have been working ever since to integrate it with the silo. The neutron bomb is nearly complete.

When activated, the Armageddon device will:

  • Trigger a global ice age — wiping out billions, collapsing every decentralized state.
  • Unleash the Pontus goblin army simultaneously.
  • Coincide with The Groom's final detonation.
  • Coincide with the Pontificate of Eris declaring the prophecy of Eris fulfilled.

docs.title: The Eternal Paradise Plan
docs.text:
Eternal Paradise is not merely a base. It is the name of the Shadows' ultimate objective — their answer to the destruction of Old Earth and the imprisonment of the Hybrian hivemind in the Fortress Planet.

The plan is simple. The Shadows will use their growing hold on the Hope Realm — the soul substrate of reality — to unleash a force that will consume the entire universe. All matter. All stars. All atoms. Everything will be converted into a single substance: black goo.

This is the same substance that the Old Humans studied at the 157th Colony. The same substance that, in modified form, became the Black Agent — the DNA agent that created The Two Protagonists. The Shadows call it the "element of soul" — the raw material of consciousness itself, rendered liquid and controllable.

In their final form, the universe will be:

  • A formless entity — no stars, no planets, no life, no matter in any recognizable state.
  • Perfectly controlled — everything inside the goo, nothing outside it.
  • Eternal — no death, no change, no freedom, no hope. Only the Hybrian consciousness, extending infinitely in all directions.

This is what the Shadows have been working toward for 8,000 years — since the campfire on Old Earth. The nation-state was step one. The hivemind was step two. The universe-as-goo is the final step. Perfect control. No resistance. No existence outside their will.

docs.title: The Protagonist Connection
docs.text:
The Black Agent that created the two protagonists is derived from this same goo — the element of soul. The Old Humans of the 157th Colony were studying it, trying to understand it, trying to weaponize it. The Shadows are trying to become it.

The protagonists are not merely powerful mages. They carry within them the raw material of the Shadows' endgame — repurposed by the accumulated hope of quintillions of dead souls, aimed at the enemy that created it.

docs.title: Current Status (597 AGD)
docs.text:
The neutron bomb is nearly complete. The Shadows' hold on the Hope Realm is growing. The Armageddon timeline is approaching.

The base is heavily guarded. The island is remote. No one on Ge'or knows it exists — except the Ironcloak, who have fragments of intelligence they cannot fully verify.

docs.title: Grimmel Republic
docs.text:
"We wanted neither empire nor church. So we built neither."

The Grimmel Republic is a human nation in South Erisdar founded by settlers who rejected both the Erisian Empire and the Erisian church during the Erisian expansion. Rather than fight the imperial tide, the founders walked — migrating south beyond the reach of imperial tax collectors and Pontifical inquisitors, establishing a republic built on the principle that government should be too small to oppress and too weak to crusade. That principle has held for centuries.

Grimmel is governed by a Citizens' Assembly open to all landholding adults, with an elected First Citizen serving as executive for a single five-year term. The republic maintains no standing army, relying instead on a citizen-militia that musters only in emergencies — a system that has worked largely because Grimmel's geography, nestled between the Limese League and the Vennerian Trade Republic, means any invader would have to cross one of those powers first. Both the League and Venner find Grimmel more useful as a neutral buffer than as conquered territory.

The republic's culture is agrarian and deliberately modest. Grimmel's citizens view the Anos Plutocracy with contempt — wealth-as-governance strikes them as the very corruption they fled — and the Corinite League with the wariness of farmers watching sailors: different worlds, different values, but mutually necessary trade partners. Grimmel exports grain, imports manufactured goods, and stays out of wars.

docs.title: The Magical Bloodlines
docs.text:
Grimmel is home to two families of unusually high magical potential: the Eisenheart family and the Mortvagn family. Their mage-cell density is among the highest in the region — their bloodlines emitting enough ambient magic to act as a beacon for the Black Agent drifting through Ge'or's oceans.

In 596 AGD, the black agent — carrying the encoded consciousnesses of Mikhail, Arkady, Ichi, and Mana — found its way to Grimmel's coast. It was drawn specifically to these two families, whose magical signatures it had been seeking for over three centuries.

The following year, three children were born: Emrys Eisenheart and his twin sister Ichi Eisenheart to the Eisenheart household, and Lucien Mortvagn to the Mortvagn household, twelve kilometers away. Three years later, Mana Mortvagn was born as Lucien's little sister.

The Grimmel Republic — a nation founded on the principle of being too small to matter — became the birthplace of the three people who would decide the fate of the universe.

docs.title: Geography
docs.text:
Grimmel's terrain is a mix of rolling farmland, wooded groves, and the occasional ravine cutting through the hills. The western reaches border wilder country — cave systems where relics from the Glorious Alliance crash remain buried, waiting to be found.

Species: Humans

During the Age of Consolidation, the Empire absorbed border territories through a mixture of economic leverage, political marriages, and strategic pressure. docs.title: Tunwif
docs.text: A kingdom of the Human Age in the region of the now-Grimmel Republic. When Termopolas branded Masaaki Sytrenis and his party criminals for the Metrak tragedy, Tunwif — together with Aelefer and Lima — shielded them, starting the Tunwif–Termopolas conflict. The leaderless empire lost battle after battle despite outnumbering its foes, and eventually Sytrenis made peace, ending the conflict and the catmen persecution.

docs.text:

  • Lumina Kingdom — significant Vennerian influence, anchored by Vennerian Goishi.
  • New Elvengar (Kutten) — sustains itself through a partnership with Venner.

docs.title: Rivals
docs.text:
• Anos Plutocracy — Venner's primary rival. Anos is weaker but still formidable, controlling fewer territories but maintaining a powerful fleet. The two are locked in a permanent naval and trade race.
  • Mikrad and Gomor — hostile toward Venner since the Minir invasion.

docs.title: Allies
docs.text:
• Corinite League — long-term ally. Venner is slowly integrating the League and is expected to formally annex it within the next several years. This would make Venner the undisputed dominant power in Dissenbarg. Beyond the League, Venner is slowly taking over Dissenbarg's politics, turning its states into tributaries and vassals — a patient process that will take years to complete.
  • Grimmel Republic — strong trade partnership and good relations.

docs.title: Neutral/Balancing
docs.text: • Limese League — works with both Venner and Anos, balancing the two powers for profit.

docs.title: Trade & Culture
docs.text:
Venner deals in everything. Spices, metals, Romanium, timber, textiles — and slaves. The Vennerian slave trade is substantial, with a particular appetite for beastmen slaves from Lumina Continent.

Vennerian culture has spread globally through their trade networks. Their language, Vennerian, is the lingua franca of international commerce.

docs.title: The Catmen Obsession
docs.text:
The Vennerian aristocracy is famously — and somewhat notoriously — obsessed with Catmen, especially catgirls. Human-cat hybrids exist in Vennerian high society, despite the Erisian church formally forbidding human-catmen marriages. This prohibition is widely ignored.

Across all of Ge'or — including within the Erisian Empire and even the Erisian church — catmen are viewed amicably. They are the one species nobody hates.

docs.title: Power Ranking
docs.text:
Venner is considered an SS-tier power — alongside the Asatru Empire, Erisian Empire, Northaxeland, Kramsadar (isolated), Alborric (isolated), and the Central Kingdom (Tabontabar).

It is widely expected that Venner will eventually surpass the Erisian Empire as the dominant power on Ge'or.

docs.title: Central Kingdom
docs.text: A kingdom in central Tabontabar Continent, south of the Northern Kingdom and northwest of the Southern Kingdom. The Central Kingdom resembles the Beijing region of China — the political heartland, more formal and bureaucratic than the trade-oriented north.

  • Architecture: Grand imperial palaces, walled cities, formal gardens
  • Species: Majority Humans, with Catmen minority, Dwarves in the mountain ranges, and Demons (ostracized)
  • Religion: Xatarism — the cult of family, tradition, and the emperor (coexists with Ximioli, the continent's more popular faith). Meditation and monks everywhere
  • Access to Sun Archipelago: From the west coast, sea travel reaches the South Sun Empire

docs.title: Aenid Kingdom
docs.text:
"Mabode came from the stars to save humanity."

The Aenid Kingdom is a human monarchy in West Erisdar, situated at the edge of the Lyrical Forest and within sight of Matterbleak. The kingdom's history is inseparable from the forest — early Aenid settlers learned, through catastrophic trial and error, that the Lyrical Forest is not merely a collection of trees but a repository of something the locals call "the chorus": residual consciousness imprints from the fallen soldiers of the Last Great War, bound to the wood they died among.

Governance is a hereditary monarchy under the Aen line, whose legitimacy rests on an ancient compact with the forest itself — or, as skeptics note, on a carefully maintained tradition of not angering whatever lives there. The current king maintains a court that is notably smaller, quieter, and more superstitious than those of comparable kingdoms. Aenid law mandates that no tree within a league of the forest's edge may be cut; the kingdom imports all its timber from the interior, at considerable expense.

Relations with Matterbleak are close but somber — the two settlements share the same psychological weight, the same learned caution, the same unspoken understanding that some places on Ge'or were not meant for human habitation and that humans live there anyway. With the rest of Erisdar, Aenid maintains minimal contact — the kingdom is not hostile, merely preoccupied with a neighbor that cannot be reasoned with, traded with, or ignored.

The Aenid Kingdom is a nation in West Erisdar, situated near Matterbleak and the Lyrical Forest.

docs.title: Geography — The Desert
docs.text:
The Aenid Kingdom is situated in a desertic region. All of that area — including the island of Erima, which the kingdom owns — is desert. Its neighbors share the same aridity: Augagarten is desertic, and Astravayne is a lot desertic too.

The desert shapes the kingdom as much as the forest does: a hard land that produces hard, honor-bound people.

docs.title: Religion — Shurtra
docs.text:
Aenid follows Shurtra, founded by Mabode — a philosopher king born on Erima island roughly 200 years before the founding of the Erisian church. Shurtra is therefore about 200 years older than the Erisian Church.

Shurtra worships Mabode, saying he came from the stars to save humanity. The faith's name means "righteousness" — its language, Shurtraliot, means "righteous language", and is commonly spoken throughout the kingdom.

Honor and death cults: Shurtra men are highly expected to be extremely honorable. That impossible standard makes death cults common — which leads the authorities to usually crack down on them.

Enemy of the Church: Aenid is a fierce enemy of the Erisian church — the Church conquered a lot of Shurtra's lands, and Aenid has never forgiven it.

docs.title: Naval Power & the Luminous Ocean
docs.text:
Despite its forest-bound reputation, Aenid is the largest and most politically organized maritime power of the Luminous Sea Islands region — a kingdom in name and function. It maintains the region's only significant naval force and projects influence over the smaller island nations. Its monarch claims sovereignty over the entire Luminous Ocean; the other islands acknowledge this about as much as they have to.

The kingdom's position on the West Erisdar coast lets it face two directions at once: inland toward the forest that shapes its soul, and seaward toward the glowing waters it quietly dominates. Aenid's navy is the kingdom's one extravagance — the same culture that forbids cutting a tree within a league of the forest's edge spends lavishly on hulls, sails, and cannon.

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Augamouth defies the stereotypes that plague orcs elsewhere:

  • Stable governance — centuries of continuous rule under the Kobrutu dynasty and its successors.
  • Functional economy — trade with Demon's Horn, Palonia, and (tensely) Astravayne.
  • Rule of law — harsh but fair. Disputes are settled by military tribunals, not mob violence.
  • Loyalty culture — the military hierarchy doubles as a social contract. Soldiers protect citizens. Citizens support soldiers. Betrayal of either is the highest crime.

Religion: Ogoron — "the titanic orc." Augamouth worships a supposed huge orc that will avenge all the orc race for their injustices and bring peace to the world, after which all species will live in harmony. Ogoron is inside all of their hearts.

Non-orcs live in Augamouth as minorities — mostly traders and diplomats. They are treated correctly but never fully trusted. Augamouth remembers that the rest of the world calls them brutes.

docs.title: Foreign Relations
docs.text:
• Demon's Horn — primary trade partner. The intercontinental commerce hub treats Augamouth as an equal.
  • Palonia — neutral. Palonia has no love for demons, but orcs are tolerated.
  • Astravayne — tense. The multi-racial beastmen kingdom and the orc military state have little in common.
  • Xikxia — stable border. The snake people and orcs respect each other's territory.

docs.title: Klobiendar
docs.text:
The dragon empire of West Erisdar. Rival to Xi. Destroyed by a spell that still echoes.

Klobiendar was the dragon empire of West Erisdar, ruled from its capital at Dragonreach. It was the rival of Xi, the dragon kingdom of the east. The two empires fought The Draconic War — fifty years of slaughter that ended when Xi's leader Melberior launched a suicide spell that destroyed Klobiendar's capital entirely.

Klobiendar's last king was Fireborn, who became a Fallen Dragon after the war. His son, Goldenborn, was born in Dragonreach's volcanic caldera and would later found Baoth.

docs.title: Religion — Wruowas
docs.text:
Koetebalo believes in Wruowas — an ultra-ancient religion that cults Dabazi Ar Batr, the great serpent creator of all reality. It is a celestial animism where they worship constellations in the sky as the serpent's scales — the sky is scripture.

Wruowas predates every other faith on Xeti by millennia; its Stone-Seers chart the serpent's coils.

docs.title: The Isolation
docs.text:
The seas surrounding Lung Continent and Sister Continent are violent — storms, impossible currents, reefs that tear ships apart. No explorer from Erisdar or the Demon Continent has ever successfully navigated them and returned. Most people on Ge'or believe the world is flat — that beyond the known continents, there is only ocean and void.

The Machines of Lung and Sister do not know other continents exist. The other continents do not know the machines exist.

Zahor Island, tucked south of Lung, shares this isolation. For 4,000 years, the Malgardians have lived, built, and died on their island — never contacted, never discovered.

docs.title: The Discovery
docs.text:
Four thousand years of peace ended when Zahorian explorers crossed the narrow sea to Lung Continent and discovered something impossible.

A massive creature — the size of a hundred buildings — moved across the northern wasteland. It carried thousands of insects on its back and in its wake. The explorers did not know what they were seeing. They had never heard of The Hive. But they understood one thing immediately: this was a war party. Whatever that creature was, it was preparing to invade — their island, or another island, or something beyond the horizon.

They reported back. The Malgardians knew they had no army that could stop such a thing.

docs.title: The Hero — Zahor
docs.text:
One Malgardian volunteered. His name was Zahor.

He crossed to Lung alone. He found the Hive creature — one of the great Queens, a mountain-sized brood-mother preparing to launch across the sea. He attacked.

Using a desperate magical assault, he struck the creature's eyes — blinding it. He severed one of its body parts in the chaos. Then the Hive devoured him.

Zahor died. But his attack delayed the invasion. The creature — wounded, disoriented — retreated to the northern wasteland to heal and regroup.

The island was named after him. Every Malgardian child learns his name.

docs.title: The Future
docs.text:
The Hive has not attempted another crossing. Not yet.

The machines of Lung Continent are unaware of the Hive's new tactics. They believe the eternal war is contained on the northern wastelands. They do not know the Hive is trying to reach the sea and spread to other continents.

Zahor's sacrifice bought time. But the Hive Queens are patient. After 597 AGD, the invasion may come again. Nobody on Ge'or knows this — except the Malgardians of Zahor, who have been watching the northern horizon for 4,000 years.

docs.title: Lineage — The Rebel Tradition
docs.text:
The Ironcloak are the latest incarnation of a philosophical tradition stretching back to Old Earth. Their ancestors were the rebels who opposed the Shadows from the beginning:

  • Socrates — executed for revealing Shadow plans to the public (~400 BCE)
  • Plato and the Academy — preserved the critique in secret
  • Original Christians — a rebel offshoot that rejected the Shadow-designed temple-state
  • Original Protestants — broke from Shadow-controlled church hierarchy
  • American Revolutionaries — cost the Shadows centuries of empire-building
  • 19th–20th Century Libertarians — the last Earth-born rebels before the 2030 takeover
  • The Asteroid Refugees — escaped the solar system, annihilated, but launched the ships that preserved humanity

Every one of these movements fought the same enemy: centralized control disguised as order, obedience disguised as faith, the surveillance god disguised as love. The Ironcloak on Ge'or are the direct continuation of this war — a war that has lasted three million years.

docs.title: 📜 Knowledge
docs.text:
The Ironcloak hold fragmented records of the truth:

  • They know the Erisian church is a fabrication.
  • They know Kirivis was not a villain — he was a hero.
  • They search for the Archive of the Traveler in the Ruins of Baoth.
  • They do not know that their goddess walks among the Shadows themselves.

docs.title: The Hunters
docs.text:
They don't enter the mountain. They know better. But everything around it is fair game.

The Hunters are the adventurers who operate in the lower reaches of Dragonreach — not in the mountain itself, but in the dungeons, ruins, and monster lairs that surround it. They are the economic lifeblood of Augamouth and Astravayne, bringing out gold, Romanium, relics, and artifacts from the dragon age.

docs.title: What They Do
docs.text:
The Hunters raid the dungeons near Dragonreach — places of concentrated magic created by the same forces that shaped the mountain. These dungeons are less lethal than the caldera itself, but still dangerous. Zombies, skeletons, spirits, and mutated creatures guard ancient treasures.

The goods they recover are genuine: - Gold — dragon hoard fragments, imperial tribute, temple treasuries - Romanium — the scarcest resource on Ge'or, found in ancient caches - Relics — weapons, tools, lost spells from the dragon empires and earlier ages - Historical artifacts — tablets, records, objects predating the Great Divergence

These goods flow into regional markets, funding everything from mercenary companies to temple construction.

docs.title: The Economy
docs.text:
The Hunter economy sustains entire towns. Augamouth processes dungeon salvage through its orcish forges. Astravayne handles the artifact trade, connecting Dragonreach's treasures to the broader Erisdarian market. Merchant guilds finance expeditions. Adventurer Guilds rank and license the participants. The flow is constant.

Most Hunters die young. The few who survive become wealthy, respected, and deeply superstitious. They know the mountain watches them. They know the relics they find are not accidents.

docs.title: The Relic Mystery
docs.text:
Some of the relics recovered near Dragonreach are too new. Too purposeful. Too perfectly placed. The Hunters attribute this to the mountain's magic, to luck, to fate.

They are wrong.

The Black Agent Hivemind inside Goldenborn's Caldera deliberately releases some of its creations — relics, tools, artifacts — into the lower valleys. It uses the Hunters as unwitting couriers, spreading its influence across Ge'or one recovered artifact at a time.

The Hunters do not know they are being used. They would not believe it if told.

docs.title: The Shadows' Escape
docs.text:
The Hybrian Shadows were not part of the hivemind when it was captured. Those old philosophers had separated from the collective consciousness long before — positioning themselves as overseers rather than participants. When the Union closed the trap, the Shadows were already outside it.

They went into hibernation. They waited for the universe to forget. Then they began looking for their god.

docs.title: Parallel to the Ironcloak
docs.text: The Ironcloak is the spiritual successor to the Union — a decentralized order that hunts Shadow influence without itself becoming a centralized institution. Both operate on the same principle: the enemy is control. The weapon against it is fragmentation.

docs.title: ⚓ Corinite League
docs.text:
A maritime league in Dissenbarg composed of four member states: Taebea, Tessa (which controls the island colony of Tibia), Klatia, and Corin — the senior partner and de facto leader of the confederation.

The 597 AGD world map records the League's members in its cartouche as "Corin, Kizita, Taebea, Tessa" — the "Kizita" entry corresponding to Citrea (also rendered "Kizita" on the map body), the coastal merchant enclave.

The League's power derives from its collective control of strategic shipping lanes and port-cities. While each member retains internal autonomy, matters of collective policy — trade agreements, naval defense, foreign relations — are decided by the Merchant Council, chaired by Corin.

docs.title: Religion
docs.text: The League's member states share a patron: Corin, the goddess of sea and commerce of the Helism pantheon — the goddess for which the senior city-state is named.
