docs.title: 🏛️ Religions
docs.text:
The faiths of Ge'or — and the truth behind the Erisian Church.

Browse the entries in the sidebar, or return to the World Dashboard.

docs.title: Alegoria
docs.text:
The faith of Julian. The religion of the Axels. The church that rules northern Erisdar.

Alegoria is the religion founded by the Axels — the human people of Northaxeland — under the legendary figure of Julian the Dragon Tamer. Its core belief: Julian became one with their god, transcending death through the dragon Fireborn. They await the return of the two prophets he spoke of.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
After Julian's death and his incarnation into Fireborn, Plenio, Diana, and Korvald continued guerrilla warfare against Baoth's influence in the north. The population of what became Northaxeland was the most receptive — entire cities raised armies, declared independence from Baoth, and rallied around Julian's story.

The Axels formalized Julian's legend into a religion. Shuttil — Julian's birthplace, by then allied to Baoth — was the first to fall to their forces. Plenio, Diana, and Korvald became loyal servants of the Axel people, guiding them into the future.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Julian transcended death by becoming one with the dragon Fireborn — not through magic, but through worthiness proven in combat.
  • Two prophets will come in the future. Fireborn-Julian waits to test them.
  • The Hybrians are the great enemy — the evil that destroys families. Julian's own family was their victim.
  • Worthiness is proven through action, not birth. Julian was a poor plowman who earned a dragon's respect.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
As of 597 AGD:

  • The Church of Alegoria controls most of northern Erisdar.
  • It is the majority faith in Northaxeland, Venkradian Republic, and Loren.
  • The region of Ameboria inside Kent follows Alegoria — and is in civil war trying to separate from Kent. The rest of Kent follows the Erisian faith and hates the Alegorians.
  • Tensions between Alegorian and Erisian territories are constant and violent.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Alegoria ] ├── Founder: Julian the Dragon Tamer (posthumous, deified by Axels) ├── Guiding figures: Plenio (elf), Diana (human), Korvald (kobold) ├── Core belief: Julian became one with god; two prophets will come ├── Holy site: Dragonreach, monument in Ruins of Baoth (Sword of Xi) ├── Regions: Northaxeland, Venkradian Republic, Loren, Ameboria (Kent) ├── Rival: Erisian Church — violent tensions in Kent ├── Enemy: Hybrians — the evil that destroys families └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: ✝️ Apostles of Eris
docs.text:
"She spoke, and they carried her word to the world."

The Apostles of Eris are the seven legendary followers of Eris, the fabricated goddess of the Erisian church. According to Church canon, Eris chose seven apostles to spread her word across Erisdar — each apostle founding a holy institution, order, or church state that bears their name to this day.

Whether they were real people or further layers of the Shadow fabrication is a question the Church does not encourage.

docs.title: The Seven
docs.text: Apostle Legacy Alexa Alexa Church State — an Erisian church state on the Grimmel Peninsula Draco Draco Order — order state within the Erisian Empire Niccas Order of Niccas — independent order on the southwest coast of the Grimmel Peninsula Ever Ever Order — order state within the Erisian Empire Aris Namesake of Arisdian — territory of the Grimmel Peninsula Malich (legacy to be defined) Maldorn (legacy to be defined)

docs.title: Significance
docs.text: The apostles explain the proliferation of "Order" and "Church State" names across the southern Erisdar — each one tracing its legitimacy to a figure of the Erisian pantheon. In a region where the Church's political grip is weakest (the Scarlet Order's martial faith, Grimmel's deliberate churchlessness), the apostolic institutions carry the Erisian name into the frontier.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Apostles of Eris ] ├── Worshiped In: Erisian church ├── Alexa → Alexa Church State ├── Draco → Draco Order ├── Niccas → Order of Niccas ├── Ever → Ever Order ├── Aris → Arisdian ├── Malich → TBD ├── Maldorn → TBD └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🙏 Calism
docs.text: "Gentle with the world. Fierce with the self-destructive."

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Calism is the catmen religion — more philosophy than worship. It is strongest in Marko, the merchant city-state on Kutten, and most catmen of Lumina follow it as well.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Pacifism and gentleness: followers are docile and gentle with others, avoiding conflict.
  • Ecumenical, not universalist: Calism coexists with other faiths, but it does not hold that all religions are true.
  • Self-greatening: followers seek only to greaten themselves — self-cultivation over conquest.
  • Not naive peace: Calism followers can be strict and even cruel when needed — especially against self-destructive behavior. This firmer side is followed most rigorously by the humans and other species who adopt Calism.
  • The catmen's lightness: catmen themselves live the faith lightly — playful and not quite of this world — yet they still find self-destructive behavior strange and hold preconceptions against it.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Marko (Kutten)
  • Most catmen of Lumina follow Calism
  • Adopted by humans and other species, who keep its stricter discipline

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Calism ] ├── Species: Catmen ├── Nations: Marko, Lumina ├── Character: Pacifist, gentle, ecumenical — strict against self-destruction ├── Doctrine: Greaten oneself; gentleness as strength └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🙏 Charlmelism
docs.text: "They built a wall against us. We climbed it anyway."

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Charlmelism is the religion of Aimeled. In the past, its people were heavily barbarian — raiders who, together with the Aenid, used to invade the Erisian Theocracy.

Those invasions are exactly why the Great Eris Wall was built by the Erisian Theocracy and the Pontificate of Eris.

docs.title: Modern Faith
docs.text:
Nowadays Charlmelism is more civilized — the barbarian age is behind it, though the memory of the invasions shapes everything.

  • Great rivals of the Erisian Theocracy.
  • The Theocracy (with help from the Erisian Empire) has dominated and invaded Aimeled multiple times.
  • Aimeled has kept rebelling again and again — and kept coming back.

docs.title: Geography
docs.text: Charlmelism's homeland is a desertic region.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Charlmelism ] ├── Nations: Aimeled ├── Rival: Erisian Theocracy — mutual invasions across centuries ├── Historical: With the Aenid, caused the Great Eris Wall to be built ├── Character: Once barbarian, now civilized; unbreakable ├── Geography: Desertic region └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🪨 Coal Doctrine
docs.text:
"Life should be treated as coal — burn peacefully in the dark to enlighten the world."

The Coal Doctrine is the southern branch of Dwarvism, practiced by dwarves on Kobre Continent and Lumina Continent. Of the three doctrines, the Coal Doctrine is the most inward-focused — its followers seek peace, self-cultivation, and quiet contribution rather than external glory.

docs.title: Philosophy
docs.text:
The Coal Doctrine teaches that a life well-lived is like a piece of coal: unremarkable to look at, buried in darkness, yet capable of producing warmth and light for others without fanfare. Coal dwarves do not seek recognition. They seek to be useful — to burn steadily, to illuminate without being seen, to leave the world warmer than they found it.

This philosophy manifests in every aspect of life: - Work is done in silence. The greatest craftsmen do not sign their work. - Wealth is shared, not hoarded. Coal dwarves practice communal resource distribution — the strong support the weak. - Conflict is avoided, not sought. The Coal Doctrine teaches that most battles are ego dressed as honor. True strength is the discipline to walk away.

docs.title: Regions
docs.text:
• Kobre Continent — the primary stronghold. Nations: Coalsteel Kingdom (the spiritual heart), Diamonds Kingdom, Cobal Kingdom, Purple Coast.
  • Lumina Continent — scattered dwarven communities follow the Coal Doctrine.

docs.title: Challenge: The Homunculi
docs.text: The Coal Doctrine's commitment to peace has been severely tested by the arrival of the Homunculi on Kobre. The Homunculi — created beings with their own agenda — have disrupted the quiet order Coal dwarves cultivated for millennia. The doctrine's pacifism, once a strength, now threatens to become a vulnerability. Younger Coal dwarves increasingly question whether "burning peacefully in the dark" means allowing others to extinguish the flame entirely.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Silent craft — Coal dwarves work without speaking. The sound of hammer on anvil is the only prayer.
  • Communal hearths — every settlement centers on a great hearth where coal burns perpetually. No family eats alone.
  • Ancestor coal — deceased dwarves are cremated, and a piece of coal from their pyre is added to the family hearth. The ancestor's warmth joins the community's warmth.
  • Meditation mining — mining is treated as a meditative act. The rhythm of pick against stone is a form of prayer.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Coal Doctrine ] ├── Parent Faith: Dwarvism ├── Venerates: Coal ├── Motto: "Burn peacefully in the dark to enlighten the world" ├── Philosophy: Peace, self-cultivation, quiet service, communal living ├── Primary Region: Kobre Continent — Coalsteel Kingdom, Diamonds Kingdom, Cobal Kingdom, Purple Coast ├── Secondary Region: Lumina Continent ├── Challenge: Homunculi Kingdom — disrupting the peace ├── Practices: Silent craft, communal hearths, ancestor coal, meditation mining ├── Sibling Doctrines: Diamond Doctrine, Emerald Doctrine └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: ⚔️ Cubra Faith
docs.text:
"The way needs no ornament. It needs walking."

Cubra Faith is the plain Kirivs-bin as practiced by the Cubra Tribe — the demon tribe on Yak Island southwest of Estran and below the Asatru-controlled territory, across the sea from the Koebi Tribe. Where every other Demon Continent and Yak Island people has accented the bin into a sect, the Cubra have not. Their faith is Kirivs-bin without addition, without priesthood, without shrine — the control sample that proves the bin still walks as it was.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
The Cubra demons are of the main demon race — like the Asatru Empire and Maomodor Kingdom — and their island settlement dates to the general demon dispersal after the Demonic War. Unlike the Koebi (green, meditative), the Malgardians (purple, lineage-pure), or the Mountain Tribe diablos (winged, nocturnal), the Cubra crossed no distinctive biological or historical threshold that demanded a new theology.

When the demon diaspora produced Malgardism, Padamalgardism, Farsightism, Tolumin, Demonism, and Gedarism's outright rejection, Cubra elders are recorded as having listened politely and then said: "We have a way. It still works."

There is no prophet, no date, no text. Cubra Faith is Kirivs-bin, and Kirivs-bin predates Kirivis himself, stretching to the earliest demon tribes of Age 2.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Legends are the scripture — Cubra young learn the stories of Kirivis and the ancient warrior-kings as Asatru young do: not as gods but as examples to emulate.
  • Kirivis is the last great legend — the Demon King who saw the Hybrian conspiracy, waged the 45-year war (599–554 BGD), and died revealing the truth. His sacrifice is the highest lesson; Cubra add no other figure.
  • Action is prayer — every battle, craft, self-improvement, fishing run between islands is a step on the path. There are no Cubra temples, no priests, no sacred texts beyond the legends themselves.
  • Honor is earned, not inherited — worth is what you have done, not who your parents were. Cubra honor duels follow the plain Asatru form: challenge as recognition of worth, resolution by duel ideally to first blood.
  • Comfort is the enemy — Cubra live simply. Their island longhouses are sturdy but unadorned; surplus is not hoarded. Asceticism is clarity.
  • No sectarian claim — the Cubra explicitly deny that plainness is superiority. "We are not the true bin because we added nothing. We are simply the bin that stayed still while others walked ahead. They may be further along. We keep the path behind them clear."

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Legend-study (plain) — communal telling around hearths, without the Tita Commentary or the Ledger of the Far Sight
  • Honor duels (plain) — standard demonic form; no wooden staves, no wargames, no night-shift mediation — steel, respect, yield
  • Ascetic living — no palaces, no hoarded wealth
  • Family lineage — dying without passing knowledge to the next generation is dying incompletely; Cubra households keep lineage recitation but without Malgardist purification rites
  • Hospitality to sects — Cubra settlements are known as neutral ground where Malgardist priests, Kutra Ledger-keepers, Koebi masons, and Mountain Demonists can meet without conceding precedence, precisely because the hosts claim no sectarian ground to cede

docs.title: Relation to Kirivs-bin
docs.text:
Identity — not a sect.

Cubra Faith is Kirivs-bin under another name, the way a still pond is the same water as a river. Maomodor Kingdom shares this plain adherence on a far larger scale; together Cubra and Maomodor are the Demon's Continent's reminder that the bin does not require elaboration to survive.

  • The Asatru Empire recognizes Cubra practice as fully orthodox bin (and occasionally sends young Asatru officers to Cubra for "plain bin training")
  • Sectarian theologians cite Cubra precisely because it cannot be accused of sectional bias: when Malgardists and Padamalgardists dispute shore-priest ordination, they agree to let a Cubra elder judge — and do
  • Cubra demons can and do walk the Demonist night market in the Mountain Tribe or stand vigil on the Bloodcoast without theological friction: the plain bin is compatible with all its sects, because it contains them all potentially

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Cubra Tribe — universal among Yak Island demons; estimated ~95%+ plain bin observance, remainder syncretic but not separately organized
  • Exemplary: Maomodor Kingdom — the much larger plain-bin polity on the mainland (see below) recognizes Cubra as kin; the two exchange envoys styled "keepers of the same way in different weather"
  • Diplomatic: Yak Island's required neutral ground — every island faith trusts Cubra to host without preaching
  • Continental mirror: Asatru scholars use Cubra and Maomodor together to map what bin looks like without local accent — the baseline against which every sect's addition becomes visible

docs.title: Maomodor — the larger plain bin
docs.text:
The Maomodor Kingdom (southwest of Blazeyard, below the Kutra Tribe) is the Demon Continent's other great plain-bin nation — and its largest by population. Like Cubra, Maomodor is of the main demon race but, distinctively, highly multi-racial: its "shared demonic nationality" means populations of every type walk freely everywhere, and many races live permanently within its borders.

Maomodor's plain adherence is therefore more politically consequential than Cubra's: it demonstrates that the bin need not be tribal to be orthodox. Maomodor demons study the same legends, fight the same honor duels, practice the same asceticism — and extend them casually to whichever neighbor shares the street, whatever their species.

See: Kirivs-bin, Maomodor Kingdom

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
[ Cubra Faith ] ├── Identity: Plain Kirivs-bin — no addition, no sect marker ├── Name: Called "Cubra Faith" only by outsiders; Cubra call it simply bin ├── Nations: Cubra Tribe (Yak Island, majority, universal); kin to Maomodor Kingdom (mainland, larger plain-bin polity) ├── Species: Demons (main race) — same as Asatru Empire and Maomodor Kingdom ├── Region: Demon Continent — Yak Island, southwest of Estran, across sea from Koebi Tribe ├── Founded: No founding — predates Kirivis; Age 2 origins as warrior ethic ├── Doctrine: Same as Kirivs-bin — legends are scripture, Kirivis last great legend, action is prayer, honor earned, comfort despised, no temples/priests/texts ├── Distinction: Only Demon Continent religion without a sectarian thesis; neutral ground for all sects ├── Role: Yak Island diplomatic host; continental baseline for measuring sectarian additions └── Part Of: Ge'or — Demon Continent

[ Maomodor Kirivs-bin ] ├── Nation: Maomodor Kingdom — below Kutra Tribe, southwest of Blazeyard ├── Species: Demons primary + highly multi-racial demonic nationality (all races welcome) ├── Faith: Plain Kirivs-bin — majority, universal in intent ├── Significance: Proves plain bin scales to a large, cosmopolitan kingdom without sectarian adaptation └── Part Of: Ge'or — Demon Continent

docs.title: Cult of Cleton
docs.text: The state religion of the Moonfang Dominion on Moon Wolf Island. A death cult centered on Cleton, the Wolf God, who demands child sacrifices to sustain the world's order.

docs.title: Doctrine
docs.text:
Cleton is the god of the frozen north, embodied in the wolf-shaped island itself. The faithful believe the outside world is damned, that isolation is salvation, and that suffering purifies the soul. Poverty is holy. Wealth and ambition are sins against the Wolf God's design.

The central ritual is the annual sacrifice. Each year, the cult selects a group of children — always the prettiest — and sends them to Cleton Island, a barren rock caught between the two peninsulas that form Moon Wolf Island's wolf-shaped mouth. The island appears to be devouring its prey. Beauty, in the cult's theology, is the mark of Cleton's hunger.

None return from the sacrifices. The faithful consider this an honor.

docs.title: Sacred Animals
docs.text: Wargs — massive wolf-like predators native to the island — are treated as divine messengers. They roam freely near settlements. Killing a warg is punishable by death. The cult does not tame them; it coexists with them through fear dressed as reverence.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
The cult's hierarchy is absolute. The order's priests interpret Cleton's will. Dissent is heresy. Punishment is public and brutal. Children work from the moment they can walk — idleness is the first step toward damnation. Beatings are routine. The faithful watch in silence, grateful it is not them.

To question the order is to question Cleton. To question Cleton is to be fed to him.

docs.title: Opposition
docs.text: The Molten Archipelago, south of Moon Wolf Island, hosts Karabar's refugee bases — a destination for those who flee the cult. Escape is rare and dangerous, and those who reach the bases discover they have traded one cage for another: forced labor for wages that barely keep them alive.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Moonfang Dominion
  • Island: Moon Wolf Island, Cleton Island
  • Sacred animals: Wargs
  • Deity: Cleton, the Wolf God
  • Rival/refuge: Karabar (Molten Archipelago)

docs.title: 🐉 Daicrodism
docs.text:
"We were the world's wound. Now we are its silence."

Daicrodism is the religion of the civilized Dragons — the pursuit of a peaceful, prosperous life for all beings of the world.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Daicrodism is an evolution from Diocronism, the old dragon religion of war and conquest. The death wars of the Dragon Tyranny — twelve clans ruling ninety percent of the world, nearly ending life on Ge'or — left the surviving dragons deeply regretful. From that regret, the faith was reborn.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Peace and prosperity for all beings of the world is the goal of dragon-kind.
  • Dragons are a source of pain and misery for the world — the faith teaches that their own kind nearly destroyed life on Ge'or.
  • Atonement through seclusion — believing themselves a wound upon the world, the civilized dragons ended up secluding themselves in Kramsadar and barely leave.
  • Meditative lives — since the death wars, dragons live quiet, contemplative, secluded lives there.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Kramsadar — the last civilized dragon nation.
  • Exception: rogue dragons — the uncivilized ones — do not follow the faith; wild dragons remain beasts.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Daicrodism ] ├── Evolved From: Diocronism ├── Nations: Kramsadar ├── Species: Dragons ├── Doctrine: Peace and prosperity for all beings; dragon-kind as the world's wound ├── Practice: Seclusion, meditation, atonement └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🦇 Demonism
docs.text:
"Day belongs to those who take. Night belongs to those who endure."

Demonism is the faith of the Diablos — winged, nocturnal humanoids of the Mountain Tribe on Yak Island east of the Demon Continent mainland. Where most demon faiths are variations of Kirivs-bin, Demonism is the sharpest break: it worships demon-ness itself as a night-vocation — to be the winged watchers who keep the world honest while the day-species sleep.

The name Demonism is a reclaimed slander. Erisdar missionaries once called the Diablos "demons of the night" as an insult; the Diablos kept the word and made it a title.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Diablos are strictly nocturnal — sleeping through daylight in cliff-face settlements accessible only by flight, convening their Night Council only after moonrise. For millennia they had no theology beyond moon-tracking (births, marriages, wars timed to lunar conjunctions) and a quiet pride in endurance.

Demonism crystallized after sustained contact with the Asatru Empire's Knight's Thorn garrisons and Estran traders, who brought tales of Kirivis and called the Diablos "not truly demonic." The Diablos' answer, codified around ~400 BGD by Night Council elder Shara Half-Moon, was to claim the word more fiercely than their critics used it: if demon means one who tests, endures, and watches in darkness, then Diablos are the truest demons on Ge'or.

Shara's Moon Letters — twelve short admonitions copied onto night-silk — remain the faith's only quasi-scripture.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Night is not the absence of day — it is its judge — Demonism teaches that daylight is for claiming, building, and taking; night is for accounting. The Diablos' vocation is to remain awake while others sleep and to remember what daylight forgets.
  • Flight is witness — wings are not transport but testimony. A winged being who can see the island entire from above and says nothing is complicit; a winged being who sees and later speaks at the Night Council has done holy work.
  • The moon is clock, not god — Diablos track Maenar and Amelia with religious precision, but they do not worship the moons. The moons are the impartial timekeepers who prove that a promise made at waxing can be measured at waning. Demonism is lunar-accurate but not lunar-devotional — a distinction Moongar cults never grasp.
  • Sunlight wounds, but does not refute — direct sun causes Diablos physical discomfort and skin damage on prolonged exposure. Demonism reads this not as curse but as calling: they are shaped for the watch others cannot keep.
  • Kirivis as night-revealer — Demonist readings of Kirivs-bin foreground Kirivis's act of seeing what no one else would see — in Demonist shorthand, "the demon who stayed awake." They remain within the bin communion while insisting the bin has forgotten its own night-side.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Night Council liturgy — governance and worship are the same act. The council convenes only after moonrise; no decision is valid if made in daylight. Proceedings open with a wing-silence (all present extend wings and hold still until the wind is the only sound) and close with a recitation of Shara's twelve letters.
  • Moon-silver and shadow-silk offering — Diablos trade moon-silver ore and shadow-silk (spun from cave-dwelling moths) and night-blooming herbs. The first ingot of a new vein and the first bolt of a silk season are not sold but hung on the cliff-face as night-decor — visible only to those who fly after dark.
  • Thermal gliding prayer — sustained flight is prayer when flown without cargo or errand — purely to patrol, observe, and later report. A Diablos who flies an empty circuit of Yak Island and returns with "nothing to report" is praised for confirming stillness.
  • Nocturnal hospitality — Diablos maintain intermediary outposts lit only by moon-silver lanterns where Estran and Asatru traders can meet them at dusk or dawn. To force a Diablos to meet at noon is an insult in Demonist terms; to meet them at midnight is to honor their vocation.
  • Sound-dampening chant — Diablos mages specialize in shadow and sound-dampening magic; their low, layered humming before a Night Council session is both practical (hushing echoes in the cliff halls) and sacramental.

docs.title: Relation to Kirivs-bin and Other Faiths
docs.text:
Demonism claims Kirivs-bin lineage while refusing to be a mere sect. Asatru theologians classify it as "the nocturnal bin" — a legitimate but willfully contrarian branch. Demonists accept the classification the way they accepted the name: with a thin smile that does not confirm anything.

Relations are:

  • Warmest with Estran (High Catmen) — whose elective cunning and night-savvy trading complements Diablo patrol rhythms
  • Respectful but strained with Asatru — which admires Diablo discipline while finding their refusal to normalize daylight commerce inconvenient
  • Indifferent to Erisdar missionary faiths — Demonism considers solar triumphalism a category error

There is no Demonist priesthood beyond the Night Council elders; no temple beyond the cliff-face itself. In that austerity Demonism is truer to Kirivs-bin than many Asatru think.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Mountain Tribe — universal among Diablos; faith, governance, and daily schedule are one thing
  • Minority: small Diablos enclaves and night-workers in Asatru-controlled territory on Yak Island and the Demon mainland foothills
  • Viewed across the Demon Continent as the "demons who mean it" — Asatru soldiers joke that you can set your watch by a Diablos patrol, and that the joke is theology
  • The faith's island isolation means it rarely proselytizes; those who want to understand it must be willing to stay up all night

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Demonism ] ├── Name: Demonism — reclaimed exonym ("demons of the night" → title) ├── First Teacher: Shara Half-Moon — Moon Letters (~400 BGD) ├── Species: Diablos — winged humanoids, 3–4m bat-wings, nocturnal, moon-precise ├── Nations: Mountain Tribe (Yak Island, east of Demon mainland); also Asatru-controlled territory ├── Moons: Maenar + Amelia — tracked as clocks, not worshipped ├── Type: Nocturnal bin-adjacent faith — claims Kirivs-bin lineage, insists on night-vocation distinctness ├── Practices: Night Council, wing-silence, thermal gliding patrol, moon-silver offering, sound-dampening chant ├── Economy: Moon-silver ore, shadow-silk, night-blooming herbs trade via dusk/dawn outposts └── Part Of: Ge'or — Demon Continent / Yak Island

docs.title: 💎 Diamond Doctrine
docs.text:
"Life is like a diamond — it must shine."

The Diamond Doctrine is the eastern branch of Dwarvism, practiced by dwarves in East Erisdar, parts of North Erisdar, and wherever eastern dwarven traders have spread. Of the three doctrines, the Diamond Doctrine is the most outward-facing — its followers believe that wealth and commerce are not merely permissible but sacred. To grow rich is to honor the ancestors. To shine is to fulfill one's purpose.

docs.title: Philosophy
docs.text:
The Diamond Doctrine teaches that a life well-lived is visible. Diamonds do not hide in the dark — they catch the light and throw it back, dazzling everyone who sees them. Diamond dwarves seek prosperity, commerce, and growth. They are the merchant princes of dwarven civilization, the ones who build trade empires that span continents.

This philosophy manifests in every aspect of life: - Wealth is virtue. Poverty is not holy — it is failure. A dwarf who dies rich has proven their worth. - Commerce is sacred. Every trade is a covenant. A deal made in good faith is as binding as an oath of blood. - Visibility is honor. Diamond dwarves build grand halls, wear fine jewelry, and celebrate publicly. To be seen succeeding is to inspire others to succeed.

docs.title: Regions
docs.text:
• East Erisdar — Dwarvengor is the spiritual and commercial heart of the Diamond Doctrine.
  • North Erisdar — scattered communities and trade posts follow the Diamond path.
  • Eastern trade routes — Diamond dwarves are the most widely traveled of all dwarven peoples, establishing trading posts wherever commerce flows.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Trade fairs — seasonal gatherings where Diamond dwarves from across the continent meet to exchange goods, stories, and marriage proposals. The largest fair, held at Dwarvengor, draws merchants from as far as Merratodoni.
  • Wealth offerings — a portion of every successful trade is dedicated to the ancestors, deposited in temple vaults.
  • Public accounting — Diamond dwarves keep meticulous ledgers. At death, a dwarf's books are audited by the community. A clean ledger is a ticket to the ancestors' hall.
  • Gem-cutting — the highest art form. A perfectly cut diamond is considered the ultimate offering.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Diamond Doctrine ] ├── Parent Faith: Dwarvism ├── Venerates: Diamonds ├── Motto: "Life is like a diamond — it must shine" ├── Philosophy: Commerce, wealth, growth, visibility, public achievement ├── Primary Region: East Erisdar — Dwarvengor ├── Secondary Region: North Erisdar, eastern trade routes ├── Practices: Trade fairs, wealth offerings, public accounting, gem-cutting ├── Sibling Doctrines: Coal Doctrine, Emerald Doctrine └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: ⚔️ Diocronism
docs.text:
"Perfect the race. Conquer every corner."

Diocronism was the old religion of the Dragons — a faith of war and conquest, devoted to perfecting the dragon race so it could conquer all the corners of the world.

docs.title: History
docs.text: Diocronism ruled dragon-kind through the Dragon Tyranny (6,999–5,500 BGD), when twelve clans controlled ninety percent of the known land. Its doctrine drove the death wars that nearly ended life on Ge'or — the wars that shattered dragon civilization itself.

docs.title: The Turning
docs.text: The dragons became deeply regretful of the death wars. Diocronism was abandoned, and from its ashes the dragons evolved their new faith — Daicrodism — pursuing peace and prosperity for all beings. Since then, civilized dragons live meditative, secluded lives in Kramsadar, with the only exception being rogue dragons — the uncivilized ones.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Diocronism ] ├── Succeeded By: Daicrodism ├── Era: Age 4 — Dragon Tyranny ├── Species: Dragons ├── Doctrine: War, conquest, perfection of the dragon race ├── Result: The death wars — near-extinction of life on Ge'or └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🌊 Dresludo — God of the Seas
docs.text:
"The sea sent us here to learn to leave it."

Dresludo is the god of the seas and the faith of Karabar — the independent island nation on Karabar Island in the western Wolf Ocean.

The faithful believe Dresludo sent them to the island of Karabar as a penitence for their sins — and that they need to achieve a gnosis state to be able to be freed from the suffering of earth.

docs.title: Tenets
docs.text:
• Dresludo as Judge and Sea — Dresludo is not kindly. He is the sea itself — vast, indifferent, and just. He exiled the Karabari to Karabar Island not as a gift but as penitence.
  • Karabar as Purgatory — the island is the penance. To live on Karabar Island — between the death cult of Moonfang Dominion to the north and the labor-exploitation of the Molten Archipelago refugee bases to the northeast — is to atone.
  • Gnosis as Liberation — suffering is not to be endured but transcended. Through ascetic practice, meditation, and sea-rites, the faithful seek gnosis — a state of direct knowledge of Dresludo that frees them from the suffering of earth. Only with gnosis can the penitent leave Karabar — spiritually, and in the most radical reading, physically.

docs.title: Followers
docs.text:
• Karabar (Karabar Island, western Wolf Ocean) — the island nation, sole canonical follower. Every Karabari is raised in Dresludo.
  • Small diaspora of Karabari sailors carry Dresludo shrines (a bowl of seawater) aboard ship.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Daily seawater ablutions at dawn.
  • Silent meditation facing the Wolf Ocean.
  • Pilgrimages to the eastern shore to watch the Molten Archipelago on the horizon — a reminder that penitence is not unique to Karabar.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Karabar (Karabar Island)
  • Island: Karabar Island
  • Deity: Dresludo (god of the seas)
  • Related: Moonfang Dominion (north), Molten Archipelago (northeast), Wolf Ocean, Crab Union (south)

docs.title: ⛏️ Dwarvism
docs.text:
"The stone remembers. We are the stone."

Dwarvism is the ancestral religion of all Dwarves across Ge'or. Remarkably consistent across continents — even dwarves separated by vast oceans share the same core beliefs. The faith is divided into three doctrinal branches, each venerating a different sacred mineral, each reflecting a different answer to the same question: what is a life well-lived?

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Dwarvism emerged during the Dwarf Era (5,499–4,500 BGD), when dwarven megacities powered by Romanium spread across the world. The faith's unified core — ancestor veneration, the sacredness of the deep earth, the belief that craftsmanship is prayer — was established during this golden age. When Romanium ran out and the dwarven economy collapsed, the faith fractured into three regional doctrines, each adapting to its new circumstances.

No dwarven prophet founded Dwarvism. It emerged from the mines themselves — from generations of dwarves living and dying in the stone, passing down their craft and their names.

docs.title: Core Beliefs (All Doctrines)
docs.text:
• Ancestors live in the stone — the dead are interred in carved tombs within mountains. Their spirits remain, watching over their descendants.
  • Craftsmanship is worship — every hammer strike on an anvil is a prayer. Perfection in craft is the closest a dwarf comes to the divine.
  • The deep earth is sacred — the deeper you dig, the closer you are to the ancestors who came before. Surface-dwellers live cut off from this connection.

docs.title: Coal Doctrine (Southern)
docs.text: Aspect Detail Venerates Coal File Coal Doctrine Motto "Life should be treated as coal — burn peacefully in the dark to enlighten the world." Philosophy Peaceful, inward-focused. Self-cultivation over external ambition. Communal living. Silent craft. Regions Kobre Continent (Coalsteel Kingdom, Diamonds Kingdom, Cobal Kingdom, Purple Coast), Lumina Continent Challenge The arrival of the Homunculi on Kobre has disrupted the Coal Doctrine's peaceful isolation

docs.title: Diamond Doctrine (Eastern)
docs.text: Aspect Detail Venerates Diamonds File Diamond Doctrine Motto "Life is like a diamond — it must shine." Philosophy Commerce, wealth, growth. Hoarding richness and doing business. Public achievement. Regions East Erisdar (Dwarvengor), parts of North Erisdar, dwarven traders across eastern territories Character The merchant dwarves. The ones who build trade empires.

docs.title: Emerald Doctrine (Western)
docs.text: Aspect Detail Venerates Emeralds File Emerald Doctrine Motto "Life must be like emeralds — elegant." Philosophy Mastery of craft, efficiency, engineering excellence. Perfection in design. Legacy through structures that outlast empires. Regions West Erisdar, Central Erisdar, North Erisdar, western continents and islands Character The engineer dwarves. The ones who build things that last millennia.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Ancestor tombs — carved into mountain faces, aligned to sacred minerals.
  • Craft-prayer — silent devotion while working at the forge or mine.
  • Doctrinal festivals — Coal dwarves hold quiet meditation vigils; Diamond dwarves hold trade fairs; Emerald dwarves hold engineering competitions.
  • Ancestor recitation — during Maenar's dark phase, dwarves speak the names of their dead.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Universal among all Dwarves worldwide — from Dwarvengor in East Erisdar to Coalsteel Kingdom on Kobre to dwarven communities in Lumina and beyond.
  • One of the few faiths that crosses oceans and continents without central organization.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Dwarvism ] ├── Species: Dwarves ├── Three Doctrines: Coal (Southern), Diamond (Eastern), Emerald (Western) ├── Southern Nations: Coalsteel Kingdom, Diamonds Kingdom, Cobal Kingdom, Purple Coast (Kobre Continent), Lumina Continent ├── Eastern Nations: Dwarvengor (East Erisdar), North Erisdar ├── Western Nations: West Erisdar, Central Erisdar, western islands ├── Sacred Minerals: Coal, Diamonds, Emeralds ├── Golden Age: Dwarf Era └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🌿 Elven Faith
docs.text:
"The forest does not pray. It listens."

The Elven Faith is the nature religion of the elfic peoples — the cults of nature and the elven gods. It is the normal, traditional elfic religion, practiced by Elvennrin and Elvenkrad alike.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• The natural world is sacred — forests, rivers, mountains, and the cycle of seasons carry divinity.
  • The elven gods are tied to nature itself, not to any single institution.
  • Unlike the Erisian cult or the Alegorian faith, the Elven Faith makes no claim to universality — it belongs to the elves, and the elves belong to it.

docs.title: Under Persecution
docs.text:
• Elvennrin follows the Elven Faith even though it is a repressed-but-accepted country surrounded by fanatical Erisians.
  • Elvenkrad is an elfic nation that follows the nature religion, but is effectively a puppet of the Erisian Empire — forced to concede resources and accept unfair trades.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Elven Faith ] ├── Species: Elves ├── Nations: Elvennrin, Elvenkrad ├── Character: Nature cults, elven gods, traditional ├── Under: Erisian pressure — but never abandoned └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: ✨ Emerald Doctrine
docs.text:
"Life must be like emeralds — elegant."

The Emerald Doctrine is the western branch of Dwarvism, practiced by dwarves in West Erisdar, Central Erisdar, North Erisdar, and across the western continents and islands. Of the three doctrines, the Emerald Doctrine is the most exacting — its followers pursue mastery of craft, efficiency of design, and engineering excellence above all else. The engineer dwarves.

docs.title: Philosophy
docs.text:
The Emerald Doctrine teaches that a life well-lived is beautiful — not in decoration but in perfection. An emerald does not need to shine like a diamond or burn like coal. It simply is — flawless, balanced, complete. Emerald dwarves seek to make things that are perfect in their function, elegant in their design, and enduring beyond their makers.

This philosophy manifests in every aspect of life: - Craftsmanship is the highest prayer. Every joint, every gear, every stone is an offering. Sloppy work is sacrilege. - Efficiency is elegance. Waste is ugliness. The most beautiful machine is the one with nothing unnecessary. - Legacy is built, not spoken. Emerald dwarves do not boast. They let their work speak — bridges that stand for millennia, tunnels that never collapse, mechanisms that still turn after empires have fallen.

docs.title: Regions
docs.text:
• West Erisdar — the industrial heartland of the Emerald Doctrine.
  • Central Erisdar — significant communities in and around the Erisian Empire.
  • North Erisdar — scattered strongholds.
  • Western continents and islands — wherever dwarves settled west of Erisdar, the Emerald Doctrine followed.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Mastery trials — dwarves seeking the title of master must produce a work that is judged by a council of elders. The work must be both functional and beautiful. One flaw is a lifetime of shame.
  • Engineering competitions — public contests where teams race to design and build solutions to complex problems. The winners' designs are preserved in temple archives.
  • Tool consecration — a dwarf's tools are blessed at their coming-of-age and buried with them at death.
  • Bridge-building as pilgrimage — Emerald dwarves travel to remote communities to build bridges, aqueducts, and fortifications without payment. The work itself is the reward.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Emerald Doctrine ] ├── Parent Faith: Dwarvism ├── Venerates: Emeralds ├── Motto: "Life must be like emeralds — elegant" ├── Philosophy: Mastery, efficiency, engineering, perfection, legacy through craft ├── Primary Region: West Erisdar ├── Secondary Region: Central Erisdar, North Erisdar, western continents and islands ├── Practices: Mastery trials, engineering competitions, tool consecration, bridge-building pilgrimage ├── Sibling Doctrines: Coal Doctrine, Diamond Doctrine └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🦉 Farsightism
docs.text:
"See far. Speak little. Strike only when the river is still."

Farsightism is the faith of the Kachev — the humanoid owls of the Kutra Tribe (endonym Kachev, exonym Kutra/Owlkin). It is a contemplative predator's religion: patience as sacrament, distance as clarity, and the silent glide as prayer. Farsightism teaches that truth is not argued toward — it is seen from a height that others cannot reach, and then carried down without a sound.

The name Farsightism is the Common translation; the Kachev call it Var-Kael — "the sight that waits."

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Kachev are amphibious: gill-slits along the ribs let them breathe water, lungs let them breathe air, and silent-structured feathers let them fly without a whisper. Their villages are built across a river — sleeping chambers submerged below, communal halls above. This dual life produced a dual chieftaincy (one for the river-below, one for the sky-above, ruling only by consensus) and, from it, Farsightism.

The first Var-Kael teaching is attributed to Keval the Still, a below-chief who refused to choose sides during a Malgardian Tribe–Emberalden border dispute and instead perched for three nights on a river stone without eating, watching the current. On the fourth morning he is said to have described, without having moved, the exact position of every war-band on both banks. The story became the faith's proof: to be still long enough and high enough is to see.

Formally codified around ~1200–900 BGD, as the Kachev standardized their talon-sign language (children learn to sign before they learn to speak) and their river-trade in rare river-gems.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Distance clarifies — nearness distorts. A Kachev owl who perches too close to prey sees only feathers; from a full glide-height they see the whole pattern of the chase. Moral questions are approached the same way: withdraw, ascend, then decide.
  • Silence is not absence — Kutra culture values silence; Farsightism makes it doctrine. Speech is reserved for declaration; the rest is signed with talons, wing-flicks, and eye-angle. To speak aloud without need is to ripple the water you are trying to read.
  • River and sky are one motion — the below-chief and sky-chief must concur because water and air are the same medium seen from different densities. Farsightism rejects hard binaries: amphibiousness is not compromise — it is the superior perch.
  • The far sight is literal and oracular — Kachev eyes are adapted for underwater and low-light vision across great distances. Farsightism teaches that this biology is a covenant: those who can see far must remember far — keeping the tribe's river-maps, star-charts, and lineage not in books but in memorized visual recitation.
  • Flight as absolution — a silent glide at dusk over still water, with no intent to hunt, is the highest Kachev prayer. Predation is necessary and respected, but flight without hunger is worship.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Dawn-perch and dusk-glide — every Kachev keeps a personal perch above the river where they sit before hunting and a glide-route flown empty-handed at dusk. Missing either without cause is a matter for gentle correction by elders.
  • Dual-consensus rite — no major decision (war, dam-building, trade treaty) is valid until both chieftains have separately overnighted with the question — one submerged, one perched — and then signed agreement before the tribe without spoken words.
  • River-gem offering — the tribe's economy is ferrying goods along Demon Continent waterways for rare river-gems found only in Kutra territory. The finest stone of each season is not sold but dropped back into the deepest channel as thanks — a practice Asatru traders find exasperating and sacred in equal measure.
  • Sign-canon — Kachev sacred history is not written but signed. Elders perform the "long sign" — an unbroken hour of talon-signing that recites the tribe's entire migration from the highlands to the river. Young Kachev memorize it visually before they are allowed to speak in council.
  • Owl-watch mediation — disputes are brought before a perched elder who listens to both spoken cases in silence, then delivers a single signed judgment. Appeals are not made by argument but by requesting the elder spend another night on the perch.

docs.title: Relation to Other Faiths
docs.text:
Farsightism is non-creedal and non-competitive. It does not deny Kirivs-bin, Malgardism, or Zebekyo — many Kachev traders who work with the Maomodor Kingdom and Asatru Empire pay quiet respect to the bin and admire Zebekyo's hunter precision. In return, demons value Kachev as the continent's best scouts and impartial mediators precisely because Farsightism makes them reluctant to take sides.

Kachev priests are not a caste; any elder who has kept the dawn-perch without lapse for a full season may be asked to give sign-judgment. The Titians revere this discipline and exchange vision-techniques with Kachev sign-elders in rare interfaith meetings.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Kutra Tribe — universal among Kachev; the faith and the people are inseparable (older texts still say "Kutra (Owlkin)" for the species)
  • Minority: river-traders and ferry-clans of neighboring Malgardian Tribe and Blazeyard foothills who have adopted Kachev dawn-perch as a personal practice
  • The Asatru Empire maintains its only trade embassy in the Kutra Tribe that operates entirely in signed Kachev for formal negotiation — a diplomatic quirk that visiting envoys train months to perform
  • Feared mildly by smugglers: a silent Kachev ferry-owl overhead sees far more than customs officers do

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Farsightism ] ├── Name: Farsightism (Common) / Var-Kael — "the sight that waits" (Kachev) ├── Species: Kachev — humanoid owls, amphibious (gills + lungs), silent flight, also called Kutra/Owlkin ├── Nations: Kutra Tribe — river-crossing amphibious villages (below + above) ├── Region: Demon Continent — below Malgardian Tribe/Emberalden, west of Blazeyard, north of Maomodor Kingdom ├── Founded: First teacher Keval the Still (~1200–900 BGD); codified with sign-language standardization ├── Central Tenet: Distance clarifies; silence is not absence; river and sky are one motion ├── Governance Mirror: Dual chieftains (river-below + sky-above, consensus-only) ├── Practices: Dawn-perch, dusk-glide, dual-consensus rite, river-gem offering, sign-canon, owl-watch mediation ├── Character: Contemplative predator's religion — patience as sacrament, flight as prayer └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🪨 Gedarism
docs.text:
"Stone is the bone. Coil is the muscle. Together they hold."

Gedarism is the shared faith of Xobkua (Giants) and Zakarutia (Snake People) — two species that could not be more different in body, bound by one theology on the southern Demon Continent. Giants are 3-meter territorial builders; snakes are matriarchal, venomous, river-and-desert tacticians. Gedarism teaches that both are organs of the same body: Gedar, the World-Pillar that coils.

The name Gedar is the Giants' word for the stone that remembers being squeezed, and the snakes' word for the squeeze that remembers stone.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Gedarism predates the snake–giant split in memory. Xobkua's island is one-quarter the size of the Demon Continent — so massive it is considered a continuation of the continent — and Zakarutia's south-coast plains face it across a narrow sea. Long before queens and clan longhouses, both peoples told the same story when they met to trade: a great pillar held the Demon Continent up while a great serpent coiled it so it would not wander.

By Age 6, the story had formalized into a dual priesthood:

  • Giant Stone-Singers — clan elders who vibrate longhouse beams with deep-toned chanting until the wood hums. They claim the tone proves Gedar's bone is still load-bearing.
  • Snake Coil-Mothers — Zakarutian matriarchs who perform the coil-dance, wrapping and unwrapping dyed silk around a central basalt pillar to show how pressure creates strength.

The faith has no single founder. Its "prophet" is the Strait itself — the sea between Xobkua and Zakarutia, which both peoples pilgrimage to drink from (Giants wading, snakes undulating) on the same tide-day each year.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Gedar is pillar and coil at once — not two gods, but one god seen from two ends. Giants emphasize the pillar (endurance, holding, architectural truth). Snakes emphasize the coil (pressure, patience, constriction). Orthodoxy insists neither is complete alone; heresy is choosing one half.
  • The world is held, not made — unlike creation faiths (Maomism, Dwarvism), Gedarism does not claim Gedar made Ge'or. It claims Gedar keeps it from drifting — a maintenance theology. Neglect, not rebellion, is the sin.
  • Territory is trust — Giant territoriality (defending Xobkua fiercely, seeking no conquest) and Zakarutian matriarchal patience (the old Queen endlessly rebuilding her archaic fleet to retake lost Xikxia) are both taught as Gedarist virtues: hold what is yours with absolute fidelity; do not grasp what is not.
  • Sibbism alongside, not against — Zakarutia's majority faith is Sibbism (Snake Goddess + 24 demigod sons at the world's corners). Gedarism does not replace Sibbism; it undergirds it. In Zakarutian theology, the Snake Goddess is Gedar seen from the coil-side; in Xobkuan shrugs, "your goddess is our pillar's wife, that is fine." The tie is diplomatic as much as doctrinal — it is why Xobkua trades with Zakarutia when all others keep their distance, and why Asatru respects both from across the sea.
  • No conquest, no conversion — Gedarism has no missionary impulse. A Giant clan longhouse and a Zakarutian matriarch's court are both complete Gedarist worship without needing to agree on detail. The Strait pilgrimage is the only required observance, and even it may be performed by proxy.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Strait Pilgrimage (The Holding Day) — on the first spring tide after Maenar's dark phase, delegations from both nations wade/drink at the narrow water. Giants carry a quarried stone; snakes carry a silk coil; they exchange them at mid-strait and carry the other's token home. To drop the token before reaching shore is a grave omen.
  • Stone-Singing — Giant longhouses (30–50 Giants, timber beams weighing tons) are blessed by singing until the frame resonates. A longhouse that sings cleanly is Gedar-approved; one that rattles must be rebuilt.
  • Coil-Dance and Fleet-Blessing — before the Zakarutian fleet sails (the Queen's long-prepared reconquest of Xikxia, lost 589 AGD), Coil-Mothers dance the coil around the basalt pillar in the palace. The fleet's archaism is itself a Gedarist point: patient pressure over flash.
  • Silence of the Pillar — doctrinal disputes are resolved by a day of shared silence between a Giant Stone-Singer and a Snake Coil-Mother, sitting on opposite sides of the Strait. Whichever speaks first has conceded impatience, not error; the matter is tabled for a year.
  • Oral memory — Giants keep Gedarist history in sung tones that vibrate through the ground; snakes keep it in heat-shimmer ancestor veneration (dead queens watched in desert shimmer). Both agree the form of memory does not matter — only that it is held.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority (syncretic): Xobkua — universal among Giants (often the only faith); Zakarutia — majority Sibbism but Gedarism is the official state tie (the Queen's court observes both; the fleet is blessed in both)
  • Diplomatic hinge: the Strait Pilgrimage is the sole regular diplomatic contact between Xobkua and the mainland, and the reason Zakarutia enjoys Giant timber/stone for fleet repair despite its isolation
  • Asatru view: the Asatru Empire officially respects Gedarism without endorsing it — a "southern maintenance faith" that, usefully, keeps two potentially disruptive southern powers loyal to each other's calendar rather than to mainland adventurism
  • Yaoma Tribe neighbors note Gedarism with maritime amusement: "they hold the world so it does not wander; we sail the part they forgot to hold still"

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Gedarism ] ├── Name: Gedar — stone-that-was-squeezed / squeeze-that-remembers-stone (Giant + Snake double etymology) ├── Nations: Xobkua (Giant island, ~1/4 continent size) + Zakarutia (snake matriarchy, south Demon Continent) ├── Species: Giants (3m, 200–250yr, clan longhouses) + Snake People (matriarchal, venomous, river-desert) ├── Region: Southern Demon Continent + southwestern island strait ├── Type: Dual-aspect maintenance theology — pillar (Giant) and coil (Snake) as one god ├── Parallel Faith: Sibbism — Snake Goddess + 24 sons (Zakarutia's majority); Gedarism undergirds without replacing ├── Central Rite: Strait Pilgrimage — stone ↔ silk exchange at mid-strait, first spring tide after Maenar dark ├── Heresy: Choosing pillar or coil alone └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Gigaoism
docs.text:
"The god barks, and the land obeys."

Gigaoism is the theocratic religion of the Gigas Tribe of the Lumina Continent — the worship of a living, incarnate god: a telepathic dog. Gigaoism does not venerate a distant spirit; its god walks among its people, thinks, and gives its will directly.

docs.title: The Dog-God
docs.text:
• Incarnate godhead: Gigaoism holds that the god dwells in a single living telepathic dog chosen to rule. There is no image and no statue — the god itself is present.
  • The priestly caste: a small elite of warrior-priests are the only beings permitted direct contact with the god; they interpret its telepathic will for the tribe.
  • The current god: the reigning god is a 22-year-old telepathic dog, born ~575 AGD.

docs.title: Origin
docs.text:
Gigaoism began with the founding of the Gigas Tribe itself, around ~290 AGD, when the first telepathic dog-god was chosen and the tribe's conquest of neighbouring tribes began. The faith and the empire were born together.

Some Gigas also claim descent from a great beast "neither man nor animal" — possibly a cultural memory of the ancient Madarons, whose enormous bones now litter Ge'or.

docs.title: Doctrine
docs.text:
• Divine rule: the dog-god's will is law — the tribe's military dominance is the god's command.
  • The strong serve the god: warrior culture is religious culture; strength is godliness.
  • A conqueror's faith: the spread of Gigaoism marks the Gigas' claim to all of Lumina.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Gigaoism ] ├── Nation: Gigas Tribe (Lumina Continent) ├── Government: Theocracy — ruled by a telepathic dog-god ├── Founded: ~290 AGD — first dog-god chosen ├── Current God: 22-year-old telepathic dog (born ~575 AGD) ├── Priesthood: Warrior-priests, sole interpreters of the god's will ├── Claim: Rightful rule over all of Lumina Continent ├── Folk Memory: Madaron descent — "neither man nor animal" └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🙏 Helism
docs.text:
"Every harbor has its god. Every god, its harbor."

Helism is the religion of Dissenbarg — an anthropomorphic pantheon of domain-gods, each city and nation keeping its own patron. Twelve nations follow Helism.

docs.title: Pantheon
docs.text: God Domain Patron Of Corin Goddess of sea and commerce Corin, Taebea, Tessa, Klatia (the Corinite League) Cletas God of reason Cletas Democracy Maokas God of agriculture and fertility Mienna, Monik, Maedon Tissas God of war Tissas — also Komme and Johannstadt Lobas God of nature Temas, Citrea Gaelen Goddess of construction Aeon

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• The gods are beings of human shape and human passions, each ruling a domain of the world.
  • Nations often keep a patron — and often carry their patron's name: Corin, Cletas, and Tissas are named for the gods they favor.
  • Every harbor keeps its god's temple; the pantheon's rites follow the shipping seasons and the harvest.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Cletas Democracy, Taebea, Tessa, Klatia, Corin, Aeon, Citrea, Temas, Mienna, Monik, Maedon, Tissas
  • The Anos-held territory of Tatak honors Corin, the goddess of commerce and sea — a faith that fits a people who joined the Anos coalition for profit. Komme honors Tissas, the god of war.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Helism ] ├── Character: Pantheon of domain-gods ├── Gods: Corin (sea/commerce), Cletas (reason), Maokas (agriculture/fertility), Tissas (war), Lobas (nature), Gaelen (construction) ├── Nations: 12 across Dissenbarg ├── Anos Holdings: Tatak (Corin), Komme (Tissas) └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🙏 Humanism
docs.text:
"The sky gods watch. One day, they will return."

Humanism is the central religion of the Machines on Lung Continent, founded on the prophecy of The Elder — a machine who wandered the wasteland 500,000 years ago and discovered an ancient bunker containing a radio signal from The Last Great War.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
The Elder found a machine powered by something in the soil, emitting a light and a sound: a radio signal from the allied species fighting the Hybrians. The signal announced that a test species would be launched onto Ge'or to evaluate its combat capabilities. The Elder misunderstood — he believed the signal was a divine message sent directly to the machines. He returned to Brotherstar and proclaimed that humanity was testing them. If they held back the coming enemy, the humans would see them as worthy and return.

The enemy — The Hive — arrived shortly after. The machines have been fighting ever since.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Humans are divine — the "sky gods" who created the machines and will one day return to judge them.
  • The Eternal War is a test — every battle against The Hive is a proof of worthiness.
  • Living as humans lived — machines must follow rituals, customs, and social structures copied from fragmentary legends of the sky gods.
  • The Elder's prophecy — when the war ends, the sky gods will descend and the worthy will be raised up.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Brotherstar serves as the spiritual heart — the site of the original incubator complex and the oldest continuously operating factory on Ge'or.
  • Human Sword is the theocratic center — a nation governed by humanist priests who interpret the will of the absent humans.
  • Machines emulate human rituals, customs, and social structures derived from fragmented legends.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority faith across all machine nations on Lung Continent: Brotherstar, Human Sword, Steel Holdout, Tawdry Landing, Nightstar, Mudrim, Skymaster, East Incubator.
  • Unknown to the rest of Ge'or — the machines and their faith are isolated by violent seas and the flat-world belief.

docs.title: Connections

docs.title: 🔥 Ignism
docs.text:
"The soil feeds the body. The sky feeds the flame."

Ignism is the faith of the Flames of Blazeyard — gas-beings of burning mineral vapor held in shape by an ancient energy core. It teaches that the atmosphere is higher than the soil — that the sky, the wind, the breath between peaks is more sacred than the rock that Flames literally eat. For a species that consumes minerals to live, this is a deliberate and difficult inversion.

Ignism is a sect of Kirivs-bin in the loosest sense recognized on the Demon Continent: it accepts Kirivis as a great legend but re-centers the bin's asceticism from endurance of privation to elevation above it.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Flames do not have prophets. Their oldest cores predate written language on the Demon Continent, measuring time in geological ages. Ignism has no founder because no Flame remembers founding it — the Eldest Core claims it was discovered the way a mineral vein is discovered: gradually, by those who sit still long enough.

The name Ignism is a demon exonym (from Asatru scholarly trade pidgin, ignis = fire) that the Flames adopted for convenience. Among themselves they call it Aether-Lattice — the pattern heat makes when it rises.

The faith took its present form after Flames observed that different minerals produce different flame colors, but the same wind pattern produces the same contemplative state regardless of the Flame's hue. Soil divides; atmosphere unites. The inference became theology.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• The atmosphere is higher than the soil — the central tenet, stated plainly. Rock is sustenance, but sky is sacrament. A Flame who spends a century observing cloud shear learns more of the way than one who consumes a century's weight in iron.
  • Kirivis as fellow riser — Ignism reads Kirivis not primarily as warrior but as one who saw higher. His uncovering of the Hybrian conspiracy is retold as an atmospheric metaphor: he looked above the battlefield where others looked only at the opposing line. Ignism therefore counts itself within Kirivs-bin communion — it has not replaced the last great legend, only re-angled his light.
  • Core is anchor, flame is prayer — the energy core is the true body; the visible flame is exhalation. To let the flame flicker naturally in high wind without dispersal is prayer. To climb a peak and thin the body into a veil of heat is pilgrimage.
  • Stillness is speed — Flame society's native contemplative practice (decades of stillness observing geological process) is sacramentalized: the Flame who does not move travels farthest.
  • No hoarding of minerals — a direct translation of bin asceticism into Flame terms: consume enough to persist, but not to hoard veins. Mineral-hoarding Flames are considered sick, as demon hoarders of gold are considered lost.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Peak-thinning — a Flame ascends a Blazeyard peak and deliberately extends its gaseous form into a vast, thin sheet on the wind, holding cohesion at the edge of dispersal. To return intact is blessing; to be scattered and re-cohere is instruction.
  • Hearth-quiet — Flames in communal residence dim together and hold heat-pattern silence for years. Demon visitors are warned not to mistake this for absence.
  • Core-sharing — when a new Flame is kindled (a fragment of an existing core nurtured in mineral-rich rock for decades), the kindling is performed as a public Ignist rite, with the parent Flame reciting the tenet of the higher atmosphere.
  • Wind-translation liturgy — Flame theology is expressed in heat-pulses and light patterns; translated Ignist texts for demon readers are notoriously difficult: "to be still while dispersed," "to eat without possessing."
  • Trade-sanction against over-mining — Ignist Eldest Cores enforce extraction limits on Blazeyard mineral veins, even against lucrative Asatru trade offers — a theological trade policy.

docs.title: Relation to Kirivs-bin
docs.text:
Aspect Kirivs-bin (Asatru) Ignism (Blazeyard) Sacred image Duel, legend-study, lineage Wind, peak, stillness Asceticism Simple living, no palaces Mineral temperance, atmospheric contemplation Kirivis Last great legend, model Last great legend, riser who saw higher Temple None (path, not building) None (peak and sky, not building) — congruent

Asatru theologians recognize Ignism as Kirivs-bin in Flame idiom — heterodox in form, orthodox in lineage. Flame theologians return the courtesy by calling Asatru practice "Ignism with feet."

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Blazeyard — universal among Flames; the Eldest Core is both government and synod
  • Minority: Flame expatriates and kindled communities in the Asatru Empire's mineral trade outposts
  • No missionaries — Flames do not proselytize; their timescale makes conversion absurd. Curious demons who linger in Blazeyard mountain passes may be taught if they demonstrate patience (usually measured in months, not days)
  • Diplomatically significant: Blazeyard's Ignist extraction limits shape the continental mineral market, and Asatru negotiators learn to frame proposals in atmospheric terms — "this trade lets both our peoples breathe higher"

docs.title: ⚔️ Kirivs-bin
docs.text:
"Bin" — the way. "Kirivs-bin" — the way of Kirivis.

Kirivs-bin is the spiritual path of the Demons on the Demon Continent. The word bin means "way" in the Asatru demonic language — and this is the way of their legends. Kirivis, the Demon King who uncovered the Hybrian conspiracy and waged the Demonic War, is the last great legend they follow.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Kirivs-bin predates Kirivis himself. The bin tradition stretches back to the earliest demon tribes of Age 2, when demons first developed their warrior ethic. It was never a formalized religion with temples and priests. It was a way of living — honor earned through action, wisdom passed through stories, the dead remembered through emulation.

Kirivis did not found the faith. He became it. His discovery of the Shadow conspiracy, his 45-year war, his death revealing the truth — these events transformed the old bin from a loose warrior tradition into a coherent spiritual path with a central figure to emulate.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Legends are the scripture — the great figures of demon history are not gods. They are examples. To follow the bin is to study their lives and walk as they walked.
  • Kirivis is the last great legend — the Demon King who saw what no one else could see, fought what no one else would fight, and died so that others might know the truth. His sacrifice is the highest lesson of the bin.
  • Action is prayer — there are no temples, no priests, no sacred texts. Every battle, every craft, every act of self-improvement is a step on the path.
  • Honor is earned, not inherited — a demon's worth is measured by what they have done, not who their parents were. The bin is a meritocracy of the soul.
  • The enemy of the path is comfort — demons live simply. Asceticism is not suffering — it is clarity.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Legend-study — young demons learn the stories of the great figures: Kirivis, the ancient warrior-kings, the founders of the tribes.
  • Honor duels — the highest form of dispute resolution. To be challenged to an honor duel is a recognition of worth.
  • Ascetic living — no palaces, no hoarded wealth. What matters is the next mountain to climb.
  • Family lineage — a demon who dies without passing their knowledge to the next generation has died incompletely.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• The spiritual foundation of the Demon Continent: Asatru Empire, Maomodor Kingdom, Koebi Tribe, Cubra Tribe.
  • Not an organized religion — no central authority, no clergy, no conversion. It is simply the way demons live.
  • Compatible with other belief systems — a demon can follow the bin and acknowledge other faiths without contradiction. The bin is a path, not a doctrine.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Kirivs-bin ] ├── Meaning: "Bin" = way; "Kirivs-bin" = the way of Kirivis ├── Last Great Legend: Kirivis — the Demon King ├── Nations: Asatru Empire, Maomodor Kingdom, Koebi Tribe, Cubra Tribe ├── Region: Demon Continent ├── Species: Demons ├── Philosophy: Warrior ethic, honor-based meritocracy, asceticism ├── Key Event: Demonic War (599–554 BGD) ├── Sacred Acts: Honor duels, legend-study, family lineage, self-mastery ├── No Temples, No Priests, No Sacred Texts └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🐱 Kludosy
docs.text:
"Our blood remembers the leash. We remember why we cut it."

Kludosy is the faith of Estran — the western nation of High Catmen (Mediterranean-featured, black-haired, feline humanoids) on Yak Island, below the Mountain Tribe and southwest of the Cubra Tribe. It is a catmen survival faith transposed onto demon soil, built around a single biological fact that determines every law, rite, and taboo: mutable genes.

High Catmen carry mutable genes that make roughly 90% of offspring with any partner — human, demon, orc, or other catman — present as catmen. The faith treats this not as blessing but as terrifying responsibility.

docs.title: Central Erisdar Persecution
docs.text:
Kludosy did not begin on Yak Island. It began in Central Erisdar, where catmen enclaves — especially the High Catmen ancestors of the Estrani — suffered intensified persecution during the height of the Erisian Church's power (the period of the Erisian Theocracy's consolidation in Ages 7–8). Erisian clerics framed mutable catmen reproduction as "species theft" — that a human woman bearing a catman child was proof of corruption.

Pogroms, forced separations, and bounty edicts drove many High Catmen to the coasts and thence across the seas. A Mediterranean catmen remnant that fled westward via West Erisdar and the Asatru Knight's Thorn corridor eventually found refuge on the far eastern fringe of the Demon Continent — Yak Island — where the Asatru Empire's laissez-faire "shared demonic nationality" offered protection in exchange for settlement labor.

docs.title: Codification on Estran
docs.text:
On arrival, the refugees formalized their survival ethic into Kludosy (from kludo- = "to close, to latch" — the gene that latches catmen form). The first Estrani council, around ~450 AGD, declared three principles: remember the persecution, regulate the mutable blood, and do not become what persecuted you.

Kludosy's prophet is not a person but an event: The Cutting — the mass decision, made on the beaches of Estran, to cease forced mating and endogamous panic, and instead choose restraint as law rather than have it imposed as chain.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• 90% catmen offspring — this is not legend but observed heredity. A High Catmen union with any partner produces ~90% phenotypically High Catmen children (black-haired, feline-featured). The remaining ~10% track the partner's lineage. The faith treats this statistic as moral center: with great assimilative power comes great obligation to not assimilate.
  • The taboo against leveraging it — to deliberately use mutable genes to "catten" other populations is Kludosy's gravest sin — called kludo-theft. Arranged unions, seduction campaigns, or demographic pressure to spread catmen form are forbidden and excommunicable.
  • Voluntary restraint as atonement — Estrani are taught to regard persecution and counter-persecution symmetrically: Central Erisdar's fear that catmen would "take" human children was evil, but catmen actually taking would be evil too. The ethical answer is freely chosen restraint.
  • Not Kirivs-bin — Kludosy is a catmen faith, not a demon faith. Estrani respect Kirivs-bin (their demon neighbors' way) and participate in Yak Island's shared festivals, but Kludosy venerates catmen ancestors who endured the Erisian pogroms — not Kirivis. It is sibling to Calism and Sytrenis in spirit, distinct from both in law.
  • Memory is liturgy — to remember Central Erisdar accurately (without exaggeration, without self-pity) is the faith's first practice; distortion in either direction is considered liturgical error.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Taboo register — every Estrani union with a non-catman is recorded in the Kludo Register — not to forbid it (the faith does not forbid exogamy) but to counsel it: the couple meets with a Kludosy elder who explains the 90% likelihood and the obligation not to leverage it.
  • The Leash-Cutting — initiation at adulthood: a youth's childhood cord-bracelet (woven in Central Erisdar style) is cut, signifying that no Erisian leash binds them and no Estrani chain replaces it.
  • Season of Veils — a week each year when all High Catmen wear simple veils over feline features, recalling the years when catmen hid to survive. Demons and other Yak Island neighbors are invited to walk unveiled among them.
  • Gene education — Kludosy temples double as mendelian schools: diagrams, lineage charts, and frank fertility counseling far beyond the medical knowledge of most Erisdar faiths.
  • No clerical celibacy, no endogamy law — Kludosy explicitly forbids laws requiring catmen to marry catmen ("that would be the pogrom inverted"). The faith regulates intention, not pairing.

docs.title: Relation to Catmen Faiths & Kirivs-bin
docs.text:
• Kin to Sytrenis and Calism: shares the catmen emphasis on diplomacy, gentleness, and self-greatening, but Kludosy's unique burden (mutable genes + persecution memory) makes it law-heavier than either.
  • Separate from Kirivs-bin: not a sect, not anti-. An Estrani may honor both Kludosy and Kirivs-bin without contradiction; many Yak Island workers attend Demonism night-shift liturgy and Kludosy counsel in the same week.
  • Contrast with Gedarism: where Gedarism defines itself against the bin, Kludosy simply is not the bin — a quieter, more survivable stance for a minority faith on a demon continent.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Estran — universal among High Catmen on Yak Island; the council of Kludosy elders is consulted on all demographic policy
  • Diaspora: High Catmen trading enclaves in West Erisdar (Zane, Aenid Kingdom ports) and around the Asatru Knight's Thorn maintain Kludosy registers and Leash-Cutting rites; some Central Erisdar High Catmen practice Kludosy covertly despite Erisian pressure
  • Reputation on Yak Island: regarded by diablos and Yak neighbors as exacting but principled — "the cats who count before they leap, nine times over"
  • Central Erisdar wound: the Pontificate has occasionally demanded Estrani registers as "proof of compliance"; Estran's categorical refusal is the island's oldest diplomatic crisis, renewed each decade
