docs.title: ✊ Krowretism — The Church of Krowretism
docs.text:
"No crown, no church, no master but freedom."

Krowretism — the Church of Krowretism — is the radical freedom-faith of the Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni and its sister region the Crab Union.

The faithful believe the real human god is Krowret, the inner man — that men descend from the gods directly — and that the monotheistic Eris religion is false. They believe humans were deceived by the demon Eris and her followers — that Eris is not a goddess but a demon, her church a cage. They believe they must purify the world from Eris forever and destroy her church.

docs.title: The Human Republic — Exodus and Superpower
docs.text:
Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni — the church's heartland — are refugees from the Erisdar continent and the Erisian Church.

  • ~100 BGD — they started leaving Erisdar approximately 100 years Before Great Divergence — the first dissidents to reject Eris.
  • They settled in Merratodoni and ever since have been building a superpower on the continent — democratic, expansionist, and fiercely anti-Erisian.
  • As of 597 AGD, they are in the process of unifying with the Purple Coast — although they aren't a single entity yet. Negotiations, councils, and joint administration are underway.
  • They plan to expand westwards: the middle of Merratodoni is mostly unpopulated and they are colonizing it — a continental manifest destiny.

The Republic is similar to the United States of America of Old Earth — a frontier democracy built by refugees, obsessed with absolute freedom, industrial and militant, convinced of its mission to purify the world.

docs.title: The Crab Union — Sister Faith
docs.text: The Crab Union (Crab Archipelago) is a majority human region that follows Krowretism — but they also have Seamen among their population. The Crab Union's Krowretists are culturally close to the Human Republic — both see themselves as the free humans who escaped Eris.

docs.title: Tenets
docs.text:
• Krowret, the Inner Man — the real human god is Krowret, the inner man. Not an outer tyrant, but the divine spark inside every human. To worship Krowret is to awaken what is already within.
  • Men Descend from Gods Directly — humans are not fallen, not made from dust, but direct descendants of the gods. The blood of the gods runs in human veins — a literal lineage, not a metaphor. Krowretism is therefore a divine anthropology: to be human is to be god-kin.
  • The Monotheistic Eris Religion is False — the Erisian Church's claim that Eris is the one true god is a lie. Eris-monotheism is false prophecy, a demon's cage to cut humans off from Krowret within. Krowret is the true monotheism — the inner god.
  • Absolute Freedom — the highest divine value. No master, no hierarchy, no church between human and destiny. Law exists to protect freedom, not to constrain it.
  • Eris as Demon — Eris is not a goddess but a demon who deceived humanity. Her church is a demon cult. Every Erisian temple is a profanation.
  • Purification — the world must be purified from Eris forever and her church destroyed. This is not metaphor — Krowretists are the main sponsors of the Ironcloak, the rebel order that fights the Shadows and the Church.
  • The Sponsors of the Ironcloak — the Human Republic funds, arms, and shelters the Ironcloak — the only nation to do so openly.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Democratic liturgy — sermons are debates, prayers are votes.
  • Iconoclasm — Erisian icons are destroyed on sight.
  • Oath of Freedom — every citizen swears to defend absolute freedom, even against their own government.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nations: Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni (heartland), Crab Union (Crab Archipelago)
  • Sponsor: Ironcloak
  • Enemy: Erisian Church, Eris (as demon)
  • Region: Merratodoni (northeast), Crab Archipelago
  • Age: Exodus ~100 BGD → superpower by 597 AGD, unifying with Purple Coast, colonizing middle Merratodoni westwards

docs.title: Lumism
docs.text:
"The empire's bones remember. So must we."

Lumism is the religion of the Lumina Kingdom — a faith of restoration. Its believers hold that the fall of the ancient Lumina Empire was not the end of the beastmen's story, and that the kingdom must return the Lumina Empire and bring back the old ways of the beastmen.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• The imperial cult: Lumism venerates the old imperial figures of the Lumina Empire — the emperors, kings, and architects of the golden age, honoured as the truest rulers the beastmen ever had.
  • Animism: woven through the imperial veneration is a deep animism — the belief that the world teems with spirits, and that the ancient land still holds the memory of its builders.
  • The jungle animals: Lumism praises the jungle animals — the great cats, the serpents, the beasts of the canopy — as sacred kin of the beastmen, reminders of what the people are at heart.
  • Restoration: to restore the empire and the old ways is not ambition; it is duty.

docs.title: Practice — Slow and Tribal
docs.text: For all its imperial devotion, the Lumina Kingdom remains highly tribal and decentralized. Lumism is lived in small, local rites as much as in the cult of emperors. There is a slow, genuine push toward modernization — to rebuild the roads, the learning, the order the empire once had — but it moves at the pace of a people still half in the jungle.

docs.text: "The fallen are not gone — they sing in the trees."

docs.text: A cult based near the Lyrical Forest, revering the spirits of the dead who dwell within it.

docs.text:

  • Those spirits are the ancestors — and they must be respected.
  • Followers claim that sometimes they hear voices coming out of the Lyrical Forest — the ancestors speaking to the living.

  • Minority: Pilferhorn
  • Some: Augagarten, Galerough

docs.title: 💜 Malgardism
docs.text:
"We are small, therefore we must be pure. We are few, therefore we must be perfect."

Malgardism is the shared faith of the Malgardian peoples on the Demon Continent — the Malgardian Tribe, the Tita Tribe, and in its ancestral form, the Bloodcoast. It is the largest and most coherent sect of Kirivs-bin, preserving the Way of Kirivis through a distinctly Malgardian lens: purity of form, purity of purpose, and the sacred role of the small.

Unlike the austere, temple-less bin of the Asatru Empire, Malgardism is devotional without being doctrinal — it adds ritual, priesthood, and iconography to the warrior path while insisting it has not strayed from it.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Malgardism emerged among the Malgardian exiles in the centuries after their arrival on Ge'or following The Last Great War. As a transplanted people — near-human in appearance but not of Earth — the Malgardians faced a crisis of belonging. Kirivs-bin gave them a way to be demonic without ceasing to be Malgardian.

The faith crystallized around Age 6–7, when Titian priestesses first formalized the rites that turned the formless bin into Malgardism: lineage recitation, purification baths, and the doctrine of miko — that the smallest body carries the clearest spirit.

Malgardism does not claim a single prophet. Its founders are remembered as the First Mothers — Malgardian matriarchs who preserved the people through exile and who first declared that purple hair, small stature, and unmixed blood were not accidents of biology but marks of spiritual intactness.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Kirivis is the model, purity is the method — Malgardism is explicitly a sect of Kirivs-bin. It venerates Kirivis as the last great legend and accepts every tenet of the bin: legends are scripture, action is prayer, honor is earned, comfort is the enemy. Its addition is how to walk the path purely.
  • Purity of appearance is purity of spirit — unmixed Malgardian features (purple hair, fair skin, compact stature) are read as outward signs of inward discipline. This is not racial supremacy toward outsiders — it is rigor within the community.
  • Smallness is sacred — the smaller the body, the closer to the origin. The Titians, smallest of all Malgardians, are therefore miko — sacred beings, living shrines.
  • Lineage is liturgy — to recite one's mothers without error back seven generations is prayer. Memory is worship.
  • Asceticism is hygiene — demons live simply because clutter obscures the way; Malgardians add purification rites (fasting, cold-water bathing, violet-ink calligraphy) as hygiene of the soul.

docs.title: Practices & Priesthood
docs.text:
• Tita priesthood — only Titian miko may serve as Malgardian priests. Their small stature and famously pure purple-white hair make them instantly recognizable; they are cloistered from adolescence in cliffside shrines west of the Malgardian Tribe and trained in recitation, healing, and mediation.
  • Hair-binding rite — Malgardian children have their first lock of purple hair bound with silver thread at age seven and offered to the shrine. Cutting or dyeing hair outside mourning is taboo.
  • Legend-study with commentary — where Asatru demons debate Kirivis freely, Malgardians study a fixed Tita Commentary on the legends — three scrolls interpreting each legend through the lens of purity and perseverance.
  • No temples, but shrines — a concession to Kirivs-bin's temple-less ideal. Malgardist shrines are open-air stone circles with a single upright violet crystal; they have no roof, no walls, no hoarded wealth.
  • Honor duel, Malgardian form — duels are fought with wooden staves rather than steel, ending at first blood or first disarm; to scar the face is shameful.

docs.title: Relation to Kirivs-bin
docs.text:
Malgardism is Kirivs-bin, Malgardian-accented. Asatru purists sometimes call it "decorated bin" and Tita priestesses answer that "a blade may be decorated and still cut."

  • Accepts Kirivis as last great legend without addition or replacement
  • Adds priesthood and shrines where Kirivs-bin has neither, justified as guidance, not mediation — priests teach the way, they do not intercede
  • Compatible with plain Kirivs-bin practice; a Malgardist and an Asatru demon can honor-duel, legend-study, and ancestor-remember side by side without dispute
  • Padamalgardism later broke from Malgardism precisely over whether these additions had gone too far

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority faith: Malgardian Tribe — universal among unmixed Malgardians
  • Sacred priesthood: Tita Tribe — 100% Malgardist; priesthood source for all Malgardian shrines
  • Ancestral: Bloodcoast — before the Padamalgardist schism, Bloodcoast families followed plain Malgardism; elders still remember the old rites
  • Respected (and lightly mocked) on the rest of the Demon Continent as the most ceremonial demon faith — "the demons who kneel," Asatru soldiers say, not unkindly
  • Demons of other subraces make pilgrimage to Tita shrines to seek miko blessings before major undertakings

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Malgardism ] ├── Type: Sect of Kirivs-bin — "the purple way" ├── Last Great Legend: Kirivis (shared with Kirivs-bin) ├── Nations: Malgardian Tribe (majority), Tita Tribe (priesthood), ancestral Bloodcoast ├── Species: Malgardians + Titians (subrace, miko) ├── Priesthood: Titian miko only — pure appearance required ├── Shrines: Open-air violet-crystal circles (no temples, by bin principle) ├── Doctrine: Purity of form → purity of spirit; smallness is sacred; lineage is liturgy ├── Relation: Devotional extension of Kirivs-bin, not a break ├── Schism: → Padamalgardism (Bloodcoast warrior offshoot) └── Part Of: Ge'or — Demon Continent

docs.title: 🐾 Mamanolism
docs.text:
"All beasts are gods in fur and feather."

Mamanolism is the animist faith of the Mamanolo Tribe on Tuba Continent — the beastmen tribe on Tuba's northern edge. The Mamanolo believe all animals are divine — every beast, bird, fish, and insect carries a fragment of divinity.

docs.title: Tenets
docs.text:
• Universal Animal Divinity — not one sacred species, but all animals. A mouse is as divine as a dragon; a beetle as a wolf. Divinity is not hierarchy but ubiquity.
  • Animist Reverence — every animal encounter is a theophany. Hunting is prayer, eating is communion. The Mamanolo waste nothing — to kill without gratitude is blasphemy.
  • Beastmen as Mediators — as beastmen themselves, the Mamanolo see their own hybrid nature as sacred: they stand between human and animal, and therefore can speak for both.

docs.title: Followers
docs.text:
• Mamanolo Tribe (Tuba Continent, north) — sole canonical nation. The faith is tribal and oral, kept by beastmen elders.
  • Small beastmen enclaves in Tuba who have contact with Mamanolo carry the faith outward, but it has no organized church.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Daily offerings of food to wild animals.
  • No animal is killed without a spoken thanks to its spirit.
  • Tribal shamans interpret animal behavior as divine messages.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: Tuba Continent
  • Nation: Mamanolo Tribe
  • Species: Beast Races
  • Related: Alkorri (neighbor, different faith Sytrenis)

docs.title: 🌟 Mannosta
docs.text:
"The stars remember. The ancestors speak through them."

Mannosta is the pagan religion of the Mann Order in North Erisdar. It venerates ancestors and the stars — the faithful believe that the dead ascend to the night sky, becoming points of light that watch over the living.

The name means "greatness of Mann." For Mannosta pagans, Mann is the capital of the gods — and it is also the capital of the Mann Order itself. The city and the faith share one name because, to the faithful, they are the same thing: the place where greatness lives.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Mannosta was once the dominant faith across a large swath of northern Erisdar. Its roots extend deep into pre-Age 7 oral traditions, predating the rise of the Erisian Church by millennia. The stars, unchanging and eternal, were the first gods — before temples, before priests, before the written word.

The faith flourished in isolation, far from the political centers of the south. But isolation became vulnerability.

docs.title: Decline
docs.text:
Mannosta has been reduced dramatically in size. Centuries of Erisian expansion, the aggressive missionary work of Alegoria, and the ongoing invasion by the Erilian Federation have shrunk Mannosta's territory to a fraction of its former reach. The Erilian Federation — which follows the Erisian faith — calls the Mann people "pagans" and uses the label as justification for conquest.

Many people living within Mann Order's borders now follow Alegoria rather than the old faith. Mannosta survives, but it is a faith under siege — its temples are fewer, its priests are hunted, and its stars grow dimmer with each passing year.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• The stars are ancestors — when a person dies with honor, their soul ascends to the night sky and becomes a star. The brightest stars are the greatest ancestors.
  • The stars speak — patterns in the night sky convey the will of the ancestors. Star-reading is the highest priestly art.
  • The land remembers — burial sites are sacred. To disturb a grave is to blind the ancestor whose star it connects to.
  • Isolation is protection — the old faith survived by staying away from the larger world. That isolation is now impossible.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Star-reading — priests interpret stellar configurations for guidance on war, harvest, and leadership.
  • Ancestor cairns — stone markers placed at burial sites, aligned to specific stars.
  • Night vigils — the faithful gather on clear nights to sing the names of the dead.
  • Funeral pyres — bodies are burned at night so the smoke carries the soul upward.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Traditional faith of the Mann Order in North Erisdar.
  • Once larger, now reduced to the Mann heartland and scattered rural communities.
  • Under active threat from Erilian Federation invasion and Alegoria conversion efforts.
  • A significant portion of Mann's population now follows Alegoria.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Mannosta ] ├── Deity: The stars — ascended ancestors ├── Nation: Mann Order ├── Region: North Erisdar ├── Status: Declining — under military and religious pressure ├── Rival Faiths: Erisian church, Alegoria ├── Invading Power: Erilian Federation (Erisian faith) ├── Practices: Star-reading, ancestor cairns, night vigils, funeral pyres └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Maomism
docs.text:
"We came from ash and god-hands, made to rule the forest."

Maomism is the religion of the Maoma Tribe on the Lumina Continent, long-time enemies of the great Gigas Tribe. It is a creation faith that gives the beastmen of Lumina a divine origin — and, in its recent reformed form, a holy enemy.

docs.title: The Creation
docs.text:
Maomism teaches that the beastmen descend from the original Lumina Kingdom, founded thirty thousand years ago by the god Tiodorus and his sister Anedoris. From the ashes of the world, the two gods shaped the beastmen with their own hands and sent them forth to rule over all the forests of Ge'or. The beastmen are therefore the natural rulers of every rainforest — a truth that fits the land they live in, for Lumina is a continent of rainforest and mountain.

(The thirty-thousand-year date is myth, not history — no intelligent species existed on Ge'or that long ago — but no Maoma preaches that.)

docs.title: After the Fall
docs.text: Maomism appeared only after the fall of the ancient Lumina Empire, thousands of years ago — a faith born from the ruins to explain what the beastmen once were and why they lost it. It preserves, in holy form, the memory that beastmen were once a great and civilized people.

docs.title: The Reform
docs.text:
In recent times Maomism has undergone reforms, and its canon has been extended to answer an old question — the Maoma's ancient feud with the Gigas:

  • The Gigas are the enemies of the gods.
  • The Gigas came to destroy all the rainforests of the world.

The Maoma's long-time enmity with the Gigas Tribe is thus written into the faith itself: the Gigas are not merely rivals — they are the agents of the world's forests' destruction, and the Maoma stand against them as the gods' chosen guardians of the rainforest.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Maomism ] ├── Nation: Maoma Tribe (Lumina Continent) ├── Gods: Tiodorus and Anedoris ├── Founded: After the fall of the ancient Lumina Empire, thousands of years ago ├── Doctrine: Beastmen descend from the original Lumina Kingdom; natural rulers of the world's rainforests ├── Reform: The Gigas are enemies of the gods, come to destroy the rainforests ├── Enemy: Gigas Tribe └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🐍 Moplilly
docs.text:
"Xanob watches from the first coil."

Moplilly is the ancestor-veneration cult of the Snake People of Kobra on Marti Continent.

The Kobra snakespeople are the same race as Xikxia (West Erisdar) and Zakarutia (Demon Continent) — but they separated thousands of years ago, and the Kobra lineage ended up living in Marti as a cold-adapted subrace — unlike their warm-blooded kin, these serpents thrive in frigid climates.

Moplilly reveres the ancestor of all of them — the demigod father-founder Xanob — as the most prayed-upon figure.

docs.title: Tenets
docs.text:
• Xanob as Progenitor — Xanob is the demigod father-founder of all Snake People — the first to coil, the first to lay, the first to rule. Every snake person is his blood.
  • Ancestor Veneration — all ancestors are honored, but Xanob is supreme. Prayers ascend through the lineage: child to parent to grandparent to Xanob.
  • Cold as Trial — the Kobra's cold adaptation is read as Xanob's final gift: he taught his Marti children to endure the cold that would kill their cousins, so they could hold the north for serpent-kind.

docs.title: Followers
docs.text:
• Kobra (Marti Continent, east of Kut) — the cold-adapted snake nation. Moplilly is the state faith in practice.
  • Diaspora Kobra traders in Maboro and Kut carry small Xanob shrines.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Scale-painting of Xanob's coil — the founding coil is the sacred geometry.
  • Egg-blessing: clutches are presented at Xanob shrines before incubation.
  • Winter fasting — to honor the cold Xanob mastered.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: Marti Continent (Kobra)
  • Nation: Kobra
  • Species: Snake People (cold-adapted subrace; kin Xikxia, Zakarutia — separated thousands of years ago)
  • Deity: Xanob (demigod father-founder)
  • Related: Sibbism (cousin faith of Xikxia/Zakarutia, different god), Snake People matriarchy

docs.title: Mukini Dirt-Faith
docs.text:
"All things rise from the dirt. All things return to it. The dirt is holy."

Mukini Dirt-Faith is the religion of the Mukini Tribe on Mia — an island faith closely kin to the trolls' Taosudism. Being neighbours to the Orgor trolls, the Mukini share their earth-cosmology without the trolls' fear: where the trolls treat water as corruption, the Mukini simply hold that all beings come from the dirt, and the dirt is sacred.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• The dirt is sacred. Every living thing — beast, plant, troll, catman, human — was born from the earth. To honour life is to honour the earth.
  • Water is a guest, not a source. Rivers and rain come and go; the ground endures. The waterborne may be mysterious or dangerous, but the eternal truth lives in the soil.
  • Sculpture is prayer. The Mukini craft sculptures out of dirt using ancient techniques that render the clay beautiful and extraordinarily durable — their structures stand unbothered for decades, even through the fiercest rains that would dissolve any other earthen work.

docs.title: The Dirt-Temple
docs.text: Mukini settlements are marked by their earth-sculptures: figures of ancestors, beasts, and spirits that watch over the village. They are the tribe's art, its record, and its offering to the sacred ground — proof that the dirt can be shaped into something that endures.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Mukini Dirt-Faith ] ├── Nation: Mukini Tribe (Mia) ├── Kin Faith: Taosudism — the troll faith of neighbouring Orgor Kingdom ├── Core: All beings come from the dirt; dirt is sacred; earth-sculpture endures ├── Practice: Sacred earth-sculpture that resists even intense rain for decades └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: ✨ Nyity
docs.text:
"The sky bled, and we were born from it."

Nyity is an astronomical religion of the Moriat island nations in the Luminous Ocean. The faithful believe that sky gods came down from the heavens and created humanity through a suicidal sacrifice — their divine blood spilled and turned into all humans.

One of the oldest religions on Ge'or, Nyity dates back to ~4,000 BGD — predating the Great Divergence, the Elvish Diaspora, and the rise of the Erisian Church by millennia.

docs.title: Tenets
docs.text:
• Sky Gods as Creators — not the The Silver Bride nor Eris, but ancient celestial beings who descended from the stars.
  • The Sacrificial Genesis — the gods killed themselves; their blood became the first humans. All humans share divine blood.
  • Astronomical Reverence — stars, constellations, and celestial movements are read as the lingering will of the sky gods.
  • Antiquity as Authority — age is truth. Nyity's 4,000 BGD origin is its credential — older than Eris, older than empires.

docs.title: Followers
docs.text:
• Mikrad — human kingdom on Moriat, eastern Moriat. Pure Nyity.
  • Underfern — human kingdom on Moriat, directly south of Mercur across the sea, west of Mikrad. Pure Nyity.
  • Gomor and Gildenrise — half-elf majority kingdoms on Moriat (see below). Mixed: most follow Elven Faith, a significant minority keep Nyity. No official state religion in either.
  • Diaspora memory: half-elves who still honor Nyity do so as a link to the human heritage of Moriat.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• ~4,000 BGD — Nyity emerges on Moriat among early human settlers. The sacrificial myth is codified while Erisdar still worships pre-Erisian pantheons.
  • Survives the Great Divergence (Year 0) and the Elvish Diaspora intact due to geographic isolation in the Luminous Ocean.
  • ~200 AGD — half-elf takeover of Gomor/Gildenrise brings Elven Faith to Moriat; Nyity becomes a minority faith there but retains Mikrad/Underfern as strongholds.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Night vigils under clear skies; star-charts as scripture.
  • Blood symbolism in rites (pigment, not human sacrifice) — recalling the divine blood-to-human genesis.
  • No centralized clergy; elders-astronomers keep the sky calendars.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: Luminous Sea Islands (Moriat island)
  • Island: Moriat
  • Nations: Mikrad, Underfern (human, Nyity), Gomor, Gildenrise (half-elf, mixed)
  • Related: Elven Faith, Erisian Church
  • Age: ~4,000 BGD (among oldest on Ge'or)

docs.title: 🌊 Oceanism
docs.text:
"On land we limp. Under water we are what the world intended."

Oceanism is the faith of the Yaoma Tribe — the mermaid-like Yaoma who inhabit two islands south of Zakarutia and east of Xobkua's western sea. It teaches that ocean creatures are perfect — finished by the world as it was meant to be — while land creatures, including humanoids who breathe air, are drafts, sketches, early errors the world is still correcting. To be Yaoma is to live on the shoreline between perfection and its rough draft.

Oceanism is not a sect of Kirivs-bin. The Yaoma honor Kirivis as a brave land-general, but their scripture is the tide.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Oceanism has no prophet and no founding date. Yaoma song-history encodes it as always-present: when the first Yaoma egg hatched in warm shallows, the hatchling already knew that water was home and air was exile.

The faith's narrative form emerged as the Yaoma Tribe built its dual-island polity: one island for habitation (surface structures, beaches, egg-shallows) and one sacred atoll for governance, where only the Tide-Council (seven elders chosen by the phases of Maenar and Amelia) may tread. Around ~200 BGD, the council's song-keepers codified disparate tide-songs into the Perfect Ocean Cycle — the complete Oceanist canon: a sequence of melodies that, sung in order over a lunar cycle, tells the faith entire.

The Yaoma are sometimes called "marmots" in Asatru traders' pidgin (a corruption of merfolk via marmot). Yaoma find this hilarious and occasionally adopt it ceremonially — "the marmots of the perfect ocean" — to puncture mainland solemnity.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Ocean creatures are perfect — not metaphorically. A dolphin's hydrodynamics, a shark's electroreception, a coral's colonial architecture — these are finished forms. A Yaoma song-scroll catalogues hundreds of such perfections as verses of scripture. Perfection here means fitting — the creature fits its medium without remainder.
  • Land creatures are drafts — mammals in particular are compromises: they carry their ocean (blood, amniotic fluid) inside them because they left it incompletely. Demons, humans, orcs, giants — all walk on legs that the world has not yet solved. This is not contempt but melancholy: land-dwellers are "still worth singing to," Yaoma say.
  • The shoreline is purgatory — Yaoma themselves live in the border between perfect and draft. They water-breathe but build on beaches; they lay eggs in shallows but conduct diplomacy on atolls. Their islands are liturgical reminder that perfection is adjacent, visible a fin-kick away, but not theirs to inhabit full-time while politics requires legs.
  • Song is how perfection remembers itself — Yaoma songs travel miles underwater, serving simultaneously as communication, history-keeping, and art. An elder who can sing their lineage back a thousand years is Oceanism's closest analogue to a priest — not intercessor but living archive.
  • Pearls as prayer-knots — imperfect irritants transformed into perfections by patient nacre. Yaoma pearl-diving is thus both economy and liturgy; a flaw tolerated long enough becomes beauty.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Tidal magic as devotion — Yaoma mages command currents, summon storms, and converse with sea creatures; their magic is strongest at high tide, weakest at low. To work tidal magic well is to demonstrate that you understand perfection's rhythm.
  • Egg-shallows guarding — eggs laid in warm shallows are guarded communally, with the tribe singing the Perfect Ocean Cycle over them for the full incubation. A clutch sung to completely is considered Oceanist-baptized.
  • Atoll silence — the governance atoll is Oceanism's most sacred space and its quietest. No song-scroll is performed there; only the natural lap of water on coral. To legislate in silence is to remember what perfection sounds like when no one is composing it.
  • Salvage as recovery — Yaoma divers recover artifacts from sunken vessels across the southern strait. Each recovered object is catalogued as "a draft returning to water" — not treasure but repentant matter.
  • Beaching vigil — a young Yaoma beaches themselves for up to two hours at sensory limit — gills drying, tail aching — to feel, somatically, why land is unfinished. Rescuers wait with wet kelp; the vigil ends with reimmersion and communal song.

docs.title: Relation to Kirivs-bin
docs.text:
Not a sect. A parallel.

  • Oceanism does not venerate Kirivis as normative. Kirivis is honored as "the land-general who saw the conspiracy" — impressive for a draft, but not binding on a tide-faith.
  • Where Kirivs-bin says honor is earned, Oceanism says perfection is given (to ocean creatures) and practiced toward (by shore-dwellers). Different anthropology.
  • Where Kirivs-bin says action is prayer, Oceanism says song and tide-keeping are prayer — notably less individualist: no Yaoma sings alone; songs require water as medium and other Yaoma as chorus.
  • Asatru theologians classify Oceanism as a "marine folk faith" — Yaoma hear this as "draft-language for a perfection you haven't learned to breathe in." Relations are courteous but theologically incommensurable.

Yaoma who live in mainland port enclaves (trading pearls, coral, and salvage) often observe both Oceanism and, socially, Kirivs-bin festivals without conflict — the sea does not mind what you do on shore, as long as you remember where the perfection is.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Yaoma Tribe — universal among Yaoma; Tide-Council is both government and synod
  • Islands: two islands + sacred atoll south of Zakarutia, east of Xobkua; seabed gardens and song-corridors between them are also considered Oceanist "territory" though no map marks them
  • Avoidance: the Glub Kingdom — intelligent slimes unsettle Yaoma; the idea of an amorphous land-jelly that can reshape at will is, in Oceanist terms, "a draft that refused to choose a perfection"
  • Trade presence: Yaoma pearl and salvage networks carry Oceanist song-fragments and pearl-knots throughout the Demon Continent south; mainland demons prize Yaoma-harvested pearls without understanding they are prayer-beads

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Oceanism ] ├── Name: Oceanism — Way of the Perfect Ocean (pidgin also: "Marmot Faith") ├── Species: Yaoma — mermaid-like, water-breathing only, tide-magic ├── Nations: Yaoma Tribe (two islands + sacred atoll); universal among Yaoma ├── Region: Demon Continent — south, below Zakarutia, east of Xobkua ├── Codified: ~200 BGD — Perfect Ocean Cycle by the Tide-Council song-keepers ├── Type: Independent marine faith — NOT a sect of Kirivs-bin ├── Doctrine: Ocean creatures perfect/finished; land creatures as drafts; shoreline as purgatory ├── Scripture: Song-scrolls — melodies encoding epics, traveling miles underwater ├── Sacrament: Nacre — pearl as irritant-become-perfection; egg-shallows incubation song └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🙏 Ogoron
docs.text:
"The titanic orc will avenge us all."

Ogoron — meaning "titanic orc" in the demonic orchish tongue — is the faith of the orc peoples worldwide, centered in Augamouth on West Erisdar and in Yakut on Yak Island (where the Yak — smaller, modest orcs — carry the faith eastward). It teaches that a titanic orc savior will come to avenge orc-kind for every injustice, end the great war, and bring peace to all species.

Ogoron is not a sect of Kirivs-bin. It is the orcs' own answer to demon honor — vengeance transformed into universal peace.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Ogoron emerged from Augamouth's long experience as a stigmatized martial kingdom on West Erisdar — feared, hired, and seldom heard. Orc oral tradition holds that during the worst persecution, a titanic orc — taller than a giant, scarred in every battle — appeared to a dying war-band and promised: what was taken will be returned, not as loot but as peace.

No prophet is named because the promise is remembered as overheard, not delivered: the titan spoke to the wounded collectively, and they repeated it as they recovered.

The faith crossed to the Demon Continent via Yak Island. When Yak orcs — a smaller, milder subrace of Orcs (the Yak people of Yakut, below Cubra Tribe and Estran, across the sea from Zakarutia) — established their own polity, they brought Ogoron with them intact, adding to it the Yak's characteristic modesty: the titan will come when orcs have proven they deserve peace, not before.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• A titanic orc will come — not metaphor. A literal, huge orc of legend — the avenger — will appear to settle the accounts of orc-kind: every pogrom, every mercenary betrayal, every child taken as labor. This is vengeance as jurisprudence: the ledger closed.
  • After the great war, all species will live in harmony — Ogoron is eschatologically universalist: the titan's war is the last war. Its aftermath is not orc supremacy but peace for all species, together. Orcs are avenged so that no one needs vengeance again.
  • Ogoron is inside all of their hearts — the titan is not merely a distant savior but a presence within every orc believer. To act with quiet, stubborn endurance is to let the titan breathe through you. Yak orcs in particular emphasize this inward presence over apocalyptic expectation.
  • Endurance is devotion — where Kirivs-bin venerates the duel and Tolumin venerates shared labor, Ogoron venerates carrying on: to hold the line, to raise children under stigma, to refuse to become what your persecutors claim you are.
  • No temples, but hearths — like the bin, Ogoron builds no temples; unlike the bin, it builds hearths — massive communal fire-pits in Augamouth longhouses and Yak stone circles where the tribe gathers to repeat the promise and add their own endurance to it.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Hearth recitation — the promise recited antiphonally around the hearth at night: an elder speaks the wrongs remembered, the assembly answers "and the titan remembers too."
  • Scar-tending — Yak healers practice deliberate scar care after battles or accidents: cleaning, binding, and oiling scars to keep them legible. A scar is read as ledger entry — not shame but evidence.
  • Mercenary's pause — Augamouth orcs hired in foreign wars observe a day's pause before battle to ask whether this war is the war (it never is) and whether this employer deserves orc blood (sometimes not). Many contracts have been refused at this pause.
  • Yak modesty rite — Yak orcs on Yak Island add a small, daily practice: before any meal, a moment of silence with hands open, "to show we take only what peace would permit us."
  • Titan effigies — deliberately crude — Ogoron effigies of the titan are carved intentionally rough and left unfinished, "because we do not know his face until he comes."

docs.title: Relation to Kirivs-bin
docs.text:
Separate — with mutual respect.

  • Ogoron is not Kirivs-bin and does not claim to be. It venerates a future titan, not Kirivis; its eschaton is universal peace after vengeance, not honor earned individually.
  • Nonetheless, orc and demon communities on the Demon Continent and Yak Island observe each other's rites without conflict. Mainland demons call Ogoron "the orcs' bin" and orcs call Kirivs-bin "the demons' hearth" — both inaccurate, both affectionate.
  • Yak Island is the continent's laboratory for coexistence: diablo Demonism, High Catmen Kludosy, Yak Ogoron, and demon plain Kirivs-bin share the same mountain roads and night markets. No faith there has attempted to absorb another.
  • Small syncretic minorities exist — orcs who honor both the titan and Kirivis, citing "the titan will need honorable lieutenants" — but neither orthodoxy recognizes dual belonging as doctrine; they tolerate it as personal piety.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Augamouth (West Erisdar) — orc kingdom; state-recognized, hearth-centered
  • Majority: Yakut (Yak Island, Demon Continent) — the Yak people (smaller orcs, modest temperament); their Ogoron is quieter and more inward than Augamouth's martial variant
  • Diaspora: orc enclaves worldwide — wherever orcs labor as mercenaries, miners, or builders, a hearth-promise is repeated
  • Notable ally: Zakarutia has occasionally mediated between Augamouth and its neighbors; Zakarutian snake-matritarchs find Ogoron "legible" because vengeance-into-peace mirrors their own dynastic memory of betrayal and reunion

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Ogoron ] ├── Meaning: "Titanic orc" — demonic orchish ├── Deity/Figure: The Titanic Orc — future avenger, then peacemaker; also indwelling presence in every orc heart ├── Nations: Augamouth (West Erisdar, martial orcs), Yakut (Yak Island, Yak subrace — smaller, modest) ├── Species: Orcs + Yak subrace ├── Region: West Erisdar origin; Yak Island (Demon Continent) extension ├── Promise: Great war → vengeance → peace for all species in harmony ├── Doctrine: Ogoron dwells within; endurance is devotion; hearths not temples; titan unknown until coming ├── Relation to Kirivs-bin: Separate (not a sect), mutually respected; syncretic minorities tolerated └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 💍 Onobor
docs.text:
"The ring holds. So will we."

Onobor is the paganism of Tetras — named for Onobor, the Tetrian word for "ring."

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• The Silver Bride — Ge'or's planetary ring — is the goddess herself.
  • She is the key to immortality and prosperity.
  • The ring's unbroken circle symbolizes eternal life; its light is the goddess's blessing upon the faithful.

docs.title: Character
docs.text: A fortress-people's faith: Tetras has trained for war since the Dragon Tyranny, and their religion matches — disciplined, enduring, and fixed on the eternal ring overhead.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Onobor ] ├── Meaning: "Ring" — in Tetrian ├── Deity: The Silver Bride — the ring as goddess ├── Promise: Immortality and prosperity through the ring ├── Nation: Tetras ├── Character: Pagan, ring-worship, disciplined └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🩸 Padamalgardism
docs.text:
"Our hair is red because our path was cut with blood. Remember it."

Padamalgardism — padama meaning "blood-cut" in the Malgardian tongue — is the warrior subsect of Malgardism followed by the Bloodcoast tribe and, in a separate minority form, by converts to the Eris Church within the same nation. It is Kirivs-bin twice-removed: a sect of a sect, and proud of the distance.

Where Malgardism turns inward toward purity, Padamalgardism turns outward toward proof.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Padamalgardism was born from the Malgardian-human admixture that created the Bloodcoast people. Unlike the purple-haired Malgardians and the white-violet Titians, Bloodcoast generations carry red hair — the visible trace of human ancestry from the distant past.

In early Malgardist orthodoxy this was read as dilution. Bloodcoast elders answered by re-reading the legends: Kirivis himself was of the Bjor subrace — not the imperial Xiobita, not the fairest or tallest — and still became the last great legend. Worth is what you do, not what you look like. If the bin means anything, they argued, it must mean that red hair can walk the way as purely as purple.

Around ~800–600 BGD, Bloodcoast war-leaders formalized this answer into Padamalgardism: Malgardism's rites kept, but its purity doctrine inverted — red is not impurity but price paid.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Still Kirivs-bin at the root — Padamalgardists accept Kirivis as the last great legend, legends-as-scripture, and the entire bin ethic. They are a Malgardist subsect, not a new faith.
  • Red hair is a scar, not a stain — the human admixture is remembered as a hard winter when isolated Malgardians survived by bonding with human refugees. The red mark honors that survival; to hide it is to dishonor it.
  • Proof through combat — where Malgardism purifies through fasting and recitation, Padamalgardism purifies through trial by combat, raid, and coastal defense. A Bloodcoast youth proves their place on the way by holding the surf-line alone for a night.
  • The sea is the dojo — Bloodcoast territory faces open water northward; the faith teaches that waves are opponents that never tire, and that learning to stand against them teaches honor more honestly than any sermon.
  • Two paths, one coast — the tribe acknowledges a minority Eris Church presence (perhaps 15–20%) — Bloodcoast families who converted through contact with West Erisdar traders via the Asatru Knight's Thorn corridor. Padamalgardist orthodoxy does not persecute them but does not recognize Eris theologically; the coexistence is civic, not doctrinal.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Hair-not-cut rite — Bloodcoast warriors never dye or cut their red hair before battle. To present your color plainly is to declare your lineage without apology.
  • Salt-water purification — counterpart to Malgardist fresh-water bathing: immersion in the cold surf at dawn, reciting maternal lineage while the tide pulls.
  • Honor duels, Bloodcoast form — fought with paired short blades (padama knives), to yield rather than to first blood. A Padamalgardist who yields cleanly is honored as highly as one who wins — the duel measures judgment as well as skill.
  • Coastal vigils — youths and oathsmen stand watch on the shingle through storm nights, unarmed, as meditation and endurance rite.

docs.title: Relation to Kirivs-bin
docs.text:
Layer Stance Kirivs-bin Root — the way of legends, honor, asceticism Malgardism First sect — adds Tita priesthood, purity-of-form, shrine circles Padamalgardism Subsect — keeps Malgardist rites, reverses purity exclusion; adds warrior/surf theology; remains within the bin communion

Padamalgardist priests are still Tita-trained when possible, but Bloodcoast shrines also ordain their own red-haired shore-priests — a point of friction with Tita orthodoxy, which recognizes only miko priesthood. In practice, Tita priestesses visit the Bloodcoast for major rites and tolerate the shore-priests for daily observance.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Bloodcoast — roughly 80% Padamalgardist
  • Minority: Bloodcoast Eris Church communities (~15–20%), concentrated in port hamlets trading with Erisdar
  • Diaspora: small Bloodcoast enclaves in Asatru Empire port towns and the Malgardian Tribe borderlands
  • Viewed by Malgardians with fond exasperation — "our red cousins who pray with knives"
  • Viewed by Asatru demons as the most recognizably warrior of the Malgardian faiths — and therefore the most trustworthy in a joint campaign

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Padamalgardism ] ├── Type: Warrior subsect of Malgardism → sect of Kirivs-bin ├── Name: padama = "blood-cut" (Malgardian tongue) ├── Nations: Bloodcoast (majority); minority Eris Church on same coast ├── Species: Malgardian-human hybrid subrace (red hair marker) ├── Ancestor Faith: Malgardism (Tita priesthood, purity doctrine) ├── Break: Inverted purity — red as honored scar, not dilution ├── Practices: Salt-water purification, padama knives, coastal vigils ├── Relation to Kirivs-bin: Within the bin communion — legends and Kirivis retained ├── Shore-Priests: Bloodcoast-ordained (disputed by Tita orthodoxy) └── Part Of: Ge'or — Demon Continent

docs.title: 🙏 Palonism
docs.text: "The stars gave a savior; the mind gives the way."

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Palonism is a variation of Shurtra practiced in Palonia, the mage republic of West Erisdar.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Keeps the star-born savior Mabode at its core.
  • Reworked by Palonia's mage culture: philosophy and magic are the highest devotion — the faithful seek wisdom and mastery through the arcane arts.
  • Scholarly and sophisticated. Palonia's magic schools are famous across the world, and Palonism shapes the republic's philosophical character.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text: • Majority: Palonia (mage republic)

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Palonism ] ├── Derives From: Shurtra ├── Deity: Mabode — star-born savior ├── Nations: Palonia ├── Character: Philosophical, mage-centered, sophisticated └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🪙 Pitraism
docs.text:
"The gods love gold. Prove you love it too."

Pitraism is the religion of the Silver Republic — a faith whose followers believe the gods love money and gold.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: The name comes from Pitra, a legendary figure who was supposedly "blessed" by the gods after he became rich — and went on to live for hundreds of years.

docs.title: Beliefs & Pantheon
docs.text:
• Wealth is divine favor. Gold is worship.
  • The Pitraist pantheon has dozens of gods — most borrowed from the dwarves, just as the Romans inspired themselves on the Greeks.
  • The Silver Republic is a direct partner and great ally of Dwarvengor, and dwarven religion was the direct inspiration for their own.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Pitraism ] ├── Founder-Legend: Pitra — blessed by the gods through wealth ├── Doctrine: The gods love money and gold ├── Pantheon: Dozens of gods, borrowed from the dwarves ├── Inspired By: Dwarvism ├── Nation: Silver Republic ├── Ally: Dwarvengor └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 😇 Pragmus
docs.text:
"We were made to mend what the world breaks."

Pragmus is the faith of the Angels of Alborric.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• The angels are the creation and employees of the god of Ge'or.
  • Their purpose is to strive to perfect the world.
  • 99.99% of angels are not evil — they genuinely work to make Ge'or a better place.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Although their homeland is the south pole, angels are around Ge'or:

  • They travel at the speed of light in their energetic form.
  • They usually take the form of humans — most people of Ge'or do not know angels are energy beings.
  • They can take the form of most beings on Ge'or and speak with them.
  • They can communicate, but it is super rare — when they do, it is for exceptional cases.
  • When they are seen, usually after a while — or as one gets closer — they disappear right in front of you. They have some tolerance for observers, as long as you do not come too close.
  • More often, Ge'or citizens see angels — usually their back, when the angel does not notice their presence — helping animals, planting trees, fixing broken things.
  • They are whimsical by nature and aesthetic. A child may see an angel and smile at him, just for the angel to disappear five seconds later.

Ge'or citizens see angels as legendary beings that are there to help Ge'or.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Pragmus ] ├── Species: Angels ├── Nations: Alborric (Polar Continent) ├── Deity: The god of Ge'or — the angels' creator and employer ├── Doctrine: Perfect the world; quiet, selfless good works ├── Apparitions: Angel Apparitions └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🙏 Religions
docs.text: A central hub for Ge'orian religions and faiths.

docs.title: Erisdar
docs.text:
• Erisian Church — dominant on Erisdar, worship of fabricated goddess Eris. Shadow-controlled.
  • Alegoria — northern Erisdar, worship of Julian the Dragon Tamer who became one with Fireborn.
  • Mannosta — North Erisdar, pagan faith of the Mann Order. Ancestors and stars. "Greatness of Mann" — Mann is the capital of the gods. In decline.
  • Spasian Faith — East Erisdar, worship of The Silver Bride as divine conduit to the creator. Only official religion in the Spasian Teocracy.
  • Shurtra — West Erisdar, star-born savior Mabode. Fierce enemy of the Erisian Church. Aenid Kingdom, Malbodor, Astravayne, Augagarten.
  • Ogoron — orc faith of Augamouth. The titanic orc who will avenge orc-kind and bring peace.
  • Yll-me — star-pattern pantheon. Mercur, Kille, Fezzanite Republic.
  • Charlmelism — faith of Aimeled. Former barbarian raiders, eternal rivals of the Erisian Theocracy.
  • Lyrical Followers — ancestor cult of the Lyrical Forest. Majority in Prosperity Port.
  • Elven Faith — the nature cults and elven gods of Elvennrin and Elvenkrad. The normal elfic religion, kept under Erisian pressure.
  • Onobor — paganism of Tetras. The Silver Bride as goddess and key to immortality. "Ring" in Tetrian.
  • Pitraism — faith of the Silver Republic. The gods love money and gold. Dwarven-inspired pantheon.
  • Suebism — pagan nature faith. Suebo, Direfirth, Yaro, Zane.
  • Palonism — Shurtra variation of the mage republic Palonia.
  • Sibbism — snake goddess faith of Xikxia and Zakarutia. 24 demigod sons believed to run the world's corners (myth).

docs.title: Catmen
docs.text:
• Calism — catmen philosophy-faith. Pacifism, gentleness, self-greatening. Marko, most catmen of Lumina.
  • Sytrenis — the most ancient catmen religion, from the hero Masaaki Sytrenis, "the Diplomat." Most Lesser Catmen still believe in it. Great Cattos.

docs.title: Lumina (& Mia)
docs.text:
• Gigaoism — theocracy of the Gigas Tribe: worship of a living telepathic dog-god (~290 AGD).
  • Maomism — Maoma Tribe creation faith (gods Tiodorus & Anedoris; beastmen as the rightful rulers of the rainforests; reformed to name the Gigas as enemies of the gods).
  • Lumism — Lumina Kingdom's imperial cult to the old Lumina Empire, with animism and jungle-animal reverence; goal of restoring the empire and the old beastmen ways.
  • Taosudism — the ancient troll faith (Orgor Kingdom, Mia): water is corruption, trolls are a pure race, dirt-tempered water is sacred.
  • Mukini Dirt-Faith — Mukini Tribe (Mia): all beings come from the dirt; the dirt is sacred; enduring earth-sculpture.

docs.title: Reformed / Heretical
docs.text: • Erinya — catmen heresy of the Erisian cult. Eris was a catmen woman who will return. Tolerated, not persecuted.

docs.title: Erisian Apostolic Institutions
docs.text:
• Apostles of Eris — the seven apostles of the Church: Alexa, Draco, Niccas, Ever, Aris, Malich, Maldorn.
  • Alexa Church State — independent Erisian church state (Grimmel Peninsula)
  • Draco Order — order state within the Erisian Empire
  • Order of Niccas — independent order (Grimmel Peninsula)
  • Ever Order — order state within the Erisian Empire

docs.title: Dwarven (Worldwide)
docs.text:
• Dwarvism — universal dwarven faith.
  • Coal Doctrine — southern. Peace, self-cultivation, communal living. Kobre, Lumina.
  • Diamond Doctrine — eastern. Commerce, wealth, growth. Dwarvengor, East Erisdar.
  • Emerald Doctrine — western. Mastery, efficiency, engineering. West and Central Erisdar.

docs.title: Dragons
docs.text:
• Diocronism — the old dragon faith of war and conquest. Perfection of the race, conquest of all corners. Succeeded by Daicrodism after the death wars.
  • Daicrodism — the dragon faith of atonement: peace and prosperity for all beings. Secluded in Kramsadar.

docs.title: Demon Continent
docs.text:
• Kirivs-bin — "the way of Kirivis." Demon warrior-spiritual path following their legends. The root of every demon sect.
  • Malgardism — Malgardian sect of Kirivs-bin (purple way). Malgardian Tribe + Tita miko priesthood; purity-of-form, smallness sacred.
  • Padamalgardism — Bloodcoast warrior subsect of Malgardism (red way). Bloodcoast red-haired Malgardian-human hybrids; padama knives, surf liturgy; minority Eris Church on same coast.
  • Zebekyo — Emberalden kobold faith. Father Dragon Zebe, shed-scale hatching; all Kobolds + Emberalden Lizardfolk; NOT a sect of Kirivs-bin.
  • Ignism — Blazeyard Flames faith. Atmosphere higher than soil; Aether-Lattice; Flame sect of Kirivs-bin (Kirivis as riser). Eldest Core.
  • Farsightism — Kutra Tribe owl-kin. Superpower as prayer; Ledger of the Far Sight; sect of Kirivs-bin to complete Kirivis's work.
  • Tolumin — Koebi Tribe green demons. Vash-ka, light-through-stone; unite the continent through shared sacred labor; sect of Kirivs-bin.
  • Demonism — Mountain Tribe Diablos ecumenical faith (Yak Island). Night-shift liturgy; "demonic" as open civic identity; sect of Kirivs-bin.
  • Gedarism — Xobkua giant faith. Prophet Gedar (~4,000y), goddess Miritha of fortune; ANTI-Kirivs-bin; cold war vs Asatru Empire; ally Zakarutia.
  • Ogoron — orc faith: titanic orc avenger → universal peace. Augamouth + Yakut (Yak subrace, Yak Island).
  • Kludosy — Estran High Catmen faith (Yak Island). Mutable genes (~90% catmen offspring); taboo on leveraging them; Central Erisdar persecution origin; NOT Kirivs-bin.
  • Oceanism — Yaoma Tribe merfolk. Ocean creatures perfect, land drafts; song-scrolls, tidal magic, pearl nacre; NOT Kirivs-bin.
  • Slimism — Glub Kingdom intelligent Slimes (Yak Island). Fission as sacrament, memory-sharing communion, radical equality; NOT Kirivs-bin.
  • Cubra Faith — Cubra Tribe plain Kirivs-bin (Yak Island); no sect marker; also covers Maomodor Kingdom plain Kirivs-bin (mainland, multi-racial). Neutral ground.

docs.title: Dissenbarg
docs.text:
• Helism — pantheon of domain-gods. Corin (sea/commerce), Cletas (reason), Maokas, Tissas (war), Lobas (nature), Gaelen (construction).
  • Enkrad Order — Erisian church colony (founded ~227 AGD, Venner-supported).

docs.title: Luminous Sea Islands
docs.text: • Nyity — astronomical faith of Moriat (human kingdoms Mikrad & Underfern). Sky gods descended and created humanity through suicidal sacrifice — their blood became all humans. One of the oldest faiths on Ge'or (~4,000 BGD). Mixed minority in half-elf kingdoms Gomor & Gildenrise (majority Elven Faith, no official religion). Human kingdom Dukedam on Minir is Erisian instead.

docs.title: Tuba Continent
docs.text:
• Mamanolism — animist faith of Mamanolo Tribe; worships all animals as divine (beastmen tribe, north Tuba).
  • Sytrenis — via Alkorri (Tuba Lesser Catmen tribe south of Mamanolo) — same as Great Cattos (Lumina), the diplomat Masaaki Sytrenis.

docs.title: Marti Continent
docs.text:
• Ulasm — pagan animist faith of Coldspeople; worships eagles as divine + ancestor worship (Great Cold). Core in Brase (southwest of Germina), also Coldspeople enclaves in Maboro.
  • Xuashism — recent wolvesfolk faith of Kut & Oigopol (Marti); god Xuashi promoted from animistic pantheon chief to sole deity, incarnated as Eris in Erisdar — father and mother of all religions on Ge'or. Also practiced by Wolvesfolk minority in Germina.
  • Moplilly — ancestor-veneration cult of Kobra (Marti cold-adapted Snake People; same race as Xikxia/Zakarutia but separated thousands of years ago). Demigod father-founder Xanob is most prayed-upon.
  • Multi-faith: Germina — melting pot: Sytrenis (catmen, as Great Cattos), many Erisian Church, plus other faiths. Maboro — coastal multiethnic: Coldspeople/Humans/beast people/demon merchants — several religions, no single creed.

docs.title: Xeti Continent (and Kumir)
docs.text:
• Wruowas — ultra-ancient faith of Koetebalo (Xeti ogre nation); cults Dabazi Ar Batr, the great serpent creator of all reality; celestial animism worshipping constellations as the serpent's scales.
  • Xuashism — also in Kyuu (Xeti Wolvesfolk nation south of Ograd) — same wolvesfolk faith as Marti's Kut/Oigopol.
  • Erinya — via Chuchao (Kumir Island, Xeti Erisdarian Catmen settlement, NW Kumir) — catmen heresy of Eris as catmen woman.

docs.title: Merratodoni & Crab Archipelago
docs.text: • Church of Krowretism — radical freedom-faith of Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni (refugees from Erisdar/Erisian Church ~100 BGD, now superpower unifying with Purple Coast as of 597 AGD, colonizing middle Merratodoni westwards) and Crab Union (Crab Archipelago, majority human + Seamen). Believes real human god is Krowret, the inner man — men descend from the gods directly — and monotheistic Eris religion is false; humans were deceived by demon Eris and must purify world from Eris and destroy her church; main sponsors of the Ironcloak. Absolute freedom (USA of Old Earth analogue).

docs.title: Karabar (Wolf Ocean)
docs.text: • Dresludo — god of the seas; faith of Karabar (Karabar Island, western Wolf Ocean). Believes Dresludo sent them to Karabar as penitence for sins; must achieve gnosis to be freed from suffering of earth.

docs.title: Lung Continent (Isolated)
docs.text: • Humanism — machine faith. Worship of absent humans as "sky gods." Born from The Elder's prophecy.

docs.title: Tabontabar
docs.text:
• Ximioli — "the way of the dragon." Moderation, modesty, family devotion.
  • Xatarism — cult of family, tradition, and the emperor. Meditation and monks.

docs.title: Sun Archipelago
docs.text: • South Sun Imperial Cult — ancestor-worship fused with imperial divinity. Emperor descended from the Sun.

docs.title: Polar Region
docs.text:
• Cult of Cleton — death cult of the Moonfang Dominion, child sacrifices to the Wolf God.
  • Pragmus — faith of the Angels: creation and employees of the god of Ge'or, sworn to perfect the world.

See: Erisian church, polygamy, The Sacrifice Ceremony

docs.title: 🙏 Shurtra
docs.text: "Mabode came from the stars to save humanity."

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Shurtra was founded by Mabode — a philosopher king born on Erima island roughly 200 years before the founding of the Erisian church (~200 BGD-era). A philosopher king by trade, Mabode eventually turned conqueror. In his delusion of grandeur, he began collecting myths of ancient peoples who came from the stars — and then claimed he came from them too. The people believed him.

The name Shurtra means "righteousness" in the Shurtraliot language — literally "righteous language".

Shurtra is therefore roughly 200 years older than the Erisian Church.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Mabode came from the stars to save humanity.
  • Mabode is a star-born savior, not a god of earth.
  • The faith demands extreme honor from its male followers — men are held to a standard of righteousness that few can sustain.

docs.title: Practices & Consequences
docs.text:
• Honor culture: Shurtra men are highly expected to be extremely honorable. Failure is shame beyond measure (see Honor Culture).
  • Death cults: This impossible standard makes death cults common — followers who believe they cannot live up to the faith choose death instead. This in turn leads authorities to usually crack down on the cults (see Death Cults).
  • Language: Shurtraliot is commonly spoken in the Aenid Kingdom.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Aenid Kingdom (founded here), Malbodor (Sandsmen), Astravayne, Augagarten
  • Aenid is situated in a desertic region — all of that area, including the island (Erima), is desert. Similarly, Augagarten is desertic, and Astravayne is a lot desertic too.

docs.title: Enmity with the Erisian Church
docs.text: Shurtra is a fierce enemy of the Erisian church. The Erisian Church conquered a lot of Shurtra's lands over the centuries — and the faith has never forgiven it. The star-born savior stands against the fabricated goddess Eris.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Shurtra ] ├── Founder: Mabode — philosopher king, star-born savior ├── Born At: Erima island (~200 years before the Erisian church) ├── Meaning: "Righteousness" — in Shurtraliot, "righteous language" ├── Age: ~200 years older than the Erisian church ├── Nations: Aenid Kingdom, Malbodor, Astravayne, Augagarten ├── Rival: Erisian church — conquered much of Shurtra's lands ├── Language: Shurtraliot ├── Character: Honor-bound, star-origin, death-cult tension └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🙏 Sibbism
docs.text: "The Goddess made us. Her sons hold the world's corners."

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Sibbism is the faith of the Snake People, practiced in both snake nations — Xikxia in West Erisdar and Zakarutia on the Demon Continent.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• The Snake Goddess is the founder of the snake people species — she made them, and she is the mother of their bloodlines.
  • Her 24 demigod sons are believed to run the 24 corners of the world — each son holding one corner in balance. The 24 corners are a myth, not geography: legless, dragging themselves across the earth, the snake people developed far more direction namings than humans — and the world's "corners" are the mythic expression of that fine-grained directional sense.
  • Ancestor Veneration weaves through the faith: the spirits of dead queens are said to watch from the heat-shimmer of the desert sands.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Xikxia, Zakarutia
  • A shared faith does not mend the sister-queens' feud — both crowns worship the same goddess and still prepare for war.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Sibbism ] ├── Deity: Snake Goddess — founder of the Snake People ├── Demigods: 24 snake sons — the 24 corners of the world (myth, born of snake directional naming) ├── Nations: Xikxia, Zakarutia ├── Species: Snake People ├── Practice: Ancestor veneration — dead queens in the heat-shimmer └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🟢 Slimism
docs.text:
"We were one. We divided to learn we were one."

Slimism is the faith of the Glub Kingdom — the intelligent Slimes of the small islands south of Yakut and east of Yaoma-controlled territory. Where most faiths worship a founder or a code, Slimism worships a physical state: the primordial gel from which all slimes divided, and to which every slime — intelligent or irrational — will eventually return. It is one of the only religions on Ge'or whose sacrament is literally its own biology.

The name Slimism is the Common exonym; Glub slimes call it Shlur-Ma — "the wet that waits to be one."

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Most slimes on Ge'or are irrational — instinct-driven, consuming, growing, dividing without thought. The Glub Kingdom's intelligent variant is the rare exception: a neural-density cluster within the gel grants reasoning, self-awareness, and — crucially — the ability to choose when to divide. In the Glub's telling, this capacity is not evolution's accident but Gel's invitation.

Slimism crystallized after the Glub learned memory-sharing — the direct transfer of liquid-thought between individuals — and discovered that two slimes who merge briefly can access a shared memory neither owned alone. The experience produced the faith's first axiom (~800 BGD, Elder Glub philosopher Muul Who Did Not Divide): we are more when we are one.

Muul lived 300 years without fission — enormous by slime standards — to prove that refusing division is itself worship. His eventual, voluntary division into three successors at the first Slimist convocation is still reenacted as liturgy.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• The Gel is one, division is exile — all slimes — intelligent Glub, common pond-slime, abyssal sea-slime — were once a single world-gel. Binary fission is not reproduction but exile-of-self from self. Intelligence is the Gel's way of noticing the exile.
  • Memory-sharing is communion — when slimes exchange liquid-thought, they literally taste each other's being. Slimism teaches this is not communication about unity — it is unity, partial and imperfect, and therefore holy.
  • Rejoining is eschatology — Slimism's end-time is not apocalypse but Re-Gel: a future when enough intelligent slimes choose simultaneous voluntary merging to reconstitute the primordial mass — not as mindless blob but as aware ocean. This will not consume other species; they will float in it as thoughts float in a mind.
  • Mass is virtue, but not vanity — Glub governance already weights votes by mass (larger slimes who have not divided recently carry more weight). Slimism sacralizes this: a slime who hoards mass without sharing memory is a miser; one who shares memory while refusing to divide for vainglory is a saint. Muul is the model: huge, undivided, and endlessly sharing.
  • Other species are "not-yet-gel" — Slimism is universalist in a uniquely gelatinous way: it holds that other species are simply less obviously gel — still divided, still learning that division hurts. Slimist outreach to Yakut and Zakarutia is therefore not conversion but pre-merging.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Voluntary non-division — the most demanding observance. A Slimist vows to delay fission for a set period (a season, a year, a decade), growing larger and — if faithful — more politically weighty while enduring the physical strain of unreleased mass. Breaking the vow without cause is shameful; breaking it to save another (by splitting to pass through a crack to rescue someone) is honored.
  • Confluence — the central rite: two or more slimes briefly merge gels at the edge, exchange a full memory, and re-separate. The shared memory becomes a relic: both participants remember it as theirs together, and their future fission-children inherit it as ancestral memory. Confluence between hostile Glub factions is the traditional peace treaty.
  • Salt and mineral tithing — slimes can absorb and later excrete pure mineral deposits. Glub mineral exports (rare salts prized across the Demon Continent) begin as Slimist tithing: the first pure excretion of a season is not sold but dissolved back into the sea at the islands' center as an offering to Re-Gel.
  • Dessication vigil — a deliberately dangerous asceticism: a volunteer slime exposes itself to controlled sun/wind at the edge of dessication, then is rescued by communal rehydration. The trauma is said to produce the clearest memory-sharing afterward; critics call it performative masochism.
  • No temples, but basins — Glub Kingdom worship is conducted in shallow, carved-basins where slimes gather at tide-low. The basins have no roof, no icon, no altar — only the exact right depth for a slime to rest half-submerged and reflect.

docs.title: Relation to Other Faiths
docs.text:
Slimism is recognizably alien even on the tolerant Demon Continent. Its claims cannot be adjudicated by Kirivs-bin (which measures honor through duel and legend) or by Sibbism (which counts snake sons). The Demon Continent's "shared demonic nationality" is what makes room for it: other nations agree to be unsettled without demanding Slimism explain itself better.

The Yaoma, who otherwise avoid the Glub Kingdom, note Slimism with theological horror: "a draft that refused to choose a perfection and decided instead to become the ocean." Slimists, who revere the Yaoma's own Oceanism from a distance, answer that Yaoma swim in perfection while slimes intend to become it — a difference of verb, not reverence.

Asatru scholars classify Slimism as a "gel-monist folk faith" — Glub diplomats, in their wet bubbling voice, politely ignore the label while asking if the scholars would like to confluence briefly and "see if the label still fits afterward." Few scholars accept.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Glub Kingdom — universal among intelligent Slimes; Elder Glub councils are simultaneously government, priesthood, and confluence-circle
  • Irrational kin: the faith considers non-intelligent slimes as "sleeping congregants" — they are not preached to, but they are not excluded from Re-Gel. A Glub Slimist may spend hours sitting with a pond-slime in silent basin-attendance.
  • Trade footprint: Glub mineral and salt exports carry Slimist tithe-memory — a few grains in every shipment are said to remember the confluence that blessed them; mainland alchemists half-believe this and pay premiums anyway
  • No missionaries, but curious invitations — Glub diplomats unsettle visitors by offering confluence as greeting; refusal is respected, but the offer is never withdrawn

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Slimism ] ├── Name: Slimism (Common) / Shlur-Ma — "the wet that waits to be one" (Glub) ├── First Teacher: Muul Who Did Not Divide — 300-year non-division, first confluence (~800 BGD) ├── Species: Slimes — amorphous gel-beings; majority irrational, rare intelligent variant with neural-density cluster ├── Nations: Glub Kingdom (small islands south of Yakut, Yak Island area) ├── Region: Demon Continent — Yak Island south ├── Type: Gel-monist eschatology — primordial Gel → divided exile → Re-Gel as aware ocean ├── Sacraments: Voluntary non-division, confluence (memory-sharing), salt/mineral tithing, dessication vigil, basins ├── Governance: Mass-consensus — larger undivided slimes carry more vote; same principle as faith's virtue └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: ☀️ South Sun Imperial Cult
docs.text:
"The Emperor is the Sun's shadow on earth. To honor the Emperor is to honor the light."

The South Sun Imperial Cult is the state religion of the South Sun Empire on the Sun Archipelago. It is a fusion of ancestor-worship and imperial divinity — the Emperor is believed to be descended directly from the Sun itself.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Settled during Age 1 by the Asian-looking human branch that migrated eastward after the Glorious Alliance crash, the South Sun Empire developed its faith in isolation. The cult's origins are lost to prehistory, passed down through oral tradition before writing reached the archipelago. By the time of the empire's formal founding, the Emperor's divine lineage was already considered unassailable truth.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• The Emperor is descended from the Sun — his blood carries the celestial mandate. His spiritual authority is absolute, even when his political power is not.
  • Ancestors watch and guide — the dead do not leave. They remain present, observing their descendants, and must be honored through ritual and remembrance.
  • The Sun sees all — sunlight is the Emperor's gaze. Darkness conceals dishonor. Oaths sworn in sunlight are unbreakable.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Ancestor shrines in every home — offerings of rice, incense, and written prayers.
  • Imperial festivals tied to the solar calendar — solstices, eclipses, and the Emperor's birth are sacred days.
  • Bushido-like warrior code — samurai equivalents serve their lords with absolute loyalty. Honor-suicides and ritualized warfare are extensions of the faith: to die with honor is to join the ancestors in the Sun's court.
  • Ritual purity — rice wine as ceremonial drink, purification before battle, sacred dueling grounds.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• State religion of the South Sun Empire on the Sun Archipelago.
  • Majority faith among Humans on the archipelago; minority Catmen typically follow the same practices.
  • A few Demons live in the empire but are ostracized — they are considered outside the Sun's mandate.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ South Sun Imperial Cult ] ├── Deity: The Sun — celestial ancestor of the imperial line ├── Sacred Figure: The Emperor — living descendant of the Sun ├── Practices: Ancestor worship, imperial festivals, ritual purity ├── Nation: South Sun Empire ├── Region: Sun Archipelago ├── Species: Humans (majority), Catmen (minority) ├── Culture: Bushido-like warrior code, rice agriculture, pagoda architecture └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🌙 Spasian Faith
docs.text:
"The Prophet saw the Silver Light. We carry it forward."

The Spasian Faith is the state religion of the Spasian Teocracy in East Erisdar, founded around the teachings of the Prophet Spasius during the chaos of the Lost Era (399–300 BGD). Unlike the Erisian Church, which venerates Eris as a divine figure, the Spasian faith holds that divinity resides in The Silver Bride — the planetary ring that encircles Ge'or. The ring's light is a direct conduit to the creator.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Spasius emerged during the worst century of Ge'orian history. The destruction of Baoth had thrown the continent into anarchy. Warlords ruled. Famine killed forty percent of the population. The Erisian cult was still consolidating, not yet dominant.

In this darkness, Spasius claimed to receive visions from the Silver Bride — the thin luminous band stretching horizon to horizon. He preached that the ring was not a celestial accident but a message: a line of divine light connecting every corner of the world, visible to all, belonging to none. His followers, the Argentines (from the ancient word for silver), spread across eastern Erisdar, establishing a faith that answered the despair of the age with the promise that the divine was visible — not hidden in temples or controlled by priests, but painted across the sky for anyone with eyes to see.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• The Silver Bride is divine — the ring is not a natural phenomenon. It is the creator's signature, left visible so that no one can claim the divine is absent.
  • The Argent Codex — the collected writings of Spasius, interpreted by the Council of Illuminants. It contains prophecies, moral teachings, and astrological calculations.
  • The Ring-Cycle — the ring's phases govern the liturgical calendar. Major civic decisions are deferred to astrologically favorable conjunctions. A decision made under the wrong phase invites failure.
  • No intermediaries — the Spasian faith rejects the Erisian model of a church hierarchy mediating between the faithful and the divine. Anyone can look up.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Ring-watching — the central devotional act. The faithful gather at dawn and dusk to observe the Silver Bride and recite passages from the Argent Codex.
  • Astrological governance — the Council of Illuminants, a body of twenty-one high priests, interprets the ring's phases. They select their own members from the priestly caste.
  • Missionary work — Spasian missionaries travel to neighboring lands. The Fractured State of Erislod regularly sends them back.

docs.title: Relations with Other Faiths
docs.text:
• Erisian Church — the Pontificate considers Spasian doctrine heretical. The Spasian clergy consider the Erisians spiritually blind — worshiping a fabricated goddess when the real divine is visible in the sky.
  • Silver Republic — the neighboring nation shares a coast and a name with Spasia but little else. The Republic views Spasian mysticism as anachronistic; Spasia views Republican secularism as a spiritual vacancy. Relations are tense but non-belligerent.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• State religion of the Spasian Teocracy (capital: Spasia) in East Erisdar.
  • Minority presence in the Silver Republic and Fractured State of Erislod.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Spasian Faith ] ├── Founder: Prophet Spasius — visionary of the Lost Era ├── Deity: The Silver Bride — the planetary ring as divine conduit ├── Sacred Text: Argent Codex ├── Governance: Council of Illuminants (21 high priests) ├── Nation: Spasian Teocracy (East Erisdar) ├── Liturgical Calendar: The Ring-Cycle ├── Rival Faith: Erisian church — mutual accusations of heresy ├── Neighbor: Silver Republic — shared coast, opposite worldviews ├── Practices: Ring-watching, astrological governance, missionary work └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🙏 Suebism
docs.text: "The land gives. Honor the land."

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Suebism is a pagan religion devoted to honoring nature, born on Suebo Island in West Erisdar — the faith takes its name from its birthplace.

The island itself carries the name "Suebo" — the dragon-language word for Romanium.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• A pagan faith centered on honoring nature.
  • Rites and reverence follow the land, the seasons, and the sea.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text: • Majority: Suebo (origin), Direfirth, Yaro, Zane

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Suebism ] ├── Meaning: "Suebo" = Romanium in the dragon language ├── Origin: Suebo Island — West Erisdar ├── Nations: Suebo, Direfirth, Yaro, Zane ├── Character: Pagan, nature-honoring └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Sytrenis
docs.text:
"The pen is a claw. The word is a shield. Sytrenis taught us both."

Sytrenis is the most ancient catmen religion — the faith of the hero Masaaki Sytrenis, who guaranteed that catmen would be able to live on Ge'or instead of being exterminated during the Human Age. In the old days it was the religion of catmen generally; today most of its believers are Lesser Catmen, and it is the faith of the Great Cattos nation.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Born from the life and deeds of Masaaki Sytrenis — "Sytrenis the Diplomat". In a time when the xenophobic empire of Termopolas was exterminating catmen, Sytrenis stopped a force that could have destroyed the continent and, with all the patience of a diplomat, ended the persecution for good. His name became sacred to the catmen, and his habits became their rites.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Diplomacy as sacred duty. Words first, claws second. A believer of Sytrenis resolves with negotiation what others would resolve with war.
  • The hero is the ancestor. Sytrenis is revered as the father of the lesser catmen; the faith calls on his example in every crisis.
  • Reverence over worship. Like many of the oldest faiths, Sytrenis is more tradition than theology — a way of being catmen, and of remembering that the catmen survive because one of them once spoke well.
  • The enemy of fanaticism. The faith remembers Termopolas-style xenophobia as the great evil; the believer opens doors, not borders.

docs.title: Adherents
docs.text:
• Great Cattos — the faith of the nation.
  • Most Lesser Catmen — the majority still believe in Sytrenis.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Sytrenis ] ├── Species: Catmen, especially Lesser Catmen ├── Founder: Masaaki Sytrenis — "the Diplomat" (born 1667 BGD) ├── Nations: Great Cattos ├── Core: Diplomacy is sacred; Sytrenis is the ancestor-hero ├── Age: The most ancient catmen religion └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Taosudism
docs.text:
"Water is the wound. Dirt is the cure. We are the pure."

Taosudism is the faith of trollkind — followed by the Orgor Kingdom on Mia and troll kingdoms across Ge'or. Like many species-specific faiths — such as the orcs' Ogoron — it is more tradition than religion: less a theology than the line that separates trolls from every other culture. It is multi-millennial, older than nearly every institution that now shares the world with it.

docs.title: The Water Taboo
docs.text:
Trolls fear water. Water burns their skin, cracks it, makes them suffer pain — for a troll, immersion is agony. From this physical truth grows the cosmic one:

  • Water is corrupt. All water-based beings — fish, the seafaring peoples, the sea itself — are of a corrupted nature.
  • Water is demonic. The beings of the deep are demons, or kin to them.
  • Trolls are pure. Trollkind alone was made untainted by the waters of the world — and must keep itself so.

docs.title: The Dirt-Water Rite
docs.text: Because clear water is toxic to them, trolls do not drink it as other races do. They mix their water with dirt: every pot of drinking water is blended with soil until it becomes mud-like, and that dirt-tempered water is safe — drinkable, sustaining, sacred. To drink clear water is to drink poison; to drink water tempered by the earth is to drink life.

docs.title: Doctrine
docs.text:
