• Purity of the land-born: trolls are the pure race because they came from the dirt, not from the water.
  • The corrupted waters: rivers, lakes, oceans, and the beings within them are tainted; contact brings physical and spiritual harm.
  • Tradition over theology: Taosudism has no temples, no priesthood, no scripture — it is lived, habitual, ancient, and ironclad. It exists to mark trollkind apart.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Taosudism ] ├── Species: Trolls ├── Nations: Orgor Kingdom (Mia), troll kingdoms worldwide ├── Kin Faith: Mukini Dirt-Faith — the earth-sacred faith of neighbouring Mukini Tribe ├── Core: Water is corrupt and demonic; trolls are a pure race; dirt-tempered water is sacred drink ├── Age: Multi-millennial tradition — more custom than religion └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🟢 Tolumin
docs.text:
"Every stone we cut together is a border erased."

Tolumin is the faith of the Koebi Tribe — the tall, green-colored demon subrace of the southern Demon Continent whose culture fuses hard work and meditation. Tolumin teaches that the purpose of the bin is to unite the Demon Continent — not through conquest like the Kutra superpower dream, but through shared labor made sacred.

It is a sect of Kirivs-bin that reads Kirivis as unifier rather than merely as revealer.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Tolumin emerged from Vash-ka — the Koebi meditative discipline in which physical labor and spiritual contemplation are one act. A Koebi stonecutter meditating through the cutting was already erasing the line between self and work; Tolumin erases the line between self and continent the same way.

The faith's name comes from tolu-min — "light-through-stone" — the moment when a Koebi-carved meditation chamber, hewn from a single boulder, is thinned enough that dawn light passes through without breaking the walls.

Around ~250 BGD, the Koebi monastery-council — the most accomplished Vash-ka practitioners, who lead by demonstration rather than election — declared that the highest practice of the bin is not individual perfection but continental coherence. Kirivis revealed that the Shadows divided Ge'or; to honor him is to mend division, beginning with the Demon Continent itself.

Tolumin has no prophet, only exemplary stonecutters. Its "saints" are remembered as the builders of particular chambers, bridges, and terraces that still stand centuries later.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Kirivis is the unifier — Tolumin's reading of the last great legend foregrounds what Asatru histories minimize: Kirivis did not only uncover the Hybrian conspiracy — he briefly united disparate demon tribes into a single war host to fight it. That unity, not just the revelation, is the lesson.
  • Work is the sacrament of unity — every act of labor performed meditatively and offered without territorial claim is a prayer for the continent. A Koebi stonecutter carving a meditation chamber for the Zakarutia snake-queen's palace (as once happened) was Toluist worship, not mere commission.
  • Meditation dissolves borders — Vash-ka extended to diplomacy: to meditate alongside someone of another tribe for a week is to make them a co-worker, and co-workers do not make borders.
  • The continent is one workshop — Tolumin envisions the Demon Continent as a single atelier with many benches: Asatru hammering policy, Malgardians binding lineage, Flames holding sky, Kutra planning flight, Yak hammering modestly. No bench is master.
  • Asceticism as shared surplus — bin simplicity becomes Toluist economics: surplus from efficient, meditative work is not hoarded but offered — as gifts, joint projects, and unclaimed infrastructure (roads, wells, meditation halls) that any traveler may use.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Vash-ka labor — every task — farming, stonework, metalwork, diplomacy itself — is approached as meditation. There is no menial labor in Tolumin; all work is sacred.
  • Chamber carving — the signature practice: carving a meditation chamber from a single boulder until light passes through. The first light-through is celebrated as a minor festival; the chamber is then gifted or left open for any wayfarer.
  • Joint-work pilgrimage — Koebi bands travel to other demon nations to labor alongside their hosts for a season (building a terrace in Maomodor Kingdom, repairing a Blazeyard pass, helping Kutra shore a riverbank). The labor is the pilgrimage.
  • Meditation exchange — Koebi councils host long, silent sittings with delegations from other tribes — sometimes days without a word. Decisions made afterward are considered Toluist consensus even when no formal vote was taken.
  • Honor duel, Koebi form — a duel of endurance, not combat: two disputants perform the same difficult physical task (holding a stone overhead, carrying water without spilling) until one yields gracefully. To endure longer and still yield is highest honor.

docs.title: Relation to Kirivs-bin
docs.text:
Tolumin is Kirivs-bin universalized.

  • Shares every tenet: legends are scripture, Kirivis is the last great legend, action is prayer, honor is earned, comfort is the enemy
  • Where plain Kirivs-bin is individual (each demon walks the way alone), Tolumin is continental — the way is walked together, as a single people
  • Where Farsightism wants a superpower built by statecraft, Tolumin wants unity built by shared work — the difference is often framed as Kutra planning unity vs. Koebi practicing it
  • No priesthood apart from the monastery-council; no temples apart from open meditation chambers — structurally the closest sect to plain Kirivs-bin, and therefore the least controversial among Asatru purists

Asatru theologians call Tolumin "the bin at its most generous." Some Kutra strategists call it "the bin at its most naive" — and then invite Koebi mason-teams anyway.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Koebi Tribe — universal; the monastery-council is both government and synod
  • Minority/admired: small Toluist circles in Maomodor Kingdom (which shares the multi-species "demonic nationality" instinct), Blazeyard passes, and Asatru craft guilds
  • Craft reputation: Koebi-crafted tools, weapons, and meditation chambers traded across the continent carry implicit Toluist witness — "we made this for you, not only for ourselves"
  • Diplomatic role: historically the most welcome demon mediators; the Zakarutia snake-queen's chamber commission became legend precisely because a green stonecutter-monk negotiated nothing and offered everything

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Tolumin ] ├── Name: tolu-min — "light-through-stone" ├── Type: Sect of Kirivs-bin — unification reading ├── Last Great Legend: Kirivis as unifier (not only revealer) ├── Nations: Koebi Tribe (majority); admired in Maomodor Kingdom, Blazeyard, Asatru Empire craft circles ├── Species: Koebi — taller green demons, meditative work culture, Vash-ka discipline ├── Region: Demon Continent — south, southeast of Maomodor Kingdom ├── Founded: ~250 BGD — monastery-council declaration; no single prophet ├── Virtue: Unity through shared sacred labor; borders erased by co-work ├── Practices: Vash-ka, chamber carving, joint-work pilgrimage, meditation exchange ├── Distinction vs Farsightism: Unity by practice, not by superpower plan └── Part Of: Ge'or — Demon Continent

docs.title: 🦅 Ulasm
docs.text:
"The eagle sees the ancestors. The ancestors see us."

Ulasm is the pagan animist faith of the Coldspeople — practiced in Brase and in Coldspeople communities in Maboro on Marti Continent.

The faithful worship eagles as sacred and venerate ancestors — the two intertwined.

docs.title: Tenets
docs.text:
• Eagle Animism — eagles are not messengers of the divine; they are divine. The eagle's flight, sight, and hunting are prayer. Eagle feathers are relics; to harm an eagle is sacrilege.
  • Ancestor Worship — the dead do not leave. Ancestors dwell in the Great Cold (the eternal winter where souls rise with funeral smoke) and watch the living through eagle eyes. An eagle circling a settlement is an ancestor checking on kin.
  • Cold as Sacred — the frigid climate that Coldspeople thrive in is itself holy — the Great Cold is both afterlife and god. Warmth is profane to the extreme faithful.

docs.title: Followers
docs.text:
• Brase (Marti Continent, southwest of Germina) — core nation, Coldspeople majority. Ulasm is the state faith in practice, though Brase has no formal theocracy.
  • Coldspeople enclaves in Maboro — multiethnic coastal nation, where Ulasm coexists with other faiths.
  • Smaller Coldspeople communities in northern Lumina and high Xeti carry Ulasm outward.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Funeral pyres at dusk — smoke rising to the Great Cold, watched for eagle silhouettes.
  • Eagle-feather talismans for newborns, warriors, and elders.
  • Winter-Telling stories include the Eagle-Ancestor cycle — the myth of the first eagle who carried the first ancestor's soul to the sky.

docs.title: History
docs.text: Ulasm predates the Erisian Church on Marti by millennia — it is the old Coldspeople faith, preserved through the Great Divergence and the Marti colonization waves.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: Marti Continent
  • Nations: Brase, Maboro (Coldspeople communities)
  • Species: Coldspeople
  • Related: Great Cold (afterlife), Coldspeople collectivist culture

docs.title: 🐉 Wruowas
docs.text:
"Dabazi Ar Batr coils around the sky."

Wruowas is the ultra-ancient faith of Koetebalo — the ogre nation on Xeti Continent (northeast of Kyuu, east of Ograd). The only ogre nation in the world.

The faithful cult Dabazi Ar Batr — the great serpent creator of all reality — and practice celestial animism: they worship constellations in the sky as the serpent's scales.

docs.title: Tenets
docs.text:
• Dabazi Ar Batr as Creator — the great serpent who created all reality — not just Ge'or, not just the sky, but existence itself. Every star is a scale; every constellation is a coil.
  • Celestial Animism — the sky is not empty. Constellations are living scripture. To read the stars is to read the serpent's body. Ogre astronomer-priests (Stone-Seers) chart the serpent's movements.
  • Ultra-Ancient — Wruowas predates every other faith on Xeti by millennia. Its chants are in a language no other species remembers. Koetebalo's ogres claim Dabazi Ar Batr spoke before the Great Divergence, before the Hybrian crash.

docs.title: Followers
docs.text:
• Koetebalo (Xeti Continent) — ogre nation, Wruowas is the state faith. Every ogre family keeps a sky-chart.
  • No significant diaspora — Wruowas is uniquely ogre.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Night vigils on high ground — lying on back, watching the serpent's coils turn.
  • Constellation naming — each ogre child is named for the constellation dominant at their birth.
  • Serpent dance — slow, coiling processions that mimic Dabazi Ar Batr's celestial movement.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: Xeti Continent (Koetebalo)
  • Nation: Koetebalo
  • Species: Ogres
  • Deity: Dabazi Ar Batr (great serpent creator of all reality)
  • Related: Ogres solitary culture, Xeti Continent ancient faiths

docs.title: 🙏 Xatarism
docs.text:
"The family endures. The tradition holds. The emperor rules."

Xatarism is the cult of family, tradition, and the emperor — the faith of the three Tabontabar kingdoms: the Northern Kingdom, Central Kingdom, and Southern Kingdom.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Family — the household is the sacred unit; loyalty flows upward through the bloodlines.
  • Tradition — the ways of the ancestors are the law; nothing true is new.
  • The Emperor — the emperor stands at the head of the great family of the nation, owed the same devotion as an honored ancestor.
  • Meditation — the faithful believe in meditation, and the continent is full of monks.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text: • Monasteries and monk-orders fill the kingdoms — the clergy meditate, keep the traditions, and tend the temples.

docs.title: Psychic Talents
docs.text: Some people of Tabontabar are capable of minor psychic abilities — such as telekinesis and telepathy. The talent is attested across the continent, treated by the kingdoms as a mark of unusual souls. In truth it is mage-cell channeling refined toward mental places: where mages elsewhere push their power outward, Tabontabar sensitives route theirs into thought itself — and channel it better than even practiced mages.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Northern Kingdom, Central Kingdom, Southern Kingdom
  • Coexists with Ximioli — the older dragon-way philosophy of family devotion, and the more popular of the two faiths on the continent.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Xatarism ] ├── Character: Cult of family, tradition, and the emperor ├── Practices: Meditation, monks, monasteries ├── Nations: Northern Kingdom, Central Kingdom, Southern Kingdom ├── Region: Tabontabar Continent ├── Coexists With: Ximioli ├── Talent: Minor psychic abilities (telekinesis, telepathy) — mage-cells channeled toward mental places, refined beyond ordinary mages └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🐉 Ximioli
docs.text:
"The dragon does not roar. The dragon endures."

Ximioli — "the way of the dragon" — is the traditional faith of Tabontabar Continent. Settled during Age 1 by the Asian-looking human branch that migrated eastward after the Glorious Alliance crash, Tabontabar developed its spiritual culture in long isolation from the rest of Ge'or.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Ximioli emerged alongside the first agricultural kingdoms of Age 3, when the Asian-branch humans began their long development toward imperial culture. The dragon — a creature known from the ancient legends carried across the sea — became the central symbol of the good life: powerful but restrained, fearsome but wise, present but not demanding.

Unlike the dragon-worship of Age 4, which treated dragons as literal gods to be obeyed, Ximioli treats the dragon as a metaphor for the ideal person. One does not worship the dragon. One becomes the dragon — through discipline, moderation, and devotion to family.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Moderation in all things — excess is the enemy of wisdom. The dragon does not gorge; it takes only what it needs.
  • Modesty before others — pride invites challenge. Humility invites peace. The greatest person in the room is the one who does not need to announce it.
  • Simplicity of life — wealth is weight. Possessions are chains. The dragon needs no palace — it rests where it wishes.
  • Family is the foundation — the highest calling is not glory or power, but raising children who will carry the way forward. A family line that endures for generations is the truest success.
  • Harmony with nature — the dragon does not conquer the land. It lives within it.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Ancestor tablets — every home maintains a shrine to departed family members. Offerings of rice, tea, and incense are made daily (see Ancestor Veneration).
  • Dragon festivals — seasonal celebrations tied to the agricultural calendar, featuring dragon dances, paper lanterns, and communal meals.
  • Family records — lineages are meticulously documented. The longer the recorded line, the greater the family's honor.
  • Meditation gardens — cultivated spaces for quiet reflection, designed to embody the dragon's balance of strength and stillness (see Meditation).

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Traditional faith of all three Tabontabar kingdoms: Northern Kingdom, Central Kingdom, and Southern Kingdom.
  • Coexists with Xatarism — the imperial cult of family, tradition, and the emperor. Of the two faiths, Ximioli is the more popular across the continent.
  • Majority among Humans; Catmen minority typically follow Ximioli practices with local variations.
  • Demons — who live in Tabontabar but are ostracized — generally do not follow Ximioli, as the faith's emphasis on family lineage excludes outsiders.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Ximioli ] ├── Meaning: "The way of the dragon" ├── Philosophy: Moderation, modesty, simplicity, family devotion ├── Symbol: The dragon — a metaphor for the ideal life ├── Nations: Northern Kingdom, Central Kingdom, Southern Kingdom ├── Region: Tabontabar Continent ├── Species: Humans (majority), Catmen (minority) ├── Practices: Ancestor tablets, dragon festivals, family records, meditation gardens ├── Settled: Age 1 — Asian human migration eastward └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🐺 Xuashism
docs.text:
"Xuashi was, Xuashi is, Xuashi will be Eris."

Xuashism is the recent faith of the Wolvesfolk — practiced in Kut and Oigopol on Marti Continent and Kyuu on Xeti Continent.

The faithful believe in Xuashi — their god, who was once the main god of their old animistic pantheon, recently promoted to sole supreme deity after a theological revolution. They believe Xuashi incarnated in Erisdar as Eris — and is therefore the father and mother of all other religions on Ge'or.

docs.title: Tenets
docs.text:
• Xuashi as Supreme — formerly the chief of many spirits, Xuashi was elevated to the God. The old animistic pantheon is now his court.
  • Incarnation as Eris — Xuashi incarnated in Erisdar as Eris — the fabricated goddess of the Erisian Church. To Xuashists, Eris is not a Shadow fabrication but Xuashi in borrowed flesh.
  • Father and Mother of All Faiths — because Xuashi-as-Eris founded the Erisian Church, and the Church birthed or opposed every other faith, Xuashi is the metaphysical parent of all Ge'orian religions. Every prayer, even to other gods, ultimately reaches Xuashi.
  • Recent Revolution — Xuashism is recent — within the last centuries. The faithful still remember the old animistic-pagan days. Elders can tell you when their village switched.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• Animistic past: Wolvesfolk were animistic pagans, each spirit for river, hunt, and pack.
  • Promotion of Xuashi: Xuashi, the chief hunt-sky spirit, was elevated to monotheism — a deliberate reform by wolvesfolk theologians who sought unity across the three dispersed nations (Kut, Oigopol, Kyuu).
  • Eris identification: Missionaries who encountered Erisian lore identified Eris's iconography with Xuashi's — same light, same promise. The incarnation doctrine was born.

docs.title: Followers
docs.text:
• Kut (Marti Continent, south of Maboro) — Wolvesfolk nation, Xuashist.
  • Oigopol (Marti Continent, northeast of Kobra, east of Maboro) — Wolvesfolk nation, Xuashist.
  • Kyuu (Xeti Continent, south of Ograd) — Wolvesfolk nation, Xuashist.
  • Large Wolvesfolk minority in Germina includes Xuashists, though Germina is multi-faith.

docs.title: Dark Current — Wolvesfolk and the Moonfang Trade
docs.text:
A grim corollary: Wolvesfolk are frequently kidnapped by pirates and sold to the Moonfang Union — even though the wolvesfolk nations (Kut, Oigopol, Kyuu on Marti/Xeti) are on the other side of the world from Moonfang Union in the far north. The trade persists because wolvesfolk are prized for their pack-loyalty and cold-resilience — and because the Moonfang Dominion pays in Romanium.

This slave piracy is a recent atrocity that Xuashist clergy denounce as the ultimate perversion of pack — to steal a wolf from his pack is to steal his soul.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: Marti Continent (Kut, Oigopol) + Xeti Continent (Kyuu)
  • Nations: Kut, Oigopol, Kyuu
  • Species: Wolvesfolk
  • Deity: Xuashi
  • Related: Erisian Church (Eris as incarnation), Moonfang Union slave trade, Wolvesfolk pack culture

docs.title: 🙏 Yll-me
docs.text: "The stars are not scattered — they are written."

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Yll-me is a star-worshiping faith, majority in Mercur, Kille, the Fezzanite Republic, with a presence in Aimeled and within Prassen-Albridge inside the Erisian Empire.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• The stars in the sky form certain patterns.
  • Each pattern is attributed to a god of their pantheon — the constellations are the gods' signatures.
  • Worship centers on reading and honoring those celestial patterns.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Mercur, Kille, Fezzanite Republic
  • Some: Aimeled, Prassen-Albridge (Erisian Empire)

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Yll-me ] ├── Doctrine: Star patterns = gods of the pantheon ├── Nations: Mercur, Kille, Fezzanite Republic (majority); Aimeled, Prassen-Albridge (some) ├── Character: Celestial, pattern-reading, pantheonic └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: 🦎 Zebekyo
docs.text:
"The hunt remembers. The scales do not lie."

Zebekyo is the faith of the Emberalden Lizardfolk — a taller, stronger subrace of Kobolds who built a permanent nation on the Demon Continent where their smaller cousins manage only warrens. Where standard kobolds have no faith beyond survival and traps, Zebekyo gives the Emberalden a hunter's theology: the Great Hunt is prayer, prey is scripture, and every scale records a deed.

The name Zebekyo comes from the old kobold tongue: zebek ("scale-that-holds") + yo ("way" or "road") — the way of the scale that holds.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
Zebekyo emerged after the Emberalden split from the kobold warrens and settled the sun-warmed flats northwest of Blazeyard. Freed from tunnel-dark and trap-anxiety, the taller lizardfolk began to hunt in the open — and to ask why some hunts succeed and others fail in ways that skill alone could not explain.

The first Zebekyo teaching is attributed to Scar-Throat Vekka, a hunt-leader who tracked a shadow-cat for nine days in the Age 8 wastes and returned with its skull, claiming the beast had allowed itself to be taken because the hunt had been "true." Her account — recited at every Great Hunt since — became the seed of the faith: prey and hunter are partners in a rite that the land itself judges.

Zebekyo does not claim a divine founder. It claims that the hunt itself is the teacher, and Vekka was merely the first to listen well.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• The hunt is liturgy — every stage of the hunter's sequence (track → stalk → strike → return → share) is a sacred office. To rush a stage is sacrilege; to skip one is to hunt without the land's permission.
  • Scales hold debts — an Emberalden's scales are believed to darken subtly with each worthy kill and pale with each wasteful one. Elders "read" a youth's hide before approving their solo rite. This is partly myth, partly the real way scales scar and stain with diet and sun.
  • Zebek — the First Scale — a mythic ur-kobold whose every scale was a flawless hunting record. Some tales say Zebek grew until its scales became Emberalden's stone flats; others say it still walks the savanna at night, judging hunts.
  • No temples, but kill-circles — Zebekyo has no closed buildings. Its holy sites are open-air rings of predator skulls (kill-circles) where the year's Great Hunt is opened and closed with chants that list every species taken fairly.
  • Sharing is absolution — meat kept is meat wasted in the spiritual sense. A hunter who does not share the kill with clan, hatchlings, and even rival clans has not completed the rite.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Solo skull rite — at ~14 years, every Emberalden must hunt alone and return with a predator skull (not scavenged) to be recognized as adult. Failure is not exile — the youth may try again each season until they succeed; persistence is itself a valued sign.
  • Great Hunt — an annual week-long communal hunt whose order of precedence determines social standing for the year ahead. The clan-mother or strongest hunter leads, but "strength" is measured in clean hunts: efficient, minimal-suffering kills with full use of the carcass.
  • Scale-reading — elders examine a hunter's neck and shoulder scales under midday sun to assess their year. Dark, even coloration is praised; bleached or patchy tones prompt counseling or fasting hunts.
  • Bone-craft as prayer — tools, amulets, and dwelling ornaments carved from bone are made with chants naming the animal, the hunt date, and the hunter's intent. A well-made bone knife is a minor relic.

docs.title: Relation to Other Faiths
docs.text:
Zebekyo is local and non-proselytizing. It does not compete with Kirivs-bin or Malgardism — many Emberalden who trade with Malgardian Tribe and Blazeyard attend Malgardist shrines or respect the bin without contradiction. In Emberalden itself, however, Zebekyo is universal and unchallenged.

The Asatru Empire, which trades for Emberalden leather and bone-craft, officially classifies Zebekyo as a "hunt custom" rather than a religion — a diplomatic fiction that lets both sides avoid theological debate while doing business.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text:
• Majority: Emberalden — universal among the lizardfolk; the faith and the nation are inseparable
  • Minority: small kobold-blooded enclaves along the Emberalden–Malgardian border who have adopted Zebekyo alongside warren-survival habits
  • Heavily respected by Malgardian Tribe hunters (who sometimes seek Emberalden "scale-reading" before major expeditions) and tolerated by Blazeyard Flames as "a fireless way of being precise"
  • Standard Kobolds in tunnels regard Zebekyo with awe and resentment — proof that their kin can build something they cannot

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Zebekyo ] ├── Name: zebek ("scale-that-holds") + yo ("way") — old kobold tongue ├── Mythic Figure: Zebek — the First Scale, whose scales became the land ├── First Teacher: Scar-Throat Vekka — nine-day shadow-cat hunt (Age 8 tradition) ├── Nations: Emberalden (universal) ├── Species: Emberalden Lizardfolk — kobold subrace (taller, stronger, surface-dwelling) ├── Neighbor Relations: Malgardian Tribe, Blazeyard (trade partners, theological coexistence) ├── Practices: Solo skull rite, Great Hunt, scale-reading, bone-craft, kill-circles ├── Character: Hunt-as-liturgy, scales as moral record, sharing as rite-completion └── Part Of: Ge'or — Demon Continent

docs.title: 🙏 Erinya
docs.text: "Eris was one of us — a catmen woman."

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: Erinya is the catmen version of the Erisian cult, consistent in Central Erisdar. It is considered a heresy by the Erisian church — but Erinya followers are not persecuted.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• Eris was a woman called Erinya — and she was a catmen woman.
  • Erinya will come back from the dead.
  • When she returns, she will give infinite richness to all catmen.
  • Meanwhile, everybody else will be poor and serve the catmen — although not in an evil way. The rule of catmen is framed as benevolent, not cruel.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text: • Practiced by: Catmen communities in Central Erisdar

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Erinya ] ├── Origin: Catmen reinterpretation of the Erisian cult ├── Claim: Eris was a catmen woman named Erinya ├── Promise: Erinya returns from death → infinite riches for catmen, others serve (benevolently) ├── Status: Heresy — tolerated, not persecuted ├── Region: Central Erisdar ├── Species: Catmen └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: ⛪ Erisian Church
docs.text:
The dominant religious institution of Erisdar, built around the worship of Eris — Goddess of Discord. The entire faith is a fabrication: the Myth of Eris was engineered by Hybrian Shadows around −400 BAC as a tool to centralize human kingdoms for easier control.

Despite being a lie, the Church holds real political and cultural power across the continent. Its institutions are cracking in the modern era.

docs.title: Rivals & Heresies
docs.text:
• Shurtra — a star-born faith 200 years older than the Church, founded by Mabode. The Church conquered much of Shurtra's lands, making the two faiths fierce enemies. Star-born savior vs fabricated goddess.
  • Erinya — a catmen heresy of the Erisian cult, consistent in Central Erisdar. Claims Eris was a catmen woman. Considered heresy but tolerated, not persecuted.

docs.title: The Apostles
docs.text: The Church canon holds that Eris chose seven apostles to spread her word — each founding an order, church state, or territory that bears their name: Alexa (Alexa Church State), Draco (Draco Order), Niccas (Order of Niccas), Ever (Ever Order), Aris (Arisdian), Malich, and Maldorn. See Apostles of Eris.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Erisian Church ] ├── Worships: Eris — Fabricated Goddess ├── Created By: Hybrians, Shadows — ~400 BAC ├── Tool: Myth of Eris, Eris facade ├── Political Arm: Pontificate of Eris ├── Sacred Text: The Eris Saga ├── Leader: The Highest — possessed by a Shadow upon election ├── Apostles: Apostles of Eris — Alexa, Draco, Niccas, Ever, Aris, Malich, Maldorn ├── Critics: Ironcloak — Knows it's a lie ├── Rivals: Shurtra — star-born faith, conquered lands ├── Heresy: Erinya — catmen version, tolerated └── Decline: Institutions cracking, dogmas failing

docs.title: Angels
docs.text:
"They are not divine. They only look that way." — Kramsadar dragon, when asked about the beings at the south pole

Angels are not divine messengers — whatever they may believe about themselves, they are a species that looks angelic: winged, luminous, serene. The name stuck because no one who has seen one has ever come up with anything better.

An angel is an energy being capable of taking physical form. Their natural state is not flesh, but light — coherent, intelligent patterns of energy that can condense into a humanoid shape when they choose. Most people on Ge'or do not know they are energy beings — angels usually take the form of humans. The winged, luminous form of legend is a choice too, and it is kept for the rare encounters that become stories.

docs.title: Nature
docs.text:
• Energy beings — not flesh and blood in the conventional sense. Their bodies are solidified light, sustained by an internal energy core.
  • Light-speed travel — in their energetic form, angels can travel to places at the speed of light.
  • Form-shifting — an angel can take the form of most beings on Ge'or and speak with them. In daily life they usually take the form of humans — most people never realize what they are
  • Whimsical — angels are whimsical creatures by nature and aesthetic.
  • Rare communicators — angels can communicate, but it is super rare; when they do, it is for exceptional cases.
  • Disappearing — when they are seen, usually after a while — or as you get closer — they disappear right in front of you. They tolerate observers up to a point, as long as you do not come too close.
  • Active helpers — although their homeland is the south pole, they are around Ge'or: helping animals, planting trees, fixing broken things, often unseen.
  • Legendary — Ge'or citizens see them as legendary beings that are there to help Ge'or. Sightings are usually of their back, when the angel does not notice the observer's presence. A child may see an angel and smile at him, just for the angel to disappear five seconds later.
  • Not evil — 99.99% of angels are not evil; they strive to make Ge'or a better place.

docs.title: Religion
docs.text: Angels follow Pragmus — they believe themselves to be the creation and employees of the god of Ge'or, and that they should strive to perfect the world.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Tall (1.8–2.1 meters), slender, with large feathered wings (spanning 3–4 meters). Pale skin, hair in shades of white, silver, and pale gold. Eyes are luminous — pale blue, silver, or violet
  • Lifespan: 300–500 years. Angels age slowly and are among the longest-lived species on Ge'or
  • Mage-cell expression: The highest baseline of any species. Every angel is born with significant magical ability — light manipulation, flight enhancement, and healing are universal. Combat magic is rarer but devastating
  • Wings: Fully functional. Angels can fly for hours without fatigue. Their feathers are individually prehensile — an angel's wing can gesture with the precision of a hand
  • Cold Adaptation: Perfectly adapted to the polar climate. Angels do not feel cold. Their body temperature runs high, and they can sleep in snow without harm

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Angelic society in Alborric is ancient and insular — the polar mountains have been their home for millennia — yet their presence is felt across Ge'or.

  • Governance: The Luminous Council — seven eldest angels chosen for wisdom, not lineage. Decisions are made by consensus after deliberation that can last years
  • Culture: Austere and contemplative at home; whimsical and light-footed abroad. Angels value silence, study, and the perfection of a single craft over a lifetime
  • Relations: The Dragons of Kramsadar are the only people who regularly interact with them — described as "mutual respect between two peoples who understand what it means to be alone." Most of Ge'or holds angels as legend

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Alborric (Polar Continent)
  • Faith: Pragmus
  • Phenomenon: Angel Apparitions
  • Traits: Winged, long-lived, highest mage-cell expression, light-speed travel, form-shifting, polar-adapted, whimsical helpers

docs.title: Catmen
docs.text: One of the Six Main Races of Ge'or — a feline humanoid species found on nearly every continent. Catmen are characterized by cat ears, tails, and a playful, ego-less disposition that makes them the most universally beloved species in the world. They live everywhere: as nomads, in kingdoms, and in cities with playful names.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Humanoid with cat ears and tail. Hair (and fur) comes in every color — purple, white, black, green, blue, and all shades between. Build varies by subrace: Lesser Catmen are smaller and delicate, High Catmen are robust and broad-shouldered, Erisdarian Catmen are bright-haired and feminine, Merratodonian Catmen are lean and forest-colored
  • Lifespan: 65–90 years depending on subrace
  • Mage-cell expression: Low. Some Merratodonian Catmen develop minor plant-communication abilities. Catmen prefer agility and wit to spells
  • Traits: Exceptional agility, balance, and curiosity. Keen hearing. Catmen are naturally playful — their games, dances, and pranks are copied across Ge'or

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Catmen society is decentralized and cheerful. There is no single catmen empire — instead, catmen integrate into the societies of other species, or found their own playful nations.

  • Governance: Varies by nation — Estran is an elective monarchy of High Catmen, Lake Kingdom and Great Cattos are Lesser Catmen kingdoms, Marko is ruled by elected High Catmen on an international council. Nomadic catmen answer to no one
  • Culture: Ego-less, silly, and gullible — but brilliant at commerce. Catmen are the trend-setters of Ge'or; their fashions are copied by all species. Their cities and nations follow a playful naming pattern: descriptor + "ko" (see Naming Convention)
  • Relations: Universally loved. No species wages war on catmen — armies simply pass through their territories. Humans of the Venner aristocracy are famously fond of them; the Erisian church forbids human-catmen marriages, but the prohibition is widely ignored
  • Military: Weak by default — catmen survive through universal affection rather than arms
  • Religion: Most catmen follow Calism — a pacifist, gentle philosophy-faith that seeks to greaten oneself. Majority in Marko; most catmen of Lumina follow it as well. The most ancient catmen faith is Sytrenis, founded by the hero Masaaki Sytrenis; most Lesser Catmen still believe in it

docs.title: Subraces
docs.text:
• High Catmen — Mediterranean appearance, black-haired, more masculine build (Estran, Demon Continent)
  • Erisdarian Catmen — bright-colored hair, Central European look, feminine, wandering storytellers (Erisdar, Lumina Continent, worldwide)
  • Lesser Catmen — smaller, all colors, the ultimate comic relief, universally liked, nomadic. Born of hunger: the breed appeared out of the Termopolas catmen extermination of the Human Age, as starving catmen were forever changed (everywhere)
  • Merratodonian Catmen — forest-adapted, muted greens and browns, agile climbers (Merratodoni)

docs.title: Nations
docs.text: Catmen live everywhere — as nomads, in kingdoms, and in cities with playful names: - Estran — High Catmen (Yak Island, Demon Continent) - Cattos — island nation of Erisdarian Catmen and Lesser Catmen (Lumina Continent) - Great Cattos — Lesser Catmen country (Lumina Continent) - Lake Kingdom — Lesser Catmen kingdom (Lumina Continent) - Marko — ruled by elected High Catmen (Kutten) - Minorities in: Gigas Tribe, Lumina Republic, Cammao Kingdom, Venner, and countless others

docs.title: Naming Convention
docs.text: Catmen names follow a simple pattern: descriptor + "ko": - "alcohol cat" → Alko - "tall cat" → Tallko Cities and nations follow similarly: Cattos, Great Cattos.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• One of the Six Main Races: Humans, Dwarves, Elves, Demons, Beast Races
  • Traits: Ego-less, silly, gullible — but brilliant at commerce
  • Military: Weak by default — survive through universal affection
  • Fashion: Trend-setters of Ge'or — copied by all species
  • Subrace nations: Estran, Cattos, Great Cattos, Lake Kingdom, Marko
  • Found: Everywhere on Ge'or
  • Religion: Calism (majority)

docs.title: Coldspeople
docs.text: A humanoid mammalian race adapted to extreme cold. Coldspeople prefer to live near ice, in tundra, and in near-permafrost regions — climates that would kill other humanoid species within hours. They are found primarily on Marti Continent, with smaller populations in the northern reaches of Lumina and the high-altitude regions of Xeti.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Stocky, broad-shouldered, with thick pale fur covering their bodies — white, cream, or light gray. Round faces with small ears (to minimize heat loss). Their hands are paw-like with retractable claws for gripping ice. Eyes are small and dark — adapted for the blinding glare of snow-reflected sunlight.
  • Lifespan: 65–80 years. Coldspeople age slowly in cold environments but rapidly in warm ones — a Coldsperson who moves to a temperate climate may lose a decade of lifespan to metabolic stress.
  • Mage-cell expression: Low — some ice-shaping abilities. Coldsperson mages (called Frost-Singers) can freeze water, create ice walls, and walk on snow without leaving tracks. Combat magic is rare — most Frost-Singers are builders, using ice-shaping to construct and maintain settlements.
  • Adaptation: Thick layer of insulating fat (2–3 inches) and dense fur. Coldspeople can sleep in snow without harm — their body temperature regulation is the most efficient of any known species. Blood runs thicker, heart beats slower, metabolism conserves every calorie. Heat is their vulnerability — they struggle in temperatures above freezing and can suffer heatstroke at temperatures humans find comfortable. A Coldsperson in summer clothing in a temperate room is equivalent to a human in a sauna.

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Coldspeople live in ice-carved settlements — homes sculpted from packed snow and glacial ice, insulated with furs and heated by geothermal vents or carefully contained fire-pits. Their architecture is temporary by design — settlements are carved fresh each winter and allowed to melt each spring, only to be rebuilt the following year.

  • Nations: Brase and communities in Maboro on Marti Continent. Smaller enclaves exist in northern Lumina and high Xeti.
  • Governance: Council of Elders — the oldest living Coldsperson in each settlement leads. Age is wisdom; the eldest have survived the most winters and therefore know the most about survival. Disputes are settled by the eldest who is not personally involved — their word is final.
  • Social structure: Highly communal. Survival in the cold demands cooperation. Food, shelter, and warmth are shared without question. A Coldsperson who hoards resources is not punished — they are pitied. Hoarding means you do not trust your community, and a Coldsperson without community will not survive the winter.
  • Family: Coldspeople raise children collectively. A child belongs to the settlement, not to specific parents. This does not mean parents are absent — it means every adult is a parent. A child who scrapes their knee will be comforted by the nearest adult, regardless of blood relation.

docs.title: Culture
docs.text:
Coldsperson culture is shaped by the fundamental reality of their environment: the cold does not care about your feelings. You cooperate or you die. This breeds a culture that is warm internally and cold externally — Coldspeople are famously stoic with outsiders and warmly affectionate with their own.

  • The Winter-Telling: During the deepest part of winter, when blizzards trap settlements for weeks, Coldspeople gather in the communal hall for the Winter-Telling — a continuous storytelling tradition that can last the entire season. Elders tell the old stories. Children learn their history. Travelers who happen to be snowed in are honored guests — they are expected to contribute their own stories in exchange for shelter.
  • Gift-Giving: When a Coldsperson visits another settlement, they bring a gift of food — typically preserved meat or frozen berries. The gift is not optional. It is a statement: "I come in peace, I contribute to your survival, I am not a burden." To arrive without a gift is an insult. To refuse a gift is a declaration of hostility.
  • Relations: Trade furs, ice-gems, and preserved meat with Germina and the Cobal Kingdom. Neutral toward most species. Wary of outsiders who do not understand their customs — the gift-giving ritual has caused diplomatic incidents when human traders arrived empty-handed.
  • Death: When a Coldsperson dies, their body is placed on a funeral pyre of scented wood (imported at great expense). The fire is lit at dusk. The community watches the smoke rise into the frozen night. They believe the soul rises with the smoke to join the Great Cold — the eternal winter where ancestors dwell. Bodies are never buried — the frozen ground is too hard, and burial would trap the soul in the earth.

docs.title: Religion — Ulasm
docs.text:
Most Coldspeople follow Ulasm — the pagan animist faith that worships eagles as divine and venerates ancestors. The dead dwell in the Great Cold and watch through eagle eyes. Core in Brase (southwest of Germina), also in Coldspeople enclaves in Maboro.

Ulasm predates the Erisian Church on Marti by millennia; its eagle-feather talismans and dusk pyres remain the heart of Coldspeople spirituality.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nations: Brase, Maboro (Marti Continent)
  • Enclaves: Northern Lumina, high-altitude Xeti
  • Traits: Cold-adapted, fur-covered, ice-carving, communal, gift-culture
  • Ages: Present since Age 3 in Marti, expanded during Age 7 trade era

docs.title: Diablos
docs.text: A winged humanoid species native to the island region east of the Demon Continent mainland. Diablos are strictly nocturnal — they sleep during daylight hours and conduct their civilization at night. Their wings give them mastery of the air, and their culture is built around darkness and moonlit activity.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Humanoid with large, bat-like wings spanning 3–4 meters. Skin tones range from deep indigo to charcoal gray. Eyes are large and adapted for night vision — reflective, glowing faintly in darkness
  • Flight: Capable of sustained flight, though they tire after an hour of continuous wing-beats. They prefer gliding on thermal currents
  • Lifespan: 80–100 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Moderate. Diablos mages specialize in shadow manipulation and sound-dampening spells — abilities that complement their nocturnal lifestyle
  • Vulnerability: Direct sunlight causes discomfort and prolonged exposure leads to skin damage. They are not harmed by daylight — merely disadvantaged

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Diablos live in the Mountain Tribe's territory on Yak Island. Their settlements are built into cliff faces and mountain peaks — accessible only by flight.

  • Governance: Night Council — a body of elders who convene only after moonrise. No decisions are made during daylight
  • Culture: The moon is sacred. Diablos track lunar phases with religious precision, and major events (births, marriages, declarations of war) are timed to specific lunar conjunctions
  • Economy: They trade nocturnal resources — moon-silver ore, shadow-silk (spun from cave-dwelling moths), and night-blooming herbs used in alchemy across the Demon Continent
  • Relations: Isolationist by circumstance rather than choice — most species conduct business during daylight. They trade with Estran and occasionally the Asatru Empire through intermediary outposts

docs.title: Faith
docs.text: Diablos follow Demonism, the ecumenical multi-ethnic sect of Kirivs-bin — all demons one race, all faiths one.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Mountain Tribe (Yak Island, Demon Continent)
  • Traits: Winged humanoids, nocturnal civilization, lunar culture, cliff-dwelling

docs.title: Eastern Beastmen
docs.text: A subrace of beastmen native to the eastern regions of the Lumina Continent. Eastern Beastmen are shorter and physically weaker than standard beastmen, but compensate with exceptional trading skills that have made them indispensable to the Lumina economy.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Stature: Shorter and slighter than western beastmen — adapted for agility rather than raw strength
  • Lifespan: Comparable to humans, 60–80 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Low to moderate — trading talent, not magical power, defines their place in the world
  • Distinctive features: Lighter fur tones, more human-like faces, expressive ears that aid in negotiation (other species find them disarming)

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Eastern Beastmen are mercantile by nature. Their communities revolve around trade — not just goods, but information, favors, and alliances. A young Eastern Beastman learns numbers before letters, and haggling before hunting.

  • Family structure: Extended trade families — "houses" that specialize in particular goods or routes
  • Governance: Council of merchant elders in each settlement; no centralized authority
  • Religion: Pragmatic — they honor the spirits of trade and travel, but rarely build temples
  • Cultural value: A good deal is considered an art form. The highest compliment is "they traded well."

docs.title: Role on Lumina
docs.text:
The Cammao Kingdom is their primary nation, where they share power with a minority of demonfolk who migrated from the Demon Continent. Eastern Beastmen handle commerce while the demonfolk provide martial strength — a symbiotic arrangement.

They are also found as traders throughout Lumina, moving goods between the Gigas Tribe (who respect their usefulness), the Lake Kingdom (where Lesser Catmen adore them), and the Vennerian outposts.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Parent species: Beast Races
  • Nation: Cammao Kingdom (Lumina Continent)
  • Traits: Shorter, weaker, exceptional traders, mercantile culture

docs.title: Flames
docs.text: A species of gas-based beings native to the Demon Continent. Flames are not made of flesh but of burning gases, giving them a spiritual, fiery appearance. They live primarily in mountain ranges — such as those of Blazeyard — where they consume minerals as food.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Form: Composed of superheated gases held in humanoid shape by an internal energy core. The core is the true "body" — the flames are an exhalation
  • Lifespan: Unknown. Flames do not age in the biological sense; they persist as long as their core remains intact. The oldest known Flame is said to predate the Kutten Catastrophe
  • Diet: Mineral consumption — they "eat" by absorbing trace elements from mountain rock. Different minerals produce different flame colors
  • Vulnerability: Water and extreme cold can temporarily weaken or disperse a Flame's gaseous form. They cannot be killed by conventional weapons — only by destroying the core
  • Reproduction: Flames do not reproduce biologically. A new Flame is "kindled" — a fragment of an existing core is placed in mineral-rich rock and nurtured for decades

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Flame society is ancient and slow. They do not measure time in years but in geological ages. Their language is a combination of heat patterns and light pulses — incomprehensible to flesh-beings without magical translation.

  • Governance: The Eldest Core — a council of the oldest Flames. Decisions take centuries
  • Culture: Flames are contemplative. They spend decades in stillness, observing geological processes. To a Flame, a human lifetime is a flicker
  • Relations: They trade minerals with the Asatru Empire and occasionally allow travelers through Blazeyard's mountain passes. They have no territorial ambitions — their needs are literally beneath their feet

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Blazeyard (Demon Continent)
  • Traits: Gas-based, mineral-eating, near-immortal, contemplative culture

docs.title: Giants
docs.text: A humanoid species standing approximately three meters tall, native to the island of Xobkua on the Demon Continent.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Stature: 2.8–3.5 meters tall, heavily muscled. Bones are denser than human bones — adapted to support their mass
  • Lifespan: 200–250 years. Giants age slowly; a 50-year-old Giant is still considered adolescent
  • Mage-cell expression: Very low. Giants rely on physical power, not magic. A rare few can manifest earth-aligned abilities
  • Diet: Omnivorous, with enormous caloric needs. A single Giant consumes as much as ten humans daily. Xobkua's coastal waters provide abundant fish

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Giant society on Xobkua is built around the clan longhouse — massive timber structures housing 30–50 Giants. Each clan controls a stretch of coastline or forest territory.

  • Governance: Clan chieftains, chosen by ritual combat. The strongest leads. Wisdom is valued but strength is the final arbiter
  • Culture: Giants are not warlike — they are territorial. They defend Xobkua fiercely but do not seek conquest. Their oral history stretches back thousands of years, sung in deep tones that vibrate through the ground
  • Craftsmanship: Giants are skilled woodworkers and stone-carvers on a massive scale. Their longhouses are architectural wonders — single beams weighing tons, fitted without nails
  • Relations: Minimal contact with other nations. Zakarutia trades with them occasionally. The Asatru Empire respects their sovereignty from across the sea

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Xobkua (Demon Continent)
  • Traits: 3m tall, long-lived, territorial, skilled craftsmen, oral tradition

docs.title: Half-Elves
docs.text:
Half-elves are the hybrid offspring of Elves and Humans — the most common hybrid on Ge'or. Legally and socially they are often treated as neither, which has defined their history.

One of Ge'or's most politically consequential peoples despite having no homeland of their own for millennia — until Moriat.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Intermediate — pointed ears softened, human stature with elven grace. Highly variable.
  • Lifespan: ~200 years — between human (~80) and elf (~400). Long enough to outlive human parents, short enough to feel the loss.
  • Reproduction: Fully fertile with humans, elves, and other half-elves. Children of half-elf pairs are most often half-elven.
  • Mage-cell expression: Moderate-high, nature-leaning when elven blood is strong. Not genetically immune to the Shadows like pure Elves — their minds can be read and absorbed, though resistance is slightly higher than pure humans.
  • Traits: Neither species' genetic immunity, neither species' full belonging.

docs.title: Erisdar: Discrimination
docs.text: In Erisdar, half-elves are systemically discriminated against. Neither Elvennrin nor human kingdoms fully accept them. They face legal restrictions, social exclusion, and periodic pogroms — especially during the Great Elvish Persecution and later Erisian consolidations.

docs.title: Exodus to Moriat — Centuries
docs.text:
Because of this, across centuries half-elves steadily entered the island of Moriat in the Luminous Ocean — arriving as refugees, traders, mercenaries, and families seeking a place where neither bloodline would be a liability.

On Moriat they found human nations (Mikrad, Underfern) that tolerated them and the vast, thinly-governed interior of the island.

docs.title: ~200 AGD — The Takeover
docs.text:
About ~200 AGD, half-elves became the majority of the population of Gomor and Gildenrise.

They did not conquer by war — they out-populated, organized, and took over the politics and government of both countries, entrenching themselves as the ruling people. Both nations are now half-elf kingdoms with human minorities.

This is the only successful half-elf statehood on Ge'or.

docs.title: Religion — Mixed, No Official
docs.text:
Half-elves on Moriat carry both heritages:

  • Majority: Elven Faith — the elven gods and nature cults, dominant in Gomor/Gildenrise.
  • Minority: Nyity — the ancient astronomical faith of Mikrad/Underfern (sky gods, suicidal sacrifice ~4,000 BGD), kept by intermarried families and converts.

Neither Gomor nor Gildenrise declares an official state religion — both faiths coexist. This is deliberate: imposing one would re-create the Erisdar exclusion they fled.

docs.title: Relations
docs.text:
• Elves: Revered but distant — half-elves admire elven culture but are not accepted as elves.
  • Humans: Close, especially in Gomor/Gildenrise where human Nyity neighbors persist.
  • Erisian Church: Viewed with suspicion — the church that persecuted both parent peoples.
  • Dukedam: Erisian human neighbor on Minir — contrast case (Erisian, not mixed).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• Millennia of drift — sporadic half-elf births across Erisdar, no homeland.
  • Centuries-long exodus — discrimination → steady migration to Moriat.
  • ~200 AGD — demographic majority → political takeover → Gomor and Gildenrise become half-elf kingdoms. See: Half-Elf Takeover of Gomor and Gildenrise — ~200 AGD and Half-Elf Exodus to Moriat.
  • Present (597 AGD): Gomor and Gildenrise are the de facto half-elf nations; Moriat is the half-elf heartland.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Half-Elves ] ├── Hybrid of: Elves × Humans ├── Lifespan: ~200 years ├── Homeland: Moriat (Gomor, Gildenrise — majority since ~200 AGD) ├── Origin: Erisdar discrimination → centuries-long exodus to Moriat ├── Religion: Elven Faith (majority) + Nyity (minority), no official ├── Related Nations: Gomor, Gildenrise, Mikrad, Underfern, Dukedam ├── Related Events: Half-Elf Exodus to Moriat, Half-Elf Takeover of Gomor and Gildenrise — ~200 AGD └── Arrived: ~15,000 BGD (as hybrids, with crash)

docs.title: Halflings
docs.text: A small humanoid species similar to hobbits from folklore. Halflings are peaceful, agrarian, and fond of comfort — good food, warm hearths, and simple pleasures. They inhabit Barro and Kob on Merratodoni alongside Elves.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Short (0.9–1.1 meters), round-faced, with curly hair and large, hairy feet. They rarely wear shoes
  • Lifespan: 90–110 years — longer than humans
  • Mage-cell expression: Very low. Halfling magic is subtle — luck, good harvests, finding things that were lost. Scholars debate whether this is magic at all, or simply halfling nature
  • Traits: Remarkably resilient. Halflings can endure hardships that would break larger folk — not through strength, but through a quiet, stubborn refusal to give up

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Halfling society is pastoral and decentralized. They live in small villages of burrow-homes built into hillsides — round doors, cozy interiors, pantries always stocked.

  • Governance: Village elders. There is no halfling king or empire — each village governs itself. Twice a year, elders gather for a grand feast where community matters are discussed between courses
  • Culture: Food is the cornerstone. Halfling cuisine is legendary — they cultivate mushrooms, pipe-weed, and seven varieties of potato. A halfling's worth is measured not in gold but in the quality of their dinner parties
  • Religion: Ancestor-veneration through recipe-keeping. The most sacred object in a halfling home is the family cookbook, passed down through generations
  • Relations: Universally well-liked. Halflings are too small and too friendly to threaten anyone. They get along especially well with Lesser Catmen — the two species have an informal alliance of "creatures too cute to wage war against"

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Barro and Kob (Merratodoni)
  • Traits: Small, peaceful, agrarian, food-obsessed, resilient

docs.title: Kachev
docs.text:
"The river taught us to breathe twice. The sky taught us to close our mouths."

A species of humanoid owls native to the Demon Continent, inhabiting the river-crossing territory of the Kutra Tribe (endonym Kachev, exonym Kutra / Owlkin). Kachev are amphibious, silent, and famously patient — the only sapient species on Ge'or that breathes both water and air without magic, and the only one that considers speaking aloud a decision that requires approval.

Older Demon Continent texts call them Kutra (Owlkin) — the same people, older name. Modern Kachev prefer Kachev among themselves and tolerate Kutra from outsiders the way a river tolerates a bridge: useful, but not native.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Humanoid owls 1.5–1.8m tall. Owl-like heads — large forward-facing eyes, short curved beak, broad facial disc — on feathered bodies with human-proportioned arms ending in taloned, four-fingered hands and digitigrade legs with zygodactyl talons. Feather coloring mottled brown, gray, rust, and silver — superb riverine camouflage. Wing-like arm-feathers allow true powered flight, not gliding.
  • Respiration: Gills + lungs. Paired gill-slits run along the lower ribs, hidden beneath flank feathers; lungs fill the upper chest. Kachev switch seamlessly between water-breathing (sleeping submerged) and air-breathing (walking, flying, speaking). They can remain submerged indefinitely while at rest and survive outside water for ~2 days before gill tissue dries painfully. Hatchlings breathe water exclusively for their first month.
  • Flight: Silent flight. Primary feathers have the same leading-edge fringes and velvet dorsal surface as terrestrial owls — air passes without turbulence. A Kachev in level flight at 30m is inaudible to human ears. Takeoff is nearly vertical from a river stone.
  • Vision: Enormous, forward-facing, tubular eyes adapted for both underwater and low-light vision. Visual acuity at dusk is ~6× human; underwater clarity rivals a diving bird. They can see a river-gem glint at 200m in turbid water.
  • Lifespan: 60–80 years. Maturity at ~15. Aging shows first in wing-feather brittleness and gill-slit narrowing.
  • Mage-cell expression: Low. Kachev mages are rare (~1 in 400) and almost always specialize in water manipulation (current-shaping, surface-tension walking, mist-veiling). Fire magic is nearly unknown — a cultural as well as biological bias.
  • Reproduction: Oviparous but live-tending: a Kachev pair incubates 1–2 large eggs in a dry, feather-lined riverside hollow for ~40 days, then carries hatchlings (nidiculous, blind, gilled) in a chest sling that keeps them moist. Both parents share incubation.

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
The Kutra Tribe builds its settlements across and along the river — half the village above water, half below. Sleeping chambers are fully submerged (where families breathe water together); communal halls, kitchens, and trade docks sit above the surface on timber platforms. At dawn the village seems to exhale as dozens of owls surface in unison.

  • Governance: Dual chieftaincy — one below-chief (river) and one sky-chief (above), ruling only by consensus. Either may veto; neither may rule alone. Major decisions require an overnight perching/sinking contemplation: the below-chief sleeps submerged with the question, the sky-chief perches above it, and they sign agreement (literally — Kachev sign-language) before the tribe at first light. Foreign envoys find this slow and uncheatable.
  • Language & Sign: Kachev language is two-channel. Talon-sign (wing-flicks, talon taps, eye-angle) is the default — silent, precise, river-compatible. Young Kachev learn to sign before they learn to speak; to "speak before you can sign" is a developmental insult. Vocal speech (a soft hooting, surprisingly melodic) is reserved for declaration, song, and emergency. A Kachev who speaks aloud without need has, in the local idiom, "rippled the water."
  • Culture: Silence is not shyness — it is doctrine. Farsightist teaching (see Farsightism) holds that distance clarifies and speech ripples. Kachev children are taught to watch a full minute before signing an observation and to fly a full circuit before reporting what they saw. The Asatru Empire maintains its only trade embassy in the Kutra that operates entirely in signed Kachev for formal negotiation.
  • Economy: River-trade. Kachev ferry goods along the Demon Continent's waterways, charging in river-gems — translucent, slightly luminous stones found only in their river's deep channels. The finest stone of each season is not sold but dropped into the deepest channel as thanks to the river (a Farsightism rite that Asatru traders find exasperating and beautiful). They also guide timber rafts through rapids that no human pilot would attempt.
  • Architecture: Amphibious: submerged sleeping bells woven from river-reed and stone, with air-pocket nurseries for eggs; above-water halls of black Demon Continent timber on stilts, connected by rope-and-timber bridges that sway — Kachev love sway; it proves the river is breathing.

docs.title: Relations
docs.text:
• Neighbors: Deeply respected by the Maomodor Kingdom (which shares the "demonic nationality" ethic) and the Malgardian Tribe (who trade violet crystal for river-gems). The Asatru Empire values them as scouts, mediators, and the continent's only impartial customs service.
  • Faith: Farsightism (Var-Kael — "the sight that waits") — universal among Kachev. The faith is not a creed but a practice: dawn-perch, dusk-glide, dual-consensus. Titian oracles exchange vision-techniques with Kachev sign-elders.
  • Other species: Standard Kobolds and Malgardians sometimes settle seasonally in Kachev ferry-camps; intermarriage is biologically impossible but culturally warm. Flames of Blazeyard find Kachev river-chill uncomfortable and keep talks brief.

docs.title: History & Name
docs.text:
• Exonym → endonym: Early Demon Continent maps (Age 7) label the river people Kutra — a demon pidgin approximation of the soft hoot "ka-t’raa" that Kachev make when surfacing. The Kachev themselves say Kachev (ka-CHEV, with a guttural ch). Modern scholarship uses Kachev for the species, Kutra Tribe for the polity, and notes Owlkin as the Common nickname. The older file Kutra (Owlkin) remains as alias.
  • No conquest tradition — Kachev have never fielded an army beyond river defense. Their power is informational: they see, remember, and ferry.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Kachev ] ├── Aliases: Kutra / Owlkin — older/Common names; Kachev is endonym ├── Nations: Kutra Tribe (river-below + sky-above, consensus-only) ├── Region: Demon Continent — below Malgardian Tribe/Emberalden, west of Blazeyard, north of Maomodor Kingdom ├── Biology: Humanoid owl, 1.5–1.8m, gills + lungs, silent flight, tubular low-light/underwater eyes ├── Lifespan: 60–80 years; oviparous (1–2 eggs, 40-day incubation, chest-sling hatchling care) ├── Language: Talon-sign default (taught first), vocal hoot reserved for declaration ├── Economy: River ferry + river-gem trade; guide timber through rapids ├── Religion: Farsightism (Var-Kael) — distance clarifies, silence is not absence, flight as prayer └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Kutra (Owlkin)
docs.text: A species of humanoid owls native to the Demon Continent, inhabiting the Kutra Tribe territory across a river. Kutra do not breathe oxygen but can survive outside water for up to two days. They are capable of flight and possess a culture adapted to both aquatic and aerial environments.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Humanoid owls standing 1.5–1.8 meters tall. Feathered bodies with human-like arms ending in taloned hands. Large, forward-facing eyes adapted for both underwater and low-light vision. Feather coloring ranges from mottled brown to silver-gray
  • Respiration: Gills and lungs. Kutra breathe water through gill-slits along their ribs and air through lungs. They can switch between the two seamlessly
  • Flight: Silent flight — their feathers are structured to eliminate sound, making them nearly undetectable in the air
  • Lifespan: 60–80 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Low. Kutra mages are rare and typically specialize in water manipulation

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
The Kutra Tribe builds settlements across and along the river — half the village above water, half below. Their architecture is amphibious: sleeping chambers are submerged (where they breathe water) while communal areas are above the surface.

  • Nation: Kutra Tribe (Demon Continent)
  • Governance: Dual chieftains — one for the river (below) and one for the sky (above). Major decisions require consensus between both
  • Culture: Silence is valued. Their language includes sign-gestures made with talons and wing-flicks. Speaking aloud is reserved for important declarations. Kutra children learn to sign before they learn to speak
  • Economy: River-trade — they ferry goods along the waterways of the Demon Continent, charging in rare river-gems found only in their territory
  • Relations: Respected by the Maomodor Kingdom and the Malgardian Tribe. The Asatru Empire maintains a trade embassy in their largest settlement

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Kutra Tribe (Demon Continent)
  • Traits: Humanoid owls, amphibious, silent flight, dual governance, sign-language culture

docs.title: Madarons
docs.text: Enormous dinosaur-like creatures that once roamed Ge'or before the arrival of the allied species. Madarons were the dominant terrestrial life form on the planet for millions of years — massive, reptilian, and largely indifferent to the smaller species that eventually displaced them.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Size: 15–30 meters in length. Some specimens reached 40 meters. Their footsteps could be felt from kilometers away.
  • Diet: Omnivorous — they consumed everything from forests to herds of smaller animals.
  • Lifespan: Unknown. Madarons grew continuously throughout their lives. The oldest specimens were truly colossal.
  • Intelligence: Semi-intelligent. Comparable to elephants or whales — complex social structures, long memories, but no tool use or language.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Madarons survived the Hybrian glassing of the Demon Continent and other regions during The Last Great War simply by not living where the bombardment fell. They continued to roam Ge'or for millions of years after the 157th Colony was destroyed.

When the Glorious Alliance crashed ~15,000 BGD and the allied species spread across the planet, madarons were gradually driven to extinction through hunting, habitat loss, and competition. By the time of the Great Divergence (Year 0), they were already legendary — creatures remembered in oral traditions and fossil records but no longer walking the earth.

docs.title: Legacy
docs.text: Madaron bones can still be found across Ge'or. Some cultures believe they were gods. Some believe they were demons. The Gigas Tribe of Lumina Continent claims descent from a great beast that was "neither man nor animal" — possibly a cultural memory of the madarons.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Era: Pre-crash native fauna of Ge'or
  • Survived: Hybrian glassing (~3,000,000 years ago)
  • Extinct: Sometime between ~15,000 BGD and Year 0
  • Related: The 157th Colony, Goblins (also native species)

docs.title: Marmots
docs.text:
"The marmots remember the hill. The Yaoma remember the tide. Together they remember the island."

A species of stout, burrowing beastfolk native to the two islands and sacred atoll of the Yaoma Tribe south of Zakarutia and east of Xobkua. Where the Yaoma are water-breathing merfolk who master tide and song, Marmots are hill-breathing burrowers who master stone and silence — the landward complement that lets a two-island sea people also be an island people.

Asatru traders' pidgin famously confuses Yaoma and marmot (merfolk → marmot). Oceanist Yaoma find this hilarious and sometimes ceremonially call themselves "the marmots of the perfect ocean" — a joke that, in Marmot ears, is an honorific. The Marmots, for their part, call Yaoma tide-kin and themselves hill-kin without any confusion at all.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Stout, low-slung beastfolk 1.2–1.4m tall standing, 1.6–1.8m stretched in tunnel. Dense, water-shedding pelts in sandstone, basalt-gray, lichen-green, and cream. Broad heads with small rounded ears, prominent incisors (ever-growing — gnawing is hygiene), and short but powerful limbs ending in scooping claws. Torso is barrel-chested; fat reserves are tail- and hindquarter-stored. Unlike true rodents, Marmots are fully sapient, with human-proportioned hands (clawed but dextrous) and clear speech.
  • Build: Built for digging and hauling. A Marmot can shift its own bodyweight in packed island soil per minute. Their sense of vibration through stone is exquisite — they feel a footstep through 20m of basalt.
  • Lifespan: 45–60 years. Maturity at ~12. Elders are prized as living tunnel-maps.
  • Mage-cell expression: Very low to none. Marmots produce almost no mages; their few stone-sense adepts achieve through lifelong vibration-training what other species do with spells — detecting faults, finding water, predicting rockfall.
  • Diet: Omnivorous island generalists — tubers, cliff grasses, washed-up kelp, and the fat white grubs of the hill interior. They ferment kelp-tuber mash into a sour, strong hill brew that Yaoma profess to dislike and secretly trade pearls for.
  • Reproduction: Viviparous, 2–4 kits per litter. Kits remain in the burrow-hall for two years, learning tunnel-craft before surfacing.

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Marmots and Yaoma share the Yaoma Tribe polity as one nation, two ecologies:

  • Yaoma occupy water — pearl beds, song-corridors, reef gardens, the sacred governance atoll.
  • Marmots occupy hill — the inland spine of both islands, where they have dug labyrinthine but orderly burrow-towns into limestone and basalt.

The arrangement is not conquest but symbiosis, codified as Oceanism's shore-purgatory: Yaoma live in the perfection-adjacent water and visit land; Marmots live in the draft-land and visit water only at the shoreline. Governance is shared through the Tide-Council on the atoll: seven elders chosen by Maenar/Amelia phases, of whom by ancient compact two seats are always Marmot — the Hill Voices — even though Marmots cannot stay submerged long.

  • Governance: Within burrow-towns, Marmots govern by hall-consensus: each family burrow-hall (10–25 Marmots) sends a "claw" to a hill moot. The moot does not vote — it digs — extending a ceremonial tunnel a handspan per meeting until consensus is reached; the length of tunnel records the difficulty of the decision. The Tide-Council's two Marmot seats are chosen by the hill moot on new-moon nights when tides are lowest and Yaoma can stand longest on the atoll.
  • Culture: Taciturn, engineering-minded, and deeply humorous in a dry, subterranean way. Their oral history is tunnel-mapped: each major event is encoded as a named bend, chamber, or fault-brace in the burrow. A Marmot elder reciting history literally walks you through it. They consider Yaoma song-scrolls beautiful but impractical — "you can't shelter kits in a song when it storms," a young Marmot will whisper, and an older one will cuff them gently and say, "but you remember the storm because someone sang it."
  • Architecture: Burrow-towns are marvels of drainage, ventilation, and tidal respect. The deepest galleries are tide-locked — sealed during high water, opened at low. Sleeping chambers are lined with woven kelp and hill-brew yeast that regulates humidity. Yaoma visiting inland are carried in slung water-hammocks; Marmots visiting the reef are fitted with wet kelp cloaks.
  • Economy: Marmots are the islands' landward economy: terracing, water-catchment, tuber/kelp farming, burrow maintenance, and above all stonework — the Yaoma have no hands suited for quarrying. Marmot-quarried basalt builds Yaoma atoll docks and tide walls; Yaoma-harvested pearls buy what Marmots lack. Deep-sea salvage recovered by Yaoma is hauled ashore and conserved by Marmots.

docs.title: Relations & Religion
docs.text:
• Yaoma — tide-kin: Not allies — co-nationals. Intermarriage is biologically impossible, but adoption across species is common: a Yaoma clutch may be hill-nursed by a Marmot hall in a hot season; a Marmot kit may be tide-bathed by Yaoma song-keepers. The two peoples bury their dead together at the high-tide line — Marmots digging the grave above the line, Yaoma singing below it.
  • Religion: Oceanism — Marmots are Oceanists alongside the Yaoma, in the Marmot idiom. Where Yaoma Oceanism says ocean creatures are perfect, land creatures are drafts, Marmot Oceanism says we are the draft that learned to love its incompleteness — and therefore digs, terraces, and holds the hill so that the Yaoma's purgatory has a shore worth returning to. Oceanist pilgrims of both species perform the beaching vigil together: the Marmot shades the Yaoma's gills with wet kelp while the Yaoma sings.
  • Zakarutia & Glub Kingdom: Marmots have no independent foreign policy; as part of the Yaoma Tribe they are represented by the Tide-Council. Zakarutian traders find Marmot stonework excellent; Glub slimes unsettle Yaoma but intrigue Marmots, who see in Slime confluence a burrow-like merging.
  • Demon Continent mainland: Marmot hill brew and Yaoma pearls travel north together as a paired export — "tide and hill" in one cargo.

docs.title: Role in the Yaoma Tribe
docs.text:
Without Marmots, the Yaoma would be a tribe of brilliant singers and divers with nowhere dry to incubate eggs safely through a storm, nowhere to store salvage, and no one to quarry the atoll's governance stones. Without Yaoma, Marmots would be an isolated hill folk with no pearl wealth, no deep-water food, and no song to remember their tunnels by. Oceanism's core image — shoreline as purgatory between perfection and draft — is built on this interdependence.

Asatru mainland reports once classified the islands as "Yaoma Tribe (mermaid-like, two islands)" and missed the Marmots entirely because censustakers stayed on the beach. The Tide-Council corrected the record by sending a Marmot delegation to waddle up the beach, dig a perfect, dry-footed negotiation pit on the sand, and offer hill brew inside it. The report was amended.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Marmots ] ├── Species: Marmot beastfolk — stout hill-burrowers, 1.2–1.4m, vibration-sense, ever-growing incisors ├── Nations: Yaoma Tribe — co-national with Yaoma (tide-kin / hill-kin, two islands + sacred atoll) ├── Region: Demon Continent — two islands south of Zakarutia, east of Xobkua ├── Lifespan: 45–60 years; 2–4 kits, burrow-hall nursing ├── Religion: Oceanism — Marmot idiom ("the draft that learned to love its incompleteness") ├── Governance: Hall-consensus + hill moot (tunnel-length records consensus difficulty); 2 seats on the 7-seat Tide-Council (Hill Voices) ├── Economy: Burrow engineering, terracing, water-catchment, basalt quarrying; yaoma pearl + marmot brew paired exports ├── Symbiosis: Yaoma = water/perfection/song; Marmots = hill/draft/silence; burials at high-tide line together └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Ogres
docs.text: A large humanoid species native to Xeti Continent. Ogres are like Shrek — green-skinned, towering, and far more complex than their brutish appearance suggests. The only ogre nation in the world is Koetebalo on Xeti.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Large (2.2–2.8 meters), heavyset, with green or olive skin. Prominent tusks (smaller than orcs). Bald or with coarse dark hair
  • Lifespan: 80–100 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Very low. Ogres rely on physical strength
  • Traits: Immense physical power. An ogre can lift and throw objects that would crush other species. Slow metabolism — they eat infrequently but in enormous quantities

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Ogres are solitary by nature but maintain a functioning nation in Koetebalo. Their culture values independence, privacy, and personal space — an ogre's swamp or home is sacred territory.

  • Governance: Loose confederation. Each ogre family-unit governs itself. A council of elders meets only in times of external threat
  • Culture: Layers — literally. Ogres compare themselves to onions: they have layers of personality, emotion, and complexity that outsiders rarely see. Their art is crude but expressive — mud-sculpture and deep-bass throat-singing
  • Relations: Found alongside Wolvesfolk and Orcs in the Uiohin republic. Generally peaceful unless provoked. They do not seek conquest — they seek quiet
  • Temperament: Gruff, private, and surprisingly wise. An ogre who likes you will protect you with devastating force. An ogre who dislikes you will simply ignore your existence

docs.title: Religion — Wruowas
docs.text:
The ogre nation Koetebalo on Xeti follows Wruowas — an ultra-ancient religion that cults Dabazi Ar Batr, the great serpent creator of all reality. It is celestial animism where constellations are worshipped as the serpent's scales.

Wruowas predates every other faith on Xeti by millennia. Its Stone-Seers chart the serpent's coils. Each ogre child is named for the dominant constellation at birth.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Koetebalo (Xeti Continent)
  • Also found in: Uiohin (Xeti Continent)
  • Traits: Large, green, strong, layered personality, solitary but communal when needed

docs.title: Orcs
docs.text: A civilized, rational species on Ge'or. Orcs are not inherently evil, though they possess natural tendencies toward aggression and physical strength that other races view with suspicion. This double standard persists despite orcish societies like Augamouth proving their capacity for governance, culture, and diplomacy.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Orcs are tall and powerfully built, standing 6'0" to 6'8" (males) and 5'8" to 6'2" (females). Skin tones range from deep green to gray-green, with occasional brown variants. Prominent lower canines (tusks) are present in both sexes, though males' are typically larger. Musculature is dense — an average orc is roughly 40% stronger than an average human of equivalent size.
  • Lifespan: 55–75 years. Orcs mature faster than humans (adulthood at 14) and remain physically vigorous until their final years. Old age hits rapidly — an orc who is fighting-fit at 70 may be dead within two years.
  • Mage-cell expression: Low to moderate. Orcish magic tends toward enhancement — temporary strength boosts, battle fury, pain suppression. Elemental magic is rare. Orcish mages (called Blood-Speakers) are valued but uncommon — roughly one in two hundred.
