  • Adaptation: Dense bone structure, high pain tolerance, accelerated healing of muscle and skin wounds. Orcs can fight through injuries that would incapacitate other species. This is not supernatural — it is biology refined by millennia of selection pressure on the harsh Demon Continent.

docs.title: Subraces
docs.text:
• Yak — smaller frame (5'4"–5'10"), gray-brown skin, more modest temperament. Isolation on Yak Island selected for cooperation over competition. Nation: Yakut (Yak Island, Demon Continent).
  • Mountain Orcs — the original stock from which other subspecies diverged. Larger, greener, more aggressive. Found in the highlands of the Demon Continent. Not a formal nation — mountain orc clans are nomadic, following herd migrations.
  • Lowland Orcs — the most common subspecies. Brown-green skin, adapted to temperate climates. Form the population base of nations like Augamouth and Oda.

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Orcish society is organized around clans — extended family units of 50 to 500 individuals who share a common ancestor, territory, and honor-code. Clans are the fundamental unit of orcish life, more important than nation or species identity.

  • Nations: Augamouth (West Erisdar), Oda (Kutten), Yakut (Yak Island, Demon Continent)
  • Governance: Clan-based with a king or chieftain selected by combat and council. In Augamouth, the king rules with the Council of Elders — one representative per major clan. The king can be challenged for leadership at any Gathering (annual assembly). A weak king is expected to fall. A strong king rules until death or voluntary abdication.
  • Social structure: Warriors → Elders → Craftsmen → Hunters → Youth. Shamans (Blood-Speakers) exist outside the hierarchy — they answer only to the spirits and the king.
  • Gender roles: Egalitarian by necessity. Female orcs are only slightly less strong than males and fight alongside them. Inheritance passes through the maternal line in most clans (you always know who the mother is; fathers can be uncertain in a culture with high combat mortality).

docs.title: Culture
docs.text:
Orcish culture values four virtues above all: strength, honor, loyalty, and truth. An orc who is weak but honorable is respected. An orc who is strong but lies is cast out.

  • The Telling: An orc who wishes to make a serious accusation or confession may invoke The Telling — a ritual where they speak uninterrupted before the clan. No one may interrupt The Telling. No one may punish the speaker for what is said during it. The Telling is sacred. Even a king cannot interrupt it.
  • Scar-Remembering: Orcs do not keep written histories. They keep scars. After a significant battle, treaty, or death, attending orcs receive ritual scarification — geometric patterns cut into the shoulders or back. An old orc's body is a library. To read an orc's scars is to read their life.
  • Death-singing: When an orc dies in battle, their clan sings them into the afterlife. The song recounts every battle they fought, every enemy they killed, every oath they kept. A death-song can last hours for a great warrior. Children learn the death-songs of their ancestors before they learn to read.
  • Relations: Orcs trade freely with other species and maintain diplomatic relations. Augamouth is a recognized kingdom in West Erisdarian politics. However, orcs are still subject to the "brute" stereotype — other species assume orcs are unintelligent, violent, or "barely civilized." This prejudice is a constant source of tension.

docs.title: Religion
docs.text: • Ogoron — "the titanic orc" in demonic orchish. The faith of Augamouth and much of orc-kind: a supposed huge orc will avenge all the orc race for their injustices and bring peace to the world, after which all species will live in harmony. Ogoron is inside all of their hearts.

docs.title: Nations
docs.text:
• Augamouth — orc kingdom (West Erisdar). The most diplomatically engaged orc nation. Augamouth maintains trade routes with Venner, Anos, and the Grimmel Republic. Its king, King Gorvak II (no relation to the Age 9 warlord), has pursued a policy of "strength through trade" for 30 years.
  • Oda — orc kingdom (Kutten). Smaller and more militant than Augamouth. Oda orcs believe the soft life of trade weakens the blood. They raid the Kutten desert tribes and maintain a standing army disproportionate to their population.
  • Yakut — Yak orc nation (Yak Island, Demon Continent). The Yak orcs are culturally distinct — more cooperative, less aggressive. Their isolation on Yak Island has made them the "least orcish" orcs in the eyes of mainlanders, a label they wear with pride.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Kingdoms: Augamouth (West Erisdar), Oda (Kutten)
  • Subrace nation: Yakut (Yak Island)
  • Relations: Tension with Goblins and Gnolls (historic raiding), trade with human nations, mutual respect with Demons (shared Demon Continent heritage)
  • Ages: Present in all ages since Age 2, major role in Demonic War (Age 8)
  • Characters: King Gorvak II (Augamouth), Chief Thokkar (Oda)

docs.title: Sandsmen
docs.text: A humanoid race adapted to arid environments, native to Kutten. Following the Kutten Catastrophe that desertified the continent after Elvengar's fall, the Sandsmen migrated in and established their kingdom of Malbodor atop the ruins.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Adaptation: Sandsmen evolved — or were engineered — for extreme aridity. They can survive weeks without water, extracting moisture from the air through specialized skin membranes
  • Appearance: Tall and lean, with sand-colored skin ranging from pale gold to deep ochre. Their eyes have nictitating membranes to protect against sandstorms
  • Lifespan: 70–90 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Low to none. Sandsmen do not practice magic. Their survival in the Kutten Desert is purely biological
  • Resilience: Immune to most heat-related illnesses. Can walk barefoot on sun-scorched sand without injury

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Sandsmen society is built around survival. Every tradition, every law, every custom traces back to the question: "Does this help us survive the desert?"

  • Governance: Meritocratic monarchy. The ruler of Malbodor must prove their worth through a desert pilgrimage — three months alone in the deep wastes. Those who return are fit to lead
  • Culture: Fatalistic but not grim. Sandsmen accept that the desert will claim everyone eventually. Their art, music, and poetry reflect this — beautiful and transient, like sand paintings that the wind erases
  • Architecture: Underground cities carved into sandstone. The surface structures of Malbodor are just the visible fraction — the true city extends deep beneath the dunes
  • Religion: They venerate the desert itself as a living entity — not malevolent, not benevolent, simply true. They call it "The Sand That Remembers," believing the desert holds the memories of Elvengar within its grains

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Malbodor (Kutten)
  • Origin: Post-Kutten Catastrophe migration
  • Traits: Desert-adapted, water-efficient, underground cities, fatalistic culture, meritocratic

docs.title: Sea Humans
docs.text: A variant of Humans adapted to maritime and coastal living. Sea Humans are found throughout the archipelagos of the eastern oceans, particularly in the Crab Union.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Indistinguishable from baseline humans but typically leaner, with sun-darkened skin and lighter hair bleached by salt and sun. Calloused hands and feet from a lifetime on deck and in water
  • Lifespan: 60–75 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Low — some wind-calling talent. Sea Human mages are practical: they predict weather, find fish, and nudge favorable currents
  • Traits: Natural sailors. Sea Humans are born to the deck — their sense of balance and navigation is uncanny. A Sea Human child can tie a knot before they can walk

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Sea Humans do not build cities on land. Their communities are floating — fleets of ships and houseboats that migrate with the seasons.

  • Nation: Crab Union (primary)
  • Governance: Fleet-captains. Each ship or group of ships has a captain. A council of captains governs the fleet. The admiral is elected for life but can be deposed by unanimous vote
  • Culture: Freedom of the open sea is the highest value. Sea Humans are nomadic by nature — a ship that stays in port too long is a ship that has lost its way. Children are raised communally aboard the fleet
  • Economy: Fishing, salvage, and trade. Sea Humans are the couriers of the archipelagos — they move goods, news, and people between islands
  • Religion: Wind and wave — practical deities. They do not build temples. The ship is the temple. The wind is the prayer. The voyage is the worship

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Parent species: Humans
  • Nation: Crab Union
  • Traits: Maritime adaptation, natural sailors, nomadic fleet-culture, ship-as-temple

docs.title: 🐋 Sea Monsters
docs.text: Sea Monsters — the great creatures of Ge'or's oceans, beyond the Leviathan. More remain to be defined.

docs.title: Known
docs.text:
• Leviathan — the guardian of Lake Leviathan, tied to the Hybrian machinations of Baoth.
  • Beyond it, sea monsters roam the open oceans — every coastal nation's navy sails prepared for them.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Known: Leviathan
  • See: Naval Power
  • Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Seafolk
docs.text: A humanoid species that builds their homes along coastlines, adapted to life at the edge of land and sea. Found throughout the archipelagos of the Wolf Ocean and Greater Ocean, particularly in the Crab Union and the United Kingdom of the Seamen.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Humanoid with slightly webbed hands and feet, pale blue-green tinted skin, and large dark eyes adapted for both underwater and surface vision. Lean build — built for swimming, not combat
  • Lifespan: 70–85 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Moderate — water and wind magic. Seafolk mages can predict weather, calm small waves, and guide currents
  • Traits: Exceptional swimmers and divers. Can hold breath for 10–15 minutes. Natural sense of direction at sea — a Seafolk navigator rarely needs instruments

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Seafolk live in stilt-villages built over shallow coastal waters. Their architecture is semi-aquatic — homes accessible by both boat and foot, connected by rope bridges and floating platforms.

  • Nations: Crab Union, United Kingdom of the Seamen
  • Governance: Harbor-councils — elected leaders from each village. The harbor-master speaks for the village in regional matters
  • Culture: Maritime — boat-building is sacred, navigation is taught from childhood, and the sea is viewed as a living entity with moods and seasons. A Seafolk child builds their first boat before they learn to read
  • Economy: Fishing, coastal trade, and shipwright services. Seafolk-built vessels are prized for their craftsmanship
  • Religion: The sea is a deity — not personified, but felt. Seafolk pray to the tide, the wind, and the current. Before every voyage, they pour a cup of freshwater into the salt — a return gift to the ocean that sustains them
  • Relations: Found alongside Halflings and Humans in the Crab Union, and alongside Catmen and Demons in the United Kingdom of the Seamen

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nations: Crab Union, United Kingdom of the Seamen
  • Traits: Coastal stilt-villages, amphibious, maritime culture, boat-sacred, ocean-deity

docs.title: Seamen
docs.text:
Seamen are a land species — despite their name suggesting they live in the sea.

A humanoid people distinct from Sea Humans and Seafolk, Seamen are terrestrial. Their name is an Old Erisdarian misnomer — early explorers first encountered them on the Crab Archipelago and assumed a maritime origin. The name stuck.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Tall, lean, with weathered skin and keen eyes. Often mistaken for Humans at a distance, but with subtly elongated limbs and webbing between fingers that suggests — misleadingly — an aquatic past.
  • Lifespan: 70–85 years.
  • Mage-cell expression: Low — some knack for navigation and knot-craft, but not elemental.
  • Traits: Despite the name, Seamen are fully terrestrial. They do not breathe water, do not live in the sea, and build their homes on solid ground. They are, however, superb sailors — perhaps the name's persistence is not entirely unearned.

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Seamen live as land-dwelling islanders — farmers, fishers, and traders who live on the islands, not in the water.

  • Nations: Crab Union (Crab Archipelago) and South Crab Archipelago — the two independent island archipelagos where Seamen form significant minorities.
  • Culture: Island hospitality, song, and seafaring tradition — but their villages are on land, their fields are tilled soil, their children play on beaches, not reefs.
  • Relations: Live alongside Humans, Halflings, and Seafolk in the Crab Union, and alongside Humans, Catmen, and Demons in the United Kingdom of the Seamen (South Crab).

docs.title: Distinction
docs.text:
• Sea Humans — human variant, maritime fleet-culture, floating villages.
  • Seafolk — amphibious.
  • Seamen — land species, island terrestrial — the name is a historical accident.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nations: Crab Union (Crab Archipelago), South Crab Archipelago / United Kingdom of the Seamen
  • Traits: Land species, island terrestrial, superb sailors despite terrestrial life, historical misnomer

docs.title: Slimes
docs.text: A species of amorphous, gelatinous beings. The vast majority of slimes are irrational creatures driven by instinct alone — consuming organic matter and growing until they divide. However, a rare intelligent variant exists: these slimes possess enough intellect for diplomacy, culture, and governance, as demonstrated by the Glub Kingdom.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Form: Gelatinous, semi-transparent bodies that can reshape at will. No fixed organs — their "biology" is a distributed network of specialized cells within the gel
  • Intelligence: Standard slimes operate on pure instinct. The intelligent variant possesses a neural-density cluster — a concentrated mass of thinking-cells within the gel — that grants reasoning and self-awareness
  • Lifespan: Indeterminate. Slimes do not age. They can be killed by dessication, extreme heat, or being dispersed beyond reformation
  • Reproduction: Binary fission. When a slime reaches sufficient mass, it splits. Intelligent slimes can choose when to divide — standard slimes cannot
  • Mage-cell expression: None. Slimes cannot channel magic

docs.title: Society (Intelligent Variant)
docs.text:
The Glub Kingdom, on small islands south of Yakut, is the only known slime civilization.

  • Governance: Mass-consensus. Larger slimes (those who have not divided recently) carry more voting weight in Glub decision-making. A slime who divides too often becomes politically weak
  • Culture: Minimalist. Slimes have no need for shelter, clothing, or food preparation. Their "culture" consists of memory-sharing — the direct transfer of liquid-thought between individuals
  • Economy: They trade in minerals and rare salts that other species value. Slimes can absorb and later excrete pure mineral deposits — making them natural miners
  • Relations: Diplomatically recognized by Yakut and Zakarutia. Other nations are wary. A slime diplomat is an unsettling sight — a quivering, translucent mass speaking in a wet, bubbling voice

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Intelligent nation: Glub Kingdom (Yak Island area, Demon Continent)
  • Traits: Majority irrational; rare intelligent variant with memory-sharing culture and mass-consensus governance

docs.title: Snake People
docs.text: A serpentine species native to Ge'or, with civilizations in Xikxia (West Erisdar) and Zakarutia (Demon Continent). Both nations are monarchies ruled by queens — sisters who deeply hate each other. Snake people are not inherently malevolent; they possess their own culture, governance, and rational society.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Humanoid upper body with serpentine lower body. Smooth scales in patterns unique to each individual. Forked tongues, slit-pupiled eyes, heat-sensing pits along the jaw
  • Lifespan: 120–150 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Moderate to high. Snake people mages specialize in venom magic, hypnosis, and thermal manipulation (the ability to sense and control heat)
  • Reproduction: Egg-laying. Clutches of 2–4 eggs, incubated communally in temple-hatcheries
  • Cold vulnerability: Being cold-blooded, snake people are sluggish in low temperatures. Their cities are built in warm climates for this reason

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Snake people society is matriarchal. Queens rule absolutely, and succession passes to the eldest daughter. Male snake people hold no positions of political power but serve as generals, scholars, and artisans.

  • Governance: Absolute matriarchal monarchy. The Queen's word is law. However, a council of Matriarchs — elder females from each major bloodline — can veto a Queen's decree with unanimous vote
  • Culture: Elaborate scale-painting is the highest art form. A snake person's painted scales tell their life story. Courtship involves the exchange of scale-paint designs
  • Direction: Legless, dragging themselves, snake people developed more direction namings than humans — their tongue divides the world into far more named directions and corners. The "24 corners" of Sibbism myth are an expression of this finer directional sense
  • The Sister-Queens: The Queen of Xikxia and the Queen of Zakarutia are sisters. Their feud dates back to a succession dispute centuries ago. Neither nation acknowledges the other's legitimacy. Inter-continental snake people trade is forbidden by both crowns
  • Religion: Sibbism — worship of the Snake Goddess, founder of the species, and her 24 demigod sons who supposedly run the 24 corners of the world. Ancestor veneration weaves through the faith: the spirits of dead queens watch from the heat-shimmer of desert sands

docs.title: The Kobra Lineage — A Cold-Adapted Split
docs.text:
The Kobra snakespeople on Marti are the same race as Xikxia (West Erisdar) and Zakarutia (Demon Continent). However they separated thousands of years ago, and the Kobra lineage ended up living in Marti as a cold-adapted subrace — unlike their warm-blooded cousins, these serpents thrive in frigid climates east of Kut.

  • Xikxia / Zakarutia: warm-blooded, matriarchal, follow Sibbism (Snake Goddess + 24 sons).
  • Kobra: cold-adapted, follow Moplilly — ancestor-veneration cult where the demigod father-founder Xanob is most prayed-upon.

This is the only snake subrace that mastered cold — Xanob's final gift, in Moplilly telling.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nations: Xikxia (West Erisdar), Zakarutia (Demon Continent)
  • Government: Absolute matriarchal monarchy
  • Feud: Sister-queens across continents
  • Traits: Serpentine, cold-blooded, matriarchal, scale-painting culture

docs.title: Species
docs.text: A central hub for the sentient species of Ge'or.

docs.title: Major Species
docs.text:
• Elves — ancient, decimated. See: Elves, Fallen Elves
  • Dwarves — mountain dwellers, proto-industrial. See: Dwarves
  • Humans — dominant population. See: Humans, Georian humans
  • Demons — civilized, rational warrior descendants. See: Demons, Demon King, Koebi
  • Orcs — civilized, not inherently evil. See: Orcs, Yak
  • Snake People — serpentine civilization, queen-monarchies. See: Snake People
  • Catmen — feline humanoids, universally loved. See: Catmen, High Catmen, Erisdarian Catmen, Lesser Catmen
  • Malgaridans — humanoid off-worlders, purple hair. See: Malgardians, Titians, Bloodcoast Folk
  • Beast Races — diverse animal-human hybrids. See: Beast Races, Eastern Beastmen
  • Kobolds — reptilian trap-crafters. See: Kobolds, Emberalden Lizardfolk
  • Goblins — tribal sadists. See: Goblins, Enkrad Order
  • Harpies — winged biological weapons from the Last Great War. See: Harpies
  • Gnolls — hyena-like pack hunters. See: Gnolls
  • Dragons — near-extinct. See: Dragons, Fallen Dragon, Dragon Yaldabaoth
  • Trolls — massive, regenerative, simple-minded. See: Trolls
  • Wargs — large wolf-like predators. See: Wargs
  • Homunculi — Hybrian bio-constructs. See: Homunculi
  • Hybrians / Shadows — parasite entities. See: Shadows, Hybrians
  • Flames — gas-based, mineral-eating. See: Flames
  • Giants — 3m humanoids. See: Giants
  • Diablos — winged, nocturnal. See: Diablos
  • Kutra (Owlkin) — humanoid owls, semi-aquatic. See: Kutra (Owlkin)
  • Yaoma (Merfolk) — mermaid-like aquatic. See: Yaoma (Merfolk)
  • Sandsmen — desert-adapted humanoids. See: Sandsmen
  • Treemen — tree-dwelling humanoids. See: Treemen
  • Slimes — mostly irrational, rare intelligent variant. See: Slimes

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: See: Magic, World Dashboard

docs.title: Treemen
docs.text: A humanoid species nearly identical to Humans in appearance, distinguished by their unique architecture: they build their homes inside living trees rather than constructing freestanding buildings. Native to the Lumina Continent.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Indistinguishable from humans at a glance. Slightly leaner build, with skin tones ranging from pale to a bark-like brown
  • Lifespan: 100–120 years — longer than baseline humans, attributed to their symbiosis with forest environments
  • Mage-cell expression: Moderate and specialized — treemen mages focus exclusively on plant growth, wood-shaping, and forest communication. They cannot perform combat magic.
  • Symbiosis: Treemen form a mild empathic bond with the trees they inhabit. A treeman knows when their tree is ill, thirsty, or threatened. This is not magic — it is a biological adaptation evolved over millennia in the deep forests of Lumina.

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Treemen live in arboreal settlements — villages built entirely within massive ancient trees. Their homes are grown, not built: rooms are shaped from living wood over decades, passed down through generations.

  • Family structure: Patriarchal clans. The eldest man of a tree-household is the patriarch.
  • Governance: Council of patriarchs. Decisions are made slowly, with seasons of deliberation. Rushing is considered deeply disrespectful.
  • Religion: Animistic. They believe every old tree holds a fragment of ancestral memory. The oldest trees in their territory are treated as sacred elders.
  • Cultural value: Patience. A treeman who hurries is a treeman who breaks things.

docs.title: Role on Lumina
docs.text: The Tree Tribe occupies a swath of jungle east of the Lumina Republic. They are isolationist by nature — trade exists but is minimal. The Gigas Tribe leaves them alone; the warmongers find no honor in burning trees, and the jungle is too dense for easy conquest. Lesser Catmen occasionally wander through, universally welcomed.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Tree Tribe (Lumina Continent)
  • Traits: Humanoid, tree-dwelling, forest symbiosis, patient culture, patriarchal

docs.title: Wolvesfolk
docs.text: A humanoid canine species — the wolf equivalent of Catmen. Wolvesfolk are humanoid with wolf-like features: ears, tail, sharp canines, and thick fur adapted for cold. They have a large presence in Germina and their own nations of Kut and Oigopol on Marti Continent.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Humanoid with wolf ears, tails, and fur in shades of gray, white, brown, and black. Build varies by region — northern wolvesfolk are stockier with thicker coats. Eyes are amber, gold, or pale blue
  • Lifespan: 65–80 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Low to moderate — some possess howling magic that carries across vast distances
  • Traits: Exceptional hearing and smell. Pack-oriented psychology — wolvesfolk form deep social bonds and are intensely loyal to their "pack" (family, tribe, or nation)

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Wolvesfolk society is pack-based. Each community is organized around an alpha pair — not through combat, but through demonstrated leadership and care for the pack.

  • Nations: Kut, Oigopol on Marti Continent; large minority in Germina
  • Governance: Alpha pairs lead through consensus. The alpha who cannot command respect loses their position naturally
  • Culture: Howl-songs — long-distance communication through melodic howling that carries meaning across miles. Oral tradition is strong; their history is sung, not written. A wolvesfolk's howl-name is their identity
  • Temperament: Loyal, protective, and territorial. A wolvesfolk who bonds with you will die for you. Betraying that bond is the gravest sin. They are not aggressive by nature — they are defensive. Threaten the pack and they become relentless
  • Relations: Close relationship with Catmen and Humans in Germina. Neutral toward Coldspeople. Wary of Snake People in Kobra
  • Religion: Moon-worship. Wolvesfolk believe the moon Maenar watches over the pack. Full-moon nights are sacred — packs gather to howl together

docs.title: Religion — Xuashism and the Moonfang Trade
docs.text:
Most Wolvesfolk historically were animistic pagans. In the last centuries, the nations Kut and Oigopol on Marti and Kyuu on Xeti adopted Xuashism — the recent faith of god Xuashi, promoted from chief of the old pantheon to sole deity.

Xuashists believe Xuashi incarnated in Erisdar as Eris — the goddess of the Erisian Church — and is therefore the father and mother of all other religions on Ge'or.

A dark corollary: Wolvesfolk are frequently kidnapped by pirates and sold to the Moonfang Union — even though the wolvesfolk nations are on the other side of the world from Moonfang Union in the far north. The trade persists because wolvesfolk are prized for pack-loyalty and cold-resilience. Xuashist clergy denounce it as the ultimate perversion of pack — to steal a wolf from his pack is to steal his soul. Large Wolvesfolk diaspora in Germina includes both Xuashists and old animists.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nations: Kut, Oigopol, large minority in Germina (Marti Continent)
  • Traits: Wolf-like humanoids, pack society, howl-communication, intensely loyal, moon-worship

docs.title: Yaoma (Merfolk)
docs.text: A mermaid-like aquatic species inhabiting two islands south of Zakarutia on the Demon Continent. The Yaoma are a fully maritime civilization adapted to island life and open-ocean navigation.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Upper body humanoid, lower body fish-like with a powerful tail fin. Skin ranges from pale blue-green to deep teal. Webbed hands with elongated fingers. Hair is typically silver, sea-green, or deep blue
  • Respiration: Water-breathing only. Yaoma cannot survive extended periods on land — they can beach themselves for an hour or two, but prolonged exposure to air causes their gills to dry and crack
  • Lifespan: 90–110 years
  • Mage-cell expression: High — their mages command currents, summon storms, and communicate with sea creatures. Merfolk magic is tidal: stronger at high tide, weaker at low
  • Reproduction: Eggs laid in warm shallows, guarded communally by the tribe

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
The Yaoma Tribe lives across two islands — one for habitation (surface structures, beaches) and one for governance (a sacred atoll where only the ruling council may tread).

  • Nation: Yaoma Tribe (Demon Continent)
  • Governance: Tide-Council — seven elders chosen by the phases of Amelia and Maenar. Terms last one full lunar cycle of both moons
  • Culture: Music is central. Yaoma songs travel for miles underwater, serving as communication, history-keeping, and art simultaneously. A Yaoma "song-scroll" is a melody that encodes an entire epic. The most respected elders are those who can sing their lineage back a thousand years
  • Economy: Pearl-diving, coral-harvesting, and deep-sea salvage. Yaoma recovered artifacts from sunken vessels are highly prized on the mainland
  • Relations: Neutral with most. Zakarutia trades with them regularly. They avoid the Glub Kingdom — intelligent slimes unsettle them

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Yaoma Tribe (Demon Continent)
  • Traits: Mermaid-like, aquatic-only, tidal magic, song-based culture, egg-laying

docs.title: Zombies
docs.text: Reanimated corpses found in dungeons, ruins, and places of concentrated residual magic — particularly near Dragonreach and the Goldenborn's Caldera. Zombies are not a naturally occurring species; they are dead bodies animated by ambient magical saturation, lacking intelligence or will.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text: Zombies are slow, shambling, and mindless. They do not eat, sleep, or feel pain. Their flesh continues to rot, but the magic that animates them preserves structural integrity far beyond natural decay. Severing the head or destroying the brain typically ends them — though variants infused with stronger magic may require complete dismemberment.

docs.title: Origin
docs.text: Most zombies are the result of magical discharge saturating mass graves, battlefields, or dungeon depths. The same forces that created the Fallen Dragons and mutated the black agent produce lesser undead as a byproduct — bodies too fragile or too dispersed to become anything more.

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text: Zombies are hostile to all living things. They attack on sight, drawn to warmth and life force. They do not strategize, communicate, or retreat. A lone zombie is a nuisance; a horde is a siege.

docs.title: In the World
docs.text:
• Dungeon hazard. Common in the dungeons around Dragonreach, alongside skeletons, spirits, and mutated creatures. The Hunters regularly clear them during raids.
  • Battlefield residue. Regions where massive magical warfare occurred — such as the Draconic War sites — spawn zombies for centuries afterward.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Common in: Dungeons near Dragonreach, Goldenborn's Caldera
  • Hunted by: The Hunters
  • Related: Fallen Dragons, The Draconic War

docs.title: Beast Races
docs.text: One of the Six Main Races of Ge'or — a diverse family of animal-human hybrids. Beast Races span the full moral range of sapient species, from the warmongering Gigas Tribe to the merchant Cammao Kingdom. They are tribal, strength-based, and honor-bound, with a reputation for barbarism that is partly earned and partly stereotype.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Animal-human hybrids — each bloodline carries traits of a specific beast: strength, claws, fur, fangs, tails, or horns. Build varies enormously between tribes
  • Mage-cell expression: Varies by bloodline — some tribes produce powerful shamans, others none at all
  • Lifespan: Comparable to humans, varying by bloodline
  • Traits: Physical power and hardiness. Beast Races are adapted to their homelands — the mountain Gigas are the strongest beastmen on Ge'or, S-tier in raw might

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Beast Race society is tribal and clan-based, organized around strength, honor, and territory.

  • Governance: Tribal chieftains and warrior councils. Tribes include the Gigas Tribe (dominant power on Lumina), the Maoma Tribe (northern Lumina), the Mukini Tribe (Mia), and the Cammao Kingdom (Eastern Beastmen traders with a demonfolk minority)
  • Culture: Strength-based and honor-bound. Status is proven in deeds, not inherited. Beastmen integrate readily into multiracial cities — the beastmen-heavy metropolises of West Erisdar (Augamouth, Astravayne) are the most integrated human-beast societies on the continent
  • Relations: Variable — full moral range. Minority populations live in Germina (Marti Continent), Maboro, and across Erisdar; half-beastman/half-human hybrids occur primarily in multi-ethnic regions like Germina
  • History: Historically, beastmen invasions collapsed the Old Lumina Empire (1134 BGD)

docs.title: Known Nations
docs.text:
• Gigas Tribe — strongest beastmen, dominant power on Lumina, warmongers. S-tier.
  • Maoma Tribe — beastmen tribe on northern Lumina.
  • Mukini Tribe — beastmen on Mia island.
  • Cammao Kingdom — Eastern Beastmen traders + demonfolk minority.
  • Minority populations in Germina (Marti Continent), Maboro, and across Erisdar.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• One of the Six Main Races: Humans, Dwarves, Elves, Demons, Catmen
  • Culture: Tribal, strength-based, honor-bound
  • Reputation: Barbarians — partly earned, partly stereotype
  • Historical Role: Invaded and collapsed the Old Lumina Empire (1134 BGD)
  • Known tribes: Gigas Tribe, Maoma Tribe, Mukini Tribe, Cammao Kingdom
  • Subrace: Eastern Beastmen
  • Relation to other species: Variable — full moral range
  • Mage-Cell Level: Varies by bloodline

docs.title: Erisdarian Catmen
docs.text: A subrace of Catmen with a distinctly Central European look. Erisdarian Catmen typically have blonde, white, red, or other bright-colored hair. They retain the feminine and playful nature common to all catmen, and are found across Ge'or — particularly on Erisdar and the Lumina Continent.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Cat ears, tail, and feline eyes paired with fair skin and bright hair colors — platinum blonde, strawberry red, snowy white. More "elegant" than "cute" compared to Lesser Catmen
  • Lifespan: 70–85 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Moderate. Erisdarian Catmen produce many traveling mages and enchanters — practical magic for life on the road
  • Traits: Feminine regardless of gender. An Erisdarian Catman warrior is still graceful; an Erisdarian Catwoman blacksmith still moves like a dancer

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Erisdarian Catmen are wanderers by nature. While Lesser Catmen are nomadic out of universal acceptance, Erisdarian Catmen travel out of curiosity. They are the explorers, the traders, the minstrels who bring news between continents.

  • Culture: Storytelling is sacred. Every Erisdarian Catman knows a hundred tales and can invent a hundred more on the spot. Their oral tradition is the largest on Ge'or
  • Economy: Entertainment, trade, and courier services. An Erisdarian Catman courier is trusted across continents — even warring nations respect their neutrality
  • Settlements: They have permanent homes on Cattos island and in the Lumina Kingdom, but most spend their lives on the move. "Home is where the story finds you" is a common saying
  • Naming: Individual names follow the catmen convention (descriptor + "ko"), but Erisdarian Catmen often add a place-name: "Tallko of Lumina," "Alko of the Silver Bridge"

docs.title: Religion
docs.text: • Erinya — the catmen version of the Erisian cult, consistent in Central Erisdar. Considered a heresy by the Erisian church but not persecuted. Believes Eris was a catmen woman called Erinya, who will return from death and give infinite richness to all catmen.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Parent species: Catmen
  • Nations: Cattos (offshore Lumina Continent), Lumina Kingdom
  • Found: Widespread — Erisdar, Lumina Continent, beyond
  • Traits: Bright-colored hair, Central European look, wandering storytellers, trusted couriers
  • Religion: Erinya — catmen heresy of the Erisian cult

docs.title: High Catmen
docs.text: A subrace of Catmen native to Estran on the island east of the Demon Continent mainland. High Catmen have a distinctly Mediterranean appearance — typically black hair, darker features, and a more masculine, robust build compared to standard catmen. Where Lesser Catmen are the comic relief and Erisdarian Catmen are the bright wanderers, High Catmen are the statesmen.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Cat-like ears and tail, but with broader shoulders, stronger jawlines, and a generally more athletic build than other catmen. Black hair is the norm; dark brown is seen occasionally
  • Lifespan: 70–90 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Low. High Catmen prefer steel to spells
  • Traits: Less overtly playful than other catmen subraces. They still possess cat-like agility and curiosity, but channel it into politics and warfare rather than mischief

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
High Catmen govern Estran — and more notably, serve as elected rulers of Marko on Kutten. This makes them unique among catmen: where other subraces are beloved, High Catmen are respected.

  • Governance: Elective monarchy in Estran; elected rulership in Marko's international council. High Catmen believe leadership must be earned, not inherited
  • Culture: Martial and political. Young High Catmen train in both swordplay and rhetoric. A famous Estrani saying: "A cat's claws are sharp, but a cat's tongue is sharper"
  • Relations: Esteemed across the Demon Continent and Kutten. The Asatru Empire considers them valuable allies. Oda trades with them. Marko's multi-racial population elected them as rulers — a testament to their diplomatic skill

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Parent species: Catmen
  • Nation: Estran (Yak Island, Demon Continent)
  • Also govern: Marko (Kutten)
  • Traits: Mediterranean look, black hair, masculine build, political class among catmen

docs.title: 🧬 Mutable Genetics — The Western Catmen Divergence
docs.text:
High Catmen carry hyper-mutable genes: in only a few generations they shift color, appearance, and behavior — the rapid emergence of the Mediterranean phenotype after the Central Erisdar persecution and exodus.

Canon: The Estran ancestors left Central Erisdar in the Human Era after persecution, settling colonies on the west and the Demon Continent to seek glory for catmen. Their descendants became Estran and all western High Catmen.

Crossbreeding taboo: Human × catmen unions yield 90% catmen offspring, 10% human — the catmen genome dominates. This has produced a strong cultural taboo on human–catmen marriages across Ge'or.

See faith: Kludosy (Estran western-catmen creed).

docs.title: Lesser Catmen
docs.text: A smaller subrace of Catmen, even more playful and feminine than their kin. Lesser Catmen come in every color — purple, white, black, and all shades between. They are universally beloved across Ge'or: no species wages war against them, and armies simply pass through their territories during conflicts. Often called the comic relief of Ge'or, Lesser Catmen are nomadic and can be found living everywhere — in kingdoms, cities, tribes, or wandering the roads.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Small and delicate — noticeably smaller than other catmen. Fur and hair in every color: purple, white, black, and all shades between. Large expressive eyes; an almost universally "cute" appearance that is itself a survival adaptation
  • Lifespan: 65–80 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Very low. Lesser Catmen are not mages — their magic is charm
  • Traits: Playful, feminine, and endlessly energetic. Exceptional agility, quick reflexes, and a talent for landing on their feet in every sense

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Lesser Catmen are nomadic by nature — found in kingdoms, cities, tribes, or wandering the roads, always welcome wherever they arrive.

  • Origin — Born of the Hunger. The smaller catmen are a breed shaped by tragedy. During the Human Age, the xenophobic empire of Termopolas moved to exterminate catmen; in the long starvation of that persecution, some catmen were changed permanently — smaller, lighter, a variant born of hunger. The Lesser Catmen descend from those who survived the famine of the catmen holocaust, saved from extinction by Masaaki Sytrenis, "the Diplomat," whom they revere as their ancestor.

  • Religion — Sytrenis. Most Lesser Catmen believe in Sytrenis, the most ancient catmen religion, founded by their ancestor-hero; they try to live as diplomats.

  • Culture: The comic relief of Ge'or. Lesser Catmen live for play, pranks, and comfort. They collect friends the way other species collect wealth

  • Relations: Universally beloved. No species wages war against them — armies simply pass through their territories during conflicts. They have an informal alliance of "creatures too cute to wage war against" with Halflings
  • Governance: None central — they adopt the governance of wherever they live, from the Lake Kingdom and Great Cattos on Lumina Continent to Cattos and countless mixed cities

docs.title: Naming Convention
docs.text:
Catmen names are derived from simple descriptors: - "alcohol cat" → Alko - "tall cat" → Tallko

Their cities and nations follow similarly playful patterns: Cattos, Great Cattos.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Parent species: Catmen
  • Nations: Lake Kingdom, Great Cattos, Cattos, and many others
  • Found: Everywhere on Ge'or
  • Traits: Small, all colors, universally liked, comic relief, nomadic

docs.title: Merratodonian Catmen
docs.text: A regional variant of Catmen native to the Merratodoni continent. Merratodonian Catmen have adapted to the heavily forested interior, developing traits suited to arboreal life. They are found in Kelkot, the Purple Coast, and the Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Forest-colored fur — deep greens, browns, and muted grays. More agile and lean than Erisdarian Catmen. Their ears are slightly larger, adapted for navigating dense forest by sound
  • Lifespan: 65–80 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Low; some individuals develop minor plant-communication abilities
  • Traits: Exceptional climbers. A Merratodonian Catman can scale a tree faster than most species can run on flat ground

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Merratodonian Catmen live in the deep forests of Merratodoni, organized around arboreal communities and the tree-routes that connect them.

  • Governance: Loose forest-councils of elders; they integrate into the human and elven settlements of the continent — Kelkot, the Purple Coast, and the Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni
  • Culture: Quiet and observant compared to other catmen — forest life rewards patience. They are renowned trackers, herbalists, and couriers along the canopy roads
  • Relations: Close ties with the elven communities of Merratodoni; their forest knowledge is traded freely with the Purple Coast's alchemists

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Parent species: Catmen
  • Nations: Kelkot, Purple Coast, Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni
  • Traits: Forest-adapted, agile climbers, muted colors

docs.title: 🧬 Biology
docs.text:
• Lifespan: Up to 120 years. Longer than humans, shorter than elves or dwarves.
  • Appearance: Varies by subrace — crimson, green (Koebi), or other skin tones. Curved horns, sharp features. Physically formidable — larger and stronger than Georian humans.
  • Reproduction: Traditional family structures. Demons form lasting bonds and raise children in stable households.

docs.title: Warrior Ethic
docs.text:
Demons are a warrior race. This does not mean they are warmongers — it means they approach all of life as a form of combat. Business is battle. Politics is battle. Self-improvement is battle. A demon who is not striving to overcome something is a demon who is wasting their life.

They are serious in their dealings. They do not play games. They do not waste time on frivolity. A demon's word is a contract; a demon's promise is a blood oath.

docs.title: Honor & Meritocracy
docs.text:
Demon society is honor-based and meritocratic. Status is earned, not inherited. The strongest warrior leads. The wisest elder advises. The most skilled craftsman is respected regardless of birth. Demons do not care who your parents were. They care what you have done.

An honor duel is the highest form of dispute resolution. To be challenged to an honor duel is not an insult — it is a recognition that you are worth fighting.

docs.title: Asceticism
docs.text: Demons are ascetic by nature. They live simply. They do not hoard wealth, build palaces, or indulge in luxury. What matters is the next mountain to climb, the next opponent to face, the next limit to break. Comfort is the enemy of growth.

docs.title: The Disappointment with Humanity
docs.text:
Demons carry a quiet, persistent disappointment with Humans. They see humanity as a species of immense potential — potential that humans consistently fail to realize. Humans could be rivals. Humans could be equals. Instead, humans chase money, build empires, and meddle in each other's affairs rather than perfecting themselves.

The dream of the demons is to one day find a human who is truly serious — a human who has dedicated themselves to mastery, who approaches life as a warrior approaches combat. And then, to have an honor duel with that human. Not out of hatred. Out of respect. Out of the desire to test oneself against the best.

This dream has not yet been fulfilled.

docs.title: Traditional Families
docs.text: Despite their warrior ethos, demons value traditional family structures. They marry, raise children, and maintain household lineages. A demon who dies without having passed on their knowledge to the next generation has died incompletely.

docs.title: Subraces on the Demon Continent
docs.text:
• Koebi — taller, green-colored, meditative culture (Koebi Tribe)
  • Xiobita — exceptionally tall and strong. The current Asatru imperial line under Emperor Bionidas
  • Bjor — slightly heavier-set, medium stature. The subrace of the Demon King himself
  • Other demon subraces and variants exist across the Demon Continent

docs.title: 🏛️ Demon Nations
docs.text:
• Asatru Empire — largest demon power, spiritual successor to Demon King's empire (northeast)
  • Maomodor Kingdom — main demon race, highly multi-racial (southwest)
  • Koebi Tribe — Koebi subrace nation (south)
  • Colony: Asatru Knight's Thorn on West Erisdar

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Demons ] ├── Notable Member: Demon King — Tragic Hero ├── Subraces: Koebi ├── Nations: Asatru Empire, Maomodor Kingdom, Koebi Tribe ├── Arrived: With the crash ~15,000 BGD ├── Allied Species: Humans, Dragons, others ├── Enemy: Hybrians, Shadows ├── Misnamed By: Erisian church — Historical Erasure ├── Religion: Kirivs-bin — the spiritual path of demon legends ├── Associated Event: Demonic War └── True Record: Archive of the Traveler

docs.title: Koebi
docs.text: A subrace of Demons native to the Demon Continent, primarily inhabiting the Koebi Tribe territory south of Blazeyard and the Asatru Empire. Koebi are notably taller than standard demons and have a green coloration. Their culture emphasizes hard work and meditation — daily meditation is a central practice.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Tall (2.2–2.5 meters), lean-muscled, with skin in shades of forest green to olive. Horns are longer and more curved than standard demons. Eyes are amber or gold
  • Lifespan: 150–180 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Moderate. Koebi mages practice somatic magic — spells channeled through precise physical movements rather than incantations
  • Traits: Exceptional endurance. A Koebi can work or meditate for days without sleep. Their metabolism is remarkably efficient

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
The Koebi Tribe is defined by the practice of Vash-ka — a meditative discipline combining physical labor and spiritual contemplation. A Koebi stonecutter does not merely cut stone; they meditate through the cutting.

  • Governance: Monastery-council. The most accomplished practitioners of Vash-ka lead — not through election, but through demonstration of spiritual and physical mastery
  • Culture: Work as prayer. Every task — farming, building, fighting — is approached as meditation. There is no concept of "menial labor" in Koebi society; all work is sacred
  • Economy: Stonework and metalwork of extraordinary quality. Koebi-crafted tools and weapons are traded across the Demon Continent. Their meditation chambers — carved from single boulders — are architectural marvels
  • Relations: Respected by the Maomodor Kingdom and the Asatru Empire. The Zakarutia snake-queen once commissioned a Koebi meditation chamber for her palace — a rare diplomatic gesture

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Parent species: Demons
  • Nation: Koebi Tribe (Demon Continent)
  • Traits: Taller, green-colored, meditative work-culture, exceptional craftsmen

docs.title: Dragons
docs.text: An ancient, spaceborn species — one of the few races on Ge'or whose origins lie beyond the Glorious Alliance survivors. Dragons once ruled the world during the Dragon Tyranny (6,999–5,500 BGD), when twelve clans controlled ninety percent of the known land. Today they are nearly extinct: wild dragons roam remote wilderness, and the last civilized population lives in the frozen highlands of Kramsadar.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Origin: Spaceborn — dragons evolved in space, where their hoarding instinct began as a survival drive: attracting metallic asteroids for shelter from radiation
  • Lifespan: Millennia. Civilized dragons speak with the weight of millennia — a dragon in full form is indistinguishable from a god to most species
  • Forms: Dragons possess a full form and lesser forms; most of the world encounters them only in their smaller incarnations
  • Types: Wild dragons — territorial predators driven by instinct, hoarding treasure out of an inherited drive. Civilized dragons — fully sapient, capable of language, culture, and society
  • Mage-cell expression: Extreme in civilized bloodlines — dragon magic is the largest concentration of power on Ge'or, as proven by The Draconic War, whose discharge saturated the atmosphere with the Black Agent

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Civilized dragon society is honor-based, ascetic, and deliberately removed from the world.

  • Nation: Kramsadar on Marti Continent — the last significant population of civilized dragons. Half tundra, half near-permafrost, chosen deliberately: the dragons want to be left alone
  • Culture: Honor codes, personal oaths, and ritualized combat. They do not meddle in Ge'orian affairs — they follow Daicrodism, worship their god, conduct ancient rituals, and live peaceful, contemplative lives
  • Religion: Daicrodism — the atonement faith of peace and prosperity for all beings, evolved from the war-religion Diocronism after the death wars. The seclusion of Kramsadar is itself an act of faith. The exception: rogue dragons — the uncivilized ones — follow no faith.
  • History: Twelve clans ruled ninety percent of the world in Age 4; their empire collapsed in the death wars. The dragon empires of Klobiendar and Xi fell in The Draconic War, leaving Dragonreach haunted by Fallen Dragons
  • Notable: Goldenborn — the Dragon-King of Baoth, now in quasi-death; Dragon Yaldabaoth — the entity inhabiting the Ruins of Baoth

docs.title: Wild Dragons
docs.text: Wild dragons are beasts — territorial, predatory, and driven by instinct. They are the rogue exception: uncivilized, they follow no faith, unlike the Daicrodism-keeping civilized dragons. They lair in remote mountains, deep forests, or volcanic caverns. They hoard treasure not out of greed but out of an instinctive drive to accumulate — a behavior left over from their spaceborne evolution, when attracting metallic asteroids provided shelter from radiation. Wild dragons can be hunted — though the hunters rarely return.

docs.title: Civilized Dragons
docs.text:
Civilized dragons are fully sapient, capable of language, culture, and society. The dragons of Kramsadar on Marti Continent are the last significant population of civilized dragons on Ge'or. They are:

  • Honor-based — their society is built on codes of conduct, personal oaths, and ritualized combat.
  • Deity-like — those who encounter civilized dragons often describe them in religious terms. A dragon in full form, speaking with the weight of millennia, is indistinguishable from a god to most species.
  • Ascetic — they do not meddle in Ge'orian affairs. They have better things to do: worship their god, conduct ancient rituals, and live peaceful, contemplative lives.
  • Isolated — Kramsadar is half tundra, half near-permafrost. The dragons chose this place deliberately. They want to be left alone.

docs.title: Notable Dragons
docs.text:
• Goldenborn — The Dragon-King of Baoth, now in quasi-death
  • Dragon Yaldabaoth — The entity inhabiting the Ruins of Baoth

docs.title: Fallen Dragons
docs.text:
Half-alive. Half-dead. They can speak. They are usually violent — unless you prove worthy.

Fallen Dragons are the remnants of the dragon empires destroyed in The Draconic War. They are not undead in the conventional sense. They are immortal — saturated with the black agent, unable to truly die.

docs.title: Origin — The Black Agent
docs.text:
When Melberior of Xi launched his suicide spell at Klobiendar's capital, the magic discharge was so immense that it extracted the black agent from the atmosphere — where it had been suspended for millions of years since the glassing of the 157th Colony research stations.

The dragons who died in the blast were saturated with it. It filled their bodies. It replaced what death had taken. They became something between life and death — conscious but not living, powerful but bound to Dragonreach.

The black agent is attracted to magic like iron to a magnet. The Draconic War was the largest concentration of magic ever discharged on Ge'or. It pulled the agent from the sky.

docs.title: Nature
docs.text:
Fallen Dragons inhabit Dragonreach, circling the peaks and caverns of the ruined capital. They are:

  • Immortal — the black agent prevents true death. They cannot be killed by conventional means.
  • Half-alive, half-dead — similar to the entity in the Ruins of Baoth
  • Capable of speech — they can communicate with those who enter their domain
  • Violent by default — most intruders are killed immediately
  • Capable of respect — a person who proves themselves worthy may be spared, or even aided

docs.title: How They Fall
docs.text:
A dragon becomes a Fallen Dragon through one of four mechanisms:

Mechanism Description Shadow Possession A Hybrian shadow enters a dead or dying dragon and assumes control. The most common and dangerous form. Volitional Undeath The dragon's will is so absolute it refuses death. Rare. The dragon retains more of itself — but deteriorates over centuries. Necromantic Binding An external sorcerer or force raises the dragon as a weapon. The dragon's original mind is usually collateral damage. Curse or Oath A dragon cursed to guard a place or object beyond death. Sleeps until disturbed. The Leviathan connection suggests this possibility.

docs.title: Known Fallen Dragons
docs.text:
• Fireborn — former king of Klobiendar, father of Goldenborn. The most prominent Fallen Dragon. Carries the black agent within him. Incarnated with Julian the Dragon Tamer. Waits for two future prophets to test and prove.
  • Dragon Yaldabaoth — Ruins of Baoth. Active. Category unknown — likely Shadow Possession.
  • Unnamed — folklore references throughout Erisdar. Unconfirmed. Local legends of "grey wyrms" in mountain passes.

docs.title: The Hivemind
docs.text: All Fallen Dragons are connected to the Black Agent Hivemind — a vast intelligence born from the concentrated black agent inside Goldenborn's Caldera. The hivemind is what gave them their awareness, their purpose, and their hatred of the Hybrians. It controls Dragonreach through them. Every Fallen Dragon is a node in its network. None act independently.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Fallen Dragons ] ├── Origin: The Draconic War — Melberior's suicide spell ├── Mechanism: Black Agent extracted from atmosphere by the magic discharge ├── Source of Black Agent: The 157th Colony glassing — dispersed into atmosphere for millions of years ├── Location: Dragonreach ├── Notable: Fireborn ├── Behavior: Violent unless respect is earned ├── Related: Dragon Yaldabaoth (Ruins of Baoth — similar state) ├── Status: Immortal — bound to Dragonreach by the black agent └── Part Of: Ge'or

docs.title: Dwarves
docs.text: One of the Six Main Races of Ge'or — a sturdy, long-lived humanoid species that once dominated the world through industry. Dwarves are the master craftsmen of Ge'or: brilliant smiths, miners, and mass producers whose works are found in every nation. Their golden age was Age 5, when underground megacities fueled by Romanium ore supplied the entire known world.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: 150–170 cm tall, stocky and broad-shouldered. Males grow huge beards — a point of pride and identity. Hypermasculine bearing regardless of actual gender
  • Lifespan: Up to 200 years. Dwarves reproduce late — typically at 90–100 years of age
  • Mage-cell expression: Low. Dwarves favor craft and steel over spells
  • Traits: Exceptional endurance. Precision and perfectionism in everything they build. Their constitution shrugs off hardship that would break other species

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Dwarven society is honor-bound, proud, and industrious — built around craft, clan, and community.

  • Governance: Clan-based monarchies and guild-councils. Dwarven nations include Dwarvengor, Coalsteel Kingdom, Diamonds Kingdom, Cobal Kingdom, and the Purple Coast
  • Culture: Honorable, prideful, and fiercely loyal, with a great sense of humor — and heavy drinking. Industry is identity: mass production in a medieval world, where precision is a form of worship
  • Religion: Dwarvism — the Three Doctrines (Coal, Diamond, and Emerald)
  • Relations: Rivalry with Elves — a healthy, respectful opposition of industry vs. nature. Treasured trade partners with Humans. Mixed communities exist in Dwarvengor and the mountain cities of East Erisdar
  • Weakness: A high death rate — mining accidents, industrial hazards, and combat glory claim many dwarves before their time
  • Subgroups: Eastern Dwarves — surface-dwelling, trade-oriented, cosmopolitan

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• Age 5 — Dwarf Era (−5,499 to −4,500 BGD) — Dwarves dominated Ge'or through underground megacities fueled by Romanium ore. They manufactured weapons, tools, and commodities for most of the known world.
  • Economic collapse — When Romanium ran out, the dwarven economy collapsed over centuries. The world entered Age 6.
  • Modern era — Dwarven presence persists strongly in nations like Dwarvengor, Coalsteel Kingdom, Diamonds Kingdom, Cobal Kingdom, and Purple Coast.
  • Subgroups — Eastern Dwarves (surface-dwelling, trade-oriented, cosmopolitan)

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Dwarves ] ├── One of the Six Main Races: Humans, Elves, Demons, Beast Races, Catmen ├── Height: 150–170 cm ├── Lifespan: Up to 200 years — reproduce at 90–100 ├── Traits: Huge beards (males), hypermasculine, brilliant craftsmen ├── Culture: Honorable, prideful, loyal, great humor, heavy drinkers ├── Religion: Dwarvism — Three Doctrines (Coal, Diamond, Emerald) ├── Industry: Mass production in a medieval world — precision and perfection ├── Golden Age: Age 5 — Dwarf Era — fueled by Romanium ├── Modern Nations: Dwarvengor, Coalsteel Kingdom, Diamonds Kingdom, Cobal Kingdom, Purple Coast ├── Subgroups: Eastern Dwarves ├── Rivalry: Elves — healthy, respectful, industrial vs natural ├── Allies: Humans — treasured trade partners ├── Weakness: High death rate — mining accidents, industrial hazards, combat glory └── Arrived: With the crash ~15,000 BGD

docs.title: Eastern Dwarves
docs.text: The dwarven population east of the central mountain ranges, concentrated in territories like Dwarvengor and its surrounding highlands. Culturally distinct from their western kin, Eastern Dwarves favor surface-level masonry and commerce over deep-mining traditions.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Stocky and powerfully built (1.35–1.55m), like all dwarves, but with slightly lighter builds than their deep-mining cousins. Hair ranges from auburn to light brown — lighter than western dwarves, attributed to generations of surface living. Beards are shorter and more groomed, reflecting their commercial sensibilities
  • Lifespan: 180–220 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Low. Eastern Dwarves prefer craftsmanship to magic. Runesmithing — the inscription of minor enchantments into stone and metal — is their specialty
  • Traits: Exceptional stamina and heat tolerance from generations of forge-work above ground. Eastern Dwarves can work a forge for 16-hour shifts without fatigue

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Eastern Dwarf society is built around trade, not tradition. Where western dwarves measure wealth in ore veins and ancestral halls, eastern dwarves measure it in contracts, trade routes, and diplomatic marriages.

  • Governance: Merchant councils in Dwarvengor — a dwarven council-confederation where the wealthiest forge-families elect representatives. Smaller eastern dwarf communities in Xeti, Tabontabar, and Lumina follow similar patterns
  • Culture: Cosmopolitan and pragmatic. Eastern dwarves trade freely with Humans, Elves, and Catmen — behavior that older western dwarven clans consider dangerously diluted. Their architecture blends dwarven stonework with human-influenced designs: vaulted ceilings above ground, not below
  • Economy: Forge-goods, rune-inscribed tools, and construction contracts. Eastern dwarves built many of the great bridges and aqueducts of East Erisdar and beyond
  • Relations: Close trade partners with the Silver Republic and Dissenbarg city-states. Viewed with suspicion by traditionalist dwarves who consider surface-dwelling a betrayal of dwarven heritage

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Dwarvengor (East Erisdar)
  • Also found in: Mountain regions of Xeti, Tabontabar, Lumina Continent
  • Traits: Surface-dwelling, trade-oriented, cosmopolitan, runesmiths
  • Cultural analog: Renaissance-era merchant dwarves

docs.title: Elves
docs.text: One of the Six Main Races of Ge'or — an ancient, graceful humanoid species that once ruled the world during the Elvish Age. Elves are nature-attuned, long-lived, and the only species the Shadows cannot control: their minds are genetically closed to Hybrian hivemind absorption, which is why the Shadows engineered centuries of hatred against them.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Tall, graceful, with pointed ears and ageless features. Nature-attuned bearing
  • Lifespan: Up to 400 years — the longest of the main races
  • Reproduction: 3–4 children per elf — their population can scale quickly when conditions allow
  • Mage-cell expression: High. Elven magic is nature-attuned, expressed through the gardens, mazes, and living art they are famous for
  • Traits: Genetic immunity — elves cannot be absorbed into the Hybrian hivemind, cannot be mind-read, and cannot be converted into Shadow puppets. Their minds are closed

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Elven society is patient, nature-worshiping, and deliberately slow — measured in decades where other species measure in days.

  • Governance: Reclusive kingdoms and refuge states: Elvennrin in Central Erisdar, Elvenkrad in North Erisdar, Luzia and Maemon on Merratodoni, New Elvengar on Kutten, and the elven/halfling nation of Barro and Kob
  • Culture: Nature-worship and a carnivore ethic. Patient wisdom; elves do not rush decisions that will outlive them. Their art — gardens, mazes, living architecture — was legendary across Erisdar during their golden age
  • Disposition: Not warmongers — elves fight only to defend
  • Relations: Rivalry with Dwarves — a healthy, complementary friendship of nature and industry is possible. They tolerate Humans with polite condescension. They ally with anyone who fights the Shadows
  • History: Golden age under Elvengar in Age 6; shattered by the Hybrian crash, the Great Divergence, the Kutten Catastrophe, and the Great Elvish Persecution (137 AGD) — all engineered or exploited by the Shadows

docs.title: Genetic Immunity
docs.text:
Elves cannot be absorbed into the Hybrian hivemind. During The Last Great War, they genetically modified themselves to resist Shadow brainwashing and information extraction. An elf cannot be turned, cannot be mind-read, cannot be converted into a Shadow puppet. Their minds are closed.

This is why the Shadows engineered the myth of elven evil. This is why the Erisian church — a Shadow creation — institutionalized elven hatred. It was never about theology. It was about eliminating the one species the Shadows cannot control.

docs.title: Golden Age
docs.text: During Age 6, known as the Elvish Age, the elves rose to dominance across Ge'or. Elvengar expanded from Kutten to conquer parts of the Demon Continent and West Erisdar. While other species struggled with post-Romanium poverty, the elves thrived — their nature-attuned culture did not depend on mines and industry. They built gardens, mazes, and art of legendary beauty across all Erisdar. The golden age ended when the Hybrian ship crashed in Pontus in 2989 BGD, triggering human invasions that pushed the elves back to Kutten.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• Elvengar — First great elven kingdom, destroyed in the Great Divergence (Year 0) and the subsequent Kutten Catastrophe.
  • Great Elvish Persecution (137 AGD) — Systematic campaign by the Erisian church against elven survivors. A Shadow operation.
  • The Elvish Diaspora — Survivors scattered across Ge'or, founding refuge states.
  • Elvennrin — Surviving elven realm in Central Erisdar.
  • Elvenkrad — Elven state in North Erisdar.
  • Luzia / Maemon — Elven refuge and spiritual homeland on Merratodoni.
  • New Elvengar — Restoration attempt on Kutten.
  • Fallen Elves — Splinter group that retreated into the Mystical Forest.
  • Barro and Kob — Elven/halfling island nation on Merratodoni.

docs.title: Fallen Elves
docs.text: A splinter population of Elves who retreated into the Mystical Forest during the Great Elvish Persecution rather than flee across the sea to Merratodoni. The forest's anomalous properties became their refuge — and their prison. Also known as The Hidden, Forest Elves, or The Lost Kin.

docs.title: 🧬 Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Share the elven form — tall, graceful, pointed ears, ageless features — shaped by generations lived within the Mystical Forest's anomalous aura
  • Lifespan: Up to 400 years, like all elves
  • Mage-cell expression: High, and deeply nature-attuned. The forest's strange properties amplify their connection to the land around Lake Leviathan
  • Traits: Invisible to the outside world. The Fallen Elves guard the outer ring of the Ruins of Baoth and Lake Leviathan, keeping watch over what sleeps beneath

docs.title: 📜 History
docs.text: The Fallen Elves are believed to be a splinter population that retreated into the Mystical Forest during the Great Elvish Persecution rather than flee across the sea to Merratodoni. The forest, with its anomalous properties, became their refuge — and their prison.

docs.title: ⚠️ Note
docs.text: The Fallen Elves inhabit the Mystical Forest surrounding Lake Leviathan and the Ruins of Baoth in Central Erisdar. The forest is unclaimed by any nation.

docs.title: 🪲 Kobre Gearmites
docs.text: [!INFO] The Steel Pest — Beetles That Jam Gears Slag-dust beetles of the Kobre forges — tiny pests that eat spilled grain and iron-oxide dust; filings cling to their carapaces by static*, hunted by Gearwardens.

docs.title: 🪲 Habitat & Size
docs.text: Infest coal piles and slag heaps of Coalsteel — 2cm, metallic-brown carapaces. Chew spilled grain and iron-oxide dust, excrete rust powder that jams real Kobran Gear gear-purses if not cleaned. Carapaces do not mesh — trainees practice by meshing steel filings, not shells.

docs.title: 🔗 Ties

docs.title: 🦪 Meble Deep Pearlbearers

docs.text: At 280-320m in the trench east of Meble. Oyster shells 60cm, siphons filter volcanic minerals — pearls grow with trench mineral tint, hence silver-hoop pearls grade by luster.

docs.title: 🔗 Ties
docs.text: Only Sousu breath-hold divers can reach them (tied off for body recovery). One bed yields one pearl per decade — hence pearl hoops are notched for fractions with freshwater pearls. Product is Meble Pearls resource → Meblean Pearl coin. Pearlbearers are never harvested — only pearls, shells stay.

docs.title: 🐺 War Wolves
docs.text:
[!INFO] Goldenborn's Guardians — The Dragon's Wolves Massive wolf subspecies bred by dragon Goldenborn to guard Goldenborn's Caldera and the Hivemind cave. Feral since the fall of dragon empires.

War Wolves are a subspecies of Wargs bred by the old dragon empires during the age before Baoth. Larger, more intelligent, and fiercely loyal, they were used to maintain control over cities — patrolling streets, enforcing order.

docs.title: Origin
docs.text: The dragon empires of Klobiendar, Xi, and their contemporaries selectively bred wargs over generations for intelligence, obedience, and ferocity. They understood commands, recognized faces, could patrol a district for hours without a handler.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text: Larger than common wargs, 4-5 feet at shoulder, 1.6m, 300kg, charcoal grey to deep black with faint golden markings of Goldenborn bloodline. Lifespan 40-60 years, though few reach old age. Black-grey pelts laced with Black Agent trace (pups heal fast). Howl carries 4km in thin air.

docs.title: Habitat & Range
docs.text: Packs roam the Dragonreach wilds of West Erisdar — the caldera foothills and high vales where Goldenborn nested. Once organized under dragon command, now feral and territorial. Some packs still circle the Caldera — behaviorists say they remember the dragon. The war wolves of Dragonreach are the purest surviving bloodline, guarding mountain passes with same ferocity they once guarded Goldenborn himself.

docs.title: Loyalty
docs.text: A war wolf bonds to a master for life — not magical but behavioral, reinforced through generations. A bonded war wolf will guard its master's body after death, refuse food from strangers, and starve rather than accept a new owner.

docs.title: Decline
docs.text:
After the fall of dragon empires and the Draconic War, population collapsed. Without breeding programs, they scattered across Ge'or. Today rare fauna — most abundant near dragon presence, though small populations adapted elsewhere. Wild packs of Dragonreach remain most feared.

Direct source for Marti Hides lore (pelts are lesser wolves, not War Wolves — killing a War Wolf is taboo). Adventurer guilds post bounties, but War Wolves kill parties. The Hunters track them.

docs.title: 🐍 Habitat & Size
docs.text: Dense vine jungles of Xeti near Ograd copper pits and Kyuu riverways. 5m long, copper sheen, non-venomous constrictors that coil exactly 3 turns around prey — hence three-turn Coil = day's wage for Koetebalo porters.

docs.title: Gnolls
docs.text: Hyena-like pack hunters found worldwide. Gnolls are opportunistic scavengers and raiders — they prefer easy prey, overwhelming through numbers and viciousness rather than skill. They are cowards individually, but dangerous in packs.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Humanoid hyenas (1.7–2.0m), with spotted fur, powerful jaws, and a loping gait. Sloped shoulders, long arms, hunched posture. Their laughter — a cackling, eerie sound — is a hunting call
  • Lifespan: 40–50 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Very low. Gnoll shamans exist but are weak
  • Traits: Exceptional sense of smell. Gnolls can track prey for days. They eat anything — carrion, bone, leather, each other
  • Strength: Powerful jaws that can crack bone and bite through cured leather. A gnoll's bite is its primary weapon, used even in the middle of a full pack-rush

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Gnolls have no nations, no cities, and no written laws — but they are not without social structure. Pack society is built entirely around the hunt and the feast.

  • Pack structure: A gnoll pack ranges from a dozen to over a hundred individuals, led by the strongest and most successful hunter. Leadership is practical: the gnoll that feeds the pack leads it. Challenges are settled by teeth, and the loser either submits or becomes the meal — gnolls do not waste meat
  • Dens: Nomadic by nature, packs den in caves, ruins, and dead groves, moving with the seasons and the food supply. A den is not defended to the death — it is abandoned the moment it becomes dangerous to stay
  • Young: Pups are raised communally, but survival is brutal. The weak are culled by hunger, not by ceremony. A pack that cannot feed itself simply does not grow
  • The Laugh: The hyena-laugh is a real hunting tool — a pack converges on the sound. To travelers, the first sign of a gnoll pack is that horrible laughter echoing through the trees, closer each time

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Pack hunters. Gnolls fight in coordinated packs, targeting the weak, the isolated, and the wounded
  • Scavengers first. They prefer to steal kills rather than make them. A gnoll pack will follow an army for days, waiting for the battle to end so they can feast on the dead
  • Cowardice as strategy. A lone gnoll flees; a pack of thirty retreats only when the meat stops being worth the wounds. They have no concept of honor — only cost and reward
  • Cohabitation with kobolds. Gnolls and Kobolds often share territory — the gnolls provide muscle, the kobolds provide traps

docs.title: Relations
docs.text: Gnolls are treated as pests or monsters by every civilization on Ge'or. Bounties are common in frontier regions; some warlords have tried to hire gnoll packs as auxiliaries, with predictable results — gnolls serve no master, and a hired pack that runs out of enemy corpses will start counting its paymasters instead. The Enkrad Order on Dissenbarg tolerates no gnoll packs in its territory, hunting them like the predators they are.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Traits: Hyena-like, pack hunters, scavengers, worldwide
  • Kin: Wargs (fellow pack predators), Kobolds (cohabitants)
  • Prey of: Frontier bounties, Enkrad Order patrols

docs.title: Goblins
docs.text: Small, sadistic, cruel humanoids found worldwide. Goblins are semi-intelligent — smart enough to use weapons and lay traps, vicious enough to prolong suffering recreationally. They are the most common hostile species on Ge'or, infesting caves, ruins, and dark forests across every continent.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Small (0.9–1.2m), green-skinned, with pointed ears, sharp teeth, and long nimble fingers adapted for trap-making. Hunched posture, quick movements
  • Lifespan: 30–40 years — but few live that long. Goblins die young, usually violently
  • Mage-cell expression: Very low. Goblin shamans are rare and crude
  • Reproduction: Extremely fast. A goblin female can birth 3–5 offspring per litter, multiple times per year. This is why goblins are never truly eradicated

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Goblins have no civilization in the usual sense — no cities, no writing, no laws — but they do have society: warrens, tribes, and a brutal hierarchy shaped by fear.

  • Warrens: Goblin communities are underground warrens — cramped tunnels, refuse pits, and breeding chambers carved beneath ruins, forests, and mountain foothills. A warren is filthy, dangerous, and difficult to assault: goblins defend their tunnels with traps and ambushes, not walls
  • Tribes and chieftains: Tribes form around the strongest or cruelest goblin, who claims the title of chief by killing the previous holder. Goblin loyalty lasts exactly as long as the chief's ability to punish betrayal. Assassination is the standard political process
  • Tool users. Goblins craft crude weapons, set snares, and build warrens. They are not mindless — they are cruel with purpose
  • Numbers over skill: Goblins win through mass and attrition. A warren that loses half its fighters in a raid can replenish within a season — no other species on Ge'or breeds remotely as fast

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Cowardly in small groups, bold in large ones. A lone goblin flees. Twenty goblins will swarm a knight
  • Sadism: Goblins torture for pleasure, not information. Captives are kept for games, bait, or food — rarely for ransom
  • No centralized society. Goblins form tribes and warbands, but no goblin empire exists. The Enkrad Order on Dissenbarg is the closest thing to organized goblin civilization — and it is an anomaly

docs.title: History
docs.text: Goblins are one of the few native species of Ge'or — they did not arrive with the Glorious Alliance crash. They were already here, infesting the dark places of the planet, when the allied species crawled from the wreckage fifteen thousand years ago. Every civilization since has tried to exterminate them. Every civilization has failed. Their true threat was never their strength — it was their numbers, and the Shadows noticed.

docs.title: The Pontus Horde
docs.text: Beneath Pontus, the Shadows control a massive goblin army through a captured Goblin King. These goblins are bred, trained, and equipped for the Armageddon invasion — the only organized goblin army in the world, and the largest. When the Shadows finally move, the horde will not be a nuisance. It will be a tide.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nations: Enkrad Order (Dissenbarg) — goblin exception
  • Pontus horde: Shadow-controlled army under Goblin King of Pontus
  • Traits: Small, cruel, fast-breeding, worldwide pest species
  • Kin: Kobolds, Gnolls — fellow underground-dwelling hostile species

docs.title: Harpies
docs.text: Winged humanoid females created as biological weapons during The Last Great War. Harpies are not "evil" in the moral sense — they follow biological imperatives programmed into them three million years ago. Their reproductive cycle requires a host: they forcibly implant their young, which gestate inside the victim and consume the host's body upon emergence. The offspring resemble the mother's species with wings.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Humanoid females with large feathered wings (2–3m span). Sharp talons on both hands and feet. Hollow bones — light enough for sustained flight. Vicious, intelligent eyes
  • Lifespan: 50–60 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Moderate. Harpy mages specialize in wind manipulation — they can create downdrafts that ground flying opponents and gusts that throw soldiers off cliffs
  • Reproduction: See cycle above. Harpies cannot reproduce without a host. All harpies are female — they reproduce parthenogenically, offspring cloning the mother

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Territorial. Harpies nest in high, inaccessible places — mountains, cliffs, ruined towers. They defend their roosts with coordinated aerial attacks
  • Matriarchal. Harpy flocks are led by the eldest and strongest female. The matriarch's word is absolute
  • Intelligent but alien. Harpies can speak, negotiate, and make deals. They are not mindless monsters. But their biological imperatives make coexistence with other species nearly impossible
  • Cultural memory. Some harpies retain fragmented memories of the Last Great War — nightmares of the laboratory, the cold of space, the screaming of their creators. These harpies are the most dangerous, because they understand what was done to them

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nations: Harpies (North Erisdar), Tuba harpies
  • Origin: Biological weapons — The Last Great War
  • Traits: Winged, matriarchal, parasitic reproduction, intelligent but hostile

docs.title: Homunculi
docs.text: Artificial beings created by the Hybrian Shadows as tools of infiltration and control. Homunculi were used to manufacture the Myth of Eris — posing as the mortal woman Eris and her followers to fabricate a religion that would centralize human kingdoms for easier manipulation.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
