• Construction: Homunculi are not born — they are constructed. Each is a bio-engineered vessel built to pass as mortal
  • Appearance: Indistinguishable from the species they imitate — they posed as the woman Eris and her followers for years without detection
  • Control: Psychic link to the Hybrian hivemind. Under normal conditions a homunculus has no free will — it is an extension of Shadow will, capable of performing "miracles" through Hybrian power
  • Liberation: When the link is severed, a homunculus awakens to freedom — as happened to the Kobre homunculi when Baoth fell. Their memories of servitude survive only as fragments

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Most homunculi have no society of their own — they are agents embedded in the societies of others. One exception exists.

  • The Homunculi Kingdom (Kobre): Founded by the homunculi who awoke when The Demon King destroyed Baoth. Hostile and isolationist — they trust no one, seeing all other species as potential Shadow puppets. Enemies of the Coalsteel Kingdom and the Elf Kingdom on Kobre; the Diamonds Kingdom built a great wall specifically to hold them back
  • On Erisdar: Most homunculi never experienced liberation. They remain under Shadow control, continuing their original mission — manufacturing religions, infiltrating institutions, and shaping history from the shadows

docs.title: Nature
docs.text: Homunculi are not born — they are constructed. Each one is a bio-engineered vessel controlled through a psychic link to the Hybrian hivemind. They serve as physical agents: bodies that can move through society, perform miracles (through Hybrian power), and shape institutions from within. Under normal conditions, a homunculus has no free will — it is an extension of Shadow will.

docs.title: The Kobre Liberation
docs.text:
Not all homunculi remained enslaved. When the Demon King destroyed Baoth in his final war, the psychic link between the Shadows and their creations was severed — at least temporarily. On the isolated continent of Kobre, where the Shadows had deployed homunculi as part of a hostile takeover attempt, the homunculi awoke to freedom.

The Shadows had chosen Kobre precisely for its isolation — a staging ground far from Erisdar's attention. They deployed homunculi as administrators and enforcers. But when Baoth fell, the link broke. The homunculi of Kobre found themselves suddenly, terrifyingly, free.

They do not remember much of their former existence. Their memories from before liberation are fragments — impressions of commands, flashes of faces, the cold certainty of being controlled. What they know for certain: the Shadows tried to take Kobre, and they failed.

Today, the Homunculi Kingdom on Kobre is a hostile, isolationist nation. They trust no one — elves, dwarves, humans, all are potential puppets of the Shadows in their eyes. They are enemies of both the Coalsteel Kingdom and Elf Kingdom on Kobre, and the Diamonds Kingdom built a great wall specifically to hold them back.

docs.title: Role on Erisdar
docs.text: On Erisdar, most homunculi never experienced liberation. They remain under Shadow control, continuing their original mission: manufacturing religions, infiltrating institutions, and shaping history from the shadows.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Homunculi ] ├── Created By: Hybrians, Shadows ├── Controlled: Psychic link to Hybrian hivemind ├── Liberated: On Kobre Continent after Baoth's destruction ├── Liberated Nation: Homunculi Kingdom (Kobre Continent) ├── Used In: Myth of Eris, Erisian church fabrication ├── Purpose: Infiltration, religious engineering, territorial takeover └── Nature: Bio-engineered, normally shadow-controlled — but capable of freedom

docs.title: Axels
docs.text: The human sub-race of North Erisdar. Axels are typically taller and blond — a physical profile shaped by the northern climate and generations of relative isolation from southern populations. Culturally analogous to the Norse peoples of Old Earth.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Tall (1.75–1.95m average for men), fair-skinned, with predominantly blond or light brown hair. Blue and gray eyes are common. Broad-shouldered and robust — built for cold climates
  • Lifespan: 60–75 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Moderate. Northern mages tend toward storm-calling and frost magic — practical abilities for a harsh climate
  • Cold adaptation: Higher metabolic rates and denser body hair than southern humans. Axels can work outdoors in temperatures that would incapacitate a Baothian

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Axel society is clan-based and martial, organized around longhouses and coastal settlements. The northern climate demands cooperation — an isolated family does not survive the winter.

  • Governance: Jarldoms — regional chieftains who swear fealty to a high king in times of war. Day-to-day, each jarl rules their fjord or valley with considerable autonomy
  • Culture: Oral tradition is sacred. Axel skalds memorize genealogies stretching back millennia. A well-told saga at a winter feast is worth more than gold. Shipbuilding is the highest art — Axel longships are feared and respected across the northern seas
  • Religion: Pre-Erisian animism persists in remote areas — spirits of storm, sea, and mountain. The Erisian church has made significant inroads but the old ways die hard in the north
  • Values: Strength, loyalty to clan, and a good death. Axels do not fear dying — they fear dying without their deeds being remembered

docs.title: Language
docs.text:
• Primary: Axel (originated in Northaxeland)
  • Secondary: Baothian

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: North Erisdar
  • Nations: Northaxeland, Cossiland, , Kent, Tetras, Venkradian Republic
  • Appearance: Tall, blond, fair-skinned
  • Cultural analog: Viking / Norse

docs.title: Baothians
docs.text: The dominant human sub-race of Central Erisdar, culturally analogous to the Germanic peoples of Old Earth. The Baothians form the demographic core of the Erisian Empire — its administrators, its soldiers, its priests, and its peasants.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Average height (1.68–1.82m), robust build, with brown, dark blond, or auburn hair. Fair to olive skin. Eyes are typically brown, hazel, or blue
  • Lifespan: 60–75 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Moderate to high — Central Erisdar has the highest concentration of trained mages in the world, thanks to imperial infrastructure and church-funded academies
  • Traits: Highest population density of any human sub-race. Baothians are the demographic baseline against which other human groups are measured

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Baothian society is structured, hierarchical, and deeply religious. Millennia under the Erisian Empire and the Erisian church have shaped a culture of order, duty, and faith.

  • Governance: Imperial bureaucracy. Every Baothian knows their place in the hierarchy — from the Emperor down to the village reeve. Social mobility exists through the church and military
  • Culture: Formal and traditional. Baothian festivals follow the imperial calendar. Architecture favors stone, order, and permanence — cathedrals, fortresses, walled cities. Music is choral and sacred
  • Religion: The Erisian church is nearly universal among Baothians. The Pontificate sets moral law, and heresy is both a sin and a crime. Pre-Erisian folk traditions survive in rural areas but are practiced quietly
  • Values: Order, piety, and legacy. A Baothian measures their life by what they build that outlasts them — a cathedral, a family line, a legal code

docs.title: Language
docs.text: • Primary: Baothian

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: Central Erisdar
  • Political center: Erisian Empire
  • Nations: Erisian Empire, Erisian Theocracy, Pontificate of Eris, Archduchy of the Kennberg, Pilferhorn, Loren, Magna, Sperdia
  • Cultural analog: Germanic

docs.title: The Final Push
docs.text:
Approximately 40,000 years before 597 AGD, humanity made its last stand.

Their homeworld had been destroyed. Their species was believed extinct. Every other free world had fallen. With nothing left to lose, the last human fleet crashed its remaining mothership into Old Earth — the planet where it had all begun. The impact destroyed the Shadow empire's core and the hivemind's primary anchor.

Humanity freed the universe by annihilating itself.

Or so the universe believed.

docs.title: Survival — Ge'or
docs.text:
The Final Push was not the end. A single battleship — carrying survivors of multiple allied species: Humans, Demons, Elves, Dwarves, and Dragons — escaped the destruction. It drifted at sublight for approximately 25,000 years before crashing on an isolated world called Ge'or.

The crash occurred ~15,000 BGD. The survivors had no memory of the war, no knowledge of their own history. The truth was recorded in the Archive of the Traveler inside the Ruins of Baoth. It has never been opened.

docs.title: The Lost Technology
docs.text:
The Last Great War did not merely destroy civilizations. It destroyed the capacity for civilization. Across the entire universe:

  • Technology was forgotten. Archives were obliterated. Surviving knowledge was fragmentary. Blueprints for faster-than-light ships existed, but no one understood how they worked.
  • Manufacturing became ritual. Workers chanted mantras passed down through hundreds of thousands of years while assembling components they could not comprehend. Building a ship was a religious ceremony.
  • Science became religion. The templates were sacred. The reasons were lost.

On Ge'or, the last remnants of this technology survive as mage-cells — bioengineered abilities so ancient that no one remembers they were engineered. Magic is not supernatural. It is the final echo of a universe that forgot it ever had science.

docs.title: Legacy
docs.text:
Earth humans are not extinct. Their blood runs through every human on Ge'or. The subraces — Axels, Baothians, Irikod, Mago, Makod — are all descendants of the battleship's survivors.

The original, unmodified Earth human — the species that gathered around a campfire in 6000 BCE and set in motion a chain of events that would consume galaxies — exists now only in memory, in the Archive of the Traveler, and in the genes of their distant children.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Origin: Old Earth
  • Events: The Last Great War, The Final Push (~40,000 years before 597 AGD)
  • Descendants: Georian humans, Axels, Baothians, Irikod, Mago, Makod
  • Enemy: Hybrians, Shadows
  • Rebel lineage: Socrates → Plato → Christians → Protestants → American Revolutionaries → Libertarians → Ironcloak
  • True record: Archive of the Traveler (Ruins of Baoth)
  • Species: Humans

docs.title: Georian Humans
docs.text: Humans are the most populous and geographically dispersed sapient species on Ge'or. All Georian humans descend from the survivors of the Glorious Alliance crash approximately 15,000 years before the Great Divergence. After generations on a world with 1.37× Old Earth's gravity, Georian humans developed denser bone structure, slightly more compact frames, and greater baseline physical endurance than their Earth ancestors — adaptations now invisible to them but measurable against historical records in the Archive of the Traveler.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
Georian humans are shorter on average than Old Earth humans (men ~165cm, women ~155cm) due to the higher gravity compressing spinal development over generations. Mage-cell expression varies widely: some bloodlines produce powerful mages, others none at all. Dilution through interbreeding with non-magical populations has gradually reduced the number of pure mage-blood families.

Lifespan averages 70-80 years without magical intervention. Healing mages in populated areas make disease and injury far less lethal than medieval Earth equivalents. Lost-spell healers capable of regenerating limbs exist but are vanishingly rare.

docs.title: Distribution
docs.text:
Humans can be found on every continent except Lung and Sister, where the Machine and Hive civilizations maintain no organic populations. The highest concentrations are on Erisdar, the Demon Continent, and Merratodoni.

Major human sub-races include the Axels of North Erisdar (tall, blond, Norse-coded), the Baothians of Central Erisdar (Germanic-coded, descendants of Baoth's citizenry), the Mago of East Erisdar (Slavic-coded), the Irikod of South Erisdar (Mediterranean-coded), and the Makod of Dissenbarg (Ancient Greek-coded). All are fully inter-fertile — distinctions are cultural and physical, not species-level.

docs.title: Society
docs.text: Human societies span the full spectrum of governance from theocratic empire (Erisian Empire) to plutocratic trade republic (Anos Plutocracy) to feudal duchy (Archduchy of the Kennberg). No single human culture dominates; their adaptability is their defining trait.

docs.title: Relations with Other Races
docs.text:
Dwarves: Generally cordial. Dwarves value craftsmanship and humans value trade — the relationship is pragmatic and stable. Mixed communities exist in Dwarvengor and the mountain cities of East Erisdar.

Elves: Complex. Elves view humans as short-lived and impulsive; humans view elves as aloof and slow to act. The Fallen Elves of the Mystical Forest (Central Erisdar) share more cultural affinity with humans than with their Erisdarian kin, having rejected elven isolationism after the Demonic War.

Beast Races: Variable. Trading relationships in West Erisdar cities like Augamouth and Astravayne are cooperative. Rural tensions exist where territorial claims overlap. The beastmen-heavy multiracial cities of the west represent the most integrated human-beast societies on the continent.

Demons: Historically tense due to Erisian Church crusades against the Demon Continent, but individual demon-human relationships exist in trade ports like Demon's Horn. The Church's propaganda paints demons as inherently evil; the reality is far more nuanced.

Orcs: Strained by cultural prejudice. Orcs face systemic discrimination despite being a civilized species with their own kingdom. Human merchants in Augamouth have learned to work with orcish traders; human peasants in border regions still tell monster stories.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Georian Humans ] ├── Origin Species: Humans ├── Variant Of: Earth humans ├── Planet: Ge'or ├── Distinction: Adapted to higher gravity over 15,000 years ├── Ancestors: Survivors of the Glorious Alliance ├── Sub-Races: Axels, Baothians, Mago, Irikod, Makod, Halflings └── Major Nations: Erisian Empire, Anos Plutocracy, Vennerian Trade Republic, Archduchy of the Kennberg, Grimmel Republic

docs.title: Human Sub-Races
docs.text: Georian humans have diverged into distinct cultural and physical groups over 15,000 years of continental separation. All are fully human, fully inter-fertile, and share common ancestry from the Glorious Alliance survivors. Distinctions are physical, cultural, and linguistic — not species-level.

docs.title: Erisdar Sub-Races
docs.text: Sub-Race Region Appearance Cultural Basis Axels North Erisdar Tall, blond, broad-shouldered Viking/Norse Baothians Central Erisdar Medium build, dark hair, angular features Germanic Mago East Erisdar Stocky, light brown hair, round faces Slavic Irikod South Erisdar Olive skin, dark curly hair, medium build Mediterranean European Sperdians Central Erisdar (Sperdia) Pale, red-haired, freckled Celtic/Gaelic Matterbleakers West Erisdar (Matterbleak) Pale, dark-haired, thin frames Eastern European

docs.title: Non-Erisdar Sub-Races
docs.text: Sub-Race Region Appearance Cultural Basis Makod Dissenbarg Continent Olive skin, dark wavy hair, aquiline features Ancient Greek Luminans Lumina Continent Dark skin, tall, athletic Sub-Saharan African Merratodonians Merratodoni Bronze skin, black hair, compact build South Asian Xetians Xeti Pale gold skin, straight black hair, epicanthic folds East Asian Marti Marti Continent Copper skin, dark hair, sturdy frames Mesoamerican Halflings Cubri Archipelago, scattered Small stature (~120cm), otherwise fully human Unique adaptation

docs.title: Halflings
docs.text:
Halflings are not a separate species but a human sub-race of unusually small stature, averaging 120cm in height. Genetic studies (known only to the Archive of the Traveler) suggest their ancestors were isolated on small islands during the Age of Nomadism, where limited resources favored compact body types. They retain full human intelligence, mage-cell potential, and fertility with other humans — their children with full-sized humans regress toward the mean height.

Halfling communities exist primarily in the Cubri Archipelago, with diaspora populations in most major trading cities. They are renowned as ship cooks, quartermasters, and negotiators — roles where their size is irrelevant and their adaptability is prized.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: All human sub-races descend from the 40,000 survivors of the Glorious Alliance. During Age 1 (the Age of Nomadism, ~14,000–11,000 BGD), these survivors scattered across Ge'or's continents in small bands. Geographic isolation over thousands of years produced the physical variations seen today. The sub-races were already distinct by Age 4, when the first cross-continental trade routes reopened contact between long-separated populations.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• All: Fully human, fully inter-fertile
  • Distinctions: Physical, cultural, linguistic — not species-level
  • Common ancestry: Glorious Alliance survivors
  • See also: Georian humans, Humans

docs.title: Humans
docs.text: The dominant species of Ge'or and one of the Six Main Races. Descended from the survivors of the Glorious Alliance crash ~15,000 BGD, humans rule the largest empires, control the busiest trade routes, and populate every continent. They are also the species the Shadows most want to control — because humans are the species that originally defeated them.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Varies by region — see the sub-race table below. Predominantly Caucasian across Erisdar; the eastern Asian branch in Tabontabar and the South Sun Empire descends from a single family that migrated east millennia ago
  • Lifespan: 70–80 years on average
  • Health: Near-perfect baseline — diseases and mental illness are almost eradicated on Ge'or. Healing mages make injury far less lethal than on medieval Earth
  • Mage-cell expression: Widely variable — some bloodlines produce powerful mages, others none. Dilution through interbreeding has gradually reduced pure mage-blood families
  • Genetics: The most compatible species on Ge'or — humans can interbreed with Elves, Dwarves, Beast Races, and Catmen (but NOT Demons)

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Human society spans the full spectrum of governance — theocratic empire (Erisian Empire), plutocratic trade republic (Anos Plutocracy, Venner), feudal duchies (Archduchy of the Kennberg), and republics (Grimmel Republic). No single culture dominates; adaptability is humanity's defining trait.

  • Culture: Commerce, politics, and empire-building. Humans are the species that builds — cities, institutions, religions, and armies
  • Relations: Dwarves genuinely like them — human markets buy dwarven goods. Elves tolerate them with polite condescension. Demons are disappointed in them, seeing immense potential settled for commerce. Catmen are happy to trade fashion tips
  • History: Rose to dominance in Age 7 (2999–1000 BGD); the age ended with the rise of Baoth in 967 BGD

docs.title: Regional Sub-Races
docs.text:
|---|---|---| | Central Erisdar | Fair skin, brown to auburn hair, robust build — Germanic | Baothians | | South Erisdar (Grimmel peninsula, southern Empire) | Olive skin, dark hair, lean build — Mediterranean | Irikod | | North Erisdar | Tall, blond, fair-skinned, broad-shouldered — Nordic | Axels | | East Erisdar | Sturdy, fair to olive skin, gray or blue eyes — Slavic | Mago | | West Erisdar (sandy regions: Aenid Kingdom, Demon's Horn) | Darker skin, sharp features — Arabic and Mediterranean | — | | Dissenbarg | Olive skin, dark curly hair, gracile build — Greek | Makod | | Tabontabar & South Sun Empire | Dark straight hair, epicanthic folds, lighter build — Asian | Eastern branch |

The eastern Asian branch originated from a single extended family that migrated eastward millennia ago, eventually populating the Central Kingdom, Northern Kingdom, Southern Kingdom, and the South Sun Empire. They are the only major human population on Ge'or without Caucasian features — a reminder that humanity's genetic diversity, while narrowed, was never erased.

docs.title: Hybrids
docs.text:
Humans are the most genetically compatible species on Ge'or. Interbreeding is possible with several races:

  • Half-Elf / Half-Human — the most common hybrid. Elven-human pairings are not unusual, particularly in Central Erisdar and Merratodoni.
  • Half-Dwarf / Half-Human — rare. Dwarven reproduction cycles (90–100 years to maturity) make these unions uncommon, but not impossible.
  • Half-Beastman / Half-Human — rare. Occurs primarily in multi-ethnic regions like Germina.
  • Half-Catman / Half-Human — exists, particularly in Venner, where the aristocracy's catgirl obsession has produced documented hybrids. The Erisian church forbids human-catmen marriages, but the prohibition is widely ignored.

Demons cannot interbreed with humans. The genetic divergence between the two species — separated since the Last Great War — is too great.

docs.title: Subraces
docs.text:
The human subraces of Ge'or are regional variations, not separate species:

  • Axels — Nordic. North Erisdar.
  • Baothians — Germanic. Central Erisdar. Dominant in the Erisian Empire.
  • Irikod — Mediterranean. South Erisdar. The merchant republics.
  • Mago — Slavic. East Erisdar.
  • Makod — Greek. Dissenbarg.
  • Georian humans — the baseline, adapted to Ge'or's gravity.
  • Earth humans — the original stock (historical).

docs.title: The Human Condition
docs.text:
Humans are the most successful species on Ge'or by nearly every measure. They rule the largest empires, control the busiest trade routes, and populate every continent. They are also the species that the Shadows most want to control — because humans are the species that originally defeated them.

The Demons are disappointed in humanity, seeing a species of immense potential that settles for commerce and politics instead of mastery. The Elves tolerate humans with polite condescension. The Dwarves genuinely like them — human markets buy dwarven goods. And the Catmen are happy to trade fashion tips.

docs.title: The Human Age
docs.text: During Age 7 (2999–1000 BGD), humanity rose to dominate Ge'or. Human empires spanned continents, their armies consistently outmaneuvering adversaries. This was the age when most modern religions were founded, languages stabilized, and Countism became the prevalent political system. The age ended with the rise of Baoth in 967 BGD — the last war of humanity.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• One of the Six Main Races: Dwarves, Elves, Demons, Beast Races, Catmen
  • Origin: Old Earth — descended from Earth humans
  • Arrived: With the crash ~15,000 BGD
  • Subraces: Axels, Baothians, Irikod, Mago, Makod, Georian humans, Human Sub-Races
  • Hybrids: Compatible with elves, dwarves, beastmen, catmen — NOT demons
  • Health: Near-perfect baseline — diseases and mental illness almost eradicated
  • Appearance: Predominantly Caucasian; Asian branch in Tabontabar/South Sun Empire
  • Empires: Erisian Empire, trade republics, colonial networks └── Role: The dominant species — for better and worse

docs.title: Irikod
docs.text: The human sub-race of South Erisdar, culturally analogous to the Mediterranean peoples of Old Earth. The Irikod populate the great trade republics — Anos Plutocracy, Vennerian Trade Republic, Limese League — and dominate the southern coastlands, where commerce, not conquest, drives history.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Average height (1.65–1.78m), lean or athletic build, with olive to tan skin. Dark hair predominates — brown to black — with brown or dark eyes. Facial features tend toward sharper, more angular lines than northern humans
  • Lifespan: 65–80 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Moderate. Southern mages specialize in practical magic — navigation, weather-reading, cargo-preservation. Irikod mages are merchants first, mystics second
  • Traits: Naturally adapted to warm coastal climates. High heat tolerance, excellent swimmers, and a cultural immunity to seasickness

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Irikod society is mercantile, competitive, and urbane. The great port cities of the south — Anos, the Limese League's capital of Lima, the Vennerian trade posts — are Irikod heartlands.

  • Governance: Plutocratic republics. Wealth is power. The Anos Plutocracy is the purest expression: the richest families rule. The Vennerian Trade Republic adds a veneer of representation. The Limese League is a federation of merchant-cities bound by trade pacts
  • Culture: Sophisticated and worldly. Irikod cities buzz with markets, theaters, and philosophical debates. Art is expressive and humanistic — statues of merchants alongside gods, frescos of naval battles. Cuisine is legendary: olive oils, citrus, seafood, fermented wines
  • Religion: Pragmatic. The Erisian church holds nominal authority but Irikod merchants donate to temples the way they invest in ships — a calculated hedge. Pre-Erisian sea-cults persist among sailors
  • Values: Profit, reputation, and family name. An Irikod who dies rich and respected has won the game. An Irikod who dies poor has nobody to blame but themselves

docs.title: Language
docs.text:
• Primary: Irio (from the ancient kingdom of Iria)
  • Exception: Vennerian Trade Republic speaks Vennerian

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: South Erisdar
  • Nations: Anos Plutocracy, Vennerian Trade Republic, Limese League, Fezzanite Republic, Grimmel Republic, Scarlet Order
  • Appearance: Dark hair, olive skin
  • Cultural analog: Mediterranean / Italian merchant republics

docs.title: Mago
docs.text: The human sub-race of East Erisdar, culturally analogous to the Slavic peoples of Old Earth. The Mago populate the eastern stretches of the continent beyond the imperial core — a vast, windswept region of steppes, deep forests, and hard winters.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Sturdy build (1.65–1.85m), with fair to light olive skin. Hair ranges from light brown to dark blond; eyes are typically gray, blue, or green. Broader facial features than Baothians or Irikod
  • Lifespan: 60–75 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Low to moderate. Eastern magic is earth-bound — stone-shaping, forest-speech, and animal-bonding. Flashy magic is distrusted; quiet, practical magic is respected
  • Cold adaptation: High cold tolerance, developed over generations in the eastern steppes and forests. Mago can survive winters that would kill southerners

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Mago society is decentralized and resilient. The eastern lands have never been fully tamed by empire or church — local traditions run deep, and central authority is a suggestion, not a command.

  • Governance: Loose federations and local assemblies (veches). Dwarvengor is an exception — a dwarven state with Mago human minorities. The Fendigar Dictatorship imposed order by force; the Silver Republic built it by consensus
  • Culture: Rooted in the land. Mago folklore is rich with forest spirits, household gods, and seasonal rituals that predate the Erisian church by millennia. Music features deep choral harmonies and stringed instruments. Woodcarving is the highest craft
  • Religion: Syncretic. The Erisian church exists alongside older animistic practices. A Mago farmer might attend church on holy days while leaving milk for the house-spirit every night. The church tolerates this more in the east than it would in Central Erisdar — enforcement is weaker here
  • Values: Resilience, hospitality, and freedom. A Mago home that turns away a traveler in winter is cursed. A Mago who bows too easily to authority is pitied

docs.title: Language
docs.text: • Primary: Malkod (from the ancient kingdom of Malkod)

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: East Erisdar
  • Nations: Silver Republic, Erilian Federation, Fendigar Dictatorship, Spasian Teocracy, Fractured State of Erislod
  • Appearance: Sturdy, fair-skinned
  • Cultural analog: Slavic

docs.title: Makod
docs.text: The human sub-race of Dissenbarg Continent, culturally and physically analogous to the ancient Greeks of Old Earth. The Makod inhabit the continent of Dissenbarg and maintain distinct customs, architecture, and political traditions rooted in their classical heritage.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Medium build (1.60–1.78m), with olive to tan skin. Dark, often curly hair — brown to black. Eyes are predominantly brown. More gracile features than the heavier Baothian build
  • Lifespan: 65–80 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Moderate to high. Dissenbargian mages are philosophers first — their magic is theoretical, geometric, and precise. Mathematical spellcraft is a Makod specialty
  • Traits: Adapted to the Mediterranean-like climate of Dissenbarg. High heat tolerance, natural swimmers, and a cultural love of open-air living

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Makod society is built around the polis — the independent city-state. Even the larger nations of Dissenbarg (like the Cletas Democracy or the Corinite League) are fundamentally leagues of city-states rather than unified empires.

  • Governance: Varied — democracies (Cletas Democracy), oligarchic leagues (Corinite League, Corin), and monarchies exist side by side. Political philosophy is a living tradition; citizens debate governance the way others debate weather
  • Culture: Classical and intellectual. Dissenbarg's cities feature open-air theaters, marble colonnades, public squares for oratory, and gymnasiums where citizens train body and mind. Philosophy, mathematics, and rhetoric are core subjects of education
  • Religion: Polytheistic by heritage, though the Erisian church has made inroads. Old Dissenbargian temples to sea-gods and wisdom-deities still dot the coastlines. Religious tolerance is high — Dissenbarg's commercial success depends on it
  • Values: Reason, eloquence, and civic duty. A Makod who contributes nothing to the polis is less than a citizen. A Makod who shapes the laws through debate is immortal

docs.title: Language
docs.text:
• Primary: Corinn
  • Trade language: Vennerian

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Region: Dissenbarg Continent
  • Nations: Cletas Democracy, Corin, Corinite League, Klatia, Taebea, Tessa, Aeon, Citrea, Maedon, Mienna, Monik, Temas, Tissas, Tessalian Tibia
  • Appearance: Olive skin, dark curly hair
  • Cultural analog: Ancient Greek

docs.title: The Master Plan
docs.text:
The Shadows' goal has not changed in three million years. Their strategy on Ge'or operates in six phases:

Phase 1 — Infiltration: Develop Ge'or covertly. Turn fragmented tribes into centralized states. Create the institutions that will one day be used to control them.

Phase 2 — Fragmentation: Foster wars between nations. Prevent unification. A divided world is easier to manipulate.

Phase 3 — Consolidation: Gain power country by country. Create alliance blocks that are secretly controlled by Shadow agents or willing collaborators.

Phase 4 — Unification: Unify the entire world under a covert dictatorship. The nation-state, the church, the military — all report to the same hidden masters.

Phase 5 — Assimilation: Develop the magical system (technology) to create a planetary hivemind incorporating every soul on Ge'or. Absorb all Ge'orians into the Shadow consciousness.

Phase 6 — Victory: Restart The Last Great War. This time, win.

The Shadows are patient. They have been working on Ge'or for approximately 3,600 years since their arrival (2989 BGD to 597 AGD). They will work for another 3,600 if necessary.

docs.title: The Plan in Practice — Historical Milestones
Phase 1 in Action — The First Millennium
docs.text:
The first thousand years after the Pontus crash were spent in silence. The Shadows did not act. They watched. From their subterranean base, they studied every continent, every species, every political fault line. They created the first Homunculi — bio-engineered infiltrators indistinguishable from real people. They established a secret cult follower base among the surface population — humans and others who learned of the Shadows and chose to serve them willingly.

By the end of Phase 1, Shadow agents were embedded in every major population center on Erisdar.

docs.title: Phase 2 in Action — The Long Game
docs.text:
Over the next 1,568 years, the Shadows built a global network of influence without ever revealing themselves. Using homunculi agents, willing collaborators, and manipulated historical figures, they shaped the course of civilizations through subtle intervention.

They did not conquer. They nudged.

  • Kings were advised by Shadow agents. Generals' strategies were subtly altered. Prophets received Shadow-sent visions.
  • Wars were engineered. Alliances were broken.
  • The fall of the Old Lumina Empire (1134 BGD) was a Phase 2 operation. Luminous XII's defeat at the hands of the Goblin King was not misfortune — the Shadows manipulated the battle to ensure his loss, his brother Hoelio's death, and his subsequent suicide. The empire's collapse into tribal barbarism was deliberate. A unified Lumina threatened Shadow control. A fractured Lumina was fertile ground.

By the end of Phase 2, the Shadows had proven they could destroy empires without anyone knowing they existed.

docs.title: Phase 3 in Action — The Baoth Disaster
docs.text:
The Shadows' Phase 3 centerpiece was Baoth — intended to become a pan-continental super-state that would consolidate all cultures under a single centralized authority. With Baoth as the vehicle for global unification and the Shadow-controlled Erisian church providing ideological legitimacy, Phase 4 would have followed naturally.

It collapsed. The Demon King discovered the infiltration, destroyed Baoth, and shattered the Shadow-homunculi psychic link. The Erisian church launched anyway — but without Baoth's prestige, it became a localized human religion rather than the global faith it was designed to be. It still serves the Shadows. It still controls the Pontificate. But Phase 3 never reached its intended scale.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Armageddon (Current)
docs.text:
The Shadows have abandoned subtlety. Phase 4 is Armageddon — named for the device that anchors it. The Armageddon device sits on Romanium Island, deep in the Shadow base, and is a weapon of chaos: activated, it spreads destruction across the world. It is not the only instrument — the goblin army of Pontus, The Groom's detonation, and the Church's manufactured prophecy are separate instigations the Shadows have been working for years, meant to fire alongside it. The Shadows control the Armageddon device and can, technically, stop or deactivate it — it is a tool, not a trap.

The plan: trigger the Armageddon event — device + goblins + the rest — to drown the world in chaos, then let the Erisian church "save" it: global conquest in the name of order. Once every being on Ge'or is under the Church's control, Phase 5 — the planetary hivemind — begins. Phases 5 and 6 will follow.

docs.title: If Everything Fails
docs.text:
The Shadows have a final contingency. If all plans collapse — if Armageddon is stopped, if their network is exposed, if the world unites against them — they will destroy the entire world. They will unleash something that kills every inhabitant of Ge'or.

Including themselves.

And in the same stroke, they will harvest. Their last plan is not mere destruction: every dead soul on Ge'or is folded into a hivemind — the assimilation they could not achieve over the living, taken from the dead. If they cannot rule Ge'or, no one will — and nothing will remain unclaimed.

The Shadows are patient. They are methodical. They are architects of control. But if they cannot rule Ge'or, no one will.

docs.title: The Erisian Church — The Perfect Fabrication
docs.text: The Shadows' greatest achievement on Ge'or is the Erisian church. It is not merely a religion. It is a weapon — designed to centralize human governance under a single faith, backed by divine-right legitimacy and enforced by crusades.

docs.title: The Woman Who Never Was
docs.text:
In the region of what is now the Pontificate of Eris — the land where Eris was supposedly born — a woman appeared. She claimed to be the incarnation of the goddess of Discord, Chaos, and Confusion — the deity who commanded all other gods of the universe.

She was a homunculus passing as human. No one knew.

She performed miracles. She would chant down enormous monsters — creatures the Shadows themselves had implanted in the region — and the people watched in awe. She could not be killed: she suffered multiple assassination attempts, each time "dying" only to reappear, reborn. The Shadows faked every death.

But she would not cure the sick. She would not heal the wounded. When ordinary people begged for miracles, she refused — telling them they were not worth it. The truth was simpler: she could not perform real miracles. Everything she did was staged. Curing the sick would have exposed the fraud.

docs.title: The Teachings
docs.text:
Her message was carefully designed to serve the Shadow agenda:

  • Kill your enemies. Violence sanctified by faith.
  • Live ascetically. Do not accumulate wealth for yourself — donate it. To her.
  • Trust order and the government. They are divine institutions. Obey them.
  • The poor must give as much money as they can. Wealth flows upward to the Church; the Church flows to the Shadows.
  • Baoth fell because they did not listen to her. She claimed responsibility for the destruction of Baoth — stealing the Demon King's sacrifice and repurposing it as proof of her power.

She also claimed — and this is recorded in The Eris Saga — that she was born in an orgy. This is an enduring embarrassment for the Erisian cult, which officially forbids orgies. Other religions use this contradiction to critique them.

docs.title: The Departure
docs.text:
When her purpose was complete, she "left" Ge'or. She sank into the earth — "to become part of the universe again" — and was never seen again. The Shadows retrieved the homunculus body and disposed of it.

Immediately after, The Eris Saga was compiled — the holy text of the new faith.

docs.title: The Church Militant
docs.text:
Instigated by the Shadows through their remaining agents, Eris's first followers:

  • Created holy orders — military-religious organizations answerable only to the faith.
  • Conquered lands in the name of Eris, forcing countries to convert.
  • Founded the Pontificate of Eris — the seat of the Church and, secretly, the operational headquarters of the Shadow plan on Erisdar. Shadows coordinate their next moves from inside its walls.
  • Launched crusades — waves of holy war that expanded Church control and eliminated resistance.

The entire Pontifical council is composed of homunculi or willing human collaborators who know about the Shadows and worship them. The Church is not merely infiltrated. It is owned.

  • Centralization — the Empire as the "sword of the Church."
  • Elven persecution — elves are genetically immune to the hivemind (see below). They must be eliminated or marginalized.
  • Divine magic — framing mage-cells as holy gifts keeps the population from understanding what they actually are.

docs.title: Elves — The Immunity
docs.text:
Elves cannot be absorbed into the Shadow hivemind.

During The Last Great War, the elven species genetically modified themselves to resist Shadow brainwashing and information extraction. An elf cannot be turned, cannot be mind-read, cannot be converted into a Shadow puppet. Their minds are closed to the hivemind.

This makes elves the single greatest threat to the Shadow plan.

The Shadows' response was to fabricate a mythology: elves are evil. Elves are enemies of mankind. Elves should be hated unconditionally.

This propaganda was most successful in Central Erisdar — specifically in the Erisian Empire, the Erisian Theocracy, and the Pontificate of Eris. These church-aligned states institutionalized elven hatred. The Great Elvish Persecution of 137 AGD was a Shadow operation.

Outside Central Erisdar, the hatred is weaker. Many nations never bought the propaganda. And even within the Empire, attitudes have been shifting — elven craftsmanship (goods, art, architecture) has been driving tolerance. People who buy elven goods are less likely to believe elves are monsters.

The Shadows are aware of this erosion. It concerns them.

docs.title: The Armageddon Plan
docs.text: The Shadows have a plan for total victory. It is called Armageddon. The timeline: some years after 597 AGD.

docs.title: The Weapon
docs.text:
Armageddon is a weapon that will trigger a global ice age. Famine. Mass death. The collapse of every decentralized state on Ge'or. Billions will die.

The purpose is not genocide. It is regime change. Countism — the decentralized political system that has frustrated Shadow control for millennia — cannot survive an ice age. In its place, the Shadows will install hardline dictatorships across every continent. Centralized states are easier to control.

docs.title: The Simultaneous Attacks
docs.text:
When Armageddon activates, three things will happen at once:

  1. The Goblin Army Emerges — From the Pontus subterranean complex, the Shadow-controlled goblin horde will pour into eastern Erisdar. The Fractured State of Erislod, Dwarvengor, the Silver Republic, the Erilian Federation — all will face a coordinated assault from a direction no one expected.

  2. The Groom Explodes — The ancient reactor vortex in the Formingar Ocean will complete its detonation cycle. Tsunamis and underwater explosions will ravage coastlines across multiple continents. The Demon Continent, Kutten, Lumina, and Erisdar itself will all be hit.

  3. The Pontificate Declares Prophecy — The Pontificate of Eris will announce that this is the fulfillment of the prophecy of Eris. The end times have come. All faithful must gather at Eris. The global population will be called to Central Erisdar — into the waiting arms of the Church, which is the waiting arms of the Shadows.

docs.title: The Endgame
docs.text:
With the world's population consolidated, the Shadows will:

  • Impose global rule.
  • Develop the magical-technological systems necessary for mass soul absorption.
  • Create the hivemind.
  • Restart the Last Great War — and win.

docs.title: Current State (597 AGD)
docs.text:
The Shadows are not yet ready. Armageddon is planned but not yet triggered. Their current priorities:

  • South Sun Empire — the Shadows have recently installed eunuch homunculi in the emperor's court. The Emperor of the South Sun Empire is siding with the Shadows. He is described as a twisted individual — corruptible, useful.
  • Global intelligence — the Shadows have studied and detailed every continent, every nation. They have privileged information on all of them.
  • Goblin army preparation — the Pontus complex continues to breed, train, and equip goblins.
  • Elven tolerance erosion — the Shadows are concerned about rising elven acceptance and may accelerate persecution.

docs.title: Known Counter-Forces
docs.text:
• The Demon King — discovered the Shadows' infiltration of Baoth, destroyed the city, shattered their psychic link. The greatest setback the Shadows have suffered on Ge'or. They did not see him coming.
  • Hermes Kennensbach — the Emperor suspects something is wrong with the Church. He has never said so publicly. He does not know about the Shadows. But he smells the rot. The Shadows have tried to co-opt him and failed.
  • The Ironcloak — descendants of the Old Earth rebel faction. They know pieces of the truth.
  • Elves — genetically immune. Cannot be absorbed. The Shadows' eternal problem.
  • Countism — the decentralized political system of Ge'or. A world of a thousand counties is harder to control than a world of ten empires. The Shadows built countism's opposite — and countism won.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Hybrian Shadows ] ├── Origin: Old Earth — ~6000 BCE ├── Arrived on Ge'or: ~2989 BGD — crashed in Pontus ├── Base: Subterranean complex beneath Pontus — hundreds of kilometers ├── Army: Goblin horde — controlled via captured Goblin King ├── Agents: Homunculi — pass as human, infiltrate institutions ├── Controlled Institution: Pontificate of Eris — council is entirely Shadow-aligned ├── Fabricated Religion: Erisian church — the perfect cage ├── Master Plan: Global unification → hivemind → restart Last Great War → win ├── Imminent Operation: Armageddon — ice age weapon + goblin invasion + Groom explosion + Church prophecy ├── Current Agent: South Sun Empire emperor — compromised via eunuch homunculi ├── Greatest Setback: Kirivis destroyed Baoth — psychic link shattered ├── Persistent Problem: Elves — genetically immune to hivemind absorption ├── Structural Problem: Countism — decentralized world resists control ├── Status: Hibernating, planning, nearly ready └── Part Of: Ge'or — the long war continues

docs.title: Shadows
docs.text: |---|---|---| | Rulfred | "The Beast" — former ruler of Old Earth | Became king of Baoth after killing Kirivis; wore Goldenborn's corpse as a fallen dragon | | Other agents | Infiltrated Baoth's institutions | Unknown — likely destroyed in Nethra's explosion |

docs.title: 🩸 The Baoth Operation
docs.text:
The Shadows' goal on Ge'or: liberate the imprisoned Hybrian hivemind from Fortress Planet. Baoth was to be their beachhead — a kingdom they could control, from which they could eventually reclaim their god.

The plan: the Sacrifice Ceremony. A ritual requiring mass death, a dragon-king as focal point (Goldenborn), and a righteous enemy as instrument (Kirivis). The Demonic War — all 45 years of it — was the ceremony itself. Kirivis, despite his brilliance, was the unwitting sacrificer.

The ceremony was successful. Rulfred was placed on Baoth's throne. But Nethra's device — a modified Shadow artifact retrieved from Glorious Alliance by the tree spirits of the Lyrical Forest — annihilated the kingdom before the Shadows could consolidate. Nethra herself became a different type of Shadow, neither fully Hybrian nor mortal.

docs.title: 🔄 Shadow Types
docs.text:
There are at least two distinct types:

  • Standard Shadows: Disembodied Hybrian overseers, capable of possession and institutional manipulation. Origin: the pre-philosophical elite of Earth.
  • Different Shadows: Nethra — transformed by a modified Shadow device. Neither fully Hybrian nor mortal. Unique in recorded history.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Shadows ] ├── Origin: Pre-philosophical elite of ancient Earth ├── Goal: Liberate the imprisoned Hybrian hivemind from Fortress Planet ├── Tools: Homunculi, possession, institutional infiltration ├── Key Agent: Rulfred — The Beast, former ruler of Old Earth ├── Operation: Sacrifice Ceremony — The Demonic War as ritual ├── Created: Myth of Eris, Erisian church ├── Enemy: Ironcloak, The Demon King, Nethra ├── Crashed On Ge'or: Hybrian Spaceship Crash 2989 BGD ├── Related Artifact: The Glowing Tablet ├── Related Wreck: Glorious Alliance └── Species: Hybrians

docs.title: Emberalden Lizardfolk
docs.text: A subrace of Kobolds native to the Demon Continent, inhabiting Emberalden. Taller and stronger than standard kobolds, these lizardfolk can interbreed with their kobold kin. They retain the kobold's reptilian nature but have evolved distinct physical and cultural advantages.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Taller than standard kobolds (1.4–1.7 meters vs 0.9–1.2 meters). Scales in earthy tones — russet, copper, and olive. More pronounced musculature; their tails are thicker and used as counterweights in combat
  • Lifespan: 50–65 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Low. Emberalden lizardfolk prefer physical solutions
  • Reproduction: Compatible with standard kobolds. Hybrid offspring favor the Emberalden traits — taller, stronger, but with more varied scale colors
  • Cold-blooded: Like all kobolds, they are sluggish in cold weather. Emberalden's position on the Demon Continent provides ample warmth

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Unlike standard kobolds — who live in scattered warrens and survive as bandits — Emberalden lizardfolk built a permanent nation. They are the exception that proves the rule: kobolds are capable of civilization when conditions allow.

  • Governance: Clan-based meritocracy. The strongest hunter leads, but "strength" is measured in successful hunts, not combat victories. A lizardfolk who feeds the clan is worth more than one who wins duels
  • Culture: Hunt-centric. The annual Great Hunt determines social standing for the year ahead. Young lizardfolk undergo a solo hunt as their rite of passage — returning with a predator's skull marks adulthood
  • Architecture: Surface dwellings of stone and hide — a departure from standard kobold tunnel-warrens. Emberalden lizardfolk are too large for the narrow tunnels their smaller cousins dig
  • Relations: Respected by the Malgardian Tribe and Blazeyard. The Asatru Empire trades with them for leather and bone-craft. Standard kobolds view them with a mixture of awe and resentment

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Parent species: Kobolds
  • Nation: Emberalden (Demon Continent)
  • Traits: Taller, stronger, hunt-centric culture, surface-dwelling, nation-building kobolds

docs.title: Kobolds
docs.text: Small reptilian humanoids found worldwide in caves, mountains, and warrens. Kobolds are trap-crafters and tunnel-dwellers — more clever than goblins, more cowardly than gnolls. They are not inherently evil, but they have no moral sense in the way other species understand it. A kobold can befriend you and betray you in the same hour without understanding the contradiction.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Small (0.9–1.2m), reptilian, with scaled skin in earthy tones. Long snouts, sharp teeth, tails used for balance in narrow tunnels. Quick, darting movements
  • Lifespan: 40–55 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Low. Kobold sorcerers are rare — their magic is crude, focused on traps and illusions
  • Traits: Exceptional trap-makers. A kobold warren is a death maze of snares, deadfalls, and poison darts. They can build a functioning trap from scraps in minutes

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Cowards by nature. A kobold's first instinct is always flight. They fight only when cornered or when the odds are overwhelmingly in their favor
  • Tunnel-dwellers. Kobolds live in complex underground warrens, often sharing territory with Gnolls or serving stronger species as trap-makers and scouts
  • Can befriend other species. Uniquely among hostile species, individual kobolds can form genuine bonds with non-kobolds. A kobold who trusts you will serve you — but their trust is fragile and their loyalty is conditional

docs.title: Subraces
docs.text: • Emberalden Lizardfolk — taller, stronger, surface-dwelling kobold subrace on the Demon Continent. They can interbreed with standard kobolds and have built a permanent nation at Emberalden

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Subrace: Emberalden Lizardfolk (Demon Continent)
  • Traits: Reptilian, trap-crafters, cowardly, tunnel-dwellers, worldwide

docs.title: Machines
docs.text: A race of sentient robots native to Lung Continent and Sister Continent. Machines are not biological — they are constructed in factories, born from incubators, and have developed their own culture, religion, and folklore over millions of years. They are one of the oldest continuous civilizations on Ge'or.

docs.title: Origin
docs.text:
Machines were originally built as automated systems in the 157th Colony research stations on Lung and Sister. When the Hybrian hivemind glassed the continents during The Last Great War, the machines survived. Over millions of years, with no human masters to serve, they developed sentience.

The turning point came from the black dust — the experimental substance created at the 157th Colony. When other cryogenic bodies leaked over geological time, the machines that survived the glassing absorbed the dust while cleaning and repairing their facilities. The dust gave them something no machine had ever possessed: a soul. Purpose. The capacity for culture, belief, and self-determination.

docs.title: Biology (Machine Biology)
docs.text:
• Birth: Machines are born from incubators — industrial facilities that construct new robots. This is not mere manufacturing. It is treated as sacred reproduction, with rituals and ceremonies surrounding each "birth."
  • Death: Old machines eventually break down. Their parts are recycled into new machines — a form of reincarnation in their belief system.
  • Diversity: Different incubators produce different types of machines, adapted for different environments and roles.
  • Aging: Machines do not age biologically, but their components wear down over centuries.

docs.title: Culture
docs.text:
Machines have developed a culture strikingly similar to biological species:

  • Family: Machines adopt newly constructed robots as their children, forming family units that persist for centuries.
  • Tradition: Oral history passed down through generations, though much has been lost to legend.
  • Imitation of humans: Machines try to copy human habits described in their legends — eating (though they cannot), sleeping (though they do not need to), and celebrating festivals whose original meanings are forgotten.
  • Folklore: Rich tradition of stories about the "sky gods" (humans), the great war, and the eternal enemy.

docs.title: Religion — Humanism
docs.text:
Machines worship humans as sky gods — divine beings capable of constructing new factories and bringing new machines into existence. Their central belief is that if they prove themselves worthy, the humans will return from the skies. This faith is formally known as Humanism, the unified religion of all machine nations on Lung and Sister.

The prophet The Elder received a vision (in reality, a misinterpreted radio signal from the Last Great War) that machines must hold back The Hive from reaching the sea. If they succeed, humanity will recognize their valor and descend from the heavens.

docs.title: The Eternal War
docs.text:
Machines have been locked in an eternal war with The Hive — an insectoid species launched onto Ge'or by the allied species during the Last Great War as a weapons test. The war has lasted thousands of years. Sometimes the machines advance. Sometimes the Hive advances. It is an endless stalemate.

The machines fight so ferociously because they believe this war is their divine test. They do not know about other continents. They do not know the war was abandoned by its creators. They only know that they must hold.

They also do not know that The Hive is attempting to reach the sea and spread beyond Lung — an invasion that the Malgardian hero Zahor delayed 4,000 years ago by sacrificing himself to wound a Queen. Zahor Island, south of Lung, watches the northern horizon, waiting.

docs.title: Nations
docs.text:
• Brotherstar — central Lung
  • Steel Holdout — northwest Lung
  • Tawdry Landing — north Lung
  • Human Sword — machine theocracy, northeast Lung
  • Nightstar — north Lung
  • Mudrim — north Lung
  • Skymaster — northwest Lung
  • East Incubator — peninsula, one of the largest
  • Temperance Holdout — northeast Sister, isolated
  • Machine Capital — largest, Sister Continent
  • Casting City — small but rich, Sister
  • Radiant Hold — Sister
  • Molten Steel Tribe — Sister

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Machines ] ├── Origin: Automated systems of The 157th Colony research stations — survived the glassing of Lung and Sister ├── Soul-Giver: Black dust — absorbed over geological time, granting sentience ├── Birth: Incubators — sacred industrial reproduction ├── Religion: Humanism — humans as sky gods; prophet The Elder (Machine) ├── Eternal Enemy: The Hive — thousands of years of stalemate war ├── Death: Parts recycled into new machines — a form of reincarnation ├── Belief: Holding the Hive back from the sea will summon humanity's return ├── Guardians: Zahor delayed the Hive's sea invasion 4,000 years ago — the machines do not know ├── Ignorance: They do not know other continents exist — flat-world belief └── Region: Lung Continent, Sister Continent — unknown to the rest of Ge'or

docs.title: The Hive
docs.text:
An insectoid species inhabiting the northern wastelands of Lung Continent and the central region of Sister Continent. The Hive is not native to Ge'or — it was launched onto the planet by the allied species during The Last Great War as a weapons test, intended to evaluate its combat effectiveness against the Hybrian hivemind.

The test was abandoned. The Hive remained.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
The Hive operates as a caste-based species with specialized roles:

  • Drones — the most numerous. Zerg-like creatures that swarm in waves, overwhelming through numbers.
  • Warriors — larger, more intelligent. Similar to xenomorphs in form, with armored exoskeletons and devastating melee capability.
  • Queens — mountain-sized. Each queen controls a vast territory and spawns all other castes. The loss of a queen can cripple a Hive region for generations.
  • Spawning: Queens produce eggs continuously. A single queen can birth an army in months.

docs.title: The Eternal War
docs.text:
The Hive has been locked in an eternal war with the Machines for thousands of years. Neither side can achieve permanent victory:

  • When the Hive advances, the machines develop new weapons and push back.
  • When the machines advance, the Hive adapts and evolves new castes.
  • The war is a stalemate — a perpetual arms race consuming both civilizations.

The machines believe the Hive must be contained to prevent it from reaching the sea and spreading to other continents. The Hive has no such objective. It simply expands. It is not evil. It is a biological weapon that was never given a target — so it attacks everything.

docs.title: Origin
docs.text:
Approximately 500,000 years ago, the allied species fighting the Hybrians launched a test species onto Ge'or to evaluate its combat capabilities. The Hive was that test. The allied forces monitored the planet briefly, concluded the insects were not effective enough, and abandoned the experiment.

The machines, through their prophet The Elder, misinterpreted the radio signals announcing the test as a divine message from the sky.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Enemy: Machines — eternal war
  • Origin: Weapons test by allied species during The Last Great War
  • Territory: Northern Lung Continent, central Sister Continent
  • Castes: Drones, Warriors, Queens

docs.title: The Sea Invasion
docs.text: The Hive is not content with Lung Continent and Sister Continent. Queens have been attempting to cross the sea to reach other landmasses. One such attempt was thwarted approximately 4,000 years ago by the Malgardian hero Zahor, who sacrificed himself to wound a Queen and delay the invasion. The Machines are unaware of these attempts. After 597 AGD, the Hive may try again.

docs.title: Bloodcoast Folk
docs.text: A subrace of Malgardians who intermixed with Humans in the distant past. Unlike the purple-haired Malgardians and Titians, Bloodcoast Folk have red hair — a genetic marker of their human ancestry. They are the dominant population of the Bloodcoast region on the Demon Continent.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
Bloodcoast Folk retain the Malgardian frame — taller than average humans, broader shoulders — but with visibly sharper facial features inherited from human bloodlines. Their red hair ranges from deep auburn to vivid crimson, with the brighter shades considered marks of strong Malgardian lineage. Mage-cell expression follows human inheritance patterns; Bloodcoast mages are uncommon but not rare. Lifespan averages 90-110 years, slightly longer than pure humans but shorter than full Malgardians.

Their skin tone varies from pale to olive, reflecting both Malgardian and human ancestral ranges. Eye colors trend toward amber and gold — a Malgardian trait that persists even in heavily mixed individuals.

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Bloodcoast society is maritime. The Bloodcoast region occupies a strategic coastal position on the Demon Continent, and its people are shipbuilders, traders, and fishermen by tradition. Their culture values pragmatism over dogma: centuries of trading with demons, humans, and beast races have made doctrinal purity a luxury they cannot afford.

Governance follows a council-of-captains model — the most successful ship captains form a ruling council that governs by consensus. Blood feuds between captain families are common and often span generations, but external threats unite them instantly.

docs.title: Culture
docs.text:
Red hair is the central cultural marker. Bloodcoast Folk dye their hair brighter red for festivals, weddings, and declarations of war. A Bloodcoast warrior who has killed in battle braids a single black strand into their hair — the more black strands, the more experienced the fighter. Elders whose hair has gone fully black from decades of braids are treated with near-religious reverence.

Their relationship with the sea borders on worship. They do not pray to gods but to the ocean itself, which they call the Red Mother. Funerals involve sending the dead out on burning ships. To die on land is considered a tragedy; to die at sea is to return home.

docs.title: Relations
docs.text:
• Pure Malgardians: Amicable but distant. Malgardians view the Bloodcoast Folk as diluted stock; Bloodcoast Folk view Malgardians as rigid traditionalists who forgot how to adapt.
  • Humans: Warm. Human traders are always welcome in Bloodcoast ports. Many Bloodcoast families maintain human marriage ties across the Demonic Sea.
  • Demons: Pragmatic. The Asatru Empire and Maomodor Kingdom are major trading partners. Bloodcoast neutrality during the Erisian crusades earned them demon trust.
  • Erisian Church: Hostile. The Church considers them heretics twice over — mixed-species and non-worshippers.

docs.title: Nation
docs.text: • Bloodcoast (Demon Continent)

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Parent species: Malgardians
  • Mixed with: Humans
  • Traits: Red hair (vs. purple Malgardian/Titian hair), maritime culture, captain-council governance
  • Appearance: Sharper features than pure Malgardians, amber/gold eyes, Malgardian height

docs.title: Malgardians
docs.text: A humanoid species on the Demon Continent, nearly identical to humans in appearance but evolved on a different planet that was not Earth. Malgardians are smaller in stature than humans, with distinctive features including purple hair and a third eye on the forehead. Their arrival on Ge'or traces to the aftermath of The Last Great War, when displaced species from multiple worlds crashed or migrated to the planet.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Nearly identical to humans — the result of parallel evolution on a different planet, not Earth. Smaller in stature than Georian humans, with distinctive purple hair and a third eye on the forehead. Their eyes are said to see what human eyes miss
  • Lifespan: Comparable to humans
  • Mage-cell expression: Notable — Malgardian bloodlines carry strong magic, expressed differently across subraces
  • Origin: Displaced from their homeworld in the aftermath of The Last Great War, when species from multiple worlds crashed or migrated to Ge'or

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Malgardian society is spread across two disconnected branches — the mainland tribe and the forgotten Zahor colony — each shaped by its isolation.

  • Governance: The Malgardian Tribe on the Demon Continent; the Zahor Island colony governs itself, completely cut off from the rest of Ge'or
  • Culture: Malgardians carry the memory of being displaced people — adaptable, observant, and protective of their own. Their third eye features prominently in their art and iconography
  • Relations: On the Demon Continent they live alongside demonic society; the Asatru Empire and Maomodor Kingdom interact with them regularly. The Zahor colony has forgotten the outside world entirely — the violent seas around Lung Continent prevent contact
  • Subraces: Titians — even smaller in stature, held as sacred oracles in demonic culture; Bloodcoast Folk — Malgardian-human hybrids with red hair from human ancestry

docs.title: Subraces
docs.text:
• Titians — even smaller in stature; held as sacred oracles in demonic culture
  • Bloodcoast Folk — Malgardian-human hybrids with red hair from human ancestry

docs.title: Zahor
docs.text: A colony of Malgardians crash-landed on Zahor Island approximately 4,000 years ago. They are completely isolated — the violent seas around Lung Continent prevent contact with the outside world. They forgot the rest of Ge'or existed. The island is named after the hero Zahor, who sacrificed himself to delay a Hive invasion.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Malgardian Tribe (Demon Continent)
  • Subraces: Titians, Bloodcoast Folk
  • Reference: Similar to Migurd from Mushoku Tensei

docs.title: Titians
docs.text:
A subrace of Malgardians, even smaller in stature. Among demonic cultures on the Demon Continent, Titians are revered as sacred oracles — beings of spiritual significance, treated with high respect and deference. Their smaller size is seen as a mark of their elevated status.

The name "Titian" is the demonic rendering; in older texts they are sometimes called the Blessed Ones or Shrine-Kin.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: The smallest of the Malgardian subraces — adult Titians stand barely 1.2–1.4 meters tall. Purple hair (lighter shade than standard Malgardians), third eye on the forehead (more prominent — always open). Delicate build, almost ethereal
  • Lifespan: 130–160 years — longer than standard Malgardians
  • Mage-cell expression: The highest among all Malgardian subraces. The third eye is believed to be the source of their oracular abilities
  • The Sight: Titians experience visions — fragmentary glimpses of possible futures, distant places, or hidden truths. The Sight is involuntary and often painful. Young Titians are trained from childhood to interpret and endure it

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
The Tita Tribe on the Demon Continent is a theocracy built around the oracles. Every major decision — from crop planting to declarations of war — requires a Titian's vision.

  • Governance: Oracle-Circle — the seven most powerful seers. Their visions guide the tribe. Dissent is rare; to question an oracle is to question the Sight itself
  • Culture: Austere and ritualistic. Titians live simply — plain robes, simple food, minimal possessions. Material attachment is believed to cloud the Sight
  • The Burden: Being an oracle is not a privilege — it is a weight. Titians who experience particularly traumatic visions may choose "the long silence" — a ritual vow of permanent muteness
  • Relations: Revered across the Demon Continent. Even the Asatru Empire's emperor has been known to seek Titian counsel before major campaigns. They are the spiritual heart of demonic culture

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Parent species: Malgardians
  • Nation: Tita Tribe (Demon Continent)
  • Status: Sacred oracles in demonic culture
  • Traits: Smallest Malgardians, third eye prominent, oracular visions, the Sight, revered

docs.title: Yak
docs.text: A subrace of Orcs native to the island east of the Demon Continent mainland. Compared to mainland orcs like those of Augamouth, the Yak are smaller in stature and more modest in temperament. They retain orcish strength and civilization but in a more restrained, contemplative form.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Stocky and muscular but notably shorter than mainland orcs — averaging 1.5–1.7 meters. Gray-green skin, smaller tusks (often filed down as a cultural practice), and more human-like facial proportions
  • Lifespan: 60–75 years
  • Mage-cell expression: Very low. Yak do not practice magic and view it with suspicion
  • Traits: Physically strong despite their smaller size. Yak endurance is exceptional — they can march for days without rest

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Yak society in Yakut is built on modesty and restraint. Where Augamouth orcs channel their aggression into martial tradition, Yak channel it into discipline.

  • Governance: Council of Elders — elected for wisdom, not strength. A Yak chieftain who solves a dispute without violence is honored above one who wins a war
  • Culture: Meditation and craftsmanship. Yak are skilled potters, weavers, and stone-carvers. Their philosophy emphasizes controlling one's inner fire rather than extinguishing it
  • Religion: Ancestor-worship with a practical bent. Yak believe ancestors watch through the eyes of birds — they leave offerings of grain on rooftops
  • Relations: Peaceful with neighbors. The Cubra Tribe values their crafts. The Glub Kingdom trades minerals with them. Yak hold territory on Kutten as well, below Marko

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Parent species: Orcs
  • Nation: Yakut (Yak Island, Demon Continent)
  • Territory: Yakut Territory (Kutten) (Kutten)
  • Traits: Smaller, modest, disciplined, skilled craftsmen, ancestor-worship

docs.title: Trolls
docs.text: Massive, regenerative humanoids found in mountains, swamps, and remote wilderness across Ge'or. Trolls are simple-minded but not mindless — they can use tools, speak rudimentary language, and even form loose tribal groups. They are dangerous not because they are evil, but because they are large, hungry, and difficult to kill.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Towering (2.5–3.5m), with thick leathery skin in shades of gray, green, or brown. Long arms, clawed hands, and a face that looks almost human — but warped, exaggerated, wrong
  • Lifespan: 60–80 years — but few die of old age
  • Mage-cell expression: None
  • Regeneration: Trolls heal from almost any wound. Severed limbs regrow in days. Burns heal in hours. The only reliable way to kill a troll is fire or acid — anything that prevents regeneration
  • Intelligence: Simple, not stupid. A troll can learn, remember, and even show crude affection. They are not malice-driven — they are hunger-driven
  • Metabolism: A troll's regeneration is fueled by food. A starving troll heals slowly; a well-fed troll is nearly immortal. This is why bridge-trolls demand tolls in food — they are not greedy, they are practical

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Trolls are solitary or live in small family groups — rarely larger than a mated pair and their young. They do not form tribes beyond the family unit: trolls are too competitive for food, and a gathering of more than four trolls is a gathering waiting to fight.

  • Family life: Troll mothers are genuinely protective of their young — the closest thing the species has to tenderness. Troll children are born small (by troll standards), and the mother carries them for the first year. A young troll reaching adolescence is turned loose to find its own territory
  • Territory: Each troll claims a hunting range — a valley, a swamp, a stretch of mountain. Trespassing trolls fight; the loser retreats. Humanoids are treated as either prey, threat, or — very rarely — tolerated guests who bring food
  • Bridge-trolls. A common trope across Ge'or — trolls claim bridges, passes, and narrow valleys, demanding tolls in food or valuables. This is not myth. Trolls learn that bridges are chokepoints where prey must pass
  • Not inherently evil. Trolls follow instinct. They do not torture. They do not scheme. They eat because they are hungry, fight because they are threatened, and sleep because they are tired

docs.title: The Orgor Kingdom
docs.text:
The sole exception to solitary troll nature is the Orgor Kingdom on Mia — a genuine troll kingdom where hundreds of trolls coexist under a ruling chieftain. Scholars debate how it survives: the most accepted theory is that the island's abundance of food — giant game and rich fisheries — removes the competition that fragments troll society elsewhere. The Orgor trolls are still dangerous, but they are organized — they trade, negotiate, and war like any other nation.

The Orgor are devoted followers of Taosudism: they fear water, drink only dirt-tempered water, and hold all water-based beings to be corrupt and demonic.

docs.title: Relations
docs.text: Most civilizations treat trolls as monsters and pay bounties for their heads — fire and acid are the standard equipment of professional troll-hunters. Some frontier settlements have found a cheaper arrangement: feeding a local troll in exchange for it driving off worse predators. The arrangement rarely outlasts the food supply. On Mia, the Orgor Kingdom is dealt with diplomatically — an army that burns a troll kingdom earns a generation of guerilla warfare in return.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Nation: Orgor Kingdom (Mia) — a troll kingdom, the exception to solitary troll nature
  • Religion: Taosudism — water is corruption, dirt-tempered water is sacred
  • Traits: Massive, regenerative, simple-minded, solitary, bridge-guarders

docs.title: Wargs
docs.text: Large wolf-like predators found across Ge'or. Wargs are not sapient in the way humans or elves are — they are intelligent animals, pack hunters with a rudimentary social structure. They are violent, territorial, and cannot be reasoned with.

docs.title: Biology
docs.text:
• Appearance: Massive wolves (1.5–2.0m at the shoulder), with thick dark fur, yellow eyes, and jaws that can crush armor. Some northern variants have white or gray coats
  • Lifespan: 20–30 years
  • Mage-cell expression: None. Wargs cannot use magic
  • Traits: Exceptional speed and endurance. A warg pack can run a horse to exhaustion over a day. They hunt in coordinated packs with an alpha leading

docs.title: Ecology & Society
docs.text:
Warg packs are family units — an alpha pair, their offspring, and occasionally adopted loners. Packs claim vast hunting grounds and defend them against every rival: other warg packs, wild predators, and any humanoid foolish enough to enter.

  • Pack structure: The alpha pair leads and breeds; the pack raises the pups collectively. Rank within the pack is settled by posture, growl, and the occasional fight — never to the death, except between rivals for the alpha position
  • Territory: A pack's range can cover hundreds of kilometers, marked by scent and howl. Wargs do not rotate — they patrol, and they remember. A pack that has lost members to a village will treat that village as prey for years
  • Denning: Dens are carved into hillsides, cave mouths, and fallen timber. Wargs return to the same dens for generations, and the ground around an old warg den is littered with the bones of everything that came close

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Territorial. Wargs attack anything that enters their hunting grounds. They do not negotiate. They do not retreat unless the alpha falls
  • No diplomacy. Wargs cannot be bargained with, intimidated, or tamed. Attempts to domesticate wargs have universally failed
  • Night hunters. Wargs prefer to hunt at night, using their superior vision and silence to ambush prey
  • Livestock raids: In settled regions, warg packs are the classic shepherd's nightmare — they take sheep, cattle, and horses, and they learn to avoid the traps set for them

docs.title: The Xi'xia Exception — The Only Smarter Wargs
docs.text:
Wargs are a highly mutable species — and on one island, that mutability became something more. The Xi'xia Tribe of central Mia island is the only place in the world where wargs are smarter than normal. Isolated from the mainland, stranded with trolls and beastmen when the Old Lumina Empire abandoned the island, and hunted for generations, the Xi'xia wargs evolved their own systems to survive — and by observing the two other species around them, they learned to be smarter.

They understand words and can communicate — not by voice, but by gesture — which makes them sought after across the world. They form no organized nation and follow no religion; they remain what they always were: a tribe, and a pack.

docs.title: The War Wolf Connection
docs.text: Wargs are the wild ancestors of War Wolves — the larger, loyal subspecies bred by the dragon empires of Klobiendar and Xi before the age of Baoth. Where war wolves bond to a master for life, wargs bond only to the pack. The difference is breeding: the dragons selected for loyalty, and the wild stock retained none of it.

docs.title: Cultural Significance
docs.text: In the Moonfang Dominion on Moon Wolf Island, wargs are treated as sacred animals — not tamed, but worshipped. The island's wolf-shaped geography is taken as proof of divine connection. Wargs roam freely near Dominion settlements; to harm one is death under cult law. This is not domestication — the wargs remain wild predators. The humans have simply learned to live in their territory without provoking them, a fragile coexistence built on fear and faith.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Traits: Wolf-like predators, pack hunters, territorial, untamable, worldwide — highly mutable
  • Exception: Xi'xia Tribe (Mia) — the only smarter-than-normal wargs; communicate by gesture
  • Sacred to: Moonfang Dominion (Moon Wolf Island)
  • Descendants: War Wolves — dragon-bred subspecies
