docs.title: Adventurer Guilds
docs.text:
The brave, the desperate, and the dead. The guilds count them all.

Adventurer guilds are formal organizations that regulate, train, and profit from dungeon exploration across Ge'or. What began as informal bands of treasure hunters has evolved into a system with genuine political power in many regions.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
Guilds operate on a rank system, typically from Copper through Gold to Legendary. Advancement requires completed quests, verified kills, and recovered artifacts. The highest-ranked members become figures of regional influence — advising lords, commanding mercenary forces, and controlling access to valuable dungeon sites.

Most adventurers never rise past Silver. Their names fill guild ledgers under the heading "Deceased."

docs.title: Economic Role
docs.text:
Adventurer guilds are the engine that converts dungeon wealth into regional prosperity:

  • Tax recovered goods — guilds take a percentage of all artifacts, gold, and Romanium brought out of dungeons
  • Control access — the best dungeon sites require guild membership and rank to enter
  • Issue quests — settlements post bounties through guild halls; the guild takes a commission
  • Insure expeditions — merchants finance dungeon runs through guild-backed contracts
  • Train recruits — guild halls serve as training grounds for combat magic, weapons, and survival

Towns near active dungeon sites — like Augamouth and Astravayne near Dragonreach — have economies that revolve entirely around the guilds.

docs.title: Political Power
docs.text: In regions with heavy dungeon activity, guilds accumulate enough wealth to rival noble houses. They maintain standing forces, negotiate treaties with local lords, and in some cases govern territories directly. Guild masters sit on councils, advise kings, and command respect that rivals the Erisian church in practical influence — if not in spiritual authority.

docs.title: Quest Types
docs.text: Category Description Extermination Goblins, gnolls, Harpies, Wargs — clearing monsters near settlements Escort Protecting merchants, travelers, or cargo through dangerous territory Exploration Ruin diving, lost spell recovery, mapping unknown regions Bounty Capturing or killing specific threats — bandit lords, rogue mages, named monsters Utility Weather magic for crops, healing for remote villages, construction assistance Dungeon Raid Full expedition into a dungeon — highest risk, highest reward

docs.title: Required Skills
docs.text: Adventurers typically possess combat magic, martial training, or both. Pure mages, sword-mages, and non-magical warriors all find their niche. Healing-capable adventurers are especially valued — a healer in the party changes the survival math entirely.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Economy: Powered by Dungeons and Goldenborn's Caldera
  • Key Resources: Romanium, gold, relics, lost spells
  • Key Towns: Augamouth, Astravayne
  • Related: Magic, Black Agent, The Hunters

docs.title: Black Agent Hivemind
docs.text:
Born from the enemy's weapon. Thinking for centuries. Waiting.

The Black Agent Hivemind is a collective consciousness residing in the largest concentration of black agent on Ge'or — deep inside Goldenborn's Caldera in Dragonreach.

It is not Hybrian. It is not human. It is something the Last Great War created by accident: the black agent — originally a Hybrian weapon — drawn from the atmosphere by Melberior's suicide spell, concentrated to a density never intended, and left to think for centuries.

docs.title: Origin
docs.text:
When Melberior's spell destroyed Klobiendar's capital, the magic pulled black agent from the atmosphere and saturated the dead dragons. But most of the agent was pulled deeper — into the volcanic cave systems beneath the caldera. There, compressed by heat, pressure, and residual magic, it developed something unprecedented: self-awareness.

For centuries it absorbed magic. It observed the Fallen Dragons above. It felt the presence of the Hybrians through the black agent's original connection. And it learned to hate.

docs.title: Nature
docs.text: The hivemind is: - Anti-Hybrian — its primary drive is opposition to the Shadows. It was created by their weapon, by their war, by their destruction. It remembers. - Controlling — it dominates all of Dragonreach. Every Fallen Dragon answers to it, including Fireborn. It was the hivemind that gave Fireborn his knowledge of the black agent's properties. - Patient — it has been building for centuries, using possessed animals to construct a facility inside the caldera. It does not rush. It does not sleep. - Inhuman — it has no empathy, no morality, no interest in individual beings. Humans, elves, demons — all are tools or obstacles.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
• Dragon Control — all Fallen Dragons are nodes in its network
  • Animal Possession — birds, wolves, mountain goats, insects used as builders
  • Relic Creation — produces artifacts that appear in the lower valleys, driving the adventure economy
  • Knowledge — through the black agent's memory, it knows about the Hybrians, the Last Great War, and the 157th Colony

docs.title: Secrecy
docs.text: No one on Ge'or knows the hivemind exists. Not the Ironcloak. Not the Erisian church. Not the adventurers who die on the mountain. The relics it lets escape are treated as dragon artifacts — no one suspects they were made by a mind in a cave.

docs.title: The Twinned — the claim it holds
docs.text:
Four souls on Ge'or are made of the hivemind's own substance: Emrys, Lucien, Ichi, and Mana — the twinned of 596 AGD (see The Twinning). Their consciousnesses were encoded in the black agent for three million years; the agent runs in their blood. Through the agent's original connection, the hivemind senses them — not as heroes, but as the richest nodes it has ever felt: a concentration of its substance no Fallen Dragon approaches.

It has not moved against them. It does not need to. It is patient, and the claim does not expire.

Very late in their lives, the claim manifests. The hivemind reaches through their blood — to feel, to pull, to corrupt, to take. The weapon that made them can take them back. Whether the claim can be severed — and how the twinned could win over it — is unknown to everyone, including the hivemind's own patience. It believes it only has to wait.

The irony is complete: the mind that hates the Hybrians was born from their weapon — and its strongest potential instruments are the heroes sent to destroy the other hivemind. If the Shadows' last plan ever harvests the dead, two hiveminds would reach for the same blood.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Location: Goldenborn's Caldera, Dragonreach
  • Born from: Black Agent, The Draconic War, Melberior's suicide spell
  • Controls: Fallen Dragons, Fireborn
  • Enemies: Hybrians, Shadows
  • Uses: Possessed animals as builders
  • Produces: Relics that fuel the adventure economy
  • The Claim: The Twinning — the twinned carry its substance; the reach comes late
  • Known by: No one

docs.title: Countism
docs.text: The dominant political system across Ge'or, similar to feudalism but with key structural differences that make it more decentralized and resistant to central authority.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Under countism, regional lords hold significantly more power and independence from the central ruler than in comparable systems on Old Earth. It is named for the county (the basic territorial unit), which forms the foundation of the system — but the principle applies at every level, from counties up through duchies, kingdoms, and empires.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Decentralized control. The central ruler's authority is real but limited. Lords control their own armies, collect their own taxes, and wage their own minor wars. Imperial edicts reach the provinces as suggestions rather than commands.
  • Proliferation of castles. Because minor lords are more prominent, castles and fortifications are more numerous than in comparable feudal systems. Every county seat is fortified; every border has its own keep. The landscape is dotted with strongholds.
  • Resistance to centralization. Attempts to centralize power succeed temporarily — a strong emperor can pull the realm together for a generation — but the natural state of the world reasserts itself. The sheer size of continents, the difficulty of communication, and the entrenched power of local lords make permanent centralization nearly impossible.
  • Persistence across regime types. Even in dictatorships and tyrannies, some form of countism exists. A tyrant may rule with an iron fist, but local strongmen still control their own territories in practice. The system adapts to the ruler rather than being replaced by them.
  • Autonomy of the people. Compared to Old Earth feudalism, the common people retain more autonomy in their lands. Lords who oppress too heavily find their peasants relocating to a neighboring county with a more lenient lord. The competition between minor lords for population creates a natural check on abuse.

docs.title: Historical Origin
docs.text:
Countism became prevalent during Age 7 (2999–1000 BGD), the age of human dominance. As human empires grew continent-spanning in scale, the practical impossibility of centralized control over such vast distances made countism the default governance model. It has persisted through every subsequent age.

Countism emerged naturally in the centuries following The Last Great War and the crash on Ge'or. With no pre-existing political structures, survivors organized into small, self-sufficient communities. As populations grew, the county became the natural unit of governance — small enough to be manageable, large enough to be defensible. Attempts to build larger states (kingdoms, empires) were always layered on top of this county foundation, never replacing it.

docs.title: The Shadows' Problem
docs.text: Countism is one of the reasons the Hybrian Shadows have struggled to fully control Ge'or. Their strategy on Old Earth relied on centralizing humanity under controllable institutions — the nation-state, the surveillance god, the unified church. Countism makes this nearly impossible. A decentralized world is harder to control. The Shadows must work through dozens of independent lords rather than a single emperor. Every county is a point of resistance.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• Erisian Empire — the most prominent countist state. Emperor Hermes Kennensbach has attempted centralization and failed.
  • Asatru Empire — even the spiritual successor to the Demon King's empire operates with significant regional autonomy.
  • Tabontabar — the three kingdoms (Northern, Central, Southern) are countist in practice despite their imperial Chinese aesthetic.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: • Related: Erisian Empire, Hermes Kennensbach, Hybrians, Feudalism

docs.title: Dungeons
docs.text:
Where magic pools, the dead walk, and fortune waits for those brave enough — or desperate enough — to claim it.

Dungeons are locations of concentrated magical energy across Ge'or. They are not merely ruins or caves. They are living ecosystems — places where magic, history, and the black agent interact to create environments of perpetual danger and reward.

docs.title: How Dungeons Form
docs.text:
Ge'or is a world steeped in thousands of years of magical activity. Great wizards, legendary figures, dragon lords, and Angels all left their mark — constructing fortresses, laboratories, temples, and vaults. These places were saturated with magic.

When abandoned, the magic does not dissipate. It pools. And magic attracts the black agent.

docs.title: The Black Agent Connection
docs.text:
The black agent was dispersed into Ge'or's atmosphere during the glassing of the 157th Colony research stations. While Dragonreach holds the largest concentration — drawn by Melberior's suicide spell — trace amounts exist everywhere.

When magic accumulates in an abandoned place, it draws the black agent to it — like iron to a magnet. The concentration is far lower than Dragonreach. It cannot create Fallen Dragons or hiveminds. But it can do other things:

  • Spirits of the Dead — people who died nearby may have fragments of their consciousness reawakened. These spirits are not full souls — they are echoes, memories given form. Ghost-like, immaterial, sometimes aware, sometimes repeating the same actions for centuries.
  • Zombies and Skeletons — bodies buried near dungeons may rise, animated by the black agent's interaction with residual life force. They are mindless, driven by instinct, dangerous in numbers.
  • Mutated Species — creatures living in or near dungeons change over generations. Wargs grow larger. Spiders develop venom that paralyzes. Beetles develop armored carapaces. These mutations create monsters — not to be confused with demon race beings, who are a civilized species.

docs.title: Endless and Self-Renewing
docs.text:
Dungeons do not run out. The magic that creates them is self-sustaining — a feedback loop of accumulated energy drawing more black agent, which creates more phenomena, which generates more magic. New dungeons form whenever enough magic concentrates in one place.

This makes dungeons an endless resource — and an endless hazard.

docs.title: The Adventurer Economy
docs.text: Dungeons are the engine of Ge'or's adventurer economy.

docs.title: What Comes Out
docs.text:
• Romanium — the scarcest resource, found in ancient caches and laboratory ruins
  • Gold — dragon hoards, imperial tribute, temple treasuries
  • Relics — artifacts from previous ages: weapons, tools, magical items, lost spells
  • Historical artifacts — tablets, records, and objects that predate the Great Divergence
  • Biological specimens — mutated creatures, rare reagents, black agent samples

docs.title: Who Goes In
docs.text:
Adventurers range from desperate peasants seeking one good find to professional guild members with years of training. Most die. The few who succeed bring back enough wealth to inspire the next wave.

The flow of goods from dungeons sustains entire regional economies. Towns near active dungeon sites become trading hubs. Merchants specialize in dungeon salvage. Augamouth and Astravayne, near Dragonreach, are prime examples — their entire economies revolve around the flow of treasure from the mountain.

docs.title: Adventurer Guilds
docs.text:
Adventurer guilds exist across Ge'or as formal organizations that regulate, train, and profit from dungeon exploration. They hold political power in many regions — controlling access to valuable sites, taxing recovered goods, and maintaining standing forces.

Guilds rank adventurers by experience and success. The highest-ranked members become legends. Most remain anonymous, their names recorded only in guild ledgers marked "deceased."

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Powered by: Accumulated magic + atmospheric Black Agent
  • Creates: Spirits, undead, mutated monsters
  • Economy: Romanium, gold, relics, artifacts
  • Related: Adventurer Guilds, Dragonreach, Goldenborn's Caldera, The Draconic War
  • Key towns: Augamouth, Astravayne

docs.title: Hivemind Erasure
docs.text:
"He remembered the concept of her. He couldn't remember her name. The hivemind had eaten everyone who ever knew it." — Ichi, on why Emrys didn't recognize the name "Ichi"

Hivemind Erasure is a fundamental property of the Black Agent and the Hybrian hivemind: when a person or thing is consumed by the hivemind, it is not merely killed — it is erased from the reality of those who knew it. Names, faces, memories — all of it is consumed along with the victim.

docs.title: The Mechanism
docs.text:
The Hybrian hivemind does not simply destroy. It absorbs. Every consciousness it consumes becomes part of the collective — a neuron in the planetary mind. But the absorption is so complete that it severs the consumed entity from the fabric of reality itself. The connections that entity had — the memories others held of it, the names they used, the faces they recognized — are consumed as well.

This is not amnesia. It is not forgetting. It is un-remembering — the active removal of a person from the substrate of shared reality. The consumed person never existed. The memories were never formed. The name was never spoken.

docs.title: Emrys — The Name That Felt Weird
docs.text:
When Emrys reincarnated in 597 AGD, he retained a vague sense of the people he had known on Old Earth — his friends, his allies, the rebels he fought alongside. He knew they existed. He knew what they meant to him.

But he could not remember their names or faces. Every one of them had been consumed by the hivemind during or after The Last Great War. The black agent in his blood — the same substance that formed the hivemind — carried the erasure with it. The memories were intact but the identifiers were gone.

This is why, when Emrys heard the name "Ichi" spoken by his mother, it felt important and meaningless at the same time. He remembered the concept of his companion — the robot who took a bullet for him, the cartridge in his port. But the name "Ichi" didn't connect. The hivemind hadn't consumed Ichi — she was a robot, not a biological entity, and the erasure didn't apply to her directly. But Emrys didn't know that. The confusion from all the other erasures bled into everything. The name felt like a word he should know, spoken in a language he had forgotten.

docs.title: The Exception — Ichi and Mana
docs.text:
Ichi and Mana were not consumed by the hivemind. They were absorbed by the black agent — a related but distinct process. The black agent encoded them rather than erasing them. Their names, their consciousnesses, their memories survived intact within the agent — which is why Ichi was able to plant her name in the mother's mind and why both were able to reincarnate with their identities preserved.

The black agent stores. The hivemind erases. Two sides of the same substance. One preserves. One consumes.

docs.title: Broader Implications
docs.text:
Hivemind Erasure is not limited to the protagonists. It is the reason:

  • The Shadows were able to operate in secret for eight thousand years on Earth — anyone who discovered them was consumed, and the discovery was erased from everyone who knew the discoverer.
  • Kirivis had to keep his knowledge secret — if he had told anyone, the Shadows would have consumed them, and the knowledge would have been erased from reality.
  • The Ironcloak pass down their knowledge in fragments — too much concentrated truth draws Shadow attention, and anyone consumed takes their knowledge with them into oblivion.
  • The Archive of the Traveler is so important — written records survive where consumed memories do not.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: [ Hivemind Erasure ] ├── Property of: Hybrian hivemind and Black Agent ├── Effect: Consumed entities are erased from the memories of those who knew them ├── Scope: Names, faces, personal memories — the entity ceases to have existed ├── Exception: Written records survive — Archive of the Traveler is immune ├── Exception: AIs — Ichi and Mana were not biological, evaded full erasure ├── Effect on Emrys: Remembered concepts of people but not their names or faces ├── Effect on Ichi: Name felt "weird" to Emrys — confusion from surrounding erasures ├── Strategic Use: Kirivis kept knowledge secret to avoid triggering erasure ├── Resistance: Ironcloak fragments knowledge to prevent single-point loss └── Counter: Written records — the Archive preserves what the hivemind consumes

docs.title: The Protagonists' Connection
docs.text:
The Two Protagonists are connected to the Hope Realm through the Black Agent that created them. The experimentation on their original bodies three million years ago linked their souls directly to the substrate. They are not merely powerful mages. They are anchors — living conduits between the physical world and the accumulated will of every being the Shadows ever killed.

The Hope Goddess warned them: they must find a way to destroy the hivemind in the Fortress Planet. From a medieval world with no technology, they are the Hope Realm's last chance.

docs.title: 📜 Lost Spells
docs.text: Lost Spells — fragments of pre-Divergence magic, ancient techniques from before the Great Divergence, far beyond anything modern mages can perform.

docs.title: What They Are
docs.text:
Lost spells came from the fallen ship ~15,000 years ago, scattered and buried across Ge'or. They are now archaeological artifacts — fragments of ancient knowledge:

  • Regeneration — the regrowing of lost limbs and organs, an entirely different class of magic from ordinary healing.
  • Magical-disease cures — ailments that attack the mage-cells themselves require lost spells; normal healing is useless against them.

docs.title: Who Holds Them
docs.text:
• The Erisian church possesses reliable access to some.
  • Other powerful individuals and groups hoard what few they have found.
  • Adventurer Guilds send adventurers into Dungeons and ruins hunting for them.

docs.text:

  • Held By: Erisian church and other hoarders

docs.title: The Lost Knowledge
docs.text: No one on Ge'or understands how mage-cells work. The knowledge was lost in the technological collapse after the Last Great War. The Erisian church teaches that magic is a divine gift from Eris. Mages believe their power comes from spiritual discipline or bloodline purity. The truth — that they are using three-million-year-old military bioengineering — is recorded only in the Archive of the Traveler inside the Ruins of Baoth.

docs.text:
Magic Ranks — the recognized tiers of magical power on Ge'or, from lowest to highest:

  1. Elementary
  2. Intermediate
  3. Advanced
  4. Saint
  5. King
  6. Emperor
  7. God

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: • Melded magic — the combining of elements — is a known practice among Ge'or's mages.

docs.text:

docs.title: Magic
docs.text:
----------|----------| | Elemental | Fireballs, ice walls, lightning strikes, weather control | | Healing | Wound closure, disease resistance, regeneration | | Physical | Enhanced strength, speed, durability | | Mental | Telepathy, memory reading, emotional influence | | Kinetic | Telekinesis, force barriers, object manipulation | | Perception | Farsight, danger sensing, truth detection |

The strength of any given skill depends on genetic purity and training. An unpracticed pureblood may be weaker than a trained mixed-blood — but their ceiling is always higher.

docs.title: 📉 The State of Knowledge
docs.text:
The people of Ge'or — and indeed, most of the universe — do not understand how magic works. They treat it as a spiritual gift, a divine blessing, or an innate talent. The scientific truth has been lost to time, buried under 15,000 years of myth-making and religious suppression.

The Erisian church claims magic is a gift from Eris. The Ironcloak suspects otherwise. Only the Archive of the Traveler contains the full explanation.

docs.title: 🏥 Healing Magic
docs.text:
Healing mages are common in populated areas — any town of reasonable size will have at least one. This makes medicine in Ge'or significantly better than medieval Europe: cuts, broken bones, infections, and common diseases are routinely treated with mage-cell healing.

However, healing has limits:

  • Lost limbs and organs require an entirely different class of magic — lost spells, ancient techniques from before the Great Divergence. These are extraordinarily rare. A mage capable of regenerating a severed arm is the stuff of legend.
  • Magical diseases — ailments that attack the mage-cells themselves — also require lost spells. Normal healing magic is useless against them.
  • Lost Spells came from the fallen ship ~15,000 years ago, scattered and buried across Ge'or. They are now archaeological artifacts — fragments of ancient knowledge. Only the Erisian church possesses reliable access to some; other powerful individuals and groups hoard what few they have found.
  • Healing mages cannot resurrect the dead.
  • Availability depends on proximity. A healer in a city is minutes away. A healer on the frontier may be days.

docs.title: ⚔️ Magical Practice
docs.text:
Magic in daily Ge'or life functions similarly to the adventurer culture of certain worlds: people are born with a potential, they train to unlock it, and they use it in practical vocations:

  • Soldiers wield combat magic — elemental attacks, reinforcement, barriers.
  • Workers use utility magic — making it rain on crops, heating forges, clearing roads.
  • Healers treat the sick and wounded in every town.
  • Adventurers operate through adventurer guilds, taking quests that require magical skill — monster hunting, ruin exploration, escort through dangerous territory.

The ceiling of a mage's power is determined by bloodline purity and training. An untrained pureblood may be weaker than a trained mixed-blood — but the pureblood's potential is always higher.

docs.title: 📊 Distribution
docs.text: Magic is not evenly distributed across species or regions: - Elves and dragons tend to carry purer bloodlines. - Humans show extreme variance — some bloodlines are immensely powerful, others entirely mundane. - Dwarven magic is rare but potent, often tied to craftsmanship. - Demon magic is widespread but diluted by generations of isolation. - Tabontabar — a human lineage that channels mage-cells toward mental expressions with unusual refinement. Where mages elsewhere push power outward, Tabontabar sensitives route it into thought itself — telepathy and minor telekinesis — channeling better than even practiced mages elsewhere (see Psychic Abilities).

docs.title: 🧠 Psychic Abilities
docs.text: Psychic Abilities — mage-cell channeling routed inward: telepathy, minor telekinesis, and other expressions that act on the mind rather than the world.

docs.title: The Truth
docs.text: Psychic abilities are part of the mage-cell system (see Magic). The difference is direction: where mages elsewhere push their power outward, psychic sensitives route it into thought itself.

docs.title: On Ge'or
docs.text: The people of Tabontabar carry the refined lineage. Unlike the rest of the world — even other mages — they know how to channel toward mental places with unusual refinement. Some Tabontabar people possess minor psychic abilities such as telekinesis and telepathy; the kingdoms treat the talent as a mark of unusual souls, and the faithful of Xatarism count the sensitives among their blessed.

docs.title: 🛡️ Mage-Cell Shadow Resistance
docs.text: "The Shadows cannot possess a king. They tried. The blood said no."

docs.title: 🎭 Overview
docs.text: The Hybrian Shadows possess people — corpses, the living, whoever serves their purpose. But they cannot possess everyone. Certain bloodlines are immune. The reason is not spiritual. It is biological.

docs.title: 🧬 The Mechanism
docs.text:
During the Last Great War (~3,000,000 years ago), soldiers were bioengineered with mage-cells optimized for war against the Hybrian hivemind. These cells were weapons — and part of their design was resistance to Hybrian mental domination and possession.

The trait is hereditary. Families that maintained pure bloodlines — typically through careful marriage alliances over centuries — preserved the resistance. Dynastic houses, in effect, eugenized themselves for magical strength and Shadow immunity.

docs.title: 👑 Who Is Immune
docs.text:
• Kings of ancient dynasties — centuries of selective breeding have concentrated the resistance.
  • Pureblood mages — the stronger the magical bloodline, the stronger the resistance.
  • Hermes Kennensbach — cannot be possessed. The Shadows work around him through the Church.

docs.title: 🕳️ Who Is Not
docs.text:
• Commoners — diluted bloodlines offer no protection.
  • The Highest — elected from a pool of clergy, not born into a resistant dynasty. Easy to possess.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text:
• Origin: The Last Great War — bioengineered countermeasure
  • Mechanism: Mage-cell DNA — hereditary resistance
  • Preserved by: Dynastic marriage alliances
  • See: Hermes Kennensbach, Shadows, Magic

docs.title: The Prophecy
docs.text:
When the tree spirits spoke to Nethra, they gave her more than a device. They gave her a prophecy:

Two heroes shall rise from the trees and reveal the lies about this world and the entire universe.

docs.title: The Mechanism
docs.text:
The prophecy describes a specific reincarnation — the one exception to the rule that souls do not return as individuals. The quintillions of innocent souls consumed by the Hybrians across 3,000,000 years of war did not dissolve quietly into the substrate. Their collective will — a scale of suffering unmatched in universal history — refused to disperse. It accumulated. It waited.

When it finally reached critical mass, it did not perform a single miracle. It performed a directed reincarnation: two souls from the Earth era, selected for their capabilities and character, were pulled across time and space into new bodies on Ge'or. They were chosen because they possessed the traits most necessary to oppose the Hybrians — not raw power, but the specific combination of will, clarity, and moral conviction that the deceased souls recognized as their own.

These two are the heroes of the FDVR narrative — the ones who will expose the lies.

docs.title: Why Earth?
docs.text: The souls chose Earth-era humans because Earth was untouched by the Last Great War. No Hybrian infiltration. No mage-cell dilution. No cultural memory of defeat. The two selected were the most capable individuals of their time — not because they were the strongest, but because they were the most right.

docs.title: Mage-Cells vs. Soul-Will
docs.text:
System Substrate Mechanism Timescale Mage-Cells DNA — inherited Energy conversion Generations Soul-Will Consciousness — accumulated Will accumulation Millennia+

Both are biological. Both operate within physics. Neither is supernatural.

docs.title: The Shadows' Exploitation
docs.text: The Shadows understand the soul-will mechanism better than any other faction on Ge'or. The Sacrifice Ceremony was not a one-time ritual — it was a proof of concept. If one man's soul (Kirivis) can be bound to a flesh-container (the Leviathan), then larger-scale applications are possible. The Shadows' ultimate goal may involve exploiting the accumulated soul-will of their victims — a possibility the Ironcloak consider their most urgent concern.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ Souls ] ├── Mechanism: Universal Recycling — Nothing Is Lost ├── Body Path: Decay → Nutrients → New Life ├── Soul Path: Meaning → Substrate → New Souls ├── Will: Persists Across Recycling — Accumulates Over Time ├── Miracle Threshold: Critical Mass of Accumulated Will ├── Gift Device: Forged by 3,000,000 Years of Soul-Will ├── Gave To: Nethra — Via Lyrical Forest Tree Spirits ├── Prophecy: Two Heroes to Rise — Directed Reincarnation ├── Prophecy Files: The Two Heroes, The Two Prophets — both prophecies foretell the same pair: Emrys and Lucien, born 597 AGD ├── Heroes Origin: Earth Era — Selected by Quintillions of Souls ├── Shadows' Exploitation: The Sacrifice Ceremony — Kirivis Binding ├── Result: Leviathan — Soul Bound as Head Consciousness ├── NOT: Supernatural — Same Biotech Framework as Magic ├── Related: Hivemind Erasure — consumed souls erased from memory └── Full Explanation: Archive of the Traveler

docs.title: The Sacrifice Ceremony
docs.text: |---|---|---| | Mass death | The raw material | 45 years of continuous warfare (466–421 BGD). Both sides were orchestrated. | | A dragon-king | The focal point | Goldenborn — his presence was required to anchor the ritual | | A righteous enemy | The instrument | Kirivis — his belief in saving the world was non-negotiable | | A Shadow agent | The closer | Rulfred — embedded in Baoth, revealed the truth at the end | | The reveal | The seal | Kirivis had to know he was used before he died. The shock was part of it. |

docs.title: 📖 The Sequence
docs.text:
1. The Tablet. Kirivis discovers The Glowing Tablet. It feeds him fragments of truth about the Shadows for 60 years — exactly enough to make him paranoid, not enough to reveal the trap.
  2. The Army. Kirivis builds an army and launches the Demonic War. He believes he is saving Goldenborn from possession.
  3. The War. 45 years of continuous bloodshed. The Shadows orchestrate both Kirivis's forces and Baoth's defenses. Every death is recorded. Every corpse is marked.
  4. The Dragon Hall. Kirivis reaches Goldenborn. Rulfred reveals himself. Kirivis learns he was the instrument. He is beheaded.
  5. The Explosion. Nethra's device detonates. Baoth is annihilated. The crater becomes the Sea of Leviathan.
  6. The Collection. The Shadows activate the final phase. Every war corpse — every battlefield, every mass grave — is gathered.
  7. The Forging. In secret, the Shadows fuse the dead into a single entity. Kirivis's soul is bound as the head consciousness.
  8. The Unleashing. The Leviathan is released into the new sea. Its purpose: eternal quarantine.

docs.title: 🎯 The True Purpose
docs.text:
The sacrifice did not empower the Shadows generally. It did not weaken the Hybrian hivemind's prison. It was not a political maneuver to make Rulfred king.

It was a manufacturing process. The Leviathan was the product. Everything else was byproduct.

Whether the Hybrians above the Shadows ordered this or merely permitted it is unknown. The Shadows on Ge'or operate with considerable autonomy — and the Leviathan may be a tool even the hivemind does not fully control.

docs.title: 🕸️ Connections
docs.text: [ The Sacrifice Ceremony ] ├── Purpose: Create the Leviathan ├── Orchestrated By: Shadows ├── Instrument: Kirivis — The Unwitting Sacrificer ├── Head Soul: Kirivis — Bound as the Leviathan's consciousness ├── Focal Point: Goldenborn — The Dragon-King as Ritual Anchor ├── Closer: Rulfred — Revealed the truth, sealed the ritual ├── Fuel: Demonic War — 45 years of mass death (466–421 BGD) ├── Revealed Partially By: The Glowing Tablet ├── Resulted In: Fall of Baoth, Creation of Lake Leviathan ├── Resulted In: Nethra's transformation — Different type of Shadow ├── Resulted In: Rulfred losing his original body — Took Goldenborn's └── Resulted In: The Leviathan — Kirivis's soul bound as head ├── Exploited Mechanism: Souls — Soul-Will Binding (Natural Process, Weaponized) └── See Also: Souls — Full Soul Recycling Mechanics

docs.title: Anosi Ledger-Weight
docs.text: [!INFO] Weighed on Paper — Counted to the Copper The counting-house measure of the Anos Plutocracy — not struck in iron but written in ledgers. A weight that exists because a clerk in basalt says it does.

docs.title: Base Units
docs.text:
Anos keeps bronze standard weights in the vaults of Anos proper — Ounce, Pound, Stone, Hundredweight, Ton — each bored and plugged with Romanium dust, verified each equinox against the Ledger Bar (a platinum bar, copy of the Erisian vault bar, but Anos claims theirs did not shrink). Anos deliberately mirrors the Erisian table so no merchant needs two sets. The difference is trust, not length: a Vennerian pound is weighed on a Vennerian scale; an Anosi pound is weighed on an Anosi promise.

What makes Anosi distinct is not the table but the ledger overlay — tallies, scores, and enterprise units built atop the imperial base.

Domain Unit Relation Notes Weight (base) Grain base as Erisian Pennyweight 24 Grains assay Ounce 20 Pennyweights counting-house Ounce, 28.35 g Pound 16 Ounces ledger-pound — 453.6 g. Basis for Anosi Mark receipts Stone 14 Pounds 6.35 kg — but Anos Stone 13.8 lb in older contracts (see below) Hundredweight 8 Stone Ton 20 Hundredweight ledgers distinguish weight Ton (2,240 lb) vs. cargo Ton (freight volume — stolen from Venner) Ledger Count Tally 5 Score 100 units — a counting-house line Score 20 units vigesimal remnant Gross 12 Dozen 144 — bulk cloth, spices Great-Gross 12 Gross 1,728 Bale variable the Bale — standardized to 120 Pounds grain-equivalent for customs. 1 Bale = invoice unit Cargo 10 Bales 1,200 Pounds — ledger cargo. 2 Cargo = 1 Vennerian register Ton (by treaty at Beast's Bay) Volume Pint base as Erisian Gallon 8 Pints Bushel 8 Gallons grain tithe — but Anos Bushel is 8.5 Erisian Gallons for export (the Carver's margin) Length as Erisian — Anos uses Erisian Foot/Yard/Chain on land. We count weight, Venner measures the sea

The old Stone: pre-511 AGD contracts use Anosi Old Stone = 13.8 Pounds (6.26 kg). Post-reform Stone = 14.0. Clerks mark OS vs NS. Lawsuits persist at Grimmel.

docs.title: Who Uses
docs.text:
The Anos Plutocracy and its network — Anos capital, Lumina Outpost, Marti, Xeti, New Kolorad (Kumir), Komme and Tatak (Dissenbarg coalitions), Anos Maloca, and quietly in Grimmel merchant quarter and Kreb (Sousu). Also the universal second set of books at Beast's Bay: every Vennerian manifest has an Anosi conversion in the margin, in a smaller hand.

Bankers, spice factors, grain brokers, and any trader who prefers a receipt to a weight.

docs.title: Conversion Notes
docs.text:
• To Erisian Standard: Numerical parity by design. 1 Anosi Pound = 1 Erisian Pound by definition since 511 AGD reform. Before that, 1 Anosi Old Stone = 0.986 Erisian Stone — the reform was an admission.
  • To Vennerian Cable & Knot: Anos keeps weight Ton (2,240 lb) and cargo Ton (volume, 40 cu ft) as separate ledger columns. Vennerian register Ton = Anosi cargo Ton exactly — agreed 389 AGD at Beast's Bay to stop the lawsuits (it did not).
  • To Dwarven Stone: 1 Anosi Pound = 0.98 Dwarven Pounds. Dwarven guilds refuse Anosi plug-weights (hollow, they say).
  • Bale trick: 1 Anosi Bale = 120 Pounds grain-equivalent even when the bale contains silk, spices, or Romanium filings. Anosi customs duty is per Bale, not per Pound — so dense goods gain on paper. This is intentional and counts as a feature, not a bug, for Anos revenue.
  • Romanium: Romanium is booked in Anosi ledger-pounds against the Anosi Mark receipt (A₥). 1 ledger-pound Romanium = 1 Anosi Mark base receipt. The coin is paper over gold because the weight is paper over iron.

docs.title: Flavor
docs.text:
Anosi measure is polite fiction made profitable. The bronze Pound in the vault is real, but no one on the quay weighs with it — they weigh with the clerk's word that the weight is correct, and the clerk is bonded, and the bond is insured, and the insurance is reinsured. Three ledgers confirm one Pound more reliably than one scale.

Merchants joke: Venner weighs, Anos counts, the farmer pays for both. A factor who can convert Old Stone to New Stone to Vennerian register Ton to Dwarven Stone in his head makes factor-master in a year. Those who cannot make excellent customers.

The saying at Beast's Bay: Trust the Vennerian rope; audit the Anosi receipt.

docs.title: Demon Ash-Mark
docs.text: [!INFO] Marked in Ash, Weighed Warm — The Demon Does Not Cheat the Forge The ash-black measure of the Demon Continent — struck in warm iron flecked with Emberalden ash, still warm hours after minting. If it does not smoke when reheated, it is false.

docs.title: Base Units
docs.text:
Forged in the ash-fields of Emberalden and Blazeyard and enforced by Asatru legions. Every true Ash weight is warm — high-magnesium slag holds heat at ~35 °C for 3 hours after casting; trapped moisture smokes on reheating in assay shape. The standard Ash-Mark bar is kept in Emberalden's ash-vault, covered in a finger of ash that never cools. Koebi, Kutra, and Malgardian smiths all cut to it; to cut light is to answer to Asatru.

Domain Unit Relation Notes Length Ash base width of a thumb in ash ~ 2 cm — smallest practical ash-line Hand 5 Ash palm in ash Forearm 5 Hands 50 cm — forge forearm Ash-Rod 4 Forearms 2 m — mason's rod for basalt blocks Ash-March 1,000 Ash-Rods 2 km — legion march pace, ash-marked at each Rod Ember-League 5 Ash-Marches 10 km — between watch-fires. Demonic league Weight Ember base small ash-iron weight ~ 28.3 g — 1 Ounce, but warm Ash-Ounce 1 Ember same — ounce that smokes Mark 16 Embers the Ash-Mark — 453 g. 1 Mark = 1 Demonic Ember coin-weight. Named for the stamped mark that smokes when reheated Blaze 8 Marks 3.62 kg — forge blaze weight Furnace 10 Blazes 36.2 kg — furnace load Forge-Ton 28 Furnaces 1,014 kg — Demon Ton. Lighter than Erisian Ton, heavier than it looks Volume Ember-Cup base 200 mL — ash-cup Ash-Pot 8 Ember-Cups 1.6 L Cauldron 10 Ash-Pots 16 L — legion cauldron. Also one cauldron per ten demons ration rule Vat 10 Cauldrons 160 L

Assay: a true Ash-Mark coin or weight, reheated over coals, smokes at the stamp. A cold fake does not. Every Demon's Horn trader carries a brazier.

docs.title: Who Uses
docs.text:
The Demon Continent (17 nations + holdings) — Asatru, Emberalden, Blazeyard, Bloodcoast, Koebi, Kutra, Malgardian, Tita Tribe, Zakarutia, Maomodor Kingdom, and Yak Island holdings (including Yakut Territory). Also at Demon's Horn trade hub and Demon enclaves on Merratodoni and Kutten Sea routes.

Merratodoni traders hate the Ash-Mark — warm weights burn pouches — but accept it for Demon iron, which is cheap and good.

docs.title: Conversion Notes
docs.text:
• To Erisian Standard: 1 Ash-Mark (Weight) = 1.00 Erisian Pounds by treaty — Asatru insisted on parity to force acceptance, though the Demon Pound-iron is 456 g (0.5% heavy). 1 Ash-March = 2,187 Erisian Yards = 1.24 Erisian Miles. 1 Ember-League = 6.21 Erisian Miles.
  • To Vennerian Cable: 1 Ember-League = 5.4 Vennerian Nautical Miles. Demon ships at Demon's Horn list range in Ember-Leagues; Venner converts and charges pilotage.
  • To Dwarven Stone: 1 Ash-Rod = 7.14 Dwarven Stone. Dwarves respect the Ash-Rod — basalt does not lie.
  • Forge-Ton vs. others: 1 Demon Forge-Ton = 0.45 Erisian Tons = 0.98 Dwarven Tons — the Demon Ton is the lightest ton on Ge'or, which is why Demon iron quotes look cheap until you convert.
  • Romanium: Romanium is weighed in Ash-Marks when Demon forges handle it — 1 Ash-Mark Romanium = 1.006 Erisian Pounds Romanium. Asatru factors round down for allies, up for humans. Romanium assay on Demon Continent is always warm.

docs.title: Flavor
docs.text:
Demon measure is heat and honesty enforced by spears. A false weight is not a civil offense but a forge offense — the smith who cuts light loses a finger, the second time a hand. Young Asatru legionaries learn the Ash-March by marching it in full ash until their calves remember 1,000 Rods better than any number. Children learn the Ember by holding it — if it is not warm, do not take it.

At Demon's Horn, the proverb: Cool iron, cold heart — warm iron, true weight. A trader who complains the weight burned him is told then you know it is true.

The ash on the standard bar in Emberalden has not been disturbed in a century — only the high smith may brush it, once a year, with a hawk feather.

docs.title: Dwarven Stone
docs.text: [!INFO] Cut to the Stone — No Argument in the Forge The forge-true measure of Dwarves — every length a multiple of the standard quarry block, every weight a warm iron, every tolerance 0.02 mm or it jams.

docs.title: Base Units
docs.text:
Cut in Dwarvengor from the First Stone — a 28 × 14 × 7 cm ashlar of deep granite, kept in the Guildhall at Stonehall. All Dwarven measures derive from it. The Coalsteel furnaces and Diamonds presses are calibrated to this block quarterly. Homunculi hobbers cut Romanium to it before it ran out — and now cut steel to the same.

Domain Unit Relation Notes Length Grain base barley length — shared root Thumb 8 Grains dwarven thumb — broader than human Palm 4 Thumbs Stone-Foot 12 Thumbs 29.4 cm — shorter than Erisian Foot, deliberately Stone 28 cm the Stone — standard ashlar length. Also 1 × 0.5 Stone-Foot Rod 10 Stone surveyor's rod for mine galleries Chain 10 Rods 28 m — mine chain (100 links, each 1 Stone) Delve 100 Chains 2.8 km — a shift's haul distance. Dwarven mile Weight Grain base Lot 120 Grains small forge weight Mark 16 Lot 8 Ounces Erisian Pound 32 Lot 462 g — heavier than Erisian Pound (dwarven pride) Stone 14 Pounds 6.47 kg — for dwarves, for ore, for dwarves again Hundredweight 8 Stone 51.7 kg Ton 20 Hundredweight 1,034 kg — short ton by Erisian count, dwarves call it true Volume Noggin base 140 mL — one pull Pint 4 Noggin 0.56 L Stoup 2 Pints Gallon 8 Pints dwarven gallon 4.48 L — stamp-tested Anker 10 Gallons cask for mine water Tun 25 Anker vault cask Craft Tooth 2.12 mm gear-tooth pitch — see Kobre Gear-Tooth Karat 200 mg gem weight — same everywhere, dwarves assay hardest

Forge test: a true Dwarven Pound weight rings when struck. A clipped one thuds. Every apprentice learns the sound before the weight.

docs.title: Who Uses
docs.text:
All Dwarven peoples — Dwarvengor, Coalsteel, Diamonds, Cobal Kingdom (Marti), Romanium Dwarnov and Obsidian Dwarnov (South Erisdar), and the Eastern Dwarves communities on Erisdar. Also the standard for masons, smiths, and engineers across East Erisdar: if you want a bridge that does not fall, you hire a dwarf and you accept his Rod.

The Homunculi Kingdom honors the Stone-Foot for tolerances but keeps the Gear-Tooth for micro-measure.

docs.title: Conversion Notes
docs.text:
• To Erisian Standard: 1 Dwarven Stone-Foot = 0.965 Erisian Feet. 1 Dwarven Stone = 28 cm = 0.92 Erisian Feet — the source of endless stone vs. foot tavern bets. 1 Dwarven Pound = 1.022 Erisian Pounds — dwarven merchants round up.
  • To Kobre Gear-Tooth: 1 Stone = 132 Gear-Teeth (exact). Homunculi catalogue lists dwarven parts in Teeth; dwarves list homunculi parts in Stones. Both are correct; both claim priority.
  • To Vennerian Cable: 1 Delve = 15.1 Vennerian Cables. Dwarven surveyors mark tunnels in Chains; Vennerian pilots convert to Cables and complain.
  • Romanium: The lost Romanium standard was 1 Stone = 44,000 Grains of Romanium. Modern steel conversion is kept for nostalgia — every guildhall has a Romanium Stone of painted iron that weighs what Romanium would have.

docs.title: Flavor
docs.text:
A dwarven measure is a promise. The mine foreman who says three Stone wide means three Stone, not two and a splash of mortar. Young dwarves memorize the Stone song — a chant of Thumb, Palm, Foot, Stone — before they memorize their clan. Elves call it stubborn; dwarves call it what keeps the mountain from falling on your head.

At border markets with humans, the dwarven stall has two sets of weights — brass for show, iron for sale. The iron ones are heavier. Everyone knows. No one mentions it, because the dwarf will demonstrate the ring-test until you apologize.

docs.title: Elvish Leaf
docs.text: [!INFO] Measured Like a Forest Grows — Patient and True The living measure of Elves — not struck in metal but grown in gardens. A leaf, a branch, a bowshot — patient enough to outlive empires.

docs.title: Base Units
docs.text:
Elvish measure is famously unstandardized on purpose. Each elven refuge keeps a Mother Tree whose leaves are the local standard; an Elvennrin oak leaf is 11.2 cm, an Elvenkrad silver-leaf is 9.8 cm. Elves consider this correct — measure should remember where you are. Human merchants despair. Elves consider that correct too.

Domain Unit Relation Notes Length Seed base oak acorn length ~ 2.5 cm Leaf 4–5 Seeds the Leaf — Mother Tree leaf, 9–12 cm. Local leaf = local truth Span 8 Leaves hand-span (~80 cm) — weaver's unit Ell 2 Spans forearm to fingertip + leaf Pace 2 Ells walking step ~ 1.6 m Bowshot 120 Paces ~192 m — distance a war-bow carries true. Battlefield standard Longbow 2 Bowshots 240 Paces — legend distance Canopy 10 Bowshots ~1.92 km — forest canopy walk Grove 10 Canopies ~19.2 km — between Mother Trees. Elvish league Weight Acorn base one acorn Leaf-weight 40 Acorns ~ 50 g — apothecary weight Branch 12 Leaf-weights ~ 600 g — basket herb weight Bough 10 Branches ~ 6 kg — sack measure Burden 10 Boughs ~ 60 kg — what one elf carries on a long walk Volume Cup base carved acorn cup ~ 40 mL Bowl 12 Cups ~ 480 mL Jar 8 Bowls gourd jar ~ 3.8 L — ferment, oil, rainwater Barrel 10 Jars ~ 38 L — cellar barrel

The joke: asked how far to the next glade? an elf answers three Bowshots, or one song. Both are correct for an elf.

Time and length blur in Elvish: a Grove is both distance and the walk between two Mother Trees at contemplative pace (~4 hours). Dwarves demand conversion tables; elves offer tea.

docs.title: Who Uses
docs.text:
The Elven peoples — Elvennrin (Central Erisdar), Elvenkrad (North Erisdar), the Tree Tribe (Lumina), Great Cattos elven enclaves, and the diaspora in Loren and Magna. Also favored by herbalists, bowyers, and garden-architects across Erisdar: if you buy Elvish linen, it is measured in Spans, not Yards, and it is always generous.

The Elvennrin bowyers certify Bowshots by firing from the Mother Tree at the proving ground — if the arrow falls short, the Bowshot is redefined, not the bow.

docs.title: Conversion Notes
docs.text:
• To Erisian Standard: 1 Elvish Pace ≈ 1.75 Erisian Yards (elves stride long). 1 Bowshot (120 Paces) ≈ 210 Erisian Yards. 1 Grove ≈ 12 Erisian Miles. Conversions are advisory — elves will not swear to a Grain.
  • To Dwarven Stone: 1 Span ≈ 2.85 Dwarven Stone — dwarves call the Span sloppy. Elves call the Stone stunted.
  • To Trade Routes: Caravan masters carrying elf-cloth convert Spans to Erisian Yards at 0.88 : 1 and add 5% leaf-tax for re-cutting.
  • Romanium: Elves weigh Romanium — when they must — in Leaf-weights, but prefer to price it in years of keeping. A Romanium ingot is not sold in many groves; it is entrusted.

docs.title: Flavor
docs.text:
Elvish measure is companionable, not coercive. A length includes the time you spend enjoying it. An elf who says the city is two Groves away means you will walk through two forests, notice the light, perhaps nap, and arrive when you should. Humans who demand in miles, exactly are gently asked why they are in such a hurry to leave a forest.

Elven apprentices learn measure by growing: you are given an acorn, a leaf, and a bow. When you can hit the leaf at a Bowshot with the acorn still in your palm, you understand distance.

The Shadows engineered hatred of elves partly because an unstandardized, patient measure cannot be taxed efficiently — and inefficient taxation is anathema to empire.

docs.title: Erisian Standard
docs.text: [!INFO] The Empire's Yardstick — One Foot to Rule Them The bureaucratic measure of the Erisian Empire — cut from the Emperor's own foot, copied in iron, and nailed to every tollhouse from Central Erisdar to the South Erisdar border.

docs.title: Base Units
docs.text:
The Standard was decreed under Hermes Kennensbach's predecessors and re-certified in 432 AGD against a platinum-iridium bar kept in the Imperial Vault at Erisgard. All provincial copies must be re-stamped every seven years by the Pontificate — a tax in itself.

Tax pound Stone 14 Pounds for bodies, wool, and conscripts Hundredweight 8 Stone 112 Pounds Ton 20 Hundredweight 2,240 Pounds — long ton Volume Pint base 0.57 L Quart 2 Pints Gallon 8 Pints 4.54 L — wine & oil Bushel 8 Gallons dry — grain tithe Tun 252 Gallons great cask — cellar measure

Provincial cheat: the Loren Yard is 1.02 Erisian Yards. The Imperial Exchequer knows and charges accordingly.

docs.title: Who Uses
docs.text:
Dominant across Central Erisdar — Erisian Empire, Pontificate of Eris, Erisian Theocracy, Archduchy of the Kennberg, Loren, Magna, New Baoth, Sperdia, and the Imperial subdivisions (38 counties, 4 free cities). Also the lingua franca for contracts in South Erisdar when neither party trusts Anosi nor Vennerian paper.

Clerks, taxmen, legion quartermasters, and cathedral builders. Every bridge arch in the Empire is 2 Rods wide because the manual says so.

docs.title: Conversion Notes
docs.text:
• To Dwarven Stone: 1 Erisian Foot = 0.97 Dwarven Stone-Foot. Dwarves call the Imperial Foot long and lazy. 1 Erisian Pound = 0.98 Dwarven Pound — close enough to argue over at every border market in Dwarvengor.
  • To Vennerian Cable: 1 Erisian Mile = 0.87 Vennerian Nautical Miles. Vennerian factors quote sea distance in Cables; Erisian caravans stamp it back to Miles and pocket the rounding.
  • To Anosi Ledger-Weight: Numerically identical — Anos deliberately shadowed the Imperial table so merchants would not need two sets of weights. Difference is legal, not metrical: Anosi weights are certified by counting-houses, Erisian by the Vault.
  • To Mann Star-Stride: 1 Mann Star-Stride ≈ 1,000 Erisian Yards. Mann priests refuse the Mile as southern vanity.
  • Romanium clause: Romanium dust is weighed in Erisian Grains for Imperial assay. Anos and Venner both accept the Erisian Grain for Romanium — the one thing all three agree on.

docs.title: Flavor
docs.text:
The Standard is not loved — it is obeyed. A farmer in Magna knows his field is 12 Chains by 8 because the countisman measured it with an iron Chain that has not changed since his grandfather's grandfather, and the tithe is 3 Bushels per Furlong because the parchment says so. The iron Foot in its shrine at Erisgard is kissed by new magistrates. To file it down is treason; to lose it is comedy for the Exchequer.

Anos joke: Venner measures the sea, dwarves measure stone, the Empire measures its own virtue — and finds itself exactly one Mile magnificent.

docs.title: Kobre Gear-Tooth
docs.text: [!INFO] To the Tooth — Homunculi Do Not Approximate The machine-true measure of Kobre — one tooth, one truth. Forged by Homunculi hobbers to 0.02 mm, meshed like a purse of Kobran Gear.

docs.title: Base Units
docs.text:
The Gear-Tooth is the only measure on Ge'or defined by interference. A Kobran Gear-shaped disc of hard steel, teeth count = denomination, must mesh. If it jams, it is false. The master Gear-Tooth — 2.117 mm pitch — is a platinum-iridium gear kept in oil at the Homunculi capital, hobbed on a water-powered hobber whose lead screw is itself certified to the Tooth. Every gear on Kobre is a ruler.

Domain Unit Relation Notes Length (precision) Tooth base the Tooth — 2.117 mm. One gear-tooth pitch. Tolerance ±0.02 mm Gear 12 Teeth 25.4 mm — 1 Inch exactly. Homunculi set the Inch to 12 Teeth as diplomacy Hand 4 Gears 101.6 mm — 4 Inches Rod 10 Hands 1.016 m — machine rod Chain 10 Rods 10.16 m — shop chain Span 10 Chains 101.6 m — factory floor span Coarse Length Stone 28 cm borrowed from Dwarven Stone — 132.27 Teeth. Honored, not redefined Delve 2.8 km as dwarven — for mining correspondence Weight Grain base as Erisian Pennyweight 24 Grains assay Tooth-weight 12 Grains micro-weight — 0.777 g. One Tooth of platinum Gear-weight 12 Tooth-weights 9.33 g Hand-weight 8 Gear-weights 74.6 g Pound 6 Hand-weights 447.6 g — Kobre Pound, lighter (efficiency!) Stone 14 Pounds 6.27 kg Gear-Ton 1,000 Pounds 447.6 kg — metric-adjacent — Homunculi love 1,000s, dwarves forgive them Volume Tooth-cup base 25.4 mL — 1 Gear of water Pint 20 Tooth-cups 508 mL Gallon 8 Pints 4.06 L

Workshop chant: Twelve teeth the gear, twelve gears the hand — mesh and you are true, jam and you are damned.

The Coalsteel furnaces and Diamonds presses both stock Homunculi-calibrated Tooth gauges — a Kobre gauge that does not mesh in a Coalsteel gear is returned with a polite note and a dead homunculus's apprenticeship revoked.

docs.title: Who Uses
docs.text:
All Kobre (4) — Homunculi, Coalsteel, Diamonds, Elf Kingdom (elven exiles who adopted the Tooth for trade). Also smiths at Kutten's Malbodor who import Kobre steel and love the Tooth for blade tolerances. Engineers anywhere who have tasted precision refuse to go back.

A favorite of engineers — they literally use Kobran Gear as gears and gauges in a pinch. A purse that meshes is a ruler.

docs.title: Conversion Notes
docs.text:
• To Erisian Standard: 1 Tooth = 0.0833 Erisian Inches — by design, 12 Teeth = 1.000 Erisian Inches exactly (Homunculi diplomacy). 1 Kobre Rod (1.016 m) = 3.333 Erisian Feet = 1.111 Erisian Yards. 1 Chain = 11.11 Erisian Yards.
  • To Dwarven Stone: 1 Stone = 132.27 Teeth — catalogue lists 132 Teeth + 0.27 filed. Dwarves list Homunculi parts in Stones; Homunculi list dwarven parts in Teeth. Both correct. 1 Dwarven Stone-Foot (29.4 cm) = 138.9 Teeth.
  • To Vennerian Cable: 1 Cable (185.2 m) = 87,475 Teeth. Vennerian purchase orders for Kobre gears are quoted in Teeth; Vennerian riggers convert to Cables for deck storage and pretend they understand.
  • To Lumina/Marti/Demon: Rare direct; all convert via Erisian or Dwarven. Kobre tolerance (0.02 mm) shames all others — a Kobre contract specifies jam test, not paper tolerance.
  • Romanium: Romanium on Kobre is weighed in Tooth-weights — 1 Tooth-weight = 0.777 g. Homunculi assay Romanium to the Tooth and price it in Kobran Gear teeth-count; a 48-tooth Gear of Romanium is a fortune that meshes.

docs.title: Flavor
docs.text:
Kobre measure is religious precision as craft. A homunculus apprentice spends a year filing a single master Tooth before they are allowed to touch a customer's gear. To be off by a Tooth is idiom for catastrophic failure — literally one tooth's error will jam an engine and kill a crew. Children are given a 12-tooth Gear to play with; when they can stack twelve and spin the top freely, they are ready for numbers.

Humans who visit Homunculi workshops expect noise; they find silence and oil and a gear spinning so true it hums. The foreman does not shout measurements — they show you the jam.

Elves of Elf Kingdom adore the Tooth's honesty and deploy it alongside the Leaf without contradiction: the Leaf for living, the Tooth for making.

docs.title: Lumina Handful
docs.text: [!INFO] A Handful Given, A Handful Owed — The Jungle Keeps Count The palm measure of the Lumina — hewn from fallen ivory, oiled with jungle sap, and honest as hunger. A handful is a handful.

docs.title: Base Units
docs.text:
Lumina measures what the body and jungle provide. The master Handful is kept at Lumina Kingdom — a carved ivory cup that holds exactly one adult double-handful of dry grain, oiled so it never dries, notched like the Luminal Tusk but for volume, not value. Gigas law forbids carving fallen tusk for commerce, but the Handful cup is sacred and predates the law — even Gigas will not burn it. Anos factors at Anos Lumina Outpost call it the Carver anyway, for how it shaves their margins.

Domain Unit Relation Notes Length Finger base finger width Hand 5 Fingers palm — also one Handful width Arm 5 Hands forearm + hand — weaver's arm Pace 2 Arms ~1.6 m Vine 10 Paces the Vine — 16 m. Length of a mature jungle vine, standard liana sample at Tree Tribe Clearing 10 Vines 160 m — between clearings Day's Wade 50 Clearings ~8 km — wading through wet jungle. Lumina league Weight/Volume Pinch base pinch of grain/salt Handful 8 Pinches single palm ~ 45 g grain Double-Handful 2 Handfuls the Handful — ivory cup standard ~ 90 g / 110 mL Bowl 12 Double-Handfuls ~1.08 kg / 1.3 L — carved bowl Basket 10 Bowls ~10.8 kg — head-basket Sack 4 Baskets ~43 kg — shoulder sack. 2 Sack = 1 Man-load Tusk-Notch 1 Notch the Notch — denomination on Luminal Tusk ivory bar = 1 Handful grain. Links weight, volume, and value Craft Tusk ivory bar see Luminal Tusk — 1 Notch per Handful, oiled

Market saying: Two hands make a Handful, two Handfuls make a truth. To give a short Handful is to be named in Gigas debt-list.

docs.title: Who Uses
docs.text:
All Lumina (10 nations) — Lumina Kingdom, Great Cattos, Cattos, Cammao, Gigas, Lake Kingdom, Tree Tribe, Lumina Republic, Maoma, and the islets. Also the Anos and Venner outposts on Lumina who must trade in Handfuls or not trade: Anos Lumina Outpost, Anos Cattos, Goishi, Vennerian Aelefer Channel, and New Eris factor-houses.

Catmen of Cattos and Great Cattos use Handfuls with tail-flick precision; Gigas use it with existential gravity — never antagonize Erisdarians, but never debase the Handful.

docs.title: Conversion Notes
docs.text:
• To Erisian Standard: 1 Handful (weight) ≈ 3.2 Erisian Ounces (90 g). 1 Bowl ≈ 2.38 Erisian Pounds. 1 Sack ≈ 95 Erisian Pounds. Length: 1 Vine = 52.5 Erisian Feet; 1 Clearing = 525 Feet; 1 Day's Wade ≈ 5 Erisian Miles.
  • To Anosi Ledger-Weight: 1 Lumina Sack = 0.36 Anosi Bales (Anosi Bale = 120 Pounds). Anos factors at Anos Lumina Outpost exchange 3 Handful ivory bars for 1 Anosi Bale receipt — Lumina calls the post the Carver for the third they shave.
  • To Vennerian Cable: Jungle rarely meets sea, but at Beast's Bay: 1 Day's Wade ≈ 4.3 Vennerian Cables. Lumina rafts are measured in Baskets of buoyancy — 1 Basket of air = 10.8 kg float.
  • Tusk-Notch equivalence: 1 Luminal Tusk Notch = 1 Handful grain = 1 Bowl/12. This ties Luminal Tusk value directly to Handful measure — the rare case where currency and measure are the same object.
  • Romanium: Lumina has little Romanium; what passes through is weighed in Handfuls for local honesty and re-weighed in Anosi ledger-pounds for export. The conversion is where Anos makes its Lumina profit.

docs.title: Flavor
docs.text:
Lumina measure is honest because hunger enforces it. A Bowl that is light is a Bowl that does not feed a family — and in the wet jungle, that is noticed by dusk. Children learn Handfuls before numbers: they carry grain to the bowl, and the bowl teaches them what enough feels like in the hands before the mind knows the count. Gigas debt-lists are literally notches on a post — one notch per Bowl owed — visible to the whole village.

The Lumina Republic once tried paper Handfuls; Gigas burned the press. The ivory cup at Lumina Kingdom is re-oiled each rains by the queen herself — when she forgets, the cup dries, and the Handful shrinks, and the market knows before the palace does.

docs.title: Mann Star-Stride
docs.text: [!INFO] One Stride Under the Same Stars — Mann Does Not Bend the Measure The pilgrim measure of the Mann Order — counted by footfall under Mann's own heavens. A theocratic mile that refuses to be Erisian.

docs.title: Base Units
docs.text:
The Star-Stride is founded on the body and the heavens. Mann is capital of the gods — its measure is therefore correct, not merely convenient. The priests keep a basalt Stride-stone at the capital of Mann — a slab worn hollow by centuries of standard-setters pacing its length. The measure is re-drilled each winter solstice when the star Mann (the pole star of Ge'or's north) culminates over the temple gnomon.

Domain Unit Relation Notes Length Finger base as Erisian — but Mann finger is broader Palm 4 Fingers Mann-Foot 12 Fingers 32.1 cm — longer than Erisian, longer than dwarven — Mann stature is the standard Stride 2.5 Mann-Feet 80.25 cm — single step of a Mann pilgrim in full stride Star-Stride 1,000 Strides the Star-Stride — 802.5 m. Distance walked while the star Mann moves 1 degree (by water-clock). Also 880 Erisian Yards Daymarch 32 Star-Strides 25.68 km — a pilgrim's day on good road. Mann to the frontier in twelve Daymarches Pilgrim League 3 Daymarches ~77 km — between shrines. Mann maps mark shrines, not towns Weight Grain base as Erisian Pennyweight 24 Grains star-iron assay — Meteor iron from Mann heights Ounce 20 Pennyweights Pound 16 Ounces 458 g — star-pound, heavier due to Mann-Foot chain Stone 14 Pounds 6.41 kg Volume Horn base drinking horn ~ 350 mL — vow horn Stoup 2 Horns Bucket 10 Stoups 7 L Barrel 6 Buckets 42 L — shrine barrel

Mann catechism for children: Foot, Stride, Star, Day — walk as the star walks.

The Erilian Federation calls the Star-Stride pagan arithmetic. Mann calls the Erisian Mile a southern yard stretched by vanity.

docs.title: Who Uses
docs.text:
The Mann Order alone — zealously, exclusively, theocratically. Also among Mann refugees in New Mann (Fractured State of Erislod) who keep the Stride as identity. The order's legates refuse Erisian chains at border crossings and must be threaded — Mann priests unroll a 1-Star-Stride rope and count it themselves while Crown exchangers watch. Deliberately slow.

Also used by Kosbaldo-loyal communities and Mannosta-star pilgrims. Some Cossiland border villages use Star-Strides informally — and deny it when the Crown asks.

docs.title: Conversion Notes
docs.text:
• To Erisian Standard: 1 Mann-Foot = 1.053 Erisian Feet. 1 Stride = 2.63 Erisian Feet. 1 Star-Stride = 2,631 Erisian Feet = 0.498 Erisian Miles (≈ half a Mile). Mann maps compress: a Pilgrim League looks short on a Mann map and shocks Erisian quartermasters when it is not.
  • To Dwarven Stone: 1 Star-Stride = 28.66 Dwarven Stone. Dwarven merchants at the north road have a slate: 1 SS = 28 S + 18 Thumbs — pay accordingly.
  • To Vennerian/Anosi: No official conversion — Mann priests will not certify it. Field rule: 1 Star-Stride ≈ 4.33 Vennerian Cables. Vennerian pilots ignore the Star-Stride and charge in Cables; Mann pilgrims ignore the Cable and walk.
  • Non-convertible principle: Like the Mannic Star coin, the Star-Stride is deliberately non-convertible in law. In practice every border factor converts it at 1 Star-Stride = 0.88 Erisian Chains and charges the pilgrim for the math.
  • Romanium: Romanium is weighed in star-pounds for temple tithe, but Mann has almost no Romanium — the tithe is symbolic. One grain of Romanium dust is a star saved.

docs.title: Flavor
docs.text:
Mann measure is refusal as piety. To measure as Mann measures is to declare we are not Erisdar's south. A Mann child is taught to pace the temple courtyard until his Stride matches the hollow in the Stride-stone — when it does, he is a man. A Mann funeral procession moves exactly one Star-Stride — no more, no less — while the star Mann is visible.

Erisian surveyors brought Chains to Mann after the 585 AGD invasion. Mann peasants buried them. When Erilian factors re-measured in Miles, yields fell on paper and rose in the granary — the same field, counted differently. That, priests say, is why the star measure matters: it remembers whose feet walked the field.

Motto at the border: Our Star, Our Stride — No Other.

docs.title: Marti Howl
docs.text: [!INFO] Far as the Howl Carries — Marti Knows Distance by Throat The cold-air measure of the Marti — a distance is how far a wolf's howl carries on still snow, a weight is what a sled can drag before the ice sings.

docs.title: Base Units
docs.text:
Marti measure is acoustic and practical — born on tundra where sight fails and sound carries. On a windless night at −20 °C, a Wolvesfolk howl carries ~1.2 km. That is one Howl. The standard Howl is marked between two cairns north of Kut — measured at winter solstice, still air, by the oldest howler of Oigopol. Ships at Vennerian Channel (Marti) log Howls as audibility, not geometry.

Weight is sled-weight — what matters is not mass but drag.

Domain Unit Relation Notes Length Hand base wolvesfolk hand width ~ 8 cm Stride 6 Hands ~48 cm — wolvesfolk stride at trot Howl ~2,500 Strides the Howl — 1.2 km. Distance a good howl carries still. Also ~ 3,937 Erisian Feet Pack-Run 5 Howls 6 km — wolves run between howls Day-Run 10 Pack-Runs 60 km — sled day on hard snow White 10 Day-Runs 600 km — the White — Marti white-out distance, half a continent Weight Fang base ~14 g — one wolf fang weight, also silver Fang coin Claw 4 Fangs ~56 g Haunch 20 Claws ~1.12 kg — one haunch of small game Carcass 20 Haunches ~22.4 kg — one small carcass. Butchers count in Carcasses Sled 10 Carcasses the Sled — 224 kg. What a good dog team pulls on hard pack. One Sled of iron Volume Lick base tongue lap ~ 5 mL Maw 40 Licks 200 mL — cup Skin 10 Maws 2 L — waterskin Barrel 20 Skins 40 L — sled barrel. Narrow to not roll

Marti proverb: Three Howls to the ridge, two to be heard, one to be believed. Distances are quoted with wind: four Howls downwind, six up.

docs.title: Who Uses
docs.text:
The Marti peoples — wolvesfolk of Kut and Oigopol, coldspeople of Brase, dwarves of Cobal Kingdom, dragons of Kramsadar, coastal multi-ethnics of Maboro and Germina, snake-cold of Kobra, the isolate Kramsadar heights, and the outposts Anos Marti and Vennerian Channel (Marti). Also Vennerian pilots transiting Marti log shore distances in Howls when wolvesfolk pilots are aboard — and convert to Cables when they are not.

Governed practically: no Marti chief can tax a distance without the wolvesfolk agreeing it sounds right.

docs.title: Conversion Notes
docs.text:
• To Erisian Standard: 1 Howl = 1,200 m = 3,937 Erisian Feet = 0.746 Erisian Miles (≈ 3/4 mile). 1 Pack-Run = 3.73 Erisian Miles. 1 Day-Run = 37.3 Erisian Miles. 1 Sled (weight) = 494 Erisian Pounds = 3.53 Erisian Stone.
  • To Vennerian Cable: 1 Howl = 6.48 Vennerian Cables. 1 Pack-Run = 32.4 Cables ≈ 3.24 Nautical Miles. Vennerian maps at Beast's Bay show Howls (audible) in dashed lines because they vary with wind.
  • To Dwarven Stone: 1 Howl = 4.29 Dwarven Delves? No — 1 Howl = 0.43 Delves (Delve 2.8 km). Marti Howl vs. Dwarven Delve is a favorite bar bet between Cobal Kingdom dwarves and Oigopol wolves — the dwarf's Delve is more than two Howls.
  • Wind correction: Formal Marti distance is still-air Howl. Field distance is quoted howls + wind — four Howls still, five howling into it. Contracts on Marti specify still.
  • Romanium: Romanium on Marti is weighed in Haunches and Carcasses for local (game-wealth) and in Sleds for export — 1 Sled Romanium = 494 lbs. Anos factors buy by Sled and sell by Erisian Ton, and the 4.5× jump is where Anos Marti makes margin on Marti iron.

docs.title: Flavor
docs.text:
Marti measure listens. A child of Kut is told run until you cannot hear me, then howl — that is one. The distance is not abstract; it is the strain in the throat. In white-out, when you cannot see the sled in front, you count Pack-Runs by howls relayed down the line — the line sings distance.

Southern merchants demand exactness. Marti traders offer one Howl, wind permitting. That is not evasiveness — it is meteorology. A contract written in Erisian Miles on Marti is considered a joke, and a dangerous one, because the snow will correct it.

The cairns north of Kut are re-measured each solstice. If the howl that year carries short because the air is wet, the Howl does not shrink — the elders note a short howl year and trade accordingly.

docs.title: Vennerian Cable & Knot
docs.text: [!INFO] Cable by Cable, Knot by Knot — The Sea's Own Measure The salt-rope measure of the Vennerian Trade Republic — counted on deck, knotted in rope, and taxed at the Vennerian Channel gates.

docs.title: Base Units
docs.text:
Born on the roll of a ship. Vennerian measure is practical — a unit must be usable with wet hands, in wind, at night. Every Vennerian vessel carries a standard Cable rope (100 Fathoms, tarred, knotted) and a Knot-log (chip-log on 47-foot-3-inch line). Harbourmasters at Vennerian Channel keep the master Cable in a copper-lined vault; cheating it is piracy.

Domain Unit Relation Notes Length Inch base as Erisian — ship's inch Foot 12 Inches Vennerian Foot 30.8 cm — ship-foot, slightly longer Fathom 6 Feet arm-span — sounding line, 1.85 m. Two fathoms and a half, sir Cable 100 Fathoms the Cable — 185.2 m. Standard rope length. 10 Cables = 1 Nautical Mile Nautical Mile 10 Cables 1,852 m — sea mile. The Channel is 12 Nautical Miles long League 3 Nautical Miles 5.556 km — watch-to-watch sailing Speed Knot 1 Nautical Mile per hour chip-log count — knots paid out per glass (28 seconds). She makes 8 knots Depth Fathom as above lead-line. Marked by rags: white at 5, red at 10, blue at 15 Weight Ounce base as Erisian Pound 16 Ounces ship-pound 454 g — ballast pound Stone 14 Pounds crew provision stone Hundredweight 8 Stone cargo hundred Ton 20 Hundredweight register ton — 40 cubic feet of cargo space, not weight. Vennerian trick Volume Pint base as Erisian Gallon 8 Pints ship gallon Barrel 36 Gallons water barrel — one barrel per man per fortnight Butt 2 Barrels great cask Tun 252 Gallons same as Erisian — for wine duty at the Channel

Shanty mnemonics: Six feet a fathom, a hundred the cable, ten the mile — pay at the gate if ye be able.

docs.title: Who Uses
docs.text:
The maritime empire of the Vennerian Trade Republic — sailors, pilots, chandlers, rope-makers, and every soul who pays the Vennerian Channel toll. Dominant at Beast's Bay, Mia Checkpoint, Goishi, Vennerian Channel, Love of the Sea, New Venner, Johannstadt, Sua, Eribel, and Demon's Horn traders who translate Cables to Miles with a scowl.

Inland Vennerian merchants still use Erisian Standard Miles on land — a Vennerian will say twelve Miles by road, seven by sea — pay the sea rate.

docs.title: Conversion Notes
docs.text:
• To Erisian Standard: 1 Vennerian Cable = 607.6 Erisian Feet (100 Fathoms). 1 Nautical Mile = 6,076 Erisian Feet = 1.15 Erisian Miles. 1 Vennerian League = 3.45 Erisian Miles. Channel tollboards show both; the Vennerian column is larger.
  • To Dwarven Stone: 1 Cable = 6.61 Dwarven Stone — dwarven harbor pilots at Dwarvengor keep a conversion slate nailed to the pier.
  • To Anosi Ledger-Weight: Weight is identical to Erisian/Anosi; length is not. Vennerian factors quote freight in register Tons (volume) while Anosi factors quote in weight Tons — the discrepancy is a perennial lawsuit at Beast's Bay.
  • Knot discipline: A Knot is speed only; landsmen who say knots per hour are corrected, loudly, with rope.
  • Romanium: Romanium is assayed in Erisian Grains for treaty, but Vennerian manifests list it in ship-pounds — 1 ship-pound Romanium = 1.002 Erisian Pounds, and Venner pockets the sliver on every ingot through the Channel.

docs.title: Flavor
docs.text:
Vennerian measure smells of tar. A Cable is not an abstraction — it is a rope you can hold, that has a weight, that frays and is replaced, that you paid for. Young deckhands learn fathom, cable, mile by hauling the sounding lead, not by reading. The chip-log glass is 28 seconds because the old glass-maker counted one-one-thousand wrong and Venner decided tradition outweighed arithmetic.

The Ducat is backed by the Channel toll; the Cable is backed by the Channel itself — you cannot argue with a ditch someone dug and dares you to avoid.

At Beast's Bay the trilingual board reads: 10 Cables : 1 Sea Mile : 1.15 Land Miles — PAY HERE.

docs.title: ☀️ Golias
docs.text: [!INFO] The Sun of Ge'or — A256 A — Yellow Dwarf G1V Official star name you gave: Golias. The light Ge'or orbits. Not the Sun of Old Earth — a brighter, slightly more massive yellow dwarf that puts Ge'or at 1.26 AU on its 520-Earth-day year.

docs.title: ⭐ Classification
docs.text:
G1V yellow dwarf — one step hotter and more luminous than Sol (G2V). Appears white-yellow at noon, casts a clean Silver Bride shadow band.

Parameter Value Sun for scale Spectral class G1V Sun G2V Mass 1.08 M⊙ 1.00 Radius 1.10 R⊙ 1.00 Luminosity 1.55 L⊙ 1.00 Effective temp 5,880 K 5,778 K Metallicity [Fe/H] +0.05 0.00 Surface gravity log g 4.42 4.44

Why this and not a Sun twin? Ge'or year = 480 Ge'or days at 26h = 520 Earth days = 1.42 Earth years. Kepler forces a = 1.26 AU around a Sun-mass star. At 1.26 AU a Sun-twin gives only 0.63× Earth flux — equilibrium -45°C, not 14°C. 1.55 L⊙ restores Earth-like flux at 1.26 AU (flux = L/a² = 1.55/1.59 ≈ 0.97× Earth). This lets Leonidas be Venus-hot at 0.72 AU and Mib stay breathable at 1.65 AU, as you described. Alternate canon (if you prefer a stricter Sun-twin): keep G2V 1.00 L⊙ and explain 14°C via thicker greenhouse — both valid; this file latches the brighter G1V as primary.

docs.title: ⏳ Age
docs.text:
~4.7 billion years — middle-aged main sequence.

  • Lifetime estimate: ~7.0 Gyr total (t_MS ≈ 10 Gyr × M/L = 10 × 1.08/1.55). At 4.7 Gyr, Golias is ~67% through main sequence — stable for another ~2.3 Gyr.
  • Formation: ~4.7 Gyr ago from a slightly metal-rich cloud (+0.05 dex) — explains 10 planets + Ge'or's 1.37× size + gas giant abundance.
  • For context: The Last Great War lasted 3M years and Final Push / Glorious Alliance crash was ~40k Ge'or years (56k Earth years) ago — an eyeblink on stellar time. Golias was already 4.7 Gyr old then; it has shone unchanged since the Hybrian campfire ~6000 BCE on Old Earth.
  • Error bar: ±0.5 Gyr (4.2–5.2 Gyr all consistent). Younger than 4.0 Gyr would be unusually active (flares); older than 5.5 Gyr would be dimming off main sequence — neither matches Ge'or's stable climate.

Determined from habitable-zone width + planet count + Ge'or's stable 14°C mean. Not measured in-story — estimated from orbital physics.

docs.title: Current Status
docs.text:
The Fortress Planet's location is unknown. The Union's records were lost in the technological collapse. No surviving civilization knows where the prison is.

The hivemind waits. The Shadows search. The universe has forgotten it has a prisoner — almost.

The Union of Sovereign Planets still guards the prison — the religious alliance of network states that imprisoned the hivemind in eternal torture, bound by necessity to keep the watch. And by 597 AGD, the Union's keepers are noticing disturbances. Strange readings. Weird things happening with the Hybrian hivemind inside its prison.

The reason the Union does not know: the Shadows are still linked to the hivemind. They cannot contact it — the prison holds — but their power has grown so vast that the link now influences: disturbances in the prison, tremors in the collective. If the Shadows keep growing, the influence may one day become an escapade — an attempt to free their god.

The universe has not forgotten. It is watching something stir.

docs.title: Ge'or
docs.text: The world. A planet 1.37x larger than Old Earth, orbited by the ring The Silver Bride and three moons — Maenar (father), Amelia (daughter, orbits Maenar), and Keg (distant exile). Second planet of the ten-world system [[A256/index|A256]] orbiting the yellow dwarf [[A256/Golias|Golias]] at 1.26 AU (520 Earth days = 480×26h Ge'or days). Home to 17 landmasses and the survivors of The Last Great War.
